Further development and external validation of integrated models are warranted.

articles.title: Temporary External-Bolster Full-Thickness Sutures Versus Conventional Buried Sutures for Double-Eyelid Blepharoplasty in Asian Women: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional buried-suture double-eyelid blepharoplasty leaves permanent suture material within the eyelid, which may cause knot-related complications or complicate revision surgery. A temporary full-thickness technique with external cotton-bolster fixation avoids retained subcutaneous sutures.

OBJECTIVE: To compare 6-month outcomes of temporary external-bolster full-thickness sutures with conventional buried-suture blepharoplasty in Asian women.

METHODS: The authors retrospectively reviewed 40 women undergoing primary double-eyelid blepharoplasty from January 2017 to January 2024. Twenty received temporary full-thickness sutures secured over external cotton bolsters, and 20 received conventional buried sutures. Outcomes at 6 months included bilateral crease symmetry, fold loss, suture-related reaction, delayed edema resolution, satisfaction, infection, and ptosis. Categorical outcomes were compared using 2-sided Fisher exact tests.

RESULTS: High bilateral symmetry occurred in 19 of 20 patients (95%) in the external-bolster group and 15 of 20 (75%) in the buried-suture group (P=0.182). Fold loss occurred in 0 versus 3 patients (P=.231), suture-related reaction in 0 versus 2 (P=0.487), and satisfaction in 19 versus 18 (P=1.000), respectively. Delayed edema resolution occurred in 0 versus 10 patients (P<0.001). No infection or postoperative ptosis was documented in the external-bolster group.

CONCLUSIONS: Temporary external-bolster full-thickness sutures were feasible and avoided permanent subcutaneous suture material. Faster recorded edema resolution was observed, whereas differences in other outcomes were not statistically conclusive. Larger prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Ocular Complications Related to Iris-Fixated Phakic Intraocular Lens Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the cumulative prevalence of ocular complications following implantation of Artisan®/Verisyse® iris-fixated phakic intraocular lenses in adult patients undergoing refractive surgery. Outcomes included postoperative ocular complications and longitudinal loss of endothelial cell density (ECD).

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Phakic intraocular lenses are widely used to correct moderate-to-high refractive errors. Available evidence on complication rates is heterogeneous and often limited to narrative reports, hindering accurate risk counseling and long-term clinical decision-making.

METHODS: This study was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251150677). Eligible studies included ≥10 eyes implanted with Artisan®/Verisyse® lenses reporting postoperative complications. Risk of bias was assessed using design-specific tools. Proportion meta-analyses were performed with subgroup analyses comparing real-world evidence studies versus clinical trials. ECD loss was analyzed from three months to 10 years post-implantation. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Fifty-five studies were included. Iris atrophy was the most common complication (20.3%, 95% CI: 5.7-52.1). Other complications included pupil ovalization (7.6%, 95% CI: 4.8-12.5), progressive reduction in visual acuity (7.6%, 95% CI: 5.8-9.5), position-related complications (including rotation, dislocation, subluxation, and luxation) (6.7%, 95% CI: 1.9-33.4), uveitis (6.2%, 95% CI: 4.3-9.1), and halos (5.3%, 95% CI: 3.2-7.9). Ocular hypertension (4.7%, 95% CI: 2.4-7.9), cataract (2.8%, 95% CI: 1.6-3.5), corneal decompensation (2.6%, 95% CI: 1.8-6.5), and retinal detachment (1.1%, 95% CI: 0.7-1.3) occurred less frequently. Subgroup analyses showed higher rates of corneal decompensation in real-world studies (4.2% vs. 1.3%; p = 0.04) and traumatic position-related complications (5.0% vs. 0.8%; p = 0.02), whereas ocular hypertension was more frequent in clinical trials (14.1% vs. 2.3%; p < 0.01). ECD loss increased from 5.3% at 3 months to 15.8% at 10 years. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, with substantial heterogeneity across outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Despite overall acceptable safety, Artisan®/Verisyse® implantation is associated with measurable ocular complications and progressive ECD loss.

articles.title: Invited Commentary: When Prevention Becomes Dogma: The Case Against Routine Anticoagulation in Abdominoplasty.
Combined suboptimal platelet inhibition and subtherapeutic anticoagulation after ad hoc percutaneous coronary intervention, a prospective pilot study.
National drug utilisation patterns of antithrombotic and anti-inflammatory therapies: a cross-national comparison between Switzerland and Germany.
articles.abstract:
STUDY AIMS: Prolonged low-dose antithrombotic and anti-inflammatory therapies have been shown to reduce cardiovascular events and are guideline-recommended in patients with coronary artery disease at high ischaemic risk. However, their real-world dispensing patterns at the population level remain insufficiently characterised. This study aimed to quantify national dispensing volumes and compare the use of these therapies in Switzerland and Germany between 2022 and 2024.

METHODS: We analysed national pharmaceutical delivery data from Switzerland and outpatient prescription data from Germany for low-dose monotherapy products containing aspirin (100 mg), clopidogrel (75 mg), prasugrel (5 mg and 10 mg), ticagrelor (60 mg and 90 mg), rivaroxaban (2.5 mg) and colchicine (0.5 mg in Germany, 1 mg in Switzerland). Drug utilisation was standardised as the number of tablets per 1000 persons per year. This metric reflects population-level exposure: based on epidemiological data indicating a substantial burden of cardiovascular disease and evidence that a relevant proportion of these patients may qualify for intensified long-term preventive therapy, dispensing volumes of long-term antithrombotic and anti-inflammatory therapies might be expected to reach a meaningful fraction of aspirin use (>10%). Values substantially below this illustrative threshold may suggest limited population-level uptake.

RESULTS: Aspirin 100 mg was the most frequently dispensed drug in both Switzerland and Germany (both >8000 tablets/1000 persons/year). Clopidogrel ranked second in both countries. Ticagrelor (60 mg and 90 mg) was more frequently dispensed in Switzerland, whereas prasugrel 10 mg was more frequently dispensed in Germany. However, absolute use of both agents remained low (all <500 tablets/1000 persons/year). Rivaroxaban 2.5 mg was the only agent that showed a consistent increase over time (+54.4% Switzerland; +40.4% Germany), although overall dispensing remained modest (538-577 tablets/1000 persons/year). Colchicine use was low in both countries (124-163 tablets/1000 persons/year). Across both countries, the combined dosing-adjusted dispensing volume of intensified long-term antithrombotic and anti-inflammatory therapies was close to or below the illustrative 10% benchmark relative to aspirin use, reaching 10.1% in Germany and 4.5% in Switzerland, suggesting limited population-level uptake, particularly in Switzerland.

CONCLUSION: Despite minor country-specific differences in cardiovascular disease prevalence, the observed dispensing patterns suggest that the population-level uptake of low-dose antithrombotic and anti-inflammatory therapies may be lower than expected when interpreted relative to aspirin.

articles.title: Serum Flt3L, sIL-2R, and Gas6 are associated with infection in indolent B-cell lymphoma.
articles.abstract: Infection poses a significant clinical challenge for patients with indolent B-cell lymphoma (iBCL), yet its assessment in this immunocompromised population remains difficult. We investigated the associations of serum FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 ligand (Flt3L), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R), and growth arrest-specific 6 (Gas6) with infection status. Our goal was to evaluate their individual and combined discriminatory performance in iBCL. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 95 iBCL patients with infection, 152 iBCL patients without infection, and 70 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Serum Flt3L, sIL-2R, and Gas6 were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), while procalcitonin (PCT) was measured via chemiluminescent immunoassay. We used multivariable logistic regression to examine independent associations with infection and assessed discrimination using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Correlations with PCT were evaluated using Spearman rank correlation. Infections were predominantly community-acquired (71.6%), respiratory (50.5%), and bacterial (63.2%). Infection status was independently associated with age ≥65 years, Ann Arbor stage III-IV, chemotherapy within the preceding 3 months, hypogammaglobulinemia, diabetes mellitus, and elevated Flt3L, sIL-2R, and Gas6 levels. The combined three-biomarker model demonstrated superior apparent discrimination compared to individual biomarkers (AUC 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.85-0.94, vs 0.73-0.76), achieving 80.0% sensitivity and 84.9% specificity. Among infected patients, all three biomarkers positively correlated with PCT (r = 0.44-0.51; all p < 0.001). Our findings indicate that higher Flt3L, sIL-2R, and Gas6 levels are associated with infection status in this pooled iBCL cohort. However, the three-marker model requires independent validation in homogeneous, subtype- and treatment-specific cohorts before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Intimal Sarcoma Mimicking Pulmonary Thromboembolism: A Challenging Case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report a case of primary pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma (PAIS) initially managed as pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE), highlighting the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion when patients fail to respond to conventional therapy.

CASE SUMMARY: An older patient presented with progressive dyspnea and hemoptysis. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography revealed extensive obstruction of the main pulmonary artery and its branches, suggestive of PTE. The patient underwent thrombolysis and anticoagulation, with only transient clinical improvement. He subsequently developed hemodynamic deterioration and persistent vascular obstruction. Given the lack of therapeutic response, bilateral pulmonary thromboendarterectomy was performed, and histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of PAIS.

DISCUSSION: PAIS is a rare and aggressive malignant neoplasm frequently misdiagnosed as PTE because of overlapping clinical and imaging findings. Early recognition is essential to ensure appropriate treatment and improve clinical outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Persistence of symptoms despite treatment for PTE should prompt investigation for alternative diagnoses, including PAIS.

articles.title: Successful Conversion of Collateral Ventilation Status Using the AeriSeal® System Enables Bronchoscopic Lung Volume Reduction with One-Way Valves: CONVERT Trial.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Bronchoscopic lung volume reduction (BLVR) with endobronchial valves is effective primarily in patients without collateral ventilation (CV-), leaving limited options for patients with collateral ventilation (CV+) in the target lobe. AeriSeal, delivered bronchoscopically, may occlude collateral channels and enable subsequent valve treatment.

OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate whether AeriSeal can convert target lobes from CV+ to CV- status in severe emphysema, enabling subsequent treatment with Zephyr valves.

METHODS: Patients with severe COPD/emphysema, fissure completeness ≥80% on quantitative CT, and Chartis-confirmed collateral ventilation-positive (CV+) status were enrolled. Eligible subjects had fissure defects involving no more than three segmental airways. AeriSeal foam (≤40 mL) was administered bronchoscopically in one or two sessions, and CV status was reassessed after 6 weeks. Subjects converting to CV- status underwent Zephyr valve placement. Primary endpoints were successful CV conversion and target lobe volume reduction (TLVR ≥350 mL) 45 days after valve implantation.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 101 subjects, 75/99 evaluable patients achieved CV conversion (75.8%; 95% exact CI, 66.1-83.8%). Following valve treatment, TLVR ≥350 mL was achieved in 64/72 evaluable subjects (88.9%; 95% exact CI, 79.3-95.1%), with mean TLVR of 1062.5 ± 676.2 mL at 45 days, sustained through 12 months. At 6 months, post-bronchodilator FEV₁ improved by 0.08 L, residual volume decreased by 0.49L, SGRQ improved by 6.4 points, and mMRC by 0.8 points. Common serious adverse events included post-acute inflammatory response (PAIR; 16.7%), pneumothorax (19.2% within 45 days post-valves), COPD exacerbation, and pneumonia. Three deaths occurred, including one probably valve-related.

CONCLUSIONS: AeriSeal effectively converts collateral ventilation status in most treated patients, enabling successful valve therapy with durable lobar volume reduction and acceptable safety.

articles.title: Supplementum 307: Abstracts of the 58th annual meeting of the Swiss Society of Nephrology (Bern, Switzerland, December 3-4, 2026).
Association of Autoimmune Diseases with Microscopic Colitis: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Microscopic colitis (MC), comprising lymphocytic colitis (LC) and collagenous colitis (CC), is a chronic inflammatory condition often linked to systemic autoimmunity. However, many prior studies were limited by sample size or inadequate confounding adjustment. We aimed to quantify the association between MC, its subtypes, and specific autoimmune diseases (ADs) using a large, multi-institutional cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized the TriNetX research network to identify adult patients undergoing colonoscopy with biopsy between 2005 and 2025. Patients with inflammatory bowel disease were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to balance cohorts for age, sex, race, smoking status, and alcohol use. Risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated for overall MC, LC, and CC.

RESULTS: Among 2,165,449 patients, several ADs showed strong associations with MC. Celiac disease demonstrated the highest risk (RR: 2.93; 95% CI: 2.54-3.39), with a stronger association for LC (RR: 3.45) than CC (RR: 2.69). Rheumatoid arthritis (RR: 1.47), RF-positive RA (RR: 2.16), psoriasis (RR: 1.48), and autoimmune thyroiditis (RR: 1.29) were also significantly associated with MC. Interestingly, RA and psoriasis showed higher risks for CC than LC. Type 1 diabetes, autoimmune hepatitis, and eosinophilic esophagitis showed no significant associations.

CONCLUSION: This large-scale analysis demonstrates significant statistical associations between specific autoimmune diseases and MC. The differential risk profiles between LC and CC suggest distinct biological pathways, particularly pro-fibrotic links between RA, psoriasis, and CC.

articles.title: Predictors of stone-free status after shock wave lithotripsy in impacted ureteral stones: a new prediction model versus established nomograms.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify preoperative predictors of stone-free (SF) status after shock wave lithotripsy (SWL) for impacted ureteral stones and to compare it with published prediction tools.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 141 patients with impacted upper or middle ureteral stones treated with up to three SWL sessions. Impaction was defined by absent distal contrast passage and/or unchanged stone position on serial imaging one month apart. Stone parameters, ureteral wall thickness (UWT), proximal ureteral diameter (PUD) and hydronephrosis grade were assessed on the non-contrast phase of biphasic computed tomography (CT), and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) was calculated. SF status was defined as no residual fragments on non-contrast CT one month after the last session without auxiliary treatment. Logistic regression, ROC analysis with DeLong tests and bootstrap validation were used; the Triple D score, Mayo Adhesive Probability (MAP) score and Niwa nomogram were calculated for comparison.

RESULTS: In total, 100 patients (70.9%) were SF and 41 (29.1%) were non-SF. PUD (odds ratio [OR] 1.39 per mm, p=0.027), NLR (OR 1.78, p=0.014) and high-grade hydronephrosis (OR 4.50, p=0.014) independently predicted non-SF status. The combined model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.825 (optimism-corrected 0.781) and a negative predictive value of 93.2%. The Niwa nomogram (AUC 0.611), Triple D score (0.564) and MAP score (0.515), which were not developed for impacted stones, showed lower discrimination (all DeLong p≤0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In impacted ureteral stones, PUD, hydronephrosis grade and NLR independently predicted non-SF status after SWL, whereas stone-burden parameters did not. A model combining these routinely available parameters discriminated well but requires external validation.

articles.title: Risk factors for gestational diabetes in pregnancies resulting from in vitro fertilisation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical, metabolic, body-composition and circulating miR-29 correlates of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in singleton pregnancies conceived after in vitro fertilisation (IVF).

METHODS: This observational cohort study included 210 singleton pregnancies (110 conceived after IVF and 100 conceived spontaneously) managed at a single tertiary centre between January 2022 and December 2024. GDM was defined as the diagnosis recorded in the clinical record and was based on the local 75-g oral glucose tolerance test protocol at 24-28 weeks. Body composition was measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis at 8-12 weeks and whole-blood miR-29a and miR-29b expression at 11-13 weeks by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR, normalised to miR-93-5p. Associations were examined using the chi-square test, Student t test, Pearson correlation, logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: GDM occurred in 43 women (20.5%) and was more frequent after IVF than after spontaneous conception (27.3% versus 13.0%; p=0.010). In multivariable analysis, pre-pregnancy obesity (adjusted OR 10.74; 95% CI 3.99-28.94), triglycerides at or above 2.0 mmol/L (6.57; 2.57-16.77), low miR-29a (5.99; 2.41-14.92) and IVF conception (4.19; 1.55-11.36) were independently associated with GDM; the association with polycystic ovary syndrome was borderline (2.69; 0.99-7.30). Women with GDM had higher body fat percentage and visceral fat area (both p<0.001), but body fat percentage was not independent of the other covariates (3.00; 0.90-10.05; p=0.075). miR-29a discriminated GDM with an area under the curve of 0.81 (0.74-0.87).

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, GDM in IVF pregnancies was associated with pre-pregnancy obesity, dyslipidaemia and lower circulating miR-29a expression. Estimates were sensitive to the diagnostic threshold applied and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Electronic Health Record-Integrated Quality Dashboard for Diabetes Care in Public Primary Health Care: Development and Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality dashboards are essential tools in health care, providing integrated and visualized data to support decision-making. Continuous monitoring of key indicators is crucial for managing chronic diseases such as diabetes mellitus and improving outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interactive diabetes quality dashboard integrated within the public health care system of Tandil, Argentina, to support monitoring and decision-making in primary care.

METHODS: A participatory and multidisciplinary approach was used to design and implement the dashboard. Development consisted of two phases: (1) indicator selection and visualization design and (2) dashboard development and iterative testing. This study was conducted between October 2024 and May 2025. Indicators were initially identified from national clinical practice guidelines and Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set standards and refined through 2 in-person workshops with 10 stakeholders (a health system decision-maker, primary care physicians, nurses, researchers, and IT specialists) who were purposively selected by the research team and local primary health care authorities based on their institutional role and involvement in diabetes care, chronic disease management, or health information systems and were personally invited to participate. Six virtual group sessions were then conducted with the same stakeholders to iteratively refine the dashboard based on their feedback. The dashboard was integrated into an existing electronic health record system and developed using Apache Superset. Usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale following an exploratory evaluation in which participants independently explored the dashboard without predefined tasks.

RESULTS: Stakeholder workshops and iterative testing informed the dashboard's content and design. The final dashboard integrated 29 indicators across 6 tabs in 3 sections for population-level monitoring of adults with diabetes. Among 9 health care professionals participating in the usability assessment, the mean System Usability Scale score was 78.7 (SD 9.4), and 8 (88.9%) scored above the standard benchmark of 68. All participants considered the dashboard useful for health decision-making, 7 suggested further data disaggregation, and 3 recommended benchmarking capabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: The dashboard received favorable usability scores and may support population-level monitoring of diabetes care in public health settings. Its integration into an existing electronic health record system and participatory development were key strengths. Future research should assess its impact on care processes and clinical outcomes and explore its adaptation to other health care systems.

articles.title: Ulceronecrotic eyelid mpox in advanced HIV infection.
articles.abstract: We report a case of ulceronecrotic eyelid mpox in a 27-year-old man with advanced HIV infection and severe immunosuppression. Clinical examination revealed painful ulceronecrotic lesions involving both eyelid margins. PCR detection of Orthopoxvirus DNA in a lesion swab supported the diagnosis of mpox. Treatment with oral tecovirimat and topical trifluridine was followed by clinical improvement and complete lesion resolution within approximately 3 months, without ocular sequelae. This case highlights the importance of considering mpox in the differential diagnosis of persistent ulceronecrotic eyelid lesions in severely immunocompromised patients.

articles.title: Epstein-Barr Virus Positive Mucocutaneous Ulcer Involving the Vagina in a Patient With HSV: An Unusual Anatomic Site.
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive mucocutaneous ulcer (MCU) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder that occurs in the setting of age-related immunosenescence or iatrogenic immunosuppression. EBVMCU most commonly involves the oropharyngeal mucosa, skin and gastrointestinal tract. We report EBVMCU involving the vagina in a 71-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate and upadacitinib. The patient presented with vaginal bleeding and the physical examination revealed a small vaginal lesion that was biopsied. Histologic examination showed ulcerated squamous mucosa with a dense, polymorphous inflammatory infiltrate containing large Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg (HRS)-like cells. Immunohistochemical studies showed that the HRS-like cells were positive for CD30, CD45, MUM1/IRF4, PAX5, and EBV latent membrane protein type 1. EBER in situ hybridization demonstrated nuclear positivity in the HRS-like cells and some small lymphocytes. The superficial surface epithelium was remarkable for multinucleated cells with inclusions that stained positive for herpes simplex virus (HSV). These findings supported the diagnosis of EBVMCU in a background of HSV infection. To our knowledge, this is the first reported example of EBVMCU arising in the vagina and expands the recognized spectrum of anatomic sites involved by this entity.

articles.title: Lymphatic filariasis-associated lymphedema: pathogenesis, diagnosis, management, and global elimination.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYFilarial lymphedema (FL), a chronic consequence of lymphatic filariasis, represents one of the most neglected manifestations of helminth infection, despite affecting an estimated 120 million individuals across tropical and subtropical regions. More than 40 million people live with irreversible limb or genital disfigurement, accompanied by lifelong pain, disability, psychological distress, and social stigma. Unlike other causes of lymphedema, FL arises from sustained host-parasite interactions, in which prolonged immune modulation, microbial persistence, and secondary infections drive progressive lymphatic damage. Disease transmission and early pathology often remain clinically silent for years, allowing lymphatic injury to accumulate before overt swelling becomes apparent. Although global elimination efforts have reduced transmission, individuals with established FL remain largely neglected, highlighting a critical disconnect between parasite control and morbidity management. Current interventions are limited to hygiene-based care, infection control, and conservative limb management; no vaccine or curative therapy exists for established lymphatic failure. Diagnostic approaches primarily capture infection status rather than ongoing immune-mediated tissue damage, constraining disease staging, monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation in resource-limited settings. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the immunopathogenesis of FL, emphasizing the roles of chronic inflammation, genetics, immune dysregulation, microbial translocation, and lymphatic adipose tissue remodeling in disease persistence. We highlight emerging diagnostic biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and integrative management strategies, and outline critical gaps that hinder effective morbidity reduction. Advancing stage-specific diagnostic approaches and exploring intervention mechanisms will be essential to improve quality of life for affected individuals and achieve meaningful, sustainable elimination of lymphatic filariasis-associated morbidity.

articles.title: Unmasking a great mimicker: Thoracic actinomycosis.
articles.abstract: Actinomycosis may easily be confused with tuberculosis, malignancy or fungal infection; its discovery demands drainage of purulent collections and long-term antibiotic treatment. Sinus tracts and sulphur granules that are usually characteristic may be absent.

articles.title: PembroPrep: Accelerating efficiency and minimizing patient chair time.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionProlonged infusion chair time negatively affects patient experience and limits operational capacity in outpatient oncology infusion settings. Advanced preparation and batching strategies reduce delays; however, the benefit of decentralized medication access has not been characterized. This study evaluated the impact of an anticipatory preparation strategy, scheduled batch preparation of pembrolizumab based on anticipated patient census data, with and without ADC point-of-care dispensing.MethodsThis single center, retrospective, pre-post study evaluated adult patients receiving pembrolizumab 200 mg monotherapy across three phases of operational changes: just-in-time compounding, after implementation of anticipatory preparation, and after anticipatory preparation plus ADC stocking in the infusion suite. The primary outcome was mean change in time from patient rooming to checkout. A secondary outcome was mean change in time from final product verification to medication administration. Outcomes were summarized using descriptive statistics and compared using one-way analysis of variance with Tukey's honestly significant difference tests.ResultsA total of 397 infusion encounters were analyzed. Mean rooming to checkout time decreased from 145.3 min at baseline to 140.4 min with anticipatory preparation and to 115.6 min following ADC stocking (P = 0.0002). Mean dispense-to-administration time decreased from 19.5 min at baseline to 17.6 min with anticipatory preparation and to 6.7 min after ADC implementation (P < 0.001).ConclusionsAnticipatory preparation of pembrolizumab was associated with modest reductions in medication administration time, while the addition of ADC stocking resulted in increased reduction of chair time. This approach may provide a scalable framework for improving operational efficiency in outpatient oncology infusion centers.

articles.title: Understanding parental perspectives on chemotherapy side effects in children with cancer at Bugando medical centre, Mwanza, Tanzania: A descriptive cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionChildhood cancer treatment often involves chemotherapy, which is associated with adverse drug reactions/side effects that require close monitoring. Parents and guardians play a critical role in identifying and managing these reactions in children. This study assessed the awareness, attitudes, and proactive monitoring practices of parents/guardians regarding chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions among children with cancer at a tertiary referral hospital in Tanzania.MethodsA descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 parents/guardians of paediatric cancer patients receiving chemotherapy at Bugando Medical Centre, Mwanza, Tanzania. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analysed using Stata version 16. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression analyses were performed.ResultsMost participants demonstrated low awareness of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions (80.5%). However, positive attitudes (58.5%) and proactive monitoring practices (69.0%) were observed. Female caregivers were more likely to demonstrate proactive monitoring practices than male caregivers (AOR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.05-3.68, p = 0.03). Participants who were aware of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions were also more likely to demonstrate proactive monitoring practices (AOR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.22-8.35, p = 0.02).ConclusionsDespite limited awareness, parents and guardians demonstrated positive attitudes and self-reported proactive monitoring of their children for chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions. Strengthening caregiver education and communication during cancer treatment may improve awareness, facilitate early recognition, reporting and appropriate management of adverse reactions.Clinical trial NumberNA.

articles.title: Finding the hidden epidemic: screening for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
Genome-wide synthetic engineering identifies essential genes and host-specific factors governing tropism switching in mycobacteriophage D29.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mycobacteriophage D29 is a phage that infects mycobacteria and has been studied as a model since its isolation in 1954. It can infect multiple species, including Mycobacterium smegmatis, nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis. D29 is now considered a potential candidate for NTM and tuberculosis treatment. However, 34% of its genes remain functionally uncharacterized. Recent advances in synthetic biology have enabled efficient phage engineering, reducing the challenges of mutant screening in bulk populations. In this study, we generated a set of single-gene deletion mutants using synthetic engineering techniques to identify genes required for phage propagation. Functional analysis of all 77 genes showed that 44 genes (57%) and all tRNAs were nonessential for phage replication. Furthermore, infection assays using the deletion mutants demonstrated that genes 55, 56, and 59 are required for efficient infection of M. tuberculosis H37Rv but are dispensable for infection of M. smegmatis, highlighting their contribution to host-specific phage infectivity. These findings provide valuable insights into D29 biology and phage-host dynamics.

IMPORTANCE: In this study, we employed synthetic biology techniques to construct a comprehensive library of the gene and tRNA deletion mutants of mycobacteriophage D29 to systematically assess gene essentiality. Notably, over half of the genes were found to be nonessential for the lytic cycle, suggesting potential roles in environmental adaptation and host-mycobacteria interactions. Furthermore, we found that the D29Δ55, D29Δ56, and D29Δ59 mutants showed markedly reduced plating efficiency on Mycobacterium tuberculosis although these genes were dispensable for infection of Mycobacterium smegmatis. Such differential genetic requirements highlight their potential roles in modulating phage-host interactions across distinct Mycobacterium species. These findings provide valuable insights into the functional genomics of D29 and phage biology and support its continued development as a candidate for phage-based therapies against nontuberculous mycobacteria and M. tuberculosis infections.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicles enable rotavirus and astrovirus infection of low-susceptibility cell lines.
articles.abstract: Rotaviruses (RVA) and human astroviruses (HAstV) are classical gastrointestinal pathogens, but increasing evidence indicates that they are also involved in a range of extraintestinal diseases. These include seizures and diabetes in RVA infections, and central nervous system infections in HAstV infections. However, the mechanisms by which these viruses disseminate beyond the intestine remain unclear. Given the previously described association of RVA and HAstV with extracellular vesicles (EVs), we investigated whether purified EV-virus complexes could mediate infection of cells with low susceptibility to these viruses. We found that the RVA strain RRV, as well as two HAstV strains (the classical HAstV-8, Yuc8 strain, and the divergent non-classical VA1 strain), could infect low-susceptibility cell lines (BHK, SK-N-SH, F11, and CHO) when associated with EVs. This infectivity was dependent on EV integrity, since disruption of vesicles by detergent treatment reduced infection. Furthermore, a fraction of viral particles was protected from neutralizing antibodies, most likely because they were enclosed within EVs. Together, these findings suggest that EVs may act as vehicles facilitating the dissemination of RVA and HAstV beyond the gastrointestinal tract.IMPORTANCEGastrointestinal viruses typically infect specific intestinal cell types; however, rotaviruses (RVA) and human astroviruses (HAstV) have been associated with a range of extraintestinal pathologies. To better understand how these viruses disseminate beyond the intestine, we investigated the potential role of their interactions with extracellular vesicles (EVs). We found that the simian RVA strain RRV and HAstV strains Yuc8 and VA1, when associated with EVs, could infect low-susceptibility cells. A fraction of the EV-associated viral particles was resistant to antibody-mediated neutralization, suggesting that EVs protected them. These observations support the possibility that EVs could serve as vehicles enabling RVA and HAstV to disseminate beyond the gastrointestinal tract.

articles.title: The β-ladder domain of TMUV NS1 enhances viral replication in avian cells by modulating its interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Tembusu virus (TMUV), a mosquito‑borne flavivirus, represents a major threat to waterfowl farming in East and Southeast Asia. In vivo studies have noted distinct viral loads and viremia between ducklings infected with mosquito‑derived TMUV (mTMUV) and duck‑derived TMUV (dTMUV), yet the viral elements driving such phenotypic divergence remain unknown. The multifunctional nonstructural glycoprotein NS1 participates in flavivirus replication, secretion, and immune regulation. Here, we generated a panel of chimeric TMUV viruses with full‑length NS1 exchanges and NS1 domain substitutions based on mTMUV and dTMUV backbones. Our results demonstrated that NS1 modulates TMUV phenotypes in a strain-, dose-, and genetic background-dependent manner. Subcutaneous inoculation mimicking natural mosquito transmission amplified inter‑group phenotypic discrepancies, verifying NS1 as a pivotal modulator of TMUV‑triggered viremia. Since duck peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) infection underpins in vivo local viral establishment, an in vitro PBMC infection model validated the key contributory roles of NS1 and its functional domains in sustaining viral infection. We further utilized duck embryo fibroblasts (DEFs) to dissect the function of candidate NS1 domains. Domain swapping identified the β‑ladder domain as a major contributor to enhanced viral replication. Mechanistically, this replication enhancement effect correlates with strengthened interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. Collectively, our results identify the NS1 β-ladder domain as a critical determinant for TMUV infection. By modulating the interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex, this domain regulates viral RNA replication efficiency in different hosts and consequently modulates viral dissemination and pathogenicity of TMUV.

IMPORTANCE: Tembusu virus (TMUV) severely threatens waterfowl production across East and Southeast Asia. Noticeable phenotypic differences exist between mosquito-derived and duck-derived TMUV; however, the viral determinants responsible for this variation remain poorly understood. Although flavivirus NS1 is a multifunctional glycoprotein, how it mediates TMUV host-specific phenotypes remains incompletely characterized. Using chimeric and mutant viruses, this study demonstrates that the NS1 β-ladder domain enhances viral replication by strengthening the interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. This domain governs TMUV replication efficiency across hosts, thereby controlling viral dissemination and pathogenicity. Our findings uncover a key molecular basis for TMUV host adaptation and provide insights into flavivirus mosquito-to-waterfowl transmission.

articles.title: The reovirus σ3 protein induces proteasomal degradation of IKKβ to modulate the host response to infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Reovirus strains differ in their capacity to modulate host antiviral signaling, but the viral factors that control these differences have remained unclear. In this study, we identify outer capsid protein σ3 as the viral determinant responsible for inducing the loss of the NF-κB kinase components, IKKβ and NEMO. We demonstrate that the introduction of the σ3-encoding gene segment of strain T3A in the background of strain T3DL recapitulates IKK loss observed during T3A infection. Our results indicate that de novo expression of T3A σ3 during infection is necessary to mediate the loss of IKK. Further, the presence of T3A σ3 alone is sufficient. We show that T3A σ3 interacts with the IKK complex and targets IKKβ for degradation through a Cullin-RING ligase-proteasome-dependent mechanism. Loss of IKKβ results in impaired NF-κB activation and reduced IFN-β expression. Consequently, the T3DL/T3A S4 monoreassortant exhibits a replication advantage compared to T3DL. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously uncharacterized mechanism by which reovirus σ3 suppresses innate antiviral signaling through targeted degradation of IKKβ, providing new insight into reovirus-mediated immune modulation.

IMPORTANCE: Successful viral infection and replication require that the virus suppress host immune defenses, particularly innate immunity, which relies on signaling cascades to produce antiviral cytokines. Many viruses encode proteins to target key signaling molecules, such as those in the NF-κB pathway, but the exact mechanisms of evasion vary across viral families and even between closely related strains. In this study, we uncover a novel function of the reovirus outer capsid protein σ3 in promoting the degradation of the IKK complex, a regulator of NF-κB. Our findings reveal that σ3 associates with IKKβ to mediate its degradation via the proteasomal pathway. σ3-mediated loss of IKK decreases type I IFN expression during infection and enhances viral replication. Coupled with previous observations that σ3 from other reovirus strains antagonizes NF-κB by altering its transcriptional activity, this work demonstrates that this conserved viral protein adopts strain-specific strategies to subvert host defenses.

articles.title: Novel wounded porcine skin ex vivo methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection models.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds are a growing challenge in clinical practice and can be associated with infection by antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. With increasing demand for pathophysiology research and therapeutic technology development, biologically relevant platforms like infected swine skin explants are used; however, explants are not typically studied in conjunction with normal microbiota, which recapitulates the clinical scenario. The current study generated 1- and 8-cm diameter wounded swine skin explants from shaved, sanitized swine skin harvested immediately after euthanasia. Tissue morphology was evaluated over 9 days using a custom histological grading scale and growth dynamics of skin microbiota monitored. Explant viability decreased after 3 days in association with a peak in normal microbiota of varying diversity. Stable co-colonization of wound beds with clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates alongside microbiota over 3 days was demonstrated. In summary, the presented 1- and 8-cm explant models maintain normal microbiota and are suitable for microbiome and/or wound infection treatment or prevention studies.

articles.title: ETEC heat-labile toxin promotes β-catenin stabilization and transcriptional reprogramming to disrupt intestinal epithelial differentiation.
articles.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC), defined by its production of heat-labile (LT) and heat-stable (ST) enterotoxins, is a common cause of acute diarrheal illness in children from low- and middle-income countries and is also linked to long-term sequelae such as malnutrition and growth impairment. While the mechanisms underlying toxin-mediated acute diarrhea are known, the molecular events involved in ETEC-related sequelae remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the ETEC heat-labile toxin (LT) profoundly remodels intestinal epithelial composition and function through modulation of WNT/β-catenin signaling. Using human ileal enteroids, we demonstrate that LT stabilizes cytosolic β-catenin independently of endogenous WNT ligands, promotes its nuclear accumulation, and enhances TCF/LEF-dependent transcription. LT exposure led to robust upregulation of canonical WNT target genes and genes promoting cell-cycle entry and progression. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed increased proliferative activity across epithelial lineages with expansion of progenitor and intermediate cell populations. Concomitantly, LT reduced the abundance of differentiated absorptive enterocytes and suppressed transcriptional programs required for epithelial maturation, nutrient transport, and digestive function. Together, these findings identify LT as a potent driver of intestinal epithelial reprogramming, providing insight into how ETEC infection may contribute to long-term consequences beyond acute diarrhea. These findings may inform strategies to prevent major sequelae, including malnutrition, that affect millions of children worldwide.

articles.title: Inhibitors of monocarboxylate transporters as host-directed antivirals against human adenoviruses.
articles.abstract: Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are non-enveloped double-stranded DNA viruses that cause a wide range of typically mild, self-limiting infections in humans, but are associated with high morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised individuals. There are currently no approved antivirals specifically targeting HAdV infection. To identify novel anti-adenoviral compounds and host factors critical for infection, we screened a target-annotated library of 13,000 compounds, covering 1,763 known human targets, against HAdV type 11 in K562 cells. This screen yielded numerous anti-adenoviral compounds, many of which were kinase inhibitors, well known to also show antiviral activity. We instead focused on potent and selective inhibitors of monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1) for further investigation. For 25 MCT1 inhibitors, antiviral activity correlated clearly with MCT1 inhibitory potency, indicating MCT1 inhibition as the likely mechanism. MCT1 exports lactate and is frequently overexpressed in cancers that rely on aerobic glycolysis; many viruses similarly reprogram host metabolism toward glycolysis, increasing intracellular lactate that must be effluxed. Unexpectedly, MCT1 inhibitors were ineffective in A549 cells due to compensatory activity of MCT4, as A549 cells express both MCT1 and MCT4, whereas K562 cells express only MCT1. A selective MCT4 inhibitor was inactive in both cell lines, suggesting that simultaneous inhibition of both transporters is required. Accordingly, combined MCT1 and MCT4 inhibition synergistically blocked HAdV infection in both transformed cell types and primary normal human bronchial epithelial cells. These findings underscore the importance of host cell metabolism in HAdV infection and identify MCTs as promising antiviral targets.

articles.title: Japanese encephalitis virus infection reshapes the gut microbiome and induces colonic inflammation in neonatal mice.
articles.abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), a neurotropic flavivirus, predominantly causes severe infection in children, leading to neuropsychiatric complications. Given that the juvenile period is a transitional window for the gut microbiota to develop into a stable community profile, any alterations to the microbiota during infections can result in chronic inflammation. Therefore, we investigated changes in the gut microbiota of neonatal mice during the early and late stages of JEV infection. Postnatal day 10, BALB/c mice challenged with JEV succumbed to acute infection at 6 to 7 days post-infection. This severity was marked by a surge in systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-6, and MCP-1) and reduced food intake. Fecal 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing revealed distinct β-diversity between mock and JEV-infected groups, with the dominant phyla being Firmicutes, Bacteroidota, and Proteobacteria. The relative abundance of these phyla shifted, with Firmicutes decreasing from ~63.7% (control) to ~39% (JEV), whereas Proteobacteria remained unchanged in JEV. The Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio decreased in JEV, along with a reduction in Lactobacillus. Simultaneously, altered mucosal secretion, reduced tight-junction protein ZO-1, increased pNF-κB, and cleaved caspase-3 together indicated colonic inflammation. Prediction of microbial pathways using PICRUSt2 suggested a reduction in specific pathways associated with beneficial secondary metabolites and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in JEV. Intragastric administration of the SCFA cocktail prolonged survival and delayed the onset of clinical signs and the inflammatory response. Our findings suggest that systemic inflammation and reduced feeding during an acute infection could result in colonic dysbiosis, reduced beneficial bacteria, and trigger inflammation. SCFAs displayed a transient therapeutic effect in JEV infection, highlighting the potential of gut microbiota modulation to manage acute viral infection.IMPORTANCEJapanese encephalitis remains a leading cause of viral encephalitis in children across the Asia-Pacific region, with new outbreaks driven by evolving demographic factors. The need for targeted therapies beyond existing supportive care underscores the need for new host-directed interventions. Our findings suggest that gut-brain axis interactions may play a role in acute viral infections, potentially amplifying disease severity through infection-driven reduction in feeding, increased cytokine production, and shifts in the gut microbiome. We propose that SCFA supplementation can serve as a microbiota-modulating strategy that offers a safe, translatable approach to managing inflammation and JEV outcomes in pediatric viral encephalitis. This could be utilized as a supplement along with supportive care in other flavivirus infections.

articles.title: Completion angiography and venous outflow assessment in arteriovenous graft placement: A retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Arteriovenous grafts are frequently used for hemodialysis access. Optimizing graft placement is important to prevent thrombosis and reinterventions. This study evaluated the association between vein diameter and clinical outcomes and evaluated the diagnostic value of completion angiography.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 113 patients who underwent graft placement between 2010 and 2017. Outflow vein diameter was measured preoperatively by duplex ultrasound and intraoperatively by angiography. Angiographies were also analyzed for abnormalities. Outcomes included early graft failure (loss of primary patency within 30 days), secondary patency and access-related intervention rates. Predictive accuracy of vein diameter was assessed with ROC curves. Categorical variables were analyzed with chi square tests; Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests, and event rates with Poisson analysis.

RESULTS: Neither duplex nor angiography-measured vein diameters were associated with early graft failure (ROC AUC 0.63, 95% CI: 0.41-0.85, p = 0.24; and ROC AUC 0.54, 95% CI: 0.40-0.69, p = 0.57) or secondary patency (HR 1.07 per mm, 95% CI 0.84-1.38 and HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96-1.18 respectively). Using the 4-mm cutoff recommended in clinical practice guidelines, vein diameter was not associated with access-related intervention rates. Completion angiography led to immediate revision in 15% of cases. Venous outflow abnormalities were present in 63% of final completion angiographies and were associated with higher intervention rates during follow-up (3.26 vs 2.58 per patient-year, p = 0.01), but not with early graft failure or 12-month secondary patency.

CONCLUSIONS: Vein diameter, ranging from 1.5 to 15 mm, did not predict clinical outcomes, suggesting using smaller veins than the recommended 4 mm-threshold may be reasonable in patients with limited access options. In contrast, completion angiography proved useful by prompting intra-operative revisions and by detecting outflow abnormalities that are associated with later reinterventions. Venous outflow, rather than vein diameter alone, should guide surgical decision making in arteriovenous graft placement.

articles.title: The SAMP algorithm: Recommendations for safe access and management of ports.
articles.abstract: Totally implantable venous access devices (TIVADs or ports) are integral to long-term intravenous therapy, particularly for patients receiving oncology treatments. Despite their widespread use, late complications, including infection, occlusion, extravasation, and pain during access, are not uncommon and are often linked to inconsistent clinical practices and the absence of standardized protocols for port management. A novel algorithm for the Safe Access and Management of Ports (SAMP) has been developed by a panel of experts from the World Conference on Vascular Access/Global Vascular Access Network (WoCoVA/GloVANet), the Italian Group for Long Term Central Venous Access (GAVeCeLT), and the Italian Society of Vascular Access (IVAS). The algorithm provides an evidence-based, standardized approach to promoting safe, consistent, and patient-centered port management. The algorithm was developed through a comprehensive review of current evidence and best-practice recommendations, and it is presented as a sequential, evidence-based approach to port management. Its key recommendations include skin antisepsis with 2% chlorhexidine in 70% isopropyl alcohol, use of sterile gloves during access, topical local anesthesia where appropriate, verification of catheter patency and/or tip location before therapy administration, and appropriate needle securement. The SAMP algorithm offers a practical, evidence-based framework intended to support safe port management, from needle access to needle removal. By standardizing procedures and consolidating best evidence, the algorithm may improve patient comfort, enhance clinician consistency, reduce preventable complications, and has the potential to strengthen quality and safety in vascular access care. It also provides a foundation for standardized education, competency assessment, and future clinical research to evaluate its impact on patient outcomes and device performance.

articles.title: Does gabapentin affect the incidence of postoperative delirium in a dose dependent pattern?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway for Colorectal Surgery (CRS) emphasizes opioid-sparing analgesia to reduce ileus and length of stay (LOS). Our hospital adopted gabapentin as part of postoperative analgesia for CRS. We evaluated the association between perioperative gabapentin use and postoperative delirium (POD).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,165 encounters of patients ≥65 years undergoing elective CRS between 04/2015-06/2023. Encounters requiring critical care, LOS>3 months, or readmissions were excluded. Delirium was identified using chart review, ICD codes and/or new antipsychotic use. Multivariate logistic regression compared delirium rates among three groups: No Gabapentin (NG), low dose (LG) and high dose (HG). Models adjusted for age, race, ethnicity, gender, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), etc. Subgroup analyses investigated delirium by age, gender, CCI.

RESULTS: 1,027 individuals were studied: 20.5% NG, 70.8% LG, and 8.7% HG. NG Individuals were older (75.5±7.2) than LG (74.2±6.7) or HG (72.7±6.6), while CCI (6.6±3.8) was similar across groups. The NG group had more patients with dementia (NG 14.2% vs LG 9.5%, p=0.05 vs HG 11.2%). A higher incidence of POD was noted in NG (34.6%) when compared with LG (25.3%, 1.74(1.22-2.47), adj. p=0.002) as well as HG (23.6%, p=0.06). Prior gabapentin exposure did not significantly impact the incidence of postoperative delirium (OR 1.33 (0.86-2.05)) when the cohort was compared based on prior gabapentin exposure.

CONCLUSION: The use of low dose gabapentin postoperatively is associated with lower incidence of delirium compared to absence of gabapentin. However, the absence of gabapentin in our study is a reflection of baseline vulnerability for delirium. Prior exposure to gabapentin had no influence on incident POD. Future prospective trials are required to address the factors to be considered when determining the optimal dosing of gabapentin in older surgical adults.

articles.title: Thia-Aza Pyridinophane Chelators for Copper Coordination and 64Cu Radiolabeling Studies.
articles.abstract: A new macrocyclic ligand, 3-thia-7-aza-1,5(2,6)-dipyridinacyclooctaphane, has been synthesized and functionalized to produce a family of nitrogen/sulfur-based chelators with tunable donor environments. Alkyl and picolyl derivatives were obtained through selective N-alkylation of the secondary amine site with methyl, isopropyl, and picolyl substituents, and a tridentate macrocyclic NNS analogue was also prepared by N-deletion. The coordination chemistry of these ligands toward Cu(II) and Cu(I) was investigated, and the copper complexes were characterized using X-ray crystallography, UV-vis, cyclic voltammetry (CV), EPR or NMR, and elemental analysis (EA). Acid dissociation constants and metal complex stability constants were determined by UV-Vis spectrophotometric titrations, providing insight into the ligands' coordination ability. Radiolabeling with 64Cu revealed that while the isopropyl-functionalized complex exhibited moderate radiolabeling efficiency, the picolyl analogue achieved quantitative 64Cu incorporation, underscoring its potential for PET imaging applications.

articles.title: Coordination Chemistry of a Hybrid N/S Macrocyclic Framework: PyN2S Chelators toward Stabilization of 64Cu(II/I) in PET Imaging Applications.
articles.abstract: In recent efforts to develop optimal 64Cu chelators with ideal thermodynamic stability and high kinetic inertness, focus has shifted to the common problem of reduction-induced demetalation of 64Cu(I). The most common approach to remedy this issue is to make the reduction of 64Cu(II) to 64Cu(I) inaccessible, with anionic ligands comprising hard Lewis bases like carboxylates. However, an alternative approach has been to focus on the stability of the 64Cu(I) species, most commonly achieved by incorporating soft sulfur donors, such as thiols or thioethers, into the chelator framework. Herein, we present a novel copper chelator, PyN2S, comprising both N and S donors, allowing for an N3S binding mode. Five new ligands are introduced, and their coordination chemistry with copper is explored. Thermodynamic stability constants with Cu2+ and Zn2+ are presented, as well as solution and solid-state characterization of the Cu(II) complexes. Finally, the radiochemistry of the PyN2S ligands with 64Cu was explored, including both in vitro characterization and in vivo biodistribution in mice. Overall, the PyN2S framework has demonstrated promising stability for both Cu(II) and Cu(I), and quantitative radiolabeling with 64Cu was achieved, while in vivo biodistribution revealed the highest uptake in renal clearance pathway organs.

articles.title: Multidimensional Deciphering Underlying Effects of PFOA Exposure in Ulcerative Colitis: From Epidemiological Insights to Toxicological Mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a representative persistent organic pollutant (POP), has been linked to numerous adverse health effects. Ulcerative colitis (UC), characterized by recurrent colon inflammation, is known to have environmental exposure as a primary etiological factor; however, the toxicological mechanisms underlying PFOA-induced UC remain unclear. This study therefore aims to comprehensively investigate the association between PFOA exposure and UC. A meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between PFOA exposure and UC onset, and network toxicology, cross-species transcriptomics, protein-protein interaction networks, and weighted gene coexpression network analysis were employed to identify potential targets and mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular docking, and Mendelian randomization were used to pinpoint and validate hub genes, while in vivo DSS-induced colitis and in vitro inflammation models were applied to assess the functional impact of PFOA. The meta-analysis of four studies confirmed a significant positive association between PFOA exposure and UC risk (Fisher z = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.13-0.27). We identified 170 overlapping targets linking PFOA to UC, predominantly enriched in immune-inflammatory activation and metabolic disruption. Seven hub genes (IRF1, CXCL1, CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CASP1, and IL1B) constituted a UC-associated coexpression module, with monocytes/macrophages as primary sources by single-cell profiling. Molecular docking confirmed PFOA binding to these proteins, and Mendelian randomization established IRF1 as a causal risk factor. In vivo, PFOA exacerbated DSS-induced colitis, impairing barrier function, promoting apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. In conclusion, PFOA exposure is associated with increased UC risk and may promote colonic inflammation by affecting the chemokine-inflammasome network and epithelial function. IRF1 may be a key hub in this process, but its upstream role needs validation. These findings highlight the potential importance of reducing environmental pollutant exposure in UC prevention.

articles.title: Screening PFAS-Mediated Inhibition of Human Cytochrome P450 Enzyme Activity Reveals Nanomolar Potency against CYP2C9.
articles.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes catalyze the biotransformation of environmental toxicants, drugs, and endogenous substrates. Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) accumulate in human liver tissue, yet the capacity of PFAS to inhibit hepatic CYP activity at human-relevant concentrations remains poorly characterized. This study tested the hypothesis that structurally diverse PFAS reversibly inhibit seven major human CYP isoforms (CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, and 3A4/5) in pooled human liver microsomes (HLM) and examined their relevance to concentrations measured in human livers. Thirteen structurally diverse PFAS were evaluated (ηpfc = 4-11). Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctane sulfonamides inhibited CYP2C9 at nanomolar concentrations, with 50% inhibitory concentrations (IC50) of 29-230 nM that exceeded the potency of sulfaphenazole, the reference CYP2C9 probe inhibitor (IC50 = 380 nM), and also exceeded several clinically used CYP2C9 inhibitors. A subset of long-chain PFAS inhibited CYP2C19, CYP2C8, and CYP2B6 at low-micromolar concentrations, while the tested PFAS inhibited CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4/5 generally weakly (IC50 typically ≥ 10 μM). Substrate-dependent experiments supported competitive CYP2C9 inhibition by PFOS and FOSA (nominal Ki = 16 and 57 nM) and mixed inhibition by EtFOSA (13 nM). Exploratory quantitative in vitro-in vivo extrapolation using unbound hepatic PFAS concentrations estimated from concentrations measured in 211 U.S. donors showed that hepatic PFAS burdens remained well below inhibitory thresholds for most individuals. However, 19% of individuals had hepatic PFOS within 10-fold of the CYP2C9 10% inhibitory concentration, and the equimolar 13-PFAS mixture inhibited CYP2C9 within 1.7-fold of the concentration-addition prediction, indicating that cumulative exposure can further narrow these margins. Because PFAS exposures are chronic and cumulative, sustained low-level CYP2C inhibition by PFAS may disrupt endogenous lipid signaling and contribute to interindividual variability in drug metabolism, particularly in subpopulations with elevated hepatic PFAS burdens or reduced baseline CYP2C9 function from genetic polymorphisms or liver disease.

articles.title: A study on viability of SARS-CoV-2 in cadavers in relation to postmortem interval.
articles.abstract: The transmission risk of SARS-CoV-2 from cadavers to health personnel remains the greatest challenge in forensic practice. This study evaluates the viability rate of SARS-CoV-2 in postmortem tissues and identifies factors influencing viral persistence. Lung and heart tissues were collected from 227 COVID-19 autopsies at Hospital Sultanah Bahiyah, Malaysia. Viral viability was determined by tissue culture and analysed in relation to postmortem interval (PMI), demographics, CT values, variants, vaccination status and comorbidities. Viral viability was highest (86%-95%) within the first 12 hours of PMI, declining to its lowest levels (0.1%-2.1%) after 3 days. Significant correlations (p-value < 0.05) were found between lower viability rates and vaccination, the Omicron variant and the absence of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). SARS-CoV-2 remains highly infectious for up to 72 hours postmortem. Strict biocontainment protocols are essential during this window. Furthermore, vaccination and respiratory health significantly reduce postmortem viral persistence.

articles.title: Cancer Incidence and Mortality Patterns in Central Asia in 2022 and an Assessment of the Future Burden in 2045.
articles.abstract: Central Asia is undergoing rapid epidemiological transition, yet internationally comparable assessments of cancer profiles in the constituent countries (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan) remain limited. We aimed to describe patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across the region and to project the future cancer burden through 2045. Cancer incidence and mortality estimates in 2022 were obtained for the five countries from IARC's GLOBOCAN database. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were compared by country, sex and cancer type. The future cancer burden was projected by applying age-specific cancer rates to population projections, assuming stable rates over time. In 2022, an estimated 92,665 new cancer cases and 56,110 cancer deaths occurred across Central Asia. Kazakhstan had the highest overall incidence and mortality rates, whereas the lowest rates across most major cancer sites were consistently estimated for Tajikistan. Breast cancer was the most common cancer among women, and lung cancer among men. The regional cancer profile was characterised by the coexistence of infection-related cancers alongside those linked to socioeconomic transition. Assuming stable rates, the annual number of new cancer cases is projected to increase by approximately 65%, reaching 152,000 by 2045, while cancer deaths are projected to increase by 73% to nearly 97,000 deaths. Cancer patterns in Central Asia suggest that regional cancer control planning should be nuanced to reflect each country's profile and resources, balancing prevention of infection-related cancers with early detection and effective management of common cancers associated with ongoing socioeconomic transitions.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension: a rapidly developing field.
Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection.

METHODS: We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection.

RESULTS: mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P < 0.0001). Integrating microbial abundance with end motif features improved differentiation between clinically significant pathogens and corresponding noise from the same microbes in noninfection samples. For Staphylococcus infections, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the combination model was higher than than that for microbial abundance alone (0.892 vs 0.431, respectively; P = 0.018).

CONCLUSIONS: mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

articles.title: Predictors of high perioperative blood transfusion during isolated CABG using minimally invasive extracorporeal circulation.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The concept of minimally invasive extracorporeal circulation (MiECC) was conceived as a strategy to reduce the effects of hemodilution, inflammation, and blood transfusions during CABG surgery. Despite these technological advancements, perioperative blood transfusion is still common practice. In this research, we sought to determine transfusion needs, the independent factors predicting high transfusion burden, and its clinical effect at an early stage after surgery.

METHODS: In this retrospective study performed at a single center, 144 patients were studied for CABG using MiECC from January 2019 to December 2025. The subjects were divided into a group requiring low transfusion (<3 units of packed red blood cells (RBC); n = 88) and a group requiring high transfusion (⩾3 units of RBC; n = 56). Characteristics were compared between the two groups. Predictors of increased need for transfusion were found using multivariable logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: In total, 109 patients (75.7%) received red blood cell transfusions, of which 56 patients (38.9%) required at least three units. Patients in the high-transfusion group were older, with lower preoperative hemoglobin levels, poor renal function, and presence of chronic kidney disease. Moreover, they also had higher skin-to-skin operative duration. High transfusion was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, increased duration of ICU stay and hospitalization, frequency of re-exploration due to bleeding, and increased in-hospital mortality. Lower preoperative hemoglobin was found to be the most significant independent factor for large transfusion requirements (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54-0.82; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the use of MiECC, perioperative blood transfusion remains common practice. Perioperative anemia, defined by low hemoglobin concentration, was identified as the strongest independent factor for significant transfusion requirement, while chronic kidney disease is another high-risk population. The findings provide support for better management of anemia before surgery and for a broader use of patient blood management programs to reduce transfusion rate and improve perioperative outcomes.

articles.title: A systematic review of albumin and septic shock: It is not a question of if but a question of when.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recently updated sepsis management guidelines no longer exclude albumin from initial fluid resuscitation as understanding of the microvascular pathophysiology differentiating sepsis from septic shock continues to evolve.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether albumin administration compared to crystalloid administration reduces 90-day mortality in adults with septic shock.

RESEARCH PLAN: The Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for systematic reviews was used. PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL were searched from 2014 to 2026 using the terms, "albumin AND fluid resuscitation AND sepsis AND crystalloid."

METHODS: After screening and eligibility assessment, three systematic reviews with meta-analyses were included. Outcomes associated with albumin-based and crystalloid-based resuscitation strategies in patients with sepsis and septic shock were compared.

CONCLUSION: Two of the three meta-analyses demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in 90-day mortality among septic shock patients resuscitated with albumin compared with crystalloid. Hyperoncotic albumin (20% or 25%) may provide additional benefit when administered at an appropriate time during resuscitation. Evidence suggests that early administration of hyperoncotic albumin following an initial 30mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus may improve mortality outcomes in patients with septic shock.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Incorporating measures of microvascular and endothelial changes may help guide the selective use of hyperoncotic 20% albumin following initial crystalloid resuscitation and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: The Inner Ear Enigma: Microvascular Occlusions as a Mechanism for Sudden Audiovestibular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: We present a 52-year-old male with antiphospholipid syndrome who developed acute left-sided sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL), tinnitus, and vertigo during an anticoagulation gap. Bedside head impulse testing (HIT) identified vestibulo-ocular reflex deficits localizing dysfunction to two distinct labyrinthine vascular territories, consistent with bilateral microvascular occlusion. In conjunction with targeted neurological examination, HIT provides a rapid means of localizing peripheral audiovestibular injury and distinguishing it from ischemic central etiologies.

articles.title: Endocardial TIE1 synergizes with TIE2 to regulate the atrial internal muscular network assembly.
articles.abstract: Atrial cardiomyopathy is characterized by altered atrial structures, yet its underlying genetic basis remains inadequately explored. TIE1 mutations are reported in lymphedema patients, but whether they exhibit cardiac defects alongside lymphatic abnormalities remains unknown. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing showed high Tie1 and Tek expression in atrial endocardial cells. TIE1 deficiency severely disrupted atrial morphogenesis, with only minor ventricular defects. Bulk RNA-seq showed reduced transcripts for endothelial development and cardiac trabeculation in Tie1 mutants. Separate RNA-seq analysis of the atria and ventricles further confirmed these findings, revealing a more pronounced downregulation of trabecular genes, including Tek, in the atria upon Tie1 loss. Endothelial deletion of Tek impaired trabeculation, particularly in atria. Consistently, Tie1 loss combined with a single null Tek allele disrupted both atrial and ventricular trabeculation. Strikingly, atrial morphogenesis defects appeared within 48 hr of induced endothelial Tie1 loss coupled with Tek heterozygous deletion, implying a critical endocardial role in organizing the atrial muscular network. The synergy of TIE1 and TIE2 in remodeling atrial trabeculae was confirmed postnatally, whereas TIE1 insufficiency alone had no obvious effect. Together, TIE1 is differentially required for atrial versus ventricular development, acting synergistically with TIE2 to regulate endocardial cell-coordinated assembly of atrial internal muscular network.

articles.title: Recent advances and translational challenges of potassium channel openers in cardiovascular medicine: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of global mortality. Potassium channel openers (PCOs) offer cardioprotective effects through modulation of cellular excitability and mitochondrial function. This narrative review critically evaluates mechanistic and clinical evidence published between 2000 and 2024, focusing on nicorandil and diazoxide in ischemia-reperfusion injury and cardiotoxicity. We examine mitochondrial ATP-sensitive potassium (mitoKATP) and large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BKCa) channels, their roles in mitochondrial energetics and redox homeostasis, and their interplay with inhibition of mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening. Clinical contexts include cardioplegic arrest, myocardial infarction, and chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity. PCOs, particularly nicorandil, combine mitochondrial protection with hemodynamic benefits, with evidence supporting reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events and preservation of mitochondrial integrity. However, routine clinical integration remains constrained by translational gaps, inconsistent electrophysiological effects, and dose-limiting adverse events, including hypotension. Future development should prioritize mitochondrial channel subtype selectivity, particularly targeted mitoKATP and BKCa modulation, alongside well-designed randomized controlled trials to establish clinical efficacy and safety. These advances may strengthen the role of PCOs in cardiovascular medicine while minimizing systemic vascular adverse effects.

articles.title: Residual HCV Transmission among People with HIV: Longitudinal Trends in Prevalence and Incidence of HCV Viremia, and Reinfection After Universal Coverage of Direct-Acting Antivirals in Taiwan (2019-2025).
articles.abstract: AbstractDuring 2017-2025, Taiwan had made substantial progress toward HCV elimination with achievement of 92.6% direct-acting antiviral coverage. In this setting, monitoring the residual transmissions of HCV among high-risk populations become essential. Therefore, we conducted this cohort study to evaluate the temporal trends in HCV infection among people with HIV (PWH). PWH who regularly sought HIV care at the National Taiwan University Hospital were included for periodical HCV antibody screening, and HCV-seropositive PWH underwent HCV RNA testing. PWH who cleared HCV viremia, by treatment or spontaneously, were followed using HCV RNA tests to detect reinfections. The prevalence and incidence of HCV viremia and incidence of reinfection were calculated yearly from 2019-2025. The estimates in 2025 were compared to the peak estimates of the cohort. Overall, 3,637 PWH, with a median age of 40.4 years and 81.4% being men who have sex with men, were included in the study. Compared to 2019, the prevalence of HCV viremia decreased from 4.4% to 0.9% in 2025, representing a 78.7% reduction (95% CI, 66.9%-86.2%); and the incidence decreased from 25.9 to 7.4 per 1,000 person-years in 2025, corresponding to a 70.9% reduction (95% CI, 51.9%-82.4%). Temporal analysis demonstrated significant declines of HCV viremia incidence in 2019-2022, followed by a plateau phase in 2023-2025. Our finding supported that nationwide progress toward HCV elimination has contributed to the significant reduction of HCV burden among PWH; however, the plateau phase indicates potential ongoing, residual HCV transmission among PWH with continued risk behaviors.

articles.title: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy and impaired awareness of hypoglycemia in adults with long-standing type 1 diabetes: results from the Hypoglycemia Awareness Study in Diabetes Type 1.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia (IAH) increases the risk of severe hypoglycemia (SH) and adverse outcomes in peoplewith type 1 diabetes (T1D). Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) has been proposed as a potential contributor to impaired hypoglycemiaperception, but the independence and direction of this relationship remain uncertain. We evaluated the association betweenconfirmed CAN and IAH in adults with long-standing T1D.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This cross-sectional Hypoglycemia Awareness Study in Diabetes Type 1 (HAD-1) included 252 adults with a T1D duration of > 10 years. Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia was defined as a Clarke questionnaire score of ≥ 4.
