Cardiovascular autonomicneuropathy was assessed using standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests; confirmation of CAN required ≥ 2 abnormal heart ratevariability tests. Skin autofluorescence (SAF) was measured as a marker of tissue accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs).

RESULTS: Participants had a median age of 41 years, diabetes duration of 22 years, and HbA1c of 8.1%. Confirmed CAN (definite or severe) was present in 39 participants (15%) and IAH in 48 (19%). Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia was more frequent in individuals withconfirmed CAN than in those without (30.8% vs. 16.9%; p = 0.043). In unadjusted logistic regression, CAN was associated with higherodds of IAH, with an odds ratio (OR) of 2.19 and a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 1.01-4.71. The estimate remained directionally positiveafter adjustment for diabetes duration, sex, and HbA1c, but the CI included the null (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.00-5.90; p = 0.051). After additionaladjustment for lifetime SH, the association was attenuated (OR 1.53, 95% CI 0.57-4.09), whereas SH remained strongly associatedwith IAH (OR 1.27 per additional lifetime episode, 95% CI 1.15-1.41). Firth penalized logistic regression yielded very similar estimates.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy and IAH frequently coexist in adults with long-standing T1D, but these data do not establish an independent or causal effect of CAN on hypoglycemia awareness.

articles.title: Synergistic modulation of cardiac lipid metabolism by Hedan Pill and Shexiang Baoxin Pill through the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α-carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A axis in experimental heart failure.
articles.abstract: Congestive heart failure (CHF) is associated with profound cardiac metabolic remodelling, particularly in lipid utilization. While Hedan Pill and Shexiang Baoxin Pill are traditional Chinese medicines with cardiovascular benefits, their synergistic mechanisms in CHF remain unclear. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were combined with in vivo validation using ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet and subjected to isoproterenol (ISO) treatment. Animals were allocated to seven groups: control, model, Entresto, Hedan Pill, Shexiang Baoxin Pill, Entresto + Hedan Pill, and Entresto + Shexiang Baoxin Pill. Cardiac function, serum lipids, myocardial histopathology, and protein expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα), carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A) and sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c (SREBP-1c) were assessed. Network analysis indicated convergence on the PPARα-lipid metabolism pathway, with strong binding affinities between several active compounds and PPARα (≤ -7.0 kcal mol-1). In vivo, Hedan Pill or ShexiangBaoxin Pill alone improved ejection fraction, reduced triglycerides, and alleviated fibrosis and lipid deposition. Compared with Entresto alone, both combination regimens further reduced serum triglycerides and LDL-C, whereas ejection fraction did not differ significantly. Mechanistically, both agents upregulated myocardial PPARα and CPT1A while suppressing SREBP-1c. Hedan Pill and Shexiang Baoxin Pill synergistically improve cardiac lipid metabolic homeostasis through the PPARα-CPT1A axis, thereby protecting against CHF-induced myocardial injury. These findings provide physiological and mechanistic evidence supporting their translational potential as complementary interventions in CHF.

articles.title: What Hypertension Care in Africa Can Learn from Tuberculosis and HIV.
Birth and long-term health outcomes of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate treatment for heterotopic pregnancy: A retrospective study and focused literature review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report birth outcomes and long-term intellectual and physical development follow-up data of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate (MTX) injection for heterotopic pregnancy (HP), and to summarize relevant published cases.

METHODS: We included 29 patients with HP involving uncommon ectopic implantation sites who underwent transvaginal ultrasound-guided local MTX injection to treat the ectopic gestation (2006-2023). We evaluated birth outcomes and the intellectual and physical development in offspring aged 4-17 years, and conducted a focused review of published cases from 1990 to 2025 via PubMed.

RESULTS: Pregnancy outcomes were available for 27 of 29 patients. Twenty-four women delivered 26 live-born offspring, including 23 without and three with congenital anomalies (congenital heart disease, hypospadias, and multiple craniofacial and limb abnormalities, respectively). Matched comparative analyses included 11 preschool-aged, eight school-aged, and seven adolescent offspring. Across the cognitive, anthropometric, blood pressure, and laboratory outcomes assessed, three between-group differences showed nominal P-values of below 0.05, involving preschool uric acid, school-age systolic blood pressure, and adolescent blood urea nitrogen. Among these, the systolic blood pressure difference was accompanied by high-normal blood pressure or hypertension in some offspring in the MTX group. None of the three differences remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. After the exclusion of overlapping observations, the focused literature review identified 14 independent live-born offspring from previously reported cases, of whom two had congenital anomalies.

CONCLUSION: Most live-born offspring following local MTX treatment for HP had no congenital anomalies, and no long-term offspring outcome comparison remained statistically significant after FDR correction. However, congenital anomalies were reported in both our cohort and the published literature, and the small sample size and limited evidence preclude firm conclusions regarding long-term safety.

articles.title: Patient Selection and Outcomes After Percutaneous Cholecystostomy for High-Risk Acute Cholecystitis: A 10-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous cholecystostomy (PC) is used for acute cholecystitis when immediate cholecystectomy is unsafe. We evaluated selection, treatment response, drain morbidity, subsequent surgery, and survival in a quaternary referral practice.

METHODS: Adults undergoing PC from January 2016 to August 2025 were retrospectively reviewed, with follow-up to September 2026. Analyses assessed operative risk, Tokyo severity, 72-h response, drain outcomes, surgery and mortality, distinguishing planned interval from acute/rescue cholecystectomy.

RESULTS: Eighty-one patients underwent PC over 9.7 years; 56.8% were interhospital transfers. Median age was 74.2 years; 97.5% were American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Grade 3 or higher, 82.7% had American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS NSQIP) predicted mortality ≥ 10%, 72.8% had Tokyo Grade III disease and 51.9% were in septic shock. Clinical improvement within 72 h occurred in 91.4%. Drain complications occurred in 21.0% and recurrent biliary events in 17.3%. Forty patients (49.4%) underwent cholecystectomy: 32 planned interval and eight acute/rescue procedures. Median time to planned interval surgery was 108 days. Lower NSQIP risk and documented bridge-to-surgery intent were independently associated with planned interval cholecystectomy. One-year mortality was 28.8% (23/80); failure to improve within 72 h was associated with 85.7% one-year mortality versus 23.3% after improvement (p = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: PC was used in a highly selected, severely unwell population and usually achieved early improvement, but drain morbidity and competing mortality remained substantial. Approximately two in five patients progressed to planned definitive surgery, supporting selective PC use when index operative risk is prohibitive.

articles.title: Evaluation of Point-of-Care Testing for Creatinine, Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate, and Potassium in a Diverse United Kingdom Population.
articles.journal: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care testing (POCT) for renal function has the potential to enhance access to kidney disease management. However, real-world validation of renal POCT devices in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains limited, particularly in diverse populations.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study to evaluate agreement between 2 renal POCT devices for serum creatinine (SCr), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and potassium. Adults with and without CKD underwent capillary and venous sampling on POCT devices, with comparison to reference laboratory standards. Creatinine was measured using NovaMax Pro and Epoc Blood Analysis System (Epoc); potassium was assessed with Epoc. Agreement was evaluated using correlation coefficients, bias, precision, accuracy, and Bland-Altman analysis. Sensitivity and specificity for detecting CKD (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) were evaluated.

RESULTS: There were 310 participants included; 49% were from ethnic minority groups (29% Black; 14% South Asian). Both POCT devices demonstrated strong correlation with laboratory SCr and eGFR. NovaMax Pro systematically overestimated SCr, particularly at higher concentrations, whereas Epoc showed greater precision and accuracy. No significant differences were observed between capillary and venous samples. eGFR bias was modest for both devices. Sensitivity was higher with NovaMax Pro (94%), while specificity was higher with Epoc (99%). Epoc potassium measurements differed significantly between capillary and venous samples (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Epoc demonstrated superior overall analytical agreement with laboratory SCr and performance for CKD classification, compared with NovaMax Pro. Device-specific biases and potassium variability highlight the importance of sampling technique, clinical context, and intended use when implementing renal POCT.

articles.title: Low-dose oral misoprostol for induction of labour.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Oral misoprostol is a common labour induction method. This review is restricted to lower doses (initially ≤ 50 µg), as higher doses pose unacceptably high risks of uterine hyperstimulation.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of low-dose oral misoprostol for labour induction in women with a viable fetus in the third trimester of pregnancy, compared with other methods of labour induction.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO ICTRP, and checked reference lists of retrieved studies. The search date was April 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised trials comparing low-dose oral misoprostol (≤ 50 µg initial dose) versus placebo, vaginal dinoprostone, vaginal misoprostol, oxytocin or mechanical methods, or comparing oral protocols (20 µg hourly titrated versus 25 µg two-hourly static; 20 µg to 25 µg versus 50 µg or one- to two-hourly versus four- to six-hourly).

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were vaginal birth within 24 hours, caesarean section and uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes.

RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias using RoB 1.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two authors independently screened reports, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. We synthesised results using random-effects meta-analysis, expressing effect estimates as risk ratios (RR) or mean differences (MD) and assessing heterogeneity using I². We evaluated evidence certainty using GRADE.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 44 trials (38 from the previous version, 6 new), involving 11,795 women.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Oral misoprostol versus placebo/no treatment (3 trials, 294 women) Vaginal birth within 24 hours was not reported. Oral misoprostol probably results in little or no difference in caesarean section (RR 0.73, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.48 to 1.11; 3 trials, 294 women; moderate-certainty evidence); its effect on uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes is uncertain (RR 5.15, 95% CI 0.25 to 105.31; 2 trials, 195 women; low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus vaginal dinoprostone (9 trials, 3188 women) Oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours compared with vaginal dinoprostone, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.05; 6 trials, 2492 women; very low-certainty evidence). It may also result in little or no difference in caesarean section (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.04; 9 trials, 3185 women; low-certainty evidence) and in uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.59 to 1.33; 7 trials, 2593 women; low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus vaginal misoprostol (20 trials, 4130 women) Oral misoprostol may result in fewer vaginal births within 24 hours (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.97; 11 trials, 2771 women; low-certainty evidence), may result in little or no difference in caesarean section (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.07; 20 trials, 4128 women; low-certainty evidence) and may result in less uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.95; 16 trials, 3431 women; low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus intravenous oxytocin (4 trials, 426 women) Oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.21; 2 trials, 210 women; very low-certainty evidence), in caesarean section (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.30; 4 trials, 426 women; low-certainty evidence) and in uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.17 to 3.08; 2 trials, 248 women; very low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus mechanical methods (9 trials, 3794 women) Oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 1.41, 95% CI 0.97 to 2.05; 5 trials, 1273 women; very low-certainty evidence), probably reduces caesarean section (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.76 to 0.95; 9 trials, 3746 women; moderate-certainty evidence) and probably increases uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 1.60, 95% CI 1.01 to 2.54; 6 trials, 3275 women; moderate-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol 20 µg hourly titrated versus 25 µg two-hourly static (1 trial, 146 women) Oral misoprostol 20 µg hourly titrated may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours compared with oral misoprostol 25 µg two-hourly static, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.24; 1 trial, 146 women; very low-certainty evidence) and may increase caesarean section (RR 2.83, 95% CI 1.18 to 6.78; 1 trial, 146 women; low-certainty evidence); its effect on uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes is uncertain (RR 3.00, 95% CI 0.12 to 72.45; 1 trial, 146 women; very low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol 20 µg to 25 µg versus 50 µg (1 trial, 64 women) The use of 20 µg to 25 µg versus 50 µg of oral misoprostol may result in little to no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.31 to 1.17; 1 trial, 64 women; very low-certainty evidence) or in caesarean section (RR 1.31, 95% CI 0.77 to 2.22; 1 trial, 64 women; very low-certainty evidence) but the evidence is very uncertain; no cases of uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes were reported. Oral misoprostol one- to two-hourly versus four- to six-hourly (1 trial; 64 women) This comparison is based on the same single trial as the previous comparison, and the findings are therefore identical.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose oral misoprostol has similar effects to other commonly used induction methods across most key outcomes. Certainty of the evidence ranged from very low to moderate, mainly due to imprecision and inconsistency. Compared with placebo, vaginal dinoprostone and intravenous oxytocin, oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours or caesarean section. Compared with vaginal misoprostol, oral misoprostol may reduce uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes, but may also reduce vaginal births within 24 hours. Compared with mechanical methods, oral misoprostol probably reduces caesarean section, although it probably increases uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Registration: Protocol PROSPERO (2018) CRD42018092212 Original review (2021) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD014484.

articles.title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics.
articles.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. We present SVP, a framework that directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and regulatory programs from spatial transcriptomic data. SVP combines location-level functional activity inference with global and local spatial autocorrelation and extends these analyses to bivariate spatial coupling across heterogeneous features. Across simulations and real datasets, SVP recovered cell-state-associated activity patterns at individual captured locations, detected spatially variable features with calibrated statistics, and scaled efficiently to large datasets. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, SVP identified a spatially co-organized hypoxic and extracellular-matrix-remodeling niche that co-localized with regions of low immune activity. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque-associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. SVP enables direct analysis of functional spatial organization, moving beyond gene-centric descriptions of tissue structure.

articles.title: A fuzzy set approach to assessing catastrophic health spending: an application to data from Nigeria.
articles.abstract: Catastrophic health spending (CHS) is conventionally assessed as a crisp set, in which a household either incurs CHS or does not. Arguably, this does not reflect reality, particularly because households often cannot determine with certainty when they transition to financial catastrophe. This paper argues that this transition is gradual and can be modelled as a fuzzy rather than a crisp set. This paper develops a fuzzy set approach to assess CHS, using a fuzzy membership function and introducing novel statistics, including closeness and vulnerability to CHS. Under the fuzzy set approach, CHS headcount adds the conventional headcount to the novel headcount of vulnerability to CHS. Data come from Nigeria, where out-of-pocket health spending is the predominant form of health expenditure. At the 10% budget share threshold, Nigeria's CHS headcount increased from 20% under the conventional approach to 42% under the fuzzy set approach, with the CHS vulnerability headcount exceeding that under the traditional approach. Focusing solely on out-of-pocket health spending, as is traditionally done in assessing CHS, the fuzzy set approach highlights the significant burden households face, which is often overlooked by conventional methods, and this is a pertinent issue for health financing policy.

articles.title: Persistence revisited: Partitioning rather than media-specific reactivity dominates persistence in the environment.
articles.abstract: Current regulation identifies environmentally persistent chemicals often using thresholds defined for single-media half-lives. This approach ignores the large and even dominating impact of multimedia partitioning on the (bio)availability of compounds that undergo degradation, and accordingly may underestimate the chemical lifetimes by orders of magnitude. This is demonstrated through comparing chemical half-lives in water with overall persistence (Pov) in terms of environmental lifetimes calculated through a steady-state multimedia mass-balance model. While Pov depends on the entrance compartment, Stroebe's τE, the temporal-remote-state expected environmental lifetime, is less sensitive to the initial entry compartment. Thus, τE appears most suited for the prediction of chemical persistence. In this study, a stepwise Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analysis showed that only four chemical properties, log values of Kow (hydrophobicity), kdeg,w and kdeg,a (degradation rate constants in water and air, respectively), and Pv (vapour pressure), are sufficient to estimate τE. But this analysis also showed non-linear error patterns despite overall good statistics, unraveling peculiarities of the non-linear log-log dependence of τE on compound properties. A machine-learning k nearest neighbors (kNN) regression model operating in the property space yields even more accurate and linear results. Application to existing data sets demonstrates the usefulness of this approach. In particular, it shows that the reduction of bioavailability due to multimedia partitioning may cause compounds classified as "readily biodegradable" to be identified as persistent when they have sufficiently high hydrophobicity (e.g. phenanthrene with log Kow = 4.5: lifetime > 30 years). The developed tools (SimpleRisk4REACH enabling τE calculation through Stroebe's mathematical procedure; kNN regression model for τE prediction) are made available to the public.

articles.title: Synergistic electro-mechanical stimulation promotes neural stem cell differentiation in a 3D conductive and stretchable hydrogel.
articles.abstract: The limited understanding of how to physically manipulate neural stem cell (NSC) differentiation into mature neurons and functional glial cells in a three-dimensional (3D) environment has constrained the potential of NSC-based therapies for neurodegenerative diseases. In this study, we develop gelatin-methacryloyl (GelMA) and polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA)-based conductive hydrogels to investigate the effects of electrical stimulation (ES) and mechanical stretching on neuronal differentiation in a 3D matrix. GelMA and PEGDA provide extracellular matrix (ECM)-like biological and physical characteristics, enabling the study of neural differentiation, development, and electrophysiology. Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) was incorporated into the GelMA/PEGDA matrix as a conductive additive to enhance hydrogel conductivity. Compared with non-conductive hydrogels, conductive hydrogels alone promoted neuronal differentiation, while conductive hydrogels combined with ES further enhanced neural differentiation, neurite extension, and neural gene expression. Mechanical stretching similarly induced neuronal differentiation and directional neurite alignment. Notably, co-stimulation with stretching and ES exerted synergistic effects, significantly promoting neurite outgrowth (2.5-fold compared to the unstimulated hydrogel control (GelMA-PEGDA)), increasing filopodia density by 15%, and enhancing neurite branching by 3%. Co-stimulation also upregulated neuronal differentiation marker expression, including for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neuron-specific class III β-tubulin (Tuj-1), and microtubule-associated protein 2 (MAP2), and increased the neuronal electrical activity of encapsulated cells. Overall, this study advances the understanding of directed NSC differentiation within a 3D microenvironment using defined physical cues and provides a theoretical basis for improving the effectiveness and feasibility of NSC-based therapies.

articles.title: A Comparison of the Global and Berlin Definitions of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The Global definition of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) expands Berlin criteria to include SpO2:FiO2 ratios, High-Flow Nasal Cannula (HFNC), lung ultrasound, and non-intubated patients outside the critical care setting. We aimed to characterize the prevalence, progression, and outcomes of ARDS as defined by the Global and Berlin definitions.

METHODS: We included adult patients admitted to multiple hospitals within a single health system between December 1, 2021 and May 31, 2022 who met criteria for ARDS according to either the Global or Berlin definition within the first 7 days of hospitalization. Chest imaging was reviewed independently by two investigators for new bilateral opacities not attributable to atelectasis, effusion, mass, or heart failure.

RESULTS: Among 3,342 admissions screened for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure (AHRF), 1,220 (36.5%) met Global ARDS criteria, of whom 535 (43.9%) met Berlin criteria at some point during hospitalization. Of these 535, 381 (71.2%) met both definitions simultaneously, and 154 (28.8%) initially met only Global criteria before subsequently meeting Berlin criteria, a median of 1 day later (IQR 1-3). The remaining 685 (56.1%) met Global criteria only and never progressed to Berlin ARDS. Patients meeting Berlin criteria at any time had higher mortality than those who never met Berlin criteria (37.8% vs. 26.7%, p < 0.001). Among the 246 HFNC-managed patients who never progressed to Berlin criteria, 84 (34.1%) died, with care-limitation directives (do-not-intubate [DNI] and/or do-not-resuscitate [DNR]) present in 103 (41.9%) and accounting for 64 (76.2%) of deaths in this group.

CONCLUSIONS: As compared to the Berlin definition of ARDS, the Global ARDS definition captures more patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure as having ARDS. Of those initially meeting only Global criteria, only a fraction progress to meet the Berlin definition. Patients meeting only the Global definition of ARDS without progression to the Berlin definition have a high mortality rate; however, much of this mortality occurs in the context of care-limitation directives related to tracheal intubation.

Timing influences detection of anti-nephrin antibodies in recurrent FSGS.
Chemogenetics reveals a surprising role for GPR18 signaling in immunometabolic regulation of β cell activity.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic islet macrophages are important immunometabolic regulators of β cell function, particularly in obesity-associated type 2 diabetes. Previous studies have established that pancreatic islet macrophages communicate with β cells through either the release of cytokines and growth factors, or direct cell-cell contact. In this issue of the JCI, Singh et al. used chemogenetics to identify a Gq/AMPK pathway that remodels sphingolipid metabolism. This pathway links macrophages to β cells through a CD36-dependent mechanism that reduces insulin secretion. Surprisingly, the orphan GPCR GPR18 was identified as the receptor that engages this pathway. These findings expand our understanding in macrophage-β cell communication and identify GPR18 as a potential therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Mucosal vaccination with hemagglutinin stalk provides broad protection against influenza virus subtypes in mice.
articles.abstract: Influenza viruses continually evolve through antigenic drift and shift, spreading via respiratory droplets and aerosols. Developing a universal nasal vaccine is essential for preventing seasonal and pandemic infections by inducing long-lasting immunity in the respiratory tract. The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) transfers IgG Abs across the epithelial barrier. This study investigates whether the i.n. delivery of the conserved Stalk antigen of HA, utilizing the FcRn, can stimulate protective immune responses against various influenza virus subtypes. We engineered a monomeric IgG Fc fused to a modified HA Stalk in its prefusion form. Mice i.n. immunized with Stalk-Fc exhibited significant protection against infections from H1N1, H5N1, H6N2, and H9N2 compared with groups of control mice. The immunized mice produced long-lasting HA Stalk-specific IgA and IgG Abs in nasal washes, bronchoalveolar lavage, and blood, along with tissue-resident memory T cells in the lungs and long-lived plasma cells in the bone marrow. This led to notably lower viral replication in the nasal turbinate and lungs. The Stalk-specific Abs demonstrated strong cross-reactivity against different influenza subtypes through neutralization, Ab- or complement-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, or phagocytosis. These results indicate that FcRn efficiently transports HA Stalk-Fc across the respiratory epithelial barrier, supporting the development of a universal influenza nasal vaccine.

articles.title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m³C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models.
articles.abstract: T follicular helper (TFH) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling TFH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m³C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of TFH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13hi TFH cells, and its deficiency impaired TFH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m³C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key TFH-associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra. Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed TFH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during TFH differentiation and suggest that modulation of this pathway may provide a strategy to tune TFH-driven immune responses.

articles.title: Association of Inflammatory and Nutritional Indices With No-Reflow in Elderly Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI.
articles.abstract: No-reflow remains an important complication after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), particularly in elderly patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). We evaluated the association of inflammatory and nutritional indices with angiographic no-reflow in 491 patients aged ≥65 years. No-reflow occurred in 55 patients (11.2%), whereas 436 (88.8%) had normal epicardial coronary flow, corresponding to an approximate group-size ratio of 1:7.9. Patients with no-reflow had higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and systemic inflammation response index and lower prognostic nutritional index (PNI). However, after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, left ventricular ejection fraction, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) presentation, continuous NLR and lower PNI were no longer independently associated with no-reflow. STEMI presentation remained strongly associated with no-reflow. NLR ≥4.31 remained associated with higher odds of no-reflow in the cutoff-based adjusted analysis, whereas PNI ≤46.28 did not. Bootstrap internal validation showed only small improvements in optimism-corrected discrimination when NLR or PNI was added to the clinical model. These findings support an association between inflammatory/nutritional markers and no-reflow but emphasize the dominant influence of ACS presentation and the need for external validation.

articles.title: Open reduction of the femoral butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures is associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union: a retrospective clinical cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether the presence of and/or open reduction of a butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures was associated with reoperation to promote union.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort.

SETTING: Single Level I Trauma Center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Included were patients who underwent surgical fixation of an acute OTA/AO 32A-C femoral shaft fracture between January 2017 and January 2024. Patients younger than 18 years, nonunion surgeries, <3 months follow-up, periprosthetic fractures, and open fractures were excluded.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Patient demographics were retrospectively collected. A butterfly fragment was defined as a singular, wedge-shaped segment of comminution from the diaphysis of the femur. Groups were stratified based on the presence or absence of a butterfly fragment. The primary outcome was reoperation to promote union. Secondary outcomes included fracture-related infection (FRI) and presence of post-operative cortical step sign (CSS). Comparisons of primary and secondary outcomes were made between patients with and without a femoral butterfly fragment. A subgroup analysis was performed within the butterfly fragment group comparing open versus closed reduction of the butterfly fragment.

RESULTS: 139 patients were included: 99 (71.2%) without a butterfly fragment (mean age 38.5years, range 18-92years; 62.6% male) and 40 (28.8%) with a butterfly fragment (mean age 35.5years, range 18-96years; 75.0% male). 10 (10.1%) patients without a butterfly fragment and 8 (20.0%) patients with a butterfly fragment underwent reoperation to promote union (p=0.2). Of the 40 patients with a butterfly fragment, 9 (22.5%) had open reduction of the butterfly fragment with cable fixation and 31 (77.5%) did not. The mean proximal and distal displacement of the butterfly fragment did not differ significantly between those managed with open versus closed reduction (38.8mm vs 35.4mm and 20.3mm vs 18.9mm, respectively, p>0.05). Open reduction to the butterfly fragment compared to closed reduction was associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union (66.7% vs 6.5%, p<0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Open reduction of the butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures was associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union compared to closed reduction. These findings emphasize biologic preservation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Perianal cutaneous amoebiasis: An unsuspected extra-intestinal manifestation of Entamoeba histolytica.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous amoebiasis is an uncommon extra-intestinal manifestation of Entamoeba histolytica infection and is easily overlooked when gastrointestinal symptoms are absent. Cutaneous involvement is particularly uncommon, mostly affecting the perianal or genital region. The importance of histopathological recognition of E. histolytica trophozoites in chronic perianal ulcers that clinically mimic other infectious or malignant conditions is stressed.

articles.title: Peripheral neurological complications associated with dengue virus infection: A retrospective case series.
articles.abstract: Neurological complications of dengue remain incompletely characterized. We retrospectively describe adults evaluated at a tertiary neurological referral centre during Argentina's 2023-2024 outbreak with peripheral neurological syndromes temporally associated with laboratory-supported or clinically suspected dengue.

articles.title: Microenvironment Matters: Venue Setting, Listener Position, and Hearing Symptoms at Live Music Events.
articles.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Exposure to loud music events increases risk of noise-induced hearing loss and tinnitus. This study examined how micro-environmental factors, setting and crowd position, relate to HP use, symptoms, and perceived efficacy.

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional survey of online music community participants' demographics and attendance characteristics (n = 2352).

METHODS: Group differences were assessed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, and Pearson's chi-square. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess factors associated with post-event hearing symptoms.

RESULTS: Respondents reported attending indoor music venues more frequently than outdoor (52.8% vs 47.2%); tinnitus was more common after indoor events (51.4% vs 37.2%, P < .001). Difficulty hearing others was more frequent after outdoor events (32.3% vs 24.3%, P = .011). Compared to the rear position, front-crowd position increased ear pain (15.0% vs 10.2%, P = .050) and required others to repeat themselves (37.0% vs 30.4%, P = .047). Front-standing attendees reported lower concern about hearing effects (5-point Likert mean = 2.51 vs 2.68; P < .001) and lower perceived HP effectiveness (2.84 vs 3.00; P = .001). Lower odds of tinnitus were associated with outdoor venues (OR = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.44-0.98) and HP use (OR = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.46-0.94). Attending events for ≥3 hours was associated with higher odds of difficulty hearing others (OR = 4.06, 95% CI = 1.62-10.22), and attending >20 events annually was associated with increased odds of ear pain (OR = 8.42, 95% CI = 2.11-33.57). Standing position was not independently associated with symptoms.

CONCLUSION: Music venue type and listener position are important determinants of post-event hearing symptoms, suggesting that targeted, environment-specific hearing conservation counseling and preventive strategies could be given to patients attending music events.

articles.title: Transulnar Access With Ipsilateral Radial Artery Occlusion for Percutaneous Coronary Procedures: Results From the ULNAR RAO Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the safety of transulnar artery access (TUA) in patients with ipsilateral radial artery occlusion (RAO).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between March 2011 and December 2021, 1756 consecutive patients with RAO underwent percutaneous angiographic procedures via ipsilateral TUA in a high-volume radialist center. All patients were assessed for procedural safety. A more detailed analysis was performed on the last 103 consecutive patients with anatomical, functional, and pain assessment of the punctured arm, at baseline and up to 1 year of follow-up. Functional assessment was performed using a hydraulic hand dynamometer for hand strength and self-assessment with the QUICK-DASH questionnaire. A visual analog scale was used for pain assessment. Ulnar artery (UA) patency was evaluated clinically and by duplex ultrasound. UA diameter was measured using quantitative angiography and compared with previous forearm angiograms obtained before documentation of RAO.

RESULTS: All 1756 TUA procedures were performed without clinical or ischemic hand complications, with a median follow-up of 83 months [IQR 56-108]. In the more intensively evaluated group of 103 patients (mean age 62.9 ± 9.0 years, 30% females), primary puncture success was 96.1%, with 3.9% requiring crossover to left radial access. Dynamometer assessment found a numerically small, transient reduction in grip strength, observed 12-24 h after procedure (72.6 ± 23.0 before vs.71.9 ± 23.0 lbs post-procedure), with subsequent recovery. QUICK-DASH scores remained unchanged during follow-up. No UA occlusion was detected. UA diameter increased following RAO by 0.28 ± 0.35 mm (p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: Ipsilateral TUA in patients with RAO is safe and successful when performed at experienced radial centers.

articles.title: Incidence and predictors of hypertensive heart disease among hypertensive patients: A retrospective cohort study in South Gondar Zone Hospitals, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive heart disease, including left ventricular hypertrophy and heart failure, is a neglected chronic disease in sub-Saharan Africa, causes a significant increase in morbidity and premature mortality. Despite this problem, studies on early development, incidence, and potential biochemical and behavioural predictors in Ethiopia, particularly in the study area, are scarce.

METHODS: An institution-based retrospective cohort study was conducted on 531 hypertensive patients in selected South Gondar Zone hospitals in Ethiopia from September 2019 to June 2024. Data were collected using a structured checklist-based chart review. EPI data version 4.2 for data entry and STAT version 17 for analysis were used. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests, as well as Cox proportional hazard regression models, were used for survival data analysis.

RESULT: The incidence rate of hypertensive heart disease was 14.93 (95% CI: 12.94-17.23) per 1000 person-months of observation. The median survival time for the development of hypertensive heart disease was 18 months (IQR, 12-24 months). Older age group (≥60 years) (AHR = 1.82, 95%CI:1.12,2.97), obesity (AHR = 1.90,95%CI:1.29,2.79), low HDL (AHR = 1.78, 95%CI:1.21,2.64), and high non-HDL cholesterol level (AHR = 2.22,95%CI:1.51,3.25) were significant predictors of early development of hypertensive heart disease as compared to their counterparts.

CONCLUSION: Hypertensive patients in this setting had a high incidence rate and short survival time to develop hypertensive heart disease. In this study, existence of hypertensive heart disease as a common and rapidly progressing complication of hypertension was confirmed and the prognosis was poor. Routine screening for early cardiac remodelling in older patients, integration of weight management into hypertension care, and attention to lipid abnormalities should be considered as part of serious public health response, though causal conclusions require further prospective research.

articles.title: Prognostic Predictors in Patients With Necrotizing Otitis Externa: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Necrotizing otitis externa (NOE) is a rare infection with a heterogeneous clinical course that complicates prognostication. The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes remains controversial, and objective predictors of treatment duration are unclear. This study aimed to identify the factors associated with prolonged hospitalization in patients with NOE.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

SETTING: Tertiary academic medical center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 61 patients with NOE admitted between September 2009 and October 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and radiological data, as well as length of hospital stay, were analyzed. Magnetic resonance imaging assessed skull-base osteomyelitis and white matter lesions using the Fazekas scale. Multivariable linear regression identified factors associated with hospital stay.

RESULTS: The mean age was 70.25 ± 13.11 years (63.9% male; mean hospital stay 46.02 ± 37.50 days). Diabetes was present in 75.4% of the patients, but neither diabetes nor hemoglobin A1c levels were associated with hospital stay. In the univariate analysis, diabetic complications, external auditory canal swelling, cranial nerve palsy, peak inflammatory marker levels, inflammatory marker normalization times, and higher Fazekas scores were associated with prolonged hospitalization, whereas only diabetic complications and higher Fazekas scores remained independently associated in the multivariable analysis (adjusted R2 = 0.425).

CONCLUSION: Diabetic complications and higher Fazekas scores were independently associated with prolonged hospitalization in patients with NOE. These findings suggest that chronic microvascular disease burden, rather than conventional vascular risk factors alone, may contribute to a prolonged disease course. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: 18F-FDG PET/MR Findings in Sturge-Weber Syndrome During Presurgical Evaluation of Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
articles.abstract: 18F-FDG PET/MR demonstrated extensive right cerebral cortical hypometabolism in a 52-year-old man with Sturge-Weber syndrome undergoing presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy. Clinical photographs showed capillary malformations involving the face and both hands. CT revealed prominent right hemispheric gyriform calcifications, while integrated 18F-FDG PET/MR demonstrated ipsilateral cerebral atrophy and reduced cortical uptake in the frontoparietal and temporal lobes. These images illustrate the complementary roles of CT and 18F-FDG PET/MR in characterizing structural abnormalities and regional metabolic impairment in longstanding Sturge-Weber syndrome.

articles.title: Initial Experience with Bachmann Bundle Pacing Lead Implantation as a Rhythm Control Strategy in Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) is challenging during atrial fibrillation (AF) because ECG based endpoints cannot confirm lead positioning. We aimed to demonstrate the feasibility of a practical approach to BBP implantation during AF and propose a framework for comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) for rhythm control in patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Twenty-four consecutive patients with persistent or longstanding persistent AF and preserved ejection fraction underwent dual-chamber BBP and LBBP implantation with individually optimized pacing rate and AV interval. Twelve underwent BBP during AF (Group 1) and 12 during sinus (Group 2), including six cardioverted intraprocedurally. During AF, lead positioning was guided by anatomical landmarks, local electrograms, current of injury, and impedance changes. After sinus rhythm restoration, BBP was confirmed in 11/12 Group 1 patients. Reductions in P-wave duration and interatrial block were observed in both groups. Seventeen had been referred for pace-and-ablate therapy; three in Group 1 reverted spontaneously to sinus rhythm before cardioversion. Over a median 192 [139-212] days after sinus restoration, 12/17 maintained sinus rhythm; 2 underwent AV node ablation, 1 AF ablation, 1 repeat cardioversion, and 1 required rate-control medication for paroxysmal AF. No complications occurred.

CONCLUSION: BBP implantation during AF is feasible using anatomical and electrophysiological markers, with Bachmann bundle capture confirmed after sinus rhythm restoration. Exploratory findings suggest that comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and LBBP may support a rhythm-control (pace-and-wait) strategy in persistent AF patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

articles.title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma: Results from the China Pulmonary Health study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a common comorbidity of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. However, limited information is available on GERD among community-sourced patients with COPD and asthma in China. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of GERD and its association with respiratory symptoms and airway reversibility in these patients from the general population.

METHODS: The China Pulmonary Health (CPH) study, a national cross-sectional survey, enrolled 57,779 adults aged ≥20 years from June 2012 to May 2015. Participants completed standard questionnaires and underwent pulmonary function tests. GERD was defined using the Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Questionnaire (GerdQ). Airway reversibility was assessed via post-bronchodilator pulmonary function changes. Multivariate regressions examined the association of GERD with respiratory symptoms and airway reversibility.

RESULTS: In total, 47,226 participants were included in the final analysis. The prevalence of GERD was 6.62% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.89-7.34%) in patients with COPD, and 13.73% (95% CI: 12.19-15.27%) and 12.38% (95% CI: 9.84-14.93%) in patients with asthma and asthma with airflow limitation, respectively. GERD was associated with nasal symptoms, cough, sputum, wheezing, and dyspnea in patients with COPD. GERD was also associated with nasal symptoms and dyspnea in patients with asthma. After adjusting for confounders, the asthma group with GERD had smaller postbronchodilator changes in forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) compared with those without GERD (B = -0.030, 95% CI: -0.055 to -0.005, P = 0.018), and the association remained after further adjusting for respiratory symptoms (B = -0.033, 95% CI: -0.058 to -0.008, P = 0.009). But postbronchodilator changes in FEV1 or forced vital capacity (FVC) did not differ between COPD patients with and without GERD.

CONCLUSIONS: GERD is prevalent and significantly associated with respiratory symptoms in patients with COPD and asthma. In patients with asthma, those with GERD had worse airway reversibility.

articles.title: Oral-gut-vaginal microbiota crosstalk with host immunity and metabolism in pregnancy disorders.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy represents a critical stage in which both maternal and fetal health are of paramount importance. This review systematically examines the temporal dynamics of maternal microbial communities across multiple anatomical niches-including the vaginal, intestinal, and oral ecosystems-during pregnancy, and explores their profound connections with gestational health. We highlight the specific associations between site-specific microbial dysbiosis and adverse outcomes such as preterm birth, gestational diabetes, and preeclampsia. In addition, we delineate the mechanisms by which the immune microenvironment at the maternal-fetal interface maintains dynamic equilibrium under microbial regulation, and underscores the role of microbial metabolites as transgenerational signaling molecules critical for fetal development. Furthermore, we dissect the pathological disruption of the "microbiota-immune-metabolism" network in pregnancy-related disorders and evaluate the potential of targeted strategies-including probiotic supplementation and nutritional interventions-to restore microbial homeostasis and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. Finally, we emphasize the contribution of breast milk microbiota and immune components to offspring immune programming and outline future translational research directions, aiming to provide a scientific foundation for microbiota-based monitoring and early intervention in pregnancy health.

articles.title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Acute Cardiac Care and General Cardiology Science Committee of the Council on Clinical Cardiology; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Cardiovascular Radiology and Intervention; Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young; Council on Peripheral Vascular Disease; and Council on Quality of Care and Outcomes Research
articles.abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

articles.title: Myocardial Work Analysis: A Novel Echocardiographic Approach for Early Detection of Myocardial Fibrosis in Pediatric Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy With Preserved LVEF-A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While myocardial work (MW) indices have shown diagnostic and prognostic value in various cardiovascular diseases, their role in detecting myocardial fibrosis in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains unexplored. This prospective study investigates MW's potential for early identification of fibrosis in pediatric DMD patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.

METHODS: In this large prospective cohort, we enrolled 242 genetically confirmed DMD males (aged 6-18 years) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% by cardiac magnetic resonance and 54 age-matched controls. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment included global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work, and global work efficiency analysis. Myocardial fibrosis was assessed via late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline at 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: Patients with DMD demonstrated significantly impaired MW indices versus controls (global work index, 1371.4±225.84 versus 1598.04±207.01 mm Hg%; global work efficiency, median 94.67% [Q1-Q3, 93.00-96.00] versus 95.33% [94.30-96.33]; global constructive work, 1630.34±246.37 versus 1900.22±195.84 mm Hg%; global wasted work, median 67.67 [Q1-Q3, 50.17-86.25] versus 59.00 [48.00-73.00] mm Hg%; all P<0.01). Notably, MW abnormalities preceded global longitudinal strain reduction, with significant differences even in patients with DMD with normal global longitudinal strain (≥18%). Global work efficiency showed moderate diagnostic accuracy for baseline late gadolinium enhancement (area under the curve, 0.618) and was associated with subsequent late gadolinium enhancement development in exploratory longitudinal analysis (area under the curve, 0.798; cutoff of 95.85%), providing complementary information beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters.

CONCLUSIONS: This large-scale prospective study suggests that MW analysis, particularly global work efficiency, might be useful for early detection of cardiac dysfunction and might be associated with short-term fibrosis in patients with DMD and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. However, given the limited number of progression events, this finding should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Phenotypic Integration at a Small Geographic Scale: Parallel Shifts in Morphology, Signaling, Behavior, and Hormones in the Italian Wall Lizard.
articles.abstract: Selection often acts on trait integration across multiple organizational levels, producing parallel shifts in suites of traits that determine performance. Understanding how selective pressures generate these coordinated shifts over fine geographic scales is central to evolutionary and functional ecology. Using mainland and islet populations of the Italian wall lizard under similar macroclimatic conditions, we tested whether divergence in body size, color signaling, and melanism parallels shifts in intraspecific aggression, sociability, and baseline and stress-induced steroid hormone levels. Mainland lizards were larger and exhibited stronger sexual dimorphism, with males possessing higher body condition than islet males. Lateral head coloration was prevalent and conspicuous on the mainland, while islet lizards showed higher melanism on head and flank and more blue ocelli on flank scales. These characteristics matched behavior: islet males showed social indifference and no aggression, while mainland males exhibited aggression and showed stronger attraction to conspecifics. Endocrine profiles paralleled these shifts: mainland males had higher baseline testosterone, whereas islet males had higher baseline corticosterone. Stress-induced levels of either hormone did not differ between populations. These shifts indicate divergence in an integrated functional phenotype, consistent with alternative strategies along an axis of competitive investment: a mainland "proactive territorial strategy" (large size, conspicuous head coloration, aggression, and high baseline testosterone) versus an islet "tolerance strategy" (smaller size, increased melanism and blue ocelli, reduced aggression, and high baseline corticosterone). By combining behavioral ecology, endocrinology, and functional morphology, we provide a comprehensive, mechanistic framework for understanding phenotypic divergence at small geographical scale.

articles.title: A smartphone-assisted immunosandwich sensor based on molecularly imprinted polymers and nanozymes for point-of-care testing of urinary microalbumin.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) poses a severe threat to human life and health. Early diagnosis facilitates timely treatment, delays disease progression, and reduces the risk of end-stage renal disease. Currently, urinary microalbumin (umALB) is a clinical biomarker for CKD, commonly detected via Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA). However, this method is limited by the difficult antibody preparation, enzyme instability, and the requirement for specialized personnel and bulky equipment. Thus, there is an urgent demand for an antibody-free and enzyme-free point-of-care testing (POCT) method for umALB. Herein, a glycated epitope template was designed based on the C-terminal nonapeptide of umALB, and epitope-imprinted microplates (Microplate@EIP) were fabricated via boronate affinity-anchored epitope controllable oriented surface imprinting for specific extraction. Subsequently, aldehyde-modified Fe3O4 nanozymes (Fe3O4 MNPs@CHO) with high peroxidase-like activity were synthesized to label the captured umALB, catalyzing the H2O2-mediated oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB). A smartphone-assisted immunosandwich sensor was then established. This method eliminates the need for antibodies and biological enzymes, exhibiting high specificity, superior sensitivity, and remarkable stability. Moreover, it obviates the need for specialized personnel or bulky equipment, enabling preliminary POCT under controlled conditions with only a smartphone. The developed sensor provides a rapid, low-cost, and user-friendly methodological platform for umALB detection, demonstrating promising application potential for CKD preliminary screening after further large-scale clinical validation.

articles.title: Early Left Bundle Branch Pacing for Complete Left Bundle Branch Block and Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction of 36%-50%: The EARLY-RESYNC Randomized Trial.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare the effects of early resynchronization with left bundle branch pacing (early-LBBP) versus guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) alone on cardiac function in patients with complete left bundle branch block (CLBBB) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 36%-50%.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective, randomized, multicenter trial, 37 patients (mean age 60.5 ± 12.3 years, male 40.5%, LVEF 42.6% ± 6.0%) were assigned to early-LBBP plus GDMT (n=19) or GDMT alone (n=18). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in the change of LVEF from baseline to 6 months. Secondary endpoints included changes in echocardiographic parameters and clinical outcomes. Analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle. At 6-month follow-up, the adjusted mean improvement in LVEF was greater in the early-LBBP group than in the GDMT group (mean difference: 7.4%, 95% CI: 1.9 to 12.9%; P =0.013), with consistent findings in the per-protocol analysis. Early-LBBP was also associated with a greater reduction in LV end-systolic volume (-23.6mL; 95% CI: -42.3 to -4.8ml) and a higher rate of final LVEF ≥50% (78.9% vs. 38.9%) at 6 months compared with GDMT alone.

CONCLUSION: In patients with CLBBB and LVEF 36%-50%, LBBP combined with GDMT resulted in greater improvement in LVEF at 6 months than GDMT alone. Larger randomized trials are needed to establish its long-term clinical benefits and optimal timing.

articles.title: First bite syndrome in neurologic practice: A narrative review of a distinct paroxysmal craniofacial pain syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the etiopathogenesis, clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment of first bite syndrome.

BACKGROUND: Though well described by the Otolaryngology and Maxillofacial surgical specialties, first bite syndrome is rarely discussed in Neurology literature. Headache specialists may see these patients as a referral for trigeminal neuralgia or undiagnosed paroxysmal facial pain.

METHODS: Relevant literature was identified through searches of major medical databases from their inception until May 29, 2026. After removing duplicates and excluded abstracts (e.g., incorrect subject matter, non-English, abstract only) and adding additional articles identified from references of reviewed articles, 163 unique articles on first bite syndrome were further analyzed for information on etiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, or treatment.

RESULTS: First bite syndrome typically presents with unilateral paroxysmal facial pain along the parotid and mandibular region, triggered by salivation. The pain is worsened by strong sialagogues such as acidic or sour foods and tends to improve after the first few bites of a meal. It may be aching/cramping or sharp, shock-like pain along the jaw or mandible, and can be mistaken for trigeminal neuralgia or temporomandibular disease. First bite syndrome can be seen following surgery in the parotid, parapharyngeal, or neck region, as well as with salivary gland tumors or other neoplasms in the parapharyngeal space. Individuals with first bite syndrome may experience gradual improvement with time, and a smaller number may experience complete resolution of symptoms. For those who do not improve, or for those with severe pain, neuropathic medications or botulinum toxin administration may be beneficial.

CONCLUSIONS: First bite syndrome is underrecognized in clinical practice. Clinicians should be familiar with its clinical presentation and maintain a high index of suspicion when patients present with facial pain associated with salivation. Differentiation of first bite syndrome from other causes of facial pain is important to guide evaluation and therapy, and to help avoid unnecessary medications and procedures.

articles.title: Comparative performance of three HPV DNA detection assays for cervical cancer screening in Algeria.
articles.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal etiological driver of cervical cancer, making accurate HPV detection central to contemporary screening strategies. This study compared three molecular assays-INNO-LiPA HPV Genotyping Extra, Cobas 4800 HPV, and Amplicor HPV-using overlapping cervical-sample subsets from Algerian women at increased risk of cervical disease. Among the 94 specimens tested by both INNO-LiPA and Cobas, HR-HPV was detected in 54.3% and 29.8%, respectively; INNO-LiPA also identified HPV16 and HPV18 more frequently. In the 18-specimen subset tested by all three assays, HR-HPV positivity was 27.8% with INNO-LiPA, 33.3% with Cobas, and 50.0% with Amplicor. Pairwise agreement ranged from weak to substantial (κ=0.116-0.667), and discordance was significantly associated with multiple HPV infections (OR=5.88, 95% CI 1.29-26.85; p=0.012). HR-HPV positivity was more frequent in specimens with abnormal cytology, with the strongest association observed for INNO-LiPA (OR=4.9, 95% CI 1.5-15.9; p=0.005). Using the study-defined composite reference classification, INNO-LiPA showed higher sensitivity (93%) but lower specificity (62%) than Cobas (71% and 88%, respectively). These findings demonstrate substantial assay-dependent variation in HR-HPV detection and highlight the value of detailed genotyping for epidemiological investigation, while supporting the use of clinically validated HR-HPV assays for screening applications.

articles.title: Lateral Flow Immunoassay Technology for Blood-Based Infection and Sepsis-Related Biomarker Detection: Trends, Analytical Performance, and Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: The assessment of infection and sepsis remains challenging because microbiological methods are time-consuming and host-response biomarkers are not sufficiently specific across clinical settings. With its turnaround time, low sample volume, portability and ability to use whole blood, serum and plasma, lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) provides a viable approach for decentralized measurement. This review examines LFIA platforms for procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, serum amyloid A, interleukin-6, pathogen antigens and multiplex panels. Special focus is placed on colorimetric, time-resolved fluorescence, quantum-dot, chemiluminescent, Raman, electrochemical, and smartphone-based readouts. The performance characteristics are evaluated with respect to analytical parameters, including detection and quantification limits, precision, calibration, and agreement with reference methods. The limitations due to hematocrit, viscosity, anticoagulants, hemolysis, and incomplete plasma separation are considered. There are platforms that demonstrate analytical sensitivity and show agreement with immunoassay platforms, but studies rely on spiked samples, single-centre cohorts, or nontransferable cutoff values. While multiplex formats may enhance biomarker discrimination, they do not resolve differences in concentration ranges or calibration complexity. Clinical translation is dependent on validation using native whole-blood samples, readouts, lot-to-lot quality control, decision thresholds, prospective studies in multiple centers and evidence that LFIA-based testing enhances antimicrobial stewardship and patient care across intensive-care settings.

articles.title: Prediction of coronary artery disease from non-invasive test reports and demographic characteristics using calibrated ensemble learning.
articles.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is commonly confirmed using invasive or imaging-based investigations, motivating transparent prediction from routinely collected clinical information. We analysed 920 records from the Cleveland, Hungarian, Switzerland, and VA Long Beach cohorts of the UCI Heart Disease database. The binary endpoint was absence versus presence of angiographic heart disease. Missing continuous and categorical variables were imputed within training folds, together with fold-contained encoding, scaling, and probability calibration. A stratified split produced 644 development and 276 untouched evaluation records. The primary ensemble averaged sigmoid-calibrated probabilities from K-nearest neighbours, logistic regression, and a support-vector classifier. It achieved accuracy 0.8297, sensitivity 0.8824, specificity 0.7642, precision 0.8232, F1-score 0.8517, AUROC 0.8840, average precision 0.8867, and Brier score 0.1325. A focused comparison of Extra Trees, gradient boosting, histogram gradient boosting, weighted blending, and probability stacking showed that the strongest deterministic and probabilistic models differed: SVC achieved accuracy 0.8333, whereas a constrained blend achieved AUROC 0.8883 and Brier score 0.1299. Permutation importance and Monte Carlo SHAP explanations identified chest-pain type, exercise-induced ST depression, exercise-induced angina, and thallium-test results as influential contributors. Leave-one-cohort-out AUROC ranged from 0.7152 to 0.9011. The combined framework integrates calibrated ensembling, uncertainty quantification, patient-level explanation, and cohort-aware validation for non-invasive CAD prediction.

articles.title: The impact of parity on postpartum recovery and perinatal outcomes among obese women.
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes and may affect postpartum recovery; however, the role of parity remains unclear. This study evaluated the relationship between maternal and neonatal outcomes and postpartum recovery quality by parity in obese women. This descriptive and correlational study included 128 women (64 primiparous, 64 multiparous) with body mass index ≥30 kg/m². Data were collected using standardized forms and the Obstetric Quality of Recovery Scale. No significant difference was found between groups in total recovery scores (p>0.05), although multiparous women had higher scores in current recovery perception (p<0.05). Mode of delivery, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and oxygen requirement were associated with recovery outcomes. Regular antenatal care was identified as a significant predictor, although the regression model explained only a limited proportion of the variance. Parity was not an independent determinant of overall recovery; maternal and neonatal factors appear to play a more important role. L'obésité maternelle est associée à des issues maternelles et néonatales défavorables et peut affecter la récupération post-partum ; toutefois, le rôle de la parité reste incertain. Cette étude a évalué la relation entre les issues maternelles et néonatales et la qualité de la récupération post-partum en fonction de la parité chez les femmes obèses. Cette étude descriptive et corrélationnelle a inclus 128 femmes (64 primipares, 64 multipares) présentant un indice de masse corporelle ≥ 30 kg/m². Les données ont été recueillies à l'aide de formulaires standardisés et de l'échelle de qualité de la récupération obstétricale. Aucune différence significative n'a été observée entre les groupes concernant les scores totaux de récupération (p > 0,05), bien que les femmes multipares aient obtenu des scores plus élevés concernant leur perception de la récupération actuelle (p < 0,05). Le mode d'accouchement, l'admission en unité de soins intensifs néonatals et les besoins en oxygène étaient associés aux issues de récupération. Un suivi prénatal régulier a été identifié comme un facteur prédictif significatif, bien que le modèle de régression n'explique qu'une faible proportion de la variance. La parité n'était pas un déterminant indépendant de la récupération globale; les facteurs maternels et néonataux semblent jouer un rôle plus important.

articles.title: Development of a large-animal model for dual-lumen venopulmonary extracorporeal membrane oxygenation using right atrium-to-pulmonary artery cannulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venopulmonary extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VP ECMO) using a right atrium-to-pulmonary artery configuration has emerged as an attractive strategy for right ventricular failure, bridge-to-lung transplantation, and selected cases of severe respiratory failure. Despite increasing clinical use of dual-lumen cannulas, dedicated large-animal models remain poorly described. We developed a reproducible swine model of VP ECMO using a dual-lumen right atrium-to-pulmonary artery cannula.

METHODS: Twelve adult male Landrace pigs underwent attempted bedside cannulation through the right internal jugular vein. After ultrasound-guided vascular access, a pigtail catheter was advanced into the pulmonary artery under fluoroscopic guidance and exchanged for an ultra-stiff guidewire. A 29-Fr dual-lumen cannula was then positioned between the right atrium and pulmonary artery and connected to a centrifugal pump and membrane oxygenator. Animals were maintained on VP ECMO support for 12 h.

RESULTS: Successful VP ECMO implantation was achieved in 8 of 12 animals (67%). Median maximal blood flow was 3.7 L/min (3.5-4.0). Median drainage and return pressures were -80 mmHg (-70 to -100) and 110 mmHg (100-122), respectively. Median pre-oxygenator venous oxygen saturation was 67% (65-75). Baseline pulmonary artery pressure was normal (20 mmHg [15-25]). Four procedures were unsuccessful, including three episodes of ventricular fibrillation and one cardiac tamponade. After refinement of the implantation technique, no clinically significant cannula migration or flow deterioration was observed during the 12-h observation period.

CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a reproducible large-animal model of dual-lumen VP ECMO suitable for procedural training, translational research, and future investigations.

articles.title: NIR-responsive SA-PDI/Ag2S nanocomposite for near-infrared photothermal antibacterial and wound healing.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infection is a major obstacle to wound healing. In this study, Ag2S nanoparticles were immobilized onto the surface of self-assembled perylene diimide nanofibers (SA-PDI) via electrostatic interactions, successfully constructing a novel perylene diimide-based photothermal composite, SA-PDI/Ag2S. The highly ordered π-π stacking structure of this material promotes non-radiative relaxation processes, thereby enhancing near-infrared light absorption and photothermal conversion performance. SA-PDI/Ag2S NPs exhibited a broad-spectrum absorption from the visible to the near-infrared region and a photothermal conversion efficiency (η) of 30.71%. Furthermore, in vitro antibacterial experiments showed that SA-PDI/Ag2S achieved nearly 100% bacterial clearance with 10 min irradiation. In a mouse infected skin wound model, photoexcited SA-PDI/Ag2S greatly facilitated wound healing, yielding a final residual wound area of only 2.9% and exhibiting far superior healing kinetics compared with the control group. Further histological examinations showed that SA-PDI/Ag2S downregulated pro-inflammatory IL-6 and TNF-α, upregulated anti-inflammatory IL-10, and enhanced collagen synthesis and ordered structural arrangement.

articles.title: Association of postpartum social support and psychological resilience with mother-infant bonding among migrant mothers.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between perceived social support, psychological resilience, and mother-infant bonding among migrant mothers in the postpartum period. This cross-sectional study was conducted with 233 migrant mothers, and data were collected between December 2023 and 2025 using structured questionnaires administered via social media platforms. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression analysis were performed. The mean age of participants was 25.4±5.3 years, and the mean duration of residence in Türkiye was 76.0±35.7 months. Perceived social support was positively associated with mother-infant bonding, whereas psychological resilience showed a weak negative relationship. Bonding scores differed significantly according to educational level, economic status, and mode of delivery. Regression analysis indicated that perceived social support was the strongest predictor, explaining 51% of the variance. These findings suggest that strengthening social support may improve maternal well-being and promote healthy mother-infant bonding among migrant mothers.

articles.title: Association of Continuous Glucose Monitoring-Based Nocturnal Glucose Patterns With Microvascular Complications in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To characterize metabolic heterogeneity in Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), we used continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data to identify nocturnal glucose patterns and examine their associations with clinical and metabolic characteristics and microvascular complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study analysed CGM data from 3218 patients with T2DM at a single centre (training set, n = 2214; validation set, n = 1004). We first identified nocturnal glucose patterns using k-means clustering based on glucose dynamic features (GDF). After excluding subtypes dominated by high or low glucose levels, we baseline-corrected the remaining nocturnal glucose curves, extracted morphological features and repeated clustering. We then compared clinical characteristics and the prevalence of diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic kidney disease (DKD) across subtypes, and evaluated reproducibility in the validation set.

RESULTS: GDF-based clustering identified five nocturnal glucose patterns that differed in CGM metrics, β-cell function and insulin resistance indices (all p < 0.001). Baseline-corrected clustering identified stable, declining and rising relative trajectories. Compared with stable trajectories, rising trajectories were associated with prevalent DR (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.04-1.82), and declining trajectories with prevalent DKD (OR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.00-1.63) in adjusted models for the training set. These associations were reproduced in temporal internal validation, and corresponding adjusted prevalence-ratio associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction.

CONCLUSIONS: Nocturnal glucose patterns characterize heterogeneity in metabolic profiles and prevalent microvascular complications in T2DM. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal direction of these associations.

articles.title: Comparison of Sensor Accuracy for Three Different CGM-Systems Using Either Displayed or Auto-Logged Values in Individuals With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
MCP-1 as a Biomarker of Vascular Function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endothelial dysfunction and arterial stiffness have been shown to be associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) outcomes but assessment of these is not straightforward. CVD risk in diabetes shows heterogeneity and new biomarkers are required to stratify CVD risk in these patients. The aim of this study was to determine the association between MCP-1 and measures of endothelial function and large artery stiffness, independently of traditional CVD risk factors, in patients with and without Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: This study analysed the association of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) with measures of vascular function in 477 patients with T2DM and 261 patients without T2DM. Endothelium-dependent and endothelium-independent microvascular responses were assessed by measuring vasodilator responses to iontophoresis of acetylcholine (ACh) and sodium nitroprusside (SNP), respectively, using laser Doppler imaging (LDI). Large artery stiffness was measured using carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cf-PWV).

RESULTS: MCP-1 was inversely associated with ACh and SNP responses, in patients with and without T2DM.
