Each SD higher MCP-1 was associated with lower ACh (β = -21.7 AU, 95% CI: -34.3 to -9.0) and SNP (β = -20.5 AU, 95% CI: -32.5 to -8.4) responses after adjustment for CVD risk factors, BMI, HbA1c, eGFR, medication and study centre, with similar associations in patients with and without T2DM. MCP-1 was not associated with the ACh:SNP ratio or with cf-PWV, and the associations were not modified by BMI.

CONCLUSION: This study shows MCP-1 to be associated with reduced microvascular vasodilator capacity, affecting endothelium-dependent and endothelium-independent responses, in patients with and without T2DM, independently of adiposity. Longitudinal studies in larger cohorts are required to determine whether MCP-1 improves CVD risk prediction and identifies patients most likely to benefit from targeted therapy.

articles.title: Reproductive History, Biological Indicators, and Pain Vulnerability in Aging Women: A Multi-Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain disproportionately affects women, yet the relationship between female reproductive history and long-term pain vulnerability remains insufficiently understood. Using three population-based cohorts from the UK, China, and the US, we evaluated associations between reproductive factors and pain-related phenotypes in aging women. Endogenous reproductive milestones showed nonlinear associations with pain risk. Specifically, both earlier and later ages at menarche and menopause, as well as shorter and longer reproductive lifespans, were linked to higher pain vulnerability. Childbirth-related characteristics, such as higher parity, earlier age at first birth, and longer interbirth intervals, were also associated with increased pain vulnerability. Reproductive surgeries and exogenous hormone use were consistently associated with pain phenotypes, with timing-dependent effects. In the UK Biobank, reproductive factors showed both shared and site-specific associations across seven chronic pain sites. These reproductive-pain associations were amplified among women with higher adiposity, greater socioeconomic deprivation, a history of depression or anxiety, and hypertension. Exploratory mediation analyses implicated inflammatory, hormonal, and metabolic indicators as potential biological correlates of several reproductive-chronic pain associations. Together, these findings highlight reproductive history as an important life-course factor associated with pain vulnerability and provide insights for future studies investigating mechanisms and risk stratification of chronic pain in women.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Anagliptin Added to Metformin and Empagliflozin 10 mg in Korean Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicentre, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase III Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of anagliptin added to metformin and empagliflozin 10 mg in adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) with inadequate glycaemic control.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial, participants receiving metformin (≥ 1000 mg/day) plus empagliflozin 10 mg/day were randomised 1:1 to anagliptin 100 mg twice daily or placebo for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at Week 24 in the full analysis set, analysed using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures. Secondary endpoints included fasting plasma glucose (FPG), HbA1c target attainment, HOMA-β and safety. Glycaemic responder analyses were conducted post hoc.

RESULTS: The full analysis set included 195 participants (anagliptin, n = 97; placebo, n = 98). At Week 24, LS mean HbA1c changes were -0.81% and -0.24%, respectively, yielding a treatment difference of -0.57% (95% CI -0.74 to -0.40; p < 0.0001). FPG was also significantly reduced (between-group difference -12.15 mg/dL, 95% CI -19.18 to -5.12; p = 0.0008). HbA1c ≤ 7.0% was achieved by 55.7% versus 25.5% of participants. HbA1c reductions ≥ 0.5% occurred in 68.0% versus 27.6%, and reductions ≥ 1.0% in 33.0% versus 9.2%. HOMA-β improved significantly with anagliptin (between-group difference 14.35, 95% CI 7.37-21.32; p < 0.0001). Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 22.7% and 17.2%, respectively; no hypoglycaemic events or deaths were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Anagliptin added to metformin and empagliflozin 10 mg provided confirmatory evidence of additional glycaemic efficacy in a separately randomised Korean population, increased glycaemic responder rates and improved estimated β-cell function, with acceptable short-term tolerability.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05814406.

articles.title: Complementary Cardioprotection and Efferocytosis by Circulating Vesicle Recruitment and SIRPα Blockade after Myocardial Ischemia/Reperfusion.
articles.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) causes heart failure and mortality, driven by ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and CD47/Signal regulator protein α (SIRPα)-impaired efferocytosis that together sustain tissue damage. Endogenous plasma small extracellular vesicles (P-EVs) offer an endogenous, multifunctional option, yet their cardioprotective efficacy is limited by low cardiac accumulation. Herein, a nanosystem (SαV-DAb) was developed by functionalizing SIRPα-variant-overexpressing nanovesicles (SαV) with dual antibodies (DAb) against CD42b (platelet marker) and CD63 (EV marker) via a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-cleavable linkage. This configuration allows the nanovesicles to hitchhike on circulating platelets for targeted delivery to the ischemic heart, while simultaneously capturing and enriching protective circulating P-EVs in the lesion. SαV could bind to CD47, avoiding the SIRPα activation on macrophages and promoting efferocytosis. SαV-DAb demonstrated significantly enhanced cardiac accumulation and promoted targeted delivery of P-EVs to the ischemic myocardium. Treatment with SαV-DAb elicited a coordinated therapeutic response, including anti-apoptosis, pro-angiogenesis, and pro-efferocytosis, ultimately leading to attenuated ventricular fibrosis and improved systolic function after I/R injury, with no observable toxicity. This strategy simplifies the preparation workflow by avoiding prior isolation of PLTs and protective vesicles, and provides a conceptual framework for endogenous-system-based nanomedicine in cardiac repair.

articles.title: Early initiation or ongoing treatment? Interpreting sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use after acute coronary syndrome.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

articles.title: Using a biopsychosocial approach to assess and manage patients' skin integrity.
articles.journal: Nursing standard (Royal College of Nursing (Great Britain) : 1987)
articles.abstract: The importance of the skin is often overlooked despite its role in providing a boundary against the external environment, including ultraviolet (UV) light and harmful microorganisms. The skin also regulates body temperature, produces vitamins and excretes waste products. Drawing on the biopsychosocial model, this article outlines the physical and psychosocial implications for patients living with impaired skin integrity and explores the nursing assessment and management of patients with wounds and/or skin conditions such as psoriasis. The author also discusses how wider determinants of health, including rising rates of comorbid conditions such as diabetes mellitus and depression, can influence wound healing.

articles.title: Indoor Air Quality Management for Patients with COPD and IPF: Practical Recommendations Based on Current Standards and Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) have reduced pulmonary reserve and increased susceptibility to airborne pollutants. However, practical guidance for managing residential indoor air quality (IAQ) remains limited. Objectives: To review evidence and reference standards relevant to IAQ management in COPD and IPF and propose practical, disease-informed recommendations for reducing indoor pollutant exposure.

METHODS: We conducted a focused narrative review of evidence on pollutant exposure, respiratory health effects, and residential exposure-reduction interventions. Domestic and international indoor and ambient air quality standards were reviewed to identify key management parameters and feasible exposure-reduction strategies. Separate decision rules were applied to action references and maintenance targets according to exposure setting, intended use, and source-specific averaging time.

RESULTS: Nine parameters were selected: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO2, formaldehyde, total volatile organic compounds, CO, O3, and relative humidity. Where applicable, action references indicated conditions under which exposure-reduction measures should be considered, whereas maintenance targets supported routine exposure management. Ambient forecast categories were used only for pollutants primarily managed according to outdoor conditions. CO2 and relative humidity were treated as operational environmental parameters. All values retained the averaging times and intended contexts of their source standards and were not considered disease-specific clinical cutoffs. Recommendations emphasized source control, outdoor air quality-guided ventilation, particle filtration, and control of cooking and combustion emissions.

CONCLUSION: This framework provides practical, parameter-specific exposure-management references and strategies for patients with COPD and IPF. Prospective studies should assess whether multicomponent IAQ interventions improve exposure and clinically relevant respiratory outcomes.

articles.title: Planned percutaneous coronary intervention around transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease frequently coexist in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We compared planned percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) around TAVI with an initially conservative or deferred PCI strategy.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, and Web of Science through 15 April 2026. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Exploratory reconstruction was a secondary analysis. The study protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO with the following ID: CRD420261397950.

RESULTS: Three randomized controlled trials including 1156 patients were identified. Planned PCI was not associated with significant differences in all-cause mortality (risk ratio = 0.90, 95% CI = 0.70-1.15), trial-defined major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; risk ratio = 0.91, 95% CI = 0.70-1.18; supportive and exploratory because composite components differed), cardiovascular death (risk ratio = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.51-1.08), or myocardial infarction (risk ratio = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.45-1.63). It was associated with fewer urgent (risk ratio = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.13-0.87) and any subsequent revascularizations (risk ratio = 0.25, 95% CI = 0.07-0.87), but more trial-reported major bleeding (risk ratio = 1.57, 95% CI = 1.07-2.32; definitions varied) and any bleeding (risk ratio = 1.77, 95% CI = 1.27-2.47).

CONCLUSION: Routine planned PCI around TAVI was not shown to reduce mortality or major ischemic outcomes. It was associated with fewer subsequent revascularizations and more trial-reported major bleeding and any bleeding, supporting selective, individualized decision-making.

articles.title: p66shc N6-methyladenosine methylation induces micronuclear rupture and promotes cardiac fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Dynamic interactions between micronuclear and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species influence micronuclear homeostasis and associated heart diseases. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying micronuclear rupture during cardiac fibrosis remain largely unknown.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Cardiac fibroblast-specific YTHDF1-deficient and wild-type mice were treated with isoproterenol/transverse aortic constriction to induce cardiac fibrosis. To investigate the roles of YTHDF1, p66shc, and m6A modification in cardiac fibrosis, AAV9 vectors carrying a cardiac fibroblast-specific periostin promoter were used to induce p66shc overexpression or deliver small hairpin RNA targeting YTHDF1, along with the m6A inhibitor 3-deoxyadenosine. Histological and molecular biology analyses were conducted to examine how YTHDF1 regulates p66shc mRNA stability during cardiac fibrosis. Additionally, p66shc reconstitution in YTHDF1-deficient cardiac fibroblasts and mouse hearts was performed to assess its effects on micronuclear rupture and fibrosis. Human atrial fibrillation heart tissue was used to validate these findings.During cardiac fibrosis, the increased micronuclear rupture was accompanied by p66shc upregulation and excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production. Fibroblast-specific p66shc depletion inhibited micronuclear rupture, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and fibroblast pyroptosis, and alleviated cardiac fibrosis. Notably, p66shc upregulation was correlated with elevated m6A modification of mRNA. Mechanistically, YTHDF1 recognized the m6A-modified site on p66shc mRNA, enhancing its stability and translation. Conversely, YTHDF1 knockdown inhibits the stability and expression of p66shc, leading to opposing effects. In human atrial fibrillation heart tissues, increased YTHDF1 and p66shc levels were associated with enhanced micronuclear rupture, excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production, fibroblast pyroptosis, and cardiac fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed a novel epigenetic mechanism in which m6A methylation of p66shc drives micronuclear rupture and exacerbates cardiac fibrosis. These findings provide new insights into potential measures for preventing cardiac fibrosis.

TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVES: These findings reveal a clinically significant role of the YTHDF1/p66shc axis in mitigating cardiac fibrosis. Targeting m6A methylation of p66shc to suppress mitochondrial ROS generation, micronucleus rupture, and cardiac fibroblast pyroptosis may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for cardiac fibrosis.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive.

OBJECTIVE: To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions.

STUDY SELECTION: RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible.

DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed.

RESULTS: Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Revisiting the Risk of Bacteremia in Well-Appearing Infants With Fever Without a Source ≥40 °C: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fever without a source (FWS) in infants is a frequent reason for emergency consultation. Historically, very high fever (≥40 °C) has been associated with an increased risk of bacteremia, prompting extensive diagnostic testing and empiric antibiotic therapy. However, recent epidemiological changes, including expanded vaccination and post-pandemic shifts in pathogen circulation, may have modified this risk. We aim to address this in our study.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study in 2 tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2018 to 2025). Well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months presenting with FWS ≥40 °C were included. The primary outcome was bacteremia. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: A total of 184 infants were included (median age 14.3 mo). Blood cultures were obtained in 168 (91.3%). Only one case of bacteremia (0.5%; 95% CI: 0.1-3.0) was identified, secondary to urinary tract infection (UTI), with no cases of occult bacteremia. UTI prevalence was 19.6%, and pneumonia 2.7%. Overall, 42.3% received antibiotics, and 16.3% were hospitalized, with all patients showing favorable outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months with FWS ≥40 °C, bacteremia appears uncommon, although the wide confidence interval precludes firm conclusions. These exploratory findings suggest that a more selective diagnostic approach may warrant consideration over routine blood cultures and empiric antibiotics, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Sex differences in mechanical circulatory support efficacy in infarct-related cardiogenic shock. An individual patient data meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine use of active mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in infarct-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains controversial. Although recent evidence suggests potential benefit in selected patients, the influence of sex on MCS efficacy is poorly defined.

AIMS: To evaluate whether sex modifies the effect of MCS in AMI-CS.

METHODS: Randomized trials comparing early routine MCS with standard care in AMI-CS and reporting 6-month mortality were identified through January 2025. Individual patient data were analyzed using study-stratified Cox models. The primary outcome was 6-month all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, major bleeding, and peripheral ischemic vascular complications.

RESULTS: Nine trials including 213 (20%) female and 845 male patients were analysed. Women were older than men (67.6 vs. 63.7 years; P < 0.001) and had higher 6-month mortality (60% vs. 52%; P = 0.03). Early routine MCS was not associated with significantly lower mortality in either women (HR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.70-1.42) or men (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.02; P for interaction = 0.41). Among DanGer Shock-like patients, MCS was associated with lower mortality in men (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.86), but not in women (HR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.72-1.91; P for interaction = 0.02). MCS increased complications in both sexes.

CONCLUSIONS: Women with AMI-CS were underrepresented and had higher mortality than men. No sex-specific treatment effect was observed overall, whereas subgroup findings suggested possible heterogeneity in DanGer-Shock-like patients. These findings, limited by small number of female patients and wide confidence intervals, support the need for adequately powered trials with sufficient female representation.

articles.title: Traumatic Diaphragmatic Crural Hematoma in Crush Trauma: Diagnostic Challenges and Management in a Rare Case.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries are uncommon in thoracoabdominal trauma, and traumatic diaphragmatic crural hematoma (TDCH) is even rarer in this context. Because of its retroperitoneal position, TDCH can be difficult to detect early. Although TDCH is usually not life-threatening and does not often require emergency surgery, it is important to note that it often coexists with other serious injuries. This report describes the case of TDCH and shock following crush trauma. After stabilization, whole-body contrast-enhanced CT identified TDCH and unstable pelvic fractures. She then underwent diagnostic angiography followed by surgical management of the pelvic injuries. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old woman with no prior health issues was brought to the emergency department after being accidentally crushed between 2 vehicles while her husband was reversing his car. She experienced pain in her chest, abdomen, and right hip. Initially in shock, she stabilized following initial resuscitation and blood transfusion. Initial evaluation, including extended FAST ultrasound (E-FAST), was negative. Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed fractures of the right sacrum, iliac wing, acetabulum, and pubic rami, along with a hematoma in the bilateral diaphragmatic crura (T12-L1) with contrast extravasation. Diagnostic angiography showed no active contrast extravasation from the diaphragm or pelvis. She subsequently underwent surgical fixation of pelvic fractures. Her postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged in stable condition. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights that TDCH is rare and may indicate a high-energy injury requiring prompt diagnosis. Whole-body contrast-enhanced CT is reasonable in patients presenting with shock and negative E-FAST findings. Management should be guided by bleeding status, and diagnostic angiography may be considered when active bleeding is suspected.

articles.title: Epidemiologic Variability and Clinical Severity Across 11 Influenza Seasons in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza is a major cause of respiratory illness, contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality in children. Seasonal influenza epidemics were profoundly disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Whether the clinical presentation and disease severity differ according to influenza virus type and subtype remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to describe temporal changes in epidemiology, clinical characteristics, outcomes and healthcare utilization among laboratory-confirmed pediatric influenza cases over 11 seasons and to explore associations between virus type/subtype and clinically important outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at a tertiary pediatric hospital, including all laboratory-confirmed influenza cases identified in children presenting with acute respiratory infection between July 2015 and June 2026, and analyzed the distribution of cases and their demographic and clinical characteristics.

RESULTS: Influenza was detected in 3105 children (median age, 4 years), the majority of whom were previously healthy (82.4%). Within this cohort, hospitalization was required in 17.9% of cases, with 1.1% requiring intensive care admission, and 22.8% developing complications, including encephalitis and sepsis. Influenza circulation patterns, including the timing of peak activity and the duration of annual epidemics, varied over time. After an 18-month absence of reported cases during the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021-2022 season was marked by a substantial resurgence, followed by 2 years of atypical year-round circulation before returning to the usual seasonal pattern. Influenza A accounted for 72.3% of cases, with alternating predominance of virus types and subtypes without a consistent epidemiologic pattern. In a restricted type/subtype analysis, influenza A(H1N1) cases had a higher frequency of hospitalization and recorded moderate-to-severe complications, and this association remained statistically significant after multivariable analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Influenza was associated with clinically important illness and healthcare use among children in this hospital-based cohort, most commonly among otherwise healthy children, highlighting the importance of influenza prevention strategies. During and after the COVID-19 pandemic, influenza epidemiology changed markedly, underscoring the need for continued surveillance.

articles.title: Survey of Gnathostoma nipponicum infection in freshwater fish around Lake Ogawara, Aomori Prefecture, Japan.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: Gnathostoma nipponicum is distributed in Aomori Prefecture, but its current infection status around Lake Ogawara has remained unclear for approximately 30 years. We investigated G. nipponicum infection in freshwater fish collected in and around Lake Ogawara from 2023 to 2026. The parasites were detected, indicating the widespread distribution of G. nipponicum in Aomori Prefecture. Among 14 freshwater fish species examined, G. nipponicum was detected in loach (Misgurnus anguillicaudatus), floating goby (Gymnogobius urotaenia), stone moroko (Pseudorasbora parva), and rosy bitterling (Rhodeus ocellatus ocellatus). Infection in stone moroko and rosy bitterling was confirmed for the first time. Sequence analysis revealed no variation in the 243-bp 5.8S-ITS2 region among the 55 G. nipponicum larvae examined, and the sequences showed 100% identity with previously reported G. nipponicum sequences.

articles.title: Transient detection of Eimeria oocysts in a Budgerigar (Melopsittacus undulatus) with morphological and molecular characterization.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: Reports of coccidiosis in Budgerigars (Melopsittacus undulatus) are scarce, and molecular data are lacking. Eimeria oocysts were detected by direct fecal examination in a 3-year-old Budgerigar two days after suspected ingestion of outdoor sun-dried potting soil, following twelve negative examinations over three years. The oocysts differed morphologically from Budgerigar-derived Eimeria dunsingi and Eimeria psittacina. Molecularly, the 18S rDNA and cox1 sequences were novel, closely related to the galliform Eimeria dispersa and Eimeria innocua and the psittacine Eimeria purpureicephali. Without treatment, no oocysts were detected 15 days later, and a cohabiting Budgerigar remained negative. Pseudoparasitism could not be distinguished from a mild, transient infection. Both possibilities should be considered when coccidian oocysts are detected in birds possibly exposed to outdoor substrates.

articles.title: Predicting Treatment Quality in Children and Adolescents with Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Using Insulin and Renin.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monitoring treatment quality in congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) remains challenging. Current approaches rely predominantly on bone age and serum steroid measurements, which are variable and require expert interpretation. Reliable, accessible biochemical indicators are lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a predictive score for undertreatment in children and adolescents with CAH using routinely available clinical and non-steroid laboratory parameters.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicenter cohort study including 81 patients with genetically confirmed 21-hydroxylase deficiency across four European pediatric endocrinology centers. Clinical features and laboratory parameters-including fasting insulin, renin, lipid profile, glucose, and growth indices-were assessed at three outpatient visits. Treatment status (optimal, undertreatment, overtreatment) was classified by expert endocrinologists. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of undertreatment and to construct a predictive model.

RESULTS: Data from 233 visits were analyzed. Undertreated patients showed significantly higher insulin (p = 0.005), higher renin (p = 0.003), increased height SDS (p = 0.014), and lower HDL cholesterol (p = 0.007) compared with optimally treated patients. The final predictive model retained insulin (coefficient 1.15) and renin (1.038) as independent predictors. At a threshold of ≥30-36, sensitivity was 71%, specificity 84%and overall correct classification 80%. The ROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.785.

CONCLUSION: Serum insulin and renin, two inexpensive and routinely measured parameters, predict undertreatment in children and adolescents with CAH with good accuracy. Their dual relevance for short-term treatment monitoring and long-term cardiometabolic risk underscores their potential as practical tools to complement current strategies.

articles.title: The future of maternal mortality measurement: implications of reduced DHS availability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) have historically filled key data gaps in global maternal mortality monitoring. Amid uncertainty regarding funding and their future availability, this study evaluates the potential impact of reduced DHS data availability on United Nations maternal mortality estimates.

METHODS: We conducted a modelling analysis using the UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group's BMat model to assess the contribution of DHS data to maternal mortality estimates. We compared three scenarios: [1] exclusion of all DHS data [2], exclusion of DHS conducted since 2015, and [3] a counterfactual with the "status quo" including all eligible data sources. Changes in 2023 maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and uncertainty intervals were evaluated globally, regionally, and nationally.

RESULTS: DHS contributed 21% of all country-year data and were the sole source of data in 23 countries. Excluding all DHS data led to a 15% reduction in the point estimate of the global MMR and a 70% increase in uncertainty. The post-2015 exclusion scenario resulted in a 10% global MMR reduction. These effects were most pronounced in countries and regions lacking alternative data sources (e.g., sub-Saharan Africa and Oceania regions). The exclusion narrowed uncertainty intervals in a few cases, mainly where DHS estimates were less consistent with other national data sources.

CONCLUSIONS: A sustained reduction in the availability of DHS data would substantially affect global maternal mortality estimation, particularly in data-scarce and high-burden settings. The findings highlight the urgent need to strengthen sustainable national data systems, including civil registration and vital statistics and health management information systems.

articles.title: Two-dimensional speckle-tracking imaging for assessing cardiac dysfunction in liver cirrhosis: correlation with Child-Pugh score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) enables sensitive and quantitative assessment of myocardial deformation, its application in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) has largely been limited to ventricular function. This study applied 2D-STI to evaluate both ventricular and atrial function in order to identify early myocardial dysfunction in this population.

METHODS: A total of 82 patients with LC were enrolled and stratified according to the Child-Pugh classification into Class A (n = 30), Class B (n = 29), and Class C (n = 23). Thirty healthy individuals served as controls. All 112 participants underwent conventional echocardiography and 2D-STI assessment.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, all LC groups showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) (both P < 0.05), with a progressive decline from Class A to Class C. In contrast, right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly decreased only in Classes B and C (P < 0.05). Left atrial conduit strain (LAScd) was significantly reduced across all LC groups (P < 0.05), whereas left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) and contractile strain (LASct) demonstrated a biphasic pattern -initially increased, then decreased- compared with controls. Overall, 2D-STI detected cardiac dysfunction earlier than conventional echocardiography. Significant negative correlations were observed between Child-Pugh score and LVGLS, RVFWLS, and RVGLS.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac function is impaired in patients with LC and deteriorates with increasing disease severity. Compared with conventional echocardiography, 2D-STI detects cardiac dysfunction at an earlier stage, providing valuable support for early clinical intervention.

articles.title: Association between periodontitis and coronary plaque composition: can early periodontal treatment influence coronary artery disease progression? A study protocol for a prospective, randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The (PERIOdontitis and Coronary Artery Disease) PERIOCAD study aims to investigate the association between periodontitis and coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and the effectiveness of early versus late periodontitis (PD) treatment on systemic inflammation and CAD progression.

BACKGROUND: PD and CAD are common diseases, sharing underlying molecular mechanisms, like systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Epidemiological and genetic studies suggest a strong link between PD and CAD. Yet, it remains unclear whether treatment of periodontitis may attenuate progression of arteriosclerosis. CCTA enables reproducible quantitative assessment of coronary plaque volumes and composition, providing metrics for both cross-sectional associations and longitudinal changes of plaque burden.

METHODS: PERIOCAD is a prospective, randomized, controlled trial (RCT) aiming to enroll 200 patients who undergo clinically indicated CCTA. All participants will undergo comprehensive periodontal status assessment and patients diagnosed with PD (estimated n = 100) will be randomized 1:1 to either early, systematic PD therapy (intervention arm) or delayed care after 2 years (control arm). CCTA analysis will include quantitative plaque volumes and composition, assessment of high-risk plaque features and evaluation of pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation (PCAT). Cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers will be assessed at baseline and after 24 months. Follow-up evaluations are scheduled at 12 and 24 months to reassess periodontal status. In addition, changes in plaque burden will be longitudinally assessed in case of clinically indicated repeat CCTA scans. The primary endpoint is the influence of periodontal treatment on cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers at 24 months. Secondary endpoints include major adverse cardiovascular events during follow-up, changes in plaque parameters and PCAT on serial CCTA, and associations between CCTA metrics and PD at baseline.

DISCUSSION: PERIOCAD is expected to provide unique insights regarding the relationship between PD and CAD, being to our knowledge the first RCT to investigate the impact of PD therapy on systemic inflammation and CAD progression in symptomatic patients. Our findings could have significant implications for interdisciplinary cardiovascular disease prevention strategies and public health policies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register DRKS00038470 (Date of registration:2025-11-24).

articles.title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional neck dissection for oral cavity cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: To compare robot-assisted remote-access neck dissection with conventional transcervical neck dissection for oral cavity cancer, focusing on oncologic adequacy, perioperative burden, complications, function, and cosmesis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception through 24 September 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and verified eligibility. Comparative studies informed quantitative synthesis; clinically informative single-arm reports characterized technical evolution. Random-effects meta-analysis used mean differences and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I-informed domains. Fifteen reports representing 14 independent cohorts were included. Five oral-cavity comparisons involved 222 patients (99 robotic, 123 conventional). Three studies involving 124 patients contributed to meta-analysis. Robotic dissection prolonged neck-dissection time by 83.9 minutes (95% CI 59.7 to 108.1; I2​=22%) but did not materially change lymph-node yield (mean difference 0.8 nodes, 95% CI -4.2 to 5.8; I2​=0%). Median-based comparisons likewise showed longer or similar perioperative courses without a consistent nodal-yield disadvantage. Five-year disease-free survival was reported by one direct tongue-cancer cohort and 2-year disease-free survival by one propensity-matched oral-cavity cohort; neither demonstrated a statistically detectable difference, but events were sparse. Scar satisfaction favored robotic access. All comparisons were nonrandomized and at serious risk of confounding bias; selection bias was serious in four cohorts and moderate in the propensity-matched cohort. Robot-assisted neck dissection consistently concealed the cervical scar and achieved similar average nodal counts in selected oral-cavity cancer cohorts, at the cost of substantially longer operating time. These findings support technical feasibility and informed patient choice, but nodal yield is a surrogate outcome and the current evidence does not establish equivalent regional control, survival, or overall morbidity.

articles.title: Dual-tracer 68Ga-PSMA and 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT characterization of solitary testicular metastasis from castration-resistant prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testicular metastasis from prostate cancer is extremely rare. We report a case of solitary testicular metastasis detected by dual-tracer PET/CT using 68Ga-PSMA and 68Ga-FAPI in a patient with castration-resistant prostate cancer.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 66-year-old man with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma developed biochemical progression after prior therapies. 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT revealed a solitary PSMA-avid testicular lesion with no significant uptake in the prostate bed. Subsequent 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated concordant intense uptake in the same lesion, while the primary site remained negative. The patient underwent orchiectomy, and histopathological examination confirmed metastatic prostate cancer.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights a rare pattern of solitary testicular metastasis from castration-resistant prostate cancer detected by dual-tracer PET/CT. The concordant uptake of 68Ga-PSMA and 68Ga-FAPI in the metastatic lesion suggests complementary information regarding tumor characteristics and the associated tumor microenvironment. Dual-tracer PET imaging may provide additional value for the characterization of atypical metastatic lesions.

articles.title: Intraoperative Mean Arterial Pressure Trajectory Classes and Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury After Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) is clinically important after bariatric surgery, yet conventional blood-pressure summaries do not capture temporal hemodynamic evolution. We aimed to identify intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) trajectory classes during laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG), evaluate their associations with recorded AKI, and explore incremental prognostic value.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 1,379 adults undergoing LSG (January 2016-March 2025). MAP was calculated from paired invasive pressures recorded every 5 min. Piecewise latent class mixed modeling (LCMM) with a 30-min knot identified trajectories. AKI was ascertained from database-coded KDIGO creatinine labels. Multivariable logistic regression with multiple imputation evaluated associations; AUC assessed discrimination.

RESULTS: Four trajectory classes were identified: moderate-decline/stable (C1, n = 492), steep-decline/low (C2, n = 177), gradually rising (C3, n = 293), and decline-rebound (C4, n = 417). Recorded AKI occurred in 78 patients (5.7%), with incidences of 5.1%, 12.4%, 2.7%, and 5.5%, respectively (P < 0.001). Trajectory class was associated with AKI overall (P = 0.028); compared with C3, C2 had higher adjusted AKI odds (OR, 3.21; 95% CI, 1.31-7.84; P = 0.011), whereas C1 (OR, 2.22; P = 0.059) and C4 (OR, 1.54; P = 0.323) were not individually significant. Apparent AUCs were 0.692, 0.730, and 0.743 across expanded models; the combined extended-bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.717.

CONCLUSION: Four intraoperative MAP trajectory classes were identified during LSG and were associated overall with recorded postoperative AKI, with higher adjusted odds in C2 than C3. Incremental prognostic value was modest, and prospective external validation is required.

articles.title: The Underrepresentation of African Immigrants in Lifestyle Interventions for Black Adults in the US: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The African immigrant population in the US is growing rapidly and is disproportionately affected by obesity. Their exposure to African cultures prior to migration heavily influences their diet and physical activity behaviors, underscoring the need for culturally tailored lifestyle interventions. Lifestyle interventions have been culturally tailored for Black adults in the US, but it is unclear whether theoretical frameworks and associated cultural tailoring are relevant to African immigrants. This systematic review examined the representation of African immigrants in lifestyle interventions that target Black adults in the US, the theoretical models underpinning these interventions, and the type of cultural tailoring that was performed.

METHODS: We conducted our literature search in CINAHL Plus, Cochrane Library, Medline, PsycInfo, and PubMed from January 2013 to December 2025. We examined lifestyle intervention trials targeting Black/African American adults with weight loss as an outcome.

RESULTS: Our search resulted in 2,320 articles, of which 43 were eligible. Only one study explicitly indicated that African immigrants were included in their sample. Most articles (65.1%) indicated that their intervention was underpinned by theoretical model(s), and the most common model was social cognitive theory. The majority of articles (58.1%) described cultural tailoring of the intervention for Black adults.

CONCLUSION: Lifestyle interventions for Black adults did not generally assess whether participants were born outside the US or take it into account in culturally tailoring interventions. Future lifestyle interventions targeting Black adults should include participants' country of birth and examine whether Black immigrants' lifestyle habits and needs are adequately addressed.

articles.title: Effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of epilepsy surgery in patients with refractory epilepsy: A systematic review of decision-analytic models.
articles.abstract: Our objective was to evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of epilepsy surgery for the treatment of patients with DRE. We carried out a systematic review of Decision Analytic Models (DAMs) in the main international databases regarding the comparison between epilepsy surgery versus medical treatment. We evaluated the relevance and credibility of the DAMs with the ISPOR-AMCP-NPC tool. We synthesized the results qualitatively. The certainty of the body of evidence was determined using the GRADE approach proposed for modeling studies. Clinical and economic outcomes were synthesized narratively because substantial heterogeneity existed across studies in epilepsy etiology, patient populations, model structures, perspectives, time horizons, and outcome definitions, precluding formal meta-analysis and quantitative pooling of cost-effectiveness estimates. Surgery was associated with higher reported rates of seizure freedom and seizure reduction than medical treatment, with seizure freedom ranging from 37.1% to 64.0% and seizure reduction from 24.6% to 42.2%. Reported QALY gains ranged from 0.3 to 3.0. Incremental costs varied substantially, ranging from savings of I$116,642 to additional costs of I$227,146 per patient. ICERs ranged from dominant (less costly and more effective) to I$291,091 per QALY gained. For seizure-related outcomes, ICERs ranged from I$454 to I$1,268 per 1% increase in seizure reduction and from I$5.83 to I$1,782 per 1% increase in seizure freedom, reflecting substantial variation in healthcare settings, perspectives, time horizons, and economic models. Epilepsy surgery is considered an effective and cost-effective option in patients with DRE, although the evidence is still low and very low certainty. So future studies of higher methodological quality are needed to better assess the picture and corroborate these results.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

articles.title: Reducing the diagnostic odyssey in childhood-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy through phenotype-guided genomic evaluation.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: Childhood-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophies (SMA) comprise a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of neuromuscular disorders in which molecular diagnosis may be delayed despite increasing access to next-generation and whole-exome sequencing. Although broad genomic testing has transformed diagnostic practice, its interpretation remains highly dependent on detailed clinical characterization. We emphasize the value of phenotype-guided genomic evaluation in children with suspected non-5q SMA. Age at onset, distribution of weakness, tendon reflexes, respiratory and skeletal involvement, creatine kinase levels, electrophysiological findings, family history, and targeted neuroimaging may reveal recognizable genotype-associated patterns that help prioritize candidate genes and facilitate variant interpretation. A recently reported pediatric case series illustrates characteristic associations including scapuloperoneal weakness with TRPV4 variants, congenital hypotonia and arthrogryposis with ASCC1-related disease, lower-extremity-predominant weakness with BICD2, pontocerebellar hypoplasia with VRK1, and bilateral thalamic abnormalities with HEXB variants. Rather than replacing genomic technologies, comprehensive phenotyping provides the clinical framework required to maximize their diagnostic yield. Following exclusion of SMN1-related disease, integrating clinical examination, electrophysiology, neuroimaging, and broad genomic sequencing may help reduce the diagnostic odyssey in childhood-onset non-5q SMA.

articles.title: Isolated body lateropulsion due to a paramedian mesencephalic stroke.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: We report a 71-year-old man who presented with acute recurrent falls due to isolated body lateropulsion to the right, as sole neurological deficit. Brain MRI revealed a left paramedian mesencephalic infarction involving the interstitial nucleus of Cajal (INC) and medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF). Isolated body lateropulsion is a rare clinical presentation produced by lesions affecting the graviceptive pathway, which processes gravitational input and body orientation relative to vertical in order to maintain upright posture and spatial orientation. Although internuclear ophtalmoplegia or abnormalities of vertical or torsional eye position have been associated with lesions of the INC and MLF, these were absent in our patient.The patient recovered fully within three months, consistent with the favorable prognosis of isolated lateropulsion due to stroke. This case highlights an under-recognized topodiagnostic pattern within the graviceptive pathway.

articles.title: Pop PK-PD model for evaluating the effects of insulin degludec in healthy adult Chinese males.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the dose-response relationship of insulin degludec (IDeg) by linking its pharmacokinetic (PK) exposure to pharmacodynamic (PD) outcomes, supporting evidence-based decision-making in therapeutic development. A single-dose euglycemic clamp study was conducted in 30 healthy adult Chinese male volunteers, from whom 408 plasma samples were collected, yielding a median plasma concentration of 9.57 ng/mL. A population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (Pop PK-PD model) was developed and validated using Maspectra® software (version 2.8.1) with the first-order conditional estimation with interaction (FOCE-I) method, following a stepwise covariate screening approach. The PK component was best described by a one-compartment model with first-order absorption incorporating an absorption lag time (ALAG) and linear elimination, while the PD component was characterized by a direct-effect Emax model with a Hill coefficient (γ). Body mass index (BMI) significantly influenced the apparent clearance (CL/F), and body weight (BW) significantly affected the apparent volume of distribution (V/F). The final model estimated CL/F = 1.49 L/h, V/F = 25.3 L, absorption rate constant (ka) = 0.10 h-1, ALAG = 0.72 h, maximum effect (Emax) = 3.70 mg/kg/min, half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) = 15.35 ng/mL, and γ = 4.13. Comprehensive model evaluation using goodness-of-fit plots, bootstrap analysis, and visual predictive check (VPC) confirmed that the model exhibits good stability, accurate parameter estimates, and reliable predictive performance. In conclusion, a robust and reliable Pop PK-PD model based on a one-compartment structure with direct effect was successfully developed in healthy adult males, providing a useful simulation foundation for subsequent insulin-related clinical trials in similar populations. Nevertheless, dedicated external validation studies in broader, more clinically representative cohorts, including female subjects and patients with diabetes across different disease stages, are strictly warranted before the model can be confidently extended to support general clinical dose selection and routine therapeutic decision-making. This study was registered on the Drug Clinical Trial Registration and Information Disclosure Platform, registration number: CTR20201129, registration date: June 5, 2020.

articles.title: Protective effects of rs7315280 on hippocampal volume and cognitive decline in aging by its enhancer activity regulating TESC expression.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hippocampal atrophy is a core biomarker of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the cognitive relevance and molecular function of its genetic determinants remain largely unknown. In this study, we aimed to bridge this critical gap by systematically identifying and functionally characterizing a key genetic determinant of hippocampal volume and its role in AD.

METHODS: We performed a cross-cohort Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analysis using data from UK Biobank (n = 33,731) and ENIGMA (n = 26,814). Phenotypic associations were validated in the ADNI-1 cohort (n = 756), adjusting for polygenic risk scores (PRS). Functional characterization included in silico annotation (3DSNP/ENCODE), dual-luciferase reporter assays, and brain-specific eQTL analysis.

RESULTS: We identified rs7315280 (A > G) as a lead genetic variant associated with hippocampal volume via meta-GWAS analysis (all P ≤ 1.37 × 10-19). In ADNI-1, G allele carriers had larger hippocampal volumes (P = 0.004), a lower AD conversion rate (3%), delayed disease onset (P = 0.015), and an odds ratio for AD of 0.663. rs7315280 localizes to hippocampal enhancer regions and binds 51 transcription factors (e.g., CTCF). The G allele enhanced transcriptional activity (P = 0.002), and rs7315280 was linked to TESC expression in the human prefrontal cortex (P = 1.30 × 10⁻5).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that rs7315280 may contribute to protection against AD by acting as an enhancer regulating TESC expression, identifying a potential novel genetic locus and a candidate therapeutic target for further investigation.

articles.title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Neurointerventional therapy is a cornerstone in managing head and neck vascular disorders, with cerebral angiography serving as its fundamental diagnostic and therapeutic backbone. However, manual cerebral angiography is associated with several inherent limitations. While existing robotic-assisted systems have shown promise in mitigating some of these issues, they face challenges such as limited compatibility, lengthy setup times, and a lack of high-quality real-world evidence. The ERASE trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). A total of 660 eligible patients will be enrolled from seven comprehensive stroke centers in China and randomized 1:1 to either the robotic-assisted group or the control group. Both groups use the Seldinger technique for femoral/radial artery access. Operators undergo standardized training on the robotic system. The trial adopts a prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint (PROBE) design, with all imaging endpoints adjudicated via blinded review by an independent imaging core laboratory. All patients are followed up at baseline, end of surgery, 24 h postoperatively, and 7 days post-discharge. The primary efficacy outcome is the clinical success rate. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of perioperative/postoperative complications (e.g., vascular perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm), serious adverse events, and device malfunctions. Secondary outcomes include technical failure rate, overall procedural time, pre-puncture setup time, mean catheterization time per target vessel, super-selective technique success rate, DSA fluoroscopy time, participant radiation dose, primary operator radiation dose, contrast agent volume and instrument performance evaluation. A key safety endpoint is the rate of new asymptomatic cerebral infarctions detected via postoperative brain MRI-diffusion-weighted imaging. As the RCT focusing on the YDHB-NS01 Ver 2.0 system, the ERASE trial addresses critical unmet needs in neurointerventional practice and will generate high-quality evidence for robotic-assisted cerebral angiography. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07182188. TRIAL REGISTRATION DATE: 2025-09-18.

articles.title: Recommendations on key aspects of migraine prevention: A Delphi consensus among experts of the headache study group of the Spanish society of neurology (GECSEN).
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: This study presents a Delphi consensus developed by the Headache Study Group of the Spanish Society of Neurology (GECSEN) to establish updated recommendations on key aspects of preventive migraine management. Given the high global burden of migraine and the emergence of novel preventive therapies-particularly OnabotulinumtoxinA and Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeted treatments-there is a need to redefine therapeutic goals and optimize clinical decision-making. A nine-member Steering Committee defined 14 statements addressing five domains: candidate patient selection, therapeutic goals, treatment discontinuation, switching strategies, and combination therapy. A systematized literature review (171 selected publications) informed statement development. Eighty-eight migraine specialists participated in the first Delphi round and 48 in the second. Consensus was determined using the RAND/UCLA appropriateness method. Agreement was achieved for all 14 recommendations after two voting rounds. Preventive therapy is recommended in patients with ≥ 4 monthly migraine or moderate-to-severe headache days and relevant quality-of-life impairment. The ideal therapeutic goal is migraine freedom or minimization of attack frequency and intensity with improved quality of life. Optimal control is defined as < 4 monthly moderateto-severe headache days within three months. Treatment should generally be maintained for at least 12 months after achieving optimal control. Switching or combining preventive therapies-including CGRP monoclonal antibodies, gepants, and OnabotulinumtoxinA-may be considered in insufficient responders. This consensus proposes a treat-to-target strategy centered on patient-reported outcomes and residual disease burden, aiming to standardize preventive migraine care and improve long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of laser-assisted and conventional techniques in vital pulp therapy of permanent teeth: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical and radiographic outcomes.
articles.abstract: To determine the difference between conventional and laser-assisted vital pulp therapy (VPT) on clinical and radiographic outcomes for permanent teeth, and to identify if there is a difference according to direct pulp capping versus pulpotomy. We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov to 15 October 2025. We included randomised controlled trials comparing laser-assisted and conventional VPT for permanent teeth with a minimum of six months follow-up. We assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 and certainty using GRADE. The outcome of interest was assessed using a dichotomous variable. We performed the analysis using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Eight studies were included, with 609 teeth randomised and 526 analysed. Overall success was higher with lasers than control (risk ratio 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.18, p = 0.01, I² = 34%). The effect size was 1.26 (95% CI 1.01-1.58) for direct pulp capping and 1.06 (95% CI 1.01-1.12) for pulpotomy, and the test for subgroup differences was not significant (p = 0.15). The effect size was 1.13 (95% CI 0.99-1.29) for mature teeth and 1.08 (95% CI 1.01-1.16) for immature teeth. Pain data from two trials could not be pooled. There was a minor improvement for laser-assisted VPT in permanent teeth when compared to the control. The evidence was limited by risk of bias and certainty was assessed as low to very low for all outcomes. Large, well-constructed randomised controlled trials with standardised parameters of the laser are required before clinical guidance is provided.

articles.title: Cross sectional analysis of major viral diseases in shrimp farms of Kerala, India.
articles.abstract: Effective disease surveillance is crucial for predicting, identifying, and managing disease outbreaks in shrimp aquaculture. A cross-sectional study was conducted to identify the occurrence of major viral diseases and assess the risk factors associated with disease in shrimp farms of Kerala, India. A two-stage random sampling was employed involving the selection of 31 shrimp farms in the first stage and 23 individual shrimp per farm in the second stage. The surveillance was carried out from October 2023- October 2024, targeting major DNA viruses: White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV), Monodon Baculovirus (MBV), Decapod penstylhamaparvovirus 1(PstDV1), Decapod hepanhamaparvovirus 1 (DHPV), Decapod Iridescent Virus 1 (DIV1) and RNA viruses: Infectious Myonecrosis Virus (IMNV), Laem-Singh virus (LSNV), Taura Syndrome Virus (TSV), Yellow Head Virus Genotype 1 (YHV-1), Covert Mortality Nodavirus (CMNV) by using PCR and histopathological techniques. Among the 31 shrimp farms surveyed, WSSV was detected in 7 farms (22.6% prevalence), while all other viral pathogens tested negative. Histopathological examination revealed characteristic Cowdry type A and basophilic inclusion bodies in the stomach, gills, and pleopods consistent with WSSV infection. Risk factor analysis using Epi Info™ 7.2.6 identified WSSV infection was significantly associated with culture duration exceeding 35 days, ammonia concentration >0.5mg/L, stocking densities >25 shrimps/m2 and Litopenaeus vannamei as the cultured species. In contrast, culture duration of 0-35 days, ammonia concentration < 0.5mg/l, and lower stocking density were associated with a decrease in WSSV occurrence. The relatively low prevalence may be attributed to the reduction in shrimp farming activity in Kerala, as most farms operated only a single production cycle per year. This surveillance study provides valuable insights into the epidemiological evidence of shrimp viral diseases in Kerala and the associated risk factors, thereby providing a foundation for developing improved prevention and control strategies for sustainable shrimp aquaculture.

articles.title: Status epilepticus in mTORopathies: a systematic review of clinical features, management, and outcomes.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway plays a critical role in epileptogenesis; however, its involvement in human status epilepticus (SE) remains poorly understood. mTORopathies, genetic disorders defined by mutations that disrupt mTOR signaling, frequently manifest severe neurological complications, among which SE is particularly consequential.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science was conducted for studies on mTORopathies and SE. We analyzed the clinical presentation, treatment strategies, and outcomes of all cases.

RESULTS: Eight hundred ninety-seven records were initially identified, of which 31 were included in this review. SE may manifest in different mTORopathies. SE often presents early, recurs frequently, and can be catastrophic. Refractory SE (RSE) predominantly affects neonates and infants and frequently occurs in the context of MCD. SE can be terminated with multiple anti-seizure medications (ASMs), alone or in combination with mTOR inhibitors. However, managing RSE is challenging. Current treatment strategies include novel ASMs, anesthetics, mTOR inhibitors, the ketogenic diet, immunotherapy, epilepsy surgery, and neuromodulation. A multifaceted approach is preferred to achieve seizure control and to improve developmental outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: SE remains a significant clinical challenge in patients with mTORopathies. mTOR signaling may contribute to the pathogenesis of SE and could represent a potential therapeutic target. Further investigation in large cohort studies is needed to clarify the role of mTOR signaling in SE and to evaluate the effects of mTOR inhibitors and immunotherapies on outcomes in patients with SE/RSE.

articles.title: Identification of associative factors for recurrent respiratory tract infection using machine learning models in preschoolers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Childhood recurrent respiratory tract infection (RRTI) poses a significant global public health burden. This study aimed to identify factors associated with RRTI in preschool children using machine learning (ML) and to develop a web-based tool for estimating individualized RRTI probabilities.

METHODS: Two cross-sectional surveys using stratified cluster sampling were conducted in 2020 and 2025. RRTI was diagnosed according to the national criteria issued by the Chinese Medical Association and China Association of Chinese Medicine. Questionnaire data covering demographic characteristics, fetal/neonatal history, and lifestyle factors were collected.

RESULTS: Total 15,075 eligible records from two surveys were included, reporting an RRTI prevalence of 14.55%. Ten ML models were trained on 29 candidate variables. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model outperformed the others, yielding an area under the curve of 0.733. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration as the top three associative variables for childhood RRTI. Forward feature selection was applied to derive a parsimonious nine-variable predictive set, which was subsequently deployed as an online application ( https://cipchina.streamlit.app/ ).

CONCLUSIONS: In a large, population-based cohort of preschool children, three factors (sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration) associated with RRTI were consistently identified across multiple high-performing ML models.

IMPACT: This study identified key lifestyle-related factors associated with recurrent respiratory tract infection in preschool children. Ten machine learning models were applied to analyze 29 variables from 15,075 Chinese preschoolers, with further importance interpreted via the SHapley Additive exPlanations. Sleep duration emerged as the primary lifestyle-related factor associated with childhood recurrent respiratory tract infection, followed by child's age and screen duration.

articles.title: Secondary Central Nervous System Lymphoma with Initial Spinal Cord Involvement: Report of One Case.
articles.journal: Zhongguo yi xue ke xue yuan xue bao. Acta Academiae Medicinae Sinicae
articles.abstract: Secondary central nervous system lymphoma (SCNSL) develops in approximately 5% of patients with lymphoma and is characterized by central nervous system involvement at the initial diagnosis or relapse of systemic lymphoma.It most commonly affects the brain parenchyma and leptomeninges,followed by the cranial nerves and nerve roots,whereas spinal cord involvement is rare,making early diagnosis challenging.We reported a case of SCNSL that initially presented with spinal cord involvement.MRI revealed multifocal signal abnormalities in the cervical and lumbar spinal cord,while whole-body PET/CT demonstrated increased radiotracer uptake in multiple organs,including the spinal cord,liver,and kidney.The diagnosis was ultimately confirmed through kidney and liver biopsies followed by histopathological examination.We further compared SCNSL with primary central nervous system lymphoma with respect to MRI findings,whole-body PET/CT findings,and cerebrospinal fluid interleukin-10 levels,with the aim of improving clinicians' recognition of this rare disease and facilitating early diagnosis.

articles.title: Long-Term Follow-up of Cerebrospinal Fluid Leakage with Intracranial Infection after Lumbar Surgery: Reportof One Case and Literature Review.
articles.journal: Zhongguo yi xue ke xue yuan xue bao. Acta Academiae Medicinae Sinicae
articles.abstract: Intracranial infection is a rare and extremely serious complication of spinal surgery,with a low incidence of 0.18%.This paper reports a case of cerebrospinal fluid leakage with intracranial infection of Enterococcus faecium after lumbar surgery,and reviews the related literature.It summarizes and analyzes the diagnosis and treatment of patients with intracranial infection after spinal surgery,aiming to improve the prevention,diagnosis,and treatment of this rare complication.

articles.title: Pharmacologic Management of Pediatric Paroxysmal Sympathetic Hyperactivity in North America.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe pharmacological management approaches to pediatric paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) among North American pediatric attending physicians.

PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional web-based survey of pediatric attending physicians conducted from March to August 2023. The questionnaire examined PSH medication utilization and preferences, subspecialty responsibilities for managing PSH, and the influence of patient age on medication selection. Descriptive statistics summarize PSH medication utilization and rank-order preferences. Chi-square analyses examined relationships between physician specialty and medication selection.

RESULTS: Among 295 respondents (33% palliative care, 23% neurology, 18% complex care, 17% physiatry), considerable heterogeneity in PSH pharmacotherapy approaches was observed. The most used abortive PSH medications were gamma-aminobutyric acid A (GABA-A) agonists (86%), alpha-2 agonists (79%), and opioids (49%). Leading preventive PSH medications included alpha-2 agonists (90%), gabapentinoids (89%), and beta-blockers (66%). Top-ranked medications for abortive management were alpha-2 agonists, GABA-A agonists, and non-opioid analgesics; and gabapentinoids, alpha-2 agonists, and beta-blockers for preventive management. While physiatrists and neurologists were most frequently identified as primary managers of PSH at participants' home institutions, several other specialties (including multidisciplinary models) were reported as well. We observed significant differences in utilization of alpha-2 agonists, opioids, dopamine agonists, and beta-blockers across subspecialties (all P < .05). Patient age influenced medication selection among 41% of our sample.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic management of pediatric PSH currently lacks clinical consensus and varies significantly based on physician subspecialty. Our findings underscore the need for focused research efforts to identify optimal treatment strategies and develop standardized and evidence-based management guidelines.

articles.title: Adult Care in a Pediatric Hospital: Patterns and Implications of an Internal Medicine Consult Service at a Children's Hospital.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adults with childhood-onset conditions are increasingly admitted to children's hospitals, yet many pediatric systems lack the infrastructure and expertise to manage adult-related medical needs. One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children's hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive cohort study was performed of admitted patients with a Hospital Medicine Adult Care (HMAC) service consult from July 2014 through June 2023.

RESULTS: Annual adult admissions increased over the study period, from 7.4% to 10.2% of all admissions. HMAC consulted on 1666 admissions for 1008 unique patients (median age, 27 years [range, 14-71 years]). The most frequent reasons for consult were venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (33.7%), age older than 25 years (21.2%), transition of care (7.6%), and hypertension (7.6%). HMAC physicians addressed a mean of 5.5 diagnoses per encounter. Patients averaged 3.6 admissions (range, 1-22) and 4.9 comorbidities (range, 0-21) each. The most common comorbidities were technology dependence (47%), solid tumor malignancy (22.5%), genetic conditions (20.2%), epilepsy (19.7%), congenital heart disease (17.4%), and cerebral palsy (15.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: Adult consult services in children's hospitals support a medically complex population with diverse childhood-onset and adult conditions and function as longitudinal clinical partners. These findings support the role of adult medicine expertise in children's hospitals to help recognize and manage adult-specific care needs and transitions.

articles.title: Social Media Asthma Education to Reduce Pediatric Health Care Use: A Bayesian Randomized Control Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Traditional pediatric asthma education is often fragmented and time limited. Social media may provide a more sustained platform for education. We hypothesized that social media-based education (SME) about asthma would reduce health care use the year after asthma hospitalization.

METHODS: In a 2-center Bayesian randomized trial, caregivers of patients aged 3 to 17 years hospitalized for asthma were randomly assigned to social media plus usual care or usual care alone, stratified by age (3-11 vs 12-17 years) and center. The SME group received at least weekly educational post via Facebook and Instagram. The primary outcome was total number of treatment days in a medical setting within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included treatment days across different settings, time to emergency department (ED) revisit or hospital readmission, missed school days, and patient satisfaction. Analyses were conducted using Bayesian generalized linear models with a neutral prior.

RESULTS: Two hundred participants were enrolled. Compared with usual care, SME had a 93% probability of reduced total treatment days (relative risk [RR] 0.80; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.59-1.07) and a 96% probability of decreased unplanned treatment days (RR 0.67; 95% CrI, 0.43-1.05). Mean time to ED revisit was 186 days in controls vs 225 days in the SME arm, with a 92% probability of reduction. Social media participants had longer time to readmission (293 vs 218 days; 81% probability of reduction) and greater satisfaction with education (73% vs 36%) than controls.

CONCLUSIONS: SME was well accepted and likely reduced health care use and delayed posthospitalization ED visits and readmissions compared with usual care.

articles.title: 2025 Annual Australian Measles and Rubella Genotyping Surveillance Program Report.
articles.abstract: Molecular characterisation is a critical component of Australia's measles and rubella surveillance systems, supporting outbreak investigations, identifying sources of infection, and providing evidence for the continued maintenance of Australia's measles and rubella elimination status. This annual report summarises measles and rubella molecular epidemiology in Australia during 2025 and evaluates the utility of whole genome sequencing (WGS) for measles surveillance. In 2025, there were 181 confirmed measles cases notified in Australia, representing a 217.5% increase on the number notified in 2024. Measles virus genotypes B3 and D8 were detected, together with 21 vaccine-associated genotype A cases. Genotype B3 predominated during the first half of the year and was largely associated with importations from Vietnam, whereas genotype D8 predominated during the second half of the year and was primarily associated with importations from Indonesia. Thirty-one epidemiologically confirmed outbreaks were identified, comprising 13 genotype B3 outbreaks and 17 genotype D8 outbreaks. The discriminatory power and concordance with epidemiological data in the context of outbreak investigations was substantially greater for WGS data than for conventional N450-based genotyping. Viruses sharing the same N450-based distinct sequence identifier (DSid) differed by up to 33 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for genotype B3 and 36 SNPs for genotype D8, whereas genomes obtained from epidemiologically linked cases differed by a maximum of four SNPs. Despite increased national case numbers in 2025, available molecular and epidemiological evidence indicated that cases were associated with importations or import-related transmission events, with no evidence of sustained endemic measles transmission. Rubella activity remained extremely low, with no rubella virus detections identified among 157 specimens tested by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and only two notified cases nationally, neither of which had material available for genotyping. These findings support the continued absence of endemic measles and rubella transmission in Australia and highlight the value of WGS for enhancing measles surveillance and outbreak investigations.

articles.title: National position statement: diagnosis and treatment of tuberculosis infection.
articles.abstract: This updated National position statement replaces the National Position Statement for the Management of Latent Tuberculosis Infection (2017) and incorporates current evidence and guidance for the diagnosis and treatment of tuberculosis infection (TBI) in Australia. It provides nationally consistent recommendations on the diagnosis, risk assessment and management of TBI , including updating terminology, testing approaches, priority populations for screening and treatment, and recommended preventive treatment options.

articles.title: Childhood insulinoma after years of recurrent hypoglycemia: the role of GLP-1 receptor imaging.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To highlight the diagnostic challenges of childhood insulinoma and the complementary role of GLP-1 receptor-targeted imaging in localizing a small pancreatic lesion.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 12-year-old boy had a history of recurrent episodes suggestive of hypoglycemia reportedly beginning at approximately 4 years of age, with reported glucose concentrations as low as 15-20 mg/dL and associated night sweats. Diagnostic evaluation was fragmented over several years due to frequent family relocations. During a critical sample, plasma glucose was 37 mg/dL, with insulin 105.2 µIU/mL and C-peptide 5.48 ng/mL, supporting endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. MRI demonstrated a small lesion in the pancreatic body. 68Ga-Exendin-4 PET/CT demonstrated focal GLP-1 receptor-targeted uptake corresponding to the pancreatic lesion, with a delayed SUVmax of 9.1. The patient underwent open surgical enucleation. Histopathology demonstrated a 1.7-cm well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, WHO Grade 1, with a Ki-67 index of 1 %, negative margins, and no necrosis, lymphovascular, or perineural invasion. Postoperatively, glucose concentrations remained normal.

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent or unexplained hypoglycemia in children warrants consideration of insulinoma when endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia is demonstrated. In this case, GLP-1 receptor-targeted imaging provided complementary functional localization alongside MRI and supported focused curative surgery.

articles.title: UDR-PREDICT: a malignancy prediction model for rapid diagnostic units.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hospital rapid diagnostic units (RDUs) assess outpatients with suspected serious disease, yet no validated tool estimates malignancy risk at the first RDU visit. We developed and internally validated UDR-PREDICT, a logistic prediction model with a derived integer score.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained registry of first RDU visits (2022-2025) in a Spanish tertiary hospital. The outcome was a final diagnosis of solid or haematologic malignancy. Candidate predictors available at referral were selected by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), refitted by logistic regression and shrunk. An integer score was derived with the Framingham points method. Both were validated by bootstrapping the full procedure and by internal-external cross-validation across calendar periods; 2025 served as an exploratory temporal test.

RESULTS: Of 975 analysable patients, 147 (15.1 %) had malignancy. The model retained age, sex, abdominal mass, lymphadenopathy, pulmonary nodule and bone lesions.
