Optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) was 0.719 for the model and 0.721 for the score (calibration slopes 0.857 and 0.859). Across periods the pooled AUC was 0.693 (95 % CI 0.641-0.741) and the pooled calibration slope 0.737 (0.550-0.924). In 2025 (19 events) the AUC was 0.731 (0.618-0.826). Predicted risk rose from 3.9 % at 0 points to 64.9 % at 14 points; a score ≥9 identified 9.9 % of patients, 48.5 % of whom had malignancy.

CONCLUSIONS: UDR-PREDICT showed modest discrimination and some overfitting. It may help order first-visit priorities but requires external validation and recalibration before clinical use.

articles.title: Genetic determinants of direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) response: evidence, limitations and barriers to clinical implementation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) offer predictable pharmacokinetics and simplified dosing compared with warfarin, yet clinically important inter-individual variability in drug exposure, efficacy, and safety persists. Pharmacogenomics can help explain this variability and advance precision anticoagulation.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on genetic determinants of the pharmacokinetics and clinical outcomes of dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban, identified by searching PubMed, Embase and Web of Science from inception to May 2026. Evidence from candidate-gene studies, genome-wide association studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses was synthesized, and the magnitude of reported genetic effects were compared with the non-genetic determinants of exposure. Variants in CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CES1, ABCB1, and ABCG2 have been investigated for their potential effects on DOAC disposition and response. CES1 variants, particularly rs2244613, rs8192935, and rs71647871, may influence dabigatran exposure, while transporter variants may affect absorption and elimination. CYP3A4/5 and ABCG2 variation has also been associated with altered rivaroxaban and apixaban pharmacokinetics. Evidence for edoxaban, including SLCO1B1 variation, remains limited.

EXPERT OPINION: Pharmacogenomics represents a promising component of individualized DOAC therapy, but routine clinical implementation is in progress. Prospective genotype-guided studies, validated polygenic and clinical-genetic scores, therapeutic concentration thresholds, and diverse multi‑ethnic validation are needed before pharmacogenomic testing can reliably inform DOAC selection and dosing.

articles.title: Importance of recognising faciobrachial dystonic seizures in LGI1 antibody autoimmune encephalitis.
Quantifying multi-lesion detection and localization in whole-body FDG PET/CT with a multimodal foundation model.
articles.abstract: Objective. To develop a three-dimensional AI framework for detecting and localizing multiple lesions in whole-body FDG PET/CT, and to evaluate whether a pretrained PET/CT multimodal foundation model can improve lesion detection performance compared with conventional training from scratch.Approach. The AutoPET cohort comprised 1014 studies divided into 700 training, 114 validation, and 200 subject-independent test studies. Lesion masks were converted into three-dimensional bounding boxes. We developed a one-stage 3D lesion detector using a PlainConvUNet backbone to extract multi-scale encoder-decoder features for lesion classification and box regression. To leverage foundation-model representations, the PlainConvUNet backbone was initialized with weights from our previously developed multi-center PET/CT multimodal foundation model, pretrained using masked autoencoding, and subsequently fine-tuned for lesion detection. Four configurations were compared: PET+CT trained from scratch, PET only, CT only, and PET+CT initialized from the pretrained PET/CT foundation model. Detection performance was evaluated using free-response receiver operating characteristic (FROC) and alternative FROC (AFROC) analyses, sensitivity at fixed false-positive (FP) rates, qualitative analysis, and lesion-size-stratified operating curves.Main results. Multimodal PET+CT consistently outperformed either modality alone across task-based detection metrics, demonstrating the complementary contributions of metabolic and anatomical information. Importantly, initialization from the pretrained PET/CT multimodal foundation model further enhanced lesion detection performance compared with training the same PET+CT detector from scratch, increasing absolute FROC sensitivity by 0.034-0.041 across the evaluated 1-4 FP-per-scan operating range and improving AFROC AUC by 0.028. Detection performance increased with lesion size, with small lesions remaining the most challenging. The separation between the pretrained and randomly initialized PET+CT configurations was more evident in the smaller-lesion strata, whereas their operating curves increasingly overlapped for larger lesions.Significance. This study provides a detection-centered, task-based characterization of multi-lesion analysis in whole-body PET/CT. Multimodal PET+CT improves lesion detection compared with either modality alone, lesion size is a major determinant of detection performance, and initialization from a pretrained PET/CT multimodal foundation model provides an additional performance improvement without modifying the downstream detector architecture.

articles.title: Assessing infection and inflammation in people with cystic fibrosis using their breath: a pilot longitudinal study.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators have revolutionized cystic fibrosis (CF) management, but airway infections and inflammation persist. This study evaluates longitudinal exhaled breath profiles and identifies volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that correlate with sputum bacterial load and neutrophil elastase (NE) levels during ivacaftor and/or antibiotic treatment. Eight people with CF (pwCF) with a heterozygous R117H CFTR mutation and chronic lung infection withP. aeruginosa(Pa) and/orS. aureus (Sa)were enrolled in a longitudinal study at St. Vincent's University Hospital in Dublin, Ireland. Breath samples and sputum samples were collected at multiple time points. Correlation analyses were performed between VOC abundances and bacterial load or NE levels. We observed temporal changes in breath profile across the eight subjects during the ivacaftor and/or antibiotic treatment. WithinPa-infected subjects, 54 VOCs showed consistent directional Pearson correlation and at least moderate repeated measures correlation (rmcorr) coefficient (rrm) with bacterial load, including the 12 VOCs previously reported asPa-associated markers. Similarly, withinSa-infected subjects, we identified eight VOCs that showed consistent directional correlation and at least moderaterrmwith bacterial load, including four previously reportedSa-associated markers. Additionally, we identified 7 exploratory VOC candidates that consistently correlated with changes in NE levels, each demonstrating agenerally weakrrmacross eight subjects. This study demonstrates that breath profiles of pwCF change over time during ivacaftor and/or antibiotic treatment. Identifying specific breath VOCs whose levels correlate withPaorSaCFU/ml, as well as NE levels, supports further evaluation of exhaled breath VOCs as non-invasive markers for monitoring airway infection and inflammation in pwCF.

articles.title: A Flexible Meal-Building Web Application for Food Is Medicine Programs: Development and Usability Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food Is Medicine (FIM) interventions are increasingly integrated into health care and community settings. Although FIM interventions show promise for improving diet and clinical outcomes, results have been mixed, and positive effects may attenuate over time. Digital nutrition and cooking mobile apps and web applications have emerged as part of FIM interventions and may help FIM participants apply nutrition education to develop meal-preparation skills. The GRACE (get a base, round with real produce and proteins, add aromatics, cook gently, and enhance with flavor to align with dietary guidance) Framework provides the foundation for integrating ways to create and adapt meals. The GRACE Kitchen progressive web application (PWA) prototype was designed to operationalize this framework.

OBJECTIVE: This study describes the development of the GRACE Framework, its translation into the GRACE Kitchen PWA prototype, and examines preliminary user feedback on the prototype.

METHODS: An iterative developmental design based on 2 separate pilots (Food Is Medicine Healing Together [FIM-HT] and Food Is Medicine for Black Breast Cancer Survivors [FIM-BCS]) was organized into 3 developmental stages. In stage 1, qualitative interviews (n=17) with participants with hypertension from a 12-week pilot FIM intervention (FIM-HT) were analyzed to identify facilitators and barriers to sustaining Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH)-aligned eating, including produce delivery and nutrition education. Themes elicited from the FIM-HT interviews informed the development of the GRACE Framework. In stage 2, the GRACE Framework was translated into the GRACE Kitchen prototype. In stage 3, breast cancer survivors (n=12) participated in an 8-week FIM pilot (FIM-BCS) and simultaneously underwent preliminary testing of GRACE Kitchen. User experiences were assessed using a modified Mobile App Usability Questionnaire and focus group data.

RESULTS: Across the 3 developmental stages, feedback from 29 participants contributed to the development of the GRACE Framework and the GRACE Kitchen prototype. During stage 1, initial conceptual ideas for the GRACE Framework were based on 3 themes identified in the FIM-HT interview data: Changes in Eating Behaviors, Challenges to Cooking, and the Maintenance of Healthy Cooking and Eating Behaviors. Participants emphasized finding new ways to incorporate vegetables, spices, and herbs; swapping in healthier ingredients; adapting recipes to their preferences; and navigating the challenges of meal preparation and cooking. In stage 2, this feedback informed the development of the GRACE Kitchen PWA. During PWA testing (stage 3), FIM-BCS participants (n=12) reported ease of use (2.70/4), satisfaction (2.67/4), and usefulness (2.71/4). The FIM-BCS participants also provided qualitative feedback indicating strong acceptability of GRACE Kitchen's guidance on making meals easier to prepare. However, they found the interface challenging to use and preferred a more mobile-friendly, easier-to-navigate approach.

CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary feedback suggests that GRACE Kitchen was perceived as moderately useful and highly acceptable, while also revealing important usability limitations. Although participants reported that the GRACE Framework was supportive, further evaluation is needed to determine whether GRACE Kitchen can help sustain dietary practices.

articles.title: A Potent Antifouling and Antimicrobial Wound Dressing to Accelerate Diabetic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are a severe and prevalent complication of diabetes, often resulting in high healthcare costs and an increased risk of amputation. Infection and insufficient angiogenesis are two primary factors that severely impede diabetic wound healing. In this study, we developed a potent antifouling and antimicrobial SBHA hydrogel incorporating zwitterionic and N-halamine moieties. The zwitterionic moieties effectively resist protein adsorption and bacterial adhesion while simultaneously promoting angiogenesis, thereby accelerating wound repair. Meanwhile, the N-halamine moieties exhibit excellent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, achieving a bactericidal efficacy of 99.999% within 5 min of contact. Importantly, in vivo studies demonstrate that SBHA hydrogels used as wound dressings significantly accelerate the healing of diabetic infected wounds in rats, reaching a healing rate of up to 93.3% on day 13 compared with the control group. This enhanced therapeutic outcome may be attributed to the ability of the SBHA dressing to prevent infection, promote angiogenesis, modulate macrophage polarization, upregulate the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, and suppress the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of SBHA hydrogels as advanced wound dressings and provide a promising strategy for diabetic wound healing.

articles.title: Exercise-induced lactylation in WDR41 initiates autophagy and improves fatty liver diseases.
articles.abstract: Excess lipid accumulation and a sedentary lifestyle are associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), but the causal mechanisms and preventive methods are not fully understood. Macroautophagy/autophagy is a lysosomal degradation pathway robustly induced by exercise and plays a key role in lipid metabolism. Understanding the mechanisms by which exercise activates autophagy and elicits metabolic benefits in the liver will provide important insights into the pathogenesis of MAFLD. Here, we discovered negative correlations between expression and lactylation of WDR41 (WD repeat domain 41) and pathogenesis of a series of human hepatic metabolic diseases. We found that WDR41 was a pro-autophagy protein that underwent lactylation in response to autophagy-inducing conditions, such as exercise. WDR41 was lactylated at lysine 319 (K319), a modification facilitated by LDHA (lactate dehydrogenase A) upon autophagy induction, and delactylated by SIRT2 (sirtuin 2). Lactylated WDR41 promoted autophagy initiation by directly interacting with the autophagy proteins ATG13 (autophagy related 13) and RB1CC1/FIP200 (RB1 inducible coiled-coil 1) and driving the ULK1 (unc-51 like autophagy activating kinase 1) complex assembly. Physiologically, WDR41 and WDR41K319 lactylation, were important for exercise-induced improvements in insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism against excess lipid accumulation in the liver. Thus, we demonstrated that WDR41 lactylation at K319 is an important regulatory mechanism by which exercise regulates autophagy and hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism.Abbreviations: AV: adeno-associated virus;
