articles.title: Cellular and molecular imaging of coronary atherosclerosis: clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Reversing initial gains realized in the 1990s-2010s, coronary artery disease rates are now increasing and represent the dominant cause of death in many parts of the world. In recent years, substantive advances in non-invasive and invasive structural-based imaging techniques that delineate atheroma burden and anatomical composition have increased understanding of the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis. Driven by advances in imaging agent and hardware technology, the burgeoning field of molecular imaging has enabled clinical visualization of molecules and cells that underpin atherosclerosis pathobiology. Integrating the molecular and anatomical measures of atherosclerosis has promoted a deeper understanding of disease progression, patient-specific risk, and the effects of atherosclerosis pharmacotherapeutics and devices. With the great recognition of the role of inflammation as a residual risk marker of adverse outcomes for coronary artery disease patients, cellular and molecular imaging of inflammation and other disease activities is positioned to usher in a new era of risk assessment and personalized medical and interventional therapeutics for atherosclerosis patients. Moreover, molecular imaging offers the potential for assessing the actions of interventions on atherogenic processes, validating effects in vivo, and possibly informing optimal dose selection and treatment duration. This review will present the state-of-the-art in coronary artery disease cellular and molecular imaging and provide a roadmap for near-term translational and clinical applications.

articles.title: Left ventricular geometry, brain architecture, and cognition: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cardiovascular (CV) diseases and dementia share common risk factors and often coexist in older adults. Understanding the CV-brain interaction is essential for tackling their interconnected burden. This study investigated the link between CV phenotypes, brain architecture, and cognition.

METHODS: Overall, 15 519 UK Biobank participants without neurodegenerative diseases or stroke (median age 64 years, 49% female) were analysed. Confirmatory factor analysis aggregated 18 CV magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) biomarkers into latent variables for left ventricular systolic function (gSyst), diastolic (gDiast) function, and geometry (gGeom); arterial compliance was measured by aortic distensibility (AoD). Multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with brain MRI phenotypes, including grey matter volume, white matter hyperintensities, MRI diffusion white matter microstructure, and hippocampal volume. Models were adjusted for age, body mass index, height, mean blood pressure, and CV risk factors. Exploratory mediation models evaluated whether hippocampal volume accounted for associations between CV phenotypes and cognition.

RESULTS: gGeom, reflecting greater myocardial mass, wall thickness, and ventricular volumes, showed the strongest association with hippocampal volume [β = 0.082 (0.048-0.117) in females; β = 0.039 (0.006-0.071) in males] and was the only CV phenotype associated with better cognition, including higher fluid intelligence and faster reaction time. Hippocampal volume significantly accounted for the positive relationship between gGeom and cognition across sexes. In contrast, gSyst, gDiast, and AoD demonstrated weaker and less consistent associations with brain structure and were unrelated to cognition.

CONCLUSIONS: Ventricular geometry emerged as the CV phenotype most strongly associated with brain architecture and cognition. Hippocampal volume may help explain this association, but further studies are needed to investigate causality.

articles.title: [Early effectiveness of patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks for hip revision in patients with Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects].
articles.journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the early clinical and radiographic outcomes of patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks for the reconstruction of Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects in hip revision.

METHODS: The clinical data of 17 patients (17 hips) with Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects undergoing revision after hip arthroplasty between January 2022 and January 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The cohort comprised 6 males and 11 females, with a mean age of 59.4 years (range, 37-80 years). Nine patients had Paprosky type ⅢA defects and 8 had type ⅢB defects, including 5 with pelvic discontinuity. All patients underwent acetabular side (9 cases) or both acetabular and femoral components (8 cases) reconstruction with patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks combined with revision acetabular cups. Harris hip score (HHS) and visual analogue scale (VAS) score were compared between preoperative and last follow-up. The position of radiographic hip center of rotation (rCOR), acetabular cup inclination and anteversion, osseointegration, and implant stability were evaluated by anteroposterior pelvic X-ray films and CT, and perioperative complications and re-revision were recorded.

RESULTS: The operation was successfully completed in all patients, with a mean operation time of 141.2 minutes (range, 80-280 minutes) and a mean intraoperative blood loss of 752.9 mL (range, 300-1 500 mL). All patients completed follow-up, with a mean duration of 22.1 months (range, 13-41 months). At last follow-up, the HHS score significantly increased from 37.0±5.8 to 87.9±3.0, while the VAS score significantly decreased from 6.0 (5.5, 7.0) to 0.0 (0.0, 1.0) (P<0.05). The horizontal rCOR distance on the operated side improved significantly when compared with the preoperative value (P<0.05) and did not differ significantly from that on the contralateral side (P>0.05). The vertical rCOR distance decreased significantly (P<0.05) but remained greater than that on the contralateral side (P<0.05). At last follow-up, all acetabular reconstructions remained radiographically stable, with an acetabular cup inclination of (41.87±4.38)° and an acetabular cup anteversion of (19.47±3.77)°. No intraoperative screw penetration through the inner pelvic cortex or neurovascular injury was recorded. No heterotopic ossification, clinically significant limb-length discrepancy, implant mismatch requiring additional adjustment or component replacement, tantalum blocks migration, screw loosening or breakage, or aseptic loosening was observed. Postoperative venous thrombosis occurred in 2 patients, both of whom improved following treatment. No other major complication was reported.

CONCLUSION: Patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks demonstrated favorable early clinical and radiographic outcomes in the reconstruction of Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects, with improvements in hip function, pain relief, radiographic stability, and restoration of the hip center of rotation. Larger multicenter and random clinical trials with longer follow-up are warranted to establish long-term outcomes and potential advantages over alternative reconstruction techniques.

articles.title: [Effect of sequential multi-dose tranexamic acid administration on perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty and its safety].
articles.journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups. Placebo control group (group A): received 100 mL of normal saline intravenously at 30 minutes before incision (after anesthesia induction); the same dose was repeated every 5 hours for a total of 3 administrations. Single-dose control group (group B): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, followed by 100 mL of normal saline every 5 hours for a total of 2 additional doses. Sequential multi-dose group (group C): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, with an additional 1.0 g of TXA administered intravenously at 5 hours and 10 hours postoperatively, for a total dose of 3.0 g. A total of 120 patients met the selection criteria and were included in the study. After excluding lost-to-follow-up and withdrawn patients, 39 cases in group A, 37 in group B, and 38 in group C were included in the final analysis. There was no significant difference between groups (P>0.05) in age, gender, height, body weight, body mass index, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes), and preoperative hematocrit (HCT), hemoglobin, D-dimer (D-D), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. The primary outcome was total blood loss (TBL). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative blood loss (IBL), postoperative blood loss (PBL), drain removal time (DRT), HCT, D-D, IL-6, CRP, allogeneic blood transfusion rate, and incidence of complications.

RESULTS: Blood loss assessment: TBL, PBL, DRT, postoperative decline in HCT, and the allogeneic blood transfusion rate were all the lowest in group C, followed by group B, and the highest in group A, with significant differences between groups (P<0.05). The IBL was significantly lower in groups B and C than in group A (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference between groups B and C (P>0.05). Changes in inflammatory indicators: the levels of D-D and IL-6 in 3 groups reached peak at 1 day, the level of CRP reached peak at 3 days, and both decreased at 5 days, but still remained higher than preoperative levels, with significant differences (P<0.05). At different time points, the levels of D-D, IL-6, and CRP were significant lower in group C than in groups A and B (P<0.05), and in group B than in group A (P<0.05). Safety evaluation: During the 30-day postoperative follow-up, no deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, incisional infection, incisional hematoma, or TXA-related allergic reaction occurred in 3 groups.

CONCLUSION: Sequential multi-dose TXA administration effectively reduces perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door LMP, suppresses postoperative hyperfibrinolysis and inflammatory response, shortens drainage duration, and does not increase the risk of thromboembolic events. This regimen represents a safe and effective optimization strategy for perioperative blood management in LMP.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on clinical trials of bilayer artificial dermis].
authors: Writing Group For Expert Consensus On Clinical Trials Of Bilayer Artificial Dermis
articles.journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
articles.abstract: Bilayer artificial dermis is an important tissue-engineered medical device for repairing and reconstructing dermal defects, and multicenter clinical trials are essential for evaluating the efficacy and safety of these products. However, a unified clinical trial evaluation system is currently absent. Inconsistent implementation standards in key aspects, including follow-up time points for skin graft survival rate and scar assessment, impede cross-center data comparison and reduce the scientific rigor and normativity of clinical trials. This consensus was developed by the modified Delphi method. Based on systematically collected clinical trial literature on bilayer artificial dermis and relevant domestic and international guidelines and expert consensus on wound repair, the initial draft was produced. Two rounds of expert questionnaires together with one expert seminar were implemented for statement argumentation, revision and voting. Consensus was achieved with an agreement rate ≥85%, classified as strong consensus (95.0%-100%), general consensus (90.0%-94.9%), and moderate consensus (85.0%-89.9%). This expert consensus was developed through multidisciplinary expert deliberations based on evidence-based medicine, focusing on key trial contents such as overall trial design, primary and secondary efficacy endpoints, safety evaluation indices, and study duration. The consensus aims to unify clinical trial evaluation criteria for bilayer artificial dermal repair materials used in dermal defect repair and reconstruction, guide standardized trial practice for analogous products, and provide a scientific reference for the research, development, and translational application of such innovative medical devices in China.

articles.title: Associations of heat with kidney-related mortality and the role of humidity: a multi-country study in 10 countries.
authors: de Sousa Zanotti Stagliorio Coelho M
articles.abstract: Although heat and humidity can affect kidney health, global evidence on the impact of heat on kidney-related mortality is sparse, and humidity's modifying role remains unquantified. This study aimed to examine the association between heat, humidity, and kidney-related mortality in 128 locations across 10 countries. To estimate the association between summer temperature and kidney-related mortality, a case time-series design was applied using a distributed lag nonlinear model with 10 lag days. Effect modification by humidity was assessed by adding an interaction term between temperature and humidity in the model. We further examined the association in three climate regions stratified by clustering method. The relative risk (RR) of total kidney disease-, acute kidney injury-, and chronic kidney disease-related mortality at the 99th (30.6℃) versus 75th (26.5℃) percentile of summer temperature was 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.04, 1.11), 1.13 (1.06, 1.21), and 1.01 (0.96, 1.07), respectively. The heat-mortality risk was more evident at high humidity than at low humidity: RR (95% CI) of total kidney disease at the 99th versus 75th percentile temperature was 1.10 (1.06, 1.14) and 1.05 (0.99, 1.11) at high and low humidity, respectively. The difference in RR between low and high humidity widened with increasing temperature, though CIs overlapped considerably. The suggestion of effect modification by humidity was more pronounced in cool-dry and humid tropical climate regions, but absent in the humid mid-latitude region. These findings suggest the need for region-specific preparedness against potential increase in kidney deaths in a future with rising temperature and humidity levels.

articles.title: Single-Cell Profiling Reveals an Aging-Enriched TLF⁺CD209hi Resident Macrophage State and Candidate Profibrotic Macrophage-Fibroblast Interactions in the Aging Heart.
articles.abstract: Cardiac aging is characterized by diastolic dysfunction, interstitial fibrosis, and increased risk of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), yet how macrophage heterogeneity, senescence, and intercellular signaling converge during physiological aging remains unclear. We integrated echocardiography, histology, immunostaining, flow cytometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing of sorted CD45+ cells from young and aged C57BL/6J mouse hearts, alongside human cardiac immunostaining. Aged mice developed diastolic dysfunction, ventricular remodeling, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and interstitial fibrosis, accompanied by immune-cell expansion. Exploratory single-cell transcriptomic analysis of pooled young and aged cardiac immune-cell libraries highlighted macrophages as a prominently remodeled immune population and identified an aging-enriched TLF⁺ (expressing Timd4 and/or Lyve1 and/or Folr2) CD209hi state within the tissue-resident macrophage compartment. Aged macrophages displayed increased senescence-associated secretory phenotype-related transcriptional activity, pro-inflammatory and profibrotic programs, and subset-specific metabolic and regulatory transcriptional programs. MHC-II+ macrophages showed a glycolytic inflammatory state, whereas TLF+CD209hi macrophages exhibited profibrotic programs enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling, epidermal growth factor family signaling, and IL-10-associated communication. Cell-cell communication and flow cytometry nominated HB-EGF/AREG-EGFR and IL-10-associated PDGF-A/PDGFRα signaling as candidate macrophage-fibroblast profibrotic circuits. In primary adult mouse cardiac fibroblasts, HB-EGF and PDGF-AA increased selected fibrosis-associated markers and EGFR/ERK or PDGFRα/ERK phosphorylation, respectively; pharmacological inhibition attenuated some responses. These findings link macrophage senescence-associated remodeling and an aging-enriched TLF⁺CD209hi state to fibrosis-associated features and nominate EGF-family ligands and IL-10-associated PDGF-A/PDGFRα signaling as candidate contributors to fibroblast activation and myocardial fibrosis during physiological cardiac aging. However, their causal roles in vivo remain to be established by targeted genetic or pharmacologic perturbation.

articles.title: Sesamin Ameliorates Insulin Resistance in Association With Gut Microbiota Remodeling and ICA-AhR-GLP-1 Signaling in Diabetic Mice.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with insulin resistance and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Here, we identified a microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde (ICA)-AhR-GLP-1 pathway that contributes to the glucose-lowering effect of sesamin (Ses), a major sesame lignan. In db/db mice, Ses improved hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, while remodeling the gut microbiota and enriching Ligilactobacillus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from Ses-treated donors partially transferred these metabolic benefits. Integrated bacterial isolation, Ses-based fermentation, fecal metabolomics, and clinical LC-MS/MS analysis identified ICA as a Ses-responsive microbiota-associated metabolite. Serum ICA levels were reduced in newly diagnosed patients with T2DM and negatively correlated with FBG, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR. Oral ICA reproduced key metabolic effects of Ses and enhanced intestinal Gcg expression and GLP-1 production. Mechanistically, ICA bound to AhR, promoted AhR nuclear translocation, increased AhR occupancy at the XRE-containing region of the Gcg promoter, and stimulated GLP-1 secretion in STC-1 cells and intestinal organoids. AhR inhibition reduced Ses-induced GLP-1 production and partially attenuated its metabolic effects, whereas acute GLP-1R blockade blunted Ses- and ICA-induced improvements in glucose tolerance and early insulin secretion. Together, these findings support a model in which Ses improves glucose homeostasis in association with gut microbiota remodeling and engagement of an ICA-AhR-GLP-1 pathway.

articles.title: Discovery of an NCoA4 Ligand That Suppresses Ferroptosis and Attenuates Kidney Injury by Limiting Ferritinophagy-Mediated Iron Release.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is increasingly recognized as a key driver of renal tubular injury and kidney disease progression. Here, screening a focused library of nitrogen-containing heterocycles identifies benzo[d]imidazo[1,2-a]imidazoles as a selective ferroptosis-inhibitory chemotype, with little or no protection against apoptosis, necrosis, cuproptosis, parthanatos, necroptosis, or pyroptosis. Structure-activity relationship analysis of 40 derivatives yields X27, which inhibits RSL3-induced ferroptosis in HT-1080 and renal tubular epithelial HK-2 cells with EC50 values of 0.13 and 0.19 µM, respectively, without detectable radical-scavenging or iron-chelating activity. Mechanistically, X27 binds the NCoA4383-522 fragment with a KD of 0.28 µM, suppresses ferritin degradation and labile iron accumulation, and attenuates lipid peroxidation. An activity-retaining photoaffinity probe, X31, enriches endogenous nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCoA4), while LC-MS/MS localizes probe modification to a peptide spanning Asp440-Lys452, defining a putative small-molecule interaction region. In mice, X27 attenuates cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury and unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced renal injury and fibrosis. Together, these findings expand the chemical space of NCoA4 ligands, provide peptide-level insight into small-molecule recognition by NCoA4, and establish ferritinophagic iron mobilization as a chemically tractable node for controlling renal injury.

articles.title: Defeating Multidrug-Resistant ESKAPEE Pathogens With Polymer Nanomaterials.
articles.abstract: The clinical efficacy of antibiotics has progressively declined over the past decades as a consequence of the global spread of antimicrobial resistance, a phenomenon that is particularly pronounced among the so-called ESKAPEE pathogens: Enterococcus species, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter species, and Escherichia coli. Collectively, these bacteria are responsible for more than 50% of infection-related deaths worldwide, and multidrug-resistance is highly prevalent among them. This alarming trend poses a critical threat to global public health and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. One such approach involves the use of polymers as drug delivery systems for both conventional antibiotics and novel antimicrobial compounds, in the form of nanoparticles or polymer prodrugs, to circumvent resistance mechanisms. Other promising strategies are polycations with intrinsic antibacterial activity that act through mechanisms not yet widely exploited and polymers exerting photodynamic and photothermal effects. In this review, we summarize and discuss the current evidence for the efficacy of polymer-based strategies against drug-resistant ESKAPEE infections.

articles.title: GhILL8 Interacts With GhREF to Coordinate Jasmonate-Auxin Signalling and Positively Regulate Cotton Defense Against Verticillium Wilt.
articles.abstract: Auxin homoeostasis is a critical determinant of plant growth and environmental adaptation, yet its precise role and regulatory mechanisms in Verticillium wilt resistance remain largely unexplored. Here, we systematically characterized the IAA amidohydrolase (ILL) gene family across cotton species and identified GhILL8, a gene strongly induced by Verticillium dahliae infection and jasmonic acid (JA) defense-related signalling molecules. Functional dissection through virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) revealed that GhILL8 knockdown severely compromises cotton resistance to V. dahliae, as evidenced by elevated disease indices, exacerbated vascular browning, and significantly increased fungal colonization. Notably, the early transient burst of free indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) observed in wild-type plants at 1 h post-inoculation, a hallmark of pattern-triggered immunity was completely abolished in GhILL8-silenced plants, correlating with accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and extensive cell death. RNA-Seq data analysis further revealed that GhILL8 positively regulates cotton resistance to V. dahliae by modulating both JA and auxin (IAA) signalling pathways. Conversely, heterologous overexpression of GhILL8 in Arabidopsis and tobacco markedly enhanced tolerance to V. dahliae, underscoring its evolutionarily conserved positive role in plant immunity. Mechanistically, yeast two-hybrid and luciferase complementation imaging assays demonstrated that GhILL8 physically interacts with the rubber elongation factor GhREF. Loss of GhREF phenocopied GhILL8 silencing, impairing defense gene activation and aggravating vascular wilt symptoms. Collectively, our findings establish GhILL8 as a pivotal metabolic rheostat that calibrates the free auxin pool during early fungal infection and uncover a previously unrecognized GhILL8-GhREF module that orchestrates JA and IAA signalling crosstalk to fine-tune crop immunity. This work provides new mechanistic insights and valuable genetic resources for breeding Verticillium wilt-resistant cotton cultivars.

articles.title: Sex-Based Differences in Procedural Success and One-Year-Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding sex-related differences in outcomes and procedural characteristics of percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion (CTO-PCI) remains limited, particularly in Japanese populations.

AIMS: This study investigated sex-based differences in procedural success, complications, and 1-year clinical outcomes in patients undergoing CTO-PCI and examined the clinical implications of sex-specific risk factors.

METHODS: A total of 11,147 patients who underwent CTO-PCI between January 2014 and December 2022 were analyzed from the Japanese CTO-PCI expert registry. Baseline clinical, angiographic, and procedural characteristics were compared between women and men. Study endpoints included technical success, in-hospital procedural complications, and 1-year major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and stroke. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of procedural failure, and Cox proportional hazards models identified predictors of 1-year MACCE.

RESULTS: Among 11,147 patients, 1,579 were women (14%) and 9,568 were men (86%). Women were older, had a lower body mass index, and more frequently had heart failure and chronic kidney disease, whereas men had higher rates of smoking, prior myocardial infarction, and reduced left ventricular systolic function. Women exhibited significantly lower procedural success rates and higher incidences of procedural complications. Female sex was independently associated with procedural failure. In women, older age, hemodialysis, and procedural failure were independently associated with an increased risk of 1-year MACCE.

CONCLUSION: Clinically significant sex-based differences exist in procedural success, complication rates, and determinants of adverse outcomes after CTO-PCI. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating sex-specific factors when selecting patients and formulating procedural strategies.

CONDENSED ABSTRACT: Sex-based differences in outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) remain controversial, and data from Japanese populations are lacking. Using a large Japanese multicenter registry, we examined sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics, procedural success, complications, and 1-year major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). Women undergoing CTO-PCI were older and had a higher burden of comorbidities, including heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Procedural success rates were significantly lower and complication rates were higher in women. Importantly, predictors of 1-year MACCE differed between women and men, highlighting the need for sex-specific considerations when considering the procedural strategies for CTO-PCI.

articles.title: Twelve-Year Follow-Up Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Coronary Chronic Total Occlusion.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over decades of advancement, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) has achieved high success rates and acceptable safety outcomes. However, the survival benefits of CTO-PCI are still debated.

AIMS: To understand the clinical benefit of CTO-PCI better, we present the 12-year follow-up results of a prospective CTO registry study, with the aim of describing the clinical course according to patients' risk characteristics.

METHODS: Between March 2003 and February 2015, 1219 consecutive patients with CTO of native coronary vessels requiring PCI were enrolled. Among them, CTO-PCI was successful in 1047 patients (85.9%). The primary outcome of this study was all-cause death at maximum available follow-up between patients with successful and failed CTO recanalization.

RESULTS: During the median follow-up of 12.1 years, all-cause death was not significant difference between the CTO-PCI success group and the CTO-PCI failure group (15.6% vs. 18.0% at 12 years, p = 0.69). In multivariable analysis for the primary outcome, the failure of CTO-PCI was not an independent risk factor for all-cause death (adjusted hazard ratio 0.842; p = 0.302) or myocardial infarction (adjusted hazard ratio 0.667; p = 0.345). Independent predictors of all-cause death included diabetes, previous history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease.

CONCLUSION: Compared with successful PCI for CTO, failed PCI for CTO was not associated with a higher long-term risk of all-cause death or myocardial infarction. Adverse clinical characteristics were an independent predictor of adverse clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Dual Biologic Therapy With Dupilumab and Mepolizumab in Refractory Atopic Dermatitis and Severe Eosinophilic Asthma.
Atherogenic index of plasma and risk of reduced eGFR with age-adapted eGFR thresholds in the elderly general population.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the correlation between atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and prevalence of reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 4885 participants aged ≥60 from southeast China from 13 September 2023 to 30 November 2023. AIP was calculated as the logarithmic ratio (base 10) of triglycerides to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. This study used categorical age-adapted eGFR thresholds in two age groups to analyze: <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 for those aged 60-65 years old and <45 mL/min/1.73 m2 for those over 65 years old. The category-free analysis was performed to corroborate whether AIP enhanced the ability to estimate reduced eGFR.

RESULTS: The prevalence of reduced eGFR in the general population aged ≥60 was 2.7%. After adjustment, each SD increase in AIP was associated with a 52% additional risk for reduced eGFR. When dividing AIP into quartiles, the top quartile had a 2.95 times higher risk than the bottom quartile. Subgroup analysis revealed that the association remained robust against several risk factors for renal damage.

CONCLUSION: This study reveals an association between AIP and reduced eGFR with age-adapted eGFR thresholds, independent of conventional risk factors.

articles.title: Comparison between genetic profiles of Amblyomma sculptum ticks from areas with and without Rickettsia rickettsii circulation in the state of São Paulo, Southeastern Brazil.
articles.abstract: The expansion of Brazilian spotted fever (BSF) transmission areas in the interior of the state of São Paulo, southeastern Brazil, has been associated with the expansion of capybaras (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris L.) population, the main amplifying hosts of the BSF etiological agent (Rickettsia rickettsii) for the tick vector Amblyomma sculptum Berlese (Ixodida: Ixodidae). However, many areas with capybaras and A. sculptum remain free of R. rickettsii, indicating that other factors may be involved in the establishment of R. rickettsii infection in ticks in a given area. This work aimed to evaluate the genetic profile of A. sculptum tick populations in areas with and without R. rickettsii circulation in the state of São Paulo, seeking differences that may be related to the vector's ability to transmit and spread the bacteria and, thus, to the establishment of BSF. To this end, sequences were generated for two mitochondrial genes of A. sculptum, namely, 16S rRNA and cytochrome oxidase subunit I (COI), from adult specimens collected in 29 areas of the state of São Paulo, where the population of this tick is primarily maintained by capybaras, with 16 of these areas with confirmed circulation of R. rickettsii and 13 areas considered free of circulation of the bacterium. As a result, five distinct haplotypes for the 16S rRNA gene and 14 for the COI gene were identified, with greater haplotype and nucleotide diversity rates observed in areas with no R. rickettsii circulation. In contrast, when compared with sequences from other geographic regions, a greater number of mutations separating the haplotypes was observed, indicating a higher degree of genetic structure between the sequences from the state of São Paulo and those from other regions. Despite this, some sequences detected in the study, especially from areas without R. rickettsii circulation, were closer to those from other locations than to those detected in the study region. In a nutshell, the data obtained in the study indicate that the endemicity of the area does not coincide solely with the presence or absence of a specific haplotype but is possibly related to the genetic structure of the tick population, which was reflected by the relative frequency of different haplotypes, and its interaction with other factors yet to be described.

articles.title: CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) Study of the OMERACT Ultrasound CPPD Subtask Working Group: Interim Analysis of Automated Ultrasound Grading of Knee Meniscal CPPD.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to develop and evaluate artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods for automated grading of calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) in ultrasound (US) images according to the Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT) US scoring system.

METHODS: Within the OMERACT CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) project, two deep learning strategies were explored using knee meniscus US images graded from 0 to 3. Image-level classification was evaluated using convolutional neural networks (CNN) trained directly on cropped meniscus images (n = 446). A semantic segmentation approach was developed using a subset of 279 images with manually annotated masks identifying meniscus and deposits. Models were evaluated using an 80/20 training-validation split and stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Segmentation was assessed using Intersection over Union (IoU). For automated grading, an area ratio (AR), representing CPPD pixels relative to meniscus and CPPD pixels, was applied to predicted masks.

RESULTS: Image-level classification achieved an accuracy of 0.69 in the single-split analysis and a mean accuracy of 0.59 (SD 0.10) in 5-fold cross-validation. End-to-end AR grading achieved accuracies of 0.64 and 0.61 (SD 0.10), with a grade 3 recall of 0.25 in the single split. AR grading on manually annotated reference masks achieved an accuracy of 0.82. The best-performing segmentation model achieved mean IoUs of 0.86 for background, 0.60 for meniscus, and 0.37 for CPPD.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide a methodological basis for automated CPPD US grading, but performance remains far from clinical applicability, highlighting the need for larger datasets and improved segmentation.

articles.title: Vanadium Oxide Nanoregulator Modulates cGAS-STING Pathway-Associated Immune Dysregulation in Sepsis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is driven by cytosolic accumulation of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and consequent overactivation of the cGAS-STING axis, which serves as a nodal upstream trigger for innate immune dysregulation. However, interventions directly targeting this subcellular event remain largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we synthesized a library of vanadium oxide nanostructures with distinct morphologies and identified nanospheres (VO NSs) as the optimal candidate. These VO NSs act through a multimodal mechanism, scavenging reactive oxygen species, stabilizing mitochondrial membrane potential, and blocking permeability transition pore opening, to physically constrain mtDNA egress from mitochondria, thereby ablating STING-dependent inflammatory signaling. In murine models of sepsis, administration of VO NSs confers marked survival advantage and robust protection against multi-organ injury. Mechanistically, using STING-knockout mice, we demonstrate that STING ablation fully recapitulates the prophylactic efficacy of VO NSs, establishing STING as the pivotal downstream mediator. Beyond acute protection, VO NSs preserve mitochondrial genomic integrity and have the potential to disrupt the self-reinforcing cycle between oxidative stress and immune exhaustion. This work offers an initial demonstration of a subcellular-targeted intervention strategy for sepsis regulation, while also highlighting the potential of a modular nanoplatform for broader application in mitochondrial dysfunction-associated diseases.

articles.title: KRT16 From Diverse Tumors Induces Atrial Remodeling and Fibrillation via Endothelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition.
articles.abstract: Anticancer therapy increases the incidence of atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide. However, whether multiple cancers directly promote AF independently of anticancer therapy through shared mechanisms remains unclear. Here, retrospective clinical analyses revealed significantly increased AF prevalence in pre-treatment female patients with breast cancer (BC), lung cancer (LC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), independent of anticancer therapy. Consistently, orthotopic tumor-bearing mouse models exhibited enhanced AF inducibility accompanied by atrial enlargement, fibrosis, and electrical remodeling. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, combined with the TCGA datasets, identified endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) as a shared atrial remodeling pathway underlying tumor-associated AF across multiple cancers. Mechanistically, keratin 16 (KRT16) acted as a shared circulating factor across multiple malignancies. KRT16 accumulated in atrial endothelial cells and promoted EndMT through annexin A2 (AnxA2)-dependent activation of TGF-β1/Smad signaling. KRT16 promoted abnormal membrane retention of AnxA2 by suppressing Tyr23 phosphorylation, thereby sustaining profibrotic signaling and atrial remodeling. Genetic silencing of KRT16 in cancer cells or endothelial knockdown of AnxA2 markedly attenuated EndMT, atrial fibrosis, and AF susceptibility in tumor-bearing mice. Our findings demonstrate that multiple cancers directly induce atrial remodeling and AF through a shared mechanism centered on KRT16-driven EndMT, identifying this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Tolerogenic Immunotherapy for Type 1 Diabetes Through Sustained Autoantigen Delivery in a Transient Inflammatory Niche.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a T-cell-mediated autoimmune disease characterized by destruction of pancreatic β-cells, resulting in lifelong insulin therapy dependence and risk of severe complications. Tolerogenic immunotherapies offer a promising strategy to restore antigen-specific immune tolerance and prevent T1D but have been limited by challenges in controlled spatiotemporal exposure of antigens and immunomodulators to achieve robust tolerance. Here, we report the development of injectable hydrogel depot formulations providing sustained co-delivery of insulin autoantigen and low-dose interleukin-2 (IL-2) and which form transient tolerogenic niches following subcutaneous administration. These treatments recruit and expand regulatory T cells both within the hydrogel niche and draining lymph nodes, inducing tolerance responses in the spleen and pancreas and increasing the median time to diabetes onset in non-obese diabetic mice from 20 to >40 weeks. These studies suggest that sustained co-exposure of autoantigen in the appropriate immune environment can promote durable tolerance for T1D prevention.

articles.title: Targeting Fibroblast Foxc2 Promotes Neurovascular Recovery by Suppressing Sdc4 After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, with current reperfusion therapies limited by narrow therapeutic windows and inability to promote sustained neurovascular repair. Here, we developed YZD-27, a rationally designed Tanshinone IIA (TSA) derivative with improved druggability, and show that it remains therapeutically effective when administered up to 24 h after ischemic injury in transient and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO and dMCAO) mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and cell-cell communication analysis revealed broad cellular responses to YZD-27 and identified fibronectin-1 (Fn1)/syndecan-4 (Sdc4) as a predicted endothelia-fibroblast ligand-receptor interaction. Mechanistically, YZD-27 directly binds forkhead box protein C2 (Foxc2), enhances its protein stability by limiting proteasomal degradation, and increases its occupancy at the Sdc4 promoter, thereby repressing Sdc4 transcription in fibroblast. Fibroblast-conditioned medium experiments further supported a role for Foxc2/Sdc4 regulation in modulating endothelial barrier-related protein expression. These findings identify Foxc2/Sdc4 signaling as a regulatory mechanism associated with the therapeutic effects of YZD-27, and establish YZD-27 as a promising neurovascular therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Stage-predominant epigenetic framework across the MASLD spectrum: global evidence and the Saudi Arabian context.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, encompassing a spectrum from simple steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and fibrosis, with the potential to progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). While genetic factors influence disease risk, accumulating evidence highlights epigenetic regulation as a crucial factor connecting environmental and metabolic stressors to disease onset and progression. This narrative review adopts a stage-based approach, synthesizing current knowledge of epigenetic remodeling across the MASLD spectrum. We focus on three major epigenetic modulations, i.e. DNA methylation, histone modifications, and noncoding RNAs, and distinguish findings derived from human liver tissues, circulating biomarkers, and experimental models. This organization clarifies how epigenetic changes and shared regulatory pathways evolve throughout disease progression. Focusing on the Saudi Arabian context, we identify a substantial gap between the high regional burden of MASLD and the limited availability of liver-specific, longitudinal, and ancestry-aware epigenomic data. We propose research priorities and a framework to address these gaps, aiming to guide future studies in Saudi Arabia and the broader region toward clinically relevant biomarker discovery and precision hepatology.

articles.title: Rifampicin and long-acting cabotegravir-rilpivirine: Therapeutic drug monitoring-guided management of a major drug-drug interaction-A case report.
articles.abstract: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine (LAI CAB/RPV) is subject to clinically significant drug-drug interactions with strong enzyme inducers such as rifampicin due to markedly reduced drug exposure and potential development of resistance. However, real-world evidence on managing this interaction remains scarce. We report a person with HIV, virologically suppressed on LAI CAB/RPV, who developed an orthopaedic implant-associated infection requiring 10-week rifampicin-containing therapy for its antibiofilm activity. Further LAI CAB/RPV injections were withheld, and oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine once daily plus dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily was initiated. This regimen was continued until 3 weeks after rifampicin discontinuation; afterwards, dolutegravir was reduced to once daily. LAI CAB/RPV was restarted 5 weeks after rifampicin withdrawal; oral antiretroviral therapy was discontinued. Serial therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) showed a rapid decline in plasma CAB and RPV concentrations from day 8 after rifampicin initiation, with both drugs falling below the efficacy thresholds by day 10. In contrast, tenofovir and dolutegravir concentrations remained within the therapeutic range during rifampicin co-administration, whereas twice-daily dolutegravir concentrations exceeded the therapeutic range 3 weeks after rifampicin discontinuation. HIV RNA remained undetectable throughout follow-up. This case confirms the clinically relevant interaction between rifampicin and LAI CAB/RPV, as illustrated by the rapid decline in residual CAB and RPV plasma concentrations following rifampicin initiation. Temporary substitution with a recommended first-line oral antiretroviral regimen maintained adequate drug exposure, was well tolerated and preserved virological suppression throughout rifampicin treatment. TDM allowed to characterize the interaction and may support individualized management in selected complex clinical situations.

articles.title: Symptom burden and patient activation in maintenance hemodialysis patients: chain-mediating effects of illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue.
articles.abstract: This study examined the association between symptom burden and patient activation in maintenance hemodialysis patients and tested the mediating roles of illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue.A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 265 patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis at a tertiary hospital in China from November 2025 to March 2026. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Dialysis Symptom Index, the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire, the Self-Regulatory Fatigue Scale and the Patient Activation Measure. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, Harman single-factor test and structural equation modeling were performed. Bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5000 resamples was used to test mediating effects. Symptom burden had a significant direct effect on patient activation, accounting for 53.58%of the total effect. Illness perception, self-regulatory fatigue and the sequential pathway from illness perception to self-regulatory fatigue also mediated the relationship between symptom burden and patient activation, accounting for 29.28%, 11.84%and 5.30%of the total effect, respectively. Symptom burden was associated with patient activation both directly and indirectly through illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue. These findings suggest that illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue may help explain the association between symptom burden and patient activation in patients receiving maintenance haemodialysis.

articles.title: Smoking and fibrosis risk progression: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Around 40% of patients with chronic liver disease (CLD) have a history of tobacco smoking, but the impact of smoking on fibrosis progression remains unclear. This study investigates the association between tobacco smoking and Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) risk progression high-risk FIB-4 in primary care patients with CLD.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of primary care patients with CLD and inputs for at least two separate FIB-4 calculations. Patients with an initial FIB-4 ≥3.25, or prior diagnoses of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, or liver transplant were excluded. The primary outcome was time to FIB-4 ≥3.25, indicating a high-risk for advanced fibrosis. Tobacco smoking status (never, former, current) was the primary exposure. We used univariate and bivariate analyses to describe the cohort and unadjusted and adjusted Cox regression models to evaluate the association of tobacco smoking with time to FIB-4 ≥3.25.

RESULTS: The cohort had 2547 patients, with 24%, 36%, and 41% identified as current, former, and never tobacco smokers, respectively. After a mean follow-up of 5.4 years, 24% of the cohort progressed to high-risk FIB-4. In unadjusted Cox models, former (HR 1.35; 95% CI 1.11-1.63) and current (HR 1.49; 95% CI 1.21-1.83) tobacco smoking were associated with an increased risk of progression to high-risk FIB-4. Current (HR 1.27; 95% CI 1.02-1.59), but not former (HR 1.18; 95% CI 0.97-1.43), tobacco smoking was significantly associated with time to a high-risk FIB-4 after adjusting for CLD etiology, cardiometabolic, and demographic variables.

CONCLUSION: Current tobacco smoking is associated with progression to a FIB-4 at high-risk for advanced fibrosis in patients with CLD.

articles.title: Bacterial DnaK Promotes CHIP-Mediated GPX4 Degradation: A Bone-Targeted DNAzyme-Nanozyme Strategy for Repair of Infected Bone Defects.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus infection impairs bone repair, but how bacterial proteins disrupt osteogenic progenitors remains unclear. The bacterial chaperone DnaK promotes glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) degradation in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), accompanied by lipid peroxidation, ferroptotic injury, and impaired osteogenic differentiation. GPX4 protein turnover increases without a change in Gpx4 mRNA abundance. A candidate E3-ligase screen identifies the C terminus of Hsc70-interacting protein (CHIP) as a mediator of this response. Catalytically inactive CHIP attenuates DnaK-associated K48-linked GPX4 ubiquitination, while CHIP knockdown preserves GPX4 and osteogenic proteins in primary BMSCs. To target bacterial DnaK and host oxidative injury, a bone-targeted deoxyribozyme (DNAzyme)-nanozyme platform (DMPA) combines a dnaK-targeting DNAzyme with manganese hexacyanoferrate, polydopamine, and alendronate. In infected cultures, DMPA reduces bacterial dnaK transcript and DnaK protein abundance and improves BMSC redox balance and matrix mineralization. In a mouse model of infected tibial defects, DMPA promotes bone regeneration. These findings link bacterial DnaK to host GPX4 degradation through CHIP and establish a bone-targeted DNAzyme-nanozyme strategy that combines bacterial DnaK suppression with redox regulation to promote repair of infected bone defects.

articles.title: Drug-drug interactions and risk of central nervous system depression in preterm infants: Clinical outcomes from a prospective study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are frequently exposed to central nervous system (CNS) depressant medications, increasing the risk of potential drug-drug interactions (DDIs). However, evidence on the clinical outcomes associated with these interactions remains limited. This study evaluated the association between DDIs with the potential for CNS depression and clinical outcomes in neonates admitted to a NICU.

METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 600 neonates admitted to a NICU in Brazil. Pharmacotherapy was monitored daily, and DDIs with the potential for CNS depression were identified using the UpToDate® database. Clinical outcomes associated with specific drug combinations were analysed.

RESULTS: A total of 89 neonates (14.8%) were exposed to at least one DDI with the potential for CNS depression. These interactions were associated with a higher occurrence of hypoactivity, reduced peripheral oxygen saturation and mortality. The fentanyl/phenobarbital combination showed the most consistent risk profile, being associated with all evaluated outcomes. Interactions involving magnesium sulphate were associated with reduced oxygen saturation, while fentanyl/fluconazole was associated with increased mortality.

CONCLUSION: DDIs with the potential for CNS depression were associated with clinically relevant adverse outcomes in neonates. The findings highlight fentanyl/phenobarbital as the combination of greatest clinical concern and suggest that oxygen saturation may be a useful marker for monitoring CNS-related DDIs in neonatal intensive care.

articles.title: High-fat diet-altered expression profile of mitochondrial functional molecules contributes to myocardial remodeling in type 1 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The most frequent underlying cause of death for type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is cardiovascular damage. Extreme fat consumption causes deterioration in lipid metabolism in DM; however, how a high-fat diet (HFD) affects the progression of pathological process of diabetic myocardial dysfunction, especially the identification of candidate intervention targets, has become an urgent need.

METHODS: The T1DM Syrian golden hamster model was induced by streptozotocin (STZ) injection, and a 6-week HFD intervention (42.0% calories from fat) was given in the early stage of T1DM. Changes in body weight and biochemical indicators of glucose and lipid were tracked weekly. Echocardiography and histopathology were used to evaluate how HFD affected myocardial remodeling at the overall, ultramicroscopic, and microscopic levels. Using proteomics, the STRING database, molecular biology analysis, and reverse validation via an in vitro model, we further gathered mechanistic insights.

RESULTS: HFD caused severe lipid metabolism disorders in the STZ/HFD group. HFD induced more severe inhomogeneous hypertrophy, cardiac diastolic dysfunction, interstitial collagen deposition, and lipid droplet accumulation in the myocardium of T1DM hamsters. Mechanistically, HFD influenced the protein composition profile, mainly in lipid metabolism as well as mitochondrial metabolism. Furthermore, HFD caused more severe damage to mitochondrial morphology. Moreover, metabolic disorder of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) was mediated by PPM1K, which finally aggravated surplus oxidative stress accumulation and damage in the myocardium of T1DM hamsters.

CONCLUSIONS: Mitochondrial repair, especially the metabolic replenishment of BCAAs, holds potential as a treatment in situations with excessive fat intake in T1DM and should be investigated in vivo and in clinical validation studies in the future.

articles.title: Conduction system pacing vs biventricular pacing in heart failure patients undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy: an updated grade-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared conduction system pacing (CSP) with biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception through 16 May 2026 for randomized trials. Random-effects Mean Difference/Odds Ratio and Peto pooling were performed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 and GRADE assessment.

RESULTS: Twelve trials (1,152 patients) were included. CSP shortened QRS duration (mean difference [MD] -10.03 ms, 95% confidence interval [CI] -15.95 to -4.12) and increased absolute left ventricular ejection fraction at 6 months (MD 3.67% points, 95% CI 1.38-5.95). Six-month change was not significantly different (MD 2.07% points, 95% CI -0.66 to 4.80); 12-month improvement favored BVP (MD -3.28% points, 95% CI -5.00 to -1.55). Mortality (risk ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.33-1.48), heart failure hospitalization (Peto odds ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.47-2.33), and pneumothorax (Peto odds ratio 1.94, 95% CI 0.20-18.71) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: CSP showed physiological benefits without established clinical superiority. Heterogeneity, small trials, and limited follow-up restrict interpretation.

REVIEW REGISTRATION: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO): CRD420261413053. Registry: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/.

articles.title: Biological Reconstruction of the Anterior Skull Base Using Liquid Nitrogen-Treated Autologous Bone.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rigid skeletal restoration after anterior skull base resection remains unresolved. Alloplastic implants increase exposure and infection risk, whereas vascularized bone flaps increase donor-site morbidity. Liquid nitrogen (LN2)-treated autologous bone, Tsuchiya method, is unexplored for anterior skull base reconstruction.

METHODS: We report cases of two patients (48-year-old man with olfactory neuroblastoma and 50-year-old woman with SMARCB1-deficient chondromyxoid tumor) undergoing anterior craniofacial resection with rigid reconstruction using LN2-treated autologous bone. After periosteal-plane tumor stripping, the bone underwent one LN2 cycle and was re-implanted; the skull base was sealed with a free flap, and the graft was covered with a vascularized pericranial flap. Margins were negative.

RESULTS: At 34 and 33 months, both patients remained disease-free without graft interface recurrence or graft resorption.

CONCLUSIONS: The technique, with preserved margins, thus appears feasible and oncologically defensible in selected patients. We propose a three-criterion indication framework and call for its prospective validation.

articles.title: Upfront venetoclax plus quizartinib with low-dose cytarabine or azacitidine in older unfit patients with acute myeloid leukemia: the phase I/II VEN-A-QUI trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many older patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. Quizartinib, an oral, selective, FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) inhibitor is approved in combination with intensive chemotherapy for patients with newly diagnosed (ND) FLT3-internal tandem duplication (ITD)-positive AML. Quizartinib efficacy and safety in combination with venetoclax plus either azacitidine (VEN-AZA-Quiz) or low-dose cytarabine (VEN-LDAC-Quiz) were investigated in patients ineligible for intensive chemotherapy.

METHODS: The phase I/II, multicenter, prospective, open-label, VEN-A-QUI trial enrolled patients aged ≥ 60 years with ND FLT3-ITD-positive or -negative AML.

PHASE I: patients were assigned to parallel VEN-AZA-Quiz or VEN-LDAC-Quiz dose-escalation cohorts.

PHASE II: patients were randomized 1:1 to VEN-AZA-Quiz or VEN-LDAC-Quiz. Primary endpoints were the determination of quizartinib recommended phase II dose (RP2D; phase I) and composite complete remission (CRc) rate (phase II).

RESULTS: Fourteen and 60 patients received treatment in phase I and II, respectively. The quizartinib RP2D was 60 mg/day for VEN-AZA-Quiz and 40 mg/day for VEN-LDAC-Quiz. In phase II, CRc by Cycle 4 was achieved in 18/31 patients (58.1%) receiving VEN-AZA-Quiz and 15/29 (51.7%) receiving VEN-LDAC-Quiz (p = 0.80). Median overall survival (OS) was 16.9 months and 8.9 months for VEN-AZA-Quiz and VEN-LDAC-Quiz, respectively (p = 0.81), with 3-year OS rates of 22.6% and 27.6%. Overall, a high CRc rate (10/13, 76.9%) and median OS (29.3 months) was observed in FLT3-ITD-positive patients. Median OS was 32 months for de novo AML and 7.5 months for secondary AML (p < 0.001). The most common adverse events were infectious and hematologic toxicity.

CONCLUSIONS: VEN-AZA-Quiz and VEN-LDAC-Quiz regimens demonstrated clinical activity in patients with ND AML aged ≥ 60 years ineligible for intense chemotherapy, particularly in patients with de novo AML, with an acceptable safety profile.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04687761.

articles.title: Urinary Metabolic and Hemodynamic Protein Signatures in Canagliflozin Treated Patients With Diabetic Kidney Disease: Findings From CREDENCE.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide kidney protection in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD). There is limited knowledge about the mechanisms by which they protect the kidney. We investigated which urinary proteins and pathways are associated with progressive kidney disease and canagliflozin treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This case-control study included patients from the CREDENCE trial. Cases and controls were defined by annual eGFR decline of ≥ 5 or < 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 and propensity score-matched within treatment arms. High-throughput urinary proteomics (SomaLogic, n = 5284 aptamers) was performed at baseline and year 1. Differential abundance analysis assessed 1-year changes between cases and controls, and between canagliflozin and placebo-treated patients. Identified proteins were mapped to kidney biopsy single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from patients with type 2 diabetes, with or without SGLT2i treatment to identify cell type-specific expression.

RESULTS: Of 392 included participants, 250 were randomized to canagliflozin and 142 to placebo. After 1 year, 124 proteins were changed by canagliflozin compared to placebo (92 increased and 32 decreased). Enolase 1, SLIT, NTRK Like Family Member 1, and leucine-rich repeat containing 15 increased more than 3-fold, while decreases were observed in alanyl aminopeptidase, discoidin domain receptor 1 and ameloblastin. Pathway analysis revealed enhanced activity of metabolic pathways. scRNA-seq data showed increased expression of metabolic genes after SGLT2i treatment in distal tubular cells.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that SGLT2i administration induces a redistribution of tubular workload through compensatory sodium reabsorption in distal parts of the nephron, which may contribute to kidney-protective effects in DKD.

articles.title: Pre-Treatment Biomarkers Associated With Remission of Type 2 Diabetes in Response to Short-Term Insulin-Based Therapy.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Short-term insulin-based therapy can induce remission of Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) in some but not all patients. The underlying determinant of whether remission can be achieved is beta-cell function, but its assessment typically requires complex challenge testing. We thus sought to determine if there exist circulating biomarkers associated with the likelihood of achieving remission prior to initiating short-term insulin-based therapy, without requiring challenge testing.

METHODS: Adults with T2DM of ≤ 7 years duration were randomized to 8 weeks treatment with (i) insulin glargine, (ii) glargine + thrice-daily lispro or (iii) glargine + twice-daily exenatide, followed by 12 weeks washout that enabled assessment for remission (A1c < 6.5% after ≥ 3 months without glucose-lowering therapy). We assessed the following fasting biomarkers at baseline in relation to subsequent remission: fibroblast growth factor-21 (FGF-21), C-reactive protein (CRP), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-4 (IL-4), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4).

RESULTS: Remission occurred in 31 of 90 participants (34.4%). At baseline, compared to their non-remitting peers, those in whom remission was subsequently achieved had higher Homeostasis Model Assessment of beta-cell function (HOMA-B; p = 0.02), lower fasting proinsulin: C-peptide ratio (p = 0.008) and borderline higher prevalence of detectable IL-4 (p = 0.06), though significance did not persist after multiplicity-adjustment. On exploratory logistic regression analyses, baseline detectable IL-4 (aOR = 3.58; 95% CI: 1.25-10.99) and HOMA-B (aOR = 1.77; 95% CI: 1.11-2.99) were associated with remission.

CONCLUSION: Prior to treatment, higher HOMA-B and detectable IL-4 are candidate markers warranting further study for association with subsequent remission of T2DM in response to short-term insulin-based therapy.

articles.title: Clostridioides difficile-commensal interactions are impacted by diet more than differences between strains.
articles.abstract: The primary risk factor for C. difficile infection (CDI) is broad-spectrum antibiotic use which clears the intestinal microbiome leaving an open niche for C. difficile to colonize. During infection, C. difficile metabolism is highly responsive to its nutritional environment. For example, in mice with CDI, a high protein diet exacerbates disease severity while a high carbohydrate, high fiber diet ameliorates disease. However, C. difficile is a genetically and metabolically diverse species with often significant differences between strains. To investigate how C. difficile metabolism differs between strains as a function of diet, we reconstructed genome-scale metabolic models of 105 C. difficile strains from publicly available, whole-genome sequencing data and then simulated metabolic flux for each model under three unique diet conditions. We found that strains cluster in two metabolically distinct groups by diet. Metabolomics of spent media from C. difficile strains grown in diet conditions found both unique and shared metabolic pathways across conditions. We also simulated the growth of the C. difficile strains in the presence of 8 different commensals to understand the impact of diet on common microbiome interactions in the large intestine. We found that C. difficile-commensal interactions were more impacted by diet than by differences between C. difficile strains. Overall, the diverse metabolic responses of both C. difficile strains and commensals to different diet conditions have therapeutic implications, particularly for fecal microbiota transplants where differences in metabolism could impact the effectiveness of treatment and as an important parameter to incorporate in the design of therapeutic synthetic bacterial communities to resolve CDI.

articles.title: Polygenic Risk for Type 2 Diabetes, Multiple Risk Factor Control and Cardiovascular and Non-Cardiovascular Mortality.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine the independent and joint associations of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) genetic susceptibility and control of multiple modifiable cardiovascular risk factors with all-cause and cause-specific mortality.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included 314 737 UK Biobank participants. T2DM genetic susceptibility was assessed using a polygenic risk score and categorized as low, intermediate or high. Control of multiple modifiable cardiovascular risk factors was classified as poor, intermediate or ideal. Cox models evaluated associations with all-cause, cardiovascular, cancer and other-cause mortality.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.2 years, 24 287 deaths occurred, including 4937 cardiovascular, 12 234 cancer and 7116 other-cause deaths. High versus low genetic risk was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR: 1.11, 95% CI: 1.06-1.15), cardiovascular mortality (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.21-1.44) and other-cause mortality (HR: 1.11, 95% CI: 1.04-1.20). Ideal versus poor risk factor control was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.47-0.54), cardiovascular mortality (HR: 0.35, 95% CI: 0.31-0.40) and cancer mortality (HR: 0.55, 95% CI: 0.50-0.61). Participants with high genetic risk and poor risk factor control had the highest risks of all-cause mortality (HR: 2.14, 95% CI: 1.88-2.43) and cardiovascular mortality (HR: 3.72, 95% CI: 2.92-4.74). Results were robust in subgroup and sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: T2DM genetic susceptibility and modifiable risk factor control were associated with mortality, particularly cardiovascular mortality. These findings are hypothesis-generating and may inform future research on integrated risk stratification.

articles.title: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of FreeStyle Libre Real-Time Continuous Glucose Monitoring System Compared With Self-Monitoring of Blood Glucose in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes on Basal Insulin Plus SGLT2 Inhibitor and/or GLP-1 Agonists in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We previously showed that FreeStyle Libre (FSL) real-time continuous glucose monitoring system (rtCGM) reduces glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at 16 and 32 weeks compared with capillary self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) in adults with Type 2 diabetes and above target glucose levels, managed with basal insulin and SGLT-2 inhibitor and/or GLP-1 agonist therapy. We assess the cost-effectiveness of rtCGM compared with SMBG.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Participant-level baseline and follow-up health status (Euroqol-5-dimensions-5-levels) and within-trial healthcare resource-use data were collected. We estimated quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) and participant-level costs at 16 and 32 weeks. Long-term cost-effectiveness from the United Kingdom National Health Service perspective was evaluated using the IQVIA CORE Diabetes Model with a 3.5% discount rate. Sensitivity analyses assessed structural and parameter uncertainty.

RESULTS: Within-trial analyses found no significant difference at 32 weeks between rtCGM and SMBG in QALYs or healthcare costs. At 32 weeks, adjusted incremental QALYs were -0.015 (95% CI: -0.031 to 0.003) and incremental costs were £254 (95% CI: -£587 to £1070). The lifetime projected incremental QALYs were 0.730 (95% CI: 0.688-0.773) and incremental costs were £4341 (95% CI: 3558-5125), generating an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of £5943 per QALY. At least 4 years of maintained glycaemic benefits are required for rtCGM to be cost-effective. Sensitivity analyses were robust to the base-case results.

CONCLUSIONS: Benefits of FSL rtCGM in lowering HbA1c in people with Type 2 diabetes on basal insulin plus SGLT-2 inhibitor and/or GLP-1 agonist therapy is likely to justify costs through improved health outcomes and reduced long-term costs of diabetes-related complications.

articles.title: Five-year outcomes after brace-free versus brace-based rehabilitation following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative knee bracing following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains common practice despite growing evidence questioning its clinical benefit. Previous studies demonstrated that brace-free rehabilitation was noninferior to brace-based rehabilitation one year after isolated ACLR using hamstring tendon autograft; however, its long-term effects remain unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term effects five years after surgery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients enrolled in a prospective randomized controlled trial conducted between 2016 and 2019 were recontacted approximately five years after isolated primary ACLR with hamstring tendon autograft for a long-term follow-up. In the original trial, 139 patients had been randomized to postoperative rehabilitation without a brace (n = 71) or with a functional knee brace (n = 68). Participants completed several patient-reported outcome measures. Furthermore, a standardized telephone interview was performed. Changes between the one-year and five-year follow-up were analyzed.

RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients participated in the long-term follow-up (n = 45 brace-free group, n = 52 brace group). Mean follow-up was 5.2 ± 1.0 years. No significant differences were observed between groups regarding subjective knee function, activity level, quality of life, rerupture rate, revision surgery, or persistent knee-related complaints at final follow-up. However, there was a significant interaction between treatment group and time for the subjective IKDC score. Patients treated without postoperative bracing showed stable or slightly improved subjective knee function, whereas patients treated with a brace demonstrated a significant decline between one and five years.

DISCUSSION: Brace-free rehabilitation after isolated ACL reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft remains safe and effective more than five years after surgery. Postoperative bracing did not reduce rerupture rates, revision surgery, or long-term functional impairment. Instead, brace-free rehabilitation demonstrated a more favorable longitudinal development of subjective knee function. These findings further question the routine postoperative prescription of rehabilitative knee braces following isolated ACL reconstruction.

articles.title: Societal and Economic Burden of Type 1 Diabetes Across Disease Stages in Italy.
Osteomyelitis after open supracondylar fracture in a child: a case report and review of the literature.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract: The management of open fractures in children relies on several critical strategies to minimize the risk of infection, including the timing of surgical debridement, appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis, and the choice of osteosynthesis technique. Despite these considerations, the overall rate of postoperative infection in children remains relatively low. Consequently, clinical experience with deep postoperative infections in pediatric patients is limited. Furthermore, the highly variable and often subtle clinical presentation can make early diagnosis challenging. We present the case of an 8-year-old child who developed osteomyelitis following a Gustilo-Anderson grade III open supracondylar humerus fracture.

articles.title: Correction to "Advances in insulin pump systems lead to stepwise improvements in treatment satisfaction in people with type 1 diabetes: A single-center retrospective study.".
Quadratus lumborum versus transversus abdominis plane block for postoperative analgesia in laparoscopic colorectal surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective pain management after surgery is crucial for recovery following laparoscopic colorectal resection in enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programs. While the transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block is commonly used, it may not fully address visceral pain. The quadratus lumborum (QL) block might provide better coverage for both somatic and visceral pain due to its ability to spread to the thoracolumbar fascia and paravertebral space.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare the clinical outcomes of QL versus TAP blocks in laparoscopic colorectal surgery. The main outcome was total opioid use within 24 h. Secondary outcomes included early pain scores, time until the first rescue analgesic was needed, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), length of stay, surgical complications, and side effects related to the blocks.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic literature search using PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to 27 July 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing QL and TAP blocks. Two reviewers independently screened the studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. We calculated pooled estimates using a random-effects model and evaluated the reliability of the evidence on the basis of the grading of recommendations, assessment, development, and evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: Four RCTs (n = 419) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with the TAP block, the QL block led to lower opioid use within 24 h (MD [mean difference] -8.92 mg morphine equivalents; 95% CI -11.57 to -6.28) and reduced pain scores both at rest MD -0.25 (-0.37 to -0.21) and during movement MD -0.40 [-0.52 to -0.29]. Operative time numerically favored the QL block, but the pooled difference was not statistically significant. The rates of PONV (OR 0.54; 95% CI 0.25-1.19) and dizziness (OR 0.60; 95% CI 0.22-1.63) were not significantly different between the two groups. The evidence was rated high for PONV and operative time, and moderate for opioid consumption, pain at rest, pain during movement, and dizziness, reflecting downgrades for imprecision and, for opioid consumption and pain during movement, substantial-to-high heterogeneity (I2 85% and 93%, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: In laparoscopic colorectal surgery, the QL block shows better opioid-sparing effects and lower pain scores at rest and during movement than the TAP block. Operative time numerically favored the QL block but did not differ significantly between groups. Importantly, it does not lead to more adverse effects. These findings suggest that the QL block may be a useful opioid-sparing option within ERAS-based perioperative care, although larger multicenter RCTs are needed before routine preference over the TAP block can be firmly recommended.

articles.title: Adjuvant capecitabine-based oral chemotherapy plus trastuzumab as adjuvant therapy in patients with HER2-positive, node-negative breast tumors measuring 1 cm or smaller (ORCHID study).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant treatment decisions for patients with small (T ≤ 1 cm), node-negative, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast tumors remain challenging, particularly regarding whether oral chemotherapy is comparable to intravenous regimens. We therefore conducted a phase II trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of an oral chemotherapy plus trastuzumab regimen in this population.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients received either single-agent capecitabine (1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 every 3 weeks) or vinorelbine capsules (60 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 3 weeks) plus trastuzumab, followed by trastuzumab monotherapy for a total of 12 months of therapy. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS). The secondary end points were distant disease-free survival (DDFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04296162).

RESULTS: The analysis population included 182 patients, of whom 81% had tumors measuring ≤ 0.5 cm and 74% had hormone receptor (HR)-negative disease. Of the 181 treated patients, 176 (97.2%) received capecitabine and 5 (2.8%) vinorelbine, with agent selection at the physician's discretion. After a median follow-up of 5.7 years (range, 1.0-6.2 years), the 5-year DFS rate was 97.3% (90% Confidence interval [CI], 94.4-98.7). The lower bound of the 90% CI exceeded the prespecified threshold of 92%, meeting the primary endpoint. Among the 6 observed invasive disease events, 2 involved distant metastasis, 3 involved local or regional recurrence, and 1 involved contralateral breast cancer. Among the secondary endpoints, the 5-year DDFS rate was 97.2%, with a 5-year OS rate of 100% (no deaths) during follow-up. Among the 176 patients treated with capecitabine, the most common capecitabine-related adverse event (AE) was hand-foot syndrome, which occurred in 66.5% of patients, with 8.0% of patients experiencing a grade 3 event.

CONCLUSIONS: Among women with HER2-positive, node-negative breast tumors measuring ≤ 1 cm, capecitabine-based oral chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab was associated with a low risk of cancer recurrence and favorable toxicity in this single-arm cohort, supporting further prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Predictors of Parental Strain in Pediatric Atopic Dermatitis: Findings From the US National Survey of Children's Health.
articles.abstract: Caring for a child with atopic dermatitis (AD) places strain on parents, but it remains unclear whether additional atopic comorbidities or psychosocial context compounds this burden.
