Data from the 2007-2008 National Survey of Children's Health among 6913 children aged 6-17 years was analyzed using survey-weighted multivariable regression to examine associations between a 5-item parental strain scale and parent-reported AD severity, comorbid asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy, along with family, social, and healthcare access factors. Increased parental strain was associated with AD severity and with delayed or forgone care. Decreased parental strain was associated with better maternal mental health and with the female sex of the child. Atopic comorbidities were not associated with strain. Parental strain was more strongly associated with psychosocial factors and the severity of AD than the presence of additional atopic comorbidities.

articles.title: Risk factors for surgical site infection in clean surgeries at a modern small animal teaching hospital-a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: There are various studies on potential risk factors for the development of a surgical site infection (SSI). None of them analyse the factors with a focus on the daily practice of a small animal teaching clinic, especially the studies on the influence of personnel in the operating room are sparse. Over a period of 7 months, 102 dogs and cats belonging to private owners that had undergone clean surgery were prospectively studied for the occurrence of an SSI and potential associated risk factors. Patients were followed up 30 or 90 days later, either through examinations at the clinic or via telephone interviews with the pet owners. An SSI occurred in a total of 12% of surgeries (12/102). Although no significant risk factors for SSI were identified, surgery duration was longer and perioperative body temperatures were lower than reported in previous literature. The high number of personnel present in the operating room and the differences in SSI risk between surgical categories warrant further investigation. Skin surgeries tended to have a higher SSI risk than orthopaedic and neurosurgical procedures.

articles.title: RNA virus-induced metabolic reprogramming in a bloom-forming marine diatom.
articles.abstract: Diatoms are a widespread group of phytoplankton that disproportionately influence the global carbon cycle through substantial contributions to primary production and carbon export in the ocean. Marine viruses are major drivers of host metabolic reprogramming and mortality, and it is increasingly clear that RNA viruses, which primarily infect eukaryotes, are abundant and distributed throughout the global ocean. Using an integrated, multi-omics approach, we characterized the molecular and metabolic response of the model, bloom-forming, centric diatom Chaetoceros tenuissimus to RNA virus infection. Time-resolved transcriptomics revealed coordinated, differential expression of more than a third of host genes before host lysis, eliciting a cascade of metabolic responses that included early shifts in sulfur and lipid metabolism, induction of nitrogen assimilation pathways and late-stage activation of stress, signaling and death-related genes. Lipidomics revealed substantial cellular enrichment of phosphatidylethanolamine, ceramide, and triacylglycerol during RNA virus infection, as well as an infection-specific shift in fatty acid composition. Collectively, these findings provide insight into the intracellular requirements for RNA virus replication and illustrate a fundamental shift in resource partitioning in infected diatoms, advancing our understanding of how RNA virus infection transforms diatom host metabolic function and downstream ecosystem dynamics.

articles.title: A process-based, weather-driven forecaster for grape white rot caused by Coniella diplodiella.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: White rot, mainly caused by Coniella diplodiella, is a severe fungal disease affecting grape berries. Its management heavily relies on repeated fungicide applications, which often fail to achieve adequate disease control because their scheduling is based on empiricism rather than actual infection risk. To inform farmers about infection risk periods, this study aims to develop a novel, weather-driven mechanistic model by using available information and data from the literature.

RESULTS: The model simulates three epidemiological processes: (i) production and dispersal of primary inoculum; (ii) infections caused by primary and secondary conidia; and (iii) symptom onset and production of secondary inoculum. The model was validated against 16 independent epidemics (vineyard × year combinations) from different grape-producing regions in China between 1982 and 2021. Overall, the model provided an accurate prediction for infection events, with an accuracy of 0.971, a sensitivity of 0.929, and a specificity of 0.991. The model was also robust in reflecting seasonal disease progression under diverse conditions (weather and disease pressure), with an overall concordance correlation coefficient between observed and predicted disease severities of 0.946, a root mean square error of 0.112, and a coefficient of residual mass of -0.047.

CONCLUSIONS: The transparent mechanistic structure of the model will enable future integration of diverse epidemiological data, potentially including other species causing white rot (e.g., Coniella vitis). In the future, the model is expected to improve disease management of white rot via timely, risk-based interventions. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Isolation of fungal strains from soybean pastes and preparation of DPP-IV inhibitory peptides from quinoa proteins by fungal fermentation.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus and the side effects of synthetic DPP-IV inhibitors have increased demand for food-derived dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) inhibitory peptides. Quinoa is a promising source of such bioactive peptides, while fungi from soybean paste exhibit high proteolytic activity. However, the use of fungi to produce quinoa-derived DPP-IV inhibitory peptides via fermentation remains unexplored. This study focused on isolating fungal strains from soybean pastes and preparing DPP-IV inhibitory peptides from quinoa proteins.

RESULTS: Results suggested that 33 strains were isolated from 37 soybean paste samples, among which 16 strains exhibited high protease activity (>30 U mL-1). Among these, three strains, identified as Zygosaccharomyces sp. (a1), Cladosporium sp. (D1), and Talaromyces sp. (E2), yielded fermentates with the most potent DPP-IV inhibitory activities, with median inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of 4.55 ± 0.10, 4.36 ± 0.04, and 4.16 ± 0.04 mg mL-1, respectively. The fermentation conditions of the three strains were optimized using single-factor tests and orthogonal tests. After desalting and simulated gastrointestinal digestion, the product of strain a1 showed significantly enhanced DPP-IV inhibitory activity, with marked inhibition in murine ileal tissue and Caco-2 cells. Furthermore, the peptide VPQNFA was identified as the most potent DPP-IV inhibitor (IC50 = 190.84 ± 8.58 μmol L-1), acting as a competitive inhibitor and forming a stable VPQNFA-DPP-IV complex via multiple hydrogen bonds.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide a novel strategy for preparing DPP-IV inhibitory peptides via fungal fermentation, which holds potential as diabetes-targeted functional food ingredients. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Sex-Related Differences in Long-Term Graft Failure After Coronary Bypass Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing evidence suggests coronary graft failure is more prevalent in female than in male patients. However, multivariable adjustment for important graft-level confounders such as coronary target territory and preoperative stenosis remains uncommon in existing studies, which may critically confound outcomes. Furthermore, no long-term follow-up data exists, with previous studies limited to the early postoperative period.

METHOD: We performed a retrospective cohort study on patients who received follow-up coronary angiography at our institution, mainly for symptoms, following coronary artery bypass grafting. Patients with available operative reports and with no subsequent percutaneous coronary intervention were included in the study. The primary outcome compared the rate of graft failure between female and male patients, stratified by internal mammary artery (IMA), radial artery (RA), and saphenous vein grafts (SVG). A sensitivity analysis exclusively considered arterial graft failure in patients with available preoperative coronary stenosis data, ensuring robustness of our primary observations. A graft was defined as the segment of conduit supplying one distal coronary anastomosis. All analyses were performed with an exchangeable Generalised Estimating Equations multivariable binary logistic regression model.

RESULTS: Overall, 976 patients, 178 females and 798 males, who received follow-up coronary angiography between August 1997 and March 2020, were included in the study. Mean time to angiography was 8.9±5.9 years postoperative. Females received a total of 519 grafts, including 200 IMA, 258 RA, and 61 SVG. In males, a total of 2,525 grafts were performed, including 946 IMA, 1,268 RA, and 311 SVG. IMA graft failure was more prevalent in females, 9.5% vs 5.3% (odds ratio [OR] 2.60; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28-5.28; p=0.008). RA graft failure was also more common in females, 21.3% vs 11.4% (OR 2.06; 95% CI 1.36-3.13; p<0.001). Cumulative arterial graft (IMA+RA) failure was greater in female than in male patients, 16.2% vs 8.8% (OR 2.22; 95% CI 1.51-3.28; p<0.001). After further adjustment for preoperative coronary stenosis, female sex remained an independent predictor of arterial graft failure, 13.4% vs 8.5% (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.18-3.10; p=0.009). Conversely, the frequency of SVG failure was not different between females and males, 18.0% vs 28.3% (OR 0.62; 95% CI 0.26-1.48; p=0.280).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients who presented for postoperative coronary angiography at our institution, arterial graft failure was more commonly observed in female than in male patients, with no difference for SVGs.

articles.title: Can Pediatric Emergency Medicine Clinicians Identify Solid Organ Injuries Using Contrast-Enhanced FAST in Abdominal Trauma?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-enhanced FAST (cFAST) has demonstrated superior sensitivity to B-mode FAST for detecting solid organ injury in blunt abdominal trauma, yet no prior study has evaluated cFAST image interpretation by pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) clinicians. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of cFAST interpretation for solid organ injuries by PEM clinicians following a web-based didactic.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center study (February-May 2026), PEM clinicians credentialed in B-mode FAST without prior cFAST training completed a web-based didactic. Participants interpreted 12 simulated cases (25 cine clips), evaluating 41 organs (15 injured, 26 non-injured), all reviewed by a cFAST expert or cFAST-trained pediatric radiologist with CT confirmation. Pooled organ-level sensitivity and specificity were calculated with clustering correction using robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Among 41 participants, 1681 organ-level decisions were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 87.97% (95% CI: 84.96%-91.09%), specificity was 89.12% (95% CI: 86.53%-91.78%), negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.77% (95% CI: 90.99%-94.59%), and positive predictive value was 82.34% (95% CI: 78.68%-86.17%). False-negative decisions occurred in 4.4% (n = 74/1681).

CONCLUSION: After a web-based curriculum, PEM clinicians achieved high sensitivity, specificity, and NPV with few missed injuries, supporting future investigation of cFAST as an adjunctive screening tool in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma risk-stratification assessments.

articles.title: Serological Evidence of Leptospira Infection in Sheep in Central Appalachia, United States.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leptospirosis is a globally important zoonotic disease affecting diverse animal species, including sheep. Although multiple studies have reported leptospiral seroprevalence in wildlife, livestock and companion animals in the United States (US), data on sheep populations remain limited. To address this knowledge gap, the present study assessed serological evidence of leptospiral exposure in sheep from Central Appalachia.

METHODS: We conducted a descriptive study using 257 archived serum samples collected through convenience sampling from sheep with no history of vaccination against leptospirosis across 17 flocks in northeastern Tennessee and western Virginia, within the Central Appalachian region. The archived sera were tested for the presence of leptospiral antibodies using the microscopic agglutination test (MAT). Animal-level sample positivity and flock-level positivity were summarized using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 257 archived sheep serum samples from 17 sheep flocks were analysed; the mean number of samples was 15 and ranged from 9 to 18 per sheep flock. Katahdin (24%) and mixed-breed sheep (23%) were the most common breeds, and 99.6% of sampled sheep were female. Most samples were collected in 2024 (88%), primarily during October and November. Overall, 44/257 sheep (17%) were seropositive for leptospiral antibodies, and 15/17 flocks (88%) had at least one seropositive sheep. Among the MAT-positive sheep, serovars Pomona (6.61%; 17/257), Bratislava (5.90%; 15/257), and Icterohaemorrhagiae (5.45%; 14/257) were most prevalent.

CONCLUSIONS: The detection of leptospiral antibodies in sheep from most sampled flocks indicates that exposure to Leptospira spp. occurred across multiple locations within the study area. Although the use of archived samples precludes interpretation of these findings as population-level prevalence estimates, the results provide evidence of leptospiral exposure among sheep in Central Appalachia and support the need for larger, representative studies to better define the prevalence, geographic distribution and potential epidemiological significance of leptospiral exposure in regional sheep populations.

articles.title: Spatial and Temporal Patterns of Blacklegged Tick (Ixodes scapularis) Populations and Lyme Disease Cases in Ontario, Canada, From 2007 to 2019.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lyme disease, caused by Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, is a growing human and animal health concern in Canada due to the rapid range expansion of its vector, the blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis). Various forms of surveillance have been performed for Lyme disease in Ontario, including mandatory human case reporting, passive tick surveillance (tick submissions from the public), active tick surveillance (tick dragging), and canine seroprevalence (proprietary data).

METHODS: This study assessed and compared the temporal trends, seasonality, and spatial distribution of blacklegged ticks and Lyme disease in Ontario using data from four types of surveillance. Time series analysis was applied to visualize temporal trends, followed by a generalized linear auto-regressive moving average modelling approach to assess the trend and seasonal effects. Human Lyme disease incidence per 100,000, passive I. scapularis submission rate per 100,000, B. burgdorferi prevalence in I. scapularis from active surveillance, and canine B. burgdorferi seroprevalence were spatially displayed at the public health unit level.

RESULTS: An increasing trend in human cases, I. scapularis collected via passive and active approaches, and canine seropositivity were observed over time. Ixodes scapularis counts from passive and active surveillance peaked in May and October. Human cases peaked in July, while canine seroprevalence peaked in May. Human case incidence, tick submission rate, B. burgdorferi infection prevalence in I. scapularis from active surveillance, and canine seroprevalence were highest in public health units in eastern Ontario, but this was not consistent from year to year.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates a significant disparity in Ontario's yearly, seasonal, and spatial patterns of I. scapularis, human Lyme disease cases, and canine seropositivity, challenging the comparability of risk across regions. A One Health surveillance approach that systematically collects and integrates animal, human, and environmental data at finer spatial and temporal scales is proposed.

articles.title: Proteome-Wide Genetic Study Identified ENTPD5 as a Candidate Target for Obesity-Related MASLD.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to discover causal plasma proteins for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using trans-ancestry genetic data.

METHODS: We performed proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) for 1256 proteins and MASLD using genome-wide association data from East Asian (n = 85,124) and European (n = 500,348) populations. Colocalization was conducted to validate putative causal proteins for MASLD, followed by two-step MR assessing adiposity mediation. Longitudinal cross-lagged analysis in a bariatric surgery cohort (n = 53) was used to assess temporal associations.

RESULTS: ENTPD5 and APOE showed consistent causal effects in both East Asians and Europeans, both supported by colocalization. Both proteins influenced MASLD risk through adiposity, with BMI mediating 15.7% of the ENTPD5 effect. Longitudinal analysis in the bariatric surgery cohort supported the temporal pathway "ENTPD5→BMI reduction→MASLD remission (assessed by the fatty liver index)," with 29.2% mediation by BMI. Phenome-wide MR revealed a broad pleiotropic profile of ENTPD5, warranting further evaluation of target safety and repurposing potential.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ENTPD5 and APOE are potential causal biomarkers for MASLD and may contribute to its pathogenesis. ENTPD5 represents a candidate target for obesity-related diseases, although its pleiotropic profile warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Association between NT-proBNP levels and future cardiovascular events in systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicenter longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Current strategies for identifying individuals at high risk of cardiovascular events (CVE) in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are lacking. A previous cross-sectional study in SLE showed that NT-proBNP > 133 pg/mL was associated with cardiovascular damage. Our objective was to assess the association between NT-proBNP at a threshold of 133 and incident CVE in SLE.

METHODS: All SLE patients who were included in the randomised controlled trial PLUS between 2007 and 2010 in France were screened. Patients with a history of CVE, an unavailable serum sample at PLUS inclusion, or incomplete follow-up were excluded from the primary analysis. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of CVE during follow-up.

RESULTS: A total of 351 patients (out of 573 included in PLUS) were analyzed. Of these patients, 316 (90.0%) were women with a median age of 38 [30-48] years. Among them, 24 (6.8%) patients experienced at least one CVE that occurred a median of 5 [3-7] years after baseline. Five patients had more than one CVE. In the multivariable analysis, age, dyslipidemia and NT-proBNP were significantly associated with the occurrence of CVE. NT-proBNP was >133pg/mL in 22 (6.3%) patients at baseline. The 133 pg/ml threshold was significantly associated with the occurrence of CVE during follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio [CI 95]: 2.94; 95% CI: 1.12-7.71).

CONCLUSION: A NT-proBNP threshold of 133 pg/ml is associated with future CVE in SLE. SLE care guidelines could consider including NT-proBNP measurement in order to better stratify the cardiovascular prevention strategies in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Selection Collider Bias in Rheumatology.
articles.abstract: Conditions affecting the selection of individuals for a study are a common source of bias in epidemiological and medical research. A recent trend in epidemiology has been to link selection conditions to the concept of collider variables. The effects of selection and associated collider variables depend on the composition of the study population, the study selection process, the target of inference, and methods of data collection and analysis. We give here an introduction to bias arising from selection effects, termed selection collider bias, and discuss ways of avoiding it. We provide illustrations related to two apparent paradoxes in rheumatology that involve smoking. The first paradox is that smoking, a risk factor for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), appears to be protective for disease progression in RA. The second is that smoking is a risk factor for psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but in some studies involving persons with psoriasis it appears to reduce the risk of PsA. Using data from the Gladman-Krembil Psoriatic Arthritis Research Program we examine the effect of smoking on the development of PsA in individuals with psoriasis and resolve the paradox. collider variables, confounding, directed acyclic graphs, observational data, selection effects.

articles.title: PREGNANCY OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY COHORT OF WOMEN WITH REPAIRED TETRALOGY OF FALLOT.
articles.abstract: Most women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) now reach reproductive age, but pregnancy outcomes in contemporary cohorts, particularly after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), remain uncertain. The aim of this study as to assess maternal cardiac, obstetric and neonatal outcomes in a contemporary cohort of women with rTOF. We retrospectively included all pregnancies in women with rTOF followed at a tertiary referral center for complex congenital heart disease (CHD) and high-risk pregnancy between 2013 and 2024. A total of 44 pregnancies in 32 women with rTOF were included, resulting in 45 live births. Severe PR was present in 43% of pregnancies, and 40% had undergone prior PVR. Maternal cardiac events occurred in 6.8%: 2 cases of supraventricular arrhythmias and 1 case of thrombosis on an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead. Among women with prior PVR, transvalvular gradients increased transiently during pregnancy and returned to baseline postpartum. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks, vaginal birth was preferred and cesarean section was performed in 18% of pregnancies. The most frequent adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes were low birth weight (22%) and preterm birth (11%), both associated with lower pre-pregnancy right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) possibly reflecting impaired uteroplacental perfusion related to right ventricular dysfunction. In conclusion, in this contemporary cohort, pregnancy in women with rTOF was associated with low risk of maternal cardiac events, mainly supraventricular arrhythmias. However, low birth weight and preterm birth remained frequent and were associated with lower pre-pregnancy RVEF, underscoring the importance of specialized cardio-obstetric follow-up.

articles.title: Eupnea in severe airflow limitation identifies a Favorably clinically distinct phenotype.
articles.abstract:
RATIONAL: In Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), as disease severity worsens, lung function declines and symptom burden increases. The characteristics of individuals with severe airflow limitation who report no dyspnea (eupnea) are not well described.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether eupneic individuals with severe airflow limitation exhibit different clinical and imaging characteristics compared to those who are dyspneic.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 1713 COPDGene participants with GOLD 3-4, categorized by mMRC dyspnea scores: 0 (eupneic), 1-2, and 3-4. Baseline assessments included spirometry, CT imaging, 6-min walk, and symptom questionnaires. Longitudinal outcomes included FEV1 decline, exacerbation frequency, and mortality. We replicated the analysis in participants with GOLD 1-2, GOLD 0, and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm).

RESULTS: Among GOLD 3-4 participants, 8.2% were eupneic. Compared to those with mMRC 3-4, eupneic individuals had lower prevalence of chronic bronchitis and worse health-related quality of life, better exercise capacity, and less CT emphysema, gas trapping, and PRMfSAD. They experienced fewer exacerbations [incidence rate ratio (IRR) = 0.54; 95% CI: 0.42-0.69; P < 0.001] and had lower mortality (HR = 0.62; 95% CI 0.48-0.80). Rates of longitudinal FEV1 decline were similar across mMRC groups. We observed similar findings in the GOLD 1-2, GOLD 0, and PRISm analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: A modest proportion of individuals with severe respiratory function impairment are eupneic, showing better clinical outcomes and less structural lung damage than their dyspneic counterparts. Our findings support a multidimensional COPD assessment that incorporates symptom burden alongside spirometry.

articles.title: ImmunoPET-guided TIM-3 theranostics enables dynamic visualization of adaptive immune escape and targeted radioimmunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Suboptimal responses and adaptive resistance remain major hurdles to immunotherapy, necessitating noninvasive dynamic in vivo monitoring of emerging immune checkpoints and the subsequent development of targeted interventions. TIM-3 is closely associated with T-cell exhaustion and immunotherapy resistance. Nevertheless, no remarkable breakthroughs have been achieved in TIM-3-targeted therapeutic strategies. Here, we report a first-in-class TIM-3-targeted radio-theranostic platform based on the humanized anti-TIM-3 antibody T21(TQB2618), radiolabeled with 89Zr (zirconium-89) for immunoPET imaging and 177Lu (lutetium-177) for radionuclide therapy. 89Zr-T21 exhibited high TIM-3 affinity and target specificity at protein and cellular levels and enabled clear visualization of TIM-3-positive expression tumors. In a hTIM-3 humanized animal model, 89Zr-T21 initially showed dominant splenic uptake and limited tumor accumulation, consistent with a peripheral TIM-3 antigen sink, whereby abundant TIM-3-expressing immune cells sequester the tracer outside the tumor. Pre-administration of unlabeled T21 reduced splenic sequestration and optimized tumor visualization, with maximal tumor uptake achieved at a 25-fold pre-dosing level. Notably, 89Zr-T21 enabled longitudinal and noninvasive monitoring of immunotherapy-induced TIM-3 remodeling in vivo, revealing time-dependent TIM-3 upregulation following PD-1 blockade and dose-dependent TIM-3 expression changes after immunotherapy. The matched therapeutic agent 177Lu-T21 significantly inhibited A549hTIM-3 tumor growth with favorable safety. Collectively, this study establishes the first TIM-3-directed radio-theranostic framework for imaging adaptive immune resistance and advancing TIM-3 targeted radioimmunotherapy.

articles.title: Metabolic Reprogramming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Liver-Specific Immune Dysfunction, Immunotherapy Resistance, and Translational Biomarker Development.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises in chronically injured, often fibrotic or cirrhotic liver, where metabolism, immunity, vascular and stromal organization, disease etiology, tumor state, and hepatic reserve are tightly interconnected. Although immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies have expanded treatment options for advanced HCC, responses remain heterogeneous because of both primary and acquired resistance. Metabolic reprogramming may shape these outcomes by altering nutrient availability, metabolite accumulation, antigen presentation, immune-cell fitness, stromal organization, and spatial immune access. This review provides an evidence-weighted assessment of major immunometabolic mechanisms in HCC, focusing on the glycolysis-hypoxia-lactate and tryptophan-kynurenine/IDO1 axes, lipid and cholesterol metabolism, purinergic signaling, mitochondrial and redox regulation, and ferroptosis. We emphasize that these pathways are context dependent, with effects determined by cellular source, differentiation state, spatial organization, and tumor-intrinsic versus immune-cell metabolic adaptation. Molecular heterogeneity, etiology, and cirrhosis are considered together, with WNT-β-catenin/CTNNB1-associated states illustrating their intersection with immune organization and ICI response. Because translational maturity varies widely, we distinguish mechanistic evidence, biomarker association, predictive validation, and clinical utility. We propose a framework integrating HCC specificity, primary human validation, cellular and spatial localization, causal immune-functional evidence, treatment-linked and longitudinal assessment, biomarker feasibility, and liver-specific safety. The framework also considers intervention timing and the distinction between primary and acquired ICI resistance. It may guide progression from metabolic discovery to spatially resolved mechanism, biomarker development, pharmacodynamic validation, and clinical evaluation while accounting for cirrhosis-associated remodeling, hepatic reserve, and treatment-related toxicity.

articles.title: Association between long-term blood pressure metrics and progression from prediabetes to diabetes: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have linked blood pressure to incident diabetes, but most used single measurements and did not control for temporal ordering. Whether long-term blood pressure exposure remains associated with progression from prediabetes to diabetes is unclear. We examined this association using long-term systolic blood pressure (SBP) metrics in a prospective cohort.

METHODS: We included 2115 participants with prediabetes at baseline from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). SBP was measured in 2011, 2013, and 2015. Cumulative SBP, time-weighted SBP and SBP burden score were calculated. The outcome was self-reported diabetes at 2018. Multivariable logistic regression was used.

RESULTS: During a follow-up of 7 years, 139 participants (6.6%) progressed to diabetes. After full adjustment, each 20 mmHg increase in time-weighted SBP was associated with 26% increased odds of progression (OR = 1.26, 95% CI 1.03-1.54, P = 0.021). Compared with participants in the lowest quartile (Q1), those in the highest quartile (Q4) had a nearly two-fold increased odds of progression (OR = 1.94, 95% CI 1.14-3.38, P = 0.017; P for trend = 0.012). The association was robust to inverse probability weighting and attenuated after additional adjustment for BMI (OR = 1.20, 95% CI 0.98-1.47). No non-linearity was observed (P = 0.898). The E-value was 1.49.

CONCLUSION: Higher time-weighted SBP was associated with increased odds of progression from prediabetes to diabetes in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. These findings suggest that sustained blood pressure exposure may be a marker for risk stratification in prediabetic individuals.

articles.title: Directional spine-femur bone mineral density discordance: Associations with metabolic factors and lumbar spine T-scores.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lumbar spine-femoral neck BMD discordance is common but usually analyzed as a binary category; the distribution of its direction and distinguishing factors remains poorly described.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cross-sectional study, 2737 patients with paired DXA T-scores were analyzed. Directional discordance was defined by ΔT (lumbar spine minus femoral neck): ≤-1.0 lumbar spine-dominant, -1.0 to 1.0 balanced, ≥1.0 femoral neck-dominant. After multiple imputation, multinomial logistic regression identified factors associated with each discordant pattern versus balanced; binary logistic regression among discordant participants identified factors associated with direction.

RESULTS: Femoral neck-dominant discordance occurred in 952 (34.8%), lumbar spine-dominant in 399 (14.6%), and balanced in 1386 (50.6%). The femoral neck-to-lumbar spine ratio was 2.39, falling to 1.15 after excluding lumbar T-scores ≥+1. Male sex most strongly separated directions (OR 11.59, 95% CI 7.60-17.66). Male sex and higher BMI were associated with femoral neck-dominant discordance versus balanced (OR 3.59, 95% CI 2.93-4.40; OR 1.06 per kg/m2, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). Among discordant patients, higher uric acid (OR 1.004 per μmol/L, 95% CI 1.001-1.006) and diabetes (OR 1.72, 95% CI 1.15-2.57) accompanied femoral neck-dominant direction; lower uric acid (OR 0.997, 95% CI 0.996-0.999) and borderline lower diabetes prevalence (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.53-1.01; P = 0.059) accompanied lumbar spine-dominant direction. Fracture-related diagnoses were recorded in 12.5% of the lumbar spine-dominant group, 6.8% of the femoral neck-dominant group, and 8.4% of the balanced group; lumbar spine-dominant discordance was associated with higher prevalence (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.01-2.13), attenuating after mean T-score adjustment (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.89-1.90).

CONCLUSIONS: Femoral neck-dominant discordance was more common, but the difference narrowed after excluding high lumbar T-scores. The directions had distinct correlates. Lumbar spine-dominant discordance was associated with more fracture-related diagnoses, not independent of overall bone mass.

articles.title: Inflammatory biomarkers in late-life depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis of interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein.
articles.abstract: Late-life depression (LLD)-encompassing both major depressive disorder and clinically significant depressive symptoms-affects approximately 1-5% of adults aged 60 and older when defined by strict diagnostic criteria, while clinically significant depressive symptoms affect 8-16% of community-dwelling older adults. Antidepressant treatment in older adults is challenging due to smaller effect sizes, higher treatment resistance, and greater risk of adverse effects, pointing to unique, understudied mechanisms. The inflammatory hypothesis of depression and the "inflammaging" theory together suggest that chronic peripheral and central inflammation drive LLD pathogenesis. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized data from 18 observational studies (1,593 LLD patients, 2,776 healthy controls) to evaluate peripheral levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, C-reactive protein (CRP), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). All four markers were significantly elevated in LLD (Hedges' g = 0.52-0.80, all p < 0.01), with high between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 83-90%). Sensitivity analyses restricting to studies with adequate confounding adjustment attenuated effect sizes, particularly for CRP (57% reduction) and TNF-α (36% reduction), but all markers remained significant. Subgroup analyses identified study population, geographic region, medication status, and sample size as potential effect moderators, but these should be interpreted as study-level moderators rather than evidence for patient-level subtypes. These findings are consistent with an inflammatory contribution to LLD, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and the magnitude of effect may be partially inflated by incomplete control of somatic comorbidities. Future studies should employ individual participant data meta-analyses with multi-marker profiling to test whether distinct inflammatory subtypes exist.

articles.title: Oroxylin A attenuates pneumonia via HSP90α-dependent suppression of macrophage ferroptosis-mediated inflammation.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the protective activity of Oroxylin A in pneumonia and to clarify the mechanisms involved, particularly those associated with macrophage-driven inflammation and ferroptosis. Pneumonia was induced in mice and treated with Oroxylin A, followed by evaluation of lung injury, inflammatory cytokine production, and ferroptosis-related markers. Pulmonary immune alterations were further characterized by single-cell RNA sequencing. Target-responsive accessibility profiling, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assays were subsequently applied to explore potential molecular targets, followed by functional verification in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged macrophages. Oroxylin A alleviated body weight loss, pathological lung injury, alveolar inflammation, and inflammatory cytokine production in mice with pneumonia. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified macrophages as a major responsive population and showed that Oroxylin A modulated inflammation- and ferroptosis-related transcriptional programs. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, Oroxylin A suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, whereas these effects were attenuated by erastin. Heat shock protein 90-alpha (HSP90α) was further identified as a potential binding target of Oroxylin A. In silico perturbation analyses suggested that HSP90α participates in ferroptosis-related biological processes. Functional experiments showed that HSP90α overexpression weakened the anti-inflammatory and anti-ferroptotic actions of Oroxylin A, whereas HSP90α knockdown suppressed inflammatory cytokine expression and increased GPX4 expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that Oroxylin A alleviates pneumonia-associated inflammation through an HSP90α-dependent mechanism involving the regulation of macrophage ferroptosis.

articles.title: Biological slow-release acyl-homoserine lactones carriers enhance volatile organic compounds removal in biotrickling filters.
articles.abstract: Biological purification systems for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) often face limitations, including slow start-up, susceptibility to shock loading, and competitive inhibition during the treatment of mixed VOCs. In this study, a biological slow-release acyl-homoserine lactones (AHLs) carrier was developed by immobilizing AHL-secreting bacteria (Bacillus sp. S8) and applied in biotrickling filters (BTFs) to treat single xylene and mixed VOCs (ethylbenzene and xylene). The results demonstrated that the slow-release AHLs carriers significantly shortened the start-up period, maintained stable performance under shock loading, and improved recovery following starvation stress. In the treatment of mixed VOCs, the AHLs-enhanced BTFs achieved final removal efficiencies of 87 % and 78 % with high mineralization rates, significantly outperforming the control (65 %). Biofilm studies revealed that the carriers promoted biofilm formation by enhancing extracellular polymeric substances secretion and microbial adhesion. Furthermore, they increased microbial activity within the biofilm, as evidenced by higher ATP content and a greater proportion of viable bacteria. The carriers also optimized biofilm structure and surface characteristics, enriched beneficial microbial genera (e.g., Paraburkholderia and Burkholderia), and upregulated genes associated with carbohydrate metabolism and membrane transport. These findings demonstrate the potential of the slow-release AHLs carrier strategy to regulate biofilm ecosystems and enhance biological VOC purification, offering new insights into developing efficient biofilms for industrial VOC treatment under complex conditions.

articles.title: Inflammation and the Association of Early-stage Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Incident Cardiovascular Disease and All-cause Mortality: Findings from the CARDIA and MESA Cohorts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data exist on whether inflammation modifies the association between early-stage cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and clinical events.

METHODS: We included 9,894 participants free of cardiovascular disease (CVD) from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study (CARDIA, Year 20, 2005-2006) and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA, Exam 1, 2000-2002). We examined whether interleukin-6 (IL-6; primary) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP; ≥2 mg/L; secondary) modified associations of early-stage CKM syndrome (stages 2-3 vs 0-1) with incident CVD and all-cause mortality. IL-6 was dichotomized at cohort- and sex-specific medians. Cohort-stratified Cox models were adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, smoking, and physical activity; multiplicative and additive effect modification were assessed.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 1,635 atherosclerotic CVD events, 567 heart failure events, and 2,593 deaths occurred. After adjustment for CKM stage, IL-6 at or above the median was associated with higher risks of atherosclerotic CVD (hazard ratio, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.33-1.64), heart failure (1.69; 1.41-2.03), and mortality (1.48; 1.36-1.61); hsCRP associations were smaller. IL-6 showed additive effect modification with CKM stage for atherosclerotic CVD (relative excess risk due to interaction, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.17-1.46) but no multiplicative effect modification (P = 0.59), and no effect modification for heart failure or mortality. hsCRP showed no consistent effect modification.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher IL-6 and hsCRP were each associated with higher cardiovascular and mortality risks independent of early-stage CKM syndrome. IL-6 showed additive effect modification with CKM stage for atherosclerotic CVD, indicating a positive relative excess risk due to interaction among adults with CKM stages 2-3.

articles.title: Spatial coupling between anosmia-related cortical alterations and regional gene expression: an imaging transcriptomics study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of anosmia on brain cortical structure and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated causal associations between anosmia and cortical alterations using a multi-modal approach combining neuroimaging and genetics.

METHODS: High-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging was acquired from 52 patients with anosmia and 50 healthy controls to extract cortical surface area (SA) and cortical thickness (TH). Mendelian randomization (MR) was employed to assess the causal effect of anosmia on cortical structure using summary statistics from the ENIGMA consortium. Furthermore, integrating gene expression data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA), partial least squares regression (PLSR) and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) were used to identify genes associated with changes in SA and TH due to anosmia. Gene enrichment analysis and cell type-specific analysis were then performed to explore the potential molecular mechanisms.

RESULTS: Patients exhibited significantly reduced SA in the left rostral anterior cingulate and superior temporal sulcus, while TH was increased in regions including the left cuneus and supramarginal gyrus. MR analysis identified 11 cortical structural features nominally associated with anosmia, although none survived multiple comparison correction across 138 tests. Transcriptomic analysis identified genes correlated with these structural alterations, which were significantly enriched in synaptic pathways (e.g., postsynaptic membrane modulation) and specifically implicated GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.

CONCLUSION: Anosmia is causally associated with distinct cortical structural alterations. These regional changes are spatially coupled with molecular signatures involving synaptic function and neuronal plasticity, providing novel insights into the potential pathophysiology of olfactory loss.

articles.title: Can AI-assisted analysis of antidepressant drug online reviewers (ADORE) inform real-world use of antidepressants?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antidepressant selection is constrained by limited comparative-effectiveness data, with randomized trials measuring symptom reduction rather than patient-reported tolerability. We tested whether AI-assisted analysis of patient-written online reviews recovers drug-level tolerability signals that converge with the strongest randomized evidence.

METHODS: We did a cross-sectional analysis of 8348 reviews of 16 antidepressants for major depressive disorder posted to Drugs.com (February 2008-March 2025; ≥1 month reported use). Two independent large language models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) classified each review across 17 clinical dimensions using identical structured prompts; a stratified 100-review subsample (1700 classifications per reviewer) was independently rated by two experts, with all agreement statistics highly significant. We compared per-drug top-rating prevalence with Cipriani et al.'s 2018 network meta-analysis retention and efficacy odds ratios (Spearman correlation).

RESULTS: Mean inter-LLM Cohen's κ was 0.81; expert reviewers agreed substantially with the dual-AI consensus (mean κ = 0.75 and 0.80). Top rating correlated strongly with Cipriani et al. retention odds ratios (ρ = +0.79, p < 0.001) but not with efficacy odds ratios (ρ = -0.14, p = 0.64). Within-SNRI heterogeneity was substantial. Emotional blunting was the strongest negative predictor of satisfaction (OR 0.20).

LIMITATIONS: Reviews are from a single platform and self-selected users; drug-level comparisons rest on few agents; and the design is cross-sectional and ecological.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-classified patient reviews recover the drug-level tolerability signal of randomized retention data and surface within-class heterogeneity, particularly among SNRIs, as a hypothesis-generating signal. Within the comparable-efficacy range of contemporary antidepressants, tolerability, especially emotional blunting, principally correlates with patient satisfaction.

articles.title: Surgical Management of Thoracic Aortic Mural Thrombus: Operative Strategy and Early Outcomes in a Two-Decade Retrospective Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Thoracic aortic mural thrombus (TAMT) is a rare but life-threatening condition due to the risk of systemic embolization. In this single-center retrospective surgical case series, we evaluated perioperative management, operative strategy and outcomes after surgical thrombectomy for TAMT, a condition with limited evidence and no established treatment standard.

METHODS: Between 2004 and 2025, 14 patients (median age 57.5 years; 9 male) underwent open thrombectomy for TAMT at our institution. TAMT was defined as an intraluminal, imaging-confirmed thrombus attached to a non-aneurysmal and non-dissected aortic wall without identifiable cardiac or proximal embolic source.

RESULTS: Acute systemic embolization represented the first clinical manifestation in the majority of patients, including stroke (n = 6), limb ischemia (n = 6) and visceral ischemia (n = 2). Thrombus localization included the ascending aorta (n=1), aortic arch (n=6), combined ascending aorta and arch (n=5), arch and descending thoracic aorta (n=1), and multiple thoracic aortic levels (n=1). All procedures were performed under cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic circulatory arrest allowing complete thrombus removal in all patients. One patient died within 30 days in hospital due to sepsis. Two disabling postoperative strokes and one new postoperative peripheral embolic event occurred. Median follow-up time was 3.5 months (IQR 0.4-60.7). No persistent or recurrent TAMT was observed during imaging follow-up (median imaging follow up 0.6 months).

CONCLUSION: Open surgical thrombectomy with hypothermic circulatory arrest permitted complete macroscopic thrombus removal in this selected surgical cohort and was technically feasible.

articles.title: Effects of Aging and High-Fat Diet on Hepatic Fatty Acid Composition and Delta-6 Desaturase Activity in Male Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with altered hepatic fatty acid composition, including reduced omega-3 fatty acid content. Whether these reductions relate to impaired long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid synthesis via reduced delta-6 desaturase (D6D) activity or altered dietary α-linolenic acid (ALA) intake remains unclear.

METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed low-fat (LFD; 16% kcal fat) or high-fat (HFD; 45% kcal fat) diets containing equivalent amounts of flaxseed oil for 2 or 6 months. Body weight, glucose tolerance, as well as hepatic triacylglycerol (TAG), TAG and phospholipid fatty acid composition, gene expression, and microsomal D6D activity were measured.

RESULTS: HFD feeding increased body weight and impaired glucose tolerance after 2 months but did not increase hepatic TAG until 6 months compared with LFD feeding. The hepatic n-6 / n-3 ratio was consistently elevated with HFD-feeding. Fads2 and Elovl5 expression increased only after 6 months of a HFD, whereas Fads1 expression was higher at both time points. In contrast, microsomal D6D activity was reduced with a HFD at 2 months and declined further with age, with no effect of diet evident at 6 months.

CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that hepatic fatty acid remodeling precedes overt steatosis during HFD feeding compared to LFD feeding despite equivalent dietary ALA intake. However, aging exerts a stronger influence on hepatic D6D activity than diet, highlighting the complexity of hepatic lipid remodeling during the development of MASLD.

articles.title: From Bernoulli to Bedside: Fifty Years of Doppler Echocardiography for Valvular Pressure Gradients: Lessons in Translating Ideas into Clinical Practice.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

articles.title: Spatiotemporal coordination of a bacteria-targeted ultrasound-light cascade for synergistic eradication of MRSA biofilm-associated infections.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Restricted delivery of antimicrobial agents into biofilms limits the treatment of implant-associated infections. Here, we developed UBI₂₉-₄₁-functionalized lipid nanobubbles co-loaded with vancomycin (Van) and an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizer (UBI-Van/AIE@NBs) for sequential ultrasound (US)-assisted and photodynamic treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilms. The formulation exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 480.3 ± 40.8 nm and a positive zeta potential. US increased cumulative Van and AIE release to approximately 82% and 74%, respectively, within 5 min, compared with 27-28% without US. Cell-free probe assays supported AIE-associated reactive oxygen species generation during white-light irradiation. Fluorescence imaging suggested enhanced biofilm association and prolonged signal retention at the infection site. In vitro, sequential US and light exposure reduced residual biofilm biomass and viable bacterial counts more effectively than either stimulus alone, with UBI-Van/AIE@NBs producing the lowest residual biomass and bacterial recovery under combined treatment. In a murine titanium implant-associated MRSA infection model, the combined regimen reduced implant-associated bacterial burden and accelerated wound closure, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen organization, and increased CD31 staining. The formulation exhibited low cytotoxicity and hemolysis, without apparent major-organ injury or significant changes in serum biochemical parameters under the tested conditions. These findings support integrating peptide functionalization, US-enhanced cargo release, and photodynamic treatment as a preclinical strategy for localized management of implant-associated MRSA biofilm infections.

articles.title: Complementing pharmacological interventions: How patient engagement shapes outcomes in a pharmacist-led weight management program serving desert communities.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a multifactorial condition influenced by interconnected biological, psychosocial, genetic, and environmental factors. Numerous interventions, including lifestyle modification and pharmacological treatments, have demonstrated meaningful benefits in weight management. However, psychosocial factors associated with favorable weight loss remain underexplored.

OBJECTIVES: This study examined the associations between patient engagement, weight change, and program satisfaction within a clinical pharmacist-led weight management clinic serving underserved desert communities using real-world data.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study combined retrospective and prospective designs, utilizing real-world patient registry data in desert communities. English- or Spanish-speaking adults who were consistently enrolled in the pharmacist-led weight management clinic for at least 3 months were included. A 24-item survey was developed to assess patient engagement and program satisfaction on a 4-point agreement scale. Following face and content validation, surveys were administered via telephone to eligible participants. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, survey validation, correlation analyses, and path analysis.

RESULTS: Among 733 eligible patients, survey responders (n=166) were primarily female, White, with a mean age of 57 years, some college education, annual household income ($51-100K), and private insurance. Survey respondents demonstrated a greater percentage of weight loss compared with non-respondents, even stratification by drug class. Higher patient engagement was positively associated with both weight loss (β1=11.4, p<.001) and program satisfaction (β3=0.155, p <.001). While engagement strongly predicted program satisfaction, weight loss alone did not (β2=-0.001, p =.278). Patient feedback was largely positive and centered on perceived effectiveness, service accessibility, quality of care, and clinical expertise, whereas negative feedback focused on medication availability and insufficient support.

CONCLUSION: Comprehensive pharmacist-led care models may improve weight management outcomes by enhancing patient education, medication access, and coordinated care in desert communities.

articles.title: SH2B1 modulates hepatic lipid droplet homeostasis and is associated with HSC70/LAMP2A-related PLIN2 regulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: SH2B adaptor protein 1 (SH2B1) participates in metabolic regulation, but its role in hepatic lipid-droplet homeostasis remains unclear. We investigated its role and underlying mechanisms in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Human and mouse GEO transcriptomic datasets and liver single-cell RNA-sequencing data were analyzed to characterize SH2B1 expression and identify lipid-metabolism-related candidates. SH2B1 knockdown and overexpression were performed in palmitate/oleate (P/O)-treated AML12 hepatocytes, and lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 A (LAMP2A) knockdown was combined with SH2B1 overexpression to assess its functional contribution. Molecular docking explored potential interactions, while reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence assessed protein association and colocalization, respectively. In vivo, mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) and subsequently underwent AAV-mediated hepatic Sh2b1 knockdown.

KEY FINDINGS: SH2B1 expression was reduced in human and murine fatty liver datasets and was predominantly detected in hepatocytes. Perilipin 2 (PLIN2) expression was inversely correlated with SH2B1 across GSE165855 samples. P/O exposure reduced SH2B1 expression and increased PLIN2 levels and lipid accumulation. SH2B1 knockdown increased PLIN2 abundance and lipid storage, whereas overexpression produced the opposite phenotype. Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation supported an association between SH2B1 and heat shock cognate 70 (HSC70), and immunofluorescence demonstrated their colocalization. SH2B1 manipulation bidirectionally altered LAMP2A abundance. LAMP2A knockdown attenuated the reductions in PLIN2 abundance and lipid accumulation induced by SH2B1 overexpression. Hepatic Sh2b1 knockdown exacerbated HFD-induced hepatic lipid accumulation and liver injury, with lower LAMP2A and higher PLIN2 levels.

SIGNIFICANCE: SH2B1 regulates hepatic lipid-droplet homeostasis, with LAMP2A contributing to its effects on PLIN2 abundance and lipid accumulation.

articles.title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand.

RESULTS: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06396429.

articles.title: Neutrophils suppress the anti-fibrotic activity of natural killer cells in the liver through STAT3-HLA-E-NKG2A/CD94 axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver fibrosis is a critical pathological stage in chronic liver disease progression, ultimately leading to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The role of neutrophils in liver fibrosis, particularly their effects on natural killer (NK) cells, remains poorly understood.

METHODS: Hepatic neutrophil accumulation was characterized in mouse liver fibrosis models and in human liver fibrosis tissue arrays. In carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄)-induced liver fibrosis models, neutrophils were depleted via anti-Ly6G antibody or their hepatic infiltration was blocked by a CXCR2 antagonist, followed by fibrosis evaluation and NK cell phenotype/function analysis. Transwell assay, apoptosis assay, bulk RNA sequencing, STAT3 inhibitor, anti-HLA-E and anti-NKG2A antibodies were used to explore cell-cell interactions and the underlying mechanisms.

RESULTS: Neutrophils were significantly accumulated in human and mouse fibrotic livers and localized adjacent to activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Neutrophil depletion or infiltration blockade significantly attenuated liver fibrosis and reversed NK cell exhaustion. HSCs promoted neutrophil accumulation by inducing chemotaxis and inhibiting apoptosis. Mechanistically, HSC-derived interleukin-6 (IL-6) activated the JAK/STAT3 pathway to upregulate the expression of HLA-E on neutrophils, which engaged NKG2A/CD94 on NK cells to suppress NK cell anti-fibrotic function via cell-cell contact. HLA-E blockade and STAT3 inhibitor-loaded nanoparticles abrogated neutrophil-mediated NK cell dysfunction.

CONCLUSION: This study clarifies the role of neutrophils in liver fibrosis and identifies a novel mechanism by which HSC-reprogrammed neutrophils impair NK cell function, thereby providing potential therapeutic targets against liver fibrosis.

articles.title: What every intensivist should know about pharmacology.
Systolic blood pressure variability predicts poor functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke: Influence of sex and vascular risk factors.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Although hypertension is a well-established risk factor for stroke, the factors influencing blood pressure fluctuations and its impact on the prognosis of patients with ischemic stroke remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the factors associated with blood pressure variability parameters, including systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), mean arterial pressure (MBP), and pulse pressure (PP), and their impact on functional outcomes in patients with AIS.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 414 patients with AIS who were admitted within 24 h of stroke onset between 2021 and 2023. BPV was quantified using the standard deviation (SD) of blood pressure measurements collected during days 2-4 of hospitalization. The primary outcome was a poor functional result at 180 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for age, sex, comorbidities, baseline stroke severity (NIHSS), and mean arterial pressure levels.

RESULTS: Of the 414 patients, 178 (43.0%) experienced poor functional outcomes at 6 months. In univariate analysis, higher SD of SBP, DBP, PP, and MBP were all significantly associated with poor outcomes. However, after full multivariable adjustment, only SBP variability remained a significant independent predictor. Patients in the highest quartile of SBP variability (SD SBP ≥ 18.7 mmHg) had a significantly higher risk of poor outcomes compared to those in lower quartiles (Adjusted OR 2.50; 95% CI 1.16-5.36). Subgroup analyses revealed that high SBP variability was particularly detrimental in female patients and those with pre-existing hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia.

CONCLUSIONS: Increased systolic blood pressure variability during the subacute phase of AIS is independently associated with poor 6-month functional outcomes. Female patients, as well as those with hypertension, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia, have an increased risk of poor functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke who have large blood pressure variability. These findings suggest that SBP stability may be an important prognostic indicator and a potential treatment target, especially for female patients and those with hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. Future research should investigate whether interventions specifically aimed at minimizing SBP fluctuations can improve neurological recovery in stroke survivors.

articles.title: Day-of-Surgery Hyperglycemia and Early Coded Surgical Site Infection in Open Abdominal Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Surgical site infections (SSIs) contribute to morbidity after open abdominal surgery. We estimated relative and absolute associations between day-of-surgery glucose bands and early coded SSI, including among patients without documented diabetes.

METHODS: This retrospective study used propensity score-matched TriNetX cohorts of adults undergoing open abdominal surgery. Three separate comparisons were evaluated: 140-160 versus <140, 160-180 versus <160, and ≥180 versus <180 mg/dL. Glucose timing relative to surgery was unknown. The outcome was International Classification of Diseases-10 T81.4 recorded from the index date through day 7. Analyses were repeated excluding documented diabetes (E08-E13).

RESULTS: SSI risks were 2.1% versus 1.8% (risk ratio [RR], 1.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.08-1.25), 2.3% versus 1.9% (RR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.09-1.27), and 2.2% versus 1.8% (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.12-1.30) for the three respective comparisons. Associations were also observed after excluding documented diabetes (160-180 versus <160 mg/dL: RR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.13-1.39).

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated day-of-surgery glucose was associated with early coded SSI in separate matched comparisons. Unknown glucose timing, index-date infections, and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings do not establish causality, a dose-response relationship, or benefit from lowering glucose to a particular target.

articles.title: Centrality of the periphery: Small muscle mass to bypass O2 transport limitations and maximize the benefits of exercise training in heart failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a complex, systemic cardiovascular condition characterized by a severe impairment in O2 transport to skeletal muscle that drives exercise intolerance and reduces quality of life. Although exercise training (ET) is a cornerstone of HF clinical management, patients often exhibit limited improvements in peak oxygen uptake (  V ̇ O 2 peak   ) following traditional whole-body, aerobic exercise recruiting a large muscle mass (e.g., cycling). In patients with HF, adaptations within skeletal muscle (e.g., capillarization) exert a proportionally greater influence on changes in  V ̇ O 2 peak   than adaptations in cardiac performance. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms by which traditional ET prescription may be suboptimal to elicit peripheral adaptations and argue that dynamic exercise recruiting only a small muscle mass (e.g., quadriceps) may be more effective in achieving this goal. Indeed, small muscle mass exercise reduces the cardiovascular restraints imposed by the failing heart, allowing the muscle to reach much greater metabolic rates and to be exposed to much larger degrees of homeostatic perturbations, a key factor triggering adaptations in O2 transport and utilization at the peripheral level. The intent of this review is to discuss the influence of muscle mass on exercise tolerance and adaptations to ET in HF, with the ultimate goal of promoting the integration of small muscle mass exercise into contemporary cardiac rehabilitation programmes.

articles.title: Pulmonary Vein Reconnection Burden and Extra-Pulmonary Vein Ablation During Second Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation in the Pre-Pulsed-Field Ablation Era: A Multicenter Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary procedural characteristics of second catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate procedural characteristics and clinical implications of pulmonary vein (PV) reconnection during second CA for AF.

METHODS: We analyzed 854 patients who underwent second CA for AF between April 2021 and March 2024 at nine institutions before the clinical adoption of pulsed-field ablation. Patients were stratified according to the number of reconnected PVs identified during the procedures: none (0), single (1), and multiple (≥ 2). The primary endpoint was freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence, assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: During second CA, PV reconnections (21% per vein) were identified and re-isolated in all affected PVs. Patients with no PV reconnection accounted for 55.5% (n = 474) of the cohort and underwent extra-PV ablation more frequently than those with single (n = 146) or multiple (n = 234) reconnected PVs. During a median follow-up of 706 days, multiple reconnected PVs with subsequent re-isolation were associated with a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than no PV reconnection. This association remained significant after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.95; p = 0.023) and was more pronounced in patients without symptomatic heart failure (p for interaction = 0.009). Enlarged left atrial diameter, non-paroxysmal AF, and symptomatic heart failure were also independently associated with recurrence, whereas additional extra-PV ablation was not.

CONCLUSION: Re-isolation of multiple reconnected PVs was independently associated with a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence after second CA for AF, particularly in patients without symptomatic heart failure.

articles.title: Real-World Performance of a Novel Wearable Cardioverter-Defibrillator System: Primary Results From a National Prospective Post-Approval Registry Study (ACE-PAS).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Wearable cardioverter defibrillators (WCDs) protect patients at elevated risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD) but are effective only when worn. The ASSURE WCD was designed to address historical limitations related to false alarms and patient adherence. The objective of this post-approval study was to assess safety and effectiveness in a large, real-world cohort.

METHODS: The study population was comprised of patients meeting WCD indications who were fitted with the ASSURE WCD. The primary effectiveness endpoint was overall shock conversion success for ventricular tachycardia (VT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF) (performance goal ≥ 89%), and the primary safety endpoint was the incidence of inappropriate shocks (performance goal ≤ 0.0075 per patient-month).

RESULTS: Among 21 612 patients (mean age 64.0 years, 33.9% female), median daily use was 23.1 h/day (IQR 16.1-23.9) over 54 days (IQR 20-97). WCD indications included cardiomyopathy (63.8%), post-myocardial infarction (19.3%), sustained VT/VF (11.9%) and ICD explant/other (5.0%). Both primary effectiveness and safety endpoints were met. All 303 VT/VF shock events in 261 patients (1.2%) were successfully converted, yielding an overall shock conversion success of 100% (95% CI: 98.8%-100%), with first-shock success of 97.0% (95% CI: 94.4%-98.5%). The incidence rate of inappropriate shocks was 0.0065 per patient-month (95% CI: 0.0057-0.0073). False-positive alarms occurred in 6.0% of patients. The 90-day Kaplan-Meier estimated risk of VT/VF was 3.4%, varying by WCD indication (p < 0.001) but not by left ventricular ejection fraction (p = 0.16).

CONCLUSION: In routine practice, the ASSURE WCD effectively terminated VT/VF with low false alarm and inappropriate shock rates and high patient adherence. Most VT/VF events occurred early during WCD wear. Collectively, these findings provide important contemporary evidence to inform the selection of patients who may benefit from WCD therapy during periods of elevated arrhythmic risk.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05135403.

articles.title: Exercise and insulin independently stimulate galactose uptake into human skeletal muscle.
articles.abstract: Carbohydrate choice affects glycaemic responses during and after exercise, particularly for individuals with impaired glucose regulation. Galactose causes smaller glycaemic excursions than glucose but is thought to require hepatic conversion to glucose via the Leloir pathway before peripheral use. Whether galactose is directly taken up by skeletal muscle, and whether this is regulated by exercise and insulin remains unclear. In this randomised, controlled crossover trial, eight healthy men (age 68 ± 4 years; body mass index 24.7 ± 2.1 kg/m2) completed two 4 h study days, with and without a hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (1.0 mU/kg/min). Galactose turnover was assessed using a primed-constant galactose infusion. Participants performed one-legged, high-intensity knee-extension exercise at maximal capacity, with the contralateral leg as a non-exercised control. Skeletal muscle galactose uptake was quantified by dynamic [1 8F]FDGal positron emission tomography (PET), and arteriovenous (AV) exchange across the leg was determined from femoral blood samples combined with [1 5O]H2O PET-measured leg perfusion. Exercise and insulin markedly increased galactose uptake (exercise effect: P < 0.001; insulin effect: P < 0.001; interaction: P = 0.0769). PET analysis showed that exercise primarily increased tracer influx (K1), while insulin increased intracellular trapping (k3) and modestly reduced efflux (k2). Plasma galactose concentrations were low (0.2 ± 0.1 mmol/L) and galactose AV exchange across the leg did not differ across conditions. Human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose, and this is stimulated by exercise and insulin. This challenges the assumption that hepatic conversion is required before peripheral utilisation. Future studies should determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically relevant extent. KEY POINTS: Galactose causes smaller spikes in blood sugar than glucose, and it has long been assumed that the body must first convert galactose into glucose in the liver before peripheral use. Using positron emission tomography imaging with the galactose analogue 2-[1 8F]fluoro-2-deoxygalactose in combination with a one-legged knee-extension ergometer, we demonstrated that human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose. Both exercise and insulin markedly increased skeletal muscle galactose uptake, with an additive effect when combined. Exercise primarily increased galactose uptake by enhancing muscle blood flow, whereas insulin exerted its effect by promoting phosphorylation and intracellular trapping. Further studies are required to determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically meaningful extent.

articles.title: [Screening, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of hepatitis C virus-related liver disease].
articles.abstract: Hepatitis C viral (HCV) infection has become curable. Eradication of the virus is essential from individual as well as from social aspects. Treatment in Hungary is based on a national consensus guideline, updated six-monthly. If there is no contraindication, demonstration of viral replication is the indication of therapy. Only direct-acting antiviral therapies are to be applied. At the time of publication of this guideline, only pan-genotypic combinations are available in Hungary. Based on fibrosis stage and on other (clinical, epidemiological, occupational, etc.) factors, a treatment prioritization system is available - however, all diagnosed infected individuals have access to reimbursed therapy nowadays. All infected individuals should be diagnosed and treated in a timely manner. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(46): 1847-1861.

articles.title: High-Risk Mobility and Interruption in HIV Treatment Among Men in Malawi: Secondary Analysis of Two Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Mobility is a key risk factor for interruption in HIV treatment (IIT). However, little is known about which aspects of mobility confer greatest risk (i.e., comprise high-risk mobility) and whether people prone to high-risk mobility can be identified prior to events. We conducted a secondary analysis of the IDEaL and ENGAGE trials (ClinicalTrials.gov #NCT04858243; #NCT05137210), which tested interventions to improve 6-month ART engagement among men living with HIV (MLHIV; ≥15 years old) not in care (i.e., ART naïve or missed refill by ≥ 28 days) in Malawi. We used baseline and endline (4-7 months post-enrollment) surveys and medical chart reviews of established ART clients experiencing IIT at enrollment who re-initiated ART during trials. We used Poisson regressions with random effects and receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves to identify mobility characteristics most strongly associated with repeat IIT (≥ 28 days late for ART appointment during 6-month trial period) and to identify associated baseline characteristics. Of 1,119 men, 454 (41%) experienced repeat IIT; 314 (28%) took ≥ 3-night trips during the 6-month trial period. Trips ≥ 30 nights (aIRR 1.51, 95%CI 1.14-1.99, AUC 0.648) and lasting longer than expected (aIRR 1.50, 95%CI 1.15-1.96, AUC 0.653) best predicted repeat IIT (specificity 90%). No sociodemographic or pre-trial mobility variables were independently associated with high-risk mobility during the trial period. Mobility is a key risk factor for IIT among men in Malawi, and we found "high-risk mobility" to be trips ≥ 30 nights and/or that lasted longer than expected. We were unable to predict which men would experience high-risk mobility.

articles.title: TRIM proteins in tuberculosis: from host defense to pathogen evasion and therapeutic innovation.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), remains a major global health challenge, owing in part to the ability of the pathogen to evade host immunity and the growing burden of drug-resistant disease. This review examines the role of tripartite motif-containing (TRIM) proteins, a family of E3 ubiquitin ligases that regulate diverse aspects of host immunity during MTB infection. Several TRIM proteins, including TRIM16, TRIM22, TRIM27, and TRIM32, have been implicated in host-protective responses by regulating autophagy, lysosomal function, and inflammatory signaling, thereby contributing to intracellular bacterial control. In contrast, at least three TRIMs, TRIM21, TRIM25, and TRIM14, have been associated with impaired bacterial control: MTB can exploit TRIM21-dependent ferritinophagy to increase intracellular iron availability and create conditions favorable for bacterial persistence, and TRIM21 also limits host resistance through a ligase-independent mechanism in macrophages and mice; TRIM25 overexpression increases intracellular bacterial survival; and loss of TRIM14, which restrains type I interferon signaling, improves bacterial control in macrophages. Differences in TRIM expression among individuals with latent TB infection, active disease, and drug-resistant TB have also raised the possibility that selected TRIMs could serve as biomarkers of disease status. Mechanistic studies further point to TRIM-associated pathways as potential targets for host-directed therapy, either by limiting pathways exploited by MTB, such as TRIM21-mediated iron acquisition, or by strengthening protective responses such as the TRIM27-TFEB pathway.
