However, the functions of individual TRIM proteins are context dependent, and functional overlap among family members, together with the limited amount of in vivo evidence, remains an important challenge. Defining the specific contributions of TRIM proteins to MTB infection will therefore require further mechanistic, animal, and clinical studies before their diagnostic or therapeutic potential can be established.

articles.title: [Urinary stone prevention: non-surgical options].
articles.abstract: Kidney stone disease is a chronic, recurrence-prone condition with increasing prevalence worldwide, placing a significant burden on healthcare systems. Its development is influenced by lifestyle factors, metabolic syndrome, genetic predisposition, and environmental factors. Based on their chemical composition, stones can be classified as calcium-oxalate, uric acid, infection-related, or cystine types, each requiring specific therapeutic an preventive strategies. Key elements of prevention include adequate fluid intake, a balanced diet, optimization of urinary pH, and targeted pharmacological therapy, including citrate, phytate, tiopronin, and methionine. In infection-related stones, stone removal and antibiotic therapy are essential, whereas in uric acid stones, urinary alkalinization is critical for reducing recurrence. Cystine stones are rare but represent a significant therapeutic challenge. Long-term treatment success relies on active patient participation, consistent adherence to therapeutic recommendations, and regular medical follow-up. A multidisciplinary approach combined with patient education can substantially contribute to recurrence prevention and improvement of quality of life. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(46): 1862-1866.

articles.title: Circulating C-Terminal Agrin Fragment is Associated with Impaired Physical Performance in Aging and Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating C-terminal agrin fragment (CAF22) is a biomarker of neuromuscular junction degradation and sarcopenia. However, its relationship with objective measures of physical performance has not been systematically evaluated. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined associations of circulating CAF22 concentrations with gait speed and Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores in aging and chronic disease populations.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched to identify studies reporting associations between circulating CAF22 concentrations and gait speed and/or SPPB scores. Correlation coefficients were extracted, transformed to Fisher's z values, and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Risk of bias, heterogeneity, subgroup differences, and publication bias were assessed.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies met the inclusion criteria, contributing 33 cohorts for gait speed (n = 3136) and 28 cohorts for SPPB (n = 2773). Higher circulating CAF22 concentrations were significantly associated with slower gait speed in controls (r = - 0.309, 95% CI - 0.371 to - 0.244%) and disease cohorts (r = - 0.309, 95% CI - 0.361 to - 0.254%), yielding an overall pooled correlation of r = - 0.308 (95% CI - 0.346 to - 0.269%). CAF22 concentrations were also inversely associated with SPPB scores in controls (r = - 0.335, 95% CI - 0.415 to - 0.250%) and disease cohorts (r = - 0.368, 95% CI - 0.422 to - 0.312%), with an overall pooled correlation of r = - 0.353 (95% CI - 0.397 to - 0.307%). No significant subgroup differences were detected.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated circulating CAF22 concentrations are consistently associated with poorer physical performance across healthy and chronic disease populations, supporting CAF22 as a promising biomarker of functional decline.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Distribution and Projections to 2050 of the Disease Burden of Early-Onset Chronic Diseases Attributable to Low Physical Activity: A Global Burden of Disease Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low physical activity is a modifiable risk factor for non-communicable diseases, but its contribution to early-onset chronic disease burden remains insufficiently quantified. We estimated global, regional, and national burdens of selected early-onset chronic diseases attributable to low physical activity from 1990 to 2021 and projected burden to 2050.

METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 estimates for 204 countries and territories, we quantified disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and age-standardized DALY rates (ASDRs) attributable to low physical activity for cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease among adults aged 25-49 years. Because GBD low physical activity exposure estimates are mainly modeled for adults aged ≥25 years, individuals aged 15-24 years were not included in the risk-attributable analyses. Trends, Socio-demographic Index (SDI)-related inequality, and future burden were assessed using estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs), inequality indices, and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling.

RESULTS: Global DALYs attributable to low physical activity increased by 94.2%, from 686,847 in 1990 to 1.33 million in 2021. ASDR increased from 25.3 to 33.8 per 100,000 population (EAPC = 0.84; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.70-0.97). Diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease showed the fastest ASDR increases, whereas cardiovascular disease and cancer showed no statistically robust trends. In 2021, regional ASDRs varied more than 11-fold, were highest in Oceania, and were higher among females and in middle-SDI settings. Absolute inequality widened, while relative inequality remained uncertain. By 2050, DALYs are projected to reach 1.76 million.

CONCLUSION: Early-onset chronic disease burden attributable to low physical activity has increased substantially and unevenly. Targeted physical activity strategies for young and working-age adults are needed to reduce preventable future burden.

articles.title: Clostridioides difficile-derived membrane vesicles induce pro-apoptotic effects in human intestinal epithelial cells and macrophages in vitro.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE : infection involves interactions between bacterial virulence factors and host cells; however, the contribution of C. difficile membrane vesicles (MVs) to host cell death remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the pro-apoptotic effects of C. difficile MVs on human intestinal epithelial cells and macrophages in vitro. METHODS AND RESULTS: MVs were isolated from a toxigenic clinical strain of C. difficile (RT001) and a non-toxigenic strain (ATCC 700057). The pro-apoptotic effects of MVs on Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells and THP-1-derived macrophages were assessed using cell viability assays, Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and Western blotting. MV exposure decreased cell viability and increased apoptotic populations, with effects becoming more pronounced following prolonged exposure in both cellular models. The gene expression of the initiator caspases CASP8 and CASP9, the executioner caspases CASP3 and CASP7, and the pro-apoptotic factors BAX and BAD increased, whereas that of the anti-apoptotic factor BCL-2 expression decreased. Corresponding changes in BAX and BCL-2 protein expression supported the involvement of mitochondrial apoptotic signaling. RT001-derived MVs generally caused stronger cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects, although the magnitude of apoptosis differed between the two cell types examined. Notably, MVs from the non-toxigenic strain also induced apoptosis, indicating that these effects are not exclusive to toxin-producing C. difficile strains. CONCLUSIONS: C. difficile MVs induce modest, cell type-dependent apoptotic responses and alter apoptosis-associated markers in intestinal epithelial and macrophage-like cells. The ability of MVs from both toxigenic and non-toxigenic strains to induce apoptosis highlights a toxin-independent mechanism of C. difficile-host interaction and provides new insights into how this pathogen may impair host intestinal epithelial integrity. Although the results support the involvement of apoptosis-related signaling, the specific vesicular components and molecular pathways underlying these effects remain to be elucidated.

articles.title: Three-dimensional automated muscle and adipose analysis to predict hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Overt hepatic encephalopathy (HE) limits the use of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) in portal hypertension. We aimed to determine whether automated three-dimensional (3D) body composition analysis could improve pre-TIPS prediction of overt HE compared with conventional two-dimensional (2D) manual assessment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter study included 593 eligible patients from seven institutions (training cohort: n = 308; external validation 1 cohort: n = 151; and external validation 2 cohort: n = 134). After evaluating L3-based 2D measurements, we developed a fully automated 3D muscle and adipose assessment incorporating morphologic and radiomic features. We combined the 3D assessment with selected clinical variables to predict post-TIPS overt HE risk, and benchmarked the final model against published clinical scores. Model performance was evaluated via ROC analysis, DeLong tests, calibration, decision curve analysis, and subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Traditional 2D measurements showed poor reproducibility, with significant variation in 96.2% (25/26) of features. The 3D Model significantly outperformed the 2D Model. The Integrated Model yielded AUCs of 0.78, 0.73, and 0.77 in the training and two external validation cohorts, exceeding those of Child-Pugh, MELD, ALBI, AMMON-OHE, and Lambda (AUCs 0.47-0.64; all p < 0.05). No significant subgroup differences were observed. High-risk patients had 2- to 4-fold higher overt HE incidence. The model reclassified 40.2% of patients with low pre-TIPS ammonia as high risk and 60.2% of those with high ammonia as low risk.

CONCLUSION: Automated 3D muscle and adipose analysis enables objective preprocedural prediction of overt HE after TIPS, which may facilitate clinical decision-making and optimize patient selection.

KEY POINTS: Question Can automated three-dimensional muscle and adipose analysis improve reproducible preprocedural prediction of overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt beyond conventional two-dimensional assessment? Findings In 593 patients from seven hospitals, an Integrated Model combining automated three-dimensional body composition and clinical variables outperformed five published clinical comparator scores. Clinical relevance This fully automated three-dimensional body composition (muscle and adipose) analysis enables objective preprocedural risk stratification for overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, supporting more consistent patient selection.

articles.title: Ultrasound quantification of liver fat in MASLD.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently first recognized at ultrasound, but conventional B-mode assessment is limited by subjectivity and reduced sensitivity for mild steatosis. Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) techniques address these limitations by converting acoustic signal properties into numerical biomarkers of hepatic fat, including attenuation coefficient, backscatter coefficient, speed of sound, and composite measures. This review summarizes the technical principles, current evidence, clinical implementation, and limitations of ultrasound-based liver fat quantification techniques in MASLD. Their major advantages are accessibility, integration into routine ultrasound examinations, and potential use alongside elastography for multiparametric assessment. However, thresholds vary across vendors, software implementations, acquisition protocols, reference standards, and patient populations, limiting interchangeability and universal cutoffs. In clinical practice, ultrasound fat quantification should not be interpreted in isolation but integrated with fibrosis risk stratification and metabolic risk assessment. Further multicenter studies are needed to standardize acquisition and reporting, define clinically meaningful longitudinal changes, and link ultrasound-derived fat reduction with patient outcomes. QUS is therefore best regarded as an evolving, practical framework for objective steatosis assessment that complements, rather than replaces, comprehensive MASLD risk stratification. KEY POINTS: Question Conventional B-mode ultrasound is subjective and insensitive to mild hepatic steatosis, creating an unmet need for objective, reproducible liver fat quantification in MASLD. Findings Attenuation-based and composite quantitative ultrasound methods provide objective liver fat assessment, but vendor-dependent thresholds currently limit interchangeability and universal clinical application. Clinical relevance Quantitative ultrasound enables accessible, objective liver fat assessment during routine imaging, improving detection and grading of hepatic steatosis and supporting risk-based MASLD care; however, vendor-specific thresholds and acquisition variability require technique-specific interpretation.

articles.title: Advancements in understanding the pathogenic mechanisms of Treponema pallidum.
articles.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (T. pallidum) is the etiological agent of syphilis, which has been regarded as a great imitator with its multiple possible clinical manifestations. The mechanisms by which this spirochete enters the host, elicits inflammation, causes host cell damage, and persists in its natural host are not adequately understood. This review aims to briefly introduce the microbiology of T. pallidum as a unique pathogen and summarize the recent advancements in understanding the molecular basis behind the immune evasion mechanisms of this pathogen. The basic scientific discussions herein should provide a framework for understanding the clinical and epidemiological outcomes described in this review.

articles.title: An Oscillometric Readout Assessing the Degree of Airway Smooth Muscle Activation In Vivo.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oscillometry is a technique for probing respiratory mechanics that is emerging in clinical settings. One advantage of oscillometry that has yet to be fully exploited is its fine temporal resolution, which makes it suitable for capturing changes in lung mechanics that occur over short timescales, such as those caused by a deep inspiration (DI) or by airway smooth muscle. Herein, we hypothesized that the short-lived decrease in respiratory system resistance at 5 Hz (Rrs5) induced by a DI is attributable to airway smooth muscle. We assessed, for the first time, the temporal response to DI following administration of the bronchodilator salbutamol to confirm that the DI-induced decrease in Rrs5 is mediated by airway smooth muscle.

METHODS: Thirty-seven very mild-to-mild asthmatics underwent oscillometry before, during, and after a DI, both before and after the inhalation of salbutamol (200 µg). Rrs5 pre-DI and during the first tidal breath post-DI was compared to quantify the DI response.

RESULTS: Rrs5 decreased by 12.7 ± 19.8% in response to DI, and this response was virtually abolished by salbutamol (p = 0.001). The DI response also correlated with the response to salbutamol (r = 0.47, p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: These results indicate that the temporary decrease in Rrs5 caused by DI is attributable to airway smooth muscle. This change in Rrs5 pre versus post-DI is readily measured, and its magnitude is likely to reflect the degree of airway smooth muscle activation. It holds the potential to aid in the diagnosis of asthma and in predicting responses to bronchodilator drugs.

articles.title: Difficult Extubation After Thoracoscopic Surgery in a Patient With Hypothyroidism: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder with a prevalence of 0.4% to 1.7%, affecting predominantly women and older adults. Common anesthetic and surgical complications in patients with hypothyroidism include delayed emergence, myocardial and pulmonary infarction, respiratory arrest, hemorrhage, and fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Severe hypothyroidism can rarely trigger myxedema. This case report describes the case of a patient with hypothyroidism who underwent difficult extubation after thoracoscopic lung surgery. CASE REPORT A 62-year-old woman with hypothyroidism developed shortness of breath, stridor, hypoxemia, and decreased muscle strength in the extremities following the removal of a double-lumen endotracheal tube after thoracoscopic resection of the right lung S6 segment. Reintubation revealed marked periglottic edema. Upon admission to the intensive care unit, she presented with lethargy, cold extremities, and edema of the eyelids and dorsum of the feet. A detailed medical history revealed irregular use of levothyroxine sodium and self-discontinuation of the medication for 3 days prior to surgery. Postoperative laryngeal edema was considered the direct cause of extubation difficulty, while inadequately controlled hypothyroidism was identified as a major contributing factor to tissue edema, impaired respiratory muscle function, and delayed postoperative recovery. Following respiratory support and supplementation with levothyroxine sodium, respiratory function and muscle strength gradually improved, and the patient was discharged on the sixth postoperative day. CONCLUSIONS This case suggests that in patients with hypothyroidism experiencing difficulty with extubation during the perioperative period, a comprehensive assessment of common causes, such as airway edema and residual neuromuscular blockade, is necessary, and the adverse effects of hypothyroidism on airway edema and recovery from anesthesia should be given due attention.

articles.title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

articles.title: Navigating complexity: applying machine learning to improve SWL outcome prediction.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Shock wave lithotripsy (SWL) remains a cornerstone of non-invasive urolithiasis treatment, yet its success is highly variable and difficult to predict using traditional linear statistical models. Traditional models often fail to account for the complex, non-linear interactions between stone characteristics and procedural variables. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of machine learning (ML) algorithms in predicting stone-free status (SFS), post-SWL renal colic, and the requirement for subsequent ureteroscopy (URS).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a multicentric database of 1498 patients treated with SWL over a six-year period. A total of 23 clinical features, including patient demographics, stone characteristics (size, density, and location), and surgical parameters, were utilized as inputs. We compared 15 different ML algorithms (including LightGBM, CatBoost, and Random Forest) and a multitask Artificial Neural Network against conventional logistic regression. Models were evaluated using validation accuracy, confusion matrices, cross-imbalance metrics (AUC-ROC, AUPRC), and F1-scores. "SFS" was defined as the primary endpoint, while secondary endpoints were represented by "Need for secondary URS" and occurrence of "Post-SWL colic".

RESULTS: On logistic regression analysis, stone characteristics (size, density) resulted as the most important predictors of treatment failure. Treatment parameters (sessions, power) reflected procedural difficulty, and SWL success decreases with increasing stone complexity. ML models consistently outperformed traditional logistic regression across all endpoints. For the primary endpoint (SFS), LightGBM achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.79-0.86) and an AUPRC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84-0.91). For secondary endpoints, the Need for secondary URS was predicted with high discrimination by LightGBM (AUC-ROC = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.89-0.95; AUPRC = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.71-0.84) and CatBoost (AUC-ROC = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.85-0.92; AUPRC = 0.73, 95% CI: 0.65-0.80). For Post-SWL colic (2.7% prevalence), LightGBM achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.82-0.93) and an AUPRC of 0.42 (95% CI: 0.31-0.54), reflecting the realistic discrimination limits for rare post-procedural events.

CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly gradient boosting algorithms, demonstrate potential in predicting outcomes after SWL. While SFS remains inherently difficult to predict due to extra-procedural factors, ML provides accurate assessments of treatment failure and complications. These tools could support more personalized clinical decision-making, helping to identify patients who may benefit from primary endoscopic intervention rather than SWL.

articles.title: Urinary biomarker-guided surveillance versus standard cystoscopic surveillance for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare urinary biomarker-guided surveillance with standard cystoscopy-based surveillance in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with respect to cystoscopy use and oncological outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing urinary biomarker-guided surveillance with standard cystoscopy-based surveillance in adults with NMIBC. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through August 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses were used for comparative oncological outcomes, and pooled estimates were considered exploratory. Cystoscopy utilization was summarized descriptively using the total number of cystoscopies performed, cystoscopies per participant, absolute and relative reductions in cystoscopy use, and the number of cystoscopies performed per detected recurrence.

RESULTS: Two randomized controlled trials, DaBlaCa-15 and UroFollow, randomized 606 participants, with 590 contributing to the principal comparative analyses. Biomarker-guided surveillance reduced cystoscopy use by 55.8% in DaBlaCa-15 and 74.9% in UroFollow. There was no significant difference in any recurrence (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.77-1.41), high-grade recurrence or disease progression (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.61-1.74), or progression to muscle-invasive or metastatic disease (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.12-2.67).

CONCLUSION: In the two available randomized trials, biomarker-guided surveillance substantially reduced cystoscopy use and did not show evidence of worse recurrence or progression outcomes, although non-inferiority could not be established. However, the evidence base is small, the surveillance strategies and risk groups differ, and progression events were uncommon. This review adds randomized evidence that biomarker-guided surveillance can reduce cystoscopy use, but larger trials with longer follow-up are needed before it can replace guideline-based cystoscopy.

articles.title: Carotid CTA with automated plaque quantification for risk stratification of coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether automated carotid plaque quantification on carotid computed tomography angiography (CTA) can serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool for identifying patients with coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease (OCAD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This dual-center retrospective study included 2533 adults undergoing paired carotid and coronary CTA within 3 months. Carotid plaque components (calcified, fibrotic, and lipid) were quantified automatically. In the modeling cohort, three diagnostic models for OCAD (stenosis ≥ 50%) were developed using LASSO regression: clinical, plaque, and integrated models. Performance was assessed by AUC (with DeLong's test), decision curve analysis, and calibration curves, with validation in an internal validation set and a temporally independent validation cohort. Sensitivity analysis was performed using severe stenosis (≥ 70%) as the outcome.

RESULTS: All carotid plaque volumes were significantly associated with OCAD (p < 0.001). Calcified plaque volume (OR, 2.43; 95% CI: 1.95-3.04) and fibrotic plaque volume (OR, 1.37; 95% CI: 1.01-1.85) were independent predictors. The plaque model achieved an AUC of 0.785 (95% CI: 0.761-0.810) in the training set, comparable to the integrated model (AUC, 0.800) and superior to the clinical model (AUC, 0.723; p < 0.001). Performance remained robust in the internal (AUC, 0.824) and external validation set (AUC, 0.813). The integrated model demonstrated good calibration. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective study, automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA provides an adjunctive risk stratification tool to identify patients at high risk for coexisting OCAD, potentially guiding decisions regarding downstream coronary examinations.

KEY POINTS: Question Quantitative analysis of carotid plaque components on CTA may help identify patients with OCAD. Findings A model integrating automated carotid plaque volumes and clinical factors effectively identified OCAD. Clinical Relevance This study demonstrates that automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA may serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool to guide downstream coronary testing in patients with cerebrovascular disease.

articles.title: Integration of individual-level social determinants of health and associations with cardiovascular risk factors in breast and prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strategies to integrate multiple individual-level social determinants of health (SDOH) remain limited in cardio-oncology.

METHODS: Across two longitudinal prospective cohorts of 193 women with breast cancer (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05078190) and 195 men with prostate cancer (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05096338) who were initiating potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapy, the authors comprehensively assessed 16 individual-level SDOH (20 effective variables) before treatment initiation. For each cohort, a data-driven approach using dimensionality reduction by means of factorial analysis of mixed data was conducted. Longitudinal associations between each dimension and cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs; blood pressure, body mass index, and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity [MVPA]) over 12 months were estimated using generalized estimating equations scaled to a 1-interquartile range increase in the dimension score. As a comparator with individual SDOH measures, associations between CVRFs and the social vulnerability index were assessed.

RESULTS: In each cohort, six orthogonal dimensions explained nearly 50% of the total variability in SDOH. In breast cancer, dimension 1 (16.4% variability) reflected food insecurity and financial toxicity. Each 1-interquartile range increase in the dimension 1 score was associated with a 0.3-kg/m2 higher body mass index (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.02-0.5 kg/m2) and a 2.5-point lower MVPA score (95% CI, -4.8, -0.3). In prostate cancer, dimension 1 (16.0% variability) reflected education, occupational prestige, income, employment, and health literacy. Each 1-interquartile range increase in the dimension 1 score was associated with a 2.6-point lower MVPA score (95% CI, -4.6, -0.6). The social vulnerability index was not significantly associated with longitudinal changes in CVRFs.

CONCLUSIONS: This work supports a data-driven approach to integrate multiple individual-level SDOH measures to inform the associations between multilevel SDOH measures and cardiovascular risk in cancer.

articles.title: Ordered energy polarization confidence estimation from an absolute linear Stokes vector.
articles.abstract: This Letter proposes an absolute ordered polarization-intensity confidence metric based on local ordered-energy statistics of the linear Stokes vector. It integrates first-order uniform polarization energy and second-order anisotropic gradient energy to adapt to both uniform specular reflections and spatially varying polarization structures. Enhanced by an adaptive irradiance gate that efficiently suppresses spurious background responses without manual parameter tuning, the proposed method demonstrates superior target-background separation across various target geometries and complex cluttered environments. It preserves continuous confidence on structural edges and smooth transitions while eliminating false confidence on weak-polarization uniform surfaces, providing a robust and faithful evaluation of polarization signatures.

articles.title: Clinical Practice Guideline of Korean Pancreatobiliary Association for Autoimmune Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) is a distinct subtype of chronic pancreatitis characterized by immune-mediated inflammation and a favorable response to steroid therapy. Currently, the lack of standardized clinical practice guidelines in South Korea has led to significant variations in clinical practice, with diagnosis, steroid use, maintenance therapy, and relapse management often relying on individual clinicians' experience and judgment. To address this issue, the Pancreas Research Group of the Korean Pancreatobiliary Association has developed a clinical practice guideline for the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of AIP, reflecting the latest global evidence and the specific healthcare environment in Korea. These recommendations were established through an extensive literature review and expert consensus using the Delphi method, with the level of evidence and strength of recommendation presented according to a standardized classification system. This clinical practice guideline aims to support consistent and rational clinical decision-making for patients with AIP and to provide a standard for evidence-based treatment suitable for the Korean medical context.

articles.title: Prostate-specific antigen-based screening for prostate cancer: A systematic review to inform an American Cancer Society guideline.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this systematic review was to identify and synthesize the evidence on the benefits and harms of prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based screening for prostate cancer to inform the American Cancer Society's updated guideline. PubMed and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for published and gray literature through December 4, 2023, and updated through October 29, 2025, which allowed for approximately 3 months of overlap with searches conducted for the previous guideline. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized comparisons of PSA-based screening strategies to no screening or other screening strategies. Low- and medium-risk of bias systematic reviews were included, and their findings were supplemented with studies published after the systematic review. One investigator abstracted study data, and a second confirmed. Two investigators independently assessed the risk of bias and strength of evidence, and discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Twenty-nine publications were included: two publications from a 2018 systematic review of PLCO, CAP, and ERSPC; 23 subsequent publications from six trials (PLCO, CAP, ERSPC, Göteborg-1, Rotterdam Pilot 1, and ProScreen); and four observational studies. PSA-based screening was associated with increased detection of low-risk prostate cancer, reduced incidence of advanced or metastatic disease at diagnosis, and reduced cumulative incidence of metastatic disease. Screening was associated with a reduction in prostate cancer-specific mortality in some trials, although findings were inconsistent and likely depended on screening protocols, PSA thresholds, participant characteristics, and other factors. Harms of screening included overdiagnosis, false-positive test results, biopsy-related complications, and downstream treatment harms.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing and health-related quality of life in children with idiopathic or heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease causing elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular (RV) failure, and premature death. Idiopathic and heritable PAH impair functional capacity and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) assesses exercise limitation and disease severity, yet its relationship with HRQoL has not been investigated in pediatric PAH.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective multicenter study across three French tertiary pediatric cardiology centers was conducted (June 2023-April 2025). Children with idiopathic or heritable PAH who underwent CPET and completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL 4.0) were included. Key CPET parameters were analyzed, and associations to HRQoL scores were assessed via Spearman correlation.

RESULTS: Among 19 children (median age 11 years, median follow-up 32 months), exercise capacity was reduced (peak VO2 29 ml/kg/min; 74.5% predicted; Z-score -2.9), with ventilatory inefficiency (VE/VCO2 slope 40). QoL scores were lower than normative values. No significant correlation was found between CPET parameters and HRQoL scores.

CONCLUSION: Children with idiopathic or heritable PAH present exercise limitation and impaired HRQoL, though CPET parameters were not correlated with HRQoL scores, reflecting limited statistical power. Larger studies are needed to clarify this relationship.

articles.title: Half-Way Bayesian Calibration for Assessing Uncertainties in Quantum Chemistry Guided Catalyst Optimization.
articles.abstract: Developments in computational chemistry have made quantum chemical modeling an essential tool for catalyst design. However, so far theoretical predictions usually lack error bars, making them almost useless in guiding high-stakes decisions. Commonly used accuracy metrics such as mean absolute error are ill-defined when selectivity depends on relative energies of dozens of closely related transition states, as often happens in catalysis. The main missing ingredient is a tool for estimating errors of a computational protocol where many computed values combine into a single prediction. Here we show how Bayesian statistics can be applied to a model case of catalyst optimization, providing a framework for assessing reliability of a computational protocol as well as for telling reliable predictions from unreliable ones even for very similar compounds. We find that a modest B97-D/TZV(2d,2p)/PCM level of theory employing a semi-local GGA-level density functional provides a standard deviation of only ~0.26 kcal/mol in relative energies of enantiomeric transition states for the model reaction. Thus, we provide a practical tool for assessing uncertainties in computational predictions and integrating them into catalyst optimization pipelines, bridging the gap between quantum chemistry and experimental catalysis design.

articles.title: The roles of ROCK1 and ROCK2 in cardiopulmonary and fibrotic disease: considerations for pan-ROCK inhibition as a therapeutic approach.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) isoforms, ROCK1 and ROCK2, are central regulators of cellular functions fundamental to the pathogenesis of cardiopulmonary and fibrotic diseases. Evidence from animal and cellular models demonstrates ROCK signaling attenuation exerts potent effects on the dysregulated hyperproliferative, fibrotic, and contractile cellular components of the vascular wall and lung parenchyma. These aberrant cellular processes are central to the pathobiology of diverse cardiopulmonary diseases, including pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease, where effective treatment options remain limited. Both pan-ROCK and ROCK2-selective inhibitors are approved for various diseases. The ongoing development of more potent or isoform-selective ROCK inhibitors across emerging indications highlights an unrealized potential.

AREAS COVERED: The roles of ROCK1 and ROCK2 in tissue remodeling, inflammatory recruitment, and dysfunction in multiple cell types. Searches utilized keywords: 'pulmonary hypertension' or 'cardiopulmonary fibrosis' AND variations on 'ROCK inhibitor' and hand searching of key publications.

EXPERT OPINION: Evidence suggests that pan-ROCK inhibitors may have certain advantages over ROCK2-selective agents for complex cardiopulmonary and fibrotic diseases, as each isoform plays distinct, non-redundant roles in fibrosis and inflammation. Concerns about hypotension as a dose-limiting side effect unique to pan-ROCK inhibition versus ROCK2 inhibition are increasingly unsupported by clinical data.

articles.title: Regulation of IL-13 Signaling by Retinoic Acid in Airway Epithelial Cells.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.abstract: Dysregulated vitamin A signaling, characterized by reduced all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is associated with asthma severity, and restoration of ATRA signaling may alleviate asthma symptoms. However, the molecular changes induced by inflammatory cytokines such as IL-13 that are central to asthma pathology and the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) agonists in airway cells are not well established. This study investigates the effects of IL-13 and RAR agonists on lung epithelial cells using a mass spectrometry-based proteomics approach. A549 alveolar and BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells were treated with IL-13 in the presence of vehicle, ATRA (pan-RAR agonist), or CD1530 (RARγ agonist). Proteomic profiling revealed significant changes in proteins relevant to asthma pathogenesis in IL-13-treated cells. IL-13 upregulated pro-inflammatory signaling kinases JAK1 and AXL, cytoskeletal-associated proteins CLDN2 and ACTN4, and inflammatory proteins CD44 and HLAs in A549 cells. In BEAS-2B cells, IL-13 upregulated barrier dysfunction-related proteins P-Cadherin and α-catenin, immune activation marker ICAM-1, and pro-fibrosis marker TGF-β. Notably, IL-13 significantly reduced ATRA biosynthesis enzymes RDH10 and ALDH1A1 which were accompanied by reduced ATRA levels and reduced ATRA biosynthesis in A549 cells as quantified by liquid chromatography-multistage-tandem mass spectrometry. RAR agonists mitigated IL-13-induced upregulation of proteins involved in epithelial integrity, inflammation, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and extracellular matrix (ECM) production. CD1530 produced more pronounced changes than ATRA, underscoring the relevance of the RARγ subtype-specific activation in mitigating pathological changes in epithelial cells. These findings suggest that activating RAR restores ATRA signaling in airway cells and mitigates the pathological features of asthma.

articles.title: Association of Preoperative C-Reactive Protein/Albumin Ratio with Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation and Intensive Care Unit Length of Stay After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Single-Center, Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative complications after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) are influenced by inflammatory processes. The C-reactive protein-to-albumin (CRP/Alb) ratio combines an inflammatory marker with a marker related to nutritional and inflammatory status. This study examined whether the preoperative CRP/Alb ratio was associated with postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay after isolated CABG.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 179 patients who underwent isolated CABG between January 2019 and December 2023. Demographic, laboratory, operative, and postoperative data were retrieved from hospital records. The preoperative CRP/Alb ratio was derived from serum CRP and albumin measurements. Associations between this ratio and both POAF occurrence and ICU length of stay were analyzed.

RESULTS: POAF occurred in 26 patients (14.5%). In the unadjusted analysis, CRP/Alb ratio differed significantly according to POAF status (p = 0.043), with higher ranks observed among patients without POAF. The ratio was also weakly but significantly correlated with ICU length of stay (Spearman's r = 0.186, p = 0.013).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative CRP/Alb ratio showed associations with POAF status and ICU length of stay following isolated CABG. Nevertheless, its ability to discriminate POAF was limited, and only a small number of POAF events occurred. The findings should therefore be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Discovery and bioevaluation of cinnamic acid hydrazide as a sialic acid-dependent EV-D68 attachment inhibitor.
articles.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) poses a significant public health threat, causing respiratory illness and acute flaccid myelitis, yet no approved antiviral therapies exist. This study identified potent EV-D68 inhibitors through systematic screening of cinnamide analogs using a cell-based assay. The lead compound, CIN-01, exhibited promising antiviral activity (EC50 = 2.31 μM, SI > 43). Further structural optimization yielded CIN-12, demonstrating exceptional potency (EC50 = 0.087 μM) with remarkable selectivity (SI > 1149). CIN-12, a cinnamic acid hydrazide derivative, displayed broad-spectrum efficacy against multiple EV-D68 strains and Coxsackievirus genotypes, while maintaining minimal cytotoxicity. Time-of-addition studies revealed that CIN-12 primarily targets the early viral replication stage. Further, CIN-12 suppresses EV-D68 infection through a non-virucidal entry inhibition mechanism by selectively targeting the viral attachment phase, disrupting virus-host cell interaction in a sialic acid-dependent manner, with α2,6-linked sialic acid identified as the predominant determinant of this inhibitory effect. These findings position CIN-12 as a promising therapeutic agent that interferes with the entry/attachment phase of EV-D68 replication, offering a novel cinnamide-based approach to combat this emerging viral pathogen.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic Profile of Recombinant Antithrombin Gamma in Sepsis-induced Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation: A Prospective Observational Study.
Novel 68Ga-labeled peptide for SORT1-targeted PET imaging: development and preclinical validation in triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.abstract: To develop a non-invasive PET/CT imaging strategy for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients by targeting Sortilin (SORT1) protein, a promising therapeutic target lacking companion diagnostics, we synthesized two novel 68Ga-labeled peptide radiotracers, 68Ga-FZ-SR-1 and 68Ga-FZ-SR-2, achieving high radiochemical purity (>95%). In vitro evaluation was carried out using MDA-MB-468 (high SORT1 expression) and MDA-MB-231 (low SORT1 expression) TNBC cell lines to assess stability, binding affinity, and uptake specificity. In vivo pharmacokinetics and tumor targeting were assessed by microPET/CT imaging and ex vivo biodistribution in MDA-MB-468 and MDA-MB-231 xenografts. 68Ga-FZ-SR-1 demonstrated slightly higher tumor-targeting efficiency and contrast-to-noise ratios compared to 68Ga-FZ-SR-2. Moreover, 68Ga-FZ-SR-1 exhibited favorable tumor targeting, rapid renal clearance and favorable in vivo pharmacokinetic properties, selected for further evaluation. Ex vivo histology further revealed good consistency between radiotracer accumulation and intratumoral SORT1 expression. In summary, this proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of 68Ga-FZ-SR-1 for the noninvasive visualization of SORT1, providing an exploratory foundation for SORT1-targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

articles.title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel dual-functional NMT/IDO-1 inhibitors with fungicidal and immunomodulatory activities.
articles.abstract: Invasive fungal infections, particularly those caused by fluconazole- resistant strains, remain a major clinical challenge owing to the limited therapeutic options currently available and the immunosuppressive state induced by the infection. Herein, we report the rational design of a series of dual-targeting small molecules capable of simultaneously inhibiting fungal N-myristoyltransferase and host indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-1. The representative compounds 8a-4 and 14a-2 exhibited potent inhibitory activities against both targets, broad antifungal efficacy across clinical isolates of Candida albicans including fluconazole-resistant strains, and extremely low cytotoxicity toward host cells. Mechanistic investigations revealed that 14a-2 could induce rapid accumulation of reactive oxygen species in the fungal pathogen, trigger mitochondrial dysfunction, and provoke a cell death process resembling apoptosis, while simultaneously modulating the tryptophan-kynurenine metabolic pathway in macrophages, downregulating the expression of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase-1, and restoring the production of proinflammatory cytokines. In a mouse model of cutaneous and pulmonary candidiasis, 14a-2 significantly reduced fungal burden, alleviated histopathological damage, accelerated wound healing, and reshaped the local immune microenvironment by enhancing the infiltration of cluster of differentiation 4-positive and cluster of differentiation 8-positive T cells. Collectively, this work establishes a dual-target strategy that couples pathogen elimination with immune activation, thereby providing a promising therapeutic framework for the next generation of antifungal immunotherapies.

articles.title: Design, synthesis and bioevaluation of pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridines as potent and selective aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Due to the association of excessive aldosterone with multiple severe cardiovascular, renal and endocrine diseases, aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) as the pivotal enzyme in aldosterone biosynthesis has been manifested to be an outstanding therapeutic target. Although baxdrostat (IC50 = 35 nM; selectivity factor, SF = 102) was approved recently for treating resistant hypertension, further inhibitors with innovative scaffolds were still urgently needed attaining superior inhibitory potency and selectivity to deal with patient stratification, potential resistance, and long-term safety surveillance on cardiovascular outcomes and glucocorticoid status. Replicating the optimal binding mode of natural substrate deoxycorticosterone and baxdrostat (linear configurations), aryl sulfonamido pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridines were designed, however, with a curve molecular shape to circumvent potential steric clashes with the β-sheets. Compounds with p-F (8j) and p-CN (8 m) substituents on the distal phenyl sulfonamido moiety turned out to be approximately four-fold more potent numerically compared to baxdrostat with IC50s of 9 and 12 nM, respectively. Both compounds were around two-fold more selective numerically compared to baxdrostat with SFs of 199 and 157, respectively. They showed substantially weaker inhibition of a panel of steroidogenic and hepatic CYP enzymes than of CYP11B2 and did not disrupt the growth of HepG2 and V79 cells. Compound 8j showed good pharmacokinetic properties with a half-life of 3 h and an oral bioavailability of 39%. Compound 8j reduced plasma aldosterone concentrations in rats by twenty-fold to 12 ng/L, whereas induced no statistically significant difference on cortisol levels. Compound 8j was therefore deemed promising for further development.

articles.title: Design and Evaluation of Compritol-Oleic Acid Nanostructured Lipid Carriers: A New Approach to Type 2 Diabetes Therapy.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a prevalent metabolic disorder caused by reduced insulin production and sensitivity. Despite advancements in antidiabetic medications, many patients struggle with poor glycemic control. Combining drugs like sitagliptin (STG) and glipizide (GPZ) can improve treatment efficacy, but their low solubility and rapid excretion limit their effectiveness. To address these challenges, this study developed novel compritol and oleic acid-based nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) for the co-delivery of STG and GPZ. The NLCs were prepared using a modified microemulsion technique and optimized using the Box-Behnken model, focusing on particle size, zeta potential, and entrapment efficiency. The optimized NLCs exhibited a particle size of 275.5 nm, zeta potential of -23.4 mV, PDI of 0.134, and high entrapment efficiencies of 88% for STG and 85% for GPZ. Characterization was performed using FTIR, XRD, DSC, and TEM techniques. In vitro release studies at pH 1.2, 6.8, and 7.4 demonstrated prolonged drug release from the NLCs compared to pure drug solutions. In vivo studies in a nicotinamide-streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model revealed that STG-GPZ co-loaded NLCs (10/2.5 mg/kg/b.w.) significantly improved pancreatic and liver function histology and exhibited synergistic antihyperglycemic effects. Statistical analysis confirmed the significance of these findings, highlighting the potential of STG-GPZ co-loaded NLCs as an effective oral drug delivery system for T2DM treatment and management. This innovative approach offers a promising solution to enhance therapeutic outcomes for diabetic patients.

articles.title: Phenazine-1-Carboxylic Acid Inhibits Ferroptosis by Stabilizing EHMT2.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases. Identifying ferroptosis inhibitors may therefore provide therapeutic opportunities for these disorders. Here, we identified phenazine-1-carboxylic acid (PCA) as a potent ferroptosis inhibitor through high-throughput screening. Mechanistically, PCA reduced the accumulation of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid ROS in part by stabilizing the protein level of euchromatic histone-lysine N-methyltransferase 2 (EHMT2). PCA also markedly alleviated cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) in mice. These findings identify a previously unrecognized ferroptosis-suppressive function of PCA and support its further evaluation as a lead compound for ferroptosis-associated diseases.

articles.title: Genetic Prioritization of BTN3A2 Reveals an Interferon-Responsive T-Cell Program in Dermatomyositis Through Single-Cell Mendelian Randomization and Multi-Omics Integration.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by genetic susceptibility and dysregulated immune activation. However, the relationship between genetic variation and specific immune cell states remains poorly understood. We aimed to identify genetically supported immune-cell-specific molecular programs underlying DM and investigate their biological relevance. We integrated immune-cell-specific single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs) from the OneK1K cohort with DM genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Candidate genes were replicated using an independent sc-eQTL dataset and prioritized by Bayesian colocalization. Multi-tissue validation was performed using skeletal muscle transcriptomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and skin single-cell RNA sequencing, protein expression data, clinical phenotypes, virtual knockout analysis, and gain-of-function analyses of BTN3A2. We identified 204 immune cell-specific eGenes associated with DM and prioritized four high-confidence genes, including HLA-DRB1, HLA-C, Lnc-HLA-B-2, and BTN3A2. BTN3A2 showed robust colocalization across multiple CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell subsets and was further supported by muscle transcriptomic data. BTN3A2 was consistently upregulated in both DM muscle tissues and PBMCs and was broadly expressed across T-cell, NK-cell, and B-cell populations. BTN3A2+ T cells exhibited enhanced cytotoxic, activation, antigen-presentation, and interferon-responsive programs, which were reproduced in circulating PBMCs and lesional skin T cells. BTN3A2 expression was negatively correlated with MMT8 scores, while in silico knockout analysis implicated interferon-stimulated and antiviral pathways. Integrating cell-type-specific genetic evidence with multi-tissue immune profiling identified BTN3A2 as a genetically supported candidate associated with DM and an interferon-responsive T-cell state, providing novel insights for future mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: Aniline-linked coumarin-triazole hybrids as α-glucosidase inhibitors: An insightful study from synthesis to in vivo efficacy and mechanistic analysis.
articles.abstract: A new series of coumarin-aniline-triazole hybrids 12a-p was prepared using a multi-step approach. This synthesis involved a Knoevenagel condensation between 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde and diethyl malonate, followed by ester hydrolysis and amide coupling to yield a coumarin-based alkyne, which was then reacted with various 2-azido-N-arylacetamides via a click reaction. All synthesized compounds were evaluated for their potential antidiabetic activities through α-glucosidase inhibition, possessing remarkably superior potency compared to the reference drug acarbose (IC50 = 750.0 ± 0.8 μM), with IC50 values ranging from 1.1 to 44.2 μM. Among them, the 2-methyl derivative 12b emerged as the most potent, exhibiting approximately 750-fold greater activity than acarbose. Kinetic studies established that 12b was a competitive inhibitor (Kᵢ = 1700 nM), and selectivity assays confirmed its excellent specificity for α-glucosidase over α-amylase (no activity was observed up to 100 μM), suggesting a reduced risk of gastrointestinal side effects. Spectral investigations using circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy revealed that 12b induced significant conformational rearrangements in the enzyme, characterized by a noticeable increase in β-sheet content (from 32.3% to 81.3%), while fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed a 1:1 binding stoichiometry with high affinity (Ka = 1.75 × 105 L mol-1 at 25 °C) and an enthalpy-driven binding mechanism (ΔH = -39.19 kJ mol-1, ΔS = -31.07 J mol-1 K-1). In vivo studies in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model demonstrated that, while compound 12b at 30 mg/kg exhibited significant antihyperglycemic activity (55% reduction in FBG), its efficacy was slightly lower than that of acarbose (62% reduction in FBG). Additionally, histopathological examination confirmed dose-dependent protective effects against diabetes-induced hepatic and pancreatic damage. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations also provided structural insights into the stable binding of 12b within the α-glucosidase active site (with a mean binding energy of -10.02 kcal/mol), establishing persistent hydrogen-bonding interactions with key residues, particularly ARG439 and LYS155. Collectively, these findings represent compound 12b as a promising lead candidate for further optimization and development as a safe and effective α-glucosidase inhibitor for the management of type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: A sex ratio by incubation temperature reaction norm for the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) based on fluctuating thermal regimes.
articles.abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. For example, in species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD), the incubation temperatures an embryo experiences determine sex. Reaction norms quantifying this relationship are essential tools for predicting how climatic variability will shift population sex ratios. However, existing TSD reaction norms are derived from constant-temperature laboratory conditions, leaving open the question of their applicability to natural conditions where incubation temperatures fluctuate. In this study, we developed a TSD reaction norm for the American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) using fluctuating-temperature treatments. We incubated eggs under five fluctuating-temperature regimes, determined offspring sex using gonadal gene expression, and used the resulting sex ratios to fit reaction norms based on mean temperature and constant-temperature equivalents (CTE). The reaction norms followed the canonical female-male-female pattern of crocodilians. At lower incubation temperatures, our fluctuating-temperature reaction norms closely aligned with the reaction norm derived from constant temperatures, suggesting that mean temperature and CTE statistics perform reasonably well in this range. However, at higher incubation temperatures, the range most relevant to climate warming projections, our reaction norms diverged substantially from the constant-temperature reaction norm, with upper pivotal temperature estimates differing by up to 1.36°C. Because small thermal shifts at this critical transition can dramatically alter predicted sex ratios, these discrepancies carry real consequences for conservation forecasting. Our results underscore the importance of incorporating ecologically realistic thermal variation into TSD reaction norms and highlight the upper male-to-female transition as a priority for mechanistic study.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, antibacterial activity, and mechanistic studies of Ebselen derivatives against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: The rapid emergence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) necessitates the development of novel antibacterial agents with distinct mechanisms of action. Ebselen, has shown promising antibacterial activity through disruption of redox homeostasis. However, its poor aqueous solubility and limited therapeutic potential call for further structural optimization. In this study, 29 ebselen derivatives were designed and synthesized to systematically explore structure-activity relationships (SAR) and improve antibacterial efficacy. Antibacterial profiling evaluation identified the most potent compound HX-27, which exhibited strong activity against MRSA, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) as low as 2 μM. Its MBC was >16 μM, indicating predominantly bacteriostatic activity at low concentrations. Moreover, HX-27 demonstrated rapid bactericidal activity and effectively inhibited biofilm formation with low hemolytic activity and minimal cytotoxicity. Mechanistic investigations revealed that HX-27 exerts a pronounced membrane-disruptive effect, leading to loss of membrane integrity and bacterial cell death. Integrated metabolomic and proteomic analyses further demonstrated that ebselen derivatives induce significant perturbations in sulfur-containing amino acid metabolism and intracellular redox balance, while also affecting central metabolic pathways and protein transport systems. These results indicate that the antibacterial activity of ebselen derivatives arises from multi-target mechanisms involving both membrane disruption and metabolic dysregulation. Notably, HX-27 displayed satisfactory aqueous solubility and excellent in vivo efficacy in a Galleria mellonella infection model, significantly improving survival under severe infection conditions. Overall, this study establishes a comprehensive structure-activity-mechanism framework for ebselen derivatives and identifies promising lead compounds for the development of novel therapeutics against drug-resistant bacterial infections.

articles.title: Interrogating imidazo[2,1-b]thiazole-4-thiazolidinone hybrids as antidiabetic leads: molecular cartography, pharmacokinetic profiling and rodent therapeutic response.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of new therapeutic agents targeting key enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism. In this study, ten novel imidazo-thiazole-thiazolidinone hybrids were designed, synthesized and their structural integrity was confirmed through 1H NMR and 13C NMR along with mass determination by HREI-MS. After characterization, each derivative was subjected to in-vitro evaluation using acarbose (reference) to assess their anti-diabetic potential through the inhibition of key enzymes. Compound 3 and 6 with IC50 values 3.20 ± 0.20 μM, 2.10 ± 0.30 μM for α-amylase and 3.70 ± 0.30 μM, 2.60 ± 0.20 μM for α-glucosidase acted as the excellent inhibitors, markedly affecting rate of enzymatic reactions, with kinetic studies revealing their mode of inhibition. The SAR analysis revealed key substituents enhanced ligand-enzyme affinity, supported by molecular docking showing their specific binding. Furthermore, in-vivo cytotoxic assessment in rat models was performed to examine toxicological aspects and biocompatibility of synthesized compounds. Pharmacophore modeling, DFT calculations and MD simulations were also conducted to provide mechanistic insights. Comprehensive ADMET analysis including bioavailability, toxicity prediction, oral suitability and drug-likeness together with in-vivo safety evaluation complemented the in-vitro and computational findings, demonstrating these imidazo-thiazole based thiazolidinone derivatives hold promise as effective therapeutics against diabetes mellitus.

articles.title: Natural polysaccharides in pancreatic cancer therapy: From immunomodulation and gut microbiota regulation to metabolic intervention.
articles.abstract: Natural polysaccharides derived from plants, fungi, macroalgae, cyanobacteria, and other marine microorganisms have attracted increasing interest as adjuvant candidates for pancreatic cancer management due to their biocompatibility, structural diversity, and multi-target activities. This review consolidates current knowledge on their anti-pancreatic cancer activities, integrating findings from in vitro, in vivo, and mechanistic studies. We delineate the multi-level regulatory networks through which polysaccharides exert anti-tumor effects via four interconnected mechanisms: direct actions on cancer cells including proliferation inhibition, apoptosis and ferroptosis induction, cell cycle arrest, metastasis suppression, and autophagy modulation; immunomodulation via M1 macrophage polarization, natural killer cell activation, and cytotoxic T lymphocyte mediated killing; restoration of gut microbial homeostasis through beneficial taxa enrichment, intestinal barrier integrity enhancement, short-chain fatty acid elevation, and lipopolysaccharide driven inflammation reduction; and indirect tumor suppression by ameliorating obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The polysaccharide gut microbiota axis emerges as a critical hub integrating these pathways. Structure-activity relationship analysis indicates that low molecular weight, high galacturonic acid content, arabinose and galactose richness, and sulfation may influence activity, although robust attribution requires structurally defined polysaccharides. More than twenty well characterized polysaccharides are documented, with several showing synergistic effects with chemotherapeutics. Despite encouraging preclinical evidence, challenges remain in structural characterization, bioavailability, and clinical validation.

articles.title: A V-type starch-lycopene complex with enhanced cis-lycopene content alleviates hyperglycemia and glycogen fragility in type 2 diabetic db/db mice via gut microbiota.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major global health challenge. Resistant starch type 5 (RS5), formed by complexing starch with guest components into V-type crystalline structures, represents a promising approach for glycemia control. Native lycopene has anti-diabetic potential but limited bioactivity. Here we developed a V-type corn starch-lycopene RS5 complex (CS-LYC) and evaluated its effects in T2DM db/db mice, focusing on glycemic control and gut microbiota-liver glycogen connection. CS-LYC contained 26.07% resistant starch and 11.8 mg/g lycopene, with complexation promoting isomerization to the more bioactive (13Z)-isomer and increasing lycopene accumulation in both plasma and liver in vivo. In db/db mice, CS-LYC improved insulin sensitivity and glucose homeostasis by remodeling gut microbiota (enriching Akkermansia and Alistipes) and increasing metabolites (short-chain fatty acids and indole derivatives), subsequently maintaining intestinal barrier function and stimulating GLP-1 secretion. Through the gut-liver axis, this GLP-1 activated the hepatic PI3K/AKT pathway and increased the proportion of stable glycogen α particles, thereby reducing glycogen fragility, with fecal microbiota transplantation further confirming that these effects were mediated by gut microbiota. Collectively, CS-LYC alleviates T2DM via the gut-liver GLP-1/PI3K-AKT axis, offering a new dietary strategy for diabetes management.

articles.title: Structural complexity and biofunctional properties of highly sulfated carrageenan-agaroid galactans from Calliblepharis fimbriata: Insights from selective chemical modifications.
articles.abstract: Galactans isolated from Calliblepharis fimbriata were characterized using selective chemical modification approaches coupled with 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy to elucidate their structural complexity and structure-activity relationships. The polysaccharides comprised mixed d and l-galactopyranosyl residues associated with ι-carrageenan (G4S - DA2S) and porphyran (G - L6S) motifs. 1H13C HSQC analysis of chemically desulfated derivatives revealed preferential removal of sulfate groups at C-4, while DA2S and L6S units remained largely preserved, yielding α-carrageenan (G - DA2S) segments. Alkali treatment induced partial cyclization of precursor residues, and the principal fraction exhibited a molar ratio of d-galactose, 3,6-anhydrogalactose, and sulfate ester of 1.00:0.04:0.36. Structure-activity relationship analysis suggested that sulfate substitution at C-2 and C-4 positions contributed to an enhanced anticoagulant activity, and high anionic moieties were further associated with increased inhibition of α-glucosidase (38.2-68.8%) and α-amylase (15.3-86%). Furthermore, the galactans exhibited non-cytotoxicity toward RAW264.7 macrophages at concentrations below 32 μg/mL and significantly enhanced (p < 0.05) phagocytic activity and nitric oxide production in a concentration-dependent manner, indicating an immunostimulatory potential through macrophage activation. Overall, these findings reveal the structural complexity of C. fimbriata galactans and establish clear links between their distinct sulfation patterns and biological functions, providing a basis for their potential biomedical and nutraceutical applications.

articles.title: Multiscale ion transport channels based on chitosan and nanocellulose: Synergistic enhancement of mechanical properties and ionic conductivity, and multifunctional integration.
articles.abstract: Eutectogels are promising in flexible wearable electronics, but the inherent trade-off between mechanical strength and ionic conductivity limits their development. Here, we introduced polyethyleneimine-modified cellulose nanocrystals (PEI@CNC) and chitosan (CS) into a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix, and constructed a PVA composite eutectogel (PCxSy) with an aligned lamellar porous structure via directional freezing. The anisotropic low-tortuosity channels, combined with the incorporation of PEI@CNC and CS that provide additional ion-conducting pathways, endow the material with an ionic conductivity of 0.74 S·m-1. Meanwhile, multiple hydrogen bonds among PVA, CS, PEI@CNC, and the DES components form a dense physical network, providing excellent mechanical properties along the orientation direction, with a tensile strength of 3.60 MPa and toughness of 10.39 MJ·m-3. The eutectogel exhibits dual-mode strain/pressure sensing with favorable cycling stability under bending, shearing, and compression. Zn2+ from the DES synergizes with PEI@CNC and CS to impart antibacterial activity (95.71% against E. coli, 95.44% against S. aureus), effectively reducing skin infection risk during long-term wear.

articles.title: Injectable shape-adaptive cellulose hydrogel with antibacterial activity for diabetic wound therapy.
articles.abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are chronically trapped in persistent bacterial infection and prolonged inflammation, severely hindering tissue regeneration. However, developing hydrogel dressings that can simultaneously provide effective antibacterial function and reliable biosafety remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a shape-conformable and antibacterial hydrogel dressing constructed through dynamic coordination between endogenous histidine ligand and low-toxicity Ce3+ for infected diabetic wound repair. Histidine is covalently grafted onto carboxymethyl cellulose to obtain histidine-modified carboxymethyl cellulose, and the hydrogels are rapidly formed by simple mixing with Ce(NO3)3 solution. Reversible coordination between Ce3+ and carboxyl, hydroxyl, and imidazole groups on cellulose chains endow exceptional injectability, rapid self-healing and shape-conformability, enabling conformal filling of irregular wound cavities. Moreover, the hydrogels exhibit antibacterial activity (exceeding 99.99%) against Escherichia coli (E. coli), Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), primarily by disrupting bacterial membrane integrity. Notably, the hydrogels show favorable cytocompatibility, with no systemic toxicity in major organs. Importantly, the hydrogel can significantly accelerate infected diabetic wound closure by reducing bacterial burden, alleviating inflammation, and promoting tissue remodeling. Overall, this simple and safe strategy provides a promising platform for antibacterial and advanced dressing design for the healing of infected diabetic wounds.

articles.title: A synthetic cationic thiopyrylium compound exploits preferential phosphatidylserine recognition to exert antifungal activity.
articles.abstract: Invasive candidiasis poses a severe global health threat, with limited antifungal options and escalating drug resistance demanding novel therapeutic strategies. Here, we report IMB-G3, a cationic thiopyrylium-styryl compound, as a broad-spectrum antifungal agent that preferentially targets phosphatidylserine. IMB-G3 exhibited potent antifungal activity against multiple fungal pathogens, including fluconazole-resistant clinical isolates, with MIC values ranging from 0.25 to 4 μg/mL, and demonstrated synergistic interactions with amphotericin B and caspofungin. Meanwhile, IMB-G3 effectively promoted wound healing in a murine cutaneous infection model. For the mechanism of action, IMB-G3 accumulates at both the cell membrane and the cytoplasm without directly damaging the membrane, instead reducing membrane fluidity, inducing membrane depolarization, and triggering intracellular accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Convergent evidence from lipid feeding assays, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, untargeted lipidomics, and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy indicates that IMB-G3 interacts with several major membrane phospholipids but shows a preference for phosphatidylserine (PS), disrupting PS metabolism, impairing vesicular structure, and triggering lipid homeostasis dysregulation. The cationic thiopyrylium moiety of IMB-G3 engages the anionic phosphate headgroup of PS via electrostatic interaction as determined by 31P NMR. These findings reveal a mechanism of action in which preferential binding to PS dysregulates fungal lipid homeostasis rather than lysing the membrane, and define IMB-G3 as a promising lead compound for a novel class of antifungal therapeutics.

articles.title: Anti-HIV-1 activity and mechanism of action of homoplantaginin: A multitarget flavonoid compound.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically investigate the anti-HIV-1 activity and underlying mechanisms of the flavonoid homoplantaginin (Homo), employing integrated virological, pharmacological, and bioinformatic strategies, and to provide a theoretical foundation for its development as a multitarget anti-HIV-1 candidate .

METHODS: Anti-HIV-1 activity was assessed using three cellular infection models: TZM-bl/HIV-1IIIB, MT-2/HIV-1IIIB, and PBMCs/HIV-1Bal. Cell viability was measured with the CellTiter-Glo luminescence assay; antiviral activity was determined via luciferase reporter expression and HIV-1 p24 antigen detection. Key pharmacological parameters (CC50, IC50, SI) were derived, and cytopathic effects were observed microscopically. Mechanistic investigations included: (1) assays of HIV-1 key enzyme activities and molecular docking; (2) network pharmacology-based target prediction; (3) analysis of relevant factors by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).

RESULTS: 1. Homo exhibited moderate but significant anti-HIV-1 activity, with IC50 values of 43.52 μmol/L (TZM-bl), 13.69 μmol/L (MT-2), and 18.49 μmol/L (PBMCs), and corresponding SI values of 22.97, 57.60, and 54.08. Morphological observation confirmed that Homo reduced HIV-1-induced cytopathic effects. 2. Mechanism studies revealed that Homo dose-dependently inhibited HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) and protease (PR) activities within safe concentration ranges, while showing no significant effect on integrase (IN). The molecular docking results show that Homo may have good binding activity with RT and PR. RT-qPCR demonstrated that Homo suppressed HIV-1-induced expression of pro-inflammatory factors (down-regulation of IL-6 and CXCL10) and enhanced interferon responses (up-regulation of IFN-β and IFN-γ).

CONCLUSIONS: Homo exerts anti-HIV-1 activity through multitarget mechanisms, including inhibition of key viral enzymes, suppression of virus-induced pro-inflammatory factors, enhancement of interferon mediated antiviral immune responses. These findings highlight Homo as a promising candidate for further development as a multitarget anti-HIV therapeutic agent.

articles.title: Associations of body shape, visceral adiposity, and metabolic function indices with risk of major noncommunicable diseases: evidence from a nationwide population cohort.
articles.abstract: Comparative data evaluating the predictive performance of various obesity and metabolic indices for multiple noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) remain limited. We used the data sourced from the Health Evaluation and risk Reduction through nationwide Teamwork cohort (ChinaHEART), a national population-based study that enrolled 4,258,033 Chinese adults and followed them for more than 20 million person-years between November 2014 and December 2023. Fifteen obesity and metabolic indices were categorized into three groups: (1) body shape-related indices, including body mass index (BMI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), a body shape index (ABSI), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and conicity index (CI); (2) visceral fat-related indices, including lipid accumulation product (LAP) and Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI); and (3) metabolic function-related indices, including triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-BMI, TyG-BRI, TyG-WHtR, TyG-ABSI, TyG-WWI, and TyG-CI.
