articles.abstract: Apheresis has become a core clinical and manufacturing interface linking transfusion medicine, hematology, hematopoietic cell transplantation, immune modulation, and advanced cellular therapy. Türkiye has developed substantial activity in this field through dedicated apheresis units, high-volume transplant programs, national surveys, multicenter registries, and a growing body of PubMed-indexed scientific work. This review examines Turkish apheresis activity from the perspective of the Transplantation and Cellular Therapies Society and emphasizes how therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) and other thrombotic microangiopathies (TMAs), extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP), hematopoietic progenitor cell (HPC) mobilization and collection, and cellular-therapy leukapheresis form a unified clinical and quality continuum. A landmark national survey documented 24,912 TPE procedures in 3203 patients across 28 Turkish apheresis units, while subsequent registry and multicenter publications demonstrated the feasibility of broader collaborative data collection. Turkish investigators have contributed studies addressing hematologic TPE, HELLP syndrome, TMA, ECP for acute and chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), venous access for HPC collection, mobilization strategies and kinetics, and other procedure-related questions. The 17th International Congress of the World Apheresis Association, held in Istanbul on 14-17 September 2022, further strengthened international visibility and professional networking. The field should now transition from descriptive procedure counts to disease-specific, outcome-oriented quality systems. We propose a society-based roadmap built on five pillars: a prospective national registry, standardized high-impact clinical pathways, a common quality dashboard, structured multidisciplinary education and competency assessment, and deliberate integration of apheresis with CAR-T and other advanced cellular-therapy programs. Such an approach would position apheresis as a strategic national infrastructure for precision hematology, transplantation, and cellular therapy rather than as an isolated technical service.

articles.title: Tailoring health messages to drinking motives: effects on intentions, self-efficacy, and attentional bias to alcohol stimuli.
articles.journal: Substance abuse treatment, prevention, and policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gain and loss framed health messages are a scalable, low-cost approach to reduce alcohol consumption, yet little is known about whether tailoring such messages to individuals' drinking motives supports their effectiveness in achieving behaviour change. This study assessed whether gain- and loss-framed messages tailored to drinking motives influenced motivation to drink less alcohol.

METHOD: A three-arm parallel randomised experiment was conducted among adults who consumed alcohol at least weekly or engaged in at least one heavy drinking episode per month who expressed an interest in alcohol behaviour change (N = 554; mean age = 59.98 years; 68% male). Participants were randomised to receive either a gain-framed or loss-framed vignette (both tailored to their primary drinking motive), or a control vignette. Primary outcomes were intentions to reduce drinking, self-efficacy to reduce drinking, and attentional bias towards alcohol-related cues.

RESULTS: Gain-framed and loss-framed messages both led to greater intentions to reduce drinking than those in the control group. The strongest effect on intentions was observed for participants endorsing social motives who viewed loss-framed messages. Gain-framed messages increased self-efficacy to reduce drinking. No overall main effects were observed for attentional bias; exploratory analyses indicated motive-by-framing interactions effects.

CONCLUSIONS: Motive tailored gain- and loss-framed messages influenced motivational responses associated with alcohol reduction. Drinking motives represent a theoretically grounded and accessible way to personalise alcohol related behaviour change communication. Replication studies incorporating behavioural outcomes could help establish whether motivational effects translate into sustained reductions in alcohol use and why.

TRIAL REGISTRY: ISRCN register(ISRCH12456514), 06/03/2024.

articles.title: Emergency medical service capacity and prehospital stroke care in Africa: a critical narrative review.
articles.abstract: Stroke is a time-critical medical emergency in which rapid recognition, transport, and treatment are essential to preserving neurological function. Yet across much of Africa, the prehospital systems required to support timely stroke care remain fragmented, underdeveloped, or entirely absent. This critical narrative review examines the evidence on emergency medical service (EMS) capacity for acute stroke care in Africa. Available evidence demonstrates major deficiencies across the entire prehospital stroke pathway. Formal EMS systems are absent in many African countries, and where services exist, ambulance coverage is limited, unevenly distributed, and concentrated largely in urban settings. Community awareness of stroke symptoms and emergency response pathways remains critically low, while reliance on self-transport, pharmacies, traditional healers, and informal care pathways contributes to substantial delays in hospital presentation. Across multiple African settings, most patients with stroke arrive at healthcare facilities hours or days after symptom onset, well beyond established therapeutic windows for reperfusion therapy. The review argues that these delays are not isolated failures of individual behavior but manifestations of broader structural deficiencies in emergency care systems, transport infrastructure, health financing, and stroke preparedness. Limited integration of stroke into national EMS planning, inadequate investment in emergency care infrastructure, and the absence of African-specific implementation research have collectively constrained the development of effective prehospital stroke systems across the continent. Improving stroke outcomes in Africa will require coordinated investment in EMS infrastructure, culturally appropriate stroke awareness programs, community health worker training, mobile health-supported emergency coordination, and integrated prehospital-to-hospital stroke pathways. This evidence is drawn from Ghana, Nigeria, and South Africa, the minority of African countries with published, country-level EMS and stroke-pathway data. Findings and recommendations should be interpreted as characterizing this documented subset rather than the continent as a whole.

articles.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: A Review in Neuroimaging.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. Automated segmentation and volumetric analysis improve reproducibility, speed, and standardization of tumor quantification and response assessment. In research, large language and multimodal models extract structured information from radiology reports and medical records. Collaborative initiatives, such as BraTS and FeTS, have established standardized, privacy-compliant frameworks for large-scale quantitative analyses. Tumor-specific applications include noninvasive molecular profiling in gliomas, grading and recurrence prediction in meningiomas, detection and response assessment in brain metastases, and pediatric-specific modeling aligned with RAPNO. However, AI models remain sensitive to technical and biological variations across institutions, limiting their clinical utility unless appropriate training and validation is performed. Nevertheless, progress is evident in prospective, biopsy-validated infiltration mapping, assessment of resection extent aligned with RANO-Resect, and standardization through AI-RANO. Emerging directions include foundation models, uncertainty estimation, federated learning, AI-enhanced ultra-low-field MRI, and dual-tracer PET. When used as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for the imaging team, AI can increasingly improve the utility, reproducibility, and efficiency of quantitative, multiparametric imaging in patients with brain tumors.

articles.title: Biventricular Reverse Remodeling After Percutaneous Pulmonary Valve Implantation With a Self-Expandable Pulsta Valve in Native Right Ventricular Outflow Tract.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effects of percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI) on biventricular remodeling, ventricular interaction, and effective right ventricular (RV) forward flow in native RV outflow tract disease remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively evaluated 84 patients (46 male) who underwent PPVI with a self-expandable Pulsta valve (median age at PPVI 25.0 years) with paired cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and 1-year echocardiographic follow-up. Ventricular volumes, pulmonary regurgitation fraction, effective RV stroke volume, left ventricular (LV) filling indices, echocardiographic parameters, and cardiopulmonary exercise test results were compared before and after PPVI. The pulmonary regurgitation fraction decreased from 40.0% to 7.7%, with reductions in the RV end-diastolic volume index from 167.7 to 123.5 mL/m2and the RV end-systolic volume index from 88.3 to 65.3 mL/m2(all P<0.001). RV ejection fraction remained unchanged. Effective RV stroke volume increased from 73.5 to 83.7 mL, LV end-diastolic volume index increased from 77.2 to 84.5 mL/m2, and LV stroke volume increased from 72.4 to 80.4 mL (all P<0.001). Peak oxygen consumption improved from 25.8 to 27.8 mL/kg/min (P=0.025). Changes in the LV end-diastolic volume index were inversely correlated with changes in the RV end-diastolic volume index and RV end-systolic volume indices.

CONCLUSIONS: PPVI with a self-expandable Pulsta valve improved RV unloading, effective RV forward flow, LV filling, and exercise capacity despite an unchanged RV ejection fraction.

articles.title: Expert Opinion on Tap Test Procedures for Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus: A Nationwide Hospital-based Survey in Japan.
articles.abstract: Tap test procedures for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus are diverse; understanding expert practice may inform standardization.A web-based survey was conducted in February 2024 among representatives of idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus practices at facilities belonging to the Japanese Society of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus. Descriptive statistics were used to identify response trends.Overall, 110 valid responses were received (86.4% from neurosurgery). Most experts performed lumbar puncture with cerebrospinal fluid removal of at least 30 mL. Improvement was commonly assessed using a 10% or greater reduction in gait test time, such as the Timed Up and Go test, and a 3-point or greater increase on the Mini-Mental State Examination. The idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus grading scale was widely used. No standardized evaluation method for urinary dysfunction was established, and some institutions did not evaluate urinary dysfunction. Post-tap assessments were often performed on the tap day or the next day and again within 1 week. Experts combined scale-based criteria with patients' and families' perceptions when judging improvement. Typical imaging findings and characteristic symptoms were emphasized when considering false-negative and false-positive results.This survey identified current expert tap test practices in Japan and unresolved issues, especially urinary assessment.

articles.title: A rapid 60-minute in vitro glucose release (GR60) parameter for characterizing cooked pasta and noodles.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is a diet-related issue due to rapidly digestible starch underscoring the need for reliable indicators for dietary monitoring. A novel 60-min in vitro digestion glucose release parameter was devised for 10 pasta/noodle types made from grains. The glucose released was quantified as a rapid proxy for glycemic index using a d-glucose assay. AACC methods were used for pasta cooking and physical assessment. The different grains exhibited variable physical properties before and after cooking. The new GR60 was significantly different for the different samples with pulse-based ones showing lower values (3.12-57.37 g glucose release per 100 g cooked and freeze-dried pasta) than the cereal-based counterparts (75.83-82.50 g/100 g), except for whole durum (62.77 g/100 g). GR60 correlated with key cooking parameters, offering preliminary insights into the nutritional quality of starchy foods and demonstrating potential (after further validation) as a consistent, rapid metric for characterizing ready-to-eat foods.

articles.title: Dimensionality reduction of space-related metrics in elite football using factor analysis.
articles.abstract: Spatial organisation is fundamental to understanding football tactics and phase-dependent coordination. However, the high intercorrelation between existing spatial metrics suggests significant redundancy. This study aims to identify the latent dimensions of spatial positioning in- and out-of-possession to refine the theoretical framework of space in professional football. An open-source dataset comprising seven male German Bundesliga matches was utilised to analyse team length, width, height, surface area, convex hull, team centroid, team spread, stretch index, Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagram. Ball possession status served as the independent variable. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients were calculated, while data suitability was examined using the KMO statistic and Bartlett's test of sphericity. An exploratory factor analysis was performed to identify underlying latent constructs. High intercorrelation among spatial metrics justified factor analysis to reduce redundancy. The analysis reveals three consistent spatial dimensions that explain team organisation, regardless of possession status. These dimensions account for 77.1% and 75.5% of the variance, respectively, with the first dimension representing almost half of the variance in each case. Factor analysis reduces complex spatial data into three functional dimensions: 'team dispersion', 'longitudinal dispersion', and 'longitudinal positioning'. This facilitates a concise yet comprehensive interpretation of tactical structures and performance analysis.

articles.title: Multiparametric 0.4-T low-field MRI mapping for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in rats.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Low-field MRI may broaden access to quantitative liver imaging, but low signal-to-noise ratio and coexisting steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and iron complicate relaxometry in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We evaluated multiparametric 0.4-T MRI with deep-learning-reconstructed T1 mapping in rats.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective cross-sectional preclinical study, 90 male Wistar rats underwent 0.4-T liver MRI during dietary induction, progression, and recovery. Metrics included native T1, fat-corrected T1 (FcT1), T2, T2*, and an apparent proton density fat fraction (PDFF) estimate. Whole-section digital pathology quantified steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation, and iron. Associations were assessed using iron-adjusted and stage-aware analyses, multivariable regression with variance inflation factors, and receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: Steatosis strongly correlated with T2 (ρ = 0.90, p < 0.001) and PDFF (ρ = 0.88, p < 0.001). For high inflammation, T2 and T2* yielded areas under the curve (AUROCs) of 0.86 (95% confidence interval 0.78-0.94) and 0.80 (0.71-0.89), respectively (p = 0.294); specificities were 82.2% and 91.1%, respectively. For fibrosis, native T1 yielded higher AUROCs than FcT1 at collagen proportionate area (CPA) > 2.42% (0.77 versus 0.62; p = 0.008) and > 2.90% (0.78 versus 0.60; p = 0.001). Stage-aware analyses attenuated T1-fibrosis associations, and recovery animals showed residual fibrosis with near-baseline T1.

CONCLUSION: Multiparametric 0.4-T MRI showed complementary, partly stage-dependent associations with MASLD pathology. T2/PDFF tracked steatosis; T2* retained an inflammation-related association after stage adjustment; and T1 elevation characterized active high-burden progression rather than isolated residual fibrosis. Human validation and platform calibration are required.

KEY POINTS: Question Noninvasive MASLD assessment needs accessible imaging biomarkers that account for coexisting steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and iron-related confounding in liver MRI. Findings Multiparametric 0.4-T MRI showed complementary but stage-dependent associations: T2/apparent PDFF tracked steatosis, T2* related to inflammation, and T1 rose during high-burden progression. Relevance statement Multiparametric 0.4-T MRI provides complementary pathology-correlated measurements for MASLD assessment in rats, but reconstruction-dependent T1 bias and apparent PDFF estimation require platform calibration and human validation before clinical interpretation.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with the development of a catheter-related thrombosis in patients with critical illness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We sought to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis with the primary objective to identify prognostic factors associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity.

SOURCES: We searched, MEDLINE® and Embase® from inception through 4 May 2024 for all studies in patients with critical illness that reported catheter-related thrombosis, with an updated search performed on 23 October 2025. We included English-language studies that described prognostic factors for developing a catheter-related thrombosis or reported the incidence of this complication in the critical care setting. Two authors performed citation screening and data extraction. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) separately for prognostic factors using a random-effects model and inverse variance weighting. Risk of bias for individual studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool. We assessed certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations approach.

PRINCIPLE FINDINGS: We included 32 studies involving 11,943 patients. Identified prognostic variables with a moderate- or high-certainty association for developing a catheter-related thrombosis include increasing age (aOR per 10-yr increase, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.27; three studies; 1,594 patients; high certainty), trauma-related admission (aOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.34; three studies; 3,089 patients; high certainty), surgical-related admission (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.77 to 3.52; three studies; 2,208 patients; aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.60 to 3.02; two studies; 297 patients; high certainty), internal jugular insertion site as compared with other insertion sites (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.82 to 5.01; four studies; 4,681 patients; high certainty), single/double-lumen as compared with more lumens (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.82 to 3.13; three studies; 1,594 patients; moderate certainty), and peripheral insertion site (aOR, 2.30; 95% CI, 0.74 to 7.08; two studies; 264 patients; moderate certainty). The median incidence of catheter-related thrombosis was 13.3% [interquartile range, 3.7%-31.3%].

CONCLUSIONS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we found that increasing age, surgical type admissions, large catheters, and factors potentially related with catheter duration were associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Furthermore, we identified significant variation in the reported rates of catheter-related thrombosis, with an average rate of approximately 1 in every 8 patients. When these identified risk factors are present, clinicians may consider more aggressive thromboprophylaxis regimens to better tailor prevention strategies to individual patient risk profiles.

STUDY REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework ( https://osf.io/5zvg2) ; first submitted 15 June 2024.

articles.title: Perioperative management of aortic root thrombus following HeartMate 3 implantation: review of the literature.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
articles.abstract: Aortic root thrombosis (ART) is an increasingly recognized complication in patients supported with continuous-flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs), although its incidence, prognosis, and optimal management remain poorly defined. We report 2 cases of early, asymptomatic ART detected on postoperative day 2 by routine transthoracic echocardiography after HeartMate 3 implantation. In both cases, ART developed in the setting of a persistently closed aortic valve and was identified before embolic complications occurred. Both patients were successfully managed with intensified anticoagulation, temporary pump speed escalation to maintain valve closure, and temporary restriction of physical activity. ART resolved completely without symptomatic embolic events, invasive intervention, or antiplatelet therapy, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up. These cases and the available literature suggest that early ART may be clinically silent and underrecognized even in the contemporary HeartMate 3 era. Routine early echocardiographic surveillance may facilitate timely detection, and a conservative, physiology-guided strategy focused on anticoagulation and flow adjustment appears effective in carefully selected patients under close monitoring.

articles.title: Triphasic decline in kidney function after islet transplantation: sex-based differences and the impact of calcineurin inhibitor immunosuppression in a 20 year single-centre cohort.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Islet transplantation alone (ITA) is an established treatment for severe hypoglycaemia in type 1 diabetes, requiring calcineurin inhibitor-based immunosuppression, which is associated with nephrotoxicity. These limitations have driven longstanding interest in calcineurin inhibitor-free strategies, which are now entering clinical translation. The aim of this study was to evaluate long-term kidney function in 223 adults (41% male) undergoing ITA at the University of Alberta Hospital (1999-2018) using eGFR.

METHODS: Mixed-effects models were used to assess eGFR decline rates (ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year) stratified by sex and baseline eGFR. Acute eGFR changes were assessed within 3 months of each infusion. Univariate and multivariable Cox models and competing risk regression were used to identify factors associated with progression to stage 3b chronic kidney disease (CKD) or worse (eGFR <45 ml min-1 1.73 m-2) in individuals with baseline eGFR ≥45 ml min-1 1.73 m-2.

RESULTS: eGFR declined rapidly in the first year post-transplant (-11.52 ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year; 95% CI -13.92, -9.00), then stabilised, with decline rates of -3.12 (95% CI -3.84, -2.28) and -1.08 (95% CI -1.80, -0.36) ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year at 1-5 and 5-20 years, respectively. Female recipients experienced a greater first-year decline than male recipients (-14.79 ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year [95% CI -17.92, -11.66] vs -6.75 ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year [95% CI -10.49, -3.01]; p=0.0012). Individuals with baseline eGFR <60 ml min-1 1.73 m-2 had a similar first-year decline compared to those with preserved function (-3.99 ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year [95% CI -13.31, 5.33] vs -12.03 ml min-1 1.73 m-2 per year [95% CI -14.57, -9.49]; p=0.10). Progression to stage 3b CKD occurred in 21% of participants (47/222) over a median of 6.4 years. Female sex (sub-distribution HR 2.17; 95% CI 1.15, 4.17; p=0.017) and lower baseline eGFR (sub-distribution HR 0.96 per ml min-1 1.73 m-2; 95% CI 0.94, 0.98; p=0.0009) were independent predictors of progression.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Although calcineurin inhibitor-based immunosuppression induces rapid early eGFR decline, its progression slows substantially beyond 5 years. Female sex and lower pre-transplant eGFR independently predicted CKD progression. This sex disparity remains to be fully understood, as male and female recipients did not differ in baseline eGFR or tacrolimus exposure. These findings establish a long-term renal safety benchmark within the largest and longest-running ITA programme, and identify subgroups who are most likely to benefit from emerging calcineurin inhibitor-free strategies.

articles.title: Dual stimulation of Wnt and IFN-γ pathways in human bone marrow-derived multipotent stromal cells produces an activated secretome that modulates autoimmune diabetes in NOD mice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Type 1 diabetes is characterised by continual autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells for which no curative therapy exists. We and others have demonstrated that the paracrine secretome of human multipotent stromal cells (MSCs) can induce islet regeneration and immune modulation; however, whether these effects persist in the context of ongoing autoimmunity remains unknown. Herein, we hypothesised that pharmacological licensing of MSCs with CHIR99021 and/or IFN-γ will generate conditioned media (CdM) with complementary regenerative and immunomodulatory properties. We also aimed to assess the modulation of autoimmune diabetes progression by licensed MSC CdM after intrapancreatic injection in NOD mice.

METHODS: Human bone marrow-derived MSCs were licensed with CHIR99021, IFN-γ or a combination of both, for 24 h, to generate concentrated CHIR, IFN-γ or COMBO CdM, for intrapancreatic (iPan) injection into female NOD mice and for label-free MS-based secretome analyses. Short- and long-term glycaemic outcomes were assessed across type 1 diabetes recovery and prevention paradigms. Pancreas and spleen tissue were collected for tissue analyses to assess beta cell content and immune cell composition.

RESULTS: iPan injection of COMBO CdM immediately after hyperglycaemia onset in NOD mice transiently paused glycaemic elevation (mean ± SEM: 17 ± 3 vs 29 ± 2 mmol/l in basal media-injected controls), reduced severe insulitis and culminated in prolonged survival (mean ± SEM: 32 ± 2 days) compared with basal media-injected controls (mean ± SEM: 21 ± 3 days). In type 1 diabetes prevention experiments, COMBO CdM injection at 12 weeks of age expanded FoxP3+ Treg populations in the spleen and pancreas, and delayed hyperglycaemia onset by 4 weeks (mean ± SEM: 21 ± 0.9 vs 17 ± 0.4 weeks in basal media-injected mice). Early intervention in 8-week-old mice prior to signs of insulitis demonstrated that all CdM preparations preserved glucose tolerance, while CHIR CdM also increased beta cell mass. Proteomic profiling of COMBO CdM revealed unique upregulation of tolerogenic effectors including CD274/PD-L1, CCL7 and IDO1, alongside tissue reparative proteins including MET and TYMP, and proteins involved in extracellular matrix remodelling such as CTSB, CTSS and CTSL, providing a molecular basis for superior outcomes in vivo.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Combined pharmacological licensing of MSCs produces a biologically unique secretome with complementary regenerative and immunomodulatory properties that modulates autoimmune diabetes progression in NOD mice. These findings position MSC licensing and/or MSC CdM as an emerging therapeutic modality for the prevention of autoimmune destruction and regenerative medicine therapies for type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: Smart insulin pens with integrated bolus calculator vs tracking-only connected insulin pens in adults with diabetes on multiple daily injections: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Connected insulin pens (CIPs) have emerged as a promising tool for diabetes management with multiple daily injections (MDI), but evidence supporting the incremental benefit of integrated bolus calculator functionality (smart insulin pens [SIPs]) over tracking-only CIPs remains lacking. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of SIPs with bolus calculator compared with tracking-only CIPs in adults with diabetes on MDI. We hypothesised that SIPs with bolus calculator would improve glycaemic management compared with tracking-only CIPs.

METHODS: In this multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial conducted at nine medical centres in South Korea, we recruited adults aged 19-74 years with type 1 or type 2 diabetes on MDI therapy. Participants with HbA1c 58-108 mmol/mol (7.5-12.0%) were randomly assigned (1:1) using computer-generated block randomisation stratified by diabetes type (sequence generated by an independent statistician) to SIP with bolus calculator or tracking-only CIP for 12 weeks. All participants used continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). The primary outcome was the change in HbA1c from baseline to week 12. Secondary outcomes included CGM metrics, insulin dosing behaviour and safety.

RESULTS: A total of 120 participants were randomised to the SIP group (n=60) or the tracking-only CIP group (n=60); their mean (SD) age was 50.8 (14.8) years, 53 (44.2%) had type 1 diabetes and mean (SD) HbA1c was 69 (12) mmol/mol (8.5% [1.1%]). Of these, 116 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. HbA1c decreased more with SIP than with tracking-only CIP (adjusted mean difference -3.39 mmol/mol [-0.31%]; 95% CI -6.45, -0.22 mmol/mol [-0.59%, -0.02%]; p=0.036). Time in range (3.9-10.0 mmol/l) improved significantly with SIP (57.2% vs 50.8%; adjusted mean difference 6.58%; 95% CI 1.52%, 11.64%; p=0.012). SIP users had fewer missed bolus doses (3.4 vs 3.7 times/day; p=0.020) and higher bolus frequency (3.2 vs 2.8 times/day; p=0.011). No severe hypoglycaemia or diabetic ketoacidosis occurred in either group.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: In this randomised controlled trial of adults with suboptimally controlled diabetes on MDI, SIP with bolus calculator significantly improved glycaemic management and dosing behaviour compared with tracking-only CIP.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06406439.

FUNDING: This study was supported by G2E Co., Ltd, Korea and Huons Co., Ltd, Korea.

articles.title: Should continuous glucose monitoring redefine prediabetes?
articles.abstract: Prediabetes is a clinically useful but biologically heterogeneous risk state defined by episodic laboratory thresholds that identify overlapping rather than identical populations. Continuous glucose monitoring can reveal temporal glycaemic variation that fasting plasma glucose, OGTT and HbA1c cannot capture. Recent evidence indicates that sensor-derived metrics distinguish conventionally defined prediabetes from normoglycaemia and can stratify future glycaemic risk, making eventual incorporation into classification scientifically plausible. The case for immediate diagnostic use, however, is not established. Continuous glucose monitoring measures interstitial rather than venous plasma glucose; device performance and sampling duration influence the derived metrics; and treatment-oriented glucose targets were not developed as diagnostic cut-offs in people without diabetes. Before a continuous glucose monitoring phenotype can be incorporated into the definition of prediabetes, it should demonstrate reproducibility over time and across devices, provide clinically meaningful information beyond established tests and risk factors, change a management decision and show a favourable downstream balance between benefit and harm. Until these conditions are met, continuous glucose monitoring is better positioned as an instrument for phenotyping and risk stratification than as an independent diagnostic criterion.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of kidney adverse events associated with four commonly used proton pump inhibitors based on the PersADE database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are widely prescribed, yet their association with kidney injury has drawn increasing concern. Using the PersADE database, we compared kidney adverse drug event (ADE) signals for four oral PPIs (omeprazole, esomeprazole, lansoprazole, pantoprazole) and described reporting patterns by age, body weight, and sex for omeprazole and esomeprazole.

METHODS: In this retrospective pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis, we retrieved spontaneous reports of nine predefined MedDRA kidney ADE categories with PPIs as the primary suspected drug. Signal detection employed reporting odds ratio (ROR) and proportional reporting ratio (PRR), with positive signals defined as case count ≥ 3, ROR ≥ 2, PRR ≥ 2, and χ2 ≥ 4. Subgroup analyses were descriptive and hypothesis-generating; no formal statistical testing or adjustment for confounders was performed. Due to high missing rates for demographic variables, subgroup analyses were limited to omeprazole and esomeprazole.

RESULTS: All four oral PPIs generated positive kidney ADE signals across multiple categories. However, pantoprazole showed no detectable signals for Acute tubular necrosis, chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder or renal cancer. Higher reporting counts were observed in patients aged ≥ 70 years and those weighing > 80 kg, whereas sex was not associated with appreciable differences in reporting counts.

CONCLUSIONS: All four PPIs exhibit clear kidney ADE signals. The subgroup findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating rather than established risk factors. These findings suggest that clinicians may consider caution and renal function monitoring in elderly or overweight patients, although further validation is needed.

articles.title: SQSTM1 promotes selective autophagic degradation of multiple PRRSV proteins by recruiting E3 ligase TRAF6 to inhibit viral replication.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) is an economically important disease that endangers the global pig industry and is caused by porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). Although previous studies have reported that PRRSV hijacks autophagy to facilitate its replication, the role of selective autophagy in PRRSV propagation remains largely unclear. Here, we identified the autophagic cargo receptor SQSTM1 as a novel host restriction factor against PRRSV. SQSTM1 overexpression significantly suppresses PRRSV replication, while SQSTM1 knockdown promotes viral proliferation. Moreover, SQSTM1 overexpression enhances the autophagic degradation of multiple PRRSV proteins, including Nsp5, Nsp12, GP4, and GP5. We further selected GP4 and GP5 as target proteins to explore the molecular mechanism by which SQSTM1 degrades PRRSV proteins. SQSTM1 promotes the trafficking of GP4 to LAMP2-positive lysosomes for autophagy‑lysosome-dependent degradation. SQSTM1 directly interacts with both GP4 and GP5, and recruits the host E3 ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 to enhance the polyubiquitination of these two viral proteins. Both the LC3-interacting region (LIR) and ubiquitin-associated (UBA) domains of SQSTM1 are required for SQSTM1-mediated inhibition of PRRSV replication. Further mechanistic validation showed that TRAF6 mediates K63-linked polyubiquitination of GP4 at the K115 residue and GP5 at the K59 residue. These ubiquitination modifications are indispensable for the binding of GP4/GP5 to SQSTM1 and their subsequent autophagic degradation. TRAF6 knockdown abrogates SQSTM1-induced degradation of PRRSV Nsp5, Nsp12, GP4, and GP5, and eliminates the antiviral activity of SQSTM1, indicating that SQSTM1 and TRAF6 synergistically degrade viral proteins and constrain PRRSV replication. The present study demonstrates the critical role of selective autophagy in host defense against PRRSV infection. These findings provide novel insights for the development of targeted anti-PRRSV drugs and vaccines.

articles.title: Cytoreductive Surgery with or without Hyperthermic Intrathoracic Chemotherapy for Thymic Epithelial Malignancies with Pleural Dissemination.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Our objectives were to evaluate the comparative clinical outcomes of cytoreductive surgery with or without hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITCH) for thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) with pleural dissemination and to assess the utility of a novel Pleural Tumor Index (PTI) as a practical prognostic tool to guide patient selection.

METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients with pleural-disseminated TETs who underwent surgery with or without HITCH. The HITCH protocol utilized a standardized sequential dual-agent hyperthermic perfusion (43 °C for 60 mins per session): doxorubicin (25 mg/m2) on postoperative day 1, followed by cisplatin (50 mg/m2) on postoperative day 2. The PTI was used to quantify pleural tumor burden. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline covariates. Perioperative and oncological outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: Of 130 enrolled patients, 66 received surgery plus HITCH (Surg+HITCH) and 64 underwent surgery alone, yielding 44 propensity score-matched pairs. Surg+HITCH was associated with improved 3-year progression-free survival (87.3% vs. 48.6%; hazard ratio 0.28; 95% confidence interval 0.11-0.66; P = 0.013) and lower recurrence (9.09% vs. 36.3%). A PTI score >10 indicated a higher risk of tumor progression. Complication rates were slightly higher in the Surg+HITCH group (75.0% vs. 65.9%) but predominantly involved minor events without increasing intensive care unit stay or mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Surg+HITCH safely improves long-term tumor control in patients with pleural-disseminated TETs. The PTI serves as a practical tool for risk stratification to guide patient selection. Further prospective studies are required to validate our findings.

articles.title: Adolescent Exposure to Deadly Neighborhood Gun Violence and Asthma Burden in Early Adulthood.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Gun violence is a pervasive yet understudied neighborhood stressor that may shape chronic disease risk via inflammatory pathways. This study examined whether residential exposure to deadly neighborhood gun violence in adolescence is associated with asthma incidence, hospitalization, and functional limitation in early adulthood. Data are from the Future of Families and Child Wellbeing Study, a birth cohort across 20 U.S. cities (N = 1936 without prior asthma at age 15). Prior-year exposure to deadly gun violence within 1600 meters of participants' homes at age 15 was measured using Gun Violence Archive data linked to residential addresses. Logistic, Firth penalized logistic, and linear regression estimated associations with incident asthma diagnosis, hospitalization, and functional limitation at age 22. At age 15, nearly half of participants (48.8%) were exposed to a nearby fatal shooting. In fully adjusted models, each 1-SD increase in annual exposure rate (SD = 4.9 incidents) was associated with 25% higher odds of incident asthma by age 22 (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.06-1.49). Exploratory analyses suggested stronger associations among males, but this difference was limited to the highest exposure levels. Among those newly diagnosed, exposure was associated with greater functional limitation (β = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.06-0.44) and higher odds of hospitalization (OR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.37-5.33), although the latter was based on few events. These findings suggest neighborhood gun violence exposure during adolescence may contribute to incident asthma or clinical manifestation of previously subclinical airway vulnerability. Future research should investigate biological mechanisms and identify intervention targets.

articles.title: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults.
articles.abstract: Although population-based studies of circulating blood proteins have provided profound insight into human biology, transient changes to time-dependent exposures often remain elusive. Here, we perform a longitudinal dried blood spot (DBS) self-sampling study in 808 young adults (aged 24-27, 64% females) from the Swedish Barn [Children], Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm Epidemiology cohort. In total, we collected ~2400 samples from 2020 to 2022. Each sample was profiled for SARS-CoV-2 serological, anti-interferon autoantibodies (AAbs), and 365 inflammation-related proteins. We subsequently linked these samples to registry-confirmed infection and vaccination exposures, physiological traits, genetic variation, and blood counts. We show that data-driven seroclustering captures the response to both infection and vaccination exposures, while stable AAbs against interferon receptors IFNAR1 and IFNGR2 associate with the duration of self-reported COVID-19 symptoms. Genome-wide mapping reveals 664 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) across 65 proteins, with cis-pQTLs associated proteins showing greater longitudinal stability. Paired pre- and post-exposure samples indicate temporal changes in protein levels after infection (LAP3) and vaccination (TIMP3). This multi-molecular epidemiological profiling of self-sampled blood captures dynamic immune trajectories and shorter-term variability in a population of young adults.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines in post-marketing settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, particularly among infants and older adults worldwide. This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines.

METHODS: In this review, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 20, 2025. Grey literature and reference lists were also searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for older adults and infants. Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions.

RESULTS: Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval (CI): USD 41.89-168.21; I2 = 93.2%]. For infants, the pooled INB was USD 5.81 (95% CI: USD - 35.44-47.07; I2 = 89.4%). In the European subgroup, the pooled INB among older adults was USD 123.63 (95% CI: USD 41.23-206.02; I2 = 89.4%), while that for infants was USD 15.00 (95% CI: USD - 4.33-34.34; I2 = 43.4%). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses showed robust pooled INBs among older adults, whereas infant estimates were sensitive to study exclusion.

CONCLUSIONS: At the thresholds used in the included studies, RSV vaccination might be cost-effective for older adults in post-marketing settings, while the evidence for maternal vaccination remained inconclusive. Descriptive findings suggested that age- and risk-based targeting in older adults and seasonal maternal vaccination may yield higher INB estimates. Substantial between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates and highlights the need to consider local epidemiology and implementation conditions when developing RSV vaccination policies.

articles.title: Associations between diabetic neuropathy and bone density and bone microarchitecture in type 2 diabetes: The Deep Phenotyping Study.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diabetic neuropathy may contribute to skeletal fragility through sensorimotor and autonomic dysfunction. We investigated associations of peripheral and autonomic neuropathy with bone density, microarchitecture, and material properties in individuals with type 2 diabetes stratified by age.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, individuals with type 2 diabetes with (n = 50, mean age 67.4 years) and without (n = 73, mean age 62.2 years) diabetic neuropathy underwent assessment of bone structure and quality using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry with trabecular bone score, high-resolution peripheral computed tomography, and microindentation, alongside evaluation of neuropathy and autonomic function. Associations were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and BMI, with age-stratified analyses ( < 65 and ≥65 years).

RESULTS: In individuals < 65 years, neuropathy was associated with markedly lower areal bone mineral density at the total hip (β =-0.15 g/cm2, 95% CI -0.24 to-0.06), and femoral neck (β =-0.18 g/cm², -0.26 to -0.09), and with lower TBS (β =-1.56, -2.23 to -0.89). At the tibia, neuropathy was associated with lower total, cortical and trabecular volumetric bone mineral density, lower trabecular bone volume fraction, and higher cortical porosity. At the radius, lower cortical volumetric bone mineral density and lower trabecular number were observed. No significant associations were observed for Bone Material Strength index or in individuals ≥ 65 years.

CONCLUSION: In individuals with type 2 diabetes <65 years, diabetic neuropathy is associated with lower bone density and differences in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture. These findings suggest neuropathy may be associated with impaired bone quality in younger adults with type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling therapy with virtual reality biofeedback for functional recovery in people with chronic spinal cord injury: a feasibility case series.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Feasibility case series.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility and individual therapeutic effects of functional electrical stimulation (FES)-assisted cycling therapy combined with virtual reality (VR) biofeedback (the iCycle) on function and walking outcomes in people with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI).

SETTING: London Spinal Cord Injury Centre, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, UK.

METHODS: Participants undertook up to three 30-minute iCycle sessions weekly in 4-week blocks for up to 12 weeks. Participants were assessed at the end of each block and were given the option to opt-out or continue. FES was applied to lower-limb muscles during alternate pedal revolutions, enabling biofeedback of voluntary effort via the VR cycling platform (Zwift). Clinical outcome measures included International Standards of Neurological Classification of SCI (ISNCSCI) motor and sensory scores, Berg Balance Scale, Trunk Impairment Scale, Walking Index for SCI-II (WISCI-II), 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), 10-Metre Walk Test (10MWT) and voluntary power output during cycling.

RESULTS: Five participants completed 8 or 12 weeks of training. Functional improvements were observed primarily after the first 4-week block. Two participants increased lower extremity motor scores (+3 to +4). Four participants demonstrated gains in walking endurance (6MWT +90-135 m), reduced 10MWT times, and improved WISCI-II scores. Balance and voluntary power output continued to improve for up to 12 weeks.

CONCLUSION: iCycle training was feasible for individuals with incomplete chronic SCI. Clinically meaningful improvements in walking, balance, and endurance were observed, most prominently within the first 4-week block.

SPONSORSHIP: University College London.

articles.title: Emerging biomarkers for neonatal sepsis: beyond C-reactive protein and procalcitonin.
articles.abstract: Current biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, including CRP and PCT, lack sufficient accuracy to guide antibiotic decisions in VLBW infants. This Letter synthesizes emerging evidence that presepsin, the CRP-to-albumin ratio, and omics-derived multi-marker panels may outperform conventional markers. It reframes the debate from single-marker accuracy to pragmatic, gestational age-specific, multi-marker implementation. The impact is a concrete agenda: validate combined panels and gestational age-specific reference ranges to enable precision antibiotic therapy in the NICU.

articles.title: Hemodynamic and respiratory effects of non-invasive ventilation modalities in very preterm infants: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) minimizes lung injury in preterm infants. We compared the short-term hemodynamic and respiratory effects of different NIV modalities.

METHODS: Infants <32 weeks' gestation or birthweight <1500 g on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (NCPAP) were randomized, in a two-sequence crossover design to 2 h each of non-synchronized NIPPV (NS-NIPPV) and neurally synchronized NIPPV (S-NIPPV). Ventricular output and function were assessed by echocardiography, with diaphragm activity and lung aeration evaluated. Linear mixed-effects models were used for analysis.

RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in right (RV) or left ventricular (LV) output across modes. RV output tended to be higher during S-NIPPV than NS-NIPPV (mean difference 24 mL/kg/min [95% CI; -3 to 51]; p = 0.08). NS-NIPPV was associated with a greater magnitude of LV peak global longitudinal strain (-2.54 [95% CI; -4.61 to -0.48]; p = 0.02) and strain rate (-0.45 [95% CI; -0.78 to -0.11]; p = 0.008) compared to NCPAP. S-NIPPV reduced peak Edi (7.2 ± 5.1 µV vs NCPAP 10.0 ± 6.8 µV; p < 0.01). Both NIPPV modes improved lung ultrasound score (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: S-NIPPV showed a non-significant trend toward higher RV output and significantly reduced diaphragm activity compared with NS-NIPPV; both NIPPV modes improved lung aeration relative to NCPAP.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRY: Thai Clinical Trials Registry. Registration number TCTR20240804002. Web link: https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/show/TCTR20240804002 .

IMPACT: In clinically stable very preterm infants, short-term exposure to NCPAP, NS-NIPPV, and S-NIPPV preserved biventricular output and myocardial performance, addressing concerns regarding hemodynamic compromise with higher airway pressures. S-NIPPV was associated with a significant reduction in diaphragmatic workload (peak Edi) and a non-significant trend toward higher RVO, without evidence of adverse cardiac effects; lung aeration improved with both NIPPV modes relative to NCPAP. These exploratory findings generate the hypothesis that the observed benefits are driven by effective pressure delivery rather than synchronization alone, offering mechanistic insight to refine NIV optimization in contemporary neonatal care.

articles.title: A pulse oximetry warning system predicts severity of late-onset sepsis in very low birth weight neonates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late-onset sepsis (LOS) causes morbidity and mortality in very-low birthweight (VLBW) neonates. We previously developed a machine learning model, the Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS), to predict LOS in the next 24 h. The neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score predicts sepsis mortality. We hypothesized that POWS scores would differentiate severe LOS events, defined by nSOFA >4, from milder events.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including VLBW infants diagnosed with culture-confirmed LOS with continuous vital sign data available. Mixed-effects regression was used to examine the association between POWS and nSOFA.

RESULTS: We analyzed 89 LOS episodes in 84 VLBW infants. Severe sepsis (nSOFA >4 within 48 h of blood culture) occurred in 27 (30%) episodes. Mean POWS scores were higher in the 24 h before severe LOS than non-severe LOS. POWS rose more steeply in the hours before sepsis diagnosis among infants with severe LOS.

CONCLUSION: POWS scores, predicting risk of LOS in the next 24 h, have a significantly higher rate of rise in severe episodes as compared to less severe episodes as measured by nSOFA. This result adds to evidence that POWS could prompt earlier intervention that improves sepsis outcomes.

IMPACT: Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is a leading cause of death and disability in premature infants. The Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS) uses continuous heart rate and oxygen saturation data to predict sepsis up to 24 h before clinical diagnosis. This study demonstrates that POWS rises more steeply before severe sepsis episodes, as defined by the neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score, than before milder episodes. POWS thus may provide earlier warning of the most severe sepsis events, potentially enabling earlier intervention in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Systemic and oral adverse effects of semaglutide reported in randomized controlled trials: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To map the systemic and oral adverse events (AEs) of semaglutide reported in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

DATA: This scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Only english-language and RCTs were considered.

SOURCES: A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 2019 until 2025.

STUDY SELECTION: Of 630 identified records (300 in PubMed, 312 in Scopus, and 18 in Web of Science), 12 studies were included after screening. The review identified systemic AEs of semaglutide, primarily gastrointestinal events like nausea (12 studies) and diarrhea (11 studies). Less frequent effects included pancreatitis (5 studies), hepatobiliary (3 studies) and gallbladder disease (3 studies), dental caries (1 study) and dry mouth (1 study). Subcutaneous administration predominating (7 studies), followed by oral (3) and mixed routes (2), over treatment durations of 21-68 weeks and 4-9 weeks of follow-up. Additionally, systemic events such as nasopharyngitis (5 studies), COVID-19 (5 studies), and metabolic or nutrition-related disorders were reported in all 12 studies. Importantly, none of the included studies directly investigated oral or dental outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide demonstrated an overall favorable safety profile in the included randomized controlled trials, with adverse events predominantly gastrointestinal. However, the RCTs did not provide direct evidence regarding oral health outcomes. Therefore, the available evidence is insufficient to draw conclusions about oral adverse events associated with semaglutide, highlighting the need for randomized clinical trials specifically designed to assess oral health outcomes in patients receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists.

articles.title: The Impact of Prolonged Pre-Heart Transplantation Left Ventricular Assist Device on Post-Transplantation Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Durable mechanical circulatory support with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) serves as bridge to heart transplantation (HTx) in patients with advanced heart failure. LVAD therapy is associated with improved outcomes, but has inherent limitations, including device-related complications. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the impact of prolonged LVAD support in patients who underwent HTx as compared to those without LVAD support.

METHOD: We retrospectively analysed 148 HTx recipients at University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands (2007-2023): 52 with prior LVAD support and 96 direct HTx patients. Outcomes included post-HTx survival, rejection requiring treatment, 1-year cardiac haemodynamics, and need for kidney replacement therapy.

RESULTS: Median LVAD duration was 757 days (range 16-2,113). The LVAD group had fewer females (21% vs 54%; p<0.001). After a median 3.5-year follow-up, post-HTx survival was similar between groups (hazard ratio 0.83; 95% confidence interval 0.40-1.6; p=0.52). No significant differences were observed in the incidence of rejection requiring therapy (p=0.91) nor need for kidney replacement therapy (p=0.05-0.42). At 1-year post-HTx, the LVAD group showed modestly elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (12.7 vs 10.6 mmHg; p=0.03) and reduced cardiac index (3.0 vs 3.3 L/min/m2; p=0.03) compared to direct HTx recipients.

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged LVAD support as bridge-to-transplantation showed no statistically significant differences with direct HTx in terms of post-HTx survival, rejection rates, and renal function despite minor differences in 1-year haemodynamic parameters.

articles.title: Sensor-Based Force-Frequency Relation Assessment in Personalised Cardiovascular Care: An Overview.
articles.abstract: Contractility is the intrinsic ability of the heart muscle to generate force and shorten. The force-frequency relation can reveal initial alterations between normal and abnormal contractility, making it a practical index for clinical evaluation. This narrative review provides a picture of force-frequency relationship assessment, including stress echocardiography laboratories (echo labs), nuclear laboratories (nuclear labs), implantable systems, ambulatory sensors, and wearable sensors. Different approaches have been investigated in the literature, and their translation into practice could be valuable, even if challenging. With a vision for the future, real-time monitoring systems based on wearable or implantable devices, able to continuously track force-frequency changes during daily activities, could constitute a concrete opportunity for improved management of conditions such as chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease.

articles.title: Computed Tomography Coronary Angiography for Patients with Chest Pain: Ethnic Variation in Use, Coronary Atherosclerotic Burden, and Effect on Statin Treatment (ANZACS-QI 90).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We assessed ethnic differences in computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) utilisation, extent of coronary artery disease (CAD), and statin use among patients with chest pain at Middlemore Hospital, New Zealand.

METHOD: Patients without prior revascularisation (n=4,519) who underwent CTCA (2020-2024) were identified from the Aotearoa New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome Quality Improvement (ANZACS-QI) cardiac computed tomography registry. CTCA utilisation was assessed relative to incident acute coronary syndrome (ACS) hospitalisations in each age and ethnic group, which served as a surrogate for population CAD burden. CAD extent was assessed using the segment involvement score. Statin dispensing data were obtained from the national pharmaceutical data set.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 37.8% European/Other, 13.4% Māori, 19.8% Pacific, 15.5% Indian, and 13.5% other Asian patients. Māori, Pacific, and Indian patients (mean age, 55.7, 54.8, and 54.0 years, respectively) were younger than other Asian and European/Other patients (59.2 and 60.4 years, respectively; p<0.001). CTCA utilisation among those aged <55 years was lowest among Māori and Pacific patients, intermediate among European/Other and Indian patients, and highest among other Asian patients (CTCA-to-incident-ACS ratios, 2.5, 2.2, 3.0, 3.8, and 8.0, respectively). Indian and other Asian patients were most likely to have normal coronary arteries (p<0.001), while Māori and Pacific patients had the most extensive atherosclerosis (p<0.001). Post-CTCA statin use, for equivalent disease severity, was similar across ethnicities.

CONCLUSIONS: Young Māori and Pacific patients with chest pain are underinvestigated and undertreated relative to their population CAD burden. However, when CAD is identified, statin treatment is equal across ethnic groups. Therefore, CTCA facilitates equitable treatment for Māori and Pacific patients presenting with chest pain.

articles.title: Interpreting ANGPTL4: a compensatory marker of impending BBB decompensation in stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi

articles.title: Impact of ROI definition on head and neck cancer FDG-PET radiomics.
articles.abstract: Due to its rising incidence, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a global health challenge, and risk stratification is important for personalized treatment. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)-derived biomarkers show considerable potential for predicting HNSCC radio(chemo)therapy outcomes. However, the definition of the three-dimensional primary tumor region of interest (ROI) varies, with anatomically defined gross tumor volumes (GTV-ROIs) and PET-based metabolic tumor volumes (MTV-ROIs) often used interchangeably. Therefore, we assessed the effect of these ROI definitions on extracted radiomics features and radio(chemo)therapy outcome predictions in a multicenter dataset of 741 HNSCC patients. Features from the two ROI definitions were compared using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). The investigated study endpoints, locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS), were evaluated using the number of outcome-associated features in univariate Cox regression, as well as by the performance of multivariable machine-learning models. GTV-ROIs and MTV-ROIs yielded substantially different radiomics features, with a median ICC of 0.63 (IQR, 0.37-0.85). The MTV-ROIs led to a higher number of OS-associated features (continuous features: p = 0.003, binarized features: p = 0.015) and comparable model C-indexes, 0.61 (95% CI: 0.51-0.69; MTV-ROIs) vs.0.58 (95% CI: 0.49-0.66; GTV-ROIs) for LRC, and 0.65 (95% CI: 0.59-0.71; MTV-ROIs) vs.0.63 (95% CI: 0.56-0.69; GTV-ROIs) for OS. To conclude, the definition of the HNSCC primary tumor ROI has a notable effect on FDG-PET feature values and their prognostic potential, whereas its effect on multivariable model performance appears limited.

articles.title: Diuretic response in very elderly patients with acute heart failure. Author's reply.
Mucus Plugs in COPD: From Soft Endpoints to the Hard Evidence Based on Imaging.
Clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of ascitic fungal infections in patients with cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: To investigate the clinical characteristics, pathogen spectrum, antifungal susceptibility, and prognostic factors of ascitic fungal infections in patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: This retrospective study included cirrhotic patients with positive ascitic fungal cultures. Patients with ascitic bacterial infections served as controls. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 108 patients were included, comprising 57 with spontaneous fungal peritonitis (SFP) and 51 with fungiascites (FA). Among 116 fungal isolates recovered from ascitic fluid, 107 were Candida spp. Most isolates were susceptible to antifungal agents, although notable azole resistance was observed among non-albicans Candida species. Patients with SFP had higher mortality than those with FA (29.8% vs 13.7%, p = 0.045) and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (29.8% vs 7.0%, p = 0.002). A nomogram incorporating serum urea (>18 mmol/L), neutrophil count (>10 × 109/L), and platelet count (<75 × 109/L) may facilitate early assessment of 30-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Ascitic fluid fungal infections, particularly SFP, are associated with significantly worse outcomes than bacterial ascitic infections. The primary pathogens are Candida spp., with high susceptibility to azole antifungals.

articles.title: When It All Falls On the Physicians: A Qualitative Study of Physician Workforce Changes Post-Dobbs in Four States With Abortion Bans.
articles.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to explore how abortion bans in four highly restrictive states affected physician workforce dynamics among physicians of diverse specialties after the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision.

METHODS: The Medical Integrity Initiative conducted in-depth interviews with physicians in Alabama, Idaho, Oklahoma, and Tennessee, states with strict abortion bans and severe legal penalties for physicians. Participants included specialists in emergency medicine, maternal-fetal medicine, medical genetics, obstetrics, oncology, and reproductive endocrinology and infertility. We used stratified and snowball sampling and conducted interviews via Zoom from July to October 2024. Grounded theory methodology informed the inductive approach to data analysis. We began with open (descriptive) coding and followed it with axial (interpretive) analysis.

RESULTS: Thirty-two physicians across all specialties reported new challenges following the Dobbs decision. We identified the following overarching themes: 1) heightened liability concerns, 2) shifting burden of care onto academic hospitals, 3) added advocacy responsibilities, 4) emotional strain and ethical dilemma of leaving the state, and 5) increased challenges regarding workforce size and workload. Challenges that participants described included colleagues' exodus, difficulty recruiting providers and trainees, and labor and delivery unit closures. Many reported that they considered leaving their state. Participants expressed a desire for their institutions to support evidence-based clinical practice.

CONCLUSION: Physicians experienced changes in workforce composition and responsibilities following the Dobbs decision. Collective action and robust occupational, legal, and mental health support from their institutions and medical societies might enable physicians to safely stay and sustainably advocate in states with abortion bans.

articles.title: Effectiveness and safety of lumbar erector spinae plane block versus no locoregional block in hip surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia in hip surgery has been shown to reduce the need for opioids and conventional analgesics, facilitate ambulation and early recovery, improve respiratory dynamics, and reduce the incidence of venous thrombosis and pneumonia. Lumbar erector spinae plane block (L-ESPB) has been put forward as a novel ultrasound-guided locoregional technique to relieve pain in hip surgery; however, the supporting evidence remains scarce.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to provide evidence on the role of L-ESPB in perioperative pain management during hip surgery. We hypothesized that patients receiving L-ESPB compared to no nerve block would require fewer opioids and experience less pain after hip surgery. The primary outcome was the difference in pain intensity between the L-ESPB group and the control group measured at rest at 2 hours postoperatively using the visual analogue scale (VAS). We compared postoperative analgesic needs and opioid consumption in both groups, assessed the technical difficulty involved in performing L-ESPB, and recorded any side effects in both treatment arms. Finally, we evaluated the level of patient satisfaction.

DESIGN: This is a pragmatic, single-centre, parallel-group randomized controlled trial in 180 patients.

SETTING: Patients seen at a tertiary care hospital were recruited between June 2024 and May 2025.

PATIENTS: Inclusion criteria were: age >18 years (irrespective of sex), scheduled for hip surgery, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class I to III, willing to sign the study informed consent form, and able to understand and use the VAS for pain assessment. Exclusion criteria were: contraindications for the study technique or drugs used, inability to administer the block due to technical barriers, severe cognitive impairment or documented mental disabilities, and current enrolment in another clinical trial.

INTERVENTION: Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either ultrasound-guided L-ESPB or conventional intravenous analgesia. A total of 180 patients (n = 90, 50% in each group) were enrolled. Data analysis was performed using SPSS.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was resting pain intensity measured using the VAS at 2 hours postoperatively.

RESULTS: At 2 hours postoperatively, resting VAS pain scores did not differ between groups (L-ESPB [1.81 ± 1.81]; controls: [1.76 ± 1.28]; p = [p = 0.99]).Resting pain scores were slightly lower in the L-ESPB group at 6 and 12 hours; however, the magnitude of the difference was small and did not result in reduced postoperative opioid consumption or rescue analgesic requirements. One patient in the L-ESPB group developed a high neuraxial block requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation for approximately 6 hours, with full recovery and no sequelae.

CONCLUSIONS: Lumbar ESPB did not reduce resting pain at 2 hours after hip surgery and did not reduce postoperative opioid consumption. Small reductions in resting pain scores at 6 and 12 hours were observed, but their clinical relevance is uncertain. Our results do not support routine L-ESPB as a standard analgesic technique for unselected hip surgery patients receiving multimodal analgesia. Further research into this topic is warranted.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06567522; https://www.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov/study/NCT06567522.

STUDY PROTOCOL: doi: https://doi.org/10.2196/75854.

articles.title: Fenofibrate and diabetic retinopathy: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess fenofibrate effects on diabetic retinopathy (DR) progression and need for retinal treatment.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through June 9, 2026, for randomized trials comparing oral fenofibrate with placebo in adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes and at least two years of follow-up. The primary outcome was a composite of DR progression or need for retinal treatment. Odds ratios (OR) were pooled using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Four trials (20,655 participants) were included; three (3,756) contributed to the primary outcome. Fenofibrate reduced the composite outcome (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.56-0.81; I2 = 0%), incident macular edema (0.47, 0.29-0.76; I2 = 0%) and need for retinal laser (0.75, 0.65-0.87; I2 = 7%). DR progression on imaging was reduced (0.72, 0.58-0.89; I2 = 0%), but not when FIELD one-step progression was used (0.80, 0.60-1.07). Moderate vision loss (0.99, 0.83-1.18; I2 = 0%) and all-cause mortality (1.01, 0.87-1.17; I2 = 26%) did not differ. Subgroup analyses by diabetes type and baseline retinopathy were underpowered.

CONCLUSIONS: Fenofibrate reduces the composite of DR progression or need for retinal treatment over up to five years of follow-up, without a demonstrated effect on moderate vision loss.

articles.title: Associations between U-HP, TyG-BMI, TG/Cys-C and albuminuria in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the correlations of urinary haptoglobin (U-HP), triglyceride-glucose-body mass index (TyG-BMI), and triglyceride/cystatin C (TG/Cys-C) with albuminuria in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: A total of 174 hospitalized T2DM patients were retrospectively enrolled and divided into non-albuminuria (n = 88) and albuminuria (n = 86) groups according to the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR). Spearman correlation, multivariate logistic regression, and characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed. Internal bootstrap validation with 1000 resamples was conducted to assess model optimism.

RESULTS: U-HP and TyG-BMI were higher, while TG/Cys-C was lower in the albuminuria group (all P < 0.05). U-HP was correlated with the UACR (r = 0.57) and was identified as an independent factor associated with albuminuria (OR = 1.233 per 100 μg/L increase;95%CI: 1.045-1.455; P = 0.013). The AUC of U-HP was 0.755 (95%CI: 0.682-0.827). The fully adjusted model including clinical variables and medication use achieved an AUC of 0.867 (95%CI: 0.813-0.921).

CONCLUSION: U-HP is independently associated with albuminuria in hospitalized T2DM patients with moderate discriminative value and high specificity. However, owing to the cross-sectional design and the inherent correlation between U-HP and UACR, these findings reflect associations rather than predictions and require validation in prospective cohort studies.

articles.title: Temporal Changes in Body Mass Index among Patients with Severe COVID-19 in Japan.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize temporal changes in body mass index (BMI) among patients with severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) admitted to intensive care units in Japan.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study using the Japanese Intensive care PAtient Database. We included 8,159 patients with confirmed COVID-19 admitted to 95 intensive care units during fiscal years 2020-2023. BMI distributions were compared across fiscal years and 10 epidemic waves. Sensitivity analyses restricted the cohort to patients with viral pneumonia, patients requiring advanced respiratory support, and patients without major comorbidities.

RESULTS: BMI was highest in 2020-2021 and declined markedly from 2022 onward. The distribution showed a distinct downward shift between the fifth and sixth epidemic waves and remained lower thereafter. This pattern persisted across sensitivity analyses despite higher severity scores in 2022 and less frequent invasive respiratory support and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

CONCLUSIONS: The phenotype of patients reaching critical illness changed during the pandemic. Risk factors derived from early-pandemic cohorts should therefore be interpreted dynamically as viral variants, population immunity, and clinical context evolve.

articles.title: Natural History and Clinical Outcomes of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-Producing Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Bacteriuria.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the natural history of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-producing carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (NDM-CRPA) bacteriuria and predictors of progression from asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) to symptomatic urinary tract infection (sUTI).

METHODS: We retrospectively included adults with NDM-CRPA bacteriuria at a South Korean tertiary-care hospital (2021-2024). Progression was analyzed using a prespecified two-covariate Firth penalized logistic regression and competing-risk methods.

RESULTS: Of 271 patients, 220 initially had ASB and 51 had sUTI; of the 220 with ASB, 15 (6.8%) progressed to sUTI (10 within 30 days) and 205 remained asymptomatic. With death as a competing event, the 1-year cumulative incidence of progression was 7.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.5-12.2%). Younger age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.94 per year; 95% CI, 0.91-0.97) and complicated urologic history (aOR 4.77; 95% CI, 1.51-18.60) were associated with progression. Among 66 patients with sUTI, 50.0% had catheter-associated infection and 9.1% died within 30 days. Sequence type (ST) 773 predominated (83.2%) and was more often aztreonam-susceptible than other clones (84.0% vs. 13.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Most NDM-CRPA bacteriuria remained asymptomatic; progression was uncommon, occurred early, and was associated with younger age and complicated urologic history. These single-center findings from an ST773-dominant setting support avoiding routine treatment of NDM-CRPA ASB but require multicenter confirmation.

articles.title: JCF: In Case You Missed it! Summary of HFSA 2026.
Unveiling the mechanisms of glucokinase variants implicated in human disease through molecular dynamics simulations.
articles.abstract: Glucokinase (GK) is considered a critical glucose sensor in pancreatic β cells. Variants in the GCK gene cause a range of diverse glycemic disorders, from hyperinsulinism to mild and severe diabetes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of variant-specific effects in different GCK-related disorders remains a significant challenge. Here, we employed comprehensive molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how specific GK variants: W99C (hyperinsulinism), H50D (neonatal diabetes), V226M (GCK-MODY), and two novel variants, Y61D and M115V, affect enzyme dynamics and function. Through 12 μs of cumulative simulations, we analyzed protein stability, domain flexibility, relative binding energetics, and correlated motions across all variants. Our findings suggest distinct mechanistic patterns: the hyperinsulinism-associated W99C variant is consistent with increased local flexibility and enhanced anticorrelated domain motions, potentially facilitating catalytic turnover despite reduced glucose affinity (ΔGbind = -22.26 kcal/mol). Conversely, diabetes-associated variants H50D and V226M enhance glucose binding (ΔGbind = -36.27 and -35.30 kcal/mol, respectively) but reduced conformational flexibility, suggesting a "substrate trapping" mechanism that may impairs catalysis. The GCK-MODY variants, Y61D and M115V, exhibited distinct molecular profiles, demonstrating unique perturbations in glucose binding and allosteric regulation that offer insights into their potential pathogenic mechanisms. Our detailed analysis suggest that different GK variants might affect enzyme conformation and function through different mechanisms, resulting in varying clinical phenotypes.

articles.title: DEGORA: turning heterogeneous published DEG summaries into an inspectable gene-evidence atlas.
articles.abstract: Published tables of differentially expressed genes (DEG tables) can support secondary transcriptomic analyses when expression matrices or variance estimates are unavailable, but they are not consistently deposited in public repositories. DEGORA converts curated DEG tables into a local database that links gene-level evidence to original studies. It standardizes gene identifiers, collapses related contrasts within studies so that each study contributes once, applies fixed heuristic quality weights, and ranks genes by cross-study support and directional concordance. An optional search module identifies potentially reusable tables. We evaluated DEGORA using four human transcriptional programs as positive-control benchmarks, each represented by 2 to 15 publication-level source units and by up to 20 after human microarray sources were added. DEG tables for three programs were generated from publicly available count matrices, whereas those for the fourth were obtained from the original publications. Using RNA-seq evidence, DEGORA recovered 93% of interferon, 59% of endoplasmic reticulum stress, 73% of heat-shock, and 85% of hypoxia markers among the top 100 ranked genes. In three confirmatory datasets, DEGORA showed no consistent ranking advantage over alternative methods applied to the same tables.
