The same workflow organized published Alzheimer's disease cohort evidence without recomputing differential expression. Across ten evaluated datasets, performance varied with how the input tables were generated. Overall, DEGORA organizes differential expression evidence at the study level and keeps every ranked gene linked to the publications, assays, and reported statistics behind it.

articles.title: The impaired white matter integrity and altered functional connectivity in Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by structural abnormalities in the cerebral cortex and subcortical regions. Nevertheless, functional connectivity (FC) alterations within these affected white matter (WM) regions have not been fully clarified.

METHODS: We combine diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) to explore abnormalities in WM structure and FC in 20 PD patients and 22 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (HCs).

RESULTS: Compared with the HCs, PD patients showed lower fractional anisotropy (FA) values in multiple widespread WM tracts, including the the forceps minor, the bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculus, the right inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus, corticospinal tract (CST) and superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), the left anterior thalamic radiation (ATR), uncinate fasciculus and cingulum. Seed-based FC analysis revealed that: for the CST seed, PD patients exhibited reduced FC with the bilateral postcentral gyrus and precentral gyrus, the right superior occipital gyrus and left inferior parietal lobule. For the SLF seed, PD patients exhibited reduced FC with the bilateral anterior cingulate cortex. For the ATR seed, hypoconnectivity was found in multiple cerebellar subregions, including the bilateral cerebellum VIII and cerebellum IX, the right cerebellum VI and cerebellar crus I, and the left middle temporal gyrus.

CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that PD patients exhibit widespread WM microstructural damage and some of these damaged fibers show abnormal FC, which may account for motor deficits and cognitive decline observed in PD. The combined use of DTI and rs-fMRI provides novel perspectives on the neural mechanisms underlying PD.

articles.title: Continuous positive airway pressure versus high-flow nasal oxygen in adults with pneumonia-related acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) are both used to avert invasive mechanical ventilation in patients with pneumonia-related acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), but head-to-head evidence comparing these two modalities specifically, rather than each against conventional oxygen, remains fragmented.

METHODS: We searched major databases for studies enrolling adults with pneumonia-related AHRF, including COVID-19-related pneumonia, managed with CPAP versus HFNO. The prespecified primary outcome was intubation within 30 days; secondary outcomes were time to intubation, in-hospital, 30-day, and 90-day mortality, and length of hospital stay.

RESULTS: Seven studies (n = 1551), met the inclusion criteria. CPAP was associated with a significantly lower risk of intubation within 30 days than HFNO (RR 0.75 [0.65-0.86], p < 0.0001; I2 = 33%; moderate certainty of evidence). This benefit was significant among patients with COVID-19 pneumonia (RR 0.75 [0.65-0.86], p < 0.0001) but not among those with non-COVID-19 pneumonia (RR 0.67 [0.31-1.45]), although no significant subgroup interaction was detected (p = 0.78). CPAP was also associated with a significantly longer time to intubation than HFNO (MD 22.27 h [16.22-28.33]). No significant differences were observed between CPAP and HFNO for 30-day mortality, 90-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, or length of hospital stay. The reduction in intubation was attenuated but persisted when the analysis was restricted to the four randomized trials (RR 0.81 [0.70-0.95]; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with pneumonia-related AHRF, CPAP probably reduces the risk of intubation compared with HFNO without conferring a mortality advantage or reducing length of stay. HFNO remains a reasonable, generally better-tolerated alternative.

articles.title: Vilanterol/Umeclidinium versus Vilanterol/Glycopyrronium via Metered-Dose or Dry-Powder Inhaler in Indian Adults with COPD: Two Randomized Phase III Non-Inferiority Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) plus long-acting β2-agonist (LABA) fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) are recommended for symptomatic at-risk patients, and are available on both metered-dose inhaler (MDI) and dry-powder inhaler (DPI) platforms. We evaluated new, locally manufactured MDI and DPI formulations of vilanterol/umeclidinium in Indian adults with COPD.

METHODS: Two independent Phase III, randomized, parallel-group, active-controlled non-inferiority trials (MDI study: double-blind; DPI study: open-label) were conducted in India over 12 weeks, using a -100 mL non-inferiority margin for trough forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). The MDI study (n=226) enrolled adults aged 40-75 years with moderate-to-very-severe COPD, while the DPI study (n=230) enrolled patients with moderate-to-severe COPD. Each trial was analyzed separately, without pooling.

RESULTS: Non-inferiority was demonstrated in both studies, with least-squares mean (LS mean) trough FEV1 differences of 49.18 mL (95% confidence interval [CI]: -24.08, 122.43) in the MDI study and 6.1 mL (95% CI: -47.32, 59.46) in the DPI study (Test - Reference; per-protocol population); both lower 95% CI bounds exceeded the -100 mL margin. No statistically significant between-arm differences were detected for secondary endpoints. Adverse events were predominantly mild, with no deaths or serious adverse events over 12 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Vilanterol/umeclidinium FDC delivered via MDI and DPI was non-inferior to vilanterol/glycopyrronium FDC delivered by the same device type for change in trough FEV1 at 12 weeks in Indian adults with COPD. Longer-term studies in broader populations are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI) CTRI/2025/03/082314 (MDI study) and CTRI/2025/06/088810 (DPI study).

articles.title: Impact of pharmacist-led interventions on clinical and economic outcomes of hospital-acquired infections: A scoping review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) are commonly associated with increased morbidity, mortality, and higher healthcare costs. Pharmacists play an expanding role in infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship (AMS), however, evidence supporting the impact of pharmacist-led interventions remains fragmented.

OBJECTIVE: This review aims to identify pharmacist-led interventions used for HAIs, evaluate their characteristics, reported clinical and economic outcomes and identify gaps in the literature.

METHODS: A scoping review of studies published between 2015 and 2025 identified from PubMed and Cochrane Library databases was conducted. Studies that involved pharmacists-led interventions on HAIs in acute care settings were included. A narrative synthesis of clinical and economic outcomes was performed.

RESULTS: From the initial 1024 studies identified, ten studies met the inclusion criteria. Two studies were conducted in the United States, two in China, two in Pakistan, and one each in Japan, Ethiopia, Iraq and Sudan. Four studies evaluated hospital-acquired pneumonia, including two that examined ventilator-associated pneumonia. Other studies addressed Clostridioides difficile, postoperative pulmonary and surgical site infections and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Overall, the studies reported an association between pharmacist-led interventions and an improvement in clinical cures, a general decrease in mortality, reductions in length of stay and HAI incidence and improved antimicrobial prescribing. Readmission findings were mixed with no increase in adverse drug reactions. The studies also showed a decrease in antimicrobial consumption, days of therapy, antibiotic use and antibiotic treatment duration. All studies reporting direct costs reported cost reductions following pharmacist-led interventions.

CONCLUSION: Pharmacist-led interventions show promising clinical and economic benefits in HAI management and should be implemented in acute care settings. However, the current evidence base is limited by the underrepresentation of HAI types, reducing its generalizability. Further high-quality studies across diverse settings are needed to strengthen the evidence base of pharmacist-led interventions on HAI prevention and management.

articles.title: Impact of a multi-site, multidisciplinary self-measured blood pressure monitoring program.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improving hypertension control is designated as a Healthy People 2030 Leading Health Indicator. Self-measured blood pressure (SMBP) monitoring programs can help fill care gaps for underserved patients, including patients in rural locations. Local community healthcare institutions can expand SMBP program access to people with transportation and telemedicine barriers.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify the effects of a multi-site, multidisciplinary SMBP monitoring program on participant blood pressure measurements in 11 rural, underserved counties.

PRACTICE DESCRIPTION: The MPower Consortium, a regional health improvement network, serves 11 Southeast Missouri counties through collaborations among community pharmacies, public health departments, non-profit organizations, Federally Qualified Health Centers, and behavioral health organizations. Following a successful pilot, a SMBP monitoring program was expanded across the consortium.

PRACTICE INNOVATION: This study evaluated the first year of the MPower Consortium SMBP monitoring program. The program included initial patient education and three follow-up visits conducted by Community Health Workers, pharmacists, and nursing professionals in 11 counties.

EVALUATION METHODS: Outcomes included change in blood pressure and percent of participants meeting hypertension treatment goals.

RESULTS: There were 302 patients included in the intent-to-treat analysis. Mean systolic blood pressure decreased from 144.3±21.9 mmHg to 134.2±14.8 mmHg (p<0.001) and mean diastolic blood pressure decreased from 83.1±13.3 mmHg to 77.5±9.0 mmHg (p<0.001). There was a statistically significant increase in percent of participants meeting goal blood pressure (p=0.008). The ANOVA analysis was significant for decrease in systolic blood pressure at each visit (p<0.001). There was no significant difference in the average systolic blood pressure decrease between the intent-to-treat and per-protocol groups (p=0.85).

CONCLUSION: This multisite, multidisciplinary SMBP monitoring program lowered blood pressures in patients in rural, underserved areas. This study demonstrates benefit of a collaborative SMBP monitoring program performed by a multidisciplinary group of local healthcare organizations in reaching a vulnerable population.

articles.title: Mapping the Molecular Interaction Profile of 5-(1,3,4-Oxadiazol-2-yl)-Substituted Pyrimidine Hybrids in Diabetes Mellitus: Synthetic Development, Enzyme Kinetics, Molecular Recognition, In Vivo Toxicology and Therapeutic Translation.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a major metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia and remains a significant therapeutic challenge. Inhibition of α-amylase and α-glucosidase, key enzymes involved in carbohydrate digestion, represents an effective strategy for controlling postprandial glucose levels. In the present study, a novel series of pyrimidine-oxadiazole hybrid derivatives was designed, synthesized, structurally characterized, and evaluated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. The synthesized compounds exhibited promising inhibitory activity against both enzymes, with compound 5 having IC50 = 5.20 ± 0.10 μM and 5.90 ± 0.30 μM for α-amylase and α-glucosidase, respectively,emerging as the most potent derivative against α-amylase and α-glucosidase, showing greater activity than the reference drug acarbose. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the electronic and steric characteristics of substituents substantially influenced enzyme inhibitory activity. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding orientations. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided insights into the electronic properties, frontier molecular orbitals, and chemical reactivity of the active derivatives. Furthermore, in silico ADMET profiling indicated favorable drug-like and pharmacokinetic characteristics. Overall, these findings identify compound 5 and the pyrimidine-oxadiazole scaffold as promising frameworks for further development of dual α-amylase/α-glucosidase inhibitors.

articles.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation Has Coronary and Other Selective Health Benefits: Comprehensive Results from the VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL) is the only large-scale randomized trial of marine omega-3 fatty acid (n-3 FA) supplementation for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cancer in a general population unselected for elevated risk. This article provides an integrated overview of the results of the n-3 FA component and its ancillary studies.

METHODS: VITAL is a completed nationwide, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2x2 factorial trial of n-3 FAs (1 g/day) and vitamin D3 (2000 IU/day) for a median of 5.3 years for primary prevention of CVD and cancer among 25,871 U.S. men aged ≥50 and women aged ≥55 years. Ancillary studies investigated effects on heart failure, atrial fibrillation (AF), autoimmune disease, and other endpoints.

RESULTS: Compared with placebo, the n-3 FA supplement did not significantly reduce the primary endpoint of major CVD events (hazard ratio [HR]=0.92 [95% confidence interval 0.80-1.06]) but did significantly reduce total myocardial infarction (MI; HR=0.72 [0.59-0.90]), fatal MI (HR=0.50 [0.26-0.97]), percutaneous coronary intervention (HR=0.78 [0.63-0.95]), and recurrent hospitalization for heart failure (HR=0.86 [0.74-0.998]). The intervention was not associated with AF risk. Supplemental n-3 FAs did not reduce total cancer incidence, other cancer endpoints, or all-cause mortality but was associated with significantly decreased risk of autoimmune disease (confirmed plus probable cases; HR=0.82 [0.68-0.99]). Effect modification by demographic, dietary, and clinical factors was observed for several endpoints, with greater benefits in Black participants and those with lower fish intake or cardiovascular risk factors, but with variable effects in women vs. men.

CONCLUSION: Supplemental n-3 FAs did not significantly reduce major CVD events or cancer but decreased multiple cardiac endpoints and autoimmune disease. Several factors modified treatment effects. Although the findings do not support routine n-3 FA supplementation among healthy adults for prevention of chronic disease, targeted supplementation of those with low fish intake and other select groups warrants consideration.

articles.title: Papillary Necrosis Masquerading as a Stone.
9-N-dodecyltetrahydroberberine exhibits hypoglycemic activity through direct interaction with the transmembrane domain of the insulin receptor and potentiation of its basal activity.
articles.abstract: In the present study, a series of novel 9-N-n-alkyl derivatives of tetrahydroberberine was synthesized, and their hypoglycemic activity was screened using an OGTT. Based on the results, the most active compound (9-N-dodecyltetrahydroberberine) was selected for further investigation upon long-term administration in mice with genetically determined T2DM (Ay/a mice, AY) and STZ-induced T2DM. Administration of this compound at a dose of 30 mg/kg improved glucose tolerance in both AY mice and mice with STZ-induced T2DM, enhanced insulin sensitivity, and led to a significant reduction in body weight in AY mice. However, no effect of the studied compound on lipid metabolism and liver enzyme activity was observed in the experimental animals. To investigate the mechanism underlying the enhanced insulin sensitivity observed in vivo, we examined the interaction of the compound with the insulin receptor in vitro. Using NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrated that 9-N-dodecyltetrahydroberberine selectively interacts with the N-terminal part of the transmembrane domain of the insulin receptor (IR), presumably potentiating the receptor switching to an active conformation. Enhanced phosphorylation of IR after incubation with 9-N-dodecyltetrahydroberberine was also detected. Overall, these findings suggest that 9-N-dodecyltetrahydroberberine exerts its effects on glucose metabolism by specifically targeting IR, positioning this novel compound as a promising pharmacological agent for diabetes treatment.

articles.title: Development of a novel blocking ELISA based on a monoclonal antibody targeting conserved epitope on ApxIVA for evaluating Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Porcine contagious pleuropneumonia (PCP) caused by Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae (APP) severely threatens the global swine industry. Reliable differential diagnosis is crucial for disease control and APP eradication. The ApxIV toxin, a species-specific virulence factor secreted by all APP serovars and expressed exclusively in infected animals, serves as a key target for differentiating naturally infected pigs from vaccinated pigs. In this study, a monoclonal antibody (mAb) 1D5 against ApxIVA was generated using hybridoma technology. Through protein truncation, prediction of antigen-antibody complex structures, and point mutation validation, TYR436 was identified as a residue critical for mAb-1D5 recognition. This residue was conserved in all 169 ApxIVA sequences included in the analysis. A soluble truncated ApxIVA protein, rApxIVA T2 (348573 aa), containing TYR436, was constructed and successfully expressed in a prokaryotic system and purified. A blocking ELISA (bELISA) antibody detection method was established based on this protein and mAb-1D5. A cutoff value of 42.86% was established using a development panel of 206 sera. The analytical sensitivity was 1:8, and no cross-reactivity was observed with the tested sera positive for antibodies against eight other swine pathogens. Intra- and inter-batch coefficients of variation were below 10%. In an independent panel of 305 field sera, the positive, negative, and overall percent agreements with a commercial APP ApxIV bELISA kit were 90.4%, 100%, and 96.1%, respectively, with a Cohen's kappa of 0.917 (95% CI: 0.872-0.963). Further validation using samples with independently confirmed infection status is required to establish its diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Largemouth bass virus (LMBV) utilizes GADD45b to induce ferroptosis for facilitating viral replication.
articles.abstract: Largemouth bass virus (LMBV) causes high mortality rate and significant economic loss in largemouth bass aquaculture. We previously identified growth arrest and DNA damage-inducible 45 beta (GADD45b) as a candidate resistance/susceptibility factor in largemouth bass, yet its functional role in LMBV infection remained unclear. Here, transcriptomic analysis suggested that GADD45b knockdown was mechanistically associated with pathways related to LMBV-induced ferroptosis. We found that LMBV infection induced ferroptosis in fathead minnow (FHM) cells, accompanied by significant upregulation of GADD45b. Subsequently, we discovered GADD45b overexpression promoted LMBV-induced ferroptosis and enhanced viral replication, whereas its knockdown suppressed both processes. Mechanistically, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry identified the viral major capsid protein (MCP) as a potential interacting partner of GADD45b. Moreover, the GADD45b-MCP interaction was associated with the regulation of FTH1a methylation, reduced FTH1a expression, and triggered ferroptosis. Importantly, both in vitro and in vivo experiments showed that the ferroptosis inhibitor liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1) suppressed LMBV infection, while the ferroptosis inducer Erastin promoted viral infection. In summary, our findings indicated that GADD45b plays an important role in ferroptosis induced by LMBV infection. Our study elucidated the pathogenesis of LMBV infection and identified ferroptosis as a potential target for the viral disease.

articles.title: Multifunctional bioactive glass platforms for bone regeneration: from material design to microenvironment modulation.
articles.abstract: Bone defects caused by trauma, tumor resection, infection, and degenerative diseases remain a major clinical challenge, especially critical-sized defects that surpass the inherent regenerative capacity of native bone tissue. Conventional bone grafting approaches, including autologous and allogeneic bone transplantation, are widely adopted in clinical practice. Nevertheless, their applications are limited by donor-site morbidity, immune rejection, and insufficient donor supply. Bioactive glasses (BGs), a family of inorganic biomaterials, can initiate cascaded regenerative responses through surface reactions and tunable ion release, covering osteogenesis, angiogenesis and immunomodulation. Therefore, BGs have become promising candidates for bone repair. To date, various BG-based forms have been fabricated, ranging from nanoparticles and porous scaffolds to injectable systems and surface-modified implant coatings. This review summarizes recent advances of BG biomaterials for bone defect repair, with particular focus on ion-mediated biological mechanisms, material modification strategies, and microenvironment regulation. Additionally, we discuss major bottlenecks hindering their clinical translation and propose prospects for future research.

articles.title: Amitriptyline alters gut microbial composition and compromises host resistance to enteropathogenic infection.
articles.abstract: Amitriptyline, a tricyclic antidepressant commonly prescribed for depression and various other disorders, has been reported to possess both anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. Paradoxically, clinical evidence suggests that patients with depressive disorders receiving pharmacological treatment exhibit an increased susceptibility to infections, though the mechanisms behind this increased susceptibility remain unclear. This study investigates the impact of amitriptyline on intestinal homeostasis and vulnerability to enteropathogenic infection in a murine model. Oral administration of amitriptyline was found to significantly reduce gut microbial diversity and alter microbiota composition under both homeostatic and infectious conditions, as determined by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Importantly, there was a marked depletion of butyrate-producing bacteria, accompanied by decreased fecal butyrate levels. Additionally, amitriptyline treatment led to a reduction in colonic regulatory T cells and cytokine production in specific pathogen-free mice, but not in germ-free animals. These results indicate that amitriptyline directly modulates host-microbiota interactions, and suggest that disruption of the gut microbiota may underlie the increased susceptibility to infection. Overall, this study underscores the critical role of the gut microbiome in shaping host responses to pharmacological interventions and identifies it as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate infection risks associated with amitriptyline use.

articles.title: Preventive Carbapenem Stewardship and Clinical Outcomes in a Low-Resistance Setting: A Multicenter Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on whether antimicrobial stewardship improves patient-centered outcomes in low-resistance, non-endemic settings is limited. The CASAS intervention combined automated electronic alerts with repeated infectious diseases (ID) specialist reassessment of ongoing carbapenem therapy.

METHODS: This multicenter quasi-experimental study included 3,271 carbapenem treatment courses across four hospitals in Southern Switzerland from 2022 to 2025 (2022-2025; two pre- and two post-intervention years, intervention implemented January 2024). An alert triggered after ≥72 hours of carbapenem therapy prompted structured ID review, repeated every 72 hours until discontinuation. Primary outcomes were hospital length of stay (LOS) and 30-/90-day all-cause mortality from carbapenem initiation (including deaths during therapy). Analyses included ANOVA, multivariable linear/logistic regression (adjusted for ICU admission, Charlson Comorbidity Index, age, sex, septic shock, recent hospitalization, infectious focus), and interrupted time series (ITS).

RESULTS: Mean LOS decreased from 20.85 days in 2022 to 14.55 days in 2025 (p<0.001), with the reduction persisting after adjustment (2025 vs 2022: -6.81 days; 95% CI -8.52 to -5.10). Crude 30-day mortality decreased from 13.77% to 9.92% and 90-day mortality from 17.63% to 11.73%. Advancing calendar year was independently associated with lower 30- and 90-day mortality, while high Charlson Comorbidity Index, older age, and septic shock predicted mortality. ITS showed an immediate reduction in 30-day mortality followed by attenuation of this effect; no significant change was observed for 90-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: A technology-supported, preventive carbapenem stewardship intervention was associated with shorter hospital stay and lower short-term mortality in a low-resistance setting. Mortality findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design and potential residual confounding.

articles.title: The conversion of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells to eosinophil-like cells exacerbates the progression of pulmonary arterial hypertension with increased secretion of 12-HETE.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterised by progressive pulmonary arterial (PA) vascular remodeling, with abnormal phenotypic transformation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) playing a central role. Arachidonic acid (AA) metabolites have been implicated in this process, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms by which its metabolite 12-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-HETE) contributes to PAH remain incompletely understood. Plasma concentrations of 12-HETE were significantly elevated in PAH patients. In SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx)-induced PAH mouse model, the 12/15-lipoxygenase (12/15-LOX) inhibitor ML-351 markedly attenuated disease progression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis revealed a unrecognized phenotypic transdifferentiation of a subset of PASMCs into eosinophil-like (Eos-like) cells. Mechanistically, studies utilizing EOS-deficient (ΔdblGATA) mice demonstrated that these newly Eos-like cells, along with native eosinophils (EOS), secrete 12-HETE. In vitro CCK-8 assays confirmed that hypoxia-induced PASMC proliferation was attenuated by the leukotriene B4 receptor 2 (BLT2) antagonist LY255283, confirming that the 12-HETE/BLT2 axis drives PASMC proliferation, thereby creating a positive feedback loop that amplifies vascular remodeling. These findings establish the 12-HETE as a critical mediator of a novel EOS-PASMC signaling axis that drives PA vascular remodeling in PAH. This study highlights a promising new therapeutic strategy for PAH.

articles.title: Blockage of Pcsk6-mediated autophagy is involved in the protection of Znf667 against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: The objective of this study is to elucidate the function and mechanism of Pcsk6 in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Serum PCSK6 levels were increased in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction patients following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (p < 0.0001) and positively correlated with cTnI (r = 0.511) and NT-proBNP levels (r = 0.464). Pcsk6 levels were elevated in myocardial tissues 6 h after I/R (p = 0.0001) and cardiomyocytes 12 h after hypoxia-reperfusion (H/R) (p < 0.0001). Pcsk6 knockdown reduced the LC3B-II/I ratio in myocardial tissues and H/R-treated cardiomyocytes (p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0020, respectively) and decreased INF/AAR in mice (p = 0.0303). Conversely, Pcsk6 overexpression increased the LC3B-II/I ratio (p = 0.0338) and reduced cell viability (p = 0.0293) under H/R. Znf667 was downregulated in H/R cardiomyocytes (p = 0.0096). Znf667 overexpression reduced wild-type Pcsk6 promoter activity (p = 0.0004) and Pcsk6 mRNA expression (p = 0.0011). Moreover, Znf667 overexpression reduced INF/AAR in mice (p = 0.0216) and the Nf-κB p-p65/total p65 ratio in H/R cardiomyocytes (p = 0.0164), which were restored by combined overexpression of Pcsk6 (p = 0.0005 and p = 0.0297). In H/R cardiomyocytes overexpressing both Znf667 and Pcsk6, BAY11-7082 increased cell viability (p = 0.0203) and reduced the LC3B-II/I ratio (p = 0.0146). In conclusion, Znf667 alleviates enhanced autophagy and myocardial I/R injury by transcriptionally suppressing Pcsk6. The current findings suggest that Nf-κB may be involved in this process and that PCSK6 may be a biomarker for assessing reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE OR PURPOSE: To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

PARTICIPANTS: Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded.

METHODS: Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation.

RESULTS: Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.

articles.title: Comparison of pegfilgrastim and daily G-CSF for CD34+ cell mobilization in healthy donors and post-transplant engraftment: The Pegfilgrastim-23 Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pegfilgrastim (Peg-G), a long-acting formulation of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), enables single-dose administration and effectively mobilizes CD34+ cells into the peripheral blood of healthy donors undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, prospective comparisons with conventional daily G-CSF (Daily-G) regarding mobilization efficacy and safety remain limited. Moreover, no previous studies have compared the differentiation profiles of CD34+ cells mobilized by these two agents.

METHODS: In this multicenter, prospective observational study, we assessed the efficacy, kinetics, safety and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34+ cells induced by either 7.2 mg dose of Peg-G on day 1 (n = 29) or Daily-G at 400 μg/m2/day from day 1 (n = 31) in 60 healthy related donors scheduled to undergo CD34+ cell collection. Hematopoietic engraftment was also evaluated in 60 recipients following infusion of the collected peripheral blood stem cells.

RESULTS: Of the 60 enrolled donors, 50 were evaluable for peripheral blood CD34+ cell counts. The mean CD34+ cell counts were 85.6 ± 48.0 × 10⁶/L in the Peg-G group and 84.6 ± 42.4 × 10⁶/L in the Daily-G group, with no significant difference between the groups (P = .992). Similar findings were observed in the analyses stratified by collection on days 4 and day 5. No significant differences were observed in the differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells. The kinetics of peripheral blood cell counts were generally comparable between the groups in both the day 4 and day 5 collection cohorts, except for a higher white blood cell count on day 4 in the Peg-G group among donors collected on day 5. In exploratory analyses, CD34⁺ cell mobilization efficacy was not correlated with day 4 serum G-CSF concentrations, donor age, body weight, body mass index, or body surface area in either of the treatment groups. Adverse events were common but predominantly consisted of pain-related symptoms that were manageable with supportive care. Grade 3 adverse events included liver dysfunction in three donors and hypertension in one. All laboratory abnormalities and clinical symptoms resolved by the follow-up assessment, and no grade ≥4 adverse events were observed in any donor. Median times to neutrophil engraftment were 16 and 15 days in the Peg-G and Daily-G groups, respectively (P = .73), and those to platelet engraftment were 30 and 27 days, respectively (P = .68).

CONCLUSIONS: Single-dose 7.2-mg Peg-G and conventional Daily-G resulted in comparable peripheral blood CD34⁺ cell mobilization and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells in healthy related donors, with generally manageable safety profiles. No significant differences in the time to neutrophil or platelet engraftment were observed between recipients in the two groups. These findings suggest that both mobilization strategies are clinically applicable and that regimen selection may be tailored according to drug-specific characteristics and donor convenience.

articles.title: Endogenous hypercortisolism and cardio-liver-metabolic dysfunctions: from pathogenesis to the effects of therapeutic strategies targeting hypercortisolism.
articles.abstract: Endogenous hypercortisolism, namely Cushing's syndrome (CS) is a rare but severe endocrine disorder caused by chronic exposure to excess glucocorticoids and characterized by substantial morbidity and increased mortality. Persistent hypercortisolism profoundly affects multiple cardiovascular and metabolic pathways, leading to a broad spectrum of cardio-liver-metabolic complications including arterial hypertension, cardiac and vascular remodelling, thrombotic diathesis, hepatic steatosis, visceral obesity, impaired glucose metabolism, and dyslipidemia. These alterations arise from complex interactions between direct glucocorticoid effects on target tissues and indirect mechanisms, mainly involving insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and altered lipid metabolism. The primary therapeutic objective in CS is the normalization of cortisol excess through surgery, radiotherapy, or medical therapy, namely pharmacological treatment. In recent years, the availability of medical drugs targeting pituitary ACTH secretion, adrenal steroidogenesis, or glucocorticoid receptor signalling has expanded therapeutic options for patients with CS, especially with persistent or recurrent disease. Beyond biochemical control of hypercortisolism, namely normalization of urinary free cortisol (UFC) (UFC ≤ upper limit of normal), accumulating evidence suggests that these treatments may improve several cardiometabolic manifestations associated with cortisol excess. However, although remission of hypercortisolism leads to significant clinical improvement, complete normalization of cardio-liver-metabolic alterations is not consistently achieved. Many patients continue to exhibit persistent cardiovascular and metabolic abnormalities even after long-term biochemical remission, highlighting the need for active long-term monitoring and multidisciplinary management to prevent disease progression and optimize long-term outcomes. This mini-review briefly outlines the pathogenesis of cardio-liver-metabolic dysfunctions and discusses the potential effects of currently available therapeutic strategies targeting hypercortisolism on these comorbidities.

articles.title: Obesity-Induced Alterations in Linezolid Tissue Distribution Revealed by Dynamic Positron Emission Tomography Imaging.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of obesity and its associated susceptibility to infection raise concerns about the adequacy of fixed linezolid dosing. Obesity-related alterations in tissue drug exposure remain poorly characterised. This study quantified the in vivo biodistribution and pharmacokinetics of linezolid in diet-induced obese and control mice using positron emission tomography (PET).

METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice received a high-fat (n=6) or standard diet (n=8) for ten weeks. [¹⁸F]F-Linezolid was produced by copper-mediated ¹⁸F-fluorination of a boronic ester precursor under optimised low-base conditions. Following intravenous administration, dynamic whole-body PET images were acquired over 90 minutes, followed by computed tomography (CT) imaging. Volumes of interest (brown and subcutaneous white adipose tissue, heart, knee, brain, and lung) were analysed using radioactivity concentration, total radioactivity, standardised uptake values, and kinetic modelling with an image-derived input function. Plasma radiometabolites were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography.

RESULTS: [¹⁸F]F-Linezolid was obtained with >99% radiochemical purity and molar activity of 28-92 GBq/µmol. Obese mice showed lower blood radioactivity, with comparable parent-fraction profiles between groups. The one-tissue compartment model and Logan analysis provided optimal fits. Volume of distribution was significantly reduced in obese animals exclusively in adipose depots, accompanied by lower influx rate constants, whereas exposure was fully preserved in lung, brain, and bone/joint tissue.

CONCLUSION: Obesity induces selective pharmacokinetic alterations confined to adipose compartments without compromising linezolid delivery to clinically relevant target tissues, revealing a plasma-tissue dissociation and a tissue-specific distribution that may limit the interpretation of plasma-based therapeutic drug monitoring.

articles.title: Mu (μ) opioid receptors (MOP) in food addiction.
articles.abstract: The 21st century has been plagued with obesity worldwide, mostly in developed countries where access to food is plentiful. Obesity can be a precursor for many other diseases, such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, etc. Therefore, the underlying mechanism of obesity must be understood to cease its progression to other morbidities. There are two aspects of food intake: homeostatic feeding, which regulates energy intake so that the organism has a balanced energy level, and the hedonic feeding, which often causes the organism to consume food greater than its metabolic needs due to the food palatability and motivational alterations. The opioid system, specifically the mu (μ) opioid receptor (MOP), has been heavily implicated in playing an important role in both of these feeding processes. This article aims to review the literature regarding the role of the MOP on different aspects of food intake, including homeostatic and hedonic feeding, binge eating, as well as the existence of sexual dimorphism in food intake regulation via MOP.

articles.title: PIAS1 mitigates vascular calcification through regulating mitochondrial DNA leakage mediated by VDAC1-NLRX1 axis in diabetic models.
articles.abstract: Vascular calcification, an important pathological process of cardiovascular remodeling, is primarily driven by the transition of vascular smooth muscle cells from contractile to osteogenic phenotype. Protein inhibitor of activated STAT1 (PIAS1) is closely associated with diabetes and vascular diseases, but its role and underlying mechanisms in the progression of diabetic vascular calcification (DVC) remain unclear. Herein, we investigated the role of PIAS1 in DVC by genetic modulation and explored its molecular mechanisms by transcriptomics and co-immunoprecipitation with mass spectrometry (Co-IP-MS). We demonstrate that PIAS1 expression is downregulated in both in vitro and in vivo DVC models; furthermore, PIAS1 overexpression alleviates DVC, whereas PIAS1 knockout exacerbates it. Mechanistically, Co-IP-MS analysis reveals an interaction between PIAS1 and voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), which enhances the SUMOylation of VDAC1 while inhibiting its oligomerization. PIAS1 also reduces the binding between NLR family member X1 (NLRX1) and VDAC1, ultimately attenuating mitochondrial DNA leakage into the cytoplasm. More importantly, we find that Ginsenoside Ro is a PIAS1-targeting natural product which alleviates DVC. These findings identify PIAS1 as a novel therapeutic target for DVC and provide a new candidate for DVC prevention and treatment.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Fatty Acid Oxidation Dysregulation in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Mechanistic Roles and Emerging Diagnostic and Therapeutic Advances.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is a chronic metabolic liver disorder driven by the convergent effects of obesity, insulin resistance, lipid overload, gut-liver axis disruption, and immune inflammation. Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation is central to the disposal of excess fatty acids and the maintenance of hepatocellular energy homeostasis; under sustained metabolic stress, however, this process can shift from an adaptive response to a molecular hub for incomplete oxidation, oxidative injury, inflammatory amplification, and fibrotic progression. This review examines fatty acid uptake and activation, carnitine-dependent transport, sequential β-oxidation, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, electron transfer, mitochondrial quality control, and immunometabolic crosstalk, and explains how diet, circadian disruption, aging, gut dysbiosis, drug exposure, and genetic susceptibility destabilize oxidative homeostasis through defined molecular pathways. From a translational perspective, we propose a functional-endotype framework that integrates imaging, acylcarnitine profiling, lipidomics, oxidative-damage markers, inflammatory and fibrotic indices, and genetic risk to guide stratified interventions targeting thyroid hormone signaling, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, incretin pathways, bile-acid signaling, fibroblast growth factors, energy-sensing networks, and precision nanomedicine.

articles.title: Neuroprotective Effects of hAEC-Derived Exosomes Against Ischemic Injury Are Associated with Foxm1 and IGF1.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exosomes secreted by human amniotic epithelial stem cells (hAECs-Exos) have attracted considerable attention as potential therapeutic candidates for ischemic stroke. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying their neuroprotective effects remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Oxygen-glucose deprivation followed by reoxygenation (OGD/R) was applied to HT22 and BV2 cells, and a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion (MCAO) was also established. The involvement of Foxm1 in hAECs-Exos-mediated protection was investigated using Foxm1 overexpression and hAECs-Exos derived from Foxm1-knockdown donor cells. Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) was examined as a potential downstream mediator of Foxm1 through gene silencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP). A rescue experiment combining Foxm1 overexpression with IGF1 silencing was performed to examine the functional relationship between these molecules. In vivo, the effects of hAECs-Exos or Foxm1-knockdown hAECs-Exos on MCAO rats were assessed via intracerebroventricular injection.

RESULTS: Upregulation of Foxm1 significantly mitigated neuronal damage triggered by OGD/R, as indicated by enhanced cellular viability, alleviated oxidative stress, suppressed inflammation, and decreased apoptosis. Conversely, hAECs-Exos derived from Foxm1-knockdown donor cells exhibited attenuated protective effects in both cell types. Mechanistically, ChIP supported the association of Foxm1 with the IGF1 promoter region, while Foxm1 overexpression increased IGF1 protein expression. IGF1 silencing attenuated the protective effects of hAECs-Exos, and simultaneous IGF1 silencing weakened the protective effects associated with Foxm1 overexpression. In vivo, hAECs-Exos increased Foxm1 and IGF1 expression in MCAO rat brains, improved neurological function, decreased infarct areas, and mitigated pathological damage. These effects were attenuated following administration of hAECs-Exos derived from Foxm1-knockdown donor cells.

CONCLUSIONS: hAECs-Exos protect against ischemic injury in cellular and animal models, with Foxm1 and IGF1 implicated in the observed neuroprotective effects.

articles.title: Cardiac biomarkers for risk stratification based on clinical outcomes after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Following ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, patients remain at increased risk of adverse neurological and cardiovascular events. Cardiac biomarkers reflecting distinct pathomechanisms may improve risk stratification. We evaluated associations of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), midregional pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (MR-proANP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hsTnI) with stroke severity and adverse events and explored a two-step biomarker approach to identify high-risk patients.

METHODS: In the prospective, single-center bioMARKers in STROKE (MARK-STROKE) cohort (University Medical Center Hamburg Eppendorf, Germany), MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, and hsTnI were measured in 374 patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. Biomarker concentrations were log2-transformed, with effect estimates expressed per doubling. Follow-up was available for 273 patients. Stroke severity was assessed by the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS). Adverse events (death, myocardial infarction, recurrent stroke, rehospitalization) were recorded during a median of 278 days (interquartile range 184-367). Associations were investigated using age- and sex-adjusted linear, logistic, and Cox regression models. To explore whether combining biomarkers provides additional prognostic information, patients were stratified by the MR-proANP median, with those above the median further stratified by the subgroup-specific hsTnI median.

RESULTS: Higher MR-proANP concentrations were associated with higher NIHSS scores on admission (adjusted β 0.64; 95% CI 0.25-1.02; p=0.001) and an increased risk of adverse events (adjusted HR 1.50; 95% CI 1.21-1.87; p<0.001). NT-proBNP showed similar but weaker associations, whereas hsTnI was not significantly associated with adverse events. Among patients with MR-proANP concentrations above the median, those with hsTnI concentrations above the subgroup-specific hsTnI median had the lowest event-free survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank p=0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac biomarkers, particularly MR-proANP, provide prognostic information after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. A two-step algorithm using MR-proANP for initial classification and hsTnI for refinement may identify patients at increased risk and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Making IMPACT (Improving Methodology for Proteinuria and Albuminuria measurement in Clinics and Trials): A Report of the 2025 Proteinuria-Albuminuria Workshop Sponsored by the National Kidney Foundation.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Glomerular damage is traditionally assessed by measuring urinary protein loss. While both the urinary albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) and protein-creatinine ratio (UPCR) are used in clinical practice via 24-hour or spot urine samples, a more uniform approach to the assessment of urinary proteins and guidance when and how to assess urinary proteins would facilitate the diagnosis and monitoring of CKD. The United States National Kidney Foundation sponsored a scientific workshop to define optimal methods for the measurement of urinary proteins in April 2025. Based on existing literature, prospective studies and meta-analyses, workshop participants concluded that in general the measurement of urinary albumin is preferred over measurement of total urinary protein for several reasons. Firstly, urinary albumin assays are expected to be internationally standardized beginning in 2027, allowing optimal comparability within laboratories over time and across laboratories. Secondly, optimal pre-analytical handling of urine samples are well documented for urinary albumin unlike protein. Thirdly, urinary albumin concentration shows a moderately stronger association with clinical outcomes compared to urinary total protein, particularly in high-risk individuals. Thus, measurement of urinary albumin concentration should in general be preferred when determining the urinary excretion of proteins in future clinical practice and trials.

articles.title: CDKN1A promotes pulmonary endothelial ferroptosis via PI3K/Akt signaling in sepsis-induced lung injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced lung injury (SLI) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Endothelial cell (EC) ferroptosis contributes to SLI, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role of CDKN1A in pulmonary EC ferroptosis during SLI.

METHODS: Bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were performed to identify ferroptosis-related endothelial targets and signaling pathways. CDKN1A expression and PI3K/AKT signaling were validated in cecal ligation and puncture-induced SLI mice and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-treated primary murine pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (MPVECs). Functional studies were conducted using the CDKN1A inhibitor UC2288, CDKN1A siRNA, a PI3K inhibitor, and a PI3K agonist.

RESULTS: Integrated transcriptomic analyses identified CDKN1A as a key ferroptosis-related endothelial gene associated with PI3K/AKT signaling. CDKN1A expression and PI3K/AKT activation were increased in SLI lung tissues and LPS-treated MPVECs. CDKN1A inhibition or silencing attenuated ferroptosis, as evidenced by reduced PTGS2 and TFRC expression, restoration of SLC7A11 and GPX4, decreased ferroptosis-associated fluorescence, and alleviation of mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities. PI3K inhibition phenocopied the protective effects of CDKN1A knockdown, whereas PI3K reactivation reversed these effects in CDKN1A-silenced MPVECs.

CONCLUSIONS: CDKN1A promotes pulmonary EC ferroptosis in SLI, at least in part, through activation of PI3K/AKT signaling. Targeting the CDKN1A-PI3K/AKT axis may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for SLI.

articles.title: Loss of osteoblast restraint on osteoclasts in diabetes: RhoA/Drp1-driven mitochondrial fission and RhoA/Cx43-dependent mitochondrial transfer blockade.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether high glucose activates osteoblastic Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) to concurrently drive Dynamin-Related Protein 1 (Drp1)-dependent mitochondrial fission and suppress Connexin 43 (Cx43)-dependent mitochondrial transfer to osteoclast precursors, impairing osteoblast restraint and promoting bone resorption in diabetic osteoporosis.

METHODS: Streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mice were used. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were isolated for co-culture. Mitochondrial morphology, membrane potential, and ROS were assessed by fluorescent probes. Mitochondrial transfer was quantified by flow cytometry using Mito-DsRed2 transfection and F4/80 labeling; gap junction function by dye transfer. Inhibitors of RhoA, Drp1, or Cx43 were applied. Osteoblast mineralization and osteoclast differentiation were examined by staining and marker gene expression (RT-qPCR and western blot).

RESULTS: High glucose activated RhoA and upregulated Drp1, causing mitochondrial fragmentation, reduced membrane potential, and impaired mineralization. It also decreased Cx43, disrupted gap junctions, and reduced mitochondrial transfer. Recipient cells co-cultured with high glucose-treated osteoblasts displayed elevated mitochondrial ROS and reduced membrane potential, consistent with the possibility that the transferred mitochondria may carry functional impairment. In co-culture, impaired transfer relieved osteoblast inhibition, increasing osteoclast markers. Inhibiting RhoA/Drp1 or RhoA/Cx43 restored transfer and suppressed osteoclasts.

CONCLUSION: High glucose activates RhoA to drive Drp1-mediated damage and downregulate Cx43-dependent transfer, reducing mitochondrial quantity and quality delivered to osteoclasts. This dual defect abolishes osteoblast restraint, enhancing osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption, revealing a dual pathogenic mechanism for diabetic osteoporosis.

articles.title: QRICH1 promotes PDK4-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction and pyroptosis in diabetic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by myocardial metabolic remodeling and inflammatory cell death, yet the transcriptional regulators linking metabolic stress to cardiomyocyte injury remain poorly defined.

METHODS: Glutamine-rich protein 1 (QRICH1) expression was examined in hearts of mice with high-fat diet and streptozotocin-induced type 2 diabetes and in cardiomyocytes exposed to high glucose plus palmitic acid. QRICH1 transcriptional regulation of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 (PDK4) was verified by chromatin immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase assays, and the effects of QRICH1 overexpression and PDK4 knockdown were assessed in vitro. Drug repurposing was performed by molecular docking and a drug affinity responsive target stability assay.

RESULTS: QRICH1 was markedly upregulated in diabetic myocardium and under glucolipotoxic conditions. QRICH1 directly bound the PDK4 promoter and transactivated its expression. QRICH1 overexpression induced caspase-1-dependent pyroptosis, impaired mitochondrial respiration, and promoted cytosolic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) leakage with inflammatory signaling activation, and these changes were partially reversed by PDK4 knockdown. Vericiguat showed the strongest binding affinity for QRICH1 among screened cardiovascular drugs. In DCM mice, vericiguat significantly improved cardiac function, downregulated PDK4, and restored myocardial AKT phosphorylation.

CONCLUSIONS: QRICH1 sustains PDK4 expression under glucolipotoxic stress, driving mitochondrial dysfunction, mtDNA release, and pyroptosis, and vericiguat represents a repurposing candidate for myocardial protection in DCM.

articles.title: Impact of preoperative cardiology consultations on perioperative management in patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiology consultations may be requested during preoperative anesthetic assessment before non-cardiac surgery. However, data regarding their impact on perioperative management are limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of preoperative cardiology consultations on perioperative patient management.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, observational, single-center study in the Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care at Angers University Hospital from September 1st, 2024, to August 31st, 2025. All patients referred for cardiology assessment after the anesthetic consultation were included. The primary endpoint was any change in perioperative management, including specific preoperative cardiac treatment, postponement or cancellation of surgery, and modification of anesthetic or surgical protocols. The secondary endpoint was to assess adherence of preoperative cardiac evaluation to current guideline recommendations.

RESULTS: Among 9,621 preoperative anesthetic consultations, 138 (1%) patients were referred for cardiology assessment by the anesthesiologist and included in the study. 59 (43%) patients experienced a change in perioperative management. Of them, surgery was postponed in 52 (38%) patients, with a median delay of 81 [47-145] days, whereas only 6 patients underwent an invasive cardiac intervention (angioplasty, valvuloplasty, or electrical cardioversion). A previously unknown cardiac condition was identified in 19 (15%) patients. 111 (80%) cardiology referrals were consistent with current recommendations.

CONCLUSION: In our study, preoperative cardiology consultations requested by an anesthesiologist were rare but frequently responsible for modification of perioperative management. These consultations often resulted in postponement of surgery, while only a small proportion of patients underwent an invasive cardiac intervention.

articles.title: Renal Replacement Therapy in Cardiogenic Shock supported by microAxial Flow Pumps: A European multicentre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microaxial flow pumps (mAFP) improve hemodynamics and outcomes in myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (CS) but are associated with an increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). We aimed to determine the incidence and factors associated with RRT and evaluate its association with mortality in a real-world cohort of miscellaneous CS patients supported with mAFP.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicentre registry including CS patients supported with mAFP across 11 European centres. The association between RRT and the primary outcome of 180-day all-cause mortality (with survival censored at heart transplantation or durable left ventricular assist device implantation) was assessed using a 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort. Factors associated with RRT were identified using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 1043 patients, 972 were included, of whom 340 (35.0%) required RRT. RRT was associated with higher 180-day all-cause mortality both before (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 59.7% vs. 35.2%; HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.67-2.49; p < 0.01) and after propensity score matching (59.0% vs. 41.4%; HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.14-1.92; p < 0.01); restricted mean survival difference -25.5 days, 95% CI - 39.9 to -10.2. Factors associated with RRT included BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.69; 95% CI 1.15-2.46), baseline serum creatinine (per 20 µmol/L increase: aOR 1.18; 95% CI 1.12-1.24), norepinephrine use (aOR 1.72; 95% CI 1.19-2.49), and lactate ≥4 mmol/L at implantation (aOR 1.56; 95% CI 1.11-2.20).

CONCLUSIONS: In this large European registry of mAFP-supported CS, RRT was frequent and associated with increased 180-day mortality and greater shock severity.

articles.title: Functional primary human 3D skeletal muscle models enable exercise and metabolic research.
articles.abstract: Human skeletal muscle is the principal site of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal and a major mediator of exercise-induced metabolic benefits, yet human models that preserve metabolic and exercise responsiveness remain limited. We generated primary human skeletal muscle organoids from donor-derived CD56+ myoblasts using a collagen-based extracellular matrix and serum-free IGF1-guided differentiation. The organoids formed aligned contractile tissues containing oxidative and glycolytic fiber type-like myotubes, displayed enhanced mitochondrial respiration, insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, and reproducible force generation. Electrical pulse stimulation induced AMPK activation, increased glucose utilization and lactate production, and upregulated canonical exercise-responsive genes including NR4A3 and PPARGC1A. Notably, transcriptional responses to in vitro exercise overlapped with acute exercise responses observed in skeletal muscle biopsies from the same donors. The organoids further detected functional impairments of skeletal muscle performance induced by TGF-β1 and metformin and increased speed generation by testosterone treatment. These findings establish a donor-derived human skeletal muscle platform that recapitulates key features of insulin action and exercise adaptation and may enable mechanistic studies of skeletal muscle metabolism, exercise responsiveness, and therapeutic interventions relevant to diabetes.

articles.title: Machine-Learning Derived Individual Risk Prediction in Congenital Heart Surgery: Development and internal validation of risk prediction models for in-hospital mortality after congenital heart surgery using data from the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Machine learning (ML) methods may improve prediction of individual risk of mortality risk after congenital heart surgery (CHD) by identifying nonlinear relationships/novel combinations of variables. Improved risk discrimination may improve outcomes by optimizing resource allocation and patient surveillance.

METHODS: Children and adolescents (age≤18 years) undergoing CHD surgery at Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium hospitals 9/1/2014-12/30/2019 were studied. Non-collinear potential predictors were identified empirically and used to create a logistic regression risk (LR) model (mimicking traditional risk-adjustment models) and ML (random forest and gradient boosting model) models. Model performance was evaluated using net reclassification index (NRI), the proportion of subjects in which either the absolute risk category or estimated risk relative to other subjects changed between each model and one composed only of STAT category as the primary outcome. This metric reflects how often a model changes how a clinician views the risk of a patient relative to a parsimonious model and provides some measure of the utility of these models. Secondary analyses compared overall model fit.

RESULTS: In total 51,475 operative encounters from 52 hospitals were studied. Subjects were 45% female, 20% neonates, and 5% underwent STAT 5 operations. C-statistics and Brier scores did not differ significantly between ML and LR models. For absolute risk categorires, point estimates for NRI between ML-models and STAT category (0.76 95%CI: 0.68-0.83) suggested at best modest improvements compared to logistic regression model (0.75 95%CI 0.67-0.83), but the difference was not significant. Similarly, for rankings of risk within the cohort, NRI for ML models (0.26 95%CI: 0.19-0.32) was not significantly different to that for the LR model (0.24 95%CI: 0.17-0.33).

CONCLUSION: ML derived models did not improve overall model fit. Magnitude of improvement in reclassification was at best modest and not statistically significant. Future research is necessary to evaluate the added values of incorporating more comprehensive data and/or advanced computational techniques and use of reclassification in risk prediction.

articles.title: Reply to: Accounting for pubertal maturation in the vitamin D-bone mineral density association in youth with type 1 diabetes.
Integrative genomic analyses and Fine-Mapping of the 5q31.1 Cytokine Locus Links Food Allergy Risk to Asthma and Atopic Dermatitis Through Shared Causal Variants.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food allergy (FA) is a common immune-mediated disorder, yet its genetic architecture and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize the genetic architecture of FA, refine association signals through multi-ancestry fine-mapping, and investigate shared genetic and regulatory mechanisms linking FA with asthma and atopic dermatitis (AD).

METHODS: We performed a multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis of FA including more than 16,000 cases and over 1 million controls of European, African, and East Asian ancestry. We used sequential conditional analysis and Bayesian fine-mapping to identify independent association signals and prioritize candidate causal variants. We further evaluated shared genetic architecture with asthma and AD through conditional colocalization analysis and integrated FA-associated variants with cis-eQTL and single-nucleus ATAC/RNA-seq data from blood and skin to nominate candidate target genes and disease-relevant cell types.

RESULTS: This trans-ancestry design enabled fine-mapping of the 5q31.1 locus (IL4, IL5, and IL13), revealing multiple independent disease-associated signals, including a secondary genome-wide significant variant (rs6873732; p ≤ 5 × 10-8) and a tertiary signal surpassing Bonferroni significance (rs4608913; p = 9.1 × 10-6). Bayesian fine-mapping identified credible causal variants that also associate with asthma and atopic dermatitis (AD). Genetic colocalization demonstrated that the primary FA signal at 5q31.1 aligns with a secondary AD signal (rs11242122), while the secondary and tertiary FA signals at 5q31.1 colocalize with two independent asthma signals (rs12652920 and rs77450473). Outside 5q31.1, we confirmed a genome-wide significant association at 1q21.3 and identified candidate loci at 11q13.5 and 18q21.33-q22.1, each showing strong evidence of shared causal variants (PP > 0.8) with asthma and AD. To connect genetic risk to cellular mechanisms, we integrated single-nucleus ATAC/RNA-seq from blood and skin. At 5q31.1, three variants within the primary credible set overlapped accessible chromatin in basophils and T cells, while seven tertiary-signal variants overlapped open chromatin in basophils, monocytes, keratinocytes, and CD8+ T cells. Integration with cis-eQTL data demonstrated that primary and tertiary FA signals were associated with increased SLC22A5/IL13 expression and upregulation of IRF1, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of FA, reveal shared and disease-specific mechanisms with related allergic diseases, highlight the value of integrating ancestry-diverse GWAS with multi-omics data to prioritize regulatory mechanisms in complex immune-mediated conditions.

articles.title: Silent cerebral ischemia after anticoagulation- or TEE-guided cardioversion: The randomized AFTER-CV trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Silent cerebral ischemia after elective cardioversion is incompletely characterized, and randomized MRI-based evidence comparing anticoagulation-guided and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided pathways is limited.

METHODS: AFTER-CV was a prospective, randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial of 112 patients undergoing elective cardioversion, assigned 1:1 by sealed-envelope randomization to at least 3 weeks of therapeutic oral anticoagulation or a TEE-guided strategy. Brain diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI-MRI) was performed before and 1 week after cardioversion and was interpreted by an experienced radiologist blinded to treatment allocation. Clinical thromboembolic and bleeding outcomes were assessed during 2 years of follow-up.

RESULTS: New silent cerebral ischemic lesions were detected in 2 of 56 patients (3.6%) in the anticoagulation-guided group and 4 of 56 (7.1%) in the TEE-guided group (absolute risk difference, -3.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -13.7 to 6.0; Fisher exact p = 0.68). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for the reported long-term clinical efficacy, bleeding, or composite outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: New MRI-detected cerebral ischemic lesions were uncommon in both randomized groups. The small sample, few imaging events, single-center design, and predominantly warfarin-treated cohort preclude conclusions of equivalence or non-inferiority.

articles.title: Time-Restricted Eating and Blood Pressure: Disentangling the Components of a Multidimensional Intervention.
articles.abstract: Time-restricted eating (TRE) has emerged as a promising chrononutritional strategy for improving cardiometabolic health, with human and experimental evidence suggesting beneficial effects on blood pressure (BP). However, attributing these effects specifically to meal timing remains challenging because TRE is not a single physiological exposure. Restricting the eating window may simultaneously modify fasting duration, circadian timing, energy balance, diet quality and nutritional composition, and body-weight dynamics, each of which may independently or interactively influence BP regulation. Interpretation is further complicated by how and when BP is assessed, particularly because BP is an intrinsically circadian phenotype. We propose a multidimensional framework that distinguishes these interconnected biological components from the methodological dimension of BP assessment. Disentangling them is essential to determine whether meal timing itself exerts an intrinsic antihypertensive effect and under which metabolic and circadian conditions such an effect emerges.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of co-administered cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each in adults with overweight or obesity (REDEFINE 9): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 2·4 mg each has shown clinically meaningful bodyweight reductions in global phase 3 studies. Different dosing options might support individual treatment responses and tolerability. We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of once per week subcutaneous cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each or 1·0 mg each versus placebo in participants with obesity or overweight and at least one obesity-related complication.

METHODS: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial (REDEFINE 9) was conducted across 24 sites in Canada, France, Germany, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older; with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m2 or at least 27 kg/m2 and one or more obesity-related complication; and without diabetes. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1:2:1) centrally, using block randomisation (block size of six) and a web-based system, to receive cagrilintide 1·7 mg plus semaglutide 1·7 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 12 weeks), placebo 1·7 mg plus 1·7 mg (hereafter placebo 1·7 mg each), cagrilintide 1·0 mg plus semaglutide 1·0 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 8 weeks), or placebo 1·0 mg plus 1·0 mg (hereafter placebo 1·0 mg each) for 68 weeks, plus nutrition and physical activity counselling until week 74. All treatments were administered subcutaneously once per week. The coprimary endpoints were relative mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 and proportion of participants reaching a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% at week 68, assessed in the full analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants). Safety was assessed in the safety analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of the study drug). This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06388187 (completed).

FINDINGS: From June 24 to Oct 30, 2024, 333 participants were assessed for eligibility and 24 were excluded. 309 participants were randomly assigned (full analysis set: 104 assigned to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 103 to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 102 to pooled placebo). 308 participants received at least one dose of the study drug. 291 (94%) of 309 participants completed the study and 254 (82%) were on treatment at week 68. The mean age was 48·0 years (SD 13·6) and mean BMI was 39·1 kg/m2 (6·8). 239 (77%) participants were female, and 70 (23%) were male. For the efficacy estimand, the mean relative change from baseline in bodyweight at week 68 was -20·7% (SE 0·9) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, -21·0% (1·0) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and -2·0% (1·0) with the pooled placebo. Bodyweight reductions were significantly greater with both doses of cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -18·8 percentage points [95% CI -21·5 to -16·0]; p<0·0001 for the 1·7 mg each dose and -19·0 percentage points [-21·8 to -16·2]; p<0·0001 for the 1·0 mg each dose). The proportion of participants reaching bodyweight reductions of at least 5% at week 68 was significantly greater with cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (95·1% [SE 2·7] with the 1·7 mg each dose vs 33·4% [5·6] with placebo, ETD 61·7 percentage points [95% CI 49·5-74·0], p<0·0001; and 96·3% [2·2] with the 1·0 mg each dose, ETD 63·0 percentage points [51·1-74·9], p<0·0001). Adverse events were reported in 102 (99%) of 103 participants receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 98 (95%) of 103 receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 93 (91%) of 102 receiving the placebo. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and gastrointestinal-related. No deaths were reported.

INTERPRETATION: Cagrilintide-semaglutide at 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each was superior to placebo at reducing bodyweight in adults with overweight or obesity, suggesting that different dose levels might support treatment flexibility.

FUNDING: Novo Nordisk.

articles.title: LYPLA2 inhibition alleviates hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome by suppressing pSTAT3-dependent HSP60 transcription.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: To investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms involved in the progression of hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (HSOS) and the mechanisms by which low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) alleviates HSOS. Monocrotaline (MCT) was administered to establish rat and cellular models of HSOS. Rats received subcutaneous injections of enoxaparin (EPN; 8 mg/kg) at three time points: 48 h, 24 h, and 30 min prior to MCT administration. Liver tissue protein expression profiles from the Control, MCT, and MCT + EPN groups were subsequently analyzed using proteomics. Lysophospholipase 2 (LYPLA2) inhibitor ML349 (35 mg/kg) was intraperitoneally injected daily for 7 consecutive days before MCT administration. The results showed that LYPLA2 protein level in liver tissues of HSOS rats was increased (log2FC = 1.05, p = 0.047) but decreased by EPN (log2FC = -1.11, p = 0.037). Treatment with LYPLA2 inhibitor ML349 or LYPLA2 knockdown alleviated MCT-induced liver tissues and human hepatic sinus endothelial cells (HSECs) injury by reducing cell apoptosis and inflammation. The underlying mechanism was that LYPLA2 inhibition decreased pSTAT3 level in cytoplasm and nucleus. Meanwhile, LYPLA2 inhibition increased palmitoylation of pSTAT3, which is known to mediate plasma membrane retention of pSTAT3. The decrease of pSTAT3 in nucleus suppressed the transcription of heat shock protein 60 (HSP60). HSP60, a driver of HSOS progression, overexpression reversed the effects caused by ML349 or LYPLA2 knockdown. The observations demonstrate that LYPLA2 inhibition alleviates MCT-induced liver injury by inhibiting pSTAT3-mediated HSP60 transcription, suggesting that ML349 may confer preventive protection against HSOS.

articles.title: Reply to Ortega and Alarico regarding 'Behavioral change intervention to promote healthy diet and physical activity in overweight/obese adults with diabetes in primary health care: Results from a cluster randomized control trial'.
Time-series modelling and forecasting of acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) in the Gaza Strip before and during the war in October 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the temporal consistency and plausibility of manually collected data on acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) consultations reported by UNRWA staff based in Gaza and Cairo relative to the historical surveillance baseline. Further, the study aims to show the impact of the war in the Gaza Strip that began in October 2023 and the massive forced displacement of the Gaza population from Rafah governorate on the shape of the AWD curve.

STUDY DESIGN: We used epidemiological modelling with time-series analysis and forecasting.

METHODS: Negative Binomial Regression was chosen based on the results of over-dispersion test. We obtained data prior to the war from UNRWA's electronic health system, while the health team (HT) collected data during the war manually during the war, and the Gaza office in Cairo audited them. We used October 7, 2023, and the Rafah mass incursion in late May (Epidemiological week 22) as cut-off points for forecasting.

RESULTS: The regression model showed good reliability in trend prediction, though confidence declined during the war. Decomposition revealed a hump-shaped trend between 2023 and 2025, with descriptive seasonality and notable white noise. The model adequately addressed overdispersion in the weekly counts but did not completely capture their short-term temporal correlation. The outbreak prediction model showed an exponential rise in cases at the onset of the war. Forecasts exhibited similar trends between observed and predicted data before and after the cut-off points.

CONCLUSIONS: The analysis supports the accuracy and credibility of the reported data during the catastrophic humanitarian conditions and acknowledges the efforts of UNRWA Gaza HT. Time series analysis is a robust method for evaluating and interpreting humanitarian data.

articles.title: Retraction notice to "Genipin attenuates sepsis-induced immunosuppression through inhibition of T lymphocyte apoptosis" [Int. Immunopharmacol. 27(1) (2015) 15-23].
