Multidisciplinary Learning Profiles in Surgical Services: A VARK and Experiential Learning Theory Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical services engage multidisciplinary residents from various specialties; however, the educational delivery frequently adopts a "one-size-fits-all" model. This reliance on passive, aural-visual instruction may not adequately address residents' diverse cognitive preferences, leading to a misalignment between instructional design and residents' specific needs.

OBJECTIVE: To identify Visual, Aural, Read/Write, and Kinesthetic (VARK) learning preferences among surgical and nonsurgical residents who rotate through surgery services and examine associations with specialty, gender, and postgraduate year (PGY).

DESIGN: This is a single-institution, retrospective, cross-sectional study that assessed VARK learning style profiles in general surgery, emergency medicine (EM), obstetrics and gynecology (OB-GYN), and orthopedics residents through the lens of Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory, using descriptive statistics and Chi-square analyses.

SETTING: St. Luke's University Health Network, at the level I and level II academic trauma centers located in Bethlehem and Easton, Pennsylvania.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 123 residents in general surgery, EM, OB-GYN, and orthopedics who rotated through Trauma and Surgical Critical Care from 2023 to 2025.

RESULTS: This study included 78 male and 45 female residents. Multimodal was the most common preference (N = 60; 48.8%), followed by Kinesthetic (N = 40; 32.5%). OB-GYN uniquely favored Aural as a secondary preference, while EM and Orthopedics demonstrated the strongest Kinesthetic profiles. Gender was statistically significantly associated with VARK preferences (p = 0.037). Females predominantly preferred Multimodal (28; 62.2%) compared to males (28; 41%). In contrast, males showed higher Kinesthetic preferences (27; 34.6%) than females (13; 28.9%). Learning profiles remained stable across PGY levels.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that a uniform instructional approach is suboptimal. Educators should move away from passive observation to active, multimodal engagement, incorporating kinesthetic and specialty-aligned strategies to better support the diverse educational needs of residents in high-acuity surgical services.

articles.title: Reduction of laundering-induced microplastic release from recycled polyester yarns by chain extender modification.
articles.abstract: The increasing use of recycled polyethylene terephthalate (r-PET) fibers in textiles has raised concerns regarding microfiber and microplastic release during laundering. This study investigated the effect of chain extender (CE) incorporation on microplastic release from r-PET yarns. Yarns containing 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 wt% CE were produced and subjected to 1, 5, 10, and 20 laundering cycles. Microplastic release was quantified by gravimetric filtration using 0.2 µm filters, and particle size distribution was determined using a particle size analyzer. CE incorporation reduced microplastic release, particularly after repeated laundering. After 20 cycles, release decreased from 9.8 mg in untreated r-PET to 3.4 mg in the 0.5% and 1.5% CE-modified samples, corresponding to an approximately 65% reduction. CE modification generally increased particle size, indicating reduced formation of fine microplastics. Overall, CE modification offers an effective strategy for reducing microplastic release from recycled polyester textiles. From a circular-economy and waste-management perspective, this source-reduction approach is relevant because it targets microfiber generation before particles enter wastewater streams. The results indicate that optimized chain-extender modification can reduce particulate release from recycled polyester while retaining the material-resource benefits of recycling.

articles.title: Packaging reverse logistics in Bahia, Brazil: participatory importance ratings to inform materiality assessment in S-LCA.
articles.abstract: Stakeholder participation can inform the selection of social topics in Social Life Cycle Assessment (S-LCA), but importance ratings alone do not establish materiality. This study develops and applies a structured procedure to describe and compare the importance assigned to 27 pre-selected social impact subcategories in packaging reverse logistics in southern and southwestern Bahia, Brazil. Four respondent groups were analysed separately: recyclable material pickers, waste generators, public authorities, and S-LCA practitioners. An individual online questionnaire administered between May and September 2024 used a 10-point numerical importance scale and common written definitions. Group means were used descriptively, and between-group comparisons employed Kruskal-Wallis tests, Holm-adjusted Dunn post-hoc comparisons, and signed rank-biserial correlations with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Thirteen subcategories yielded statistically significant overall differences at the exploratory 0.05 threshold. The largest pairwise effect estimates involved recyclable material pickers and public authorities or S-LCA practitioners in Worker-related subcategories. Non-significant comparisons were treated as inconclusive regarding equivalence. Of 1,242 individual item ratings analysed, 830 (66.8%) were at the scale maximum, indicating substantial upper-end concentration that restricts fine discrimination among highly rated topics. The instrument was not piloted or cognitively pre-tested in this application, and equivalence of item interpretation across groups was not established. The findings provide context-specific participatory evidence for broader materiality assessment alongside information on social impacts, affected populations, vulnerability, and decision relevance; yet they do not measure impact occurrence, social performance, or causal mechanisms underlying respondents' judgements. The documented procedure provides a basis for further applications, subject to local adaptation and validation.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicles in viral myocarditis: Mechanisms, biomarkers and emerging therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Viral myocarditis (VM) is an inflammatory heart disease most commonly triggered by viral infection and represents a major cause of acute cardiac dysfunction and chronic inflammatory cardiomyopathy. Although cardiomyocyte injury and immune activation are central to VM pathogenesis, the mechanisms by which viral infection coordinates intercellular communication to drive disease progression remain incompletely understood. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as key mediators of cell-to-cell signaling, capable of transporting viral components and host-derived factors that modulate immune responses and cardiac function. In this review, we integrate preclinical and clinical evidence to define the mechanistic roles of EVs in VM and evaluate their translational potential. We highlight circulating EVs as minimally invasive biomarkers for early diagnosis and disease monitoring. We further discuss emerging strategies to therapeutically target or engineer EVs to modulate both viral replication and maladaptive host responses.

articles.title: The impact of temperature variation on the incidence of cardiovascular diseases in hypertensive populations: Evidence from CHARLS and the UK biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is the most prevalent chronic disease. The link between temperature changes and cardiovascular disease incidence in hypertensive populations is not well understood.

OBJECTIVE: To explore how temperature fluctuations affect cardiovascular disease incidence in hypertensive populations and identify the most impacted cardiovascular diseases.

METHODS: Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and the UK Biobank, which provide long-term follow-up information on hypertensive patients, we applied logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards regression models to analyze the relationship between temperature and cardiovascular disease occurrence.

RESULTS: In CHARLS (2011-2020), 4321 hypertensive individuals were studied, with 1079 developing cardiovascular diseases. A significant positive correlation was found between annual average daily temperature difference and cardiovascular disease incidence (OR: 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, P < 0.001). In the UK Biobank, 30,551 participants were followed for an average of 12.4 years, with 3611 diagnosed with cardiovascular diseases. Those exposed to alternating cold and hot temperatures had a higher risk of cardiovascular events (HR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.09-1.29, P < 0.001). Specifically, heart failure (HR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.21-1.73, P < 0.001), multivalvular disease (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.04-1.68, P < 0.05), and chronic ischemic heart disease (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.28, P < 0.05) were associated with such temperature exposure.

CONCLUSION: Our study highlights the need to enhance cardiovascular disease monitoring and management in hypertensive populations under varying temperatures, which is crucial for disease prevention and control.

articles.title: Prevalence, underdiagnosis, and its impact on exercise capacity and physical activity of lower extremity artery disease in Japanese patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) is a common cardiovascular comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), its prevalence and clinical impact in Japanese patients remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence of LEAD, including the proportion of previously undiagnosed cases, in Japanese patients with stable COPD, and to compare exercise capacity and physical activity between patients with and without LEAD.

METHODS: LEAD was defined as an ankle-brachial index (ABI) ≤ 0.90 in either leg. Six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and physical activity assessed using a triaxial accelerometer were compared between patients with and without LEAD, with adjustment for potential confounders using analysis of covariance. The associations of ABI as a continuous variable with exercise capacity and physical activity were examined using restricted cubic spline analysis.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients with COPD (median age, 75.0 years; 88 % male), 18 (18 %) had coexisting LEAD; 78 % were previously undiagnosed and 72 % were asymptomatic. In crude analyses, patients with LEAD had significantly shorter 6MWD (p = 0.007), lower daily step count (p = 0.011), and more comorbidities. After adjustment, differences in 6MWD (-47.9 m; 95 % CI, -124.0 to 28.5) and step count (-1,035 steps/day; 95 % CI, -2,645 to 575) were not statistically significant, whereas ABI was significantly associated with 6MWD (p = 0.009).

CONCLUSION: A substantial proportion of patients with COPD and coexisting LEAD were previously undiagnosed. Lower exercise capacity and step counts in unadjusted comparisons were not significant after adjustment, suggesting that these differences may reflect multiple contributing factors.

articles.title: Development and validation of an ML-driven risk prediction model for stroke-heart syndrome after acute ischemic stroke.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing prediction models for stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) have limited generalizability due to population heterogeneity.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a generalizable risk prediction model for SHS following AIS.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 1404 AIS patients from the MIMIC-IV database was utilized. After feature selection, 14 machine learning algorithms were evaluated. All algorithms were trained under identical preprocessing with per-algorithm automatically tuned hyperparameters and evaluated by five-fold cross-validation and hold-out internal validation. The final model-a logistic regression-based nomogram-was externally validated on an independent single-center cohort (n = 321). Performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves, Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). Model interpretability was augmented using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).

RESULTS: Seven early-admission predictors were identified: age, heart rate, prothrombin time, blood urea nitrogen, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, and body temperature. The model demonstrated strong, consistent discrimination across datasets: training AUC=0.789, internal validation AUC=0.802, and external validation AUC=0.810. Calibration was good on internal validation (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.614) but showed external under-dispersion (slope 1.72, P = 0.004); local recalibration is indicated. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities.

CONCLUSION: We developed and validated a parsimonious SHS risk prediction model using seven early-admission indicators that overcomes the generalizability limitations of prior tools through multi-algorithm validation and external testing. Relying on routine clinical variables, this tool facilitates rapid risk stratification for precision prevention, though future prospective validation in diverse populations is warranted.

articles.title: Measurement error and repeatability of weighing scales: implications for heart failure care.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body weight guides decongestion in acute decompensated heart failure and is frequently used as a trial outcome, but scale performance in routine care is insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To assess how closely household and medical scales measured known reference loads, how much measurements varied between scales, and how consistently scales performed during repeated measurements and across measurement days.

METHODS: We tested 37 digital scales (29 household and 8 medical) at two Danish hospitals using reference loads from 25 to 125 kg. Each scale underwent three measurements per load on two days.

RESULTS: Household scales showed modest mean measurement error at most reference loads, but variability between devices increased and repeated and day-to-day measurements became less consistent as load increased. At 125 kg, median absolute measurement error was 1.13 kg on Day 1 and 1.43 kg on Day 2, while between-scale standard deviations (SDs) were 2.30 kg and 6.27 kg, respectively. Medical scales showed mean errors of 0.00-0.25 kg, between-scale SDs of 0.00-0.12 kg, consistently high repeatability, and small day-to-day differences.

CONCLUSION: Among the scales tested, household scales showed modest mean measurement error but substantial between-scale variability and poorer repeatability at higher loads, whereas medical scales performed consistently. These findings support preferential use of medical scales in hospitals and use of the same device for serial measurements when household scales are used.

articles.title: Frontocentral theta oscillations bias perceptual judgments of ambiguous visual causality.
articles.abstract: Human perceptual decisions frequently rely on incomplete, ambiguous sensory inputs resolved prior to stimulus onset. Prior electrophysiological work confirms pre-event frontocentral ERP components predict ambiguous visual causal judgments, yet the spectrotemporal signatures of spontaneous oscillatory biases remain uncharacterized. Frontocentral theta signals proactive cognitive control, but whether pre-event theta oscillation modulates high-order causal inference independently of stimulus-locked ERPs remains untested. Thirteen volunteers (16 recruited, 3 excluded) completed a staircase-calibrated Michotte launching task with 64-channel EEG recorded. Time-frequency decomposition, permutation tests, and ERP-subtraction controls isolated pre-coincidence oscillatory patterns distinguishing causal bouncing and non-causal streaming percepts under PSE level. Elevated pre-coincidence Fz theta power robustly biased observers toward causal reports, showing a negative linear relationship between theta magnitude and streaming response ratios. The theta bias survived single-trial ERP removal, proving oscillatory signals carry predictive information distinct from known ERP markers. These findings imply frontocentral theta pre-allocates anticipatory cognitive resources to support intuitive causal reasoning, separating theta's executive regulatory function from alpha's modulation of basic sensory awareness. This study constructs a novel spectrotemporal framework explaining how spontaneous frontal oscillations sculpt ambiguous causal perception.

articles.title: Epiberberine attenuates diabetic atherosclerosis by inhibiting the Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic atherosclerosis (DA) is a major macrovascular complication of diabetes with limited therapeutic options. Epiberberine (EPI), an isoquinoline alkaloid, has shown anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects, but its role in DA remains unknown. This study investigated whether EPI ameliorates DA and explored the mechanisms involving endothelial pyroptosis and the Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 signaling pathway.

METHODS: Diabetic apolipoprotein E-deficient mice were induced by streptozotocin (55 mg/kg daily for 5 days). Mice with fasting blood glucose >15 mM were randomly assigned to control, low-dose EPI (50 mg/kg/day), or high-dose EPI (100 mg/kg/day) groups. A non-diabetic control group received citrate buffer. All treatments were administered orally for 10 weeks. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells were treated with high glucose plus oxidized low-density lipoprotein, with or without EPI (20 or 40 μM). Aortic plaque area, serum lipids, pyroptosis markers (cleaved-caspase 1 and gasdermin D N-terminal domain), inflammatory cytokines, and Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway activation were assessed.

RESULTS: EPI reduced aortic plaque area by 31.4% (low dose) and 57.9% (high dose). Serum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol decreased from 2.5 mmol/L (diabetic controls) to 1.9 mmol/L (low-dose EPI) and 1.2 mmol/L (high-dose EPI). EPI also reduced cleaved-caspase 1 and gasdermin D N-terminal domain expression, indicating suppressed endothelial pyroptosis, and inhibited Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway activation in both endothelial cells and aortic tissues.

CONCLUSIONS: EPI alleviates vascular inflammation and atherosclerotic progression in diabetic mice, likely by suppressing endothelial pyroptosis through inhibition of the Raf/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathway. EPI represents a promising therapeutic strategy for diabetic macrovascular complications.

articles.title: ICU delirium: From key drivers to targeted prevention.
Perioperative management of patients with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery: A modified Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients present for surgery soon after concussion, when cerebral physiologic regulation may remain disturbed, and no evidence-based guideline or standardized consensus recommendations exist. We sought expert consensus for adults with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study (November 2025-March 2026). Round 1 items, drafted from a systematic literature search, included case vignettes. Experts identified by bibliographic screening, directories, and nomination rated items on a five-point Likert scale; "do not know" responses were excluded from the denominator. Consensus was defined a priori as 75% agreement or greater, and strong consensus as 85% or greater.

RESULTS: Thirty-five experts (33 anesthesiologists) from 17 countries completed both rounds; 13 of 16 Round 2 statements reached consensus. Agreement was unanimous for preoperative screening for concussion symptoms and neurologic red flags, and for avoidance of hypoxemia, abnormal carbon dioxide tension, sustained hypotension, and marked hypertension. Strong consensus supported generally deferring elective surgery until concussion symptoms resolve (97%), preoperative counseling (97%), structured follow-up (94%), and extended postoperative monitoring in higher-risk patients (91%). Consensus was not reached for regional anesthesia or monitored anesthesia care over general anesthesia (74%), electroencephalography-based depth of anesthesia monitoring (73%), or cautious long-acting neuraxial opioid use (69%). The panel did not define symptom resolution and established no symptom-independent waiting interval or concussion-specific numeric physiologic threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: This anesthesiology-led consensus supports symptom-guided timing, physiologic stability, counseling, and structured follow-up; anesthetic technique, electroencephalographic monitoring, and neuraxial opioid use remain unresolved. The statements form an expert-informed framework, not an evidence-based practice guideline.

Symptoms and Illness Recognition in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Qualitative Study of Peritoneal Dialysis Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease often progresses without noticeable symptoms, requiring patients to interpret disease progression primarily through biomedical information. However, little is known about how patients understand and respond to repeated warnings of worsening kidney function and recommendations to prepare for dialysis.

METHODS: This qualitative study employed semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 43 patients receiving peritoneal dialysis at a tertiary hospital in South Korea (49% men; 74% aged 50-70 years). Participants retrospectively described their experiences from chronic kidney disease diagnosis to dialysis initiation. This secondary qualitative analysis used inductive reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's framework.

RESULTS: Three themes were identified: (1) the reported absence of noticeable symptoms reduced the perceived urgency of biomedical warnings; (2) preserved physical functioning sustained expectations of reversibility; and (3) the emergence of symptoms made the invisible illness real. After dialysis initiation, improvement in symptoms and physical condition prompted some participants to retrospectively recognise earlier symptoms as manifestations of kidney failure. Across these themes, participants recalled judging the seriousness of chronic kidney disease by comparing biomedical information with their symptoms and perceived physical condition.

CONCLUSION: Participants' accounts suggest that biomedical warnings may carry limited personal urgency when patients perceive no noticeable symptoms. Whether integrating patients' experiences into pre-dialysis education improves illness recognition, dialysis preparation or shared decision-making warrants prospective investigation.

articles.title: Mechanical Ventilation Strategies and Monitoring in Patients with Right Ventricular Failure.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract: Respiratory failure is the predominant etiology for admission to the contemporary cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) and frequently requires invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). Positive pressure ventilation (PPV) delivered by IMV reverses the normal physiology of spontaneous breathing and uniquely impacts the right ventricle (RV). By increasing intrathoracic pressure, PPV reduces preload and can increase RV afterload. Given these potentially detrimental effects on the RV, patients with RV dysfunction can decompensate with instituting PPV. The peri-intubation period is particularly high-risk for these patients and requires careful planning and monitoring, which includes both non-invasive and invasive modalities. During IMV, it is necessary to optimize oxygenation, acid-base status, and reduce atelectasis while limiting airway pressures to avoid potentially worsening RV function. In this review, we discuss the epidemiology of RV and respiratory failure in the CICU, pathophysiology of PPV as it relates to the RV, and management immediately before, during, and liberation from IMV.

articles.title: RNA-binding protein Rbfox2 establishes lipid gene programs through hierarchical control of transcription factors in the embryonic heart.
articles.abstract: The role of RNA-binding proteins in metabolic gene regulation is unclear. Here, we uncover a hierarchical circuit where RNA-binding protein RBFOX2 establishes lipid gene programs and lipidome in embryonic hearts by governing transcription factors (TFs) using multi-transcriptomic and lipidomics approaches. We identified TF and lipid genes as RBFOX2 targets in the embryonic heart. TF SOX4 is a key target of RBFOX2 that drives lipid gene programs. RBFOX2 binds human SOX4 3' UTR and regulates its mRNA stability. SOX4 in turn initiates a lipid gene program by binding promoters of lipid enzymes/regulators. Restoration of SOX4 level, rescues lipid gene expression defects upon RBFOX2 loss. Strikingly, Rbfox2 loss in embryonic hearts modulates cardiac lipidome and leads to accumulation of lipid droplets. We reveal an RNA-mediated mechanism that establishes lipidome identity in the developing heart and may provide unique metabolic nodes vulnerable for pharmaceutic intervention of congenital heart disease in the future.

articles.title: Impact of oxygen delivery location during non-invasive home mechanical ventilation: a randomised cross-over simulation study.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In non-invasive home mechanical ventilation (NIV) using single-limb circuits with vented masks, supplemental oxygen can be added at different locations, potentially resulting in variable delivered inspired oxygen fractions (FiO₂). Recommendations and data comparing oxygen inlet positions are lacking.

METHODS: A lung simulator study was conducted using a 1.8 m single-limb NIV circuit with a vented mask. Oxygen was added at three locations: the ventilator oxygen port, a bleed-in connector near the ventilator outlet, and a bleed-in connector between the tube and mask. Oxygen flow rates of 1, 2, and 3 L/min were tested. Three simulated conditions were studied by adjusting lung compliance and airway resistance: healthy, COPD, and obesity. NIV was applied in pressure-controlled ventilation mode. Settings were EPAP/IPAP 4/14 cmH₂O for the healthy model, and both 4/18 and 8/20 cmH₂O for the COPD and obesity models, with a respiratory rate of 14/min. Mean resulting FiO₂ and minute ventilation from three repeated measurements in random order were recorded.

RESULTS: Oxygen delivery via the ventilator oxygen-port and ventilator-near bleed-in produced broadly similar FiO2 values, ad both generally higher FiO₂ than mask-near delivery. Differences between inlet positions became more pronounced at higher oxygen flows reaching a maximum absolute difference of 5.3 percentage points between oxygen port an mask-near delivery. FiO₂ also differed between the two tested ventilator pressure settings in the COPD and obesity simulations, despite only small differences in minute ventilation. Increasing oxygen flow increased FiO₂ across all configurations, although the magnitude of this effect depended on oxygen-injection location and the simulated condition.

CONCLUSION: In this lung simulator study using a single-limb NIV circuit with a vented mask, oxygen injection location influenced the achieved FiO₂. Under the tested conditions, oxygen delivery via the ventilator oxygen port and a ventilator-near bleed-in connector resulted in broadly similar FiO₂ values and generally achieved higher FiO₂ than mask-near delivery. These findings warrant validation across different ventilators, circuits, interfaces, and pressure settings.

articles.title: Global Burden of Heart Failure Attributable to Chronic Kidney Disease from 1990 to 2021 and Future Projections to 2050: A GBD 2021 Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure attributable to chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents an important manifestation of the cardiorenal syndrome. However, its global burden, long-term trends, and relative contribution to the overall heart failure burden remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: In this observational, GBD-based analysis, data were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study. We analyzed prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) of heart failure attributable to CKD from 1990 to 2021 at global, socio-demographic index (SDI) quintile, and national levels. Temporal trends were assessed using age-standardized rates, joinpoint regression, and age-period-cohort analysis. The relative contribution of CKD was calculated as CKD-attributable all-age numbers divided by total heart failure numbers. Future YLD rates were projected to 2050 using a Bayesian age-period-cohort model.

RESULTS: Globally, prevalent cases increased from 506,142 in 1990 to 1,543,034 in 2021. The age-standardized prevalence rate rose from 10.44 to 19.14 per 100,000 population, and the age-standardized YLD rate increased from 1.33 to 2.42 per 100,000. The CKD-attributable share of total heart failure prevalence increased from 2.03% to 2.90%, and the corresponding YLD share increased from 2.74% to 3.86%. The projected global YLD rate reached 4.67 per 100,000 by 2050.

CONCLUSIONS: CKD-attributable heart failure increased substantially from 1990 to 2021 and is projected to continue rising. CKD accounted for a small but increasing share of the global heart failure burden, supporting integration of kidney disease detection and management into heart failure prevention strategies.

articles.title: Association between triglyceride-glucose index and chronic liver disease: a longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Insulin resistance may be closely related to the occurrence and development of chronic liver diseases (CLD). But, the relationship between triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and CLD is still unknown. This study aimed to prospectively investigate the association between TyG index and CLD in Chinese middle aged and elderly adults.

METHODS: A total of 9156 participants from the China Longitudinal Study of Health and Retirement aged 45 years and older were included. The participants were divided into four groups based on the TyG index quartiles. A cox regression model was established to analyze the correlation between TyG index and CLD.

RESULTS: During 7-year follow up, 541 (5.91%) participants developed CLD. The hazard ratio (95% confidence interval) for the highest quartile of TyG index, TyGBMI, and TyGwaist was 1.42(1.10-1.83), 1.62(1.25-2.09) and 1.40(1.09-1.81) after full adjustment, respectively, with the lowest quartiles as the reference. Similarly, TyG index, TyGBMI, and TyGwaist exhibited a linear dose-response relationship with CLD (all P linearity <0.001). Furthermore, the addition of TyG-related indices to the conventional model significantly improved reclassification and comprehensive identification of risk of CLD.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher TyG index was associated with increased risk of CLD, independently of established risk factors. The TyG index may be a predictor of incident CLD.

articles.title: Psychological care of children, adolescents and young adults with diabetes.
articles.abstract: The 2026 International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes (ISPAD) Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines on psychological care provide updated, evidence-informed recommendations to support the psychological well-being and quality of life of children, adolescents, and young adults living with diabetes. This update adopts a broader biopsychosocial-spiritual and social ecological framework, recognizing the influence of individual, family, cultural, socioeconomic, and environmental factors on psychological health and diabetes outcomes. A major addition is the consideration of psychological aspects of type 1 diabetes screening, early detection, and staging, including parental anxiety, decision-making, and psychological support during ongoing monitoring. The guidelines also expand their coverage of psychological comorbidities, disordered eating behaviors and eating disorders, neurodevelopmental conditions, parental mental health, transition to adult care, and the broader social impact of diabetes, with particular attention to stigma and health equity. Updated recommendations emphasize the integration of routine psychosocial monitoring and screening into diabetes care, including the use of person-reported outcome measures, caregiver assessment, and stepped-care pathways for identifying and addressing psychological difficulties. The guidelines further highlight the importance of developmentally appropriate, person-centered, culturally sensitive, and multidisciplinary approaches to psychological care. By integrating psychological assessment and support into routine diabetes management, these recommendations aim to promote psychological well-being, strengthen family support, and improve the quality of care for young people living with diabetes across diverse healthcare settings.

articles.title: Wearable-Derived Physical Activity Patterns in Preclinical and Clinical Obesity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology Commission issued a new obesity definition to move beyond BMI and prioritize excess body fat and dysfunctional adiposity, stratified by preclinical and clinical groups. We evaluated the physical activity patterns across obesity groups with wearable-derived accelerometry and risk for cardiovascular disease.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of step count, moderate-to-vigorous exercise, and sedentary time in 24,679 adults with Fitbit and electronic health records from the All of Us Research Program, stratified by no, preclinical, and clinical obesity groups.

RESULTS: There was a decline in physical activity across obesity groups: median daily steps were 7846, 6702, and 5128, weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity exercise 140, 91, and 35 min; and daily sedentary time 12.2, 12.8, and 13.4 h for no, preclinical, and clinical obesity, respectively. Physical activity decreased with BMI and obesity-related multimorbidity.

CONCLUSIONS: Wearable-derived physical activity patterns show distinct patterns for preclinical and clinical obesity.

articles.title: Fatal Pasteurella multocida sepsis following cat bite in occult liver disease: a forensic pathological perspective.
articles.abstract: In forensic practice, fatal cases of Pasteurella multocida (P. multocida) infection following cat scratches and bites are extremely rare. We present a typical forensic case of death caused by P. multocida infection following a cat scratch injury. A 50-year-old woman who succumbed to P. multocida infection 92 h after being scratched by her pet cat. The clinical department promptly implemented a series of active medical intervention measures, such as thorough wound debridement, respiratory support, and the combined use of antibiotics. Additionally, laboratory tests gradually pointed to animal-source pathogenic bacterial infection. However, the patient's condition continued to deteriorate progressively and eventually died despite rescue efforts. Despite rapid medical intervention, such fatalities remain exceptionally uncommon. This report details a fatal P. multocida infection in which the patient exhibited clear clinical symptoms and examination findings. The cause of death was attributed to multiple organ tissue hemorrhage secondary to the cat-induced trauma, culminating in multiple organ failure primarily due to acute respiratory and circulatory collapse. This case represents the first systematic forensic autopsy of a fatal P. multocida infection, thereby filling a critical gap in the literature on P. multocida-related fatalities.

articles.title: Development of a Gliptin Screening System Based on a Recombinant Secreted Form of Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: A system was developed for screening inhibitors of dipeptidyl peptidase-4, a therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Recombinant secretory DPP4 variant lacking the transmembrane domain was expressed in a CHO-K1-S cell suspension culture. Affinity purification yielded 0.125 g/L of the target protein. The catalytic activity of the enzyme (Km = 46.75 μM) and its sensitivity to the reference inhibitor sitagliptin (IC50 = 21.1 nM) were demonstrated. This validated system represents a reliable tool for preclinical screening for new gliptins.

articles.title: Effects of Ketanserin, Reserpine, VEGF, and HGF as Monotherapy and Combination Therapy in Experimental Liver Cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of ketanserin (a serotonin 5-HT2 receptor antagonist), reserpine (a sympatholytic), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) administered as monotherapy or combination therapy was evaluated in male Wistar rats with toxic liver cirrhosis induced by carbon tetrachloride and ethanol. Ketanserin monotherapy selectively caused regression of fibrosis, reserpine had an anti-inflammatory effect, VEGF increased the number of endothelial cells, and HGF increased the number of hepatocytes. Combination therapy with ketanserin, reserpine, VEGF, and HGF exerted an antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects and stimulated regeneration of endothelial cells and hepatocytes. The observed synergistic effect of the sequential administration of monoamine-targeting drugs and growth factors holds promise for the development of multi-target therapeutic strategies for fibrosing liver diseases.

articles.title: Ultrastructural Changes in Erythrocytes and Plasma During Experimental P. aeruginosa Sepsis.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: Bacteriological and electron microscopic analyses of experimental models of sepsis induced by intraperitoneal infection of male C57BL/6 mice with clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (strains 5266 and 1623) were performed. We observed high recovery rates of P. aeruginosa from the blood as early as 15 min post-inoculation, the absence of physiological structuring of the blood plasma around the pathogens, and a transformation of erythrocytes in close proximity to the bacteria into echinocytes (senescent forms). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of early bacteriological diagnosis of P. aeruginosa sepsis and suggest that the pathogenicity factors of these bacterial strains directly affect the ultrastructure of blood plasma and erythrocytes.

articles.title: Changes in the Cecal Microbiota in a Rat Model of Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: Characteristics of the intestinal microbiota specific to metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) were studied in vivo using male Wistar rats. The consumption of high-fat diets (choline-deficient or cholesterol-supplemented) commonly used in experimental MAFLD models induced shifts in the cecal microbiota. An increase in the number of facultatively anaerobic coccal populations (Enterococcus spp. and Streptococcus spp.) was observed, including potentially pathogenic representatives. The addition of cholesterol to the high-fat diet caused more pronounced dysbiotic shifts: a decrease in the frequency of detection of methanogenic archaea (Methanobrevibacter smithii, Methanosphaera stadtmanae) and a decline in the protective butyrate-producing Faecalibacterium prausnitzii population, leading to the development of an anaerobic flora imbalance (a predominance of Bacteroides spp. over F. prausnitzii). Our findings suggest that a high-fat diet supplemented with cholesterol can cause inflammatory-type dysbiosis in the cecum, whereas choline deficiency, even under conditions of high energy intake, had a less profound impact on the composition of the main microbiota populations.

articles.title: Balanced Block of hERG/Kv11.1, CaV1.2, and NaV1.5 in Proarrhythmic Risk Assessment: An Integrated Review of In Vitro Electrophysiology, In Silico Modeling, and hiPSC-CM Evidence.
articles.abstract: Drug-induced torsade de pointes (TdP) risk is commonly assessed by measuring inhibition of the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr), mediated by Kv11.1/hERG, together with QT-interval prolongation. These endpoints are sensitive but incompletely specific because concomitant inhibition of the L-type calcium current (ICaL) or late sodium current (INaL) can attenuate IKr-block-mediated repolarization delay. This narrative review evaluates balanced ion-channel block using recombinant-cell electrophysiology, in silico models, and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). Potency ratios can describe relative channel inhibition but cannot alone establish a validated risk threshold or low clinical TdP liability. Concentration-response slopes, binding kinetics, unbound exposure, active metabolites, trafficking effects, and patient susceptibility also influence outcome. The CiPA-modified O'Hara-Rudy ventricular model and qNet-derived Torsade Metric Score are model-specific integrators rather than direct measurements of clinical repolarization reserve. The fixed-block simulations presented here illustrate interactions between inward and outward currents. hiPSC-CMs provide complementary functional evidence but remain limited by cellular immaturity and assay variability. The ICH E14/S7B Q&As (R1), adopted in August 2026, support integrated assessment and permit qualified alternative assays in defined contexts of use.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Nomogram Model for Identifying Preoperative Osteoporosis Among Metabolic Bariatric Surgery Candidates Using Routinely Available Clinical Variables.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis (OP) is a common metabolic bone disease, and metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) candidates may have impaired bone health. This study aimed to develop a nomogram model based on routinely available clinical variables for identifying preoperative OP among MBS candidates.

METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study included 738 MBS candidates who underwent preoperative evaluation between July 2020 and December 2023. All participants had available preoperative dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements. Candidate predictors were initially selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and subsequently entered into multivariable logistic regression to develop the final nomogram model. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration measures, and decision curve analysis (DCA), respectively. Internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Among 738 MBS candidates, 100 (13.6%) met the criteria for OP. Multivariable logistic regression identified seven variables independently associated with OP status, including age, body mass index (BMI), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), albumin (Alb), total bile acid (TBA), lymphocyte count, and sex, which were incorporated into the nomogram. The model achieved an AUC of 0.793 (95% CI: 0.747-0.838), with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.763 after bootstrap validation. The calibration curve showed overall agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA suggested potential clinical utility within a range of threshold probabilities.

CONCLUSION: A nomogram based on routinely available preoperative clinical variables may facilitate the identification of preoperative OP among MBS candidates and demonstrate acceptable discrimination and calibration performance.

articles.title: Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with HHV-8-negative multicentric Castleman disease.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) has been reported in HHV-8-positive multicentric Castleman disease (MCD); however, its association with HHV-8-negative idiopathic MCD (iMCD) remains undocumented. We report a 29-year-old woman with iMCD who presented with exertional dyspnea and systemic inflammation and had pre-capillary PH confirmed by right heart catheterization. Siltuximab plus corticosteroids improved symptoms and hemodynamics; after relapse on sirolimus, tocilizumab induced complete clinical remission with biomarker normalization. This first report of iMCD-associated PH underscores the need to evaluate cardiopulmonary involvement in iMCD and highlights interleukin-6-driven immune dysregulation as a potential therapeutic target in this PH subgroup.

articles.title: Hearing Loss Caused by Chronic Kidney Disease: Evidence of Cochlear Metabolic Disturbances.
articles.abstract: Hearing loss affects over 1.5 billion people worldwide. Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at an increased risk of sensorineural hearing impairment, although the mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Using an adenine-induced mouse model, we evaluated auditory function, cochlear pathology, and metabolism. The mice exhibited significant hearing loss, marked atrophy of the stria vascularis in the middle and basal turns of the cochlea, and pronounced oxidative stress. Metabolomic profiling identified substantial disruptions in cochlear amino acid and lipid metabolism, with concordant metabolic abnormalities in the serum and kidneys. Notably, the uremic toxin, p-cresyl sulfate, was significantly elevated in the cochlea. Overall, CKD induced metabolic disturbances and disrupted tight junction integrity, which may facilitate cochlear accumulation of uremic toxins, trigger oxidative stress, and contribute to hearing loss. These findings provide novel insights into CKD-associated hearing loss and identify potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Frasier syndrome presenting with persistent Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia during intensive immunosuppressive therapy: a case report.
articles.abstract: Childhood-onset steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) is caused by monogenic abnormalities in approximately 30% of cases, and is generally unresponsive to immunosuppressive therapy. However, in routine clinical practice, additional immunosuppression is often initiated before the results of genetic testing become available, thereby potentially increasing the risk of severe infection. We report the case of a 3-year-old girl with SRNS in which kidney biopsy showed focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, and there was persistent heavy proteinuria despite methylprednisolone pulse therapy and oral cyclosporin. During the clinical course, she developed persistent Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography suggested portal vein thrombosis as the infectious focus. Genetic testing subsequently identified a WT1 variant (NM_024426.6: c.1447 + 4C > T), establishing the diagnosis of Frasier syndrome. After immunosuppressive therapy was discontinued, in conjunction with ongoing antimicrobial and supportive treatment, she became afebrile and blood cultures became negative. This case highlights not only the importance of early genetic testing in SRNS to avoid ineffective immunosuppressive therapy, but also the potential for intensive immunosuppression to precipitate life-threatening infection, even in pediatric patients.

articles.title: Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide Cut-off Values for Discriminating Asthma Exacerbation and Control in Indian Children with Coexisting Allergic Rhinitis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study - Authors' Reply 3.
Histotripsy for Liver Malignancies: A Systematic Review of the Existing Literature.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histotripsy is an emerging noninvasive, nonthermal ablative therapy recently introduced for the treatment of hepatic malignancies. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy and safety of histotripsy for primary and secondary liver tumors.

METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through August 2026 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Search terms included combinations of subject headings and keywords such as "histotripsy," "hepatic," and "metastases."

RESULTS: Ten clinical studies published between 2022 and 2026 met inclusion criteria. Study populations included hepatocellular carcinoma and metastases from colorectal, neuroendocrine, pancreatic, breast, and other malignancies. Technical success ranged from 68.8% to 100%, although definitions varied across studies. Early treatment efficacy and local control were generally high among successfully treated tumors, with several studies reporting rates exceeding 90%. Longer-term oncologic data were limited by heterogeneous imaging criteria, treatment intent, and patient populations. Major complications were uncommon, although vascular thrombosis and acute kidney injury emerged as potential safety concerns.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports the technical feasibility and short-term efficacy of hepatic histotripsy. However, standardized outcome definitions, longer follow-up, and comparative studies are needed to establish its durability and role relative to existing liver-directed therapies.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of GLP-1 receptor agonists VS placebo among patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex form of heart failure which is marked by impaired diastolic function. It has complex pathophysiology involving systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis and arterial stiffness. The existence of other comorbidities namely obesity and diabetes further worsens these processes. Currently there is limited treatment option for HFpEF.

METHODS: Systematic search from 5 databases was conducted to identify studies that evaluated the impacts of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) on the clinical outcomes of HFpEF. Quantitative analysis was performed using random effect model were performed on clinical outcomes. Results are presented as odds ratio (OR) along with its 95% confidence interval.

RESULTS: 3 Studies involving 1463 patients were included. GLP-1 RA reduced NT-pro Brain Natriuretic Peptide (NT-pro BNP) levels and enhanced 6-minute walking test, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score. Significant reduction in adjudicated heart failure event was observed (OR 0.32, 95% CI: 0.15-0.67, p < 0.05, I2 = 5%). No significant difference in all-cause mortality (OR 0.63, 95% CI: 0.27-1.48, p = 0.29, I2 = 0%) and cardiovascular mortality (OR 0.27, 95% CI: 0.04-1.66, p = 0.16, I2 = 0%) were observed.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1 RA was effective in improving quality of life parameters and lowered the risk of cardiovascular events of HFpEF patients; however it did not significantly reduce mortality in those who suffered from HFpEF.

articles.title: Computed tomography derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in high-risk breast cancer using fully automated deep learning algorithms.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer.

METHODS: We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins.

RESULTS: Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis.

CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

articles.title: Modulation of the gut microbiota-arginine axis restrains inflammation and reduces post-infarction fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a robust inflammatory response that critically dictates the trajectory of cardiac repair, making the modulation of immune cells a vital therapeutic target. While the gut-heart axis is increasingly recognized in cardiovascular diseases, the upstream gut-derived signals regulating post-infarction immunity remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the dynamic changes in gut microbiota and metabolite profiles post-MI and investigate their role in cardiac inflammation and fibrosis. Using a murine model of MI, the study integrated 16 S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, flow cytometry, and histological analyses. MI induced severe intestinal barrier dysfunction and progressive gut dysbiosis, significantly depleting Desulfovibrionaceae and Helicobacteraceae. This microbial remodeling converged on a profound reduction in both intestinal and circulating arginine levels. Consequently, this metabolic deficit was associated with an exacerbated accumulation of pro-inflammatory Ly6Chigh monocytes and CD80+ M1-like macrophages in the ischemic myocardium at day 3, driving extensive fibrotic remodeling by day 14. To validate this functional axis, targeted interventions were employed. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) promoted partial microbial reconstitution and attenuated myocardial fibrosis in antibiotic-pretreated MI mice. Similarly, systemic L-arginine supplementation reduced the early accumulation of inflammatory myeloid populations and reduced myocardial fibrosis at day 14. Overall, the identified gut microbiota-arginine-immune axis acts as a critical determinant of infarct healing. These findings demonstrate that targeting upstream intestinal metabolic perturbations, through microbiota-directed therapies or metabolic recalibration, represents a biologically plausible strategy to mitigate adverse ventricular remodeling and heart failure after MI.

articles.title: Lifestyle Changes for the Treatment of Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Lifestyle interventions are foundational to hypertension prevention and treatment. We review recent evidence for weight management, dietary patterns, sodium and potassium intake, physical activity, stress reduction, alcohol reduction, and avoidance of blood pressure-raising substances, with emphasis on implementation and contemporary guidelines.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent trials extend Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) benefits to grocery delivery in populations facing barriers to food access, while potassium-enriched salt-substitution studies support cardiovascular benefit but require attention to hyperkalemia risk. Alcohol reduction lowers blood pressure most among individuals with higher baseline intake or blood pressure, and avoidance of other pressor substances remains important. Evidence for time-restricted eating and stress-reduction strategies is uncertain. Lifestyle modification is recommended for all adults with elevated blood pressure or hypertension, but sustained adherence and equitable access are major barriers. Future research should prioritize scalable, durable, culturally responsive strategies and outcomes beyond short-term blood pressure change.

articles.title: Associations of dietary magnesium intake with glomerular and tubular injury markers in type 2 diabetes: The Fukuoka Diabetes Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Higher dietary magnesium intake has been associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease and its risk factors. However, its association with CKD remains unclear. This study examined this association using glomerular and tubular injury markers.

METHODS: A total of 4,923 participants with type 2 diabetes were classified into quintiles of dietary magnesium intake. CKD was defined as decreased estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFRcr <60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and/or albuminuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio [UACR] ≥ 30 mg/g). Odds ratios (ORs) for CKD were calculated using logistic regression. Associations of dietary magnesium intake with eGFRcr, UACR, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), liver-type fatty acid-binding protein (L-FABP), and kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) were evaluated using linear regression.

RESULTS: Higher dietary magnesium intake was associated with lower prevalence of CKD. Compared with the lowest quintile, the multivariable-adjusted ORs (95% confidence intervals) for CKD across increasing quintiles were 0.84 (0.68-1.04), 0.73 (0.57-0.93), 0.58 (0.44-0.76), and 0.50 (0.35-0.71) (P for trend < 0.001). Similar inverse associations were observed for decreased eGFRcr and albuminuria analyzed separately. Higher magnesium intake was also associated with lower urinary NGAL and L-FABP.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest a potential role of dietary magnesium intake in preserving glomerular and tubular kidney health.

articles.title: Association between physical activity and circulating inflammation markers in middle-aged and older adults with chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-grade inflammation is prevalent in chronic kidney disease (CKD); however, evidence linking objectively measured physical activity to circulating inflammatory markers remains limited. This study examined associations of accelerometer-derived physical activity with circulating interleukin-6 (IL-6) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels in adults with CKD.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 118 adults aged ≥ 45 years with CKD wore a waist-mounted triaxial accelerometer for 14 days. Daily time spent in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and light-intensity physical activity (LPA) were quantified. Circulating IL-6 and hs-CRP levels were measured using serum samples. Multivariable linear regression models were used to examine associations of MVPA and LPA with circulating inflammatory markers, adjusting for covariates. An exploratory threshold analysis was conducted by dichotomizing MVPA as < 30 versus ≥ 30 min/day.

RESULTS: Higher MVPA was associated with lower serum IL-6 levels (B = - 0.052 per 30 min/day; 95% CI: -0.100 to - 0.004; p = 0.033), corresponding to an approximately 11.3% lower serum IL-6 level after multivariable adjustment. LPA was not significantly associated with serum IL-6 levels. No statistically significant associations were observed between activity metrics and serum hs-CRP levels in the primary continuous models. In additional analyses, achieving ≥ 30 min/day of MVPA was associated with lower serum IL-6 levels (B = - 0.169; p = 0.005), but not with serum hs-CRP.

CONCLUSION: Higher accelerometer-measured MVPA was associated with lower serum IL-6 levels, whereas no significant associations were observed for serum hs-CRP levels. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the direction of these associations.

articles.title: Two-year randomized clinical evaluation of catechin doped in a universal adhesive on non-carious cervical lesions restorations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This randomized, blinded clinical trial evaluated the 24-month clinical performance of a universal adhesive (Single Bond Universal) containing 0.1 wt% epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) for the restoration of non-carious cervical lesions (NCCLs using self-etch and etch-and-rinse strategies.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 160 restorations were placed in 29 patients and randomly allocated to four groups: etch-and-rinse (ER), etch-and-rinse with EGCG (ER-EGCG), self-etch (SE), and self-etch with EGCG (SE-EGCG). EGCG was directly incorporated into the adhesive, which was applied according to the manufacturer's instructions. All lesions were restored with a nanofilled composite resin (Filtek Z350XT) and evaluated at baseline and after 6, 12, 18, and 24 months according to the World Dental Federation criteria. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis and McNemar tests (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: Participant recall rates were 100% at baseline and 6 months, and 93.1%, 89.7%, and 72.4% at 12, 18, and 24 months, respectively. No significant differences were observed among groups for any evaluated clinical criterion throughout the 24-month follow-up (p > 0.05). At 24 months, retention rates were 90% for SE and SE-EGCG and 100% for ER and ER-EGCG. No significant differences were observed between baseline and 24-month evaluations within any group (p > 0.05). Incorporation of 0.1 wt% EGCG into the universal adhesive did not compromise the clinical performance of NCCL restorations over 24 months, regardless of the bonding strategy.

CONCLUSIONS: Incorporation of 0.1 wt% EGCG into a universal adhesive did not affect the clinical performance of NCCL restorations over 24 months.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Incorporation of 0.1 wt% EGCG into a universal adhesive did not improve the clinical performance of NCCL restorations over 24 months compared with the unmodified adhesive. However, EGCG incorporation did not adversely affect restoration performance when the adhesive was used with either etch-and-rinse or self-etch strategies.

articles.title: Tirzepatide and inflammation: a critical reappraisal of the immunometabolic case for incretin-based therapy.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, lowers high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) by 29-55% across randomised trials in obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obstructive sleep apnoea, and interleukin-6 by 25-30% at 72 weeks. Much of this is not weight-mediated: in SURPASS-4 the fall in hsCRP correlated with that in body mass index at r = 0.07, and mediation analysis of trials of semaglutide, a selective GLP-1 receptor agonist, attributes only 21-62% of its hsCRP effect to change in glycated haemoglobin and/or weight. The mechanism, however, is not the one usually given: the account reproduced in most reviews, that incretin receptors on macrophages and T lymphocytes signal through cyclic AMP to restrain nuclear factor-κB, is not supported by the best-controlled data. The principal antibody used to detect the T-cell GLP-1 receptor gives signal in receptor-null cells; Glp1r is undetectable by quantitative PCR in peritoneal and adipose macrophages; and haematopoietic receptor deletion does not abolish semaglutide's anti-atherosclerotic effect. I therefore propose a three-route model, graded by evidence: limited direct signalling in a few validated lymphocyte populations, a central neuro-immune relay, and a large indirect metabolic contribution. That adipose macrophages are refractory to tirzepatide while Kupffer cells respond, and that C-reactive protein is hepatocyte-derived, suggest a substantially hepatic rather than adipose effect. Because the mechanistic evidence concerns GLP-1 receptor agonism almost entirely, the appraisal applies to incretin-based therapy as a class, tirzepatide being the worked example. Five falsifiable propositions are advanced with the experiments that would refute them.

articles.title: Preventive dental scaling and cardiovascular disease according to periodontal disease status: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between the frequency of preventive dental scaling and the incidence of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a nationwide population-based cohort.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service-Health Screening Cohort were used in this study. A total of 381,530 participants were included, of whom 10,889 experienced new CVD events during the follow-up period. Preventive dental scaling was assessed using insurance claim codes over two years from 2013 to 2015, and categorized into three groups: no scaling, one session, and two or more sessions. The primary outcome was incident CVD, defined as hospitalization owing to stroke, myocardial infarction, or heart failure. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression models.

RESULTS: Compared with the no-scaling group, the fully adjusted HRs for incident CVD were 0.85 (95% CI, 0.81-0.90) in the one-session group and 0.68 (95% CI, 0.61-0.76) in the two-or-more-sessions group (P for trend < 0.001). Subgroup analyses revealed a significant inverse association among participants without claims-defined periodontal disease, whereas no significant association was observed among those with periodontal disease (P for interaction = 0.019).

CONCLUSIONS: Preventive dental scaling was associated with a lower hazard of incident CVD, with a more pronounced association among participants without claims-defined periodontal disease. A causal protective effect cannot be established from these observational findings.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The observed association between dental scaling and cardiovascular outcomes warrants further investigation but does not establish scaling as a measure for CVD prevention.

articles.title: Invasive pulmonary artery pressure monitoring in heart failure: evidence, clinical application, and future directions.
articles.abstract: Hemodynamic congestion frequently precedes overt deterioration in heart failure (HF), offering an opportunity for earlier intervention through remote invasive monitoring. Among available systems, pulmonary artery pressure (PAP)-guided management with CardioMEMS has the most mature randomized evidence for reducing recurrent HF hospitalizations and improving health status, although a consistent survival benefit across the HF spectrum has not been established. Clinical implementation requires individualized pressure targets, sustained trend interpretation, regular patient transmissions, and prompt therapeutic responses. The most directly actionable interventions are adjustments to decongestive treatment; prognostic HF therapies should be prescribed and maintained according to guideline indications rather than PAP readings alone. Persistent worsening-HF events warrant reassessment of signal quality, therapeutic response, and alternative mechanisms of deterioration. Device longevity must be distinguished from long-term calibration accuracy, while post-marketing safety data require cautious interpretation. The incremental benefit of pressure monitoring in patients receiving fully contemporary pharmacological treatment remains uncertain. Emerging pulmonary artery, left atrial, and inferior vena cava platforms have different physiological targets, monitoring workflows, and levels of clinical evidence. This narrative review critically appraises the physiological rationale, randomized and real-world evidence, clinical management, device performance, safety, and future development of implantable hemodynamic monitoring in HF.

articles.title: Exosome-based topical formulations as adjuncts to fractional Nd: YAG laser for postoperative facial scars.
articles.abstract: Commercial topical formulations marketed as exosome skin boosters are increasingly used as adjuncts to laser treatment, but their additional benefit for postoperative facial scars remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial allocated 150 patients to fractional 1064-nm Nd laser treatment followed by a control hydrogel, a human-derived formulation, or a plant-derived formulation (50 per group). Five treatment sessions were performed at 2-week intervals. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and 2 weeks after the final session using the modified Vancouver Scar Scale (mVSS), patient and observer components of the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS), and grayscale intensity (GSI) quantified from Mark-Vu images using ImageJ. Eleven participants were lost to follow-up, leaving 139 participants in the complete-case analysis: 46, 47, and 46 in the respective groups. Both adjunctive formulation groups showed significantly greater reductions in mVSS, observer POSAS, and GSI than the control group. Patient POSAS improved over time but did not demonstrate a significant time × group interaction. No statistically significant difference was detected between the human-derived and plant-derived formulations; equivalence was not established. No serious adverse events were reported during the observed period. Adjunctive formulations were associated with additional short-term improvements in clinician-rated scar outcomes and an exploratory optical measure, without a demonstrated additional patient-reported benefit. These findings apply to the complete formulations and do not establish an exosome-specific effect, sustained scar remodeling, or long-term safety.

articles.title: Survival benefit of adding carboplatin to standard anthracycline-taxane chemotherapy in triple-negative breast cancer: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Carboplatin improves pathological complete response (pCR) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but its effect on long-term survival remains uncertain. We conducted a strict randomized-contrast meta-analysis to assess the incremental effect of adding carboplatin to otherwise substantially comparable chemotherapy regimens.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from database inception. Phase II/III randomized controlled trials comparing carboplatin-containing versus carboplatin-free otherwise substantially comparable chemotherapy regimens in non-metastatic TNBC were included. Directly reported HRs for trial-defined disease-control endpoints and OS, and odds ratios (ORs) for pCR were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the disease-control and OS findings.

RESULTS: Seven randomized contrasts (2,627 randomized participants) contributed disease-control evidence. Carboplatin significantly improved trial-defined disease control (HR 0.779, 95% CI 0.671-0.904; p = 0.001; I2 = 40.6%) and increased pCR rates (OR 2.038, 95% CI 1.653-2.512; p < 0.001; I2 = 29.9%). The OS estimate favored carboplatin but was compatible with no effect (HR 0.810, 95% CI 0.627-1.046; p = 0.107; I2 = 41.4%). The sensitivity analysis restricted to aligned EFS-type endpoints remained favorable (HR 0.793, 95% CI 0.656-0.960; p = 0.017; I2 = 31.4%).

CONCLUSION: Carboplatin addition significantly improves pCR and trial-defined disease control in TNBC when evaluated in otherwise substantially comparable randomized chemotherapy contrasts. However, the strict evidence did not establish an OS benefit.

articles.title: Buttress plate augmentation offers no clear clinical advantage over compression screws alone for Hoffa fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare clinical, functional, and perioperative outcomes after fixation of Hoffa fractures using buttress plate augmentation with compression screws versus compression screws alone.

METHODS: PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through 31 July 2026 for randomized or nonrandomized comparative studies of adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using ROBINS-I. Random-effects meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.

RESULTS: Four nonrandomized studies involving 143 patients (BPCS, 63; CS, 80) were included. BPCS was associated with greater knee range of motion at 4 months (mean difference [MD], 10.85°; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.69-20.02; p = 0.04; I² = 0%) and longer operative time (MD, 23.03 min; 95% CI, 7.45-38.62; p = 0.02; I² = 84%). No significant differences were found in range of motion at ≥ 12 months, early or late functional knee scores, blood loss, or time to union. Overall risk of bias was moderate in one study and serious in three.

CONCLUSION: Limited observational evidence suggests that buttress plate augmentation may improve early knee motion but prolongs operative time, without a demonstrated durable functional or union advantage. Because the evidence is sparse and at substantial risk of bias, fixation should be individualized according to fracture characteristics and intraoperative stability.

articles.title: Changes in functional capacity, flexibility and depressive symptoms in women with breast cancer submitted to adjuvant radiotherapy: randomized controlled clinical trial with mat pilates.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the impact of Mat Pilates on functional capacity, flexibility, and depressive symptoms in women diagnosed with breast cancer who received adjuvant radiotherapy.

METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 164 women with breast cancer (stages 0-III), aged 18 years or older, were randomized, and 156 were included in the analyses (79 in the Mat Pilates group and 77 in the control group). Handgrip strength, functional exercise capacity assessed by the 2-Minute Step Test (2MST), flexibility, and depressive symptoms were evaluated at baseline, at the end of radiotherapy (RT), and at 30 days, 3 months, and 6 months after RT. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to analyze functional capacity and flexibility, while the cumulative incidence of new depressive symptoms was estimated among participants without depressive symptoms at baseline.

RESULTS: No significant group × time interactions were observed for handgrip strength (Wald χ2 = 7.834; df = 4; p = 0.098), the 2-Minute Step Test (Wald χ2 = 6.877; df = 4; p = 0.143), or flexibility (Wald χ2 = 3.728; df = 4; p = 0.444). During the RT period, the cumulative of new depressive symptoms was 14.8%.

CONCLUSION: Functional capacity and flexibility improved over time, but their trajectories did not differ significantly between the Mat Pilates and control groups. No significant between-group difference was observed in the cumulative incidence of new depressive symptoms.

articles.title: Reply to: Re: efficacy of platelet-rich plasma versus hyaluronic acid in obese individuals with knee osteoarthritis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract: In response to the correspondence by Ahmad et al., we address the concerns raised about our retrospective comparison of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and hyaluronic acid (HA) in 99 obese patients with knee osteoarthritis. We acknowledge that the non-randomised design precludes causal inference and that our original conclusion on arthroplasty was stronger than warranted by the time-to-event analysis (log-rank p = 0.177; hazard ratio 0.46, 95% CI 0.15-1.42). We clarify the overlap with our earlier reports from the same institutional database and the reasons for differing obesity counts, explain why propensity-score matching was not repeated, and discuss the unequal number of injections between groups. Estimated from mean follow-up, incidence rates were 8.1 versus 23.0 arthroplasties per 100 person-years for PRP and HA, respectively (incidence rate ratio 0.35, 95% CI 0.12-1.03). PRP remained associated with significantly lower WOMAC scores at 6 and 12 months, but the arthroplasty findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Blinded, dose-matched randomised trials with arthroplasty as a prespecified time-to-event endpoint are needed.

articles.title: Associations between white matter network alterations and visuospatial and social-emotional deficits in patients with right hemisphere tumors: a prospective clinico-radiological study.
articles.abstract: Preserving neurological function is crucial in brain tumor surgery. Because the right hemisphere supports visuospatial and social‑cognitive abilities, damage may affect quality of life. This prospective study (TANGO; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04288505) examined associations between visuospatial and social‑emotional deficits and tractography‑based white matter alterations in patients with right hemisphere tumors. Thirty‑four patients were assessed preoperatively and 22 postoperatively using diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and four neuropsychological tests. Tractography metrics were extracted for nine right hemisphere tracts. Thirty‑four Human Connectome Project participants served as controls. Preoperatively, deficits in visuospatial functioning, facial emotion recognition, and mentalizing were associated with predominantly right hemisphere microstructural abnormalities within distributed white matter networks. Visuospatial deficits were associated with alterations involving the frontal aslant tract (FAT), arcuate fasciculus (AF), superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), and SLF II; facial emotion recognition deficits with the SLF III and uncinate fasciculus (UF); and mentalizing deficits with the AF. Postoperatively, exploratory findings suggested associations between new social-emotional deficits and structural alterations involving the inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), SLF, and SLF III, whereas new visuospatial deficits showed a trend toward reduced right FAT volume. Relative to controls, left hemisphere tractographic changes were observed regardless of the presence of visuospatial and/or social-emotional deficits, whereas right hemisphere alterations were primarily observed in patients with such deficits. These findings highlight the role of right hemisphere networks in supporting visuospatial and social-emotional functioning. Further characterization of white matter connectivity may help improve risk stratification, surgical planning, and rehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Endovascular treatment for cervical internal carotid artery occlusion due to dissection: a multicenter analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evidence on endovascular treatment (EVT) for isolated cervical internal carotid artery occlusion (c-ICA-O) due to dissection is limited. We evaluated the impact of EVT for dissection-related isolated (non-tandem) c-ICA-O.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This secondary analysis of the multicenter EVT for Isolated cervical Internal Carotid Artery occlusion (ETIICA) retrospective study included patients with dissections. Patients treated with EVT were compared with those treated with best medical treatment alone. The primary endpoint was 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) shift analysis.
