Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-2 or return to baseline, early neurological deterioration (END), symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), carotid patency at the end of EVT, and intracranial embolization. Analyses used regressions with inverse probability of treatment weighting.

RESULTS: Of 998 patients, 108 (10.8%) had dissection [mean age 53.7 (SD 11.2) years, 26.9% female]. EVT was performed in 60 (55.5%) patients. EVT patients had higher admission NIHSS (median 13 [4-18] vs 2 [0-9]). There was no difference in mRS shift (acOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.29-2.20). Functional independence was observed in 64.9% of EVT patients vs 81.3% of BMT patients (aOR 1.69, 95% CI: 0.52-5.51; BMT as reference). END was numerically more frequent in the EVT group (28.8% vs 8.3%; aOR 2.38, 95% CI: 0.62-9.18). sICH occurred in 2 EVT patients. Carotid patency was achieved in 45/60 (75%) patients undergoing EVT, and 18/59 (30%) patients had intracranial embolization.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, EVT was not associated with improved 3-month functional outcomes, despite achieving carotid patency in three out of four patients.

KEY POINTS: Question What are the technical and clinical outcomes of EVT compared with best medical treatment in patients with isolated cervical internal carotid artery occlusive dissection? Findings EVT effectively recanalized acutely occluded dissected extracranial internal carotid arteries, but intracranial emboli and re-occlusion were frequent, with no adjusted 90-day clinical benefit. Clinical relevance Precaution and technical refinement of EVT for isolated cervical carotid artery dissection appear necessary. Larger studies focusing on severely affected patients are warranted. Until such evidence is available, treatment decisions should be individualized on a case-by-case basis.

articles.title: Short-term physiological responses to nocturnal pressurization in male high-altitude workers: an exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: International archives of occupational and environmental health
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial investigated whether a nocturnal pressurization intervention, designed to simulate altitude reduction during sleep, was associated with changes in multi-system physiological responses in male workers with chronic intermittent high-altitude exposure.

METHODS: Twenty-four male workers were randomized to a Pressurization group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 12); Over a 5-week protocol, the Pressurization group slept at the simulated altitudes while both groups worked at 3500 m. The primary outcome was mean nocturnal peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2); secondary outcomes were ambulatory blood pressure (BP), serum normetanephrine and metanephrine, Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System components, and oxidative stress markers.

RESULTS: The intervention was associated with short-term changes, the largest of which occurred during the 2000 m-simulated week. SpO2 was higher than in controls at 2500 m and 2000 m (both p < 0.001). Nocturnal diastolic BP was lower at 2500 m (- 7.25 mmHg, p = 0.024), normetanephrine, metanephrine and angiotensin II were reduced at 2000 m (Ang II: -23.10 pg/mL, p  = 0.011), and 8-iso-PGF2α was lower with higher total antioxidant capacity at both altitudes. None of these differences persisted at the fifth-week recovery assessment.

CONCLUSION: A nocturnal pressurization intervention simulating descent to 2000 m was associated with improved nocturnal oxygenation and short-term reductions in neurohormonal and oxidative stress in male high-altitude workers. The changes were reversible and had disappeared one week after the intervention ceased; they should therefore not be interpreted as an improvement in long-term adaptation, and the study should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Between promise and guidance: a systematic review of normative documents on polygenic risk scores in healthcare contexts.
articles.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) have shown increasing predictive value for several common complex diseases and generated expectations regarding their potential clinical and public health applications. Despite growing research and translational initiatives, PRS have yet to be integrated into routine clinical practice. The limited uptake of PRS has been linked to scientific limitations and a lack of clear guidance. More recently, the emergence of professional and policy documents addressing PRS points to an evolving normative landscape that warrants careful consideration. To this end, we conducted a systematic review of normative documents addressing the prospective use of PRS in healthcare contexts, including clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and policy reports issued by professional societies, regulatory bodies, and healthcare institutions. Searches were conducted across major biomedical and policy databases, complemented by grey literature sources and targeted website searches. Twenty-six documents met the inclusion criteria. None explicitly endorsed the routine implementation of PRS in healthcare at present. Most adopted cautious positions, citing limited evidence of clinical utility, concerns about transferability, and ethical risks. Substantial variation was observed in scope and degree of prescriptivity. While broad agreement existed on general best practices-such as defining test purpose, integrating PRS with other risk factors, and ensuring appropriate counsel​ing-guidance was often non-prescriptive, leaving key implementation thresholds and value commitments implicit. The findings highlight an emerging but fragmented normative landscape in which guidance has not yet globally translated into clear, action-guiding standards for clinical practice and implementation in healthcare. Clarifying how evidence, value commitments, and responsibilities translate into statements is essential to inform ongoing and future deliberations on the responsible use and implementation of PRS.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Fontan Circulation: Bridging the Evidence Gap Between Adult Heart Failure Data and Single-Ventricle Physiology.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have transformed the management of heart failure in adults and are now used empirically in children with Fontan-palliated single-ventricle circulation, despite an absence of trials in this population. Early observational data suggest that SGLT2 inhibitors are well tolerated in Fontan circulatory failure, with signals of reduced natriuretic peptide levels and modest improvement in ventricular function, but no study has been designed or powered to establish efficacy. This gap is compounded by a physiological mismatch: the Fontan circulation is characterized by the absence of a subpulmonary pumping chamber, resulting in passive pulmonary blood flow. Under these unique hemodynamic conditions, systemic ventricular preload is primarily determined by pulmonary vascular resistance, ventricular diastolic properties, and atrial filling pressures. These distinctive physiological characteristics may have important implications for the mechanisms underlying the effects of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Notably, diastolic dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a prevalent feature of Fontan circulatory failure. Given the established clinical benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors in adults with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, their potential therapeutic effects in the Fontan population may extend beyond conventional preload modulation to include improvements in diastolic function and ventricular filling dynamics. In this Perspective, we examine whether the principal mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitor benefit described in adults-osmotic diuresis and preload reduction, a myocardial substrate shift toward ketone metabolism, and blockade of the cardiac sodium-hydrogen exchanger-plausibly translate to Fontan physiology, review the available pediatric evidence and its limitations, and outline a framework for a prospective, phenotype-stratified multicenter trial. We argue that current practice has outpaced the evidence specific to this population, and that closing this gap requires a Fontan-specific research agenda rather than continued extrapolation from adult heart failure trials.

articles.title: Preoperative prediction of complications after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: development and internal validation of a prediction model compared with generic risk scores.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate a preoperative model predicting postoperative complications after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), and to compare its performance with generic risk scores: the ASA Physical Status, ACS-NSQIP-type variables and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively collected, multicenter cohort of 683 patients undergoing RARP within a standardized digital perioperative pathway. The primary endpoint was any patient-reported complication within 90 days. An L1-penalized (LASSO) logistic regression model using 12 preoperative candidate predictors was developed on the full cohort and internally validated with 500 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination and calibration were compared with ASA, ACS-NSQIP-type variables and CCI. A simplified additive score was derived. Major complications (Clavien-Dindo) were analyzed as an exploratory endpoint.

RESULTS: Overall, 89/683 patients (13.0%) had a postoperative complication. Four predictors were mainly retained: previous anesthesia-related complications, inpatient pathway, previous surgery and diabetes. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.587 (apparent 0.637), comparable to ASA (0.600), ACS-NSQIP-type variables (0.610) and CCI (0.585). Calibration was good (corrected calibration slope 1.05). The simplified score (corrected AUC 0.594) identified groups with observed complication rates of 2.1%, 9.0%, 16.1% and 33.3%. For major complications (27 events), the score had an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.635 versus 0.585-0.599 for generic scores.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative variables alone, whether combined in a RARP-tailored model or in generic scores, predicted complications after RARP only to a limited extent. A simple four-item score identified risk groups with markedly different complication rates and may support counselling and postoperative monitoring.

articles.title: Efficacy of HER2-targeted therapies in localized urothelial carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugates were recently approved in China for treatment of advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC). We summarise emerging evidence supporting use of HER2-targeted regimens in patients with localized disease.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL through March 29, 2026, and SinoMed, Wanfang and CNKI through October 14, 2025 to identify studies evaluating HER2-targeted therapies, in patients with localized UC. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled response rates, including pathological complete response (pCR). Clinical complete response (cCR) was stratified by response definition. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochrane's Q test. Risk-of-bias (RoB) was assessed using ROBINS-I tool. The study was registered prospectively (CRD420250650326).

RESULTS: Thirty-three studies comprising 970 patients were included (17 prospective); 30 tested disitamab vedotin (DV). In 13 studies testing DV-containing regimens as neoadjuvant therapy, the pooled pCR rate was 48% (95% CI 39-58%, N = 398; 54% among surgery-evaluable patients). Evidence was insufficient to establish an association between HER2 expression and pCR (risk ratio [RR] 0.82, 95% CI 0.52-1.29; p = 0.38; N = 72). In bladder-sparing studies, cCR was 65% (95% CI 44-82%) with definitions requiring complete absence of residual tumor and 54% (95% CI 41-67%) with definitions permitting residual Ta/Tis disease. Among included trials using DV, rate of grade ≥3 adverse events did not exceed 35% and was lower than that reported in studies evaluating other HER2-targeted agents. Major RoB concerns regarded outcome measurement as none of included trials was blinded.

CONCLUSIONS: DV-containing regimens show promising activity as neoadjuvant therapy in patients with bladder cancer. Current evidence is insufficient to establish an association between HER2 expression and response. Emerging data indicate possible role in bladder-sparing setting with low rates of toxicity and no G5 safety signals, although heterogeneous cCR definitions limit interpretation.

articles.title: Post-mortem CT angiography for fatal vascular lesions in forensic death investigation: a systematic review of diagnostic performance, added value, and pitfalls.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Post-mortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is increasingly used in forensic death investigation to assess vascular disease, haemorrhage, and traumatic or natural vascular causes of death. However, its practical value depends on the lesion being investigated, the angiographic protocol, and the way imaging findings are integrated with autopsy and pathology. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance, added value, and main pitfalls of PMCTA for fatal vascular lesions.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane/CENTRAL were searched for human post-mortem studies evaluating PMCTA in forensic, medico-legal, coronial, or post-mortem settings. Eligible studies compared PMCTA with autopsy, histopathology, targeted vascular dissection, or autopsy-based consensus. Evidence was grouped according to practical forensic use, including coronary stenosis assessment, autopsy triage, global vascular lesion detection, haemorrhage-source localization, aortic or traumatic vascular injury assessment, coronary plaque characterization, and artifact-related pitfalls. Risk of bias was assessed using a QUADAS-2-based approach adapted to forensic PMCTA studies.

RESULTS: The available evidence did not support unrestricted pooling of all fatal vascular lesions. PMCTA was used for different forensic questions, and only coronary stenosis provided data close to conventional diagnostic accuracy assessment. In this domain, available studies showed high specificity but only moderate sensitivity for critical stenosis. Autopsy-triage studies suggested that PMCTA may reduce or guide invasive autopsy in selected adult coronial workflows. Global comparison studies showed added value for vascular lesion detection, and haemorrhage-source studies suggested that PMCTA may help localize bleeding vessels. Evidence on fatal coronary plaque characterization is emerging. Pitfall studies showed that post-mortem clots, incomplete vascular filling, contrast leakage, and extravasation artifacts may mimic or obscure vascular pathology.

CONCLUSION: PMCTA is best interpreted as a complementary tool in forensic vascular death investigation rather than as a general substitute for autopsy. Its contribution is strongest when it answers a specific vascular question, such as documenting coronary stenosis, guiding autopsy, mapping vascular lesions, localizing haemorrhage, or supporting targeted histopathology. Careful correlation with autopsy, pathology, case circumstances, and protocol-related artifacts remains essential.

articles.title: Primary Cardiac Lymphoma Presenting as Recurrent Pericardial Effusion and Tamponade: Diagnostic and Palliative Management Considerations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cardiac lymphoma is a rare cause of pericardial effusion and tamponade that can present without a solid mass.

CASE SUMMARY: An 85-year-old frail man with ischemic cardiomyopathy presented with tamponade from an isolated, rapidly enlarging hemorrhagic pericardial effusion. Fluid cytology and positron emission tomography-computed tomography confirmed human herpesvirus 8-negative, effusion-based large B-cell lymphoma. Given his high surgical risk and comorbidities, a tissue biopsy was avoided. He was managed with low-dose palliative chemotherapy and adjunctive intrapericardial triamcinolone, which successfully halted persistent high-output drain output, allowing safe pericardial drain removal and pericardial effusion control without invasive surgery.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that effusion-based lymphomas can occur without mass lesions or overt immunosuppression. It highlights the utility of fluid cytology over invasive biopsy in frail patients, and showcases intrapericardial steroids as a conservative tool to control refractory malignant drain output.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Conservative management of primary cardiac lymphoma combining systemic chemotherapy with intrapericardial steroids may help delay or avoid high-risk surgical procedures in frail patients.

articles.title: Giant Coronary Artery Aneurysm at the Left Main Bifurcation Managed With Stent-Assisted Endovascular Coil Embolization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Giant coronary artery aneurysms (CAAs), defined as exceeding 4 times the reference vessel diameter or 20 mm, are rare, with no randomized trials or guidelines directing treatment.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman with exertional angina was found to have a 30 mm giant CAA at the left main (LM) bifurcation with 70% mid-LM and ostial left anterior descending stenosis. Given poor surgical candidacy, a fully percutaneous approach was used: a drug-eluting stent was placed from the distal LM into the proximal left anterior descending, followed by stent-assisted coil embolization with 13 detachable coils. Final angiography showed no residual stenosis, near-complete aneurysm exclusion, and restoration of TIMI flow grade 3 in the left circumflex artery, suggesting the aneurysm had been causing coronary steal. The patient was discharged chest pain-free on dual antiplatelet therapy.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates stent-assisted coil embolization as a viable percutaneous option for giant LM bifurcation CAAs and highlights coronary steal as a potential consequence.

articles.title: The minimally invasive soft channel brain hemorrhage evacuation for acute basal ganglia hemorrhage - small hemorrhage evacuation (MIRACLE-S) trial: rationale, design and progress.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating type of stroke, where patients with small and large hematomas usually make excellent and poor outcomes, respectively, regardless of treatment. However, for patients with a moderate hematoma volume (20-30 mL) in a deep hemispheric location, there is clinical equipoise as to the benefit of any surgical intervention, as the randomized evidence is limited.

METHODS: The minimally invasive soft-channel brain hemorrhage evacuation for acute basal ganglia hemorrhage - small hemorrhage evacuation (MIRACLE-S) trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint assessed trial conducted in China. Eligibility criteria are adult patients aged 18 to 80 years with spontaneous basal ganglionic ICH with a hematoma volume of 20 to 30 mL, Glasgow coma scale score 9 to 14, premorbid modified Rankin scale score 0 to 1, and systolic blood pressure <140 mmHg enrolled within 48 hours of symptom onset. Patients are randomized (1:1) to soft-channel minimally invasive surgery (scMIS; stereotactic aspiration with catheter-based urokinase thrombolysis) or guideline-based conservative medical management. The primary efficacy outcome is a hierarchical composite endpoint of death, disability (mRS scores 3 to 5), rehospitalization, and poor health-related quality of life assessed at 180 days and analyzed using a win-ratio approach. Safety outcomes include mortality, rebleeding (including puncture-tract hemorrhage), and infection within 30 days.

RESULTS: Recruitment started January 1, 2025. As of January 10, 2026, 148 patients have been randomized at 34 active sites. The required sample size of 420 to detect a win-ratio effect size of 1.62 (P_tie=0.05) should be achieved in 2028.

CONCLUSION: MIRACLE-S will clarify whether aspiration-based scMIS improves recovery as compared with best medical management in patients moderate-volume basal ganglionic ICH, which is a common clinical burden in China and other regions with high rates of ICH.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06688162.

articles.title: Macular Microcirculation by OCT-A in Relation to Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy and Ocular Surface Biomarkers: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Ophthalmologica. Journal international d'ophtalmologie. International journal of ophthalmology. Zeitschrift fur Augenheilkunde
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), corneal sensitivity, and tear matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) with macular microcirculatory parameters assessed by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) in patients with diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 158 eyes of 79 patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing routine retinopathy screening at a single tertiary centre. Superficial capillary plexus vessel density and foveal avascular zone (FAZ) parameters (area, perimeter, and circularity index) were obtained by OCT-A (Cirrus 6000, AngioPlex®, Carl Zeiss Meditec). Corneal sensitivity was measured with the Brill esthesiometer and tear MMP-9 was assessed with the InflammaDry test. DPN was confirmed by electroneuromyography. Linear mixed models with random intercept per patient were applied to account for bilateral data.

RESULTS: Among OCT-A parameters, vessel density and FAZ area and perimeter did not show significant association with DPN status, MMP-9 positivity, or corneal sensitivity. FAZ circularity showed a significant negative association with DPN in the multivariable model (β = -0.07; p = 0.021) and with corneal sensitivity in the linear mixed model (β = 0.01; p = 0.049), but was not associated with MMP-9 status (p = 0.691). No OCT-A parameter was associated with MMP-9 in any analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: FAZ circularity was independently associated with DPN and with reduced corneal sensitivity, suggesting a potential retinal correlate of neurovascular damage in diabetes; however, this is a model-dependent, exploratory finding requiring prospective confirmation. No OCT-A parameter was associated with MMP-9 status, suggesting compartmental dissociation between anterior segment inflammation and posterior segment microvascular status at this disease stage.

articles.title: Exploiting New Opportunities to Deliver High Fibre in White Bread and Other Bakery Products.
articles.abstract: Dietary fibre (DF) is essential for health, with higher levels of DF consumption being associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer. However, most UK consumers fall far below the recommended dietary intake of 30 g of DF a day for adults. Wheat is an important source of DF, with white bread and other products made from white flour being most widely consumed. White bread is an excellent vehicle to deliver increased intake of DF, being widely available and consumed and affordable to all socio-economic groups. Modern elite bread wheat genotypes differ in their content of DF, particularly soluble DF, in white flour and wheat breeders are now able to select for higher DF in their breeding programmes. This paper is the outcome of a 1-day discussion meeting, which focused on identifying and removing barriers to the development and cultivation of wheat types with high fibre in white flour and the delivery of high fibre products to consumers and makes recommendations for future research.

articles.title: The prognostic value of the triglyceride-glucose index in individuals with hypertension.
articles.abstract: Hypertension frequently coexists with metabolic abnormalities that contribute to cardiovascular risk. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance that may also reflect early cardiometabolic and cardiovascular vulnerability. This narrative review examines the prognostic relevance of TyG for all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and fatal or non-fatal cardiovascular events in hypertension. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 5 October 2026, without date or language restrictions. Evidence from primary hypertensive cohorts generally supports associations between higher TyG and adverse outcomes, although their magnitude and shape vary, with both linear and nonlinear patterns reported. Findings are most consistent among hypertensive patients with diabetes, whereas results from other high-risk settings and hypertension-specific subgroup analyses are more heterogeneous. Differences in TyG calculation, modeling, glycemic status, clinical settings, and overlapping cohorts complicate comparisons across studies. Overall, TyG may represent a readily available, low-cost marker of early cardiometabolic and cardiovascular vulnerability, beyond its role as a surrogate of insulin resistance, with potential to refine cardiovascular risk stratification in hypertension. Further prospective validation should establish its incremental predictive value beyond conventional cardiovascular risk factors and established risk scores.

articles.title: Evaluation of a novel transseptal puncture device for use in cardiac procedures requiring left atrial access.
articles.abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is the first step in percutaneous left-heart interventions including atrial fibrillation ablation, left atrial appendage occlusion, and percutaneous mitral valve repair/replacement. Current TSP techniques remain limited by suboptimal imaging visualization, lack of precise control over puncture sites, and a steep learning curve. The Protaryx transseptal puncture device was designed to address these limitations by incorporating a novel atraumatic highly echogenic deployable and retractable nitinol mesh end effector mounted on an extendable catheter. The key advantages of the Protaryx TSP device are the maneuverability of the extendable catheter and the visibility of the end effector that combine to enable precise targeting of the fossa ovalis during TSP. Here, we provide an overview of challenges with transseptal puncture, an overview of the Protaryx device, and early clinical evidence. This includes results of the 5-patient prospective non-randomized observational first-in-human experience with the Protaryx TSP catheter. This study demonstrated early feasibility and safety, with rapid on-target puncture of the fossa ovalis, zero adverse events, and 100% success of structural heart interventions following TSP. The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of the Protaryx device has increased options for interventional cardiologists and electrophysiologists seeking to streamline left-sided structural heart intervention.

articles.title: Points to consider on the impact of the 21st Century Cures Act Final Rule and information blocking on genomic medicine: A statement of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG).
authors: ACMG Ethical, Legal, and Social Issues Committee
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics

articles.title: Nursing Care for Managing Excess Fluid Volume (00026) in Chronic Kidney Disease Hemodialysis Patients: An Integrative Review.
articles.abstract: IntroChronic kidney disease affects 8-16% of the global population and is the seventh leading risk factor for mortality worldwide. An estimated 850 million people live with kidney disease, primarily in low- and middle-income countries. The rising prevalence of this disease is driven by rapid population growth, aging, and the dual burden of infectious and noncommunicable diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension. In advanced stages, hemodialysis remains the most common renal replacement therapy, accounting for approximately 88% of treatments worldwide. Thus, this study aims to present the main nursing interventions, activities, and outcomes related to the nursing diagnosis Excess Fluid Volume, identified through an integrative literature review.MethodsIntegrative literature review was conducted using a systematic and rigorous methodological approach. Searches were performed in the following databases: Virtual Health Library (VHL), Cochrane Library, Excerpta Medica Database (Embase), Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), PubMed, SciVerse Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), Web of Science, Nursing Database (BDENF), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), Spanish Bibliographic Index in Health Sciences (IBECS), and ProQuest LLC.ResultsThe review included 13 studies that identified key nursing care related to the diagnosis Excess Fluid Volume. Main interventions involved nursing consultation, clinical follow-up, fluid management, and health education focused on self-care and treatment adherence. Activities emphasize monitoring vital signs, weight, edema, and fluid balance, as well as medication and diet guidance. Reported outcomes included improved fluid and blood pressure control, reduced hypervolemia and symptoms, greater adherence to therapeutic regimens, prevention of cardiovascular complications, and decreased morbidity and mortality.ConclusionThe care for this population extends beyond clinical assessment, encompassing health education, self-care promotion, and complication prevention. Such nursing interventions strengthen treatment adherence, maintain hemodynamic stability, and minimize adverse events.

articles.title: Long-term Electroclinical Outcomes After Herpes Simplex Virus Encephalitis: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveHerpes simplex virus encephalitis (HSVE) remains an important cause of severe sporadic encephalitis. Electrographic seizures and status epilepticus may be underrecognized during the acute phase, and their relationship with long-term outcome is incompletely defined. We aimed to describe acute EEG abnormalities and long-term seizure and cognitive outcomes in adults with HSVE.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed adults hospitalized with HSVE in the neurology ward or neurological intensive care unit between 2013 and 2022. Demographic and clinical characteristics, MRI findings, routine or continuous video-EEG findings, antiseizure treatments, and long-term outcomes were obtained from electronic health records and the EEG archive.ResultsNine patients (7 men; age range: 30-77 years) were included. Altered mental status was the most frequent presenting feature, and 3 patients had clinical seizures at presentation. MRI abnormalities were bilateral in 4 patients. EEG showed lateralized periodic discharges in 5 patients, electrographic status epilepticus in 4, and electrographic seizures not meeting status criteria in 1. Median follow-up was 8 years (range: 4-13 years). No patient with available follow-up reported recurrent clinical seizures after discharge. Mood and/or cognitive complaints were present in 6 of 8 patients with evaluable long-term clinical data.ConclusionIn this neurologically selected HSVE cohort, electrographic seizures and status epilepticus were frequent despite clinical seizures being documented in only one-third of patients at presentation. Long-term clinical seizure control was favorable under continued antiseizure treatment, whereas cognitive and mood complaints remained common. Larger studies using systematic continuous EEG and standardized neuropsychological assessment are needed.

articles.title: Author reply to comments on "Predicting mental health-related sick leave using stress check data: development and validation of a workplace risk model".
Endothelial and Hemostatic Molecular Markers Associated With 28-Day Mortality in Sepsis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSepsis-associated coagulopathy involves disturbances in coagulation, fibrinolysis, endogenous anticoagulant pathways, and endothelial function that may not be fully characterized by routine coagulation tests or clinical severity scores. Molecular biomarkers may provide complementary information about these processes.ObjectivesTo evaluate the associations of selected endothelial and hemostatic molecular biomarkers with 28-day mortality and determine how their prognostic performance relates to established measures of illness severity in adults with sepsis and septic shock.MethodsIn this single-center analysis of prospectively collected data, 54 adults with sepsis or septic shock underwent clinical assessment and measurement of t-PAIC, TAT, sTM, PIC, and antithrombin activity on the day of enrollment. Biomarkers were log2-transformed, and associations with 28-day mortality were evaluated using logistic regression with separate adjustment for SOFA or APACHE II; Firth regression was used in sensitivity analyses.ResultsSeventeen patients (31.5%) died within 28 days. All five biomarkers were associated with mortality in unadjusted analyses. t-PAIC and sTM remained associated after adjustment for either SOFA or APACHE II, while TAT and PIC remained associated only after APACHE II adjustment. Antithrombin activity was not associated after severity adjustment. Among individual biomarkers, t-PAIC showed the highest discrimination (AUC, 0.866; 95% CI, 0.768-0.965), whereas SOFA had the highest overall discrimination (AUC, 0.933; 95% CI, 0.863-1.000).ConclusionsEndothelial and hemostatic biomarkers were associated with 28-day mortality, with t-PAIC and sTM showing the most consistent adjusted associations. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings and determine whether these biomarkers can improve biological phenotyping and risk assessment beyond established severity measures.

articles.title: Balancing Security, Autonomy, and Dignity at the End of Life in Forensic Psychiatry: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAs forensic psychiatric populations age, clinicians are increasingly required to manage advanced medical illness and end-of-life care within secure psychiatric environments. The intersection of terminal illness, forensic detention, Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD), and palliative care remains poorly described in the literature.Case PresentationWe describe the case of an adult forensic psychiatric inpatient detained under the Criminal Code of Canada who experienced progressive endstage alcohol-related liver disease complicated by hepatocellular carcinoma, hepatic encephalopathy, and increasing physical frailty. Despite longstanding psychiatric stability, his evolving medical needs required extensive collaboration among forensic psychiatry, hospital medicine, hepatology, radiation oncology, palliative care, nursing, pharmacy, occupational therapy, social work, and biomedical ethics. Throughout his illness, he consistently expressed goals emphasizing comfort, dignity, and quality of life, ultimately requesting MAiD.ConclusionIn this case, we highlight the unique clinical, ethical, and operational challenges of providing end-of-life care within forensic psychiatric settings. This case underscores the need for integrated forensic-medical models that can reconcile therapeutic security requirements with the principles of person-centered palliative care, ensuring dignity, autonomy, timely access to specialized palliative services, and appropriate support for complex capacity and MAiD related decisions. As medically frail forensic populations continue to age, healthcare systems must develop policies, infrastructure, and interdisciplinary models of care that better address the intersection of forensic psychiatry, complex medical illness, and end-of-life care.

articles.title: A practical primer on FLIM and FRET-FLIM for quantitative bioimaging.
articles.abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) measures the fluorescence decay time of a fluorophore and can therefore provide information that is not available from fluorescence intensity alone. Changes in lifetime can report on the local molecular environment and, through Förster resonance energy transfer measured by FLIM (FRET-FLIM), on interactions occurring over nanometre length scales. In this primer, we describe the basic principles of FLIM and FRET-FLIM and introduce two widely used time-domain acquisition approaches: time-correlated single-photon counting and time-gated detection. We then consider practical aspects of planning a FLIM experiment, including fluorophore choice, photon statistics, instrument response, sample preparation, and the challenges associated with imaging live and three-dimensional specimens. Three applications are used to illustrate how lifetime measurements can be applied in biological experiments: label-free metabolic imaging using NAD(P)H and FAD, intramolecular FRET biosensors that report conformational or signalling changes, and intermolecular FRET-FLIM for studying protein-protein interactions. We also discuss commonly used analysis approaches, available software, and routes through which researchers can access FLIM instrumentation. The final section considers current efforts to improve measurement standardisation and analysis, together with the growing use of computational methods and the combination of FLIM with other microscopy modalities.

articles.title: Cross-ancestry proteome-wide mendelian randomization of plasma proteins and breast cancer susceptibility.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The plasma proteome may help connect inherited breast cancer susceptibility to biologically interpretable and potentially actionable pathways, but proteome-wide evidence across ancestries remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses of breast cancer risk using cis-protein quantitative trait loci for 1,962 distinct plasma proteins from 34,557 European-ancestry participants in the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project. Breast cancer genome-wide association studies included 156,901 cases and 204,634 controls of European, East Asian, and African ancestries. Ancestry-specific MR estimates were combined by fixed-effects meta-analysis. Candidate proteins were further evaluated through subtype-specific and reverse-direction MR analyses, statistical colocalization, replication in independent European and East Asian proteomic datasets, and analyses of associations between protein polygenic scores and breast cancer status in All of Us.

RESULTS: Twelve proteins achieved Bonferroni significance in the cross-ancestry meta-analysis (P < 0.05/1,971 tests), including eight previously reported proteins and four newly prioritized by MR. DNPH1 showed cross-ancestry heterogeneity, while CASP8, RALB, and USP28 showed cross-subtype heterogeneity after accounting for shared controls (all P < 0.05/12). Complementary support varied: six candidates showed strong colocalization (PPH4 ≥ 0.80); four replicated with a consistent direction and nominal significance in deCODE, two in the Japan COVID-19 Task Force, and four in All of Us (all P < 0.05). The strongest cumulative support was observed for LRRC25, PARK7, and LRRC37A2.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings prioritize circulating protein candidates for mechanistic, prevention-oriented, and translational follow-up in breast cancer, while underscoring the need for larger ancestrally diverse proteomic resources to support equitable target and biomarker discovery.

articles.title: Handling of the Non-Assessable Verbal Glasgow Coma Scale and Computed Illness Severity in Critically Ill Adults with Acute Brain Injury: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) contributes to illness-severity scores. The verbal component cannot be observed in intubated patients; the MIMIC Code Repository sets "No Response-ETT" rows to a total of 15.ObjectiveTo quantify non-assessable verbal GCS examinations and describe how their handling changes computed severity, the analyzed population and mortality-model performance.Materials and MethodsRetrospective MIMIC-IV cohort (Boston, 2008 to 2022) of adults with acute brain injury (first intensive care unit stay per hospitalization); a "No Response-ETT" verbal entry was non-assessable. Five GCS derivation strategies were compared; four used the lowest eye-plus-motor examination of the first 24 h. The eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; United States, 2014 to 2015) supported replication.ResultsOf 14,230 stays, 45.2% had a non-assessable verbal examination; 47.5% of ventilated stays had none assessable in the first 24 h. A non-assessable lowest examination was associated with mechanical ventilation (adjusted odds ratio, 32.8; 95% CI, 27.8 to 38.6). The official first-day GCS was 15 in 44.7% of 14 215 stays; 94.1% of default-rule totals of 15 were incompatible with the eye-plus-motor sum charted at that examination. With one mortality-model specification refitted per GCS derivation on the same stays, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.749 (95% CI, 0.739 to 0.760) with the official first-day GCS and 0.820 (0.812 to 0.828) with an eye-and-motor (Brennan) estimate. Complete-case analysis excluded 5509 of 14 192 stays and 72.8% of deaths. In eICU-CRD, stays with an unscored GCS component had higher mortality (16.6% vs 9.2%), but totals of 12 or more were no more frequent after the first documented ventilation entry (17.3%) than before (19.5%).ConclusionIn this cohort, how a non-assessable verbal GCS was handled changed computed severity and the analyzed population. Studies and benchmarks that use GCS-based severity should report the handling rule.

articles.title: Construction and Validation of a Prediction Model for TACE Resistance in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Based on Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Radiomics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To construct and validate a contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) radiomics-clinical model for predicting transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

METHODS: A total of 168 HCC patients who underwent CEUS on two vendor platforms (Philips E9 and GE Logiq E95) were split into a training set (n = 118) and an internal validation set (n = 50), with an additional 80 patients forming an external validation cohort. For each patient, 2D regions of interest were manually delineated on the largest cross-sectional slice of each CEUS phase. Radiomic features were extracted and screened by LASSO regression; the twelve retained features were linearly combined into a single Rad-score. The Rad-score and three prespecified clinical risk factors (tumor size, Child-Pugh class, AFP) confirmed by multivariate analysis were combined into a parsimonious logistic regression (LR) model with four predictors in total. Performance was assessed by ROC curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA), subgroup analysis, and prospective validation.

RESULTS: The combined model had AUCs of 0.895, 0.891 and 0.846 in three sets, with subgroup AUCs >0.86. Prospective validation showed TACE plus sorafenib improved 6-month response rate from 26.7% to 53.3% for high-risk patients.

CONCLUSION: The CEUS radiomics-clinical model accurately predicts TACE resistance, guiding individualized HCC treatment.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This model integrates CEUS multi-phase radiomics and clinical factors, outperforming single clinical/radiomic models. Strict multi-step screening and comprehensive validation avoid data leakage, ensuring robust prediction and clinical translatability.

articles.title: Dynamic blood glucose trajectory is 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure: A survival prediction analysis.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a global public health issue. Blood glucose influences HF progression, but research on its dynamic changes and mortglity remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the association of baseline admission blood glucose and its dynamic changes with all-cause mortality in patients with HF.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used data from MIMIC-IV and a tertiary hospital. We identified distinct glycemic trajectories using group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) and assessed their association with 28-day all-cause mortality via Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Machine learning models were applied to evaluate the predictive value of glycemia.ResultsA total of 6142 patients from the MIMIC-IV database and 391 local patients were included. Results showed that five dynamic blood glucose trajectory groups were identified. Among them, the moderate-to-high and high-level groups exhibited elevated mortality risk [HR (95% CI): 1.546 (1.231-1.942); 1.572 (1.140-2.168)]. Incorporating blood glucose trajectories into predictive models moderately improved the predictive performance for outcomes, and the Deepsurv model demonstrated better predictive accuracy and stability.ConclusionAlthough current retrospective design limits causal inference and warrants prospective validation, the present study provides evidence that dynamic blood glucose fluctuations demonstrate superior prognostic value compared to baseline measurements for predicting mortality in severe HF patients. Furthermore, machine learning based on glucose trajectory modeling enables early identification of high-risk individuals.

articles.title: Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and two-sample Mendelian randomization reveal CD4+ T cell-expressed COMT and JUN as shared candidate genes for Alzheimer's disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are high-burden diseases; T2DM independently elevates AD risk via shared pathogenesis, yet their shared peripheral immune pathways and genetically supported cell-specific targets remain undefined.ObjectiveTo identify shared immune subsets, key genes and candidate compounds for AD and T2DM via integrated scRNA-seq and two-sample Mendelian randomization.MethodsWe constructed an integrated multi-omics framework combining peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and two-sample Mendelian randomization (2SMR) using 10 public GEO datasets, with core analyses covering cell annotation, cell-cell communication profiling, differential expression analysis, eQTL-based 2SMR, in silico gene function prediction, and molecular docking with dynamics simulation for compound screening.ResultsCD4+ T cells were inferred as the most abundant adaptive immune subset and a potential intercellular communication hub in peripheral blood of both AD and T2DM. Dual scRNA-seq/2SMR screening identified consistently upregulated shared candidate genes COMT and JUN, validated at single-cell and bulk transcriptome levels; myricetin and tauroursodeoxycholic acid were screened as candidate compounds with high predicted binding affinity to the encoded proteins. The 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation confirmed favorable structural stability of the COMT-myricetin complex (RMSD ∼1.2 Å).ConclusionsAs an exploratory bioinformatics investigation, this study proposes a testable hypothesis that CD4+ T cells and the COMT/JUN axis may act as a potential shared immune regulatory node in the concurrent pathogenesis of AD and T2DM, differing from the canonical T cell-driven pathological process in classic autoimmune diseases. All findings remain preliminary and require dedicated experimental validation.

articles.title: The p.Ser143Pro lamin A/C mutation leads to dilated cardiomyopathy and activates the unfolded protein response pathway in a knock-in mouse model.
articles.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by progressive ventricular dilation, systolic dysfunction, and an increased risk of arrythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. Variants in the LMNA gene, which encodes the nuclear lamins A and C, have been linked to the familial form of the disease and the founder variant p.Ser143Pro is particularly common among Finnish patients with DCM. To elucidate the complex and poorly understood pathogenic mechanisms behind LMNA-related DCM, we generated a mouse model carrying the p.Ser143Pro mutation in the Lmna gene. All genetically modified mice appeared normal at birth. However, based on echocardiography, necropsy, natriuretic peptide B (Nppb) expression levels, and histopathological data, homozygous males developed progressive left ventricular dilatation, myocardial fibrosis, and cardiac failure after 6 months of age, with all succumbing before 10 months. A reduced disease penetrance was observed in heterozygous male and homozygous female mice, with one-year survival rates of 40% and 60%, respectively. No signs of skeletal myopathy were observed in mice carrying the mutation. Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing analysis of left ventricular cardiac tissue from asymptomatic two-month-old homozygous male mice revealed an upregulation of classical heart failure markers, such as natriuretic peptide A (Nppa) and myosin heavy chain 7 (Myh7), and an elevated unfolded protein response signaling, as shown by elevated DNA damage inducible transcript 3 (Ddit3), BAG cochaperone 3 (Bag3) and CCAAT enhancer binding protein beta (Cebpb) levels. In conclusion, p.Ser143Pro-Lmna mice closely mimic the clinical phenotype observed in patients with the p.Ser143Pro LMNA variant and offer a valuable in vivo model for investigating the underlying pathogenic mechanisms of LMNA-related DCM. © 2026 The Author(s). The Journal of Pathology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

articles.title: Development of Prediction Model of Diabetes Self-Management Core Behaviours Based on Deep Learning.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to develop a predictive model for diabetes self-management (DSM) using a fully connected neural network (FCNN) architecture. The model's performance was rigorously evaluated using key metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC).

DESIGN: A quantitative, multicenter cross-sectional design.

METHODS: A systematic literature review identified key psychosocial factors and corresponding validated scales, which formed the initial item pool. A multicenter cross-sectional study was then conducted to collect data on these items from 2005 participants across five research centers in Hainan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, and Henan provinces. We chose to develop an FCNN model over traditional approaches including logistic regression and random forest, as it could automatically capture complex, non-linear relationships among predictors without manual feature engineering. Using this model for gradient-based feature importance ranking, we selected the most predictive items from the initial pool following preliminary screening of overlapping items. After feature selection, the model was retrained using the selected features, with 80% of the data allocated for training and 20% for testing. Finally, model performance was validated through a two-week prospective observational study.

RESULTS: Twenty-four out of 99 candidate variables were identified as model characteristics for predicting DSM behaviours. The model demonstrated strong performance across all four self-management domains. For healthy eating, the accuracy, precision, recall, and AUC were 83.34%, 88.56%, 90.05%, and 0.84%, respectively. For medication adherence, these values were 82.14%, 86.60%, 90.27%, and 0.84%, respectively. For regular exercise, they were 82.39%, 82.89%, 86.09%, and 0.89%, respectively. For blood glucose monitoring, they were 83.39%, 85.45%, 89.72%, and 0.87%, respectively. The prospective validation cohort (n = 50) further confirmed the model's robust performance, yielding AUCs of 0.84, 0.82, 0.83, and 0.89 for diet, exercise, blood glucose monitoring, and medication adherence, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The FCNN-based predictive model demonstrated promising performance in forecasting DSM behaviours, with particularly strong discriminative ability as evidenced by high accuracy and AUC values. These findings suggest that deep learning approaches incorporating psychosocial and clinical variables may help predict DSM behaviours, although the model requires further validation before it can be considered a clinical tool for personalized diabetes care. Although the prospective validation results are encouraging, they should be interpreted as preliminary given the limited sample size (n = 50); larger-scale, multicenter external validation studies are warranted to further confirm the model's generalizability and clinical applicability.

IMPACT: Predicting core diabetes self-management behaviours using an FCNN may provide useful insights into individualized adherence patterns and could inform targeted, stepped-care interventions, although further validation is needed before clinical application.

REPORTING METHOD: The reporting of this cross-sectional study followed the STROBE guideline.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus contributed to this study by completing questionnaires during the model development phase (n = 2005) and by participating in the prospective validation phase (n = 50). No patients or public members were involved in study design, data analysis, or interpretation of results. Study findings will be disseminated to participants through their respective endocrinology departments.

articles.title: Urinary peptidomic classifier for the non-invasive diagnosis of Alport syndrome.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Alport syndrome (AS) is an inherited glomerular disease that often presents with non-specific clinical and histological features overlapping with other forms of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Consequently, AS may remain unrecognised or misclassified, particularly where genetic testing is unavailable and biopsy is delayed or infeasible. We hypothesised that a non-invasive urinary peptide signature can distinguish AS from other CKD aetiologies, patients with diabetes and healthy individuals.

METHODS: In this multicentre study, we included 165 adults with genetically confirmed AS. Comparator groups comprised patients with non-Alport CKD, diabetes and healthy individuals, matched to the AS cohort by age, sex and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Urinary peptide profiles were generated by capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry. Group differences in peptide abundance were analysed, and a supervised multipeptide classifier specific for AS was constructed and evaluated in matched test cohorts and in two external validation cohorts: 145 patients with IgA nephropathy (IgAN) and 15 further patients with AS.

RESULTS: We identified 419 urinary peptides that differed between AS and comparator groups, of which 178 were incorporated into the AS-specific classifier Alport178. In matched test cohorts, Alport178 achieved an AUC of 0.999 (95% CI 0.997-1.00), with 100% sensitivity for AS and high specificity in CKD, diabetic and healthy control groups. In external validation cohorts, the classifier identified most AS cases and classified the majority of IgAN patients as non-Alport. The most informative peptides were predominantly collagen alpha chain fragments.

CONCLUSION: A urinary peptidomic classifier specific for AS enables differentiation of AS from other CKD entities, patients with diabetes, healthy individuals and IgAN. This non-invasive approach may facilitate earlier recognition of AS, reduce the need for invasive diagnostic procedures and prioritise patients for confirmatory genetic testing and targeted management.

articles.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
authors: International League Against Epilepsy Acute Symptomatic Seizure Task Force
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. We aimed to characterize international variation in ASyS management across common etiologies.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey through the International League Against Epilepsy national chapters (February to May 2025). Five etiology-based vignettes assessed clinical and electrographic ASyS scenario after ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), meningitis, hyponatremia, and alcohol withdrawal. Respondents who managed neonatal seizures completed a neonatal stroke vignette. We assessed antiseizure medication (ASM) initiation, duration after clinical ASyS, and continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) use. Interrespondent variability was quantified by normalized Shannon entropy (H'). Multivariable generalized estimating equations accounted for repeated responses.

RESULTS: Among 963 respondents (92 countries), 62% recommended ASM initiation in clinical and 61% in electrographic ASyS scenarios. Overall ASM initiation variability was high (H' = .96), highest for alcohol withdrawal (H' = 1.0), followed by stroke (H' > .9), and consistently higher for electrographic than clinical ASyS. Etiology was the strongest driver of ASM initiation. Compared with stroke, ASM initiation odds were higher for TBI (odds ratio [OR] = 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.2-2.8) and meningitis (OR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.7-2.2), and lower for hyponatremia (OR = .2, 95% CI = .2-.2) and alcohol withdrawal (OR = .5, 95% CI = .5-.6). Compared with Europe, initiation odds were higher in North America (OR = 2.7, 95% CI = 2.0-3.6), Asia-Oceania (OR = 2.4, 95% CI = 2.0-3.0), and Latin America (OR = 2.0, 95% CI = 1.5-2.7), but not Africa. These differences persisted after accounting for country income. Compared with stroke, the mean ASM duration was 3.2 months shorter for hyponatremia and .6 months longer for TBI. Alcohol withdrawal durations were polarized (41% discontinued at discharge; 20% continued >12 months). cEEG use was markedly higher in North America than Europe (OR = 11.3, 95% CI = 7.8-16.5). Among 291 neonatal respondents, 75% continued ASM beyond discharge.

SIGNIFICANCE: ASyS management varies markedly, reaching near-maximal heterogeneity in several common scenarios. Although etiology drives decisions, geography and provider characteristics also influence care, underscoring an urgent need for randomized trials and international consensus guidance to harmonize care.

articles.title: Nicotinamide riboside protects mouse kidneys from heat injury through inhibition of inflammation, oxidative stress, and hypoxia response.
articles.abstract: Supplementation with nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) precursors such as nicotinamide riboside (NR) has been shown to offer protection in experimental models of ischaemic kidney injury. Heat stress can significantly reduce renal blood flow and increase the risk of kidney injury. In this study, we aimed to investigate whether NR supplementation provides renoprotection against heat stress. Male mice were administered NR daily for 10 days before undergoing a heat exposure experiment. NR enhanced kidney NAD+ content. Compared to vehicle controls, NR improved histological signs of tubular impairment and lowered plasma urea nitrogen and creatinine levels in heat-exposed mice. NR also reduced the levels of IL-6, TNFα, TBARS, HIF-1α, and TRPM7, and increased the level of the NAD+ biosynthetic enzyme NAMPT in kidney tissues. Our results demonstrate that NR can prevent heat-induced acute kidney injury in mice. This study expands the list of potential renoprotection targets against heat stress.

articles.title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Determinants of Treatment Adherence and Illness Acceptance in Patients With Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To identify the sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with adherence to blood pressure-lowering treatment and with illness acceptance in adults with hypertension attending specialist outpatient care.

DESIGN: Single-centre cross-sectional study.

METHODS: We studied 229 adults with physician-diagnosed hypertension attending routine follow-up visits at a specialist hypertension clinic. Adherence was measured with the Hill-Bone Compliance to High Blood Pressure Therapy Scale and illness acceptance with the Acceptance of Illness Scale (AIS). Two multivariable linear regression models with the same 11 sociodemographic and clinical predictors were fitted.

REPORTING METHOD: STROBE.

RESULTS: Treatment adherence and illness acceptance were moderately correlated. Medication burden was the only factor independently associated with both poorer treatment adherence and lower illness acceptance. Better adherence was also associated with a higher number of comorbidities, rural residence, and a family history of hypertension, although the latter two associations were less robust after adjustment for multiple testing. Patients with the highest medication burden had the poorest adherence and the lowest illness acceptance.

CONCLUSION: Adherence and illness acceptance are related but distinct aspects of living with hypertension. The number of medications was the only factor independently associated with both outcomes, suggesting that medication burden should be considered in individualised care.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Assessing adherence and illness acceptance together may help nurses to separate patients who need education about their treatment from those who need psychological support or a simpler regimen.

IMPACT: Adherence and illness acceptance had different determinant profiles in patients with hypertension, with medication burden as the only factor common to both. The findings support individualised nursing assessment and multidisciplinary management of hypertension.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients completed validated questionnaires and provided clinical information during routine outpatient visits. They were not involved in the study design, data analysis, interpretation or manuscript preparation.

articles.title: Massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (Breus' mole): A nationwide retrospective study in Japan.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence, diagnostic features, and perinatal outcomes of massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (MST) in Japan.

METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective study (2018-2023) analyzed confirmed cases of MST, defined as a laminated hematoma with a maximum thickness ≥1 cm. Maternal characteristics, sonographic patterns, and perinatal complications were evaluated.

RESULTS: Of 346 741 deliveries across 87 tertiary perinatal centers, 69 pathologically confirmed MST cases were identified at 27 centers, yielding an incidence of 0.019% (69/346 741). Median maternal age was 33 years and body mass index (BMI) was 21.1. Chronic hypertension was present in 8.7% (6/69). Diagnoses occurred antenatally in 81.2% (56/69) and postpartum in 18.8% (13/69). Ultrasound findings included placentomegaly or a placental mass with variable echogenicity. During follow-up, echogenicity changed in 28% of cases and lesion size in 57%. Perinatal outcomes included induced abortion in 13.0% (9/69), miscarriage before 22 weeks in 5.8% (4/69), stillbirth in 7.2% (5/69), preterm birth in 52.2% (36/69), and term delivery in 21.7% (15/69). Among preterm births, one neonatal death and two infant deaths occurred. After excluding induced abortion and miscarriage before 22 weeks, small-for-gestational-age status was present in 53.6% (30/56) of infants, pre-eclampsia occurred in 16.1% (9/56), and preterm premature rupture of membranes occurred in 23.2% (13/56). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was required for 82.4% (42/51) of live births.

CONCLUSION: MST is a rare but high-risk placental disorder associated with miscarriage, stillbirth, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth, and pre-eclampsia. When MST is suspected antenatally, close maternal and fetal surveillance is warranted.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of teneligliptin as add-on therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes treated with empagliflozin and metformin: A 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study investigated the efficacy and safety of teneligliptin as an add-on therapy in Korean patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with empagliflozin and metformin.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, participants with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels 7.0-10.5% treated with empagliflozin 10 mg plus metformin (≥1,000 mg/day) were randomly assigned to receive teneligliptin 20 mg once daily (n = 116) or placebo (n = 119). The primary endpoint was the change in HbA1c from baseline at week 24, and secondary endpoints included changes in fasting plasma glucose (FPG), achievement rate of target HbA1c, and metabolic parameters.

RESULTS: At week 24, the teneligliptin group showed a significant reduction in HbA1c compared with the placebo group (least-squares mean difference -0.69%; 95% confidence interval -0.83 to -0.54; P < 0.0001). The proportion of participants achieving HbA1c < 7.0% was significantly higher in the teneligliptin group (59.5% vs 21.9%; P < 0.0001). Teneligliptin also resulted in significant reductions in FPG and glycated albumin compared with placebo. The treatment was well tolerated, with no significant difference in the incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events between the groups.

DISCUSSION: The addition of teneligliptin to empagliflozin and metformin therapy resulted in a significant improvement in glycemic control with a favorable safety profile in Korean patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with the dual therapy. Teneligliptin can be a viable option for patients who do not achieve adequate glycemic control with empagliflozin and metformin.

articles.title: Strengths and weaknesses in epilepsy training across residency programs in Italy: A multicenter survey by the Italian chapter of the Young Epilepsy Section (YES-I).
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of the study was to assess epilepsy-related services across Italian neurology and child neuropsychiatry residency programs, evaluate residents and early-career specialists' perceived strengths/weaknesses in epilepsy training, and identify unmet needs and expectations for improving residency programs and Young Epilepsy Section (YES)-Italy educational initiatives.

METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and April 2026 by a focus group of the YES-Italy Education Task Force. A structured questionnaire was distributed to neurology and child neuropsychiatry residents and specialists within 2 years of completing residency, assessing demographics, epilepsy-related services, self-perceived competencies, training strengths and limitations, and suggestions for improving residency curricula with YES-Italy educational activities. Descriptive statistics were used; group comparisons (neurology vs. child neuropsychiatry; residents vs. early-career specialists) employed the Mann-Whitney U test.

RESULTS: The survey was completed by 150 participants. Epilepsy training was widely available (85.3%) but variable and often brief (<6 months). EEG training was mostly embedded within epilepsy rotation (32.7%), organized as a distinct brief rotation (<3 months; 33.3%), or not available (19.3%). Core epilepsy services were widely present (inpatient wards 82.7%; neurophysiology laboratories 93.3%), while other services were less common (such as epilepsy surgery). Marked variability in Status Epilepticus management emerged across centers. Participants perceived adequate competence for core clinical-diagnostic domains, but lower competence for EEG interpretation and complementary disciplines. Perceived competence was higher in chronic than in acute care. Child neuropsychiatrists reported greater competence in neuropsychology and genetics, neurologists in neuroimaging and acute management. Clinical rotations and multidisciplinary case discussions were major strengths, whereas lectures and direct teaching required improvement. Suggestions for the YES-I group highlighted improving EEG training, structured educational initiatives, access to courses, webinars, and scientific materials.

SIGNIFICANCE: This survey highlights substantial heterogeneity and weaknesses in Italian epilepsy training, particularly regarding EEG interpretation, complementary diagnostics, and acute management, underscoring the need for national standardization, multidisciplinary educational pathways, and strengthened educational initiatives.

Outcomes of acute ischemic stroke and reperfusion therapy in patients with Moyamoya disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is an uncommon cerebrovascular condition associated with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracranial hemorrhage. This study examines outcomes of AIS in patients with MMD (MMD-AIS) and associated outcomes of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and intravascular thrombolysis (IVT).

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional analysis used the National Inpatient Sample database (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years-old) U.S. hospitalizations for AIS with reported NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS). Inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted for confounding factors. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 1,733,390 AIS hospitalizations, 3,735 (0.2%) involved comorbid MMD; 150 (4.0%) underwent EVT while 300 (8.0%) received IVT. MMD was associated with reduced use of EVT (aOR: 0.362, 95% CI [0.238-0.553], p < 0.001) and IVT (0.315 [0.242-0.412], p < 0.001) compared with non-MMD AIS. Following IPTW, MMD was associated with similar inpatient mortality (1.29 [0.797-2.09], p = 0.299), reduced routine discharge (0.639 [0.540-0.757], p < 0.001), and similar hemorrhagic transformation (1.13 [0.742-1.74], p = 0.560). Among the MMD-AIS group with NIHSS > 5, EVT was not associated with differences in routine discharge (0.672 [0.398-1.14], p = 0.137), inpatient mortality (0.072 [0.004-1.20], p = 0.067), or hemorrhagic transformation (1.61 [0.896-2.88], p = 0.111). IVT was associated with increased routine discharge (1.96 [1.35-2.85], p < 0.001), and no difference in hemorrhagic transformation (0.948 [0.542-1.66], p = 0.852) or mortality (1.74 [0.811-3.75], p = 0.155).

DISCUSSION: MMD-AIS was associated with reduced routine discharge without increased hemorrhagic risk. EVT and IVT were infrequently used but may be feasible in selected patients. Prospective studies are needed to determine the efficacy of reperfusion therapy in this population.

articles.title: Alcohol and cardiovascular disease: inter-organ crosstalk, microvascular dysfunction, and cardiovascular ageing.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-related cardiovascular risk is being fundamentally reappraised. Observational associations suggesting cardioprotection with light-to-moderate drinking have been challenged by contemporary cohort analyses, Mendelian-randomization studies, biomarker-informed investigations, and updated public-health guidance. Uncertainty nevertheless persists at very low exposure levels and for selected coronary or all-cause outcomes. Alcohol is therefore best viewed as a dose-, pattern-, and host-dependent cardiovascular stressor. Acute or binge drinking, sustained heavy intake, chronic intake with episodic binges, and withdrawal produce overlapping but distinct phenotypes, including hypertension, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden death, alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy, heart failure, stroke, and vascular disease. A systems-cardiology framework is presented in which direct myocardial injury, electrical instability, haemodynamic and autonomic stress, vascular and microvascular dysfunction, and disrupted inter-organ signalling interact. Ethanol and acetaldehyde toxicity, redox imbalance, microbial and inflammatory mediators, neurohumoral activation, and metabolic or electrolyte disturbances can impair endothelial signalling, mitochondrial energetics, excitation-contraction coupling, electrical stability, and repair. Pathway dominance varies across exposure patterns and susceptible hosts; coronary microvascular dysfunction may represent a convergence pathway rather than an obligatory mediator. Cumulative injury can diminish perfusion, contractile, electrical, autonomic, and exercise reserve. Alcohol-related cardiovascular ageing is proposed as a unifying cumulative phenotype encompassing mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, inflammageing, senescence, impaired repair, circadian and epigenetic dysregulation, fibrosis, and ventriculo-arterial uncoupling, although direct human evidence remains incomplete. Age, biological sex, genetics, comorbidities, sleep-circadian disruption, nutrition, medications, and polysubstance misuse may modify pathway dominance and reversibility. Structured exposure assessment and alcohol reduction or abstinence, when indicated, are actionable components of cardiovascular prevention and care.

articles.title: Synergistic Co-Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO2 Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid.
articles.abstract: Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ-MnO2 is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of sugars or polyols but suffers from low current densities. Here, by systematically tuning the ramsdellite-to-pyrolusite ratio of γ-MnO2 catalysts, we uncover how phase composition governs oxidative C─C bond cleavage to FA using glycolaldehyde as a model. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that ramsdellite facilitates *OH adsorption, whereas incorporating pyrolusite enhances sugar adsorption. This synergistic activation of water and sugar dramatically boosts the activity of γ-MnO2 with the intergrowth structure. The optimized catalyst delivers current densities >1000 mA cm-2 and FA productivity of 6.7-16.8 mmol cm-2 h-1 from sugars and polyols at 1.8 V vs RHE. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrated its application in stable operation for over 2,200 h at 200 mA cm-2 in a tandem acidic hydrolysis-electrolysis process for PET plastic upcycling to terephthalic acid and FA. This work establishes a structure-activity framework linking γ-MnO2 phase composition to the balance between *OH and substrate adsorption, providing design principles for MnO2-based catalysts in acidic biomass and plastic valorization.

articles.title: Manifestations of Mpox in Males: An Australian Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mpox commonly presents with anogenital lesions, creating diagnostic overlap with other causes of male genital ulceration, pustulation and oedema. Recognition is particularly relevant for clinicians assessing penile, perianal or proctitic symptoms, where delayed diagnosis may result in complications and transmission.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the male genital and anogenital manifestations of mpox in an Australian case series, including lesion morphology, co-infections, diagnostic pitfalls and complications relevant to male genital dermatology.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of 50 consecutive adults who presented to local health services between 15 July 2023 and 1 October 2025 and tested positive for mpox by nucleic acid amplification testing. Clinical notes, pathology results, immunisation records and available lesion photographs were reviewed. This analysis emphasises male genital and anogenital findings.

RESULTS: All patients were men who have sex with men, with a mean age of 38.6 years. The anogenital region was the most frequently involved anatomical area: penile swabs were positive in 25/50 patients (50%) and rectal swabs in 14/50 (28%). Presentations included penile lesions, perianal or rectal symptoms, proctitis, localised penile or perianal swelling and, in five patients, rectal mpox detected despite no visible external lesions. Lesions were described as pustular, ulcerated, crusted, papular, vesicular, erosive or exudative, and were variably painful, painless or pruritic. Differential diagnoses included primary syphilis, genital herpes simplex virus, molluscum contagiosum and folliculitis. Ten patients had concurrent sexually transmitted infections, including one lesion positive for both mpox and herpes simplex virus and one lesion positive for both mpox and syphilis. Five patients required hospital admission; male genital complications included severe proctitis, sepsis with concurrent sexually transmitted infection, penile swelling, chronic penile ulceration and urinary retention requiring catheterisation.

CONCLUSIONS: Mpox is an important cause of male genital and anogenital disease. In this cohort it most often presented as acute penile or rectal disease, but could mimic more common sexually transmitted infections or, rarely, a chronic penile ulcer requiring biopsy to exclude malignancy. Male genital dermatology services should consider mpox in new penile, perianal or proctitic presentations in at-risk men, particularly where lesions are pustular, ulcerated, exudative or associated with oedema, lymphadenopathy or concurrent sexually transmitted infection.
