Wolbachia induces excess ecdysteroid production to enhance female reproduction in Laodelphax striatellus.
articles.abstract: Wolbachia, one of the most widespread intracellular bacteria, is abundant in the ovaries of the small brown planthopper, Laodelphax striatellus. Wolbachia significantly enhances L. striatellus egg production; however, the mechanistic role of host hormones remains unclear. Here, we investigated how Wolbachia manipulates L. striatellus reproduction through the host ecdysteroid hormone pathway. Wolbachia infection elevated the levels of ovarian ecdysone and 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E), hormonal increases that are crucial as RNA interference knockdown of the synthesis genes CYP315A1 (for ecdysone) and CYP314A1 (for 20E) reduced hormone titres and suppressed fecundity, whereas 20E supplementation restored egg production. Furthermore, we precisely located germline stem cells (GSCs) in the posterior tropharium and identified mitotic nurse cell precursors (NCPs) in the anterior region. In infected females, these specific tropharia regions exhibited a high proportion of pH3-positive GSCs and NCPs and low apoptosis rate. Wolbachia microinjection into uninfected hosts recapitulated the entire phenotype, elevating 20E levels, enhancing tropharia cell proliferation, and increasing fecundity, confirming a direct causal relationship. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that Wolbachia elevates ovarian 20E levels to stimulate mitosis and suppress apoptosis within precisely mapped GSC and NCP populations in the tropharium, thereby enhancing host reproduction. These findings provide valuable insights into symbiont-driven reproductive enhancement and highlight potential strategies for insect population management.

articles.title: Colocalization between bone loading and metabolic activity in the human tibia in response to acute exercise.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: Bone strain and remodeling are important factors affecting bone strength. Better characterizing the relationship between these factors in response to acute loading will improve our understanding of bone metabolism in relation to daily physical activities. The purpose of this study was to evaluate colocalization between finite element-estimated bone strain and [18F]sodium fluoride ([18F]NaF) positron emission tomography (PET) imaging-estimated bone remodeling in the tibial diaphysis in response to acute exercise. We hypothesized that the exercise-induced change in standardized uptake values would be greatest in regions of higher strain. 26 participants underwent bilateral PET-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI) scans before and after a bout of stair ascent and descent exercise. Finite element analysis was performed to calculate principal strain distributions in the tibial diaphysis. [18F]NaF standardized uptake values (SUV) were calculated from pre- and post-exercise PET data and mapped to the tibial surface. Mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in SUV were calculated and compared between regions defined by strain percentile. Both normalized mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in [18F]NaF SUV increased with maximum principal strain in a pattern suggesting an exponential relationship. Pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in SUV were notably much greater in the region of highest maximum principal strains (estimated marginal means = 76.9 and 71.0 percentile, respectively) when compared to all other regions of the tibial diaphysis (≤ 61.1 and ≤ 57.0 percentile, respectively, p < 0.001). This study is the first to directly show a relationship between bone mechanical loads and acute [18F]NaF uptake in humans in vivo. Our results highlight the influence of tensile strain magnitude on bone metabolic activity in response to acute loading. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of a combined finite element analysis and [18F] PET approach to interrogate relationships between bone loading and bone metabolic response to acute exercise.

articles.title: Predictors of in-hospital mortality, sepsis and prolonged length of stay in burn patients: a ten-year monocentric experience and comparison with the Baux and revised Baux scores.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn mortality is usually predicted with the Baux and revised Baux scores, which do not include comorbidity; the independent role of psychiatric disease is also poorly defined. We reviewed 793 consecutive burn patients (630 adults, 163 children) admitted to a regional referral centre between 2016 and 2025. In adults, logistic models for in-hospital mortality, sepsis, and prolonged length of stay (at least 30 days) used age group, burn size by total body surface area, inhalation injury, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index as covariates, with internal bootstrap validation. Adult in-hospital mortality was 7.8% (49 of 630); no child died. Independent predictors of mortality were age 85 years or older (odds ratio 18.9), burn size 40% or more (odds ratio 40.6), inhalation injury (odds ratio 4.29), and a comorbidity index of 2 or more (odds ratio 14.2). Psychiatric disorders, not captured by the comorbidity index, were also independently associated with mortality (odds ratio 2.83). The multivariable model, a Baux-based model, and a revised Baux-based model (both including the comorbidity index) had almost identical discrimination (optimism-corrected 0.941, 0.955, 0.957; pairwise p>0.05). For sepsis and prolonged stay, burn size and age dominated, while comorbidity lost significance; the crude association between sepsis and mortality disappeared after adjustment, whereas sepsis remained strongly associated with prolonged stay (adjusted odds ratio 10.8). A multivariable model discriminates as well as the Baux scores while allowing comorbidity and psychiatric history to be quantified.

Hemodynamic effects of cycle ergometry versus dynamic unilateral arm exercise during right heart catheterization: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC).

METHODS: 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient's physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise.

RESULTS: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure increased by 12 mmHg with CE compared to 3 mmHg with AE (p<0.001), pulmonary artery wedge pressure increased by 5 mmHg versus 2 mmHg (p<0.001), cardiac output increased by 2.2 L/min versus 0.6 L/min (p<0.001) and mean pulmonary vascular resistance decreased by 0.05 WU with CE (p=0.761) and by 0.32 with AE (p=0.03). Estimated VO₂ during AE reached only 24% of the increase observed during CE, corresponding to an external workload equivalent of approximately 6 W. No patient showed an increase in pulmonary artery wedge pressure during exercise above 25mmHg to unmask left heart disease. In patients without PH at rest, CE led to the diagnosis of EPH in 5 patients while the used AE protocol was not suitable to detect EPH.

CONCLUSION: AE proved to be a safe exercise modality in our study but, with the protocol applied here, produced significantly smaller hemodynamic changes during RHC than CE and is thus not an adequate substitute in this form, leaving open whether an intensity-matched protocol could achieve comparable hemodynamic effects.

articles.title: The Role of BMP-2 in the Regulation of the Immune Response.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: The study investigated the conditions promoting inhibitory or stimulatory effects of BMP-2 on the immune response. An efficient cytokine response to ligands LPS, Poly I:C, and MDP and their interactions were demonstrated in primary bone marrow stromal cell cultures derived from CBA mice, indicating adaptability of this model for studying the immune response in vitro. Administration of BMP-2 in vivo to CBA mice and its application in vitro to intact cultures (in the absence of ligands or antigens) produced no changes in the levels of TNFα, IL-10, and IL-12 in the culture medium. In the BMP-2 (in vivo) + LPS group, the TNFα levels were markedly higher than those observed in the LPS group by 1.8-, 1.5-, and 2.9-fold at 3, 21, and 48 h, respectively. In 12-day bone marrow cultures deprived of secretome by a complete change of culture medium, LPS did not elevate TNFα in contrast to the cultures containing secretomes. In the absence of the secretome, TNFα levels in the BMP-2 (in vitro) + LPS group increased significantly by 4.5-, 4.3-, and 2.4-fold at 21 h, 48 h, and 6 days, respectively. Thus, in the absence of the secretome, BMP-2 in vitro dramatically augments the proinflammatory cytokine response to LPS. Overall, it is essential to consider that the presence of LPS in the body (e.g., due to a bacterial infection) during BMP-2 treatment can significantly increase the levels of proinflammatory cytokines; therefore, specific antimicrobial therapy can be recommended for patients treated with BMP-2.

articles.title: The incremental value of cortical renorrhaphy after base-layer closure in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: an anatomy-defined systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Renorrhaphy labels can obscure whether an outer cortical layer is added after substantive base-layer repair. We assessed this incremental step during robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN). MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched through 28 September 2026. Eligible comparisons retained base-layer repair in both arms but differed by cortical closure. Randomized and observational evidence were separated. Sparse binary outcomes underwent generalized linear mixed modeling, exact-inference sensitivity analysis, and descriptive absolute-risk estimation. Unpoolable outcomes were synthesized narratively. A second reviewer independently verified final screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias judgments. Among 23 reports assessed, nine studies were included (seven strict and two conditional). Neither protocol-defined critical outcome could be meta-analyzed. One cohort (n=146) provided three-month estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) change: mean decline was 8 mL/min/1.73 m² with omission versus 1 with double-layer closure (unadjusted mean difference -7.00; 95% confidence interval -13.03 to -0.97), although the source reported P=0.06. No study reported a comparable deduplicated 90-day reconstruction-related major-intervention composite. Four observational cohorts (n=575; 22 events) yielded an all-cause grade ≥III complication odds ratio of 0.70 (95% confidence interval 0.28-1.71); crude risks were 36 versus 41 per 1,000. Exact inference remained inconclusive. Available anatomy-defined evidence cannot establish the incremental safety benefit of cortical closure or renal-functional superiority of omission. Standardized trials with explicit layer definitions, fixed renal follow-up, and patient-level safety adjudication are needed.Registration: PROSPERO: CRD420261529497; version 1.0 published 4 October 2026.

articles.title: Optimization of Nile Red staining procedures to minimize dye residue and differentiate non-plastic particles in microplastic detection.
articles.abstract: Nile Red staining is a rapid and cost-effective method for detecting microplastics (MPs) in environmental samples; however, interference from dye residues can hinder microscopic observation and particle quantification. This study optimized the Nile Red staining procedure to enhance fluorescence response while minimizing residual dye interference. The effects of stock solvent, dispersion medium, dye concentration, staining temperature, and hot-water rinsing on dye residue formation and fluorescence intensity were evaluated. An optimized procedure using 10 mg/L Nile Red prepared with Tween 20 and 23.7% ethanol, combined with staining and rinsing at 80 °C, effectively stained MPs while minimizing interference from dye residues. The optimized method was subsequently evaluated using reference MPs of different polymer types and colors and applied to particles recovered from anaerobic digestate. Fluorescence microscopy demonstrated detectable staining of PA, PET, HDPE, LDPE, PP, PS, PLA, and PVC, whereas tested non-plastic materials, including black rubber, cellulose, and charcoal, exhibited weak or negligible fluorescence. Fluorescence intensity varied substantially among materials and was influenced not only by polymer chemistry but also by color, pigmentation, additives, and other material-specific properties. Overall, Nile Red-based fluorescence microscopy provides a rapid and practical screening approach for MP detection, although confirmatory spectroscopic analysis remains necessary for definitive polymer identification.

articles.title: In-hospital inclisiran for early LDL-C lowering after atherosclerotic ischemic stroke: an observational pilot study.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) below 55 mg/dL and a ≥ 50% reduction in very-high-risk patients, including after atherosclerotic stroke. Recurrence risk peaks in the acute phase, yet oral therapy reaches target slowly. Early in-hospital use of inclisiran after stroke is largely unexplored.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the feasibility of in-hospital inclisiran after high-risk ischemic stroke and describe the early LDL-C trajectory.

METHODS: Single-arm observational pilot study from a prospective single-center registry. Fifteen consecutive adults with ischemic stroke due to large-artery atherosclerosis or branch atheromatous disease meeting Italian fast-track reimbursement criteria received inclisiran 284 mg during admission on top of intensified oral therapy. LDL-C was measured at baseline, days 3, 7, 10, 14, and three months.

RESULTS: Fifteen of 18 eligible patients (83.3%) were treated, a median of 3 days after the LDL-C result. Baseline LDL-C was 138 mg/dL and fell to 75 and 31 mg/dL at days 3 and 14 after the dose (median reductions 45% and 77%). The composite goal (≥ 50% reduction from the acute-phase baseline and LDL-C < 55 mg/dL) was met by 33.3% at day 7, 80.0% at day 14, and 86.7% at a median of 87 days. Oral therapy was modified in 13 patients, so inclisiran's contribution cannot be isolated. No recurrent stroke or inclisiran-related adverse event occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital inclisiran was feasible, and most patients reached the goal within two weeks of the combined regimen. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant a controlled study measuring proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9, with clinical outcomes and longer follow-up.

articles.title: Microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery and endovascular treatment of sylvian fissure arteriovenous malformations: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Sylvian-fissure-region arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are uncommon and anatomically heterogeneous; published labels often describe non-comparable lesions or populations. To update evidence for microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), and endovascular treatment (EVT). Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched through May 2026 with citation chaining. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Dedicated sylvian/perisylvian cohorts were distinguished from broader cohorts and contextual technical reports. Incompatible endpoints, non-independent arms, and potentially overlapping cohorts were not pooled. Risk of bias and applicability were appraised. Nineteen reports were retained: 16 in the evidence synthesis and 3 as contextual background. Microsurgery achieved complete resection in 8/8, 40/41, and 94/94 patients. Transient deficits occurred in 4/8, 4/28, 9/94, and 18/41 patients; postoperative hematoma occurred in 2/94. Mortality windows varied. In the dedicated SRS cohort (n = 87), actuarial obliteration was 35% at 3 years, 60% at 4-5 years, and 76% at 10 years. Cumulative post-SRS hemorrhage was 5% at 1, 5, and 10 years (approximately 1% annually during latency); mortality was unreported. No dedicated curative EVT series for true sylvian AVMs was identified; available data described broader middle cerebral artery cohorts without sylvian-specific angiographic cure. Microsurgery is supported for carefully selected accessible sylvian-fissure AVMs, whereas SRS and embolization have complementary roles. Comparative superiority cannot be inferred. Future studies require explicit anatomical definitions, modality-specific denominators, angiographic endpoints, and standardized follow-up.

articles.title: Neurovascular conflict patterns in glossopharyngeal neuralgia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of offending vessels and outcomes after microvascular decompression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular decompression (MVD) for glossopharyngeal neuralgia (GPN) presumes a compressive neurovascular conflict at the glossopharyngeal-vagal root entry zone, but the distribution of offending vessels has never been quantified across series.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled prevalence of each offending vessel identified at MVD for GPN, alongside pain relief, recurrence, mortality and complications.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through August 2026. Studies with at least five GPN patients undergoing MVD and extractable outcomes were included. Proportions were pooled using the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation and a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).

RESULTS: Nineteen observational studies (1,000 MVD patients) were included, and methodological quality was acceptable to moderate (modified NOS median 5/6; comparative cohorts 6-7/9). Fifteen studies (674 patients) reported vessel-specific findings. The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) was implicated, alone or in combination, in 87% of patients (95% confidence interval [CI] 83-90), the least heterogeneous outcome (I² = 27.9%). Vertebral artery involvement was 12% (7-17), anterior inferior cerebellar artery involvement 7% (4-12) and venous conflict 3% (1-6). Multiple-vessel conflict was present in 14% (9-20). Immediate pain relief was 94% (92-97) and relief at last follow-up 90% (85-94) after a weighted mean follow-up of 66 months, with recurrence in 4% (1-9). Five deaths occurred (0.5%), four in earlier surgical eras. Sensitivity analyses for cohort overlap, rootlet section and unretrieved reports changed no estimate by 2 percentage points or more.

CONCLUSION: The PICA was involved in about nine of ten patients with vessel data, the most consistent estimate in the review. About one in seven patients had more than one offending vessel, supporting full-length inspection of the IX-X rootlets rather than treatment of the first conflict encountered.

articles.title: Effects of antimony on plant growth and soil biochemical functioning: a global meta-analysis across climatic and edaphic gradients.
articles.abstract: Antimony (Sb) is an emerging environmental pollutant that has raised growing concern due to its persistence, toxicity, and potential for bioaccumulation in food chains. Among its oxidation states, trivalent Sb (Sb(III)) is particularly hazardous, exerting more pronounced adverse effects on human health, plant physiology, and soil ecological functions. However, the literature currently lacks a systematic meta-analysis describing the impacts of Sb on plant growth and soil properties under varying environmental conditions. To fill this gap, we performed a systematic meta-analysis synthesizing 795 paired observations extracted from 28 peer-reviewed studies. Our objective was to evaluate the responses of plant biomass, soil carbon fractions (organic carbon, dissolved organic carbon, and microbial biomass carbon), nitrogen availability, and soil enzyme activities under varying climatic regimes, soil textural classes, pH levels, and C:N ratios. The results revealed that Sb consistently suppressed plant biomass production across all conditions, with the most severe reductions occurring in acidic soils (- 48.21%) and tropical regions (- 32.42%). Soil carbon dynamics showed different patterns: dissolved organic carbon was most depleted under temperate conditions (- 20.06%), whereas microbial biomass carbon was more strongly affected in tropical climates (- 24.87%). Nitrogen availability declined substantially, with reductions of about 39.04% observed in both medium-textured and acidic soils. Enzyme activities exhibited divergent and context-dependent responses; for example, urease activity decreased by more than 31.41%, and β-1,4-glucosidase decreased by 9.24% in soils with high C:N ratios. Overall, these findings suggest that Sb exerts divergent effects on plant growth, soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics, and soil microbial activities, mediated by a complex interplay of environmental factors. These findings underscore the need for site-specific strategies to effectively mitigate Sb toxicity and improve crop productivity.

articles.title: Abstracts of the 56th Annual Conference of the Italian Society of Neurology.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

articles.title: Sampling methods to describe photon statistics in large ensembles of quantum emitters.
articles.abstract: Photon-mediated interactions between quantum emitters can give rise to correlated and directional radiative emission. Many quantum optical phenomena can be characterized by the two-time quantum correlation function g(2)(t, τ), which describes the photon statistics of emitted radiation. However, the critical task of determining g(2)(t, τ) becomes intractable for large emitter ensembles due to the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space dimension with the number of emitters. Here, we analyze and benchmark two approximate numerical sampling methods applicable to emitter arrays embedded within electromagnetic environments, which generally provide upper and lower bounds for g(2)(t, 0). We also introduce corrections to these methods (termed offset corrections) that significantly improve the quality of the predictions. The optimal choice of method depends on the total number of emitters, such that, taken together, the two approaches provide accurate descriptions across a broad range of important regimes. This work, therefore, provides new theoretical tools for studying photon statistics and correlation functions in large ensembles of quantum emitters.

articles.title: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy.

METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete.

FINDINGS: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups).

INTERPRETATION: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes.

FUNDING: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership.

articles.title: Structural and mechanistic insights for calpain drug development.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Calpains are Ca2+-activated cysteine proteases with broad roles in cell signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell survival, differentiation, and tissue homeostasis. Calpain activity is implicated in multiple facets of human physiology, and its dysregulation has been reported in numerous pathologies. Yet, therapeutic targeting of calpains has been limited by challenges in achieving calpain-specific inhibition, owing to their complex biology and substrate diversity.

AREAS COVERED: This review covers structural-, molecular- and cell-biology, disease associations, and recent intellectual property activity relevant to calpain drug development. Structural aspects include the domain architecture of classical and non-classical calpains, ancillary domains, calpastatin-mediated inhibition, homo- and heterodimerization, and emerging structural models. Calpains are considered in the broader landscape of cysteine proteases to highlight likely off-target liabilities. Disease- and pathology-focused sections discuss calpain-mediated signaling in neurodegeneration, muscular dystrophy, ocular disease, diabetes, endometriosis, cardiovascular pathology, fibrosis, and cancer. Strategies for calpain modulation are overviewed, including active-site, calpastatin-mimetic, and allosteric inhibitors, gene therapy, and RNA-based approaches.

EXPERT OPINION: A shift beyond pan-calpain inhibition toward isoform-selective drug discovery, improved biomarkers, and accumulating structural insights offers new opportunities. Developing calpain-specific and isoform-selective therapeutics remains an exciting unmet opportunity in cancer, neurodegeneration, retinopathy, muscular dystrophy, and other diseases.

articles.title: Nanoplastics as hepatic toxicant vectors: interactions with environmental chemicals, organelle dysfunction, and regulated cell death.
articles.abstract: The environmental accumulation of nanoplastics (NPs) raises concerns regarding their potential effects on hepatic function. Experimental studies suggest that NP exposure can be related with altered mitochondrial electron transport chain activity, reduced ATP availability, changes in Keap1/Nrf2-mediated antioxidant responses, and impaired mitophagy. NPs have also been linked to cytoskeletal alterations, disrupted autophagic flux, and metabolic disturbances that can contribute to processes relevant to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This review critically evaluates regulated cell death pathways correlated with NP exposure, containing intrinsic apoptosis, RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL-mediated necroptosis, and NLRP3/cGAS-STING-associated pyroptosis. The available evidence implicates oxidative stress, mitochondrial and lysosomal dysfunction, altered autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, and regulated cell death in nanoplastic-associated hepatic effects. However, mechanistic evidence varies in strength, and observed responses depend on particle composition, surface characteristics, exposure conditions, and experimental models. Particular attention is given to distinguishing associative findings from experimentally supported causal mechanisms and to the limitations of extrapolating results from polystyrene nanoparticle models to other nanoplastics. By integrating evidence on mitochondrial quality control, microRNA-mediated metabolic regulation, and modulated cell death, this review identifies main knowledge gaps relevant to future mechanistic studies and toxicological risk assessment.

articles.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.

METHODS: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.

FINDINGS: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).

INTERPRETATION: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

FUNDING: Merck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

articles.title: 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.

METHODS: PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.

FINDINGS: Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.

INTERPRETATION: A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

FUNDING: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI Grant-in-Aid for Challenging Research (Pioneering).

articles.title: Prospective controlled study of the recombinant zoster vaccine in autoimmune rheumatic disease: robust seroconversion despite intravenous cyclophosphamide.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) prevents shingles in autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARD), but intravenous cyclophosphamide (IVCYC) impact on immunogenicity is unknown. Given cell depletion/cytotoxicity, IVCYC is expected to induce profound immunogenicity impairment, we therefore evaluated its impact.

METHODS: This subanalysis of prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial included ARD patients receiving IVCYC (ARD-IVCYC) compared with patients without IVCYC (ARD-no IVCYC) and healthy-controls. RZV was administered in two doses. Humoral response (≥4-fold), geometric mean titers (GMT) and cellular response were assessed after second dose. Disease activity and adverse events (AEs) were recorded.

RESULTS: Forty-one ARD-IVCYC, 164 ARD-no IVCYC, and 164 controls were included. Seroconversion did not differ between ARD-IVCYC and ARD-no IVCYC (91.9% vs. 91.5%) and were lower than controls (99.4%, p = 0.022). Post-vaccination GMTs were comparable between ARD groups (p > 0.999), but lower than controls (p = 0.006). Cellular response and ARDs flares did not differ between groups (p > 0.05), with no severe AEs.

CONCLUSION: RZV elicited >90% humoral response in IVCYC-treated patients, supporting it during IVCYC when warranted (NCT05879419).

articles.title: Ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake among among 55+ year-old Canadians: Exploring the role of racial discrimination, chronic disease comorbidities, and conspiracy beliefs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Canada's COVID-19 vaccination program achieved high overall coverage, yet older racialized and Indigenous people experienced lower uptake and far higher infection and mortality rates. Structural inequities, low health literacy, mistrust, and misinformation contributed to these gaps. Despite early vaccine prioritization, little disaggregated data exist for racialized and Indigenous older adults. This study examines vaccine uptake in these underserved groups to inform more equitable public health strategies and strengthen future pandemic responses.

METHODS: We conducted a Canada-wide cross-sectional online survey of adults aged ≥55 years in March 2025 using Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing. Participants completed measures assessing COVID-19 vaccination doses, experiences of major racial discrimination, conspiracy beliefs, health literacy, chronic conditions, and sociodemographic characteristics.

RESULTS: Of the 581participants, 90,3% received at least one dose. Black and Indigenous people were more often unvaccinated (17%), compared to 5.5-6% for Asians and Arabs. Receipt of ≥5 doses was observed in 50% of White, 41.8% of Asian and 13.8% of Black individuals. Older adults (≥65 years) had greater uptake (OR=1.58, 95%CI: 1.07-2.32), as did retirees (OR=2.47) and more highly educated participants (college OR=2.29; Bachelor OR=2.77). Higher conspiracy belief scores were significantly associated with lower odds of receiving higher doses (OR=0.91, 95%CI: 0.89-0.93; p<0.001). Additionally, a greater number of chronic diseases was associated with higher odds of being in a higher vaccine-dose category (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18).

CONCLUSION: Despite pandemic efforts, substantial ethnic disparities in COVID-19 vaccine uptake persisted, with lower coverage in racialized and Indigenous groups. Addressing structural inequities, comorbidities, and misinformation is critical to achieving more equitable, culturally responsive vaccination strategies.

articles.title: Assessment of the Fasciola hepatica saposin-like protein 2 (rFhSAP2) vaccine candidate in sheep: Immunogenicity without protective efficacy.
articles.abstract: Fasciolosis caused by Fasciola hepatica is an economically important parasitic disease of livestock and a major zoonotic disease in humans. Vaccination is a promising strategy to reduce the impact of fasciolosis and dependence on fasciolicides. Saposin-like protein 2 (FhSAP2) has previously shown high immunogenicity and reductions in fluke burden in experimental animal models; however, its efficacy has not been evaluated in sheep. Twenty-one female sheep were randomly assigned to three groups (n = 7): vaccinated, adjuvant control, and infection control. The vaccinated group received 400 μg of rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG, the adjuvant control received Montanide ISA 201 VG alone, and the infection control received saline. Animals received three subcutaneous immunizations at four-week intervals and were subsequently challenged orally with 200 F. hepatica metacercariae. Vaccine efficacy was evaluated based on fluke burden, fecal egg counts, and egg viability. Antigen-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2 antibody responses were assessed by ELISA. Vaccination with rtFhSAP2 resulted in a 16.4% reduction in fluke burden compared with the infection control group (p > 0.05). Reductions in fecal egg counts ranged from 8.9% to 34.5% (p > 0.05). Fecal egg viability remained high, ranging from 88.9% to 91.3% among groups (p > 0.05). Gallbladder-derived egg viability was lower in vaccinated sheep (56.9%) than in the infection control (75.9%) and adjuvant control (73.6%) groups (p > 0.05). Vaccination induced a strong and sustained humoral response. IgG and IgG1 levels were significantly higher in vaccinated sheep than in both control groups from weeks 4-24 and 4-32, respectively. IgG2 levels were also significantly higher from weeks 4-24, although the response was lower than that of IgG1. Overall, rtFhSAP2 formulated with Montanide ISA 201 VG was highly immunogenic in sheep, but the humoral response did not translate into significant protection against F. hepatica.

articles.title: A phase III randomized study: Immunogenicity and safety of a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: MenACYW-TT is a quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine approved for individuals aged ≥6 weeks. This Phase III study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT and MenPS-ACWY in healthy adults, adolescents, and children in India and in healthy adolescents and children in South Africa.

METHODS: In total, 1,328 participants were randomized by age into three cohorts (Cohort Ia: adults aged 18-55 years, India [N=198]; Cohort Ib: adults aged ≥56 years, India [N=200]; Cohort II: children and adolescents aged 2-17 years, India [N=465] and South Africa [N=465]). The immunogenicity of vaccines was assessed with a serum bactericidal assay using human complement (hSBA). The primary objective was to demonstrate the non-inferiority of immunogenicity of a single dose of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in terms of hSBA titers in India and South Africa.

RESULTS: The primary objective was met. The non-inferiority of MenACYW-TT versus MenACYW-DT was demonstrated on post-vaccination Day 30 in participants aged 2-17 years. The lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the difference in the percentages of the participants achieving seroprotection (hSBA titers ≥1:8) against all four serogroups was greater than -10%. MenACYW-TT demonstrated robust immunogenicity in adults aged 18-55 years and ≥56 years in India. The rates of solicited injection site and systemic reactions were comparable between the participants who received MenACYW-TT versus licensed comparator vaccines. No vaccine-related serious adverse events, study discontinuations, or deaths were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of MenACYW-TT induced non-inferior immune responses and a comparable safety profile versus MenACYW-DT in children and adolescents aged 2-17 years. MenACYW-TT was well tolerated and immunogenic in adults, adolescents, and children in India and in adolescents and children in South Africa.

articles.title: Engineered invasive Lactococcus lactis as an oral vaccine delivery platform is associated with compartmentalized immune modulation and enhances control of Leishmania infantum infection.
articles.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum remains a major challenge for vaccine development due to the intracellular localization of the parasite and the need for effective antigen delivery and cellular immune responses. Genetically engineered lactic acid bacteria have emerged as promising platforms for mucosal vaccination because of their genetic tractability and capacity to interact with the host immune system. Here, we evaluated an engineered invasive Lactococcus lactis strain expressing fibronectin-binding protein A (FnBPA) and carrying the chimeric TryPan antigen-encoding plasmid as an oral vaccine delivery platform, and compared its immunological and parasitological outcomes with subcutaneous immunization using recombinant TryPan formulated with monophosphoryl lipid A (MPLA). Oral administration of invasive L. lactis was associated with changes in intestinal chemokine expression, Th1/Th17-associated cytokines, and inflammatory cell markers, together with modulation of systemic immune parameters. Following L. infantum challenge, oral administration of L. lactis carrying the TryPan construct resulted in an approximately 99% reduction in hepatic parasite burden compared with the corresponding infected control. Notably, administration of L. lactis alone also reduced hepatic parasite burden, indicating a contribution of the bacterial vector to the observed parasitological outcome, while the greater reduction observed with TryPan delivery suggests an additional effect associated with the vaccine construct. Subcutaneous immunization with recombinant TryPan and MPLA induced broader systemic cytokine responses and reduced hepatic parasite burden by approximately 90%. Multivariate analysis identified distinct patterns of association among mucosal, systemic, and hepatic parameters according to the vaccination strategy. Together, these findings support the potential of invasive L. lactis as an oral vaccine delivery platform and highlight the contribution of both bacterial-vector-associated immunomodulation and antigen delivery to the observed control of hepatic L. infantum burden.

articles.title: Impact of digital health interventions in improving pediatric immunization coverage and timeliness in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vaccine-preventable diseases disproportionately affect children in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where barriers to vaccine demand and access limit coverage. Digital health interventions have been increasingly implemented to address these gaps; however, evidence regarding their effectiveness remains heterogeneous. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the impact of digital interventions on pediatric vaccination outcomes in LMICs.

METHODS: We systematically searched Scopus, PubMed, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov, Ovid MEDLINE, and EMBASE, and screened the reference list of relevant studies. Randomized controlled trials evaluating the effect of digital interventions on pediatric vaccinations in LMICs were included. Statistical analyses computed pooled outcomes, heterogeneity, and subgroup effects. The complete protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD:420251101655).

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies involving 68,664 participants met the inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis of pooled data showed that digital interventions delivered via reminder-only (RR 1.273; 95% CI 1.086-1.492; I2 = 93.3%), education (RR 1.953; 95% CI 1.076-3.542; I2 = 62.3%), and reminder with education (RR = 1.721; 95% CI 1.377-2.152; I2 = 0%) strategies improved immunization coverage of target vaccines as compared with usual care. Digital reminders were more effective in urban (RR 1.141; 95% CI 1.079-1.207; I2 = 51.5%) than in rural (RR 1.050; 95% CI 0.994-1.109; I2 = 0%) settings. Digital interventions also improved the timely receipt of pentavalent vaccines (RR 1.547; 95% CI 1.104-2.167; I2 = 95.4%). Among studies assessing acceptability, caregivers perceived digital interventions as beneficial, with a pooled prevalence of 94.7% (95% CI 0.765-0.990; I2 = 96.5%).

CONCLUSION: Integration of digital technologies into immunization programs enhances vaccination coverage and timeliness, supporting their wider adoption as effective and well-accepted tools for improving immunization outcomes.

articles.title: An integrated immunoinformatics and experimental pipeline identifies an LCL-scaffolded OmpA loop 3 construct as a protective vaccine candidate against Acinetobacter baumannii.
articles.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii has emerged as a critical nosocomial pathogen due to its extensive antimicrobial resistance and limited treatment options, highlighting the urgent need for effective vaccines. In this study, we developed and evaluated a rationally engineered epitope-based vaccine targeting extracellular loop 3 of outer membrane protein A (OmpA). Using an integrated immunoinformatics and experimental pipeline, the selected OmpA loop was grafted onto a loopless C-lobe (LCL) scaffold derived from transferrin-binding protein B to preserve native-like conformation and enhance epitope presentation. Four hybrid constructs were designed and comprehensively evaluated through computational analyses, including antigenicity prediction, structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulation, Toll-like receptor docking, and MHC-II binding assessment. Among them, OmpAL3-P2 exhibited the most favorable structural stability, surface accessibility, and epitope preservation profile. Experimental validation demonstrated successful recombinant expression and purification of the selected construct. Immunization of C57BL/6 mice with OmpAL3 induced strong antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses characterized by elevated IgG, predominant IgG2c production, enhanced splenocyte proliferation, and increased IFN-γ secretion, indicating a Th1-skewed response. In murine sepsis challenge models, OmpAL3 conferred significant protection, reduced bacterial burdens in major organs, and preserved tissue integrity. Passive immunization experiments further confirmed the protective contribution of vaccine-induced antibodies. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that LCL-scaffolded OmpA loop 3 is a promising subunit vaccine candidate against multidrug-resistant A. baumannii and supports the utility of scaffold-based structural vaccinology for rational vaccine development.

articles.title: Development of a genetically engineered multivalent subunit vaccine against "struck", "braxy", lamb dysentery, and enterotoxemia in sheep.
articles.abstract: The development of genetically engineered multivalent subunit vaccines is needed to provide protection against infections caused by Clostridium septicum and multiple types of Clostridium perfringens. In this study, a pET-32a(+) plasmid encoding the C. septicum α-toxin gene and the C. perfringens β-toxin gene was constructed; a positive clone was designated pET-32a-α-β1. This plasmid, along with pET-32a-α-β2-ε-previously engineered to express a C. perfringens α-β2-ε trivalent recombinant chimeric fusion protein-was transformed into Escherichia coli DE3 for recombinant protein expression after isopropyl-β-D-thiogalactopyranoside induction. Recombinant proteins α-β1 and α-β2-ε were purified, mixed at a protein concentration ratio of 1:1, and subsequently freeze-dried. The freeze-dried proteins were reconstituted with an aluminum hydroxide adjuvant and administered to sheep at various doses. Based on antibody titers and serum neutralization titers in immunized sheep, 0.2 mg of mixed protein was identified as the minimum immunization dose for the subunit vaccine. Toxin neutralization tests performed 21 days post-vaccination showed that sera from immunized sheep neutralized 10, 10, 27, and nine times the mouse lethal doses of C. perfringens types B, C, and D, and C. septicum toxins, respectively. All immunized sheep were protected against C. perfringens types B, C, and D, and C. septicum toxins, with a survival rate of 100%; the negative control group showed a survival rate of 0%. These encouraging findings provide a foundation for the development of novel subunit vaccines.

articles.title: Beyond disease prevention: rotavirus vaccine rollout and child stunting in Tanzania.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tanzania introduced the rotavirus vaccine in January 2013 to reduce the burden of diarrheal disease, a driver of malnutrition. While the vaccine's effect on diarrheal morbidity and mortality is well established, limited evidence exists on its broader effect on child growth outcomes, particularly stunting which affects about 30% of Tanzanian children under five.

METHODS: Using data from the 2015/16 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey (TDHS) with a sample of 8949 children, this study applies a reduced-form Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) exploiting the vaccine eligibility cutoff (children born ≥ November 2012) and Interrupted Time Series Analysis (ITSA) to estimate both immediate and sustained effects of the vaccine rollout on height-for-age z-score (HAZ).

RESULTS: Mean HAZ was -1.34 among vaccine-eligible children and - 1.65 among ineligible children (difference 0.31 SD, p < .001). The preferred quadratic RDD suggests a 0.44 SD gain in HAZ at the eligibility threshold (0.36 SD with covariates); local linear models indicate 0.22-0.26 SD. ITSA shows an immediate gain of 0.38-0.42 SD and a sustained positive post-rollout trend. Placebo cutoffs and falsification outcomes suggest that the effects are not driven by confounding factors.

CONCLUSION: The introduction of the rotavirus vaccine in Tanzania is associated with reductions in stunting by improving long-term growth outcomes. These findings suggest that vaccination provides benefits beyond infection prevention, serving as an investment in human capital. Policy should prioritise zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, integrate vaccination with maternal and nutrition services and sustain vaccine financing.

articles.title: Pathological, microbiological and immunological performance of three tuberculosis vaccine candidates in goats.
articles.abstract: Test and cull-based animal tuberculosis eradication programs have not succeeded in eliminating TB in various regions and implementing those programs is not feasible in others. Vaccination represents an additional control tool under study. Here we evaluated the immunologic, pathologic, and microbiological effects of heat-inactivated Mycobacterium bovis (HIMB), phage-inactivated Mycobacterium caprae (PIMC) and live Mycobacterium microti (LMM) subcutaneous vaccination in goats challenged endotracheally with M. caprae. All three vaccines were compatible with interferon-γ release assay diagnosis using defined antigens but interfered slightly when this test was performed using standard tuberculins. HIMB and PIMC candidates induced a strong anti-MPB70/MPB83 humoral response, and a modest but significant increase in phagocytic activity and/or reactive oxygen species production by peripheral neutrophils and monocytes, features not observed with LMM vaccination. Vaccination significantly reduced the lung and total lesion severity score (by HIMB, PIMC and LMM; 54, 44 and 52%, respectively), the total lesioned lymph node volume (by LMM), the total mineralized lung volume (by HIMB and LMM) and the mineralized proportion of lung lesions (by HIMB). The bacterial burden of respiratory lymph nodes was reduced in vaccinates by 2.3 (HIMB), 1.9 (PIMC) and 2.1 (LMM) Log10 in comparison to the non-vaccinated infected control. Extra-respiratory pathological and microbiological evidence of infection was mainly restricted to goats from the non-vaccinated infected group. Vaccination with all three prototypes modulated the response of goats against M. caprae experimental challenge leading to varying levels of protective efficacy, highlighting the need for further optimization and research.

articles.title: One-year antibody kinetics and effectiveness of a BNT162b2 booster after four primary COVID-19 vaccination regimens in Mongolia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Waning immunity after primary COVID-19 vaccination and the widespread use of heterogeneous vaccine platforms have created uncertainty regarding the durability of protection following booster vaccination. Mongolia implemented a mixed-platform vaccination program and deployed BNT162b2 as a booster. We evaluated the immunogenicity, effectiveness, and safety of a BNT162b2 booster following four primary vaccination regimens with 12 months follow-up.

METHODS: In this prospective observational study in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, adults (≥18 years) who had completed a homologous two-dose primary series with BBIBP-CorV, ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, Gam-COVID-Vac, or BNT162b2 received a BNT162b2 booster a median of 189 days (IQR 186-215) after the second dose and were grouped according to their primary vaccination regimen. Humoral immune responses (anti-SARS-CoV-2 N/S1-RBD IgG, S-RBD IgG, and neutralizing antibodies) were measured at baseline and at multiple time points up to 12 months after booster vaccination. Reactogenicity was monitored for 28 days. SARS-CoV-2 infection was ascertained by a positive antigen/lateral-flow test and/or RT-PCR. VE was estimated for prespecified follow-up intervals by comparing the risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection in each boosted group with that in an unvaccinated comparison group.

FINDINGS: Among 311 participants (mean age 41.88 years [SD 13.64]; 175 [56.27%] women and 136 [43.73%] men), antibody responses peaked at day 14 and declined through day 365 in all groups. At day 14, total antibody concentrations were highest in BNT + BNT (385.03 U/mL) and lowest in Gam + BNT (341.74 U/mL). S-RBD IgG at day 14 was highest in BNT + BNT (967.0 ng/mL) and lowest in BBIBP+BNT (863.70 ng/mL). Neutralizing antibodies at day 14 were highest in BNT + BNT (368.13 AU/mL) and BBIBP+BNT (336.70 AU/mL). During follow-up, 64 participants acquired SARS-CoV-2 infection and 15 (23.44%) were admitted to hospital. Reactogenicity was predominantly mild-to-moderate, and laboratory parameters were generally within acceptable ranges. Vaccine effectiveness declined from 1 month to 12 months: BBIBP+BNT 90.54% (95% CI 59.71-97.78) to 71.17% (39.66-86.23); ChAd+BNT 84.97% (49.75-95.51) to 52.59% (8.61-75.41); Gam + BNT 89.68% (23.95-98.60) to 63.84% (15.10-84.60); BNT + BNT 91.89% (40.06-98.90) to 72.29% (34.37-88.30).

INTERPRETATION: A BNT162b2 booster following diverse primary COVID-19 vaccination regimens induced strong humoral responses that declined over 12 months and showed an acceptable reactogenicity profile. VE against SARS-CoV-2 infection was highest soon after boosting and lower later in follow-up. Although antibody levels and VE showed similar temporal patterns, these findings should be interpreted as complementary outcomes rather than evidence of a direct causal relationship or a formal immunological correlate of protection.

articles.title: Empirical treatment with valganciclovir in infants living with HIV and hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa: a multicentre, open-label, factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high. This trial (EMPIRICAL) tested whether empirical valganciclovir treatment for cytomegalovirus improves survival in infants in Africa.

METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2 × 2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity to receive standard of care (SOC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SOC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SOC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, assessed at day 15 and over 1-year follow-up in the intention-to-treat population. In this Article, we report results for the valganciclovir comparison groups. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03915366 and is complete.

FINDINGS: From March 15, 2020, to Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were included in the analyses, with 276 allocated to valganciclovir groups (140 valganciclovir; 136 valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and 282 to groups without valganciclovir (142 SOC; 140 tuberculosis treatment). The median patient age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4), and 274 (49%) were female. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and tuberculosis treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·73-1·95], heterogeneity p=0·48). At day 15, 64 (23%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir group and 76 (27%) of 282 in groups without valganciclovir died (rate ratio 0·81 [95% CI 0·61-1·08], p=0·15). 24 (9%) of 276 participants and 13 (5%) of 282, respectively, were lost to follow-up. After 12 months, 119 (43%) of 276 participants in the valganciclovir groups and 134 (48%) of 282 in the groups without valganciclovir died (0·88 [95% CI 0·74-1·05] p=0·15). In a time-varying effects model, at day 15, the adjusted hazard ratio of death was 0·60 (95% CI 0·41-0·87, p=0·0063), and their hazard of death over 1 year was 0·79 (0·62-1·01; p=0·068), or 0·76 (0·58-1·00; p=0·0500) when excluding deaths within 48 h of treatment. Severe adverse events during follow-up were not more common in the valganciclovir treatment groups (odds ratio 0·64 [95% CI 0·35-1·16]).

INTERPRETATION: Empirical valganciclovir treatment appeared to be associated with a lower hazard of death in infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia than SOC alone or SOC plus empirical tuberculosis treatment, and there was little evidence of associated harms.

FUNDING: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership.

articles.title: Outcomes of Single Lung Transplantation for Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease: A Single-Center Retrospective Comparison with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
articles.journal: The Tohoku journal of experimental medicine
articles.abstract: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) is a serious manifestation of systemic autoimmune disorders and may progress to end-stage respiratory failure. Although lung transplantation represents a potential life-prolonging treatment, outcome data for CTD-ILD remain limited, particularly in single lung transplantation recipients. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study to clarify post-transplant outcomes in adult patients who underwent single lung transplantation from brain-dead donors for CTD-ILD, using idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) as a comparator. Between January 2001 and March 2024, a total of 29 single lung transplantations were performed for these patients (CTD-ILD, n = 13; IPF, n = 16). One-year overall survival was 92.3% in the CTD-ILD group and 87.5% in the IPF group, and five-year overall survival was 63.5% and 61.9%, respectively, with no significant difference observed throughout the observation period (log-rank test, p = 0.903). Freedom from chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) was significantly lower in the CTD-ILD group than in the IPF group (p = 0.048), with no CLAD cases found in the IPF group in this cohort. However, five-year CLAD-free survival did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.634). All cases of CLAD in the CTD-ILD group were classified as restrictive allograft syndrome (RAS). In a real-world Japanese clinical setting, single lung transplantation for appropriately selected patients with CTD-ILD achieved overall survival comparable to that for IPF. The high incidence of RAS among CTD-ILD recipients observed in our cohort merits further investigation.

articles.title: Genetically Proxied Antihypertensive Drug Targets and Autoimmune Disease Risk: A Drug-target Mendelian Randomization Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether genetically proxied modulation of antihypertensive drug targets is associated with autoimmune disease risk using drug-target Mendelian Randomization (MR) analysis.

METHODS: Genetic proxies for antihypertensive drug targets were selected from systolic blood pressure genome-wide association studies. For targets represented by multiple Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs), Inverse-Variance Weighted (IVW) analysis was used as the primary estimator, with weighted median, MR-Egger, and MR-PRESSO analyses performed as complementary and sensitivity analyses. The Wald ratio was used for targets represented by a single SNP. Coronary artery disease was included as a positive- control outcome. A Bonferroni-corrected threshold was applied for multiple testing, with p < 0.00125 considered strong evidence and 0.00125 ≤ p < 0.05 considered suggestive evidence.

RESULTS: Using European ancestry GWAS data, genetic proxies for Calcium Channel Blocker (CCB) targets were associated with a higher risk of asthma (OR = 1.001, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.001-1.002, p = 2.88×10-5), which was the only autoimmune disease association that met the prespecified Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold. Suggestive associations were observed between genetic proxies for beta-adrenoceptor blocker targets and a lower risk of multiple sclerosis (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.925-0.995, p = 2.16×10-2), CCB targets and a lower risk of type 1 diabetes mellitus (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.968-0.999, p = 4.19×10-2), loop diuretic targets and a lower risk of asthma (OR = 0.997, 95% CI: 0.994-0.999, p = 2.07×10-3), and CCB targets and a higher risk of rheumatoid arthritis (OR = 1.021, 95% CI: 1.006-1.037, p = 7.60×10-3). For multi-SNP analyses, sensitivity analyses did not indicate clear evidence of heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy for several of the reported associations. Analyses of angiotensin- converting enzyme inhibitor and angiotensin receptor blocker targets were based on single-SNP instruments and therefore were not amenable to conventional multi- -SNP sensitivity analyses.

DISCUSSION: The findings suggest disease-specific associations between genetically proxied antihypertensive drug targets and autoimmune outcomes. These results should be interpreted as genetic evidence of target-related effects rather than direct estimates of clinical treatment effects. In particular, although the CCB-asthma association met the Bonferroni-corrected threshold, its effect size was very small and should not be interpreted as evidence of a clinically important treatment effect.

CONCLUSION: This study provides genetic evidence for one Bonferroni-significant target- outcome association and several suggestive associations between genetically proxied antihypertensive drug targets and autoimmune disease risk. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating, require further replication and functional or pharmacological validation, and do not currently provide sufficient evidence to alter antihypertensive prescribing practices.

articles.title: Incidence of Venous Thromboembolism After Elective Isolated Lumbar Decompression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched on March 2, 2026, with surveillance through June 17, 2026. Decompression-only cohorts without fusion or instrumentation were eligible. Clinically detected, coded, or patient-reported outcomes were analyzed separately by event type and follow-up using random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models when at least five studies contributed data. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-five studies had a combined reported sample size of 831,732 patients. At 30 days, pooled DVT incidence was 0.283% (9 studies; 235,490 patients; 95% CI, 0.203%-0.393%) and PE incidence was 0.273% (7 studies; 235,341 patients; 95% CI, 0.171%-0.437%). At 90 days, DVT incidence was 0.225% (7 studies; 163,074 patients; 95% CI, 0.056%-0.905%) and PE incidence was 0.183% (6 studies; 162,772 patients; 95% CI, 0.041%-0.825%). Composite VTE estimates were heterogeneous. The low 30-day DVT and PE estimates persisted in leave-one-out analyses, while 90-day estimates were more sensitive to study inclusion. Only three studies reported chemical prophylaxis regimens. Different cohorts contributed to the two windows, which should not be interpreted as a temporal trend.

CONCLUSION: Reported 30-day DVT and PE incidences after isolated lumbar decompression were each approximately three events per 1,000 patients. These estimates provide a procedure-specific benchmark for counseling but do not establish the risk without prophylaxis or the effectiveness and overall benefit of chemoprophylaxis.

articles.title: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of the p.[H294Q];[D448H] GBA1 Allele: Severe Neonatal Cholestasis and a Rapidly Progressive Liver Disease in Gaucher Disease Type 2.
Gross motor development of infants with Down syndrome in the first year: Longitudinal comparison with reference curves.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe gross motor development during the first year of life in infants with Down syndrome (DS), compare it with published reference data, and examine its associations with maternal age, congenital heart disease, and home affordances.

METHODS: In this longitudinal observational study, 25 infants with DS, all receiving weekly physical therapy at an early intervention center since early infancy, were assessed at 6, 9, and 12 months (corrected age) with the Gross Motor Function Measure (GMFM-88). The age of attainment of six World Health Organization motor milestones was recorded prospectively. Home affordances were assessed with the Affordances in the Home Environment for Motor Development-Infant Scale. A pre-specified linear mixed model examined associated factors.

RESULTS: By 12 months, 92% of infants sat without support, 52% stood with assistance, and 36% crawled; none stood or walked independently. Crawling was more frequent and standing alone less frequent than reference probabilities. Mean GMFM-88 scores rose from 17.3% to 48.5%, exceeding reference curves at 12 months. Older maternal age was associated with lower scores across assessments (β = -0.75 per year, p = 0.028), but not with the rate of gain. Infants with congenital heart disease (32%) scored lower at 12 months, although not significantly (adjusted difference - 6.7 points, p = 0.116). Home affordances were not associated with motor trajectories.

CONCLUSIONS: Early horizontal milestones were within or above reference expectations, whereas upright skills lagged behind. These longitudinal first-year data support monitoring against DS-specific references to identify infants at risk of delayed upright skills.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture combined with traditional Chinese medicine therapy improves non-alcoholic steatohepatitis by regulating the TLR4/NF-κB and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways.
articles.abstract: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), an advanced stage of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is characterized by hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain limited. The present study investigated the therapeutic effects and potential underlying mechanisms of electroacupuncture (EA) combined with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction in a high-fat diet-induced rat model of NASH. Rats were treated with EA, TCM decoction, or their combination, and liver pathology, biochemical parameters, transcriptomic profiles, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and related signaling pathways were comprehensively evaluated. Combined EA and TCM treatment markedly reduced liver weight and liver index, alleviated hepatic steatosis and histopathological injury, improved liver function by decreasing serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels, and ameliorated lipid and glucose metabolism disorders. Transcriptome sequencing identified 351 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment analyses indicating that inflammatory and oxidative stress-related pathways were potentially associated with the interventional effect. Molecular results showed that the combined treatment significantly suppressed the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway, resulting in decreased the expression of inflammatory mediators, and simultaneously activated the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway to enhance cellular antioxidant defense. In addition, HSD11B1 expression was markedly downregulated, suggesting its potential involvement in mediating the interplay between lipid metabolism and inflammatory responses during disease progression. Overall, in this high-fat diet-induced rat NASH model, EA combined with TCM decoction ameliorates NASH-related pathological alterations by regulating the TLR4/NF-κB and Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathways, improving hepatic pathology, restoring metabolic homeostasis, suppressing inflammation, and attenuating oxidative stress damage. This combined intervention regimen provides preclinical evidence for future studies on NASH therapy.

articles.title: Evidence-based expert consensus on long-acting injectable antipsychotics for bipolar disorder: Recommendations from the TSBPN.
authors: Taiwanese Society of Biological Psychiatry and Neuropsychopharmacology (TSBPN) Working Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based expert consensus recommendations from the Taiwanese Society of Biological Psychiatry and Neuropsychopharmacology (TSBPN) on the use of long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics in bipolar disorder.

METHODS: An eight-member working group and 12-member scientific committee formed a 20-member expert panel. A narrative review of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and EMBASE from inception through February 2026 prioritized bipolar-specific evidence and incorporated relevant indirect evidence when necessary. Fourteen statements were graded using the World Federation of Societies of Biological Psychiatry framework for level of evidence (LoE) and acceptability. After expert review and revision, 18 panelists completed anonymous voting to determine the Taiwan recommendation grade (RG-T) and level of agreement.

RESULTS: The 14 statements covered LAI selection, clinical role, timing of initiation, special populations, and safety monitoring. Strong RG-T 1 recommendations supported prioritizing locally approved agents, individualized shared decision-making, use during mania as part of an acute-to-maintenance strategy, maintenance monotherapy or combination treatment, management of suspected nonadherence, earlier use in recurrent illness, use in patients with frequent manic episodes or comorbid substance use disorder, prevention of manic-spectrum recurrence, and combination with established bipolar-depression treatments when clinically indicated.
