RG-T 2 recommendations addressed older adults, children and adolescents, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and metabolic monitoring. Agreement ranged from 72.2% to 100%. Evidence was strongest for maintenance and manic-spectrum recurrence, but more limited for bipolar depression and several special populations.

CONCLUSION: This TSBPN consensus integrates available evidence with expert judgment to support individualized LAI use across bipolar-disorder treatment settings while highlighting areas requiring further research.

articles.title: Serine-functionalized liposomes enhance targeted delivery of hibifolin for acute kidney injury therapy via activating Nrf2.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains a critical clinical condition with limited therapeutic options, largely due to inadequate renal accumulation of potential drug candidates. Here, we report a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive and renal tubule-targeted liposomal platform constructed using a functional polymer conjugate, DSPE-PEG-Ser, in which L-serine serves as a targeting ligand for kidney injury molecule-1 (Kim-1) overexpressed on injured proximal tubular epithelial cells. Hibifolin (Hib), a natural bioactive constituent extracted from Abelmoschus manihot (L.) Medicus with limited renal accumulation, was efficiently encapsulated into the liposomes (SLip-Hib). SLip-Hib demonstrated enhanced cellular uptake via Kim-1 mediated endocytosis in injured HK-2 cells, followed by efficient lysosomal escape. In a cisplatin-induced AKI mouse model, SLip-Hib exhibited superior renal accumulation and retention, leading to significant restoration of renal function through activation of the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway. Notably, the degree of serine modification in the PEG-lipid conjugate directly correlated with kidney-targeting efficiency, highlighting the polymer structure-activity relationship. Biosafety assessments confirmed the biocompatibility of SLip-Hib. This study establishes that serine-functionalized liposomes offer a robust and safe strategy for renal tubule-targeted drug delivery, effectively overcoming limitations of conventional liposomes and enabling the therapeutic potential of Hib in AKI.

articles.title: Spatial and Spatiotemporal Clustering of Dengue in Jambi Municipality, Indonesia, 2010-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND OBJECTIVES: Dengue is a public health problem in Indonesia, particularly in urbanising cities where transmission patterns are spatially heterogeneous and seasonally dynamic. This study aimed to identify the spatial and spatiotemporal clusters of dengue cases in Jambi Municipality, Indonesia. A retrospective ecological study was conducted using dengue surveillance data aggregated across 62 urban villages.

METHODS: Monthly counts of clinically diagnosed dengue cases reported through routine surveillance between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2024 were obtained from the Jambi Municipality Health Office. Population data were obtained from the Central Bureau of Statistics and cases were analysed at the urban-village level to support local surveillance. Retrospective spatial and space-time cluster analyses were carried out using SaTScan TM with a discrete Poisson model. Monte Carlo hypothesis testing was used to assess statistical significance, and the clusters were visualised with Quantum GIS.

RESULTS: A total of 7,099 clinically diagnosed dengue cases were reported. Purely spatial and space-time analyses identified 24 and 39 significant clusters, respectively. Recurrent high-risk clusters were concentrated mainly in the central and southern parts of the municipality, although their locations varied by year. Among the 39 space-time clusters, 37 were in a minimum of one rainy-season month (October-April), and the other two secondary clusters were limited to the dry season (August 2011 and June 2023.

INTERPRETATION CONCLUSION: Dengue showed recurrent small-area clustering and significant overlap with rainy-season months over 15 years, suggesting the need for fine-scale surveillance and spatially targeted vector control.

articles.title: Predicting Cirrhotic Patients' Transition From Compensated to Decompensated Stage: A Graph-Based Multitask Deep Learning Method.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cirrhosis is a chronic liver disease, manifested by fibrosis and regenerative nodules. It can be classified clinically as compensated or decompensated. Accurate predictions of patients' transition from compensated to decompensated cirrhosis are important but difficult because of the multifactorial nature of disease progression, comorbid conditions, and patient heterogeneity.

OBJECTIVE: To effectively identify at-risk patients with cirrhosis and facilitate timely interventions across chronic diseases and patient populations, this study aimed to develop a deep learning-based method to estimate patient transition from compensated to decompensated cirrhosis. The proposed method seeks to provide superior predictive utilities and help physicians derive actionable clinical insights by modeling comorbidity relationships and symptom interdependencies that influence the progression of cirrhosis among patients.

METHODS: The proposed method was guided by clinical knowledge, considers patient demographics and medications, and leverages a graph structure to capture important comorbidity interplays. This method was augmented with post hoc interpretability to help clinicians understand its predictions for clinical decision-making and patient management. Using clinical data from 29,915 patients with cirrhosis, we evaluated the proposed method in comparison with 12 prevalent methods.

RESULTS: The proposed method attained an average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.871 (SD 0.004), F-measure of 0.678 (SD 0.010), recall of 0.741 (SD 0.022), and precision of 0.663 (SD 0.005). It showed a 6.09% improvement in AUC and a 13.95% improvement in F-measure over the best-performing benchmark method. Supported by post hoc interpretation analyses, this method can provide physicians with interpretable visualizations of the underlying comorbidity and symptom dynamics to better support their decision-making and adoption.

CONCLUSIONS: Empirical results underscore the value of demographic similarity, comorbidity graphs, and extended loss functions for identifying patients at higher risk of decompensation by capturing finer-grained information from essential patient features that tend to be overlooked by most existing methods. The proposed method not only supports physicians' clinical decision-making and patient management but can also enhance health care organizations' resource allocation efficiency and cost containment.

articles.title: Physician-Pharmacist PBPM for Intensive Lipid Management After Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
AIM: A physician-led lipid-lowering protocol increased early proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor use after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but workflow barriers remained. We evaluated a physician-pharmacist protocol-based pharmacotherapy management (PBPM) program designed to address these limitations.

METHODS: This single-center observational study included 438 patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and survived to discharge across PBPM (n = 162), physician-led (n = 160), and pre-protocol (n = 116) eras. The prespecified primary comparison was PBPM versus physician-led care. The primary and key secondary outcomes were evolocumab initiation and chronic-phase low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), respectively. Exploratory analyses examined outcomes across day-2 LDL-C treatment flows. Protocol adherence and reasons for non-initiation were also assessed.

RESULTS: Evolocumab initiation increased across the pre-protocol, physician-led, and PBPM eras (2.6%, 13.1%, and 24.7%; overall P＜0.001) and was more frequent with PBPM than physician-led care (24.7% vs. 13.1%, P = 0.008), although the adjusted association was nonsignificant (odds ratio 2.01, 95% confidence interval 0.94-4.29; P = 0.071). Chronic-phase LDL-C was 49.0 versus 51.5 mg/dL (P = 0.074), whereas exploratory achievement of the contemporary LDL-C ＜55 mg/dL target was more frequent with PBPM (67.6% vs. 54.0%, P = 0.034). Among eligible patients, evolocumab initiation increased from 40.0% to 61.0% (P = 0.047), while system-related non-initiation decreased from 44.4% to 4.3%. Exploratorily, chronic-phase LDL-C was lower with PBPM among patients with day-2 LDL-C ≥ 90 mg/dL (24 vs. 47 mg/dL; P = 0.011; interaction P = 0.010).

CONCLUSIONS: PBPM was associated with greater adherence to the existing lipid-lowering protocol, more frequent evolocumab initiation at discharge, and fewer system-related reasons for non-initiation compared with physician-led care after AMI.

articles.title: Salvage Heart Transplantation for Severe Biventricular Failure Associated with Systemic Sclerosis-Rheumatoid Arthritis Overlap Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multisystem autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy and fibrosis, and it often affects the heart, leading to ventricular dysfunction, conduction abnormalities, and arrhythmias. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is also complicated by pericarditis, valvular heart diseases, and diastolic dysfunction. SSc-associated right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a rare but life-threatening condition. Herein, we present a case of SSc/RA overlap syndrome associated with catastrophic biventricular failure mimicking arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy/arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ACM/ARVC), requiring central extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Urgent heart transplantation (HTx) successfully saved the patient's life, and he experienced no rejection, allograft dysfunction, or relapse of SSc/RA post-transplant.

articles.title: Rapid and Sustained Increase in Serum Transthyretin Levels Following Tafamidis Initiation in East Asian Patients with Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
Sustained Improvements in Salt Intake and Urinary Sodium-to-Potassium Ratio After Digital Therapeutics for Untreated Essential Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Long-term maintenance of lifestyle modification is essential for hypertension management but is often difficult to achieve. Digital therapeutics (DTx) have emerged as a promising tool to support behavioral change; however, evidence regarding their long-term effectiveness remains limited. This study evaluated the one-year effects and sustainability of a hypertension treatment support application. This single-center prospective study included 18 untreated patients with essential hypertension (DTx group, n = 12; control group, n = 6). Office and home blood pressure, estimated salt intake, urinary sodium-to-potassium ratio, and body mass index were assessed at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in office blood pressure. Office systolic blood pressure decreased similarly in both groups (DTx: from 144.0 [141.5-151.2] to 126.5 [122.2-137.2] mmHg at 6 months and 128.0 [123.2-133.5] mmHg at 12 months; control: from 149.0 [141.8-160.8] to 134.5 [133.2-135.8] mmHg at 6 months and 132.5 [128.2-148.8] mmHg at 12 months). No significant difference was observed in the primary outcomes. Similar findings were observed for diastolic blood pressure. Salt intake decreased in the DTx group from 8.8 [7.4-11.7] to 7.1 [6.5-8.4] and 7.0 [6.4-8.7] g/day at 6 and 12 months, respectively, whereas no meaningful change was observed in the control group from 9.3 [8.7-9.4] to 9.2 [9.0-10.3] and 9.6 [6.9-11.3] g/day, respectively. Improvement in the urinary sodium-to-potassium ratio was sustained only in the DTx group. In conclusion, this preliminary study suggests that DTx may facilitate sustained long-term dietary improvement in patients with mild or early-stage hypertension, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: The Emerging Role of Nurse Practitioners in Cardiovascular Care in Japan: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Japan is facing a rapidly aging population and an increasing burden of cardiovascular disease, which is creating substantial challenges for healthcare delivery. Simultaneously, cardiovascular care has become increasingly complex because of advances in transcatheter interventions, heart failure management, cardiac implantable devices, and mechanical circulatory support systems. These changes have intensified the demands on the cardiovascular workforce and highlighted the need for innovative care models.Nurse Practitioners (NPs) have emerged as important contributors to multidisciplinary cardiovascular care in many countries, demonstrating favorable effects on patient outcomes, care coordination, and healthcare efficiency. In Japan, NP education was introduced in 2008, and the number of certified NPs has increased steadily. However, unlike in several Western countries, Japanese NPs currently practice within a collaborative model under physician supervision, and their role in cardiovascular medicine remains undefined.In this perspective article, we discuss the current status of NP practice in Japan and examine the potential contributions of NPs to cardiovascular care. Drawing on clinical experience and the existing literature, we highlight the opportunities for NPs in heart failure management, critical care, structural heart interventions, and multidisciplinary care coordination. We also discuss key challenges, including variability in the scope of practice, lack of standardized postgraduate training, limited outcome data, and regulatory constraints. Finally, we propose future directions for developing a sustainable Japanese model of cardiovascular NP practice. Strengthening the integration of NPs into cardiovascular teams may help address workforce shortages and improve the quality and continuity of care in an aging society.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Right-Left Filling Pressure Dissociation on Long-Term Outcomes in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which discordance between right atrial pressure (RAP) and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) can occur. However, the clinical impact of isolated right-sided congestion in stable HF remains unclear.From the Acute Heart Failure Registry at Osaka Rosai Hospital (AURORA), we analyzed consecutive patients hospitalized for HF between January 2015 and December 2022 who underwent right heart catheterization within 7 days before discharge. Patients were classified by established cut-off values into four groups: Group 1 (RAP < 10 and PCWP < 22), Group 2 (RAP ≥ 10 and PCWP < 22), Group 3 (RAP < 10 and PCWP ≥ 22), and Group 4 (RAP ≥ 10 and PCWP ≥ 22). Clinical endpoints were the composite of HF readmission or all-cause death and HF readmission.Among 334 patients, 265 were in Group 1, 19 in Group 2, 34 in Group 3, and 16 in Group 4. Group 2 was independently associated with an increased risk of the composite of HF readmission or all-cause death and HF readmission compared with Group 1 across the sequentially adjusted multivariable models. In the fully adjusted model, Group 2 was associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint (hazard ratio, 2.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-3.91; P = 0.042) and HF readmission (subdistribution hazard ratio, 3.28; 95% CI, 1.67-6.43; P < 0.001) compared with Group 1.Isolated right-sided congestion was significantly associated with the composite of HF readmission and all-cause death and HF readmission in HF patients.

articles.title: Integrated Atrial Flutter/Fibrillation Ablation, Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion, and Atrial Septal Defect Closure in a Post-Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Heart Failure Patient.
articles.abstract: A one-stop strategy combining atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) has emerged as a feasible approach in selected high-risk patients. However, the integration of AF ablation, LAAO, and transcatheter closure of a large atrial septal defect (ASD) in a single session remains rarely described, particularly in patients with advanced heart failure (HF), recent critical illness, and limited tolerance to oral anticoagulation.A 73-year-old male with hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and acute decompensated HF developed severe urosepsis requiring veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Evaluation revealed a large secundum ASD with significant left-to-right shunting, biatrial enlargement, and right ventricular dysfunction. His course was complicated by recurrent AF and atypical atrial flutter (AFL), acute ischemic stroke, high bleeding risk and difficulty maintaining stable anticoagulation. After stabilization, a staged approach was considered; however, a single-session strategy was selected to avoid repeated anesthesia and prolonged ASD-related right-sided volume overload. Targeted flutter ablation and pulmonary vein isolation were performed first to stabilize rhythm, followed by left atrial appendage occlusion using the same left atrial access. Finally, transcatheter ASD closure was completed to reduce right-sided volume overload. Transient post-closure pulmonary congestion resolved with medical therapy. At 1 year, he remained in sinus rhythm without recurrent stroke, bleeding, or heart failure hospitalization.In carefully selected high-risk patients, a single-session strategy integrating AFL/AF ablation, LAAO, and ASD closure may be feasible, but its procedural benefits should be balanced against the risk of post-closure pulmonary congestion and the potential advantages of staged treatment.

articles.title: Association Between Home Exercise Patterns and Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Home-based exercise is increasingly recognized as an alternative to center-based cardiac rehabilitation for patients with coronary heart disease (CHD), yet the association between different levels of home exercise regularity and cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.This retrospective cohort study included 486 patients with angiographically confirmed CHD discharged between January 2018 and December 2021. Patients were classified into 4 EAR groups (inactive, low, moderate, and high regularity). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or unplanned coronary revascularization. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); sensitivity analyses used cohort quartiles and continuous exercise adherence rate (EAR).Over a median follow-up of 71.2 months, 78 patients (16.0%) experienced MACE. Crude MACE incidence ranged from 22.58% in the inactive group to 9.82% in the high-regularity group. In the adjusted 4-group analysis, P for trend was 0.039, and the high-regularity group had an HR of 0.49 (95% CI, 0.24-1.03) versus the inactive group. Quartile-based analysis also showed a trend (P for trend = 0.048), and each 10-percentage-point increase in EAR was associated with an adjusted HR of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.84-0.99). Among 423 patients with follow-up echocardiography, LVEF change differed across groups (P < 0.001), ranging from + 0.77 ± 3.62 to + 5.89 ± 4.08 percentage points.Higher home exercise regularity was associated with a graded decrease in observed MACE risk among CHD patients. Given the observational design, these findings do not establish a causal protective effect or a clinical EAR threshold.

articles.title: Would Body Mass Index Affect Measurement and Prognostic Value of Remote Dielectric Sensing (ReDS) in Heart Failure?
articles.abstract: Remote Dielectric Sensing (ReDS) non-invasively quantifies pulmonary congestion and is recommended for patients with BMI 22.0-39.0 kg/m2. This range may not fully represent Chinese heart failure (HF) populations, and it remains unclear whether BMI affects ReDS measurement. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the correlation between BMI and ReDS with its prognostic value across BMI categories in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF).We prospectively enrolled 172 ADHF patients (median age: 62 years, 65.1% male). ReDS was measured within 24 hours before discharge. Patients were stratified by Chinese BMI criteria: underweight (< 18.5), normal-overweight (18.5-27.9), and obese (≥ 28.0 kg/m2). The primary endpoint was a composite of HF rehospitalization or cardiovascular death at 1 month.ReDS values correlated positively with BMI (r = 0.487, P < 0.001) while the average ReDS value differed between the BMI groups (underweight versus normal-overweight versus obese: 24 ± 6 versus 30 ± 6 versus 34 ± 6%, P < 0.001). Adjusted for BMI, each unit of ReDS increase independently predicted adverse outcomes (HR = 1.09, P = 0.039). In the patient group within manufacturer-recommended BMI range (n = 91), a ReDS > 35% showed no increased risk (HR = 1.07, P = 0.226). However, in the Chinese normal-overweight group (18.5-27.9 kg/m2, n = 122), a ReDS > 35% predicted the composite endpoint (31.8% versus 11.0%, P = 0.021; HR = 3.30, P = 0.014). BMI-corrected ReDS consistently outperformed the uncorrected values in multivariable models.BMI may confound ReDS measurement. Although it is useful for risk stratification in ADHF, ReDS interpretation should account for BMI to enhance its clinical utility.

articles.title: Inverted U-Shaped Association between Hepatitis B Core-Related Antigen Levels and Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Antiviral therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus DNA replication but does not eliminate intrahepatic covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA). Hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg) reflects cccDNA transcription and may serve as a biomarker. This study investigated whether baseline HBcrAg levels can predict HCC development.

METHODS: This study included 204 CHB patients receiving antiviral therapy and followed them for HCC development. Baseline HBcrAg levels were measured using a chemiluminescence immunoassay. The patients were categorized into tertiles on the basis of their HBcrAg levels: low (<5.17 log U/mL), moderate (5.17 to <6.87 log U/mL), and high (≥6.87 log U/mL).

RESULTS: HCC was diagnosed in 24 patients. The 5-year cumulative incidence of HCC was 8.4% in the low HBcrAg group, 20.2% in the moderate group, and 3.2% in the high group (log-rank p<0.001). Multivariable Cox regression including sex, age, liver cirrhosis, platelet count, total bilirubin levels, albumin levels, creatinine levels, Fibrosis-4 Index, hepatitis B e antigen positivity, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels, and HBcrAg levels showed that higher total bilirubin and moderate HBcrAg levels were associated with an increased risk of HCC. In contrast, higher HBsAg levels were associated with lower HCC risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with moderate pretreatment HBcrAg levels exhibited the highest HCC incidence despite antiviral therapy. Thus, pretreatment HBcrAg levels may serve as a potential biomarker for predicting long-term HCC risk.

articles.title: Renal histomorphometric analysis in hyperprolactinemic rats treated with melatonin.
articles.abstract: Hyperprolactinemia, caused by elevated prolactin levels, is a pathological condition linked to several diseases, including chronic kidney disease (CKD), the most common pituitary hypersecretion syndrome. Melatonin (MEL), known for its antioxidant properties, can reduce tissue damage caused by oxidative stress. This study evaluated the renal morphometric effects of MEL in rats induced to hyperprolactinemia for 30 and 60 days. Thirty-six male rats were assigned to three groups: Control, DOMP (induced with domperidone, 4 mg/kg, SC), and DOMP+MEL (treated with MEL, 200 μg/100 g, SC). Biometric analysis showed no significant differences in renal or body weight. However, after 30 days, a significant reduction in the somatic renal index (SRI) was observed in the DOMP+MEL (0.22 ± 0.04) group compared to controls (0.29 ± 0.05). Histomorphometric analysis showed no differences in glomerular or capsule area, urinary space, or diameter, but clear tubular alterations. In the proximal convoluted tubules (PCT), MEL-treated animals had significantly increased tubular area (3020.99 ± 1267.74 μm2) and epithelial height (21.00 ± 0.68 μm), especially at 30 days. Epithelial height was also higher in both DOMP and DOMP+MEL groups compared to controls at both time points. In distal convoluted tubules (DCT), tubular area and epithelial height were significantly increased in DOMP and DOMP+MEL groups. Histopathology revealed renal alterations only in DOMP rats: 80% of 30-day rats had reduced capsular space and lumen, while 75% of 60-day rats showed enlarged urinary space and glomeruli with low cellularity. MEL treatment mitigated these changes, preserving epithelial height and glomerular structure. These findings suggest a protective role of MEL in hyperprolactinemia-induced renal alterations.

articles.title: Prenatal cannabis exposure and adverse neonatal outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression on tobacco co-use.
Comprehensive overview of atrial fibrillation trends in Estonia: a population-based cohort study from 2017 to 2024.
Angioedema risk with DPP4 inhibitors by concomitant RAAS inhibitor use.
Sample size calculations for developing clinical prediction models for binary outcomes: applied methodological study with real examples.
Improving the delivered dose achievement rate in continuous renal replacement therapy: a quality improvement project.
Reducing inhaler misuse in COPD outpatients: protocol for a randomised trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incorrect inhaler use is common in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), with 50%–70% of patients making critical technique errors and up to 40% generating inadequate peak inspiratory flow (PIF). Both mechanisms impair drug delivery and are associated with worse clinical outcomes. Evidence from randomised trials evaluating structured outpatient interventions remains limited. This study evaluates whether a physiotherapist-led inhaler optimisation programme reduces inhaler misuse at 12 months compared with usual care.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Assessment and Improvement of Inhaler Misuse in Outpatients with COPD is a pragmatic, single-centre, parallel-group, superiority randomised controlled trial conducted in outpatient respiratory clinics in Switzerland. Adults with spirometry-confirmed COPD using at least one maintenance inhaler are randomised 1:1 to a structured physiotherapist-led programme or usual care. The intervention includes visits at 3, 6 and 9 months with inhaler technique assessment, PIF measurement using a standardised protocol and teach-to-goal education, with device adaptation if needed. The primary outcome is the proportion of inhalers misused at 12 months, defined as ≥1 critical technique error or inadequate PIF. Secondary outcomes include symptoms, health status, adherence, inhaler satisfaction, lung function and COPD exacerbations. The primary analysis will use mixed-effects logistic regression with a random intercept for patient to account for clustering of inhalers within individuals.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study was approved by the Cantonal Ethics Committee of Vaud, Switzerland (BASEC 2025-02437). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications. De-identified data will be available on reasonable request.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07264140.

articles.title: Identifying Exploratory Physical Activity Thresholds Associated With Symptom Severity in Older Adults With Parkinson's Disease.
articles.abstract: This research identified exploratory physical activity (PA) thresholds associated with symptom severity in older adults with Parkinson's disease and assessed their association with cardiometabolic and cognitive health. Data were collected from 3,259 participants (age: 65.64 ± 10.37) in the Fox Insight database. PA was measured using Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly. Quadratic regression identified exploratory PA thresholds for managing motor, nonmotor, and depressive symptoms, with minimum thresholds based on literature-defined cut points and optimal thresholds based on symptom plateaus. Logistic regression assessed relationship between these thresholds and prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment. Analyses identified exploratory minimum and optimal Physical Activity Scale for the Elderly threshold of 150 and 245. Meeting minimum PA threshold was associated with lower odds of hypertension (21.1%), diabetes (40.6%), and mild cognitive impairment (57.9%; p < .01). These findings provide evidence-based exploratory PA thresholds to guide future research on PA patterns in older adults with Parkinson's disease.

articles.title: Associations of short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes among ageing adults in South Africa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to assess the longitudinal associations between short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes (mortality, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, functional limitations, depressive symptoms, loneliness, posttraumatic stress (PTSD) symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, addominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity, and general obesity) among community-residents 40 years and older, also broken down by sex.

METHODS: Data from three waves of the "Health and Ageing in Africa: A Longitudinal Study of an INDEPTH Community in South Africa (HAALSI)" (2015-2022) were utilized. There were 10483 observations of people who were 40 years of age or older. The American National Sleep Foundation was used to measure self-reported sleep duration. The association between sleep duration and 7-year mortality was assessed using hazard ratios. The longitudinal relationships between short and long sleep duration (using normal or recommended sleep length as a reference) and unfavorable health outcomes were estimated using linear, conditional, and multinomial logistic fixed effects (FE) regressions.

RESULTS: This study showed an association between short sleep duration and mortality, hypertension, depressive symptoms, and cardiovascular disease, while there were no significant associations between short sleep duration and diabetes, functional limitations, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, abdominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity and general obesity. Furthermore, this study found an association between long sleep duration and functional limitations, depressive symptoms, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired or lower cognition, dynapenia, abdominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity and general obesity, while there were no significant associations between long sleep duration and mortality, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and diabetes.

CONCLUSIONS: Short sleep duration was associated with four and long sleep duration with nine adverse health outcomes. The results can be applied to health literacy and education initiatives to promote getting adequate sleep, which is a crucial aspect of total sleep health. Future studies from other countries are recommended.

articles.title: From diagnosis to liability: the medico-legal relevance of delayed microbiological reporting in a case of healthcare-associated sepsis due to ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Healthcare-associated infections or HAIs represent a substantial global healthcare challenge, significantly impacting patient safety along with system performance. Timely microbiological diagnostics are essential, especially in cases of sepsis, where appropriate therapy delays directly compromise survival. These diagnostic delays are increasingly being examined not only as clinical shortcomings but also as indicators of systemic failures, raising questions of institutional liability. We present the medico-legal analysis of a 63-year-old male hospitalized patient who developed an HAI due to ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae and died of septic shock. Although preliminary positive blood culture results were available in the lab's system within 36-38 h, they were not communicated to the clinical team until 72 h post-sampling. During this interval, the patient, receiving an inactive empirical regimen, progressed to septic shock. Root cause analysis revealed two organizational failures: the absence of automated alert systems and inadequate weekend staffing in the microbiology lab. This post-analytical delay far exceeded international recommendations, which require positive blood culture results to be released within 2 h of instrument positivity. A counterfactual analysis, separating documented findings from inferences, supported a probable contribution of the delay to death, which can however only be expressed in probabilistic terms. The legal construct of organizational fault, analogous to corporate negligence in common law systems, holds institutions accountable for structural deficiencies that compromise patient care. This case underscores the need in this field for measurable improvements, most particularly in laboratory reporting systems and workforce management, consistent with the literature on automated alert systems and round-the-clock laboratory processing.

articles.title: Emerging molecular probes for lung cancer: Targets, translational evidence, and theranostic potential.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer incidence and mortality worldwide, and the management of both non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) has entered the era of precision medicine.

METHODS: This review summarizes current progress in radiolabeled molecular probes for lung cancer. Radiotracers were categorized according to their molecular targets, with emphasis on design strategies, preclinical and clinical evidence, current limitations, and potential theranostic applications.

RESULTS: Evidence ranged from preclinical studies to validated diagnostic or predictive performance, with occasional management changes. EGFR and FAPI imaging supported mutation assessment, response prediction, and staging, while immune-targeted probes characterized checkpoint heterogeneity and immune-cell distribution. MET, HER2, folate receptor alpha, and CXCR4 imaging showed early human feasibility; ALK and CTLA-4 imaging remained predominantly preclinical. Choline and FLT imaging assessed metabolism and early pharmacodynamic responses. Theranostic strategies enabled target confirmation and dosimetry, with FAPI-directed therapy entering clinical investigation and CXCR4-, CD133-, and DLL3-directed therapies showing preclinical efficacy. Translation still requires standardized thresholds, prospective validation, and evidence of benefit from imaging-guided decisions.

CONCLUSIONS: Molecular probes should be advanced according to the clinical decision they are intended to inform, not target expression alone. Prospective trials must compare imaging-guided pathways with FDG PET/CT and tissue-based standards and must measure downstream treatment selection and patient-important outcomes before routine implementation.

articles.title: Protocol for generating parasympathetic neurons from hiPSCs and their coculture with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: Peripheral parasympathetic ganglia lie adjacent to their target organs and are difficult to access for primary culture; their dysfunction contributes to diseases like atrial fibrillation. Here, we present a protocol to differentiate human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into parasympathetic neurons and assess their function by electrophysiological recordings, nicotinic receptor activity, and expression of cholinergic and autonomic markers. We also describe how to establish a coculture system with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes that allows neuromodulation of cardiomyocyte activity.

articles.title: Brain renin-angiotensin system: Pathophysiological mechanisms and therapeutic targets in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: This review aims to delineate the context-dependent, opposing actions of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, angiotensin II type 2 receptor, and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2/ angiotensin-(1-7)/Mas receptor axis in ischemic stroke and to discuss their translational potential for neuroprotective therapy. Although recanalization cannot guarantee favorable functional outcomes for all patients with ischemic stroke, adjunctive neuroprotective targets remain limited. Dysregulation of the brain renin-angiotensin system is increasingly recognized as a potentially modifiable pathway in post-stroke brain injury. Cerebral ischemia shifts the physiological receptor balance toward angiotensin II type 1 receptor predominance, promoting vasoconstriction, blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Conversely, the angiotensin II type 2 receptor and Mas receptor may counter these detrimental processes through temporally distinct mechanisms. The angiotensin II type 2 receptor may provide early neuroprotection through endothelial nitric oxide synthase-mediated vasodilation, suppression of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase, and inhibition of nuclear factor kappa-B signaling. By comparison, Mas receptor activation may facilitate delayed brain repair through mitochondrial stabilization, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2-mediated antioxidant responses, and preservation of blood-brain barrier integrity. This temporal framework, characterized by acute injury associated with angiotensin II type 1 receptor signaling, early protection associated with angiotensin II type 2 receptor signaling, and long-term recovery potentially supported by Mas receptor signaling, provides a rationale for time-sensitive therapeutic strategies. Preclinical evidence supports the neuroprotective effects of angiotensin II type 1 receptor blockers. Angiotensin II type 2 receptor agonists, such as compound 21, and glycosylated angiotensin-(1-7) peptide derivatives are promising approaches for engaging endogenous protective pathways.

articles.title: Longitudinal Cardiac Remodeling in High-Output Heart Failure From Intravascular Leiomyomatosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular leiomyomatosis can extend into nearby pelvic vasculature and to sites as distant as the heart and form arteriovenous malformations, leading to shunting and eventual high-output heart failure.

CASE SUMMARY: A 45-year-old woman with biopsy-proven intravascular leiomyomatosis presented with biventricular dysfunction. Right heart catheterization demonstrated significant left-to-right shunting with high cardiac output. Serial echocardiography over 12 years showed the development of both left- and right-sided cardiac dysfunction. With treatment, left ventricular function recovered; however, right ventricular dilation and functional tricuspid regurgitation from annular dilation established a self-sustaining cycle of right-sided failure.

DISCUSSION: Prior reports capture a single point in time; this 12-year echocardiographic course documents how shunt-mediated volume overload can progress to structural, self-perpetuating right heart failure independent of the original precipitant.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Shunt-mediated high-output heart failure can produce progressive cardiovascular deterioration. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are essential to prevent irreversible structural remodeling.

articles.title: Single-Access Retrieval of an Entrapped Rotational Atherectomy Burr Using Parallel-Wire STAR Technique.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotational atherectomy facilitates percutaneous coronary intervention in heavily calcified coronary lesions. Burr entrapment occurs in <1% of procedures, but it may cause vessel occlusion and myocardial ischemia.

CASE SUMMARY: An 81-year-old woman with recurrent angina underwent rotational atherectomy-assisted percutaneous coronary intervention to a heavily calcified right coronary artery. The 1.5-mm burr became entrapped, resulting in inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Successful retrieval of the burr was achieved via a single 7-F access by cutting the burr and extracting the drive shaft sheath, followed by subintimal tracking and re-entry (STAR) with a parallel wire, then external crushing to modify the calcified plaque.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates parallel-wire balloon-assisted plaque modification as an effective percutaneous bailout strategy for an entrapped rotablation burr.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Subintimal tracking and re-entry (STAR) with a parallel wire and external plaque crushing by a balloon is feasible from a single 7-F sheath by cutting the burr and extracting the drive-shaft sheath.

articles.title: Single-Port Robotic Mitral Valve Repair: First-in-Human Technique and 30-Day Outcome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comprehensive mitral reconstruction has progressed from sternotomy to minithoracotomy, thoracoscopy, and multiport robotics.

FIRST-IN-HUMAN/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY: A 59-year-old man with severe mitral regurgitation from flail middle scallop posterior mitral valve leaflet (P2) underwent single-port robotic repair using one non-rib-spreading instrument cannula and a separate accessory working port. Cardioplegic arrest, triangular resection, 2-layer reconstruction, and annuloplasty were completed with cross-clamp and bypass times of 62 and 123 minutes. He was discharged on day 3 and at 30 days was pain-free, active, and free of residual regurgitation.

DISCUSSION: Consolidating the camera and robotic instruments through 1 lateral cannula enabled intrathoracic triangulation and flexible endoscopic camera manipulation. This case establishes feasibility; however, superiority requires a comparative study.

NOVELTY: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported experience of lateral cannula single-port robotic mitral valve repair using this platform.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Single-port robotic mitral repair through consolidated instrument access allows early clinical benefit and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: An Infiltrative Left Atrial Mass With Valvular Involvement: Rare Case of Primary Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cardiac intimal sarcoma is an exceedingly rare and aggressive malignant cardiac tumor, often associated with poor prognosis.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a case of a 38-year-old woman with progressive dyspnea who was found to have a large left atrial mass involving the mitral valve apparatus, resulting in severe mitral regurgitation and stenosis. Multimodality imaging demonstrated several features concerning for malignancy, including local infiltration, heterogeneous tissue characteristics, and central necrosis. The patient underwent surgical resection with initial pathology suggesting leiomyosarcoma, though next-generation sequencing ultimately established the diagnosis of cardiac intimal sarcoma.

DISCUSSION: This case emphasizes the role of multimodality imaging in the evaluation of intracardiac masses. Although there are no established guidelines for the treatment of cardiac intimal sarcoma, the mainstay of treatment is surgical resection, with adjuvant chemotherapy considered on an individualized basis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Primary cardiac intimal sarcoma is an exceptionally rare but aggressive cause of an intracardiac mass. Multimodality imaging can help distinguish malignant from benign cardiac masses and guide operative planning. Accurate diagnosis of cardiac intimal sarcoma remains challenging because histopathologic features can overlap with other subtypes of sarcomas.

articles.title: Late Percutaneous Retrieval of a Septal Occluder to Facilitate Left Atrial Access.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We describe intentional retrieval of a well-seated septal occluder device for left atrial access.

CASE SUMMARY: A 28-year-old woman with platypnea-orthodeoxia and exertional desaturation down to 50% underwent patent foramen ovale closure. She developed refractory atrial tachycardia requiring left atrial mapping. Twenty days later, the device was retrieved percutaneously. Partial endothelization prevented resheathing, so the device and sheath were withdrawn together. The snare slipped in the inferior vena cava, and the device migrated into the main pulmonary artery before recapture and extraction. After multiple electrophysiology procedures, a Gore Cardioform occluder was implanted to preserve future transseptal access.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates the technical challenges of retrieving a partially endothelialized occluder and the value of proactive device-control strategies.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Device retrieval during early endothelialization can carry migration risk due to device stiffness; balloon stabilization may prevent it. Anticipating future transseptal needs should guide device choice at reclosure.

articles.title: Approach to the genetic evaluation of advanced paternal age: A points to consider statement of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG).
authors: ACMG Professional Practice and Guidelines Committee. Electronic address: documents@acmg.net
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics

articles.title: Prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening of chromosome abnormalities: A technical standard of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and the College of American Pathologists (CAP).
authors: ACMG Laboratory Quality Assurance Committee. Electronic address: documents@acmg.net
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.abstract: The American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the College of American Pathologists work group developed this technical standard to address challenges associated with laboratory validation and implementation of prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening. Given that cfDNA screening is the most sensitive and specific screening test available for common fetal aneuploidies, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine recommend that prenatal cfDNA screening be offered to all pregnant persons as a first-tier screening option, regardless of their risk status. Fetal cfDNA in maternal circulation originates from placenta-derived trophoblasts, allowing for the identification of fetuses at increased risk for trisomies 13, 18, and 21 and aneuploidy of sex chromosomes, in addition to recurrent segmental aneuploidies associated with syndromes. Multiple cfDNA analysis techniques exist, and because of the complex nature of this screening, this technical standard aims to promote uniform laboratory practices. This document deals with the technical standards applicable to prenatal cfDNA screening of chromosome abnormalities in maternal plasma. This document serves as a resource to assist clinical laboratories with the validation methods, ongoing monitoring of test quality and performance, and the interpretation and reporting of these results.

articles.title: Advances in HFpEF Research Based on Characteristics of Older Adults.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is the most common heart failure phenotype in older adults, associated with significant functional impairment and poor prognosis. Increasing evidence suggests that HFpEF should be considered a systemic, age-related syndrome, rather than an isolated cardiac disease. This review summarizes recent advances in the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and cellular mechanisms of HFpEF, with a particular focus on the frailty-sarcopenia-malnutrition triad. Age-related inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and anabolism resistance interact with the hemodynamic abnormalities specific to HFpEF, leading to decreased exercise tolerance and functional decline. Frailty, muscle loss, and malnutrition often coexist in elderly patients with HFpEF and synergistically exacerbate clinical outcomes. Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation and narrative lifestyle interventions are effective strategies for addressing these geriatric syndromes, and this review will address these issues. This article is a narrative review synthesizing current evidence on geriatric vulnerability phenotypes and rehabilitation-based interventions in older adults with HFpEF.

articles.title: Rare Differentiation in Genes XIRP1 and XIRP2 Associated With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The molecular mechanisms underlying hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Xin actin-binding repeat containing 1 and 2 (XIRP1 and XIRP2) are adhesion proteins localized to the adherens junctions of intercalated discs (ICDs). While mutations in these genes are known to cause cardiomyopathy, their specific contribution to HCM phenotypes is unclear.

METHODS: The study was conducted on heart tissue samples from 36 patients diagnosed with HCM and 8 healthy donors. The upregulation of XIRP2 has been observed, which was confirmed by Quantitative RT-PCR analysis. We further evaluated the association between genetic variants of XIRP1 and XIRP2 genes and HCM phenotype by targeted resequencing in 619 unrelated HCM patients and 307 healthy controls who did not carry any mutation in eight genes commonly mutated in myofilament disease. Using capillary Sanger sequencing, which excludes polymorphisms and probably neutral variants, the number of rare variants was verified in HCM patients.

RESULTS: mRNAs demonstrating a statistically significant difference in expression levels of at least twofold (p < 0.01) between experimental groups were chosen for subsequent analysis. The prevalence of rare variants in XIRP1 and XIRP2 genes was higher in HCM patients compared to controls [9.0% (56/619) vs. 3.9% (12/307), χ 2 = 7.96, p = 0.005], particularly XIRP2 (6.0% vs. 2.0%, p = 0.006). In HCM tissues, the expression of XIRP2 had increased dramatically by more than nine times (p < 0.001). The rates of inexplicable syncope (p = 0.036) and LV outflow obstruction (p = 0.012) and myocardial fibrosis (p = 0.010) were higher in the carriers.

CONCLUSIONS: Rare variants in XIRP1 and XIRP2 correlate with adverse HCM phenotypes, implicating ICD dysfunction in disease progression. Thereby giving more in-depth information about the relationship between the prognosis of HCM and XIRP1 and that of XIRP2.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A major challenge in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) care is the identification and management of individuals at risk before disease manifestation. An artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to electrocardiography (ECG) was developed to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype (left ventricular dilatation with systolic dysfunction) and was evaluated for its ability to stratify the risk of incident DCM in familial cohorts.

METHODS: A deep learning model was trained to detect the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and to predict its future onset, using more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston. Model performance was validated in cohorts from the UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital, and Antwerp University Hospital, and compared with models based on traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits. To assess performance in familial DCM, genetically predisposed individuals identified through cascade screening at the cardiogenetics clinics of Antwerp University Hospital (n = 166, 18% DCM positive) and Maastricht University Medical Center (n = 177, 18% DCM positive) were evaluated.

RESULTS: The AI-ECG model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of .87-.97 for diagnosing the prevalent DCM phenotype, outperforming traditional ECG parameters. AI-ECG was comparable to echocardiography for predicting future DCM (C-index .80-.87 and .80-.90, respectively). In familial cohorts, 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% (Antwerp) and 91.5% (Maastricht), with corresponding positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%, while high-risk scores were associated with a 5.1-6.4-fold increased risk of incident DCM.

CONCLUSIONS: The explainable AI-ECG model detects the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and predicts future disease, and supports the exclusion of short- to mid-term disease in genetically at-risk individuals. This low-cost tool could help reduce surveillance burden and facilitate earlier intervention.

articles.title: Beyond covariate balance: statistical resilience of Machine Learning-Augmented Inverse Probability Weighting versus Entropy Balancing in clinical evidence translation.
articles.abstract: Translating clinical trial evidence to heterogeneous community populations occupies a core mandate in modern drug lifecycle management. While Entropy Balancing (EB) is widely utilized to enforce exact covariate matching, its operational reliability under structural population separation and positivity violations remains insufficiently quantified. This study evaluates transportability inference risks using a dual-simulation framework, integrating theory-driven Monte Carlo stress tests with data-driven Plasmode architectures derived from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). We compared traditional parametric models, EB, and Machine Learning-Augmented Inverse Probability Weighting (ML-AIPW) across varying degrees of population overlap and functional non-linearity. Our results demonstrate that under severe representativeness gaps, EB achieves nominal covariate balance at the cost of a substantial 32% collapse in Effective Sample Size (ESS) and massive variance inflation with an RMSE of 1.701. This mechanical pursuit of strict distributional parity assigns extreme statistical weights to marginal clinical profiles, rendering EB estimates highly unstable and vulnerable to Type II errors. Conversely, the cross-fitted ML-AIPW framework achieved superior evaluative stability with an RMSE of 0.965 by non-parametrically mapping treatment response surfaces and utilizing cross-fitting to decouple nuisance parameter estimation from causal inference. By prioritizing the global minimization of Mean Squared Error (MSE) over superficial distributional symmetry, this architecture preserves inferential integrity even under sparse overlap conditions. These findings indicate that, under the overlap and misspecification conditions examined here, variance-aware estimation outperformed exact moment matching on total estimation error. Within this scope, EB is better suited to serving as a covariate-balance diagnostic than as a primary estimator, while ML-AIPW provided more stable point estimates under severe structural separation between trial and target populations.

articles.title: Clinical Predictors and a Prognostic Model for Overall Tooth Loss Following Complex Dentoalveolar Fractures: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex dentoalveolar fractures may result in irreversible tooth loss, but the clinical factors associated with overall tooth loss and their prognostic relevance at initial assessment remain insufficiently defined.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 147 consecutive patients with surgically treated complex dentoalveolar fractures between January 2018 and December 2024. Overall tooth loss was defined as the irreversible loss of one or more teeth attributable to the traumatic event, either immediately (teeth considered unsalvageable at surgery) or during follow-up; both components were also analysed separately in sensitivity analyses. Clinical and radiological variables recorded at initial assessment were analysed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination and calibration (calibration plot, calibration slope and calibration-in-the-large) were assessed, with internal validation performed using bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Overall tooth loss was observed in 86 patients (58.5%) (immediate loss, n = 63; loss during follow-up, n = 23). Univariable analysis identified alveolar bone substance loss, unfavourable dental status, gingival substance loss, positive toxicology screening at admission, and associated facial fractures as variables associated with the outcome. In the multivariable model, alveolar bone substance loss was the strongest independent predictor of overall tooth loss (adjusted OR 22.92, 95% CI 7.23-72.71; p < 0.001), while associated facial fractures also remained independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR 3.49, 95% CI 1.09-11.17; p = 0.035). Positive toxicology screening at admission was also independently associated with overall tooth loss after adjustment (adjusted OR 4.18, 95% CI 1.30-13.41; p = 0.016). The prognostic model showed excellent discrimination (apparent AUC: 0.915; optimism-corrected: 0.874) and the calibration plot showed close agreement between predicted and observed probabilities (optimism-corrected calibration slope 0.88; Brier score 0.10).

CONCLUSIONS: Alveolar bone substance loss was the strongest independent predictor of overall tooth loss following complex dentoalveolar fractures. A prognostic model based on clinical variables available at initial assessment may support early risk stratification and individualised follow-up. External validation in independent multicentre cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Lipid metabolic reprogramming in honey bee response to Hafnia alvei infection: insights from temporal transcriptome analysis.
articles.abstract: Host defense against pathogen infection relies on coordinated immune activation and metabolic reprogramming, but how these processes are temporally organized in insects remains poorly understood. Here, time-series transcriptomic analyses of honey bee fat bodies revealed that Hafnia alvei infection induced a stage-dependent response. Genes involved in carbohydrate, glycerolipid, and glycerophospholipid metabolism were rapidly induced after infection, whereas immune signaling pathways and antimicrobial peptide genes were progressively upregulated later. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis further revealed positive correlations between lipid metabolism-related genes and immune genes, indicating tight coordination between metabolic and immune responses. Comparisons among germ-free, heat-killed bacteria-colonized, and conventionally colonized bees demonstrated that live gut microbiota promoted earlier and stronger lipid metabolic remodeling and immune activation, whereas heat-killed bacteria triggered delayed responses compared to live bacteria colonization. These findings indicate lipid metabolic reprogramming as a key component of honey bee defense against H. alvei and show that gut microbiota enhances host resistance by modulating metabolic-immune coordination.

articles.title: Host-Directed Ferroptotic Stress Modulation Against Intracellular Bacterial Infections: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Translational Challenges.
articles.abstract: The rise in antibiotic resistance and the persistence of intracellular infections underscore the urgent need for novel antimicrobial agents and strategies. Ferroptotic stress is a cell state marked by transiently elevated Fe2+ levels, increased lipid peroxidation, and altered redox balance. It has gained significant attention due to its role in the progression of various diseases, especially bacterial infections. By inducing intracellular iron overload, disrupting the bacterial microenvironment, and activating innate immune cells like macrophages, it serves as a crucial strategy to restrict intracellular bacterial growth and limit the emergence of resistance. Despite growing interest, systematic reviews integrating host ferroptotic stress modulation with precision antimicrobial strategies remain scarce. This review explores recent advancements in host-directed ferroptotic stress strategies for combating bacterial infections, focusing on metabolic reprogramming, macrophage-mediated defense, membrane remodeling, nutrient deprivation, iron trafficking, direct bacteriolysis, and antibiotic synergism. It highlights the potential of precision modulation of host ferroptotic stress to enhance antimicrobial strategies and identifies key research gaps to advance related therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: Methemoglobin Causes Collapsed WDF Scattergrams and a Low-SFL Mature RBC Population in RET Scattergrams on the XR-Series Automated Hematology Analyzer.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Methemoglobinemia is characterized by increased methemoglobin (MetHb), which impairs oxygen delivery and may cause clinically significant hypoxia. Because CBC testing is more routinely performed than blood gas analysis, abnormalities detected during CBC testing may provide useful clues to unsuspected methemoglobinemia. We investigated the effects of MetHb on scattergrams and optical indices generated by the XR-Series automated hematology analyzer.

METHODS: MetHb-containing samples were prepared from five healthy donors using sodium nitrite-treated red blood cells and analyzed using the XR-9000. WDF, RET, and PLT-F scattergrams and WDF sensitivity indices were evaluated. Reference intervals were established using data from 812 individuals in the reference population. Potassium cyanide (KCN) treatment was performed on MetHb-containing samples from all five donors. Clinical cases were examined.

RESULTS: Increasing MetHb concentrations reduced side fluorescence (SFL) and produced a collapsed WDF scattergram pattern. SFL reductions were more pronounced in lymphocytes and monocytes than in neutrophils, and LY-Y and MO-Y fell below their lower reference limits even at low MetHb concentrations. MetHb induced a distinct low-SFL population of mature red blood cells in RET and PLT-F scattergrams, distinguishable even at low MetHb concentrations in the RET channel. KCN treatment restored WDF and RET scattergrams to patterns similar to those of the normal control in all five donors. Similar abnormalities were observed in clinical methemoglobinemia.

CONCLUSION: MetHb produces characteristic abnormalities in WDF and RET scattergrams on the XR-Series analyzer. These findings may provide useful clues for the incidental detection of unsuspected methemoglobinemia during routine CBC testing.

articles.title: Changing tonometers, changing intraocular pressure? Rethinking intraocular pressure interpretation in dogs.
articles.journal: The Journal of small animal practice
articles.abstract: Intraocular pressure measurement is fundamental to the diagnosis and management of canine glaucoma, yet the value reported by a tonometer is inherently dependent on the instrument used. Successive generations of veterinary tonometers have improved portability, usability, standardisation and agreement with manometric pressure; however, measurements obtained with different devices are not necessarily interchangeable. Recorded intraocular pressure is also influenced by corneal properties, measurement technique, patient state and the clinical environment. These sources of variability are particularly important during longitudinal monitoring, because replacement or recalibration of a tonometer may produce an apparent change in intraocular pressure that does not reflect biological change within the eye. For practitioners, a change in tonometer should therefore be regarded as a change in the measurement system rather than simply replacement of equipment. The tonometer model and generation should be documented, and when instruments are changed, paired measurements with the old and new devices should be obtained when feasible to help establish a new clinical baseline. Population-level inter-device differences should not be applied as simple correction factors to individual patients, and numerical thresholds for ocular hypertension or suspicion of glaucoma should not be assumed to have equivalent clinical meaning across tonometers. When an unexpected change in intraocular pressure is detected, clinicians should consider both biological change and changes in the measurement context. Glaucoma diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring should therefore integrate intraocular pressure with visual function and structural assessment of the retina and optic nerve. Preserving the clinical meaning of intraocular pressure, rather than numerical continuity alone, should guide the interpretation of serial measurements as tonometric technology evolves.

articles.title: Associations between substance use and symptomatic Long COVID in the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-adult cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To determine whether frequency of tobacco, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test result or COVID-19 symptom onset is associated with (1) presence of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and (2) development of symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up, among those without Long COVID at study entry.

DESIGN: Prospective cohort study with cross-sectional and longitudinal components.

SETTING: Multi-site study conducted across 83 clinical sites in the United States.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 9477 adults enrolled between October 2021 and July 2024 (median age 43 years; 74% female).

MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported frequency of tobacco product, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test infection (never, monthly or less, weekly or none). Symptomatic Long COVID was defined using the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-Adult Long COVID Research Index, with scores ≥ 11 classified as symptomatic Long COVID and lower scores classified as indeterminate. Covariates included sociodemographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities and COVID-19 related factors.

RESULTS: At study entry 20% of participants met criteria for symptomatic Long COVID. In the 12 months preceding infection, 14%, 21% and 38% reported any tobacco product, cannabis or binge alcohol use. At study entry, compared with no use, weekly or more tobacco use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.37, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.13-1.67]; weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID (aOR = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.00-1.52); and weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.73, 95% CI = 0.58-0.91) of symptomatic Long COVID. Monthly or less use of any substance was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Among participants without symptomatic Long COVID at study entry, weekly or more tobacco use, compared with no use, was associated with higher odds of developing symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up (aOR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.03-1.62). Neither cannabis nor binge alcohol use was statistically significantly associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12-month follow-up.

SUMMARY: Among adult participants of the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER) study, weekly or more tobacco use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and at 12 months among participants who did not meet criteria for symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months. Weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months.

articles.title: Airway collapse in small breed dogs and its association with clinical and anatomic variables.
articles.journal: The Journal of small animal practice
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate associations between clinical and anatomic variables in small breed dogs with lower airway collapse.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: One hundred and fifty dogs with chronic cough presenting between July 2017 and July 2023 were retrospectively included. Bronchoscopy recordings were reviewed to identify presence, location and severity of airway collapse. Anatomic variables were measured on computed tomography images. Cardiac variables were assessed with echocardiography or thoracic radiographs.

RESULTS: Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (Estimate: -51.75; 95% CI: -82.54 to -20.96), increasing body condition score (BCS) (Estimate: 6.45; 95% CI: 3.35 to 9.55) and presence of left atrial enlargement (Estimate: 21.97; 95% CI: 7.02 to 36.92) were associated with increasing cumulative bronchial collapse scores. Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (OR: 0.02; 95% CI: 0.0004 to 0.63), increasing age (OR: 1.02; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.03) and increasing body condition score (OR: 1.41; 95% CI: 1.04 to 1.92) were associated with increasing bronchomalacia scores. Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (OR: 0.001; 95% CI: 0.00000758 to 0.08), increasing body condition score (OR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.18 to 2.29), presence of left atrial enlargement (OR: 4.89; 95% CI: 1.19 to 21.65) and presence of airway neutrophilic inflammation (OR: 3.98; 95% CI: 1.10 to 17.39) were associated with increasing left principal bronchus collapse scores. Decreasing thoracic height:width ratio (OR: 0.003; 95% CI: 0.0001 to 0.07), increasing body condition score (OR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.20 to 1.99) and presence of left atrial enlargement (OR: 4.85; 95% CI: 1.38 to 18.99) were associated with increasing left caudal lobar bronchus collapse scores.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Variations in thoracic conformation might be involved in the aetiopathogenesis of airway collapse and reduced thoracic height:width ratio is associated with increasing airway collapse scores. Increasing body condition score is a modifiable variable associated with increasing airway collapse scores. Left atrial enlargement is associated with increased bronchial collapse scores but might directly contribute only to pre-existing collapse of the left caudal lobar bronchus.

articles.title: Alcohol Consumption as a Predictor of Outcomes in Open Carpal Tunnel Release Surgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common peripheral nerve entrapment; open carpal tunnel release (OCTR) surgery is the gold standard surgical technique. Pre-operative alcohol consumption is a known predictive factor of polyneuropathy and post-operative outcomes. The aim is to investigate the influence of alcohol consumption on OCTR surgery outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic review registered with PROSPERO was performed using PRISMA guidelines. Study selection included English language randomised controlled trials, cohort longitudinal studies and case series on adults published within a 10-year period (2015-2025). ROBINS-I was utilised for a risk of bias assessment.

RESULTS: Eight studies were eligible as per the criteria. There is little to no evidence which suggests pre-operative alcohol consumption impacts OCTR post-operative outcomes (p = 0.60); depression (p = 0.46), Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ) (p = 0.16), palmar pain (p = 0.27), wound healing disturbance (p = 0.85), numbness (p = 1.00), pain (p = 0.50), Kelly Score (p = 1.00) and return to work (p = 0.67). There is varying evidence associating pre-operative alcohol consumption with post-operative infection; one study reported little to no evidence (p = 0.39) and another reported very strong evidence (p < 0.001). There is evidence to suggest that patients requiring revision surgery are less likely to consume alcohol (p = 0.025).

CONCLUSION: There is little to no evidence that alcohol consumption impacts outcomes in patients undergoing OCTR surgery. Further studies should investigate the impact of pre-operative alcohol consumption on post-operative infection risk and revision surgery outcomes.

articles.title: Lipid-lowering therapy for secondary stroke prevention beyond statin monotherapy: a mechanism-informed approach across drug classes and stroke subtypes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intensive lipid lowering is crucial for secondary prevention of ischemic stroke, but achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets and selecting additional agents beyond statins are challenging. Stroke mechanisms vary in their contribution to atherosclerosis, so the benefits, risks, and treatment burdens of aggressive LDL-C reduction may differ among phenotypes.

AREAS COVERED: The authors searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar for studies published through September 2026 on lipid-lowering therapy after ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. The authors prioritize randomized trials, subgroup analyses, stroke-specific observational studies, meta-analyses, and major guidelines or consensus documents and assess the evidence by study design, stroke phenotype, and whether outcomes were clinical events or surrogate measures, including LDL-C target attainment and plaque imaging.

EXPERT OPINION: Future lipid management after ischemic stroke could improve by combining stroke phenotype and atherosclerotic burden with established cardiovascular risk and LDL-C targets. Early combination therapy may help plaque-driven stroke patients reach targets, but its effect on recurrence is unproven. Evidence is limited by few stroke-specific trials, reliance on surrogate endpoints, and barriers including advanced imaging and biologic reimbursement. Phenotype-stratified trials should test whether mechanism-informed care improves outcomes and cost-effectiveness beyond guidelines.

articles.title: The Safety and Feasibility of Monitoring Cardiac Arrhythmic Events Before and After Conversion From Conventional Intermittent Hemodialysis to Home Nocturnal Hemodialysis: A Pilot Study.
articles.journal: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients on hemodialysis have an increased risk of sudden cardiac death and an increased cardiac arrhythmia burden due to large fluid and electrolyte shifts, especially during the long inter-dialytic period. Arrhythmia burden may be decreased on home nocturnal hemodialysis due to prolonged fluid removal and clearance. This study examined the safety and feasibility of prolonged cardiac monitoring in patients who were converting from conventional hemodialysis (12 h) to home nocturnal hemodialysis (30+ h).

METHODS: Patients from a single center in Toronto, Ontario, Canada with a low cardiac risk profile, who were eligible to perform hemodialysis at home, were enrolled. Participants underwent the insertion of an implantable loop recorder and cardiac arrhythmia were monitored during conventional hemodialysis, and for 1 year after conversion to home nocturnal hemodialysis.

FINDINGS: Ten participants completed the study. The average ultrafiltration rate per session during conventional hemodialysis was 6.87 mL/h/kg, and the average cardiac ejection fraction was 52.6%. There were no adverse effects associated with implantable loop recorder implantation, usage, or removal. One participant recorded three sinus bradycardia and two sinus pause events during conventional hemodialysis that resolved after conversion to home nocturnal hemodialysis. All other participants did not experience any arrhythmic events before or after conversion to home nocturnal hemodialysis.

DISCUSSION: Our pilot study demonstrated a safe and feasible protocol for prolonged monitoring of cardiac arrhythmia in a stable population undergoing conversion from conventional to home nocturnal hemodialysis. Due to the small sample size, future work is required to delineate the full effect of home nocturnal hemodialysis on cardiac arrhythmia burden in patients with increased cardiac comorbidities.

articles.title: Renal Multiparametric MRI for Early Detection and Longitudinal Monitoring of Metabolic Dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Associated Kidney Injury: Histopathologic Validation and Multi-Omics Profiling.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney injury during metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progression remains incompletely characterized.

PURPOSE: To assess multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) for early detection and monitoring of MASLD-associated kidney injury.

STUDY TYPE: Animal model.

ANIMAL MODEL: Fifty male Sprague Dawley rats received high-fat diet plus very low-dose carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) underwent mpMRI before sacrifice at 0, 2, 4, 8, or 12 weeks (n = 10/time point). Ten MASLD and ten normal rats underwent serial MRI at each time point; ten CCl4-only rats served as nephrotoxicity controls. Twelve additional healthy rats underwent a scan-rescan test.

FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T; turbo spin-echo T2-weighted imaging, variable flip angle (VFA) gradient-echo T1 mapping, multi-echo gradient-echo blood oxygen level-dependent imaging, pulsed arterial spin labeling, echo-planar diffusion kurtosis imaging, and multi-echo Dixon imaging.

ASSESSMENT: Two radiologists (5 and 13 years of experience) quantified T1, T2*, proton density fat fraction (PDFF), mean diffusivity, mean kurtosis (MK), and renal blood flow (RBF) in cortex, outer/inner stripes of outer medulla (OSOM/ISOM). Early injury was defined as a tubular injury score ≥ 2. Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, transcriptomics, and serum metabolomics were performed.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Repeated-measures ANOVA; intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). p < 0.05 indicated significance.

RESULTS: Scan-rescan ICCs were 0.682-0.876. OSOM MK/PDFF significantly increased by Week 2 [MK (×10-3): 0.532 ± 0.007 to 0.574 ± 0.004; PDFF (%): 2.489 ± 0.243 to 3.600 ± 0.347]; cortical RBF and OSOM T2* showed no significant changes at Week 2 (p = 0.786, 1.000) but significantly decreased from Week 4. OSOM MK/PDFF had AUCs of 0.952 and 0.905 for early renal injury. Multi-omics revealed inflammatory and lipid/bile acid alterations. Dodecanedioic/hippuric acids potentially linked MASLD severity to OSOM MK.

DATA CONCLUSION: Renal mpMRI detected early kidney injury during MASLD progression.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

articles.title: Risk Factor Profiles May Differ Between Younger-Onset and Late-Onset Colorectal Cancer: An Exploratory Analysis of Individual and Cumulative Risk Factors Among the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of young-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) are on the rise globally. Despite this growing burden, the drivers of young-onset adult CRC remain largely unknown.

AIMS: This study aimed to compare risk factor profiles between younger-onset and late-onset CRC to evaluate differences in their risk factor profiles.

METHODS: The Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial dataset, comprising ∼155,000 US participants including 1219 CRC cases, was analysed.
