Participants were stratified by age (≤59 vs. ≥60 years). Associations of demographic, clinical and behavioural risk factors with CRC were computed using multivariable Cox regression with the multiplicative interaction of exposures. Reduced rank regression was used to derive dietary patterns (DPs).

RESULTS: Among the ≤59-year cohort, no individual risk factor (excluding age) was independently associated with the risk of CRC. However, the multiplicative effect of hypertension and smoking had a nominal association with younger-onset CRC (p = 0.047). In contrast, in the ≥60-year cohort, individual (sex, body mass index, diabetes and alcohol) as well as combinations of risk factors were associated with CRC. Significant DPs appeared exclusively to impact the risk of CRC in the ≥60-year cohort. However, no interactions remained significant following correction for multiple testing; findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the drivers of CRC in younger individuals may be different from their older counterparts. These exploratory findings offer novel insight into CRC risk in the young and highlight the need to reconsider interactions between CRC risk factors.

articles.title: Natural Bioactive Compounds Targeting Lipid Metabolism in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a common chronic liver disease worldwide, with abnormal lipid accumulation in hepatocytes as its principal pathological alteration. Disruption of hepatic lipid homeostasis is associated with processes such as fatty acid uptake, de novo lipogenesis (DNL), fatty acid oxidation (FAO), lipid transport, and autophagy-lipophagy-mediated clearance, and it drives the onset and progression of MASLD. Although some drugs have been approved for patients with specific metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and moderate-to-severe fibrosis, therapeutic options that are broadly applicable across the full MASLD disease spectrum, particularly for patients with early steatosis, complex metabolic phenotypes, and multiple coexisting metabolic abnormalities, remain limited in terms of population coverage, long-term safety, and clearly defined therapeutic targets. In this article, relevant databases, including PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection, were searched to include basic experimental and clinical studies related to lipid metabolism dysregulation and intervention with natural bioactive compounds within the MASLD/MASH disease spectrum, and the findings were organized according to molecular processes and clinical applications. The available evidence suggests that natural bioactive compounds may modulate hepatic lipid homeostasis by reducing fatty acid uptake and de novo lipogenesis, enhancing fatty acid oxidation, regulating lipid transport and export-related pathways, restoring autophagy-lipophagy-mediated lipid droplet clearance, and attenuating gut-liver axis dysregulation, oxidative stress, and inflammatory injury. From the perspective of lipid metabolism, this article summarizes the molecular processes, clinical evidence, and application barriers associated with natural bioactive compounds in the intervention of MASLD, with the aim of providing a basis for subsequent research on the prevention and treatment of MASLD using natural products.

articles.title: Design and Simulation of an AI-Powered Artificial Pancreas System With Personalized Glucose Sensing and Insulin Delivery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving tight glycemic control in Type 1 diabetes is challenged by non-linear metabolic dynamics and insulin-stacking risk. Artificial intelligence models offer improved personalization, but their opacity raises safety concerns, particularly for basal insulin dosing, which is often treated as static in existing decision-support systems.

METHODS: We propose a hybrid closed-loop system combining a data-driven LightGBM regressor for basal dose prediction, trained on the T1D-UOM dataset, with a physiologically grounded, rule-based safety layer at the edge. Basal insulin is predicted from cyclical time encoding and glucose rate-of-change; bolus dosing follows carbohydrate intake and correction requirements. A time-bounded insulin-on-board model, an uncertainty-adaptive post-bolus damping factor, and a predictive low-glucose-suspend rule reproducing the Tandem Basal-IQ protocol together suspend or reduce delivery when residual insulin is high or hypoglycemia is projected. The system was evaluated in silico over 60 continuous days under shadow-mode replay and closed-loop reduced-order simulation, including an ablation with bolus delivery suppressed.

RESULTS: Under chronological, within-subject validation, the offline basal estimator achieved  R 2 = 0.68  and MAE = 0.21  U; under strict leave-one-subject-out validation on the same real cohort, performance did not generalize to unseen subjects (  R 2 = - 0.49  , MAE = 0.49  U). The hybrid controller maintained Time-in-Range at 62.8% within the reduced-order closed-loop simulation, with no violations of the insulin-on-board suspension or damping rules; suppressing bolus delivery in an ablation within this simulation dropped Time-in-Range to 26.1%, indicating that, within the reduced-order model, bolus delivery is a determinant of simulated glycemic outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed architecture demonstrates a safety-audited template for combining machine-learning basal prediction with clinically grounded dosing rules. Validation on real outcome data and physical hardware is identified as the next steps toward clinical translation.

articles.title: Contribution of the srtBCD pilus cluster genes sbp1 and sbp3 to the virulence of Streptococcus suis serotype 2 sequence type 1.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus suis is an important zoonotic bacterial pathogen that causes substantial economic losses to the porcine industry and serious invasive infection in humans. Many virulence factors have been characterized as being involved in S. suis virulence and pathogenesis. Among these, the srtBCD pilus cluster gene, which encodes three type C sortases (srtB, srtC, and srtD) and four pilin subunit proteins, sbp1-sbp4, is associated with disease-causing S. suis isolates. In this study, we constructed mutant strains devoid of sbp1 and sbp3 in a virulent S. suis serotype 2 sequence type 1 strain, and evaluated the impact on virulence using both in vitro and in vivo models of infection. This study identifies sbp1 and sbp3 contribute to host-pathogen interactions. Inactivation of either gene reduced the bacterium's ability to damage epithelial cells, attach to host cells, and invade them, demonstrating their role in the early stages of infection. In addition, inactivation of sbp1 or sbp3 decreased the expression of the sortase-associated gene cluster (SSU1889, SSU1886, srtB, srtC, srtD) and several virulence-related genes, including the adhesin gene ssfsb, eno and the cytolysin gene sly, suggesting that these proteins influence a broader network. Among the two proteins, sbp1 appeared to have a greater impact on virulence, as the Δsbp1 mutant showed stronger reductions in virulence gene expression and caused lower mortality in mice, although statistical does not significant, suggesting that sbp1 plays a more prominent role than sbp3 in pathogenicity.

articles.title: UL45-46 as the preferred insertion site for herpesvirus-of-turkeys-vectored H9N2 avian influenza vaccines: comparative analysis of immunogenicity and protection.
articles.abstract: H9N2 avian influenza virus (AIV) has evolved into a threat to the global poultry industry, causing huge economic losses and persistent public health risks. Due to inadequate cellular and mucosal immunity, current inactivated vaccines fail to prevent infection and block virus transmission. The recombinant herpesvirus-of-turkeys (HVT)-vectored vaccine is a promising control strategy, but the insertion site with the higher immunogenicity of the hemagglutinin (HA) gene is still unclear. This study compared the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant HVT vaccines expressing the H9N2 HA gene at the unique long (UL)45-46 and unique short (US)2 sites. The HVT-HAUL45-46 virus maintained replication kinetics consistent with the parental HVT and demonstrated genetic stability through 20 consecutive passages. Compared with HVT-HAUS2, HVT-HAUL45-46 induced significantly higher hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody titers and stronger HA-specific cellular immunity. Following the H9N2 challenge, the UL45-46 vaccine completely prevented intestinal viral shedding and significantly reduced lung viral loads and histopathological lesions. These findings establish UL45-46 as a better insertion site for HVT-based H9N2 vaccines.

articles.title: Equine castration in Sweden: a retrospective study of postoperative complications across field and hospital practices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This retrospective study describes and compares the surgical techniques and medical protocols used for castration of male horses in Swedish ambulatory practices (Field group) and in Swedish equine hospitals (Hospital group). Data on patient characteristics, perioperative medical protocols, surgical techniques and postoperative complications were collected as documented in patient records of both groups. Descriptive statistics, univariable and multivariable analyses were used to evaluate factors associated with postoperative complication.

RESULTS: The overall complication rate was 35% in the Field group and 13% in the Hospital group. This difference remained significant after adjusting for age and breed in a multivariable analysis (OR 4.5; CI 3.18-6.36). In the Field group 511/521 horses (98%) were castrated standing using sedation and local analgesia, incisions were left un-sutured in all horses (100%). The surgical technique was described in 230/521 records (44%), the open technique was used in 194/230 horses (84%) and the half-closed technique was used in 36/230 horses (16%). Complication and surgical site infection were associated with higher odds in horses that did not receive perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (OR 1.5; CI 1.01-2.36 and OR 1.7; CI 1.08-2.82 respectively). In the Hospital group, 554 stallions were castrated under general anaesthesia, and the incisions were sutured in 473/554 horses (85%). The closed technique was used in 503/554 horses (91%) and the half-closed was used in 51/554 (9%). Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis was administered to all horses in the Hospital group. Postoperative antimicrobial prophylaxis did not decrease the odds of surgical site infection in any of the groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In Sweden, standing, open castration with un-sutured incisions was preferred in ambulatory practice, whereas a closed, sutured technique dominated in the hospitals. Field castration was associated with a substantially higher odds of postoperative complications, compared with hospital-based castrations performed under general anaesthesia. These findings provide locally relevant evidence to guide clinical decision-making and antimicrobial stewardship and may contribute to the ethical discussion regarding the use of standing castration when alternatives are feasible.

articles.title: Multiorgan failure in a young patient with necrotizing fasciitis: a case report of septic shock progressing to mixed shock with fatal cardiac outcome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rare, life-threatening conditions requiring immediate and aggressive treatment. Despite advances in medical care, mortality remains high, largely due to septic shock and severe complications.

CASE REPRESENTATION: We report the case of a young adult with necrotizing fasciitis (NF) of the left leg complicated by recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding and infective endocarditis, resulting in severe heart failure and ultimately leading to death. The fatal outcome was most likely attributable to prolonged sepsis with multiorgan involve- and impairment and a 1.5-cm paravalvular abscess caused by vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium.

CONCLUSION: The treatment of a septic patient with progressive heart failure highlights the value of an integrative, multidisciplinary approach to complex clinical decision-making and the real-world challenges that may require patient-tailored, nonstandard therapeutic strategies. Prompt diagnosis, aggressive surgical debridement, and rigorous management of complications are essential. In cases of aortic valve regurgitation causing heart failure, TAVI implantation might serve as a temporary bridge until definitive open valve replacement becomes feasible.

articles.title: Drawing before counting: causal diagrams and g-methods in critical care evidence synthesis.
White Matter Hyperintensities Modify CYP2C19 Effect on Stroke Progression in Small Vessel Occlusion.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between CYP2C19 loss-of-function (LOF) alleles and early neurological deterioration (END) in acute small vessel occlusion (SVO) patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remains inconsistent. We hypothesized that white matter hyperintensities (WMH) burden act as a key moderator and investigated whether this modulates the association between CYP2C19 LOF and END.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of SVO patients receiving DAPT. CYP2C19 genotypes were classified as LOF carriers or non-carriers. The primary endpoint was END; secondary and safety endpoints included severe END, 90-day mRS 0-2, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), bleeding, and mortality. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes assessed associations between CYP2C19, WMH, and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 247 patients (median age 67.0 years; 28.7% female; 60.7% CYP2C19 LOF carriers), 54 (21.9%) experienced END. Multivariable analysis identified infarct diameter (aOR 1.26, 95% CI 1.13-1.39, p < 0.001) and total cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) burden (aOR 2.02, 95% CI 1.37-2.98, p < 0.001) as independent predictors. A significant multiplicative interaction was observed between CYP2C19 LOF and severe WMH on END risk (aOR 9.34, 95% CI 2.06-48.10, p = 0.005). Stratified analysis showed CYP2C19 LOF significantly increased END risk specifically in patients with severe WMH (aOR 3.44, 95% CI 1.12-10.55, p = 0.030), but not mild WMH. Predicted probability curves suggested a Fazekas score threshold of approximately 2.70. Secondary and safety outcomes were infrequent.

CONCLUSIONS: CYP2C19 LOF alleles increase END risk in SVO patients specifically with severe WMH. These findings highlight the value of integrating genetic and neuroimaging markers for risk stratification and personalized antiplatelet therapy.

articles.title: Sex differences in fibrillar collagen composition are linked to subcutaneous adipose tissue expandability and adipocyte precursor proliferation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physiological expansion of subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) protects against harmful lipid deposition and metabolic disease and is generally greater in women than men. We hypothesised that sex differences in fibrillar collagen composition and remodelling contribute to differences in SAT expansion and function.

METHODS: SAT from age- and BMI-matched men and women, SAT from male and female mice exposed to a high-fat diet to induce adipose tissue expansion and obesity, and publicly available human SAT and VAT RNA sequencing data sets were analysed. SAT was assessed by proteomics, histology, Western blot, qRT-PCR and flow cytometry. The 3T3-L1 preadipocyte cell line was used to test the effect of altered collagen type 1-to-3 ratio.

RESULTS: Men showed greater SAT fibrosis than women. Fibrillar collagen levels correlated negatively with BMI in women but positively with cholesterol and liver enzyme levels in men. Despite similar adiposity, HFD-induced obese female mice had healthier metabolic profiles and fewer fibroinflammatory SAT changes than males. HFD preferentially induced Col1a1 in males and Col3a1 in females. Unchallenged male mice had a higher collagen type 1-to-3 ratio than females, and a similar sex difference was observed in humans. A lower, female-like collagen type 1-to-3 ratio increased preadipocyte proliferation. Consistently, acute HFD increased proliferation of SAT PDGFRβ+ adipogenic stem cells in females only.

CONCLUSIONS: Sex differences in fibrillar collagen composition and remodelling may promote greater SAT expansion in females by facilitating adipogenic precursor proliferation and limiting fibroinflammatory changes during obesity.

articles.title: An exploratory evaluation of an online course on the second victim phenomenon: effects on knowledge, perceptions, beliefs, and transfer to clinical practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Second Victim Phenomenon describes the psychological distress experienced by healthcare professionals following adverse patient events. Despite its high prevalence and implications for staff well-being, team functioning, and patient safety, awareness and structured educational approaches addressing SVP remain limited. Moreover, empirical evidence on whether educational interventions improve knowledge, influence attitudes, and enable the transfer of learning into clinical practice is still scarce.

METHODS: We conducted an exploratory multidimensional longitudinal evaluation of a 90-minute asynchronous online course on the Second Victim Phenomenon. The course was distributed through the German Interdisciplinary Association for Intensive and Emergency Medicine (DIVI) Academy. Participants completed questionnaires at three time points: before the course (T1), immediately after completion (T2), and three weeks later (T3). The survey assessed baseline characteristics, attitudes toward SVP, and case-based knowledge using vignette items. Learning transfer was examined using a validated instrument measuring training design (learning field), workplace conditions (functional field), and short- and long-term transfer success. Descriptive statistics and paired comparisons were used to evaluate changes in knowledge, perceptions and beliefs.

RESULTS: Ninety-seven participants completed the baseline survey, with 49 completing the postcourse assessment and 47 completing the three-week follow-up. The participants had a median age of 39.0 years (IQR 30-48), and a median professional experience of 13.5 years (IQR 6.5-22). Knowledge scores were significantly higher following course participation (8-item score after exclusion of two items with negative item-rest correlations: from 5.59 to 6.33; p = 0.041). Perceptions and beliefs toward the relevance of SVP and the value of prevention programs were already high at baseline and showed only minor changes. Participants rated the course highly for its didactic design, transfer orientation, and motivation to apply the content. At follow-up, participants reported moderate levels of perceived transfer into clinical practice. However, perceived support from supervisors was comparatively low, suggesting that organizational conditions may limit sustained implementation.

CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory findings suggest that an asynchronous online course may contribute to knowledge gain and early stages of perceived learning transfer regarding the Second Victim Phenomenon. However, sustainable integration of second victim support concepts appears to depend not only on individual learning but also on organizational factors such as leadership engagement and workplace support.

articles.title: Etoposide-induced angina in a patient with small cell lung carcinoma: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of cisplatin and etoposide is a standard therapy for small cell lung cancer; however, ischemic heart disease is a known complication. We report a rare case of effort angina pectoris that worsened during initial treatment of small cell lung cancer with etoposide.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old Asian male was admitted to our hospital with effort angina. Coronary angiography revealed severe stenosis with significant calcification of the proximal right coronary artery. Computed tomography revealed a 21-mm-sized nodule in the right upper lobe and hilar lymphadenopathy suggestive of lung cancer. The patient underwent thoracoscopic wedge resection before coronary revascularization, and intraoperative findings indicated a small cell carcinoma with hilar lymph node metastases. Early postoperative definitive treatment consisting of chemotherapy with cisplatin plus etoposide and accelerated hyperfractionated radiation was planned. During the first chemotherapy session, on postoperative day 7, the patient complained of chest pain, and an electrocardiogram showed slight ST depression in leads V5 and V6 while receiving etoposide; nitroglycerin improved his symptoms. Although treatment was resumed with the administration of nicorandil the next day, the same symptoms were observed during the infusion of etoposide. Accordingly, chemoradiation therapy was suspended and revascularization of the right coronary artery was performed. Etoposide and cisplatin were readministered 3 days after revascularization, without any chest symptoms.

CONCLUSION: Chemotherapy for malignant tumors carries the risk of progression to coronary artery disease. To prevent serious ischemic events, sufficient discussions between oncologists and cardiologists and careful observation of chest symptoms are needed.

articles.title: A case of complicated chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps treated with dupilumab, in the UK: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a prevalent inflammatory disorder of the nasal and paranasal mucosa, affecting approximately 1 in 10 people and contributing to substantial symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Phenotypically, CRS is classified into two subtypes based on the presence or absence of nasal polyps-benign inflammatory outgrowths of the nasal mucosa-which occur in roughly 20% of affected individuals. Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) is predominantly driven by type 2 (T-helper 2) inflammation, typically characterised by eosinophilic infiltration and involvement of interleukins, such as IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13. Given this immunopathology, biologic therapies, such as Dupilumab, Omalizumab and Mepolizumab, initially developed for asthma, have shown efficacy in this patient population. They are readily used in the United States (US) and European Union (EU) in cases of severe CRSwNP, but are not currently authorised for NHS use.

CASE PRESENTATION: We describe a case of severe, refractory CRSwNP complicated by recurrent left periorbital abscess and dehiscence of the floor of the left frontal sinus in a white, male patient in his sixties. The condition persisted despite multiple surgical polypectomies, repeated courses of systemic antibiotics (oral and intravenous), topical and systemic steroids, and drainage of periorbital collections. At the time, Dupilumab was not routinely commissioned by the NHS for this indication. However, following a successful application to NHS England's Individual Funding Request (IFR) process, funding for Dupilumab was granted.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with Dupilumab led to complete resolution of symptoms and significant improvement in quality of life. The patient remains under regular follow-up with ongoing clinical stability and no reported adverse effects.

articles.title: The global research landscape of emergency medical services in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major cause of death, and emergency medical services (EMS) are central to recognition, resuscitation, transport, and linkage to post-arrest care. Although previous bibliometric studies have mapped the broader cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation literature, the intersection of EMS and OHCA warrants focused characterization.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective bibliometric analysis of records indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 1972 through June 2026. The search combined OHCA terms with terms for EMS, paramedics, and emergency medical technicians. Annual output, research categories, journals, authors, and countries were described. VOSviewer version 1.6.20 was used for author co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and cited-reference co-citation analyses.

RESULTS: The search identified 3,005 records. Annual output increased markedly after 2010, peaked at 244 publications in 2021, and remained above 200 publications per year from 2022 to 2025; 130 records were indexed for the partial 2026 year. Emergency Medicine (1,745; 58.1%) and Critical Care Medicine (1,014; 33.7%) were the most frequently assigned Web of Science categories. Resuscitation published 694 records (23.1%). The United States had the greatest country-level output (1,022; 34.0%), followed by Japan (375; 12.5%) and Canada (281; 9.4%). The most prolific author was Shin SD (98 publications). Co-authorship mapping showed registry-centered regional communities, while keyword analysis yielded ten interpreted domains spanning epidemiology, resuscitation interventions, dispatch, registries, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, equity, and technology-related topics. Co-citation analysis identified four major intellectual communities.

CONCLUSION: EMS-focused OHCA publications indexed in Web of Science show sustained output and international collaboration associated with established registries. Limited visibility of low- and middle-income settings within this database warrants further investigation. Equity, implementation, and digital and resuscitative technologies are potential areas for further research; the pooled network analysis does not establish their temporal growth.

articles.title: Greenness, Air Pollution, and Insulin Resistance in a Latin American Megacity: A Longitudinal Mediation Analysis of the ELSA‑Brasil Cohort ​.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. The role of air pollution on this association remains unclear. We investigated whether air pollution mediated the association between greenness and insulin resistance, among non-diabetic participants (N = 2715) from the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA-Brasil) in São Paulo megacity, Brazil, followed-up for approximately 8 years (2008-2010, 2012-2014, 2017-2019). Neighborhood greenness (NDVI, in quartiles), air pollution (PM2.5 and PM10), and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) were examined using mediation analysis, allowing for exposure-mediator interaction. Total, natural direct, and natural indirect effects were estimated, using mixed-effects models, stratified by the neighborhood socioeconomic status (NSES) and adjusted for individual age, sex, education and income. In PM10 analysis for participants from low NSES, higher neighborhood greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance, in a dose-response pattern, as indicated by the total (β = -0.49, 95% CI -0.91, -0.05; β = -0.20, 95% CI -0.54, 0.16; and β = -0.07, 95% CI -0.38, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively) and natural direct effects (β = -0.59, 95% CI -1.06, -0.09; β = -0.32, 95% CI -0.67, 0.03; and β = -0.05, 95% CI -0.37, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively). The natural indirect effect indicated no mediation by PM10. Similar results were found for the PM2.5 analysis. Greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance among adults living in low NSES areas. However, no evidence of air pollution mediation was found. These results suggest that greater neighborhood greenness may be associated with better cardiometabolic health in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas.

articles.title: Early clinical experience with vericiguat after acute decompensated heart failure in elderly patients with HFrEF: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Vericiguat has demonstrated clinical benefit in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), particularly in those at high risk of recurrent heart failure events. However, evidence regarding its early use in elderly patients following hospitalization for acute decompensated HF (ADHF) remains limited. In this prospective single-center case series, 143 consecutive patients aged > 70 years hospitalized for ADHF with HFrEF were enrolled and vericiguat was administrated. Clinical evaluations, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), six-minute walk test (6MWT), Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ), and laboratory parameters were assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks. After 4 weeks of treatment with vericiguat, 44.8% of patients were in NYHA class II and 55.2% in NYHA class III, no patients were in NYHA class IV (p < 0.001); LVEF improved from 34 ± 4.7% to 46.8 ± 7.5% (p < 0.0001); exercise capacity increased significantly (p < 0.001), while a significant decrease in MLHF-Q, NT-proBNP levels and hsCRP was observed (p < 0.001). No symptomatic hypotension, syncope or relevant deterioration in renal function or electrolytes occurred during the observation period. In this single-arm cohort of older patients with HFrEF recently stabilized after ADHF, initiation of vericiguat was feasible and coincided with substantial short-term changes in functional status, LVEF, and circulating biomarkers, without major safety signals during 4 weeks of observation. Given the absence of a control group, these changes cannot be attributed to vericiguat and may reflect, at least in part, recovery from the acute event, decongestion, optimization of background therapy, learning effects, and regression to the mean. These findings should therefore be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in controlled studies.

articles.title: Beyond Caregiver Burden: Challenges of Haredi Mothers Caring for Adult Children with Mental Illness in Israel.
articles.abstract: Family caregiving for people with serious mental illness involves substantial emotional, relational, and practical demands. Yet less is known about how religion and close-knit religious communities shape mothers' caregiving challenges. This study explores the challenges faced by Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) mothers caring for an adult child with serious mental illness in Israel. Drawing on the ecological model for health promotion (EMHP), the study examines how caregiving experiences are shaped across intrapersonal, interpersonal, institutional, community, and broader systemic contexts. In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 Haredi mothers caring for an adult child with serious mental illness, and data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants' accounts suggested interconnected challenges across all ecological levels. At the intrapersonal level, mothers described shock, guilt, helplessness, and a sense of loss. At the interpersonal level, mothers described disruptions to family relationships. At the institutional level, mothers experienced exclusion from treatment decisions and tensions between psychiatric care and Haredi norms, while some questioned the professional oversight of community-based alternatives. At the community level, stigma, social distancing, secrecy, and concerns about family reputation and children's marriage prospects shaped caregiving and access to social support. At the systemic level, fragmented services, bureaucratic barriers, and limited resources increased mothers' coordination responsibilities. These accounts suggest that caregiving may be embedded across religious, familial, communal, institutional, and health-system contexts, with challenges at one level potentially intensifying demands at others. These exploratory insights suggest potential directions for culturally tailored interventions that integrate rabbinic guidance with psychiatric care and address systemic service coordination, subject to further research in larger and more diverse samples.

articles.title: Mechanism and clinical Fdiagnostic performance of miR-10b-3p as a novel biomarker for coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) continues to demonstrate escalating global incidence and mortality rates, imposing substantial burdens on both healthcare systems and socioeconomic development. This study aimed to analyze the predictive value and potential molecular mechanism of miR-10b-3p in patients with CAD. miR-10b-3p and DERL3 levels were determined by RT-qPCR. ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance. Correlations were tested by Pearson's correlation test. The viability of the cells was assessed by CCK-8 and flow cytometry. Compared with the control group, miR-10b-3p was down​regulated in CAD patients, and the expression in ischemic group was lower than that in non-ischemic group. miR-10b-3p serves as an effective biomarker for distinguishing healthy individuals from CAD patients, as well as differentiating ischemic from non-ischemic patients. Additionally, miR-10b-3p combined with CT-FFR parameters has a high diagnostic efficacy for ischemic stenosis in CAD patients. Mechanistically, miR-10b-3p mimic inhibited the proliferation and MDA levels of HASMCs after ox-LDL exposure, while promoting​ apoptosis and SOD activity. Upregulation of DERL3 partially reversed the regulation of miR-10b-3p mimic on HASMCs biological function. miR-10b-3p has a predictive effect on ischemic stenosis of CAD, and mechanistic studies indicate upregulated miR-10b-3p's protective effects via DERL3 inhibition.

articles.title: Deep learning denoising and deep learning-augmented contrast enhancement improve ultra-high-resolution photon-counting-detector CCTA image quality.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) using a photon-counting detector (PCD) provides excellent spatial resolution but is limited by increased image noise. We evaluated whether deep learning (DL)-based denoising and contrast enhancement can further improve UHR-CCTA image quality.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: UHR-CCTA scans from 25 patients with coronary artery disease were retrospectively analyzed. Images were reconstructed at 0.2-mm slice thickness without and with quantum iterative reconstruction (QIR, Qoff-Q4), and subsequently processed using a DL tool for denoising and increasing iodine contrast enhancement. Subjective image quality (sharpness, noise, vessel wall delineation, and overall quality) was assessed by three radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. Objective analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and coronary wall sharpness. Differences between image sets were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

RESULTS: DL-based CCTA demonstrated significantly superior subjective image quality across all parameters compared to standard reconstructions, with an overall median image quality ([interquartile interval, IQR]: 4 [3-5] versus 2 [2-3], p < 0.001). SNR and CNR were significantly higher for DL-based CCTA across all QIR levels (all p < 0.001). The highest values were observed for DL-based CCTAQ4 versus UHR-CCTAQ4 (SNR: 258.0 ± 147.5 versus 145.2 ± 50.1; CNR: 25.8 ± 17.1 versus 11.1 ± 4.5; both p < 0.001). Coronary wall sharpness was improved for DL-based CCTA for Q1-4 (all p < 0.027).

CONCLUSION: DL-based denoising and iodine contrast enhancement effectively reduce noise and improve anatomic detail in UHR-CCTA, providing incremental value beyond vendor-specific reconstruction, particularly at high QIR strength levels.

KEY POINTS: Question Deep learning reduces noise and enhances contrast in ultrahigh-resolution coronary CT angiography. Findings Image quality improves beyond standard iterative reconstruction methods, and vessel wall sharpness and diagnostic clarity significantly increase. Relevance statement This study aimed to determine at which levels of vendor-specific iterative reconstruction, DL-based denoising and contrast enhancement perform best in UHR CCTA, providing a foundation for future investigations on how these technical improvements may translate into diagnostic benefits.

articles.title: Calibration of the ICH Score for Mortality Prediction in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) score is the most widely used tool for early mortality prognostication after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage, but its original calibration table (derived in 1997-1998) may not generalize across settings, and its use may contribute to the mortality it predicts through early withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment (WLST). We assessed the score's calibration-in-the-large, variation across score range, and association with WLST. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases were searched for studies applying the ICH score and reporting mortality; data were extracted in duplicate [Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews of Prediction Modelling Studies (CHARMS)] and risk of bias assessed with the Prediction Model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST). The primary outcome was pooled observed-to-expected (O:E) mortality ratio by random effects; secondary outcomes included pooled discrimination (c-statistic), O:E by score point, and meta-regression of mortality on WLST rate. Out of 955 records, 137 studies (estimated 86,871 patients) were included. Among 14 studies with calibration data, the pooled O:E ratio was 0.71 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.48-1.05; p = 0.081; fixed-effect, 0.90; 95% CI 0.84-0.96; prediction interval, 0.17-2.97; I2 = 96%], driven by 1 discordant study (O:E > 2). By score point (nine studies), mortality was underestimated at 0-2 and overestimated at 3-6, crossing near 2-3. Discrimination remained good across 70 studies (c-statistic, 0.826; 95% CI 0.808-0.842; prediction interval, 0.674-0.916), unaffected by risk of bias. Across 19 studies, WLST remained significantly associated with observed mortality (coefficient, 0.021/percentage point; 95% CI 0.006-0.036; p = 0.0077; R2 = 32%). Risk of bias was high in 114/137 studies (83%), mainly in the analysis domain (105/137; 77%). Discrimination remained good throughout, but the original calibration table is not a reliable single reference for absolute mortality; the pooled deviation from it was imprecise and depended on one outlying study, and calibration moved in different directions at the two ends of the score. Because withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment tracked observed mortality, prognostic conversations after intracerebral hemorrhage should draw on current, score-specific mortality data rather than the original table alone and should avoid letting an early prediction become self-fulfilling.

articles.title: Early Postoperative Complications After Decompressive Craniectomy for Pediatric Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive craniectomy (DC) is used to treat refractory intracranial hypertension after pediatric severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI), but early postoperative neurosurgical complications and their predictors-particularly intracranial pressure (ICP) burden-remain inconsistently characterized.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive pediatric patients (< 18 years) with sTBI [Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 3-8] who underwent DC at a single high-volume trauma center. Early postoperative neurosurgical complications were defined a priori as events occurring within 7 days after DC or before hospital discharge: secondary intracranial hemorrhage, central nervous system (CNS) infection, wound dehiscence, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak. Associations with injury severity, imaging, and ICP variables (mean intraoperative ICP; cumulative duration of ICP > 20 mm Hg before DC) were evaluated.

RESULTS: Of 104 screened records, 83 children were included. At least one early neurosurgical complication occurred in 33/83 patients (39.8%). Secondary intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 29/83 (34.9%), CNS infection in 7/83 (8.4%), wound dehiscence in 6/83 (7.2%), and CSF leak in 4/83 (4.8%). Among the 69 children with ICP monitoring, patients with complications had significantly higher intraoperative ICP (40.5 ± 13.5 vs. 28.6 ± 4.3 mm Hg; p = 0.0058) and longer pre-DC duration of ICP > 20 mm Hg (4.1 ± 5.9 vs. 1.6 ± 2.5 h; p = 0.0296). At 6 months, 25/83 (30.1%) had died; among survivors, 28/58 (48.3%) achieved a favorable outcome [Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) 4-5].

CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative complications after pediatric DC were common and predominantly hemorrhagic. Greater ICP burden before and during DC was associated with these events. The co-occurrence of CSF leak and CNS infection highlights the importance of dural closure strategies that minimize CSF egress and the need for vigilant postoperative surveillance.

articles.title: Breathing in an Accelerated World: Temporality, Ethical Repertoires, and Medical Students' Examination Texts on Advanced Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Medical students are commonly examined on ethically difficult clinical decisions, yet examination scripts have rarely been treated as a distinct empirical object in medical humanities. This article analyses 61 anonymised written examination responses from Danish medical students addressing acute respiratory failure in a fictional patient with advanced amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The study is framed as a genre analysis of examination texts, operationalised through repeated close reading, inductive coding of recurrent textual moves, and abductive interpretation through Hartmut Rosa's concepts of acceleration and resonance. Four ethical repertoires were identified: accelerated stabilisation; prognostic triage and the limit of intervention; distributed responsibility and the search for a legitimate pause; and fragile resonance through attention to wishes, dignity, and palliative alternatives. Across the corpus, students wrote judgement through temporal distinctions between urgency and delay, reversibility and progression, and escalation and proportionate limitation. The findings do not show professionalism as such, but rather the institutionally legitimate ways in which professional judgement is made legible under assessment. Examination scripts matter for medical humanities because they make curricular normativity and evaluative pressure textually visible, showing how future clinicians are taught to write responsibility, uncertainty, and care into the same ethical scene. These repertoires also render an ableist prognostic imagination institutionally legible-one in which ventilator-dependent life is readily scripted in advance as a future to be avoided rather than supported-linking the temporal analysis to critical disability studies' account of the curative imaginary.

articles.title: Impact of pre-chemotherapy food intake on chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in patients with early breast cancer: a subanalysis of the randomized SUCCESS C trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) remains a challenging side effect, significantly impacting patients' quality of life [1-3]. Knowledge of eating behaviour's influence on CINV is still limited. This study improves the understanding of CINV by investigating the impact of pre-chemotherapy food intake within the randomized Phase III SUCCESS C trial.

METHODS: The SUCCESS C trial (NCT00847444), enrolled ,463 women with early-stage, HER2-negative breast cancer, receiving either three cycles of 5-fluorouracil (500 mg/m2), epirubicin (100 mg/m2), and cyclophosphamide (500 mg/m2) followed by three cycles of docetaxel (100 mg/m2) every 3 weeks (FEC), or six cycles of docetaxel (75 mg/m2) and cyclophosphamide (600 mg/m2) (TC). The present analysis included patients with completed CINV diary with hourly documentation over 5 days post-chemotherapy.

RESULTS: CINV diary data during chemotherapy cycles 1-3 were available for 1582 patients, of whom 814 received FEC and 768 TC. Patient characteristics between chemotherapy arms were comparable. For FEC, pre-chemotherapy eating behaviour had a significant impact on nausea-free survival (NFS) in cycle 1 (p = 0.04) and on emesis-free survival (EFS) in cycle 2 (p = 0.02). For TC, no effect on NFS, but a significant effect on EFS (p = 0.04 in cycle 1; p < 0.01 in cycle 2), was observed. Median EFS was approximately 120 h for all cycles and treatments.

CONCLUSION: This analysis demonstrates in both regimens less emesis, and for FEC less nausea, of patients with pre-chemotherapy food intake. The effect was most pronounced during the first 24 h after chemotherapy administration. Thus, eating behaviour influences CINV outcomes and warrants further evaluation.

articles.title: Neuronavigation-assisted versus conventional endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenomas: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence on the benefit of intraoperative neuronavigation in endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal (EET) pituitary surgery remains mixed. We conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing navigation-assisted and conventional EET surgery for pituitary adenomas, to estimate the effect size for a definitive multicentre trial.

METHODS: At Ain Shams University (April 2025-February 2026), 57 patients with pituitary adenomas were assessed for eligibility; 7 were excluded for prior Gamma Knife radiosurgery. The remaining 50 were randomized 1:1 within strata of tumor size, functional status, and surgery status, with concealed computer-generated allocation. Recruitment continued until the planned 25 patients per arm were enrolled. The primary outcome was extent of resection; secondary outcomes included operative time, blood loss, visual and hormonal outcomes, and complications.

RESULTS: All 50 patients (25 per arm) were analyzed by intention-to-treat. Gross total resection was numerically higher with navigation (28.0% vs. 16.0%; p = 0.496); adjusted for Knosp grade, the odds ratio was 2.66 (95% CI 0.41-17.06) versus a crude 2.04. Extent of resection was strongly associated with tumor size, functioning status, and Knosp grade; no giant adenoma achieved gross total resection. Blood loss was lower with navigation (median 250 vs. 350 mL; p = 0.016), with no difference in operative time, which included navigation setup (p = 0.788).

CONCLUSION: Neuronavigation did not significantly improve extent of resection, though resection completeness trended favorably with navigation across most subgroups. The associated blood-loss reduction remains hypothesis-generating. A definitive, adequately powered multicentre trial is warranted.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Pan African Clinical Trial Registry, PACTR202608562462156, registered retrospectively on 17 August 2026.

articles.title: Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previously, reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated H3K9ac were observed in placentas from women with preeclampsia. Building on these findings, this study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is associated with changes in placental histone modifications. Immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence were performed on placental sections from 60 patients stratified into four groups: women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed groups compared to unvaccinated controls, with the most pronounced reduction observed in women with prior infection during gestation. H3K9ac levels did not differ significantly between groups in any compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between SCT H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight, and a sensitivity analysis excluding cases with additional placental pathologies confirmed the robustness of the findings. As no gene expression profiling was performed, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 changes cannot be inferred. These descriptive findings warrant further investigation integrating epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches to clarify their functional relevance for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: The neuroscience of delirium: a perfect storm for acute brain dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Delirium is a frequent and distressing neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by acute disturbances of attention, awareness and cognition. Delirium emerges in response to diverse medical insults, particularly in hospitalized patients. Despite its high prevalence and association with accelerated cognitive decline, dementia and mortality, the neurobiology of delirium remains incompletely understood, and there are no treatments for delirium. Evidence from electrophysiology, neuroimaging, biomarkers and emerging animal models has begun to clarify the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying delirium. Delirium can be conceptualized as the interaction of acute systemic or cerebral stressors with pre-existing vulnerabilities, creating a 'perfect storm' for brain dysfunction. Generalized electroencephalographic slowing and network disintegration are convergent signatures across diverse types of delirium. Disruptions in neuromodulatory systems, energy metabolism and neuroimmune signalling may underlie impairment of large-scale brain function. The mechanisms that drive acute delirium may also contribute to subsequent brain injury and long-term decline, compounding its broad personal and societal impact.

articles.title: Early versus delayed impella unloading during venoarterial ECMO for cardiogenic shock: a propensity-matched analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
articles.abstract: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) restores perfusion in cardiogenic shock but increases left-ventricular afterload. Impella unloading (ECPELLA) is increasingly used, but optimal timing remains uncertain. We retrospectively analyzed adults with cardiogenic shock treated with VA-ECMO and Impella from 2016 to 2025. Early ECPELLA was Impella placement from the calendar day before through the day after VA-ECMO initiation; delayed ECPELLA was placement 2-7 days after VA-ECMO initiation. One-to-one propensity-score matching balanced 35 covariates. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Sensitivity analyses included acute kidney injury (AKI) restriction, VA-ECMO-indexed follow-up, and a 7-day landmark analysis. Matching yielded 282 per group. Mortality was similar at 30 days (48.9% vs. 49.6%; risk ratio [RR] 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.17), 90 days (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.17), and 1 year (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.18). Early ECPELLA was associated with more renal-replacement therapy (RRT) at 30 days (37.4% vs. 21.7%; RR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.31), but not when follow-up began at VA-ECMO initiation in AKI-restricted cohorts (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.81-1.22; adjusted hazard ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.82-1.26). Major bleeding, sepsis, and limb ischemia were similar. Durable LVAD implantation was less frequent with early ECPELLA at 1 year (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.34-0.95), but not in sensitivity analyses. Early ECPELLA was not associated with improved survival compared with delayed ECPELLA. The RRT association was not reproduced with aligned follow-up. Residual confounding and immortal-time bias limit causal inference and warrant randomized trials.

articles.title: Anti-IgLON5 disease presenting as recurrent life-threatening laryngospasm and respiratory failure.
Municipal Wastewater is a Significant Source of Fibrous Microplastics in the Environment.
articles.journal: Bulletin of environmental contamination and toxicology
articles.abstract: Microplastic fibers (MPFs) have been discovered as the most prevalent form of microplastics in the environment, especially in aquatic systems. Household laundries are considered to be a major source of MPFs entering our ecosystems through wastewater discharge. Here, we investigated the occurrence, distribution, and characterization of MPFs from the twenty municipal wastewater sites in Sialkot, Pakistan. Morphological analysis revealed a variety of microplastics, including fibers, fragments, films, beads/pellets, and rubber particles. The total abundance of microplastics was documented as 36.95 ± 10.39 particles/L. Fibers were noted as the most dominant forms, comprising diverse polymer types, including polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), polyamide (PA), and acrylic fibers, along with phthalic-related compounds associated with plastic additives. PVC fibers were the most abundant, contributing about 24% of the total MPFs. This study demonstrates that domestic wastewater discharge plays a key role in transporting MPFs into the aquatic environment.

articles.title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), including preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, are strongly associated with maternal cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy. We hypothesized that maternal inflammation drives persistent postpartum cardiac maladaptation after HDPs. We conducted a prospective longitudinal study assessing cardiac function and circulating inflammatory profiles during pregnancy and 3-6 months postpartum, complemented by a preclinical mechanistic mouse model recapitulating key antenatal and postpartum immune and cardiac features of HDPs. Here we show that distinct antenatal inflammatory signatures, including elevated chemokines, correlated with adverse left ventricular structure and function 3-6 months postpartum, despite resolution of systemic inflammation. Mechanistically, our preclinical HDP mouse model demonstrates that reduced antenatal progesterone, also observed in patients with HDPs, drives inflammation and postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Antenatal (embryonic day 14.5), but not postpartum (postpartum day 28), progesterone treatment prevented postpartum cardiac dysfunction, identifying both a potential mechanistic and therapeutic strategy to reduce long-term maternal cardiovascular morbidity.

articles.title: Decoding genetic cardiomyopathy through functional phenotyping.
Multiparametric assessment of TNNI3 variant phenotypes in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes correlates with disease severity in patients.
articles.abstract: Routine genetic testing of patients with cardiomyopathy has identified many causative genetic variants. However, in most instances, the impact of these variants on physiological function and clinical outcomes remains unclear. Here we develop a high-throughput human induced pluripotent stem-cell-based platform to measure the effects of variants in cardiac troponin I (encoded by TNNI3) on systolic and diastolic force generation and calcium handling. By integrating contractility and calcium signaling, we accurately distinguish pathogenic from nonpathogenic TNNI3 variants and characterize the pathogenic effects of variants of uncertain significance. Further, by evaluating the clinical presentations of patients with TNNI3 cardiomyopathy from a single site, we demonstrate that diastolic function in vitro correlates with age at onset (R2 = 0.6), a measure of disease severity. The ability to comprehensively characterize in vitro variant effects that correlate with clinical outcomes should help identify mechanisms underlying variable disease severity and enhance the discovery of class-targeted treatments.

articles.title: Perinatal maternal and child growth mediate the association between maternal education and children's overweight/obesity in Europe: the Feel4Diabetes-study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early-life factors and maternal education interact with childhood overweight/obesity through pathways that remain unclear. Our aim was to investigate the predominant perinatal correlates of childhood overweight/obesity and their mediating effects on the association between maternal education and children's overweight/obesity.

SUBJECTS/METHODS: In this cross-sectional study the total sample included 12211 children (4-12 years-old) from low socioeconomic status (SES) regions in six European countries, with 2663 having complete data for analysis.

INTERVENTIONS/METHODS: All measurements were carried out during August-September 2016. Children's anthropometrics were measured and parents self-reported all other data (perinatal/ sociodemographic) via questionnaires. Associations were adjusted for maternal education, child age and sex, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Maternal overweight (OR 1.54 (95% CI 1.19-1.99)), obesity (OR 2.51 (95% CI 1.57-4.00)), pre-pregnancy diabetes (OR 4.92 (95% CI 1.31-18.38)), smoking during pregnancy (OR 1.59 (95% CI 1.20-2.10)) and excessive gestational weight gain (OR 2.00 (95% CI 2.59-2.53)) were associated with childhood overweight/obesity. Children born small-for-gestational-age (OR 0.57 (95% CI 0.36-0.89)) had lower odds, whereas those born long-for-gestational-age (OR 1.49 (95% CI 1.15-1.92)) had higher odds of childhood overweight/obesity. Rapid weight gain during the first 6 months was positively associated (OR 1.30 (95% CI 1.04-1.63)) with overweight/obesity in children. Maternal pre-pregnancy weight status, rapid weight gain in the first 6 months and gestational weight gain mediated by 16.6%, 8.4%, and 7.8%, respectively, the maternal education-child obesity link.

CONCLUSION: Perinatal factors play a crucial role in the onset of childhood obesity, and evidence suggests their association with maternal education. Families with lower education should be targeted, aiming to raise awareness of health issues related to maternal/children's healthy lifestyle and improve nutrition knowledge, aiming to ensure healthy maternal weight prior to and during pregnancy and normal infant growth.

articles.title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.
articles.abstract: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30-60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

articles.title: The neonatal brain surface on cranial ultrasound: Developmental anatomy and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Cranial ultrasound is the most widely used neuroimaging modality in neonatal intensive care and allows the cortical surface to be followed longitudinally at the bedside; yet, a clinically applicable framework for reading it is lacking. In this narrative review we describe six landmarks-the lateral fissure, insula, sulcus centralis, sulci precentrales and frontales, sulcus cinguli, and sulcus olfactorius-each in terms of anatomy, development, sonographic appearance, and clinical relevance, and each section closing with a bedside summary for pattern recognition. Every landmark is dated twice, on ultrasound and at the postmortem examination; the interval between the two is reported to narrow from about 8 weeks before 28 weeks postmenstrual age to none beyond 31 weeks. Because the thalamus and subplate are central to cortical development, lesions of white and deep grey matter-periventricular leukomalacia and venous infarction complicating intraventricular haemorrhage-may disrupt primary gyration, including altered morphology of the sulcus centralis, whereas direct cortical injury occurs in arterial ischaemic stroke, perinatal asphyxia, sinovenous thrombosis, and meningitis. Altered folding is seen in polymicrogyria, tuberous sclerosis, arhinencephaly, and midline anomalies. Recognizing these landmarks allows cortical maturation to be judged against postmenstrual age, and a cortical lesion to be localized, attributed to a mechanism, and related to the functions it places at risk, including cerebral palsy and cerebral visual impairment.

articles.title: Switching Catalytic Modes: A pH-Responsive Bimetallic Nanozyme for Dynamic Microenvironment Remodeling and Infected Wound Self-Adaptive Treatment.
articles.abstract: Bacterial-infected wound healing is severely impeded by the complex, self-perpetuating wound microenvironment (WME) characterized by biofilm infection, hypoxia, excessive oxidative stress, and persistent inflammation. Effective repair demands smart therapeutic interventions capable of autonomously adapting to the evolving pathological landscape-a feature absent in most current treatments. To address this critical need, a novel bimetallic nanozyme (MCCN) is engineered by integrating manganese (III) porphyrin into cobalt-doped mesoporous carbon-nitrogen nanocubes, serving as a smart modulator for autonomous WME remodeling. The MCCN exhibits oxidase (OXD), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and catalase (CAT)-like activities, and enables pH-responsive catalytic switching. In acidic biofilms, it initiates a self-sustaining OXD/SOD/CAT catalytic cycle that continuously generates singlet oxygen for biofilm eradication. As infection resolves and pH neutralizes, it autonomously switches to a SOD/CAT cascade that scavenges reactive oxygen species and supplies oxygen, alleviating oxidative stress and hypoxia while promoting tissue regeneration. The data demonstrate that the MCCN integrates potent antibacterial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and pro-angiogenic functions, making it an efficient and safe nanomedicine for treating infected wounds via a WME self-adaptive intervention pathway. Our work establishes a groundbreaking "smart catalytic" paradigm for dynamic pathological microenvironment remodeling, offering a promising therapeutic avenue for refractory wounds and other microenvironment-associated diseases.

articles.title: Does the adult divisional clinical examination still reflect how physicians practise? A qualitative study of Royal Australasian College of Physicians Fellows' and trainees' perceptions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Royal Australasian College of Physicians' (RACP) clinical examination remains a high-stakes barrier assessment for physician trainees in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand. Its bedside long case and short case tasks are largely unchanged, despite a renewed basic training curriculum and advancing clinical practice, raising the question of whether the clinical examination still reflects how physicians practise.

AIMS: To explore fellows' and trainees' perceptions of how well the clinical examination's bedside tasks align to contemporary physician practice.

METHODS: Purposive then snowball sampling recruited 10 fellows and five trainees across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand. Semi-structured interviews, conducted until information power was reached, were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: The long case was consistently valued as an authentic test of physician practice. Short case alignment was specialty-dependent: neurology was perceived as having enduring validity, whereas cardiology least reflected modern practice. Participants described real-world practice as hypothesis-driven rather than a formulaic, system-based routine and valued the clinical examination not only as an assessment of competence but as a shared experience that shapes professional identity.

CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the clinical examination through Kane's extrapolation inference. This work suggests a shift towards hypothesis-driven short case examination, prioritising manoeuvres because they reflect contemporary clinical management; it could enhance the clinical examination's validity while retaining the long case as the most valid component. Reform must also recognise the clinical examination's dual role in assessing competence and forming professional identity.

articles.title: Validation of the Progression Likelihood Score (PLS) for Stratifying Progression Rates in Early-Stage Type 1 Diabetes.
Risk Factors for Diabetic Foot-Related Lower Extremity Amputation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs.

METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). Ulcer severity was associated with amputation in every study assessing it, using five different classification systems. Prolonged ulcer duration carried an adjusted odds ratio of 10.3 (95% CI 4.06-26.13), and each additional preoperative day was associated with a 9.3% increase in the odds of major amputation. Neuropathy showed no independent association of meaningful size in any adjusted analysis, and HbA1c was not associated in the largest adjusted DFU cohort analysis, although a smaller study with 10 outcome events reported a positive association.

CONCLUSION: Peripheral arterial disease, ulcer severity, osteomyelitis, prior amputation, and delayed access to care were associated with LLA in LMIC settings. Neither neuropathy nor HbA1c showed an independent association of meaningful size in adjusted analyses of established DFU cohorts. Prospective LMIC cohorts using standardized definitions are needed.

articles.title: A Ten-Year Single-Center Evaluation of In-Hospital Versus Seven- Versus Thirty-Day Outcomes as Quality Standards After Carotid Endarterectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains a cornerstone for stroke prevention. The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine. This study evaluates institutional compliance with ESVS thresholds and compares the reliability of in-hospital and 7-day outcomes versus the 30-day follow-up interval.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-center cohort study.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted at the Medical University of Graz, encompassing 2496 patients undergoing primary CEA between 2014 and 2023. Data were retrieved from the institutional information system and cross-referenced with national mortality registries (Statistik Austria) to ensure comprehensive follow-up. Primary endpoints included stroke and death within 7 and 30 days, stratified by symptomatic status and surgical technique-Eversion Endarterectomy (EEA) versus Conventional Endarterectomy (TEA) with patch angioplasty.

RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 2496 eligible procedures. Notably, a substantial proportion of events that occurred after hospital discharge, accounting for 17.9% (10/56) of all 30-day strokes and 60.0% (9/15) of all 30-day deaths were observed between hospital discharge and postoperative day 30. Overall, the in-hospital combined stroke and death rate was 1.5% for asymptomatic patients and 3.8% for symptomatic patients. Following discharge, additional events were recorded in 10 asymptomatic and 9 symptomatic patients, resulting in a cumulative 30-day combined stroke and death rate of 2.0% [95% CI: 1.4%-2.7%] for asymptomatic patients and 5.3% [95% CI: 3.5%-7.2%] for symptomatic patients, thereby meeting ESVS safety standards. While symptomatic status was a significant predictor of complications (p < 0.001), neither sex nor surgical technique (EEA vs. TEA-patch) exerted a significant influence on outcomes.

CONCLUSION: CEA is performed at ESVS-recommended safety levels in Graz. Contrasting a clinical tendency to favor more convenient in-hospital metrics, this study demonstrates that "in-hospital" data cannot be standardized due to highly variable discharge windows. Furthermore, while fixed 7-day complication rates provide a standardized timeline, they still significantly underestimate perioperative risks. The substantial rate of post-discharge perioperative strokes and deaths observed in our cohort underscores the clinical necessity of extending quality control to at least 30 days, which remains the superior metric for clinical audit.

articles.title: Evolutionary Emergence of HIV-1 Subtype G and Subtype-Linked Transmitted NNRTI Resistance Among HIV Patients in Oman.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to characterize HIV-1 subtype distribution and transmitted drug resistance (TDR) patterns among treatment-naïve individuals in Oman to inform evidence-based treatment guidelines and molecular surveillance strategies.

METHODS: A nationwide retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted to analyse HIV-1 pol gene sequences from all newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve individuals in Oman over a nine-year period. A total of 963 treatment-naïve individuals diagnosed with HIV-1 infection between 2016 and 2024 were included in this nationwide retrospective analysis. Partial pol gene sequences encompassing protease and reverse transcriptase regions were amplified and sequenced. Subtyping was performed using multiple computational tools (COMET, RIP and jpHMM) with phylogenetic confirmation using maximum-likelihood methods. Drug resistance mutations were interpreted using the Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database (version 9.5).

RESULTS: Subtype G was the predominant lineage (38.2%, n = 368), followed by subtype A1 (28.0%, n = 270), CRF01_AE (11.7%, n = 113), and subtype C (7.4%, n = 71). Sixty-four other recombinant strains were identified, including three novel CRFs candidates. Subtype A1 exhibited the highest resistance burden (21.1%, n = 57), primarily associated with the K103N substitution, whereas subtype G remained largely susceptible (96.2%, n = 354). Overall, 13.0% (n = 125) harboured at least one NNRTI resistance mutation under the ≥ 15 threshold. No major resistance mutations were detected against nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs), including tenofovir, emtricitabine, and lamivudine.

CONCLUSIONS: The Omani HIV-1 epidemic is characterized by subtype G dominance, subtype-specific resistance patterns, and identification of putative novel circulating recombinant forms (CRFs). The high NNRTI resistance burden (13.0%) supports prioritizing INSTI-based regimens. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for monitoring emerging resistance.

articles.title: Microbial medicine in clinical pediatrics: evolving approaches to diagnosis and management.
articles.journal: Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care
articles.abstract: Our increasing understanding of the microbiome has revealed its critical role in immunity, metabolism, infectious disease susceptibility, and overall human health. Advances in the detection of microbial species using new sequencing technologies has led to the emergence of a new frontier in medicine. Integrating the microbiome with diagnostics and therapeutics has introduced the field of 'microbial medicine', representing a major translational advance in pediatric healthcare. The early-life microbiome is particularly important serving as a critical developmental window during which rapidly altering microbial communities can contribute to immune tolerance and confer disease risk. Factors that can shape the early-life microbial landscape include delivery mode, breastfeeding, diet, antibiotic exposure and geography. Disruptions in the microbiome have been linked to numerous pediatric diseases including necrotizing enterocolitis, inflammatory bowel disease, neonatal sepsis, allergic diseases, metabolic syndrome, neurodevelopmental disorders and psychiatric conditions. While early microbiome research has been largely correlational, growing mechanistic insights into host-microbe interactions have paved the way for the development of microbiome-targeted therapeutics. Promising approaches include prebiotics, probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, liver biotherapeutic products, genetically engineered microbes and microbiome-derived metabolites. Studies are however lacking in the pediatric population and therefore there is a growing need for a coordinated effort to increase access to microbiome-based therapeutics in children. Significant challenges include a lack of age-specific reference standards, understanding long-term safety, and standardizing available treatments. In this review we discuss the emergence of microbial medicine in pediatric care. We examine the current evidence evaluating the development of the microbiome, the factors that shape early-life microbial colonization and the use of microbial therapeutics in clinical practice. We highlight the challenges and opportunities associated with translating these discoveries into pediatric practice and suggest research priorities and infrastructure development required to establish microbial medicine as a mainstay in pediatric practice.

articles.title: Nitric oxide, prone positioning, and sedation and analgesia in mechanical ventilation.
articles.abstract: There are complementary treatments to mechanical ventilation in critically ill pediatric patients that are essential for optimizing oxygenation, gas exchange, and adaptation to respiratory support. Inhaled nitric oxide is a selective pulmonary vasodilator useful in specific situations such as pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular failure, and refractory hypoxemia, especially as rescue therapy, although its routine use in pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has not been found to improve survival. The prone position improves ventilation/perfusion distribution, promotes alveolar recruitment, and reduces ventilator-associated lung injury, making it a valuable adjunctive strategy in patients with severe ARDS and persistent hypoxemia. Although its impact on pediatric survival is still being evaluated, it represents a physiologically sound tool for protective ventilation. Protocolized sedation and analgesia are essential to ensure comfort, synchrony with the ventilator, and prevention of complications such as delirium, withdrawal syndrome, or oversedation. The rational use of opioids, alpha-2 agonist sedatives, and neuromuscular blocking agents, along with monitoring using validated scales, allows for optimized clinical outcomes and reduced adverse effects. The individualized combination of these strategies is currently a cornerstone of advanced respiratory support for critically ill pediatric patients.

articles.title: β-Blockers in COPD: Is the Case Finally Closed?
Biologic Chronotherapy in Severe Asthma: Overlooked Opportunity or Unnecessary Complexity?
The 6-Min Walk Test-Based STEP Index for Prognosis in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is widely used to assess functional capacity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, individual test components remain underutilized despite their independent prognostic value. We aimed to evaluate a 6MWT-derived index for predicting long-term mortality and exacerbation risk in COPD.

METHODS: We analyzed 2063 COPD patients from the prospective Korean COPD Subgroup Study. The STEP (Speed Terminate Early Performance) index combined gait speed (<1.0m/s), early test termination, and the distance-saturation product (<290m%). The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included respiratory and cardiovascular mortality, exacerbations, and symptom trajectories. Discrimination was compared with the BODE and BODEx indices using Harrell C-index and time-dependent AUCs.
