RESULTS: Higher STEP scores were associated with older age, lower body mass index, more severe airflow limitation, and a greater history of exacerbations, along with higher baseline symptom burden. Higher STEP scores were associated with increased rates of moderate-to-severe and severe exacerbations. Ten-year mortality increased from 9.4% in STEP 0 to 37.5% in STEP 3 (P<0.001). The STEP, BODE, and BODEx indices showed similar discrimination for all-cause mortality (C-index 0.750, 0.739, and 0.742, respectively). Adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.61, 2.61, and 4.78 for STEP 1, 2, and 3, respectively, compared with STEP 0. Respiratory mortality increased significantly with higher STEP categories, whereas cardiovascular mortality showed no gradient.

CONCLUSION: The STEP index provides robust prognostic stratification using only 6MWT parameters, with performance similar to the BODE and BODEx indices.

articles.title: [18F]-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET in Lymphoma: Therapeutic Decision-Making and Theranostic Perspectives.
articles.abstract: [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/computed tomography is central to the management of FDG-avid lymphomas, providing whole-body assessment of viable metabolic disease across staging, treatment planning, and response evaluation. Its clinical value lies not simply in detecting residual metabolic activity, but in interpreting PET findings according to lymphoma subtype, treatment context, and their therapeutic consequences. Emerging quantitative biomarkers, long-axial field-of-view PET, and target-specific tracers may further characterize disease burden, heterogeneity, and therapeutic vulnerability, extending PET beyond conventional metabolic imaging toward more individualized and increasingly theranostic lymphoma management.

articles.title: Prevalence of Elevated Voice Handicap Index-10 Scores and Associated Factors among Adolescents in the Western Region of Saudi Arabia.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Voice problems can affect quality of life and communication, particularly during adolescence. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of elevated Voice Handicap Index-10 scores and to identify associated factors among adolescents in the western region of Saudi Arabia.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted through an electronic questionnaire comprising the Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10) and items on vocal behavior, upper respiratory tract infection burden, and other factors in 211 participants aged 13 to 18 years resident in the western region. An elevated VHI-10 score was defined as a total score greater than 11, which does not establish a clinical diagnosis of a voice disorder. Associations were evaluated using the chi-square or Fisher exact test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and one multivariable logistic regression model.

RESULTS: An elevated VHI-10 score was present in 84 of 211 participants (39.8%, 95% CI 33.15% to 46.76%). In the multivariable model the upper respiratory tract infection load index (OR 1.08 per point, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.13, P < 0.001) and anxiety or panic disorder (OR 3.24, 95% CI 1.09 to 10.54, P = 0.034) were associated with higher odds of an elevated score, and respiratory allergy with lower odds (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.84, P = 0.019). No significant association was detected for the vocal loading score (P = 0.537), sex (P = 0.531), or age (P = 0.294).

CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported voice-related handicap is frequent among adolescents in the western region of Saudi Arabia and accompanies upper respiratory tract infection burden and anxiety or panic disorder. Adolescents who report voice difficulty may benefit from assessment of respiratory symptoms and psychosocial factors, and voice screening could be considered in those with recurrent respiratory infections or anxiety. Longitudinal studies with laryngeal assessment are needed to establish whether addressing these factors changes voice outcomes.

articles.title: Comparing surgical shunting with transcatheter stenting for initial palliation of cyanotic tetralogy of fallot: An inverse probability treatment weighting study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: To compare surgical shunting with transcatheter stenting for initial palliation of cyanotic tetralogy of Fallot, including high-risk infants.

METHODS: This retrospective two-center study included 101 infants who underwent palliation before 1 year of age, including 76 who underwent surgical shunting and 25 who underwent transcatheter stenting. Outcomes were evaluated using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting with doubly robust adjustment. The primary composite outcome was death, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Secondary outcomes included recovery, reintervention, medical expenses, and pulmonary artery (PA) development.

RESULTS: After adjustment, the primary composite outcome and overall perioperative complication rate did not differ significantly between groups. Surgical shunting was associated with longer log-transformed intubation duration (β = 0.948, 95% CI 0.203-1.693; P = 0.013), intensive care unit stay (β = 0.584, 95% CI 0.050-1.118; P = 0.032), and hospital stay (β = 0.558, 95% CI 0.071-1.046; P = 0.025), but lower odds of reintervention (OR = 0.112, 95% CI 0.033-0.379; P < 0.001). In high-risk patients, surgical shunting was associated with more perioperative complications (OR = 7.712, 95% CI 1.569-37.913; P = 0.013), higher medical expenses, and lower McGoon and PA symmetry indices at total correction.

CONCLUSION: No significant between-group differences were observed in the primary composite outcome or overall perioperative complication rate. Transcatheter stenting was associated with faster recovery but more frequent reintervention. Among high-risk infants, it was associated with fewer perioperative complications, lower index hospitalization expenses, and more favorable PA development.

CLINICAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: The Research Ethics Committee of National Taiwan University Hospital (No. 202602073RIND), waived informed consent.

articles.title: The Effect of Pain Intensity and Anxiety Levels on Pain Catastrophizing Among Individuals Presenting to the Emergency Department with Chronic Pain.
articles.journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Since chronic pain negatively impacts quality of life, the severity of pain and levels of anxiety experienced by individuals presenting to the emergency department may influence pain catastrophizing. This study aimed to determine the effect of pain intensity and anxiety levels on pain catastrophizing among individuals presenting to the emergency department with chronic pain complaints.

DESIGN: This is a descriptive and correlational study.

METHODS: The study population consisted of individuals presenting to the emergency department of a university hospital in Turkey with chronic pain complaints between March 10 and July 15, 2025. From 242 individuals who met the inclusion criteria and provided informed consent, demographic characteristics were captured using a Personal Information Form. Pain intensity, anxiety, and catastrophizing levels were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale, the Visual Analog Scale for Anxiety, and the Pain Catastrophizing Scale. Data were analyzed using SPSS 22.0 through descriptive statistics, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test, and multiple linear regression with forward stepwise selection using HC3 robust standard errors, setting statistical significance at p < .05.

RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 46.78 ± 16.87; 56.6% were female, and 70.2% were married. The mean visual pain scale score was 7.54 ± 1.21, the mean anxiety scale score was 7.43 ± 1.57, and the mean total score on the pain catastrophizing scale was 37.26 ± 9.34. In the forward stepwise model, anxiety was identified as the strongest predictor of the total pain catastrophizing score (R² = 0.549, F = 294.783). Adding the visual pain scale score to the model increased the variance to 59.7% and provided additional explanatory power to the model (ΔR² = 0.048) even when pain intensity was controlled for.

CONCLUSION: It was found that pain intensity and anxiety levels significantly increase pain catastrophizing.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Pain intensity and anxiety level are significantly associated with pain catastrophizing in individuals presenting to the emergency department with chronic pain. Routinely screening both pain levels and anxiety in the emergency setting may assist healthcare professionals in identifying patients prone to high pain catastrophizing and tailoring supportive care strategies accordingly.

articles.title: Potassium and Phosphorus Food Additives in Chronic Kidney Disease: An Emerging Nutritional Challenge.
Short- and Mid-Term Effects of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Heart Rate Variability in Patients With Aortic Valve Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects autonomic nervous system balance and has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between HRV and mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear.

METHOD: This prospective cohort study included 230 patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between June 2022 and June 2024. Twenty-four-hour Holter electrocardiography recordings were obtained one day before and at 3 months after the procedure to assess HRV using both time- and frequency-domain parameters.

RESULTS: Among the 230 patients enrolled, the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%. Among frequency-domain parameters, the pre-TAVR low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio improved markedly from 2.20±1.45 to 1.54±0.85 (p<0.001). In the time domain, standard deviation of NN intervals (89-103 ms, p=0.027), standard deviation of the averages of NN intervals (68-83 ms, p=0.003), and percentage of successive RR intervals (10.0%-12.0%, p=0.036) all showed significant improvements, while root mean square of successive RR interval differences remained unchanged. The pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio was significantly lower in survivors and provided the best discrimination for 1-year mortality prediction (area under the curve 0.815; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.750-0.881). Calibration analysis confirmed excellent predictive accuracy (C-index, 0.81; Brier score, 0.104; pseudo-R2, 0.285). Patients with a pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio>1.34 had significantly lower mortality at follow-up (hazard ratio [HR] 0.103; 95% CI 0.042-0.250; log-rank p<0.001), and this association remained significant in landmark analysis beyond 3 months (HR 0.163; log-rank p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: HRV parameters provide meaningful prognostic information in patients undergoing TAVR. Among them, a reduced pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio is independently associated with increased 1-year mortality and may serve as a practical, non-invasive marker for risk stratification.

articles.title: Hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of respiratory viral infections in Spain: A population-based study using hospital data (2019-2023).
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Respiratory viral infections are a major cause of hospitalization, morbidity, mortality, and healthcare resource use in Spain. Although influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for most of the healthcare burden, the contribution of other respiratory viruses has been less studied. This study aimed to analyze the hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of these infections during the 2019-2023 period.

METHODS: A retrospective population-based study was conducted using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (CMBD), including hospitalizations with a diagnosis of respiratory viral infection between 2019 and 2023. Influenza, RSV, adenovirus, metapneumovirus, parainfluenza, and rhinovirus were analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 154,753 hospitalizations were included (mean age: 39 years; 48.6% female). Influenza and RSV accounted for most hospitalizations and total costs. A marked reduction in hospitalizations was observed in 2021, followed by recovery in 2022-2023. RSV, metapneumovirus, rhinovirus, and adenovirus predominantly affected the pediatric population, whereas influenza and parainfluenza had a greater impact on older adults. Overall, 6.5% of patients required ICU admission and in-hospital mortality was 2.7%, highest for influenza (4.2%). Metapneumovirus and rhinovirus showed the highest ICU admission rates. Mean hospital stay was 6.1 days (7.4 days in ICU). Although influenza and RSV generated the highest total costs, other viruses showed higher costs per episode.

CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory viral infections impose a substantial healthcare and economic burden, with variable impact according to virus type and age group, highlighting the need for integrated surveillance, prevention, and healthcare planning strategies.

articles.title: Ten years of Actinotignum spp. bacteremia in a tertiary-care hospital: What are we missing?
articles.journal: Enfermedades infecciosas y microbiologia clinica (English ed.)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Actinotignum is a genus of gram-positive bacteria mainly involved in urinary tract infections and invasive infections such as bacteremia. The aim of this study was to analyse clinically and microbiologically the episodes of bacteremia caused by Actinotignum spp.

METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted, including all episodes of Actinotignum spp. bacteremia in Navarra between 2014 and 2024. Clinical, demographic, and microbiological data were analysed.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight episodes were described. Twenty-six occurred in men with a mean age of 77 years. The urinary tract was the source of bacteremia in 92.8% of cases. Despite that, Actinotignum sp. was isolated in urine in a single case.

CONCLUSIONS: Actinotignum spp. bacteremia was predominantly of urinary origin and mainly affected elderly patients with underlying urological disease. Active screening for Actinotignum in selected urine samples may help reduce the underdiagnosis of urinary tract infections caused by this microorganism and its complications, such as bacteremia.

articles.title: Screening for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency in a specialized smoking cessation clinic and its relationship with the presence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Relationship between the MTHFR C677T polymorphism and essential hypertension: A clinical correlation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) C677T polymorphism affects homocysteine metabolism and may influence essential hypertension (EH), but the associated clinical phenotype in hyperhomocysteinemic patients remains unclear. We focused on differences between patients with the homozygous mutation (TT) genotype and those with non-TT genotypes.

METHODS: A total of 30 patients with EH and hyperhomocysteinemia (Hcy≥15μmol/L) admitted to Jincheng General Hospital from March 1, 2025, to July 31, 2025, were enrolled. MTHFR gene polymorphisms were determined. According to the MTHFR C677T genotype, patients were assigned to the TT group and the non-TT group (CT and CC genotypes). Demographic characteristics, blood pressure measurements, and duration of hypertension of the two groups were recorded and compared. Biochemical measures including homocysteine (Hcy), folic acid, vitamin B12, blood lipids, and fasting blood glucose were measured. Pulse pressure, mean arterial pressure (MAP), pulse pressure index (PPI), and hypertension cumulative risk index were calculated. Spearman correlation analysis was used to examine associations between folic acid levels and Hcy, pulse pressure, and PPI.

RESULTS: Compared with the non-TT group, the TT group had significantly higher concentrations of Hcy and vitamin B12, a significantly shorter hypertension duration, and significantly lower systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse pressure, PPI, and hypertension cumulative load index. Spearman rank correlation analysis showed that folic acid levels correlated inversely with Hcy, pulse pressure, and PPI.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between the MTHFR C677T TT genotype and cardiovascular risk may be confounded by vitamin B12 nutritional status and disease duration, complicating interpretation of the genotype as a simple risk factor.

articles.title: The microbial glycan landscape instructs natural antibody repertoires.
articles.abstract: The human gut mucosa presents a dynamic glycan landscape, built from host, microbial, and dietary carbohydrates and remodeled throughout life. Gut microbes deploy a vast repertoire of surface glycans that drive immune evasion, lectin signaling, immunomodulation, and ecological competition. Natural antiglycan antibodies, we argue, are not fixed baseline features of humoral immunity but are structured readouts of glycan exposure, founded during early-life colonization and revised thereafter by diet, infection, vaccination, and inflammation. We trace how microbial glycan diversity arises, how specific glycan classes instruct antibody specificity, and how disrupting this glycan-immune dialog drives inflammatory bowel disease, xenosialitis, infection, and allergy. Reframing natural antibodies as ecologically instructed rather than genetically preset identifies the glycan landscape as a lifelong determinant of immune calibration.

articles.title: Liver transplant team involvement in level III and IV renal tumor thrombectomy: Perioperative and oncologic outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Resection of renal cell carcinoma with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus above the hepatic veins requires extensive liver mobilization using techniques derived from liver transplantation. We assessed whether dedicated liver transplant team involvement in radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy for thrombi above the hepatic veins (level III and IV) was associated with perioperative and oncologic outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this unplanned, hypothesis-generating analysis of a single-center retrospective cohort (2018-2024), cases were classified by liver transplant team involvement, and intraoperative factors, 90-day outcomes, and survival were compared. Because liver transplant team involvement was adopted progressively, sensitivity analyses adjusting for year of surgery and restricted to the adoption period were performed.

RESULTS: Of 36 cases, 18 (50%) involved the liver transplant team. Intraoperative factors were similar. Liver transplant team involvement was associated with fewer major complications (Clavien grade ≥3: 11% vs. 50%, P = 0.03) and less hepatic dysfunction (0% vs. 39%, P = 0.01) within 90 days, with similar recurrence-free and overall survival. Adjusting for cardiac bypass, liver transplant team involvement was associated with lower odds of major complications (odds ratio [OR] 0.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.005-0.57) and hepatic dysfunction (OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.002-0.83). After adjustment for year of surgery, point estimates were similar but neither association remained statistically significant (OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.01-1.24; OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.001-1.22).

CONCLUSIONS: Liver transplant team involvement was associated with fewer major complications and less hepatic dysfunction. Although this association could not be reliably separated from calendar time, these findings warrant prospective, multi-institutional evaluation of liver transplant team involvement in high-level renal tumor thrombectomy.

articles.title: 18F-FDG PET-revealed cognitive outcomes of subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease with cognitive impairment.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation (STN-DBS) is a well-established treatment for advanced Parkinson's disease (PD). The coexistence of cognitive impairment (CI) in PD patients poses risks to the therapeutic outcomes of STN-DBS. PD patients with mild CI (MCI) have been shown to derive functional benefits from STN-DBS. However, the efficacy of STN-DBS in PD patients with moderate CI has yet to reach a consensus. The study aims to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of STN-DBS in PD patients with moderate CI via 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET. The study retrospectively included 117 PD patients who underwent STN-DBS and were classified into three groups: PD-Moderate CI (N = 26), PD-MCI (N = 48) and PD-NC (N = 43). They received clinical assessments and 18F-FDG PET imaging preoperatively, and were followed up within 3 years after STN-DBS. Patients with PD-Moderate CI demonstrated greater disease severity preoperatively compared to patients with PD-MCI and PD-NC, but they experienced meaningful improvements in motor symptoms and quality of life after STN-DBS. Cognitively, ten PD patients with moderate CI reverted to MCI postoperatively, with increases in global cognitive scores potentially associated with post-DBS elevation in occipital metabolism. Furthermore, patients with PD-Moderate CI who had preserved cortical metabolism and better levodopa responsiveness preoperatively were more likely to show favorable cognitive outcomes after STN-DBS. In conclusion, STN-DBS might also offer benefits to PD patients with moderate CI. 18F-FDG PET-derived cerebral metabolic patterns, beyond cognitive performance alone, may be incorporated into biomarker-guided candidate selection for STN-DBS.

articles.title: Oxidized Cellulose Nanofiber Hydrogels for 3D Airway Spheroids and Influenza Infection Modeling.
articles.abstract: Micro-physiological systems (MPS) that recapitulate tissue architecture and immune competence are urgently needed to model respiratory viral infections and accelerate antiviral discovery. Here, we create an airway spheroid-based MPS supported by an oxidized cellulose nanofiber (OCNF) hydrogel, which provides a hydrated, extracellular matrix (ECM) mimetic nanofibrillar microenvironment and supports stable long-term 3D culture. Airway epithelial-like spheroids are generated either from Calu-3 cells alone or as immunocompetent co-culture spheroids incorporating polarized THP-1 macrophage-like cells to capture epithelial-immune crosstalk. The OCNF platform promotes rapid spheroid self-assembly within 6 days and preserves structural integrity for ≥ 20 days, allowing longitudinal interrogation of influenza A virus replication and host innate immune responses. Notably, the model reveals that human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exert potent antiviral activity, significantly reducing influenza infection through activation of interferon (IFN)-associated pathways, including MX1, OAS1, and STAT1. Together, this OCNF hydrogel-enabled airway spheroid MPS provides a scalable and reproducible test-bed for mechanistic studies and preclinical evaluation of antiviral interventions and establishes an in vitro platform toward personalized patient-relevant respiratory infection models.

articles.title: Adenotonsillectomy in Children With Cerebral Palsy: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of adenotonsillectomy in children with cerebral palsy (CP) and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of children with CP and OSA who underwent adenotonsillectomy between 2011 and 2022 at a tertiary pediatric medical center. Inclusion criteria required pre- and postoperative polysomnography within 24 months. Data collected included demographics, comorbidities, perioperative complications, and polysomnography parameters. The primary outcome was the change in obstructive apnea-hypopnea index (OAHI). Secondary outcomes included changes in central apnea index, oxygen nadir, transcutaneous carbon dioxide (TcCO2), and need for noninvasive positive pressure ventilation. Logistic regression identified predictors of postoperative OAHI < 5 events/h.

RESULTS: Sixty-five children (median age: 5.0 years) met inclusion criteria. Mean preoperative OAHI was 19.6, which improved to 7.7 postoperatively (p < 0.001). OAHI was reduced by >50% in 63%; 62% achieved OAHI < 5, and 12% achieved OAHI < 1. Oxygen nadir improved from 84% to 88% (p < 0.001), TcCO2 improved from 49.2 mmHg to 45.2 mmHg. No significant change in central apnea index was noted. Postoperatively, 40% required noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, and 55% were electively admitted to the intensive care unit. Complication rate was 12%. Preoperative OAHI was the strongest and most consistently selected predictor of achieving postoperative OAHI < 5 (p = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Adenotonsillectomy significantly improves OSA severity and oxygenation in children with CP; however, complete resolution is uncommon. Preoperative OAHI severity predicts surgical success. Postoperative polysomnography and multidisciplinary follow-up are essential due to the high rate of residual disease.

articles.title: Bowel perforation following ischaemic necrosis secondary to a mesocolonic haematoma in a patient on long-term anticoagulation.
Mavacamten in midventricular obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a multicentre observational study.
Amiloride in hypertension: mechanisms, clinical use and emerging perspectives.
Optimizing Frontline Targeted Therapies in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: An Italian Inter-Regional Delphi Consensus on Patient Risk Stratification, Cardiovascular Safety, and Endpoint Interpretation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While landmark trial data have established targeted agents as the frontline standard of care in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), real-world clinical gaps remain regarding high-risk disease biology, patient frailty, cardiovascular comorbidities, healthcare accessibility, and the clinical interpretation of surrogate endpoints.

METHODS: A modified two-round Delphi process engaged an expert panel of 19 Italian hematology specialists and a multidisciplinary scientific board to evaluate 16 evidence-based statements across four key clinical domains. Statements were formulated based on literature evidence-informed from a systematic review of the literature. When high-tier evidence was lacking, statements used lower-level data and expert consensus to address clinical gaps. Consensus was pre-defined as an aggregate agreement of ≥  70% using a forced-choice 4-point Likert scale.

RESULTS: Continuous monotherapy with second-generation covalent BTK inhibitors (cBTKis) was preferred over time-limited regimens for patients with TP53-disrupted disease (94.6%), individuals aged > 80 years or meeting frailty criteria (100%), and those with socio-logistic or caregiver constraints (95.0%). Conversely, time-limited regimens were universally favored for fit patients aged < 70 years without TP53 aberrations (100%), while remaining a viable option in young, fit patients with TP53 disruptions (78.9%). Baseline cardiovascular risk stratification using population-validated tools (SCORE2, SCORE2-OP, SCORE2-Diabetes) reached 85.0% agreement. Second-generation cBTKis were preferred over ibrutinib in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk (95.0%). Panelists agreed that undetectable measurable residual disease (uMRD) is not a universal surrogate for progression-free survival (70.0%). Time to next treatment (TTNT) was unanimously endorsed as an efficacy indicator for time-limited therapy (100%), but viewed primarily as a safety surrogate during continuous cBTKi therapy (79.0%). Upon relapse after time-limited cBTKi-venetoclax therapy, re-challenge with a covalent BTKi was established as the preferred option (89.5%).

CONCLUSION: This consensus bridges clinical guidelines and real-world practice, providing a structured framework that incorporates molecular risk, functional frailty, cardiovascular scoring, and healthcare accessibility to guide frontline CLL management.

articles.title: From Diagnosis to Adaptation: Meaning-Making Throughout the Illness Experience of Patients With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension-A Hermeneutic Phenomenological Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore the illness experience and meaning-making of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension from diagnosis to adaptation.

DESIGN: A qualitative study using a Heideggerian hermeneutic phenomenological design.

METHODS: From July to December 2025, purposive sampling recruited 12 adults with PAH from a teaching hospital in northern Taiwan. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, with data collection and analysis occurring concurrently. Transcripts were read, compared, and interpreted through the hermeneutic circle, supported by field notes and reflexive notes.

RESULTS: Six interrelated themes and 15 categories were identified: (1) Cycles of hope and disappointment; (2) Physical decline and disruption to daily life after disease onset; (3) Waiting on the edge of collapse; (4) Information gaps and unmet information needs; (5) Rediscovering possibilities for living; and (6) Finding a place in life within the limits of the disease. Patients experienced diagnostic delays, physical decline, treatment waiting, and information gaps. As treatment stabilised, they shifted from hoping to return to pre-illness lives to adjusting expectations, roles, and attitudes and engaging in disease management. Adaptation was an ongoing process.

CONCLUSION: Participants' retrospective accounts suggest that adaptation to PAH involves more than accepting the illness. Patients continuously reinterpret the illness, themselves, and their future amid physical and daily-life changes. Family, peers, and healthcare professionals support hope and adaptation.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Care for pulmonary arterial hypertension should extend beyond disease control and symptom management. Nurses can support patients through case management, information, and family and peer support across illness stages.

IMPACT: This study highlights illness adaptation as a continuous process of adjusting perspectives on illness, self, and future, suggesting that care for PHA should address patients' long-term lives alongside disease management.

REPORTING METHOD: This study was reported in accordance with the COREQ guidelines.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

C2 Split/Burst Fractures in the Elderly: An Underrecognized Injury Pattern.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: C2 split/burst fractures in older adults may be incompletely characterized by conventional upper cervical fracture terminology. We examined whether their morphology and injury circumstances support interpretation as primary C2 vertebral body injuries with a hypothesized compression-dominant loading pattern.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 52 consecutive patients aged ≥65 years with cervical fractures treated between January 2022 and October 2025. Six C2 split/burst fractures were characterized using computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, Benzel mechanisms, Fujimura morphology, and AO Spine classification. Injury histories were compared descriptively across all 16 C2 fractures. Treatment outcomes were secondary descriptive observations.

RESULTS: The 6 patients (mean age, 78.3 ± 8.3 years; 3 men and 3 women) all sustained backward falls with occipital impact. The other 10 C2 fractures comprised 4 Anderson-D'Alonzo type II fractures, 3 type III fractures, and 3 additional vertebral body fractures with lateralized or asymmetric morphology; injury circumstances were heterogeneous. All 6 split/burst fractures were Fujimura type III; AO region III type A vs B could not be reliably determined from the available imaging; Benzel mechanisms were D (n = 2), E (n = 1), and F (n = 3), each incorporating axial loading. Magnetic resonance imaging was obtained in all 6 patients. After posterior fixation, all 5 survivors achieved fusion at 6 months; 1 patient died of sepsis considered unrelated to surgery before fusion assessment.

CONCLUSIONS: These observations support considering elderly C2 split/burst fractures primarily as vertebral body injuries. Compression-dominant loading is a plausible shared mechanism, but neither the loading pathway nor a separate injury entity is established. Morphological overlap with atypical hangman fractures remains possible. Treatment effectiveness cannot be inferred from this series.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Describing the predominant site of bony failure alongside regional alignment may improve characterization of C2 injuries; this concept is not a validated stability or treatment criterion.

articles.title: Crossword.
Clinical and Venographic Distinctions Between Extrinsic and Intrinsic Dural Venous Sinus Stenosis: Implications for Venous Stenting.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dural venous sinus stenosis (VSS) is associated with intracranial hypertension and may be treated with venous sinus stenting. VSS can be either extrinsic (extramural compression related to elevated ICP) or intrinsic (narrowing typically due to arachnoid granulations), with potentially important clinical distinctions and implications for venous stenting.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients evaluated with catheter venography for suspected VSS and/or cerebral venous outflow disorders from October 2021 to March 2026. Patients were categorized as having intrinsic or extrinsic venous stenosis. Clinical distinctions between groups were investigated.

RESULTS: Among 162 patients (mean age, 40.2 years; 96% female), 108 (67%) had extrinsic and 54 (33%) had intrinsic stenosis. Patients with extrinsic stenosis were younger (35.6 vs. 49.5 years; P<0.0001), had higher BMI (38.1 vs. 34.8 kg/m2; P=0.018), and higher opening pressure (36.0 vs. 29.3 cmH2O; P=0.006). Extrinsic stenosis was associated with higher torcula pressure (30.1 vs. 25.7 mmHg; P=0.03), higher trans-stenotic pressure gradient (15.8 vs. 11.9 mmHg; P=0.02), and more frequent occipital emissary venous drainage (62% vs. 44%; P=0.03). Ninety patients (56%) underwent stenting. Pulsatile tinnitus clinically resolved in 20/22 patients (91%) with intrinsic stenosis versus 29/43 (67%) with extrinsic stenosis (Fisher exact P=0.065, Pearson χ2 P=0.038). Symptomatic stent-adjacent stenosis occurred in 7/58 (12%) of stented extrinsic patients and 0/32 (0%) stented intrinsic patients and was significantly different (Fisher exact P=0.048, Pearson χ2=0.041). Other stenting outcomes did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Extrinsic and intrinsic VSS have distinct clinical and venographic profiles and may have different outcomes following venous stenting, suggesting they could represent related but distinct venous outflow disorders. Further research may optimize venous stenting patient selection and inform clinical trial design.

articles.title: Procedural Time Independently Predicts Functional Outcome After First-Pass Reperfusion in Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modified first-pass effect (mFPE) is an established benchmark of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) success in large-vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke, yet its clinical benefit may be time sensitive. Prior studies indicate that procedural time (PT) exceeding 30 minutes carries higher complications rates and worse outcomes. We assessed whether procedural duration exerts a continuous, dose-dependent effect on clinical outcomes among patients achieving mFPE.

METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study analyzed patients who achieved mFPE after MT for acute ischemic stroke between February 2018 and March 2024. Primary outcomes were 30- and 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2). Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), and mortality. Multivariate logistic regression models evaluated associations between PT (modeled continuously and dichotomized by a 30-minute cut-off) and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 417 patients achieving mFPE, 302 (72.4%) had PT ≤30 minutes. Shorter PT was independently associated with functional independence at 30 days (aOR 1.72, 95% CI 1.06-2.80; p=0.03) but not at 90 days (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 0.89-2.32; p=0.14). Modeled continuously within each time window, PT showed no significant association with functional independence, although ordinal analysis suggested worse mRS with longer PT only in the >30-minute group at 30 days (aOR 1.18; p=0.04). Median LOS was shorter for PT ≤30 minutes (6 (3-10) vs. 7 (4-13) days, p=0.01). sICH and mortality did not differ by PT.

CONCLUSION: Among patients achieving mFPE, shorter PT remained independently associated with better functional outcomes at 30 days, but not at 90 days, with no significant gradient within either window, supporting the importance of procedural efficiency even after technically successful single-pass reperfusion.

articles.title: A detailed analysis of First pass Reperfusion and Number of Passes in MeVO Stroke Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Reperfusion success after EVT and the number of EVT passes may be associated with clinical and imaging outcomes in patients with acute stroke due to Medium Vessel Occlusion (MeVO).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Secondary analysis of patients randomized to EVT in the ESCAPE-MeVO trial. Final reperfusion was assessed with the MeVO-expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (MeVO-eTICI) Score. First pass near-complete reperfusion was defined as MeVO-eTICI 2c-3 after 1 pass and multi-pass near-complete reperfusion as MeVO-eTICI 2c-3 after >1 pass. The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Score (mRS) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour NIHSS and 24-hour infarct volume, among others. Associations were assessed using regression models.

RESULTS: Of 255 patients randomized to EVT (48.3%), 206 remained for the final analysis. First pass near-complete reperfusion was associated with decreased infarct volume (median 12.8ml [IQR 0.15-25.3] versus: 22.4ml [6.71-56.38ml], adjusted beta-coefficient -1.68 [95%CI::-2.54-(-0.81)]) and improved 24-hour NIHSS (median 7 [2-13.5] versus: 2.5 [1-6.5], adjusted beta-coefficient -0.56 [95%CI:-0.74-(-0.38)]), but not with clinical outcomes. Similarly, improved reperfusion status was associated with lower infarct volumes and improved 24-hour NIHSS but not with clinical outcomes. Number of EVT passes was associated with higher 90-day mRS (acOR 1.41 [95%CI: 1.04-1.91] per 1-additional pass), higher 24-hour NIHSS and larger infarct volume.

CONCLUSIONS: Improved first-pass reperfusion with EVT in MeVO stroke patients was associated with reduced infarct volumes and improved 24-hour NIHSS. Performing more EVT passes was associated with increased infarct volume and poorer 24-hour and 90-day outcomes.

articles.title: Carotid near-occlusion pathophysiology: A narrative review and expanded cerebrovascular theory.
articles.abstract: The purposes of this review are to summarize the pathophysiology of carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and formulate how known hemodynamic theory can be expanded to specifically address CNO. A systematic search revealed 51 articles addressing CNO pathophysiology. ICA flow reduction and collateral pathway activation are hallmarks of CNO. While CNO is associated with a high prevalence of reduced cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), severely impaired CVR was uncommon. Hence, hypoperfusion stroke mechanism is uncommon. Embolic mechanism studies are few and with mixed results. In hemodynamic theory variant, we propose that good collateral capacity results in CNO early during stenosis severity progression and no hemodynamic stroke/TIA. Conversely, we propose that poor collateral capacity results in more severe stenosis for CNO to develop and hemodynamic stroke/TIA will occur when the stenosis is sufficiently severe. This suggested theory predicts that a mismatch between too little distal collapse given a certain stenosis severity might indicate hypoperfusion. In conclusion, CNOs are flow-reducing stenoses associated with collateral use and unclear stroke mechanism. We propose an expansion of known hemodynamic theory to specifically address CNO where collateral capacity is the key factor that determines what stenosis severity is required for CNO to form and for hypoperfusion occur (if it occurs at all).

articles.title: Association Between Tissue No-Reflow and Prognosis After successful Recanalization in Endovascular Treatment of Intracranial Atherosclerotic Occlusion: A Post Hoc Subgroup Analysis of the ANGEL-REBOOT Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No-reflow after successful endovascular treatment (EVT) predicts poor outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) due to intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS), but its optimal evaluation and prognostic value remain unclear. This study assessed computed tomography perfusion (CTP)-defined no-reflow for predicting outcomes in ICAS-related large vessel occlusion (ICAS-LVO).

METHODS: This retrospective post hoc analysis included patients from the prospective ANGEL-REBOOT trial with anterior circulation ICAS-LVO, successful eTICI 2b/3 recanalization, and postoperative 24-hour CTP. No-reflow was defined as persistent hypoperfusion (Tmax >4s or >6s) after recanalization. Outcomes included 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score (poor outcome ≥3) and 24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score.

RESULTS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, the optimal cohort derived cutoff value for Tmax > 4s hypoperfusion volume was 95.8 mL. Among 64 patients, Tmax >4s hypoperfusion volume ≥95.8 mL best predicted poor 90-day outcome (area under the curve [AUC] 0.75). Larger Tmax >4s volumes correlated with worse 90-day mRS scores (P=0.04) and higher 24-hour NIHSS scores (P=0.006). Tmax >6s (cutoff 9.9 mL, AUC 0.690) only predicted higher 24-hour NIHSS score (P=0.001) but not 90-day outcomes (P=0.12).

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative 24-hour CTP Tmax > 4 s hypoperfusion volume showed a trend toward better prediction of 90-day poor functional outcomes compared with Tmax > 6 s in recanalized ICAS-LVO patients.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction as a Rising Barrier to HBV Elimination.
articles.abstract: About one-third of patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) have hepatic steatosis, and cardiometabolic risk factors are increasingly prevalent. This review examines what metabolic dysfunction does to the measurements on which the elimination cascade depends, from prevention through diagnosis, treatment eligibility, on-treatment risk control, and functional cure to postcure surveillance. Metabolic dysfunction lowers the response to adult vaccination, enters three of the four routes to treatment eligibility in the World Health Organization criteria, contributes to the hepatocellular carcinoma risk that persists during antiviral therapy, and is absent from most risk scores and surveillance rules used before and after hepatitis B surface antigen loss. Its two components diverge: hepatic steatosis and cardiometabolic burden appear to additively increase the probability of hepatitis B surface antigen loss, but act in opposite directions on cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and mortality. Assessing and correcting metabolic dysfunction as part of CHB care, and including patients with CHB in trials of metabolic therapy, would allow success to be defined by liver outcomes rather than by the virus alone.

articles.title: Therapeutic Apheresis in Nigeria: Awareness, Knowledge Gaps, and Readiness for Service Expansion Among Healthcare Professionals.
articles.journal: Therapeutic apheresis and dialysis : official peer-reviewed journal of the International Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Apheresis, the Japanese Society for Dialysis Therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic apheresis (TA) is a specialized extracorporeal blood purification modality used in the management of complex hematologic, neurologic, and autoimmune diseases. Despite established global guidelines, its utilization in Nigeria remains largely undocumented. This study assessed awareness, technical knowledge, and institutional readiness for TA among Nigerian healthcare professionals.

METHODS: We conducted an open, cross-sectional online survey of licensed Nigerian healthcare professionals, recruited by convenience and snowball sampling through professional social media networks (WhatsApp, Instagram, X) over a 2-month period from January 29, 2026, to April 1, 2026. Because recruitment used an open, non-probability sampling frame, a conventional response rate could not be calculated; of 180 questionnaires received, 155 (86.1%) met pre-specified completeness and uniqueness criteria and were analyzed. The questionnaire assessed demographics, awareness of TA services, technical knowledge (10-item assessment based on ASFA guideline domains), and perceived barriers.

RESULTS: Respondents were predominantly physicians (63.2%; consultants 22.6%, residents 40.6%), practicing mainly in teaching (47.7%) and private (32.9%) hospitals; 51.6% practiced in a single state (Imo State). Awareness of TPE centers was moderate (45.2%, 95% CI: 37.6%-53.1%), and clinical exposure was low (27.7%, 95% CI: 21.3%-35.2%). The mean knowledge score was 5.10 ± 2.44 of 10. Knowledge level was not significantly associated with professional role, years of experience, or institution type (all p > 0.05), with a borderline, nonsignificant difference by specialty (p = 0.051); nephrology and critical care specialists showed the highest proportion of good knowledge. The leading perceived barriers were lack of equipment (79.4%), poor funding (75.5%), limited awareness (75.5%), and lack of trained personnel (74.2%). Nearly all respondents (95.5%) supported establishing a national TA registry.

CONCLUSION: Nigerian healthcare professionals report substantial gaps in TA awareness and technical knowledge alongside strong readiness to support service expansion. These findings, drawn predominantly from a single geopolitical zone, support targeted investment in structured training, equipment and reimbursement pathways, and a coordinated national apheresis registry, while highlighting the need for confirmatory studies with broader geographic and professional representation.

articles.title: Response to a letter to the editor entitled 'Long-acting relaxin for pulmonary hypertension: From systemic pharmacodynamics to disease-site pharmacology'.
Serious Illness Conversations in Hospital Medicine: Assessing Self-Perceived Knowledge and Skills.
articles.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
articles.abstract: IntroductionSerious illness conversations (SICs) are structured discussions intended to align medical care and treatment decisions with patients' values, goals, priorities, and preferences, often referred to as goals of care discussions. Despite the importance of these conversations, clinicians receive no standardized training. As hospitalists often lead SICs, we sought to assess baseline knowledge and perceptions surrounding SICs to help understand potential needs and interventions.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was distributed to hospital medicine clinicians at 1 academic medical center. The survey was open for 6 weeks and sought to assess clinician knowledge, self-perceptions of skills, wellness, and documentation. Descriptive statistics and inductive thematic approach were conducted.ResultsThere were 55 (43%) responses, with 74.6% being physicians. The majority of respondents had no prior SIC training. For individuals who don't use a framework during SICs, 32 reported a framework would be beneficial. Respondents reported high confidence in self-perception of SIC communication skills, but 0% exclusively identified the correct timepoints to be conducting SICs. Clinicians reported high awareness of communication tools and skills, however routine usage remained low. Clinicians reported multiple documentation locations in the electronic medical record, and only 18 (32.7%) reported knowing how to bill for these conversations.ConclusionsThis study found a discordance between clinicians' high self-perception of knowledge of communication skills and appropriate SIC timepoints when compared to a lower self-reported usage of skills. Future studies should focus on educating hospital medicine providers on appropriate communication timepoints and transitioning communication technique awareness to routine usage.

articles.title: Admission-Time Prediction of In-Hospital Major Amputation in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: Model Development and Temporal Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major above-ankle amputation is a devastating outcome of diabetes-related foot disease. The Wagner classification is routinely available but places many inpatients in the same grade; few prediction models for major amputation have undergone temporal validation or reported calibration.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an admission-time model for in-hospital major amputation from routinely collected data and to validate it internally in a later period at the same center. Its intended role is to support prognostic communication and prioritization of early multidisciplinary and vascular assessment and not to inform the decision to amputate. Secondary objectives were to compare machine learning algorithms with penalized logistic regression and to assess the added value of segmental limb pressures.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study at a tertiary center in Taiwan, adults with a single hospitalization for diabetes-related foot disease from 2015 through 2025 were divided by admission date into a development cohort (2015-2021) and a temporal test cohort (2022-2025). Twenty admission variables were modeled. Five algorithms were compared by nested cross-validation in the development cohort; the one with the lowest out-of-fold log loss became the primary model, with operating thresholds fixed before a single evaluation in the test cohort.

RESULTS: The development cohort included 1400 patients with 126 (9.0%) major amputations and the test cohort 771 patients with 51 (6.6%). In the test cohort, the primary ridge logistic regression model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.882 (95% CI 0.841-0.917) vs 0.804 (95% CI 0.737-0.867) for Wagner grade alone. Absolute risk was overpredicted: mean predicted risk was 9.6% vs 6.6% observed, with calibration intercept -0.47, slope 1.33, and observed-to-expected ratio 0.69 (95% CI 0.53-0.86). At the prespecified screening threshold, 343 (44.5%) patients were flagged; sensitivity was 0.980 (95% CI 0.897-0.997), specificity 0.593 (95% CI 0.557-0.628), positive predictive value 14.6% (95% CI 11.2%-18.7%), and negative predictive value 0.998 (95% CI 0.987-1.000). Of 771 patients, no major amputation occurred among the 396 (51.4%) patients in the lowest risk band; of 54 patients, 22 (40.7%) patients in the highest band underwent major amputation. Random forest and gradient boosting reached higher AUROCs (0.915 and 0.912) in secondary comparisons. Segmental limb pressures did not clearly improve discrimination in complete cases (change in AUROC -0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: In an internal temporal validation at a single center, a transparent model based on routine admission data added discrimination for in-hospital major amputation beyond Wagner grade alone but overpredicted absolute risk. It estimates amputation under 1 institution's care pathway and was not compared with multidimensional classifications such as Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection; whether acting on it improves outcomes is untested. Independent external validation, recalibration where needed, and prospective evaluation are required before clinical use; the model must not be used to indicate amputation or withhold limb-salvage evaluation.

articles.title: Feasibility Assessment of Smartphone Camera-Based Atrial Fibrillation Detection Compared With Portable Electrocardiogram: Single-Patient Case Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) affects more than 33 million people globally, with many cases remaining undiagnosed due to the paroxysmal nature of the condition. Current portable AF detection devices require additional hardware, and their cost may limit their accessibility in community screening programs. Facial camera-based remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is a novel alternative to conventional fingertip-based photoplethysmography (PPG) that enables contact-free cardiac rhythm assessment.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the technical feasibility of a novel smartphone camera-based facial rPPG AF detection system by comparing its performance with that of a portable electrocardiogram (ECG) device under real-world home monitoring conditions.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-patient volunteer case study involving a patient with diagnosed paroxysmal AF and atrial flutter with variable block over 12 consecutive days. Simultaneous 60-second recordings were scheduled 3 times daily using the electronRx smartphone app and a Kardia portable ECG device to obtain a total of 36 paired recordings. The primary outcome was device agreement in rhythm classification between the 2 systems. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the effect of signal quality on device agreement and analysis of discordant recordings to identify technical limitations.

RESULTS: Of the 36 scheduled recording sessions, 35 were attempted, yielding 24 successful simultaneous recordings. Of these, 23 paired recordings met the quality criteria, and device agreement was achieved in 21 (91.3%) recordings. The smartphone system detected 4 of the 5 episodes classified as AF by the Kardia device and agreed with 17 of the 18 recordings classified as normal sinus rhythm. A total of 2 discordant cases were identified: 1 false negative associated with atrial flutter presenting as a fixed 3:1 atrioventricular block and 1 false positive related to poor signal quality due to suboptimal lighting conditions. Signal quality significantly affected performance, with 94.7% agreement in recordings of good quality compared with 75% in recordings of poor quality.

CONCLUSIONS: This case study demonstrates the technical feasibility of using a smartphone facial camera-based rPPG rhythm analysis for AF detection. The approach shows promise as an accessible screening tool. However, the single-patient design, data attrition resulting from synchronization and signal quality issues, and the identified technical limitations highlight the need for larger validation studies before clinical application can be considered.

articles.title: Automated Detection of Abnormal Pediatric Electroencephalograms Using Machine Learning: Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in medicine as a technique for the assessment of several brain-related pathologies. However, EEG interpretation requires specialized expertise and remains a labor-intensive task, particularly for prolonged recordings in intensive care, where timely expert review is often challenging.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to address this problem by using AI methods to automate EEG interpretation and compare the performance of different modeling approaches.

METHODS: A gradient boosting-based model, inspired by the work of Albaqami et al, was implemented and compared to deep learning (DL)-based models using convolutional neural networks to classify images generated from raw EEG signals. The models were trained and tested on pediatric EEGs acquired at the University Hospital in Essen.

RESULTS: The DL model showed higher observed sensitivity (78.3%) and F1-score (80%) compared to the gradient boosting model (sensitivity: 65.2%; F1-score: 73.8%), indicating improved detection of abnormal EEGs. However, the gradient boosting approach achieved higher specificity (93% vs 89.6%), suggesting a stronger ability to recognize normal EEGs. Overall, both methods yielded promising results, with classification accuracies reaching up to 85.3%.

CONCLUSIONS: Both approaches show potential for automated EEG interpretation. Future improvements, including larger and more diverse datasets, refined DL architectures, and integration of explainable AI techniques, could further enhance performance.

articles.title: Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia (CTAR-SwiFt): Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-acquired pneumonia in frail older people requiring hospital admission is considered to be commonly associated with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia). A rehabilitation program (chin tuck against resistance [CTAR]) targeting the anterior neck musculature involved in laryngeal movement can improve swallowing safety. We have developed a swallowing exercise rehabilitation intervention (CTAR-SwiFt [Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia]) by adapting a previously established swallowing exercise. The CTAR-SwiFt intervention consists of a feedback-enabled exercise ball that can be squeezed under the chin, with real-time feedback provided via a mobile app.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the usability of the CTAR-SwiFt intervention and the feasibility of recruiting participants to take part in a larger-scale multicenter randomized controlled trial.

METHODS: We recruited participants aged 75 years and older who were admitted with a diagnosis of pneumonia to the acute frailty wards at 2 participating hospitals in the United Kingdom. Patients had to be medically stable. Study participants were randomized to 1 of 3 groups: standard care (control), low intensity (once daily), or high intensity (twice daily) CTAR-SwiFt exercises. The intervention period lasted for 12 weeks; the final follow-up assessment was conducted at 24 weeks. Feasibility outcomes were assessed descriptively and included participant recruitment rate, retention, compliance with the exercise regimen, and adverse incidents. The Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) and 4 Question Test (4QT) measures were used to screen for oropharyngeal dysphagia. Additionally, we assessed the usability and acceptability of the intervention device and performance of different clinical outcome measures (chin tuck strength, Functional Oral Intake Scale [FOIS], Quality of Life in Swallowing Disorders [SWAL-QOL] questionnaire, EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level [EQ-5D-3L] questionnaire, and swallow speed).

RESULTS: A total of 24 participants were recruited, and 21 were randomized at the rate of 0.91 recruits per month (95% CI 0.59-1.0). Of those approached, 32% (24/75) were willing to take part, and of those randomized, 52% (11/21) completed the study. The major reason for failing to complete the study was medical, with people becoming unwell or being readmitted to hospital. The outcome measures assessed suggested that there was an improvement in the EAT-10 and 4QT and a minimal impact on FOIS. Quality of life as measured by the EQ-5D-3L showed improvement with time. The low-intensity intervention demonstrated the best improvement. Participants were able to partake in the CTAR-SwiFt exercises. There was an improvement in the consistency of ball squeeze over the course of the intervention and an increase in maximum chin tuck strength by a mean of 0.8 (SD 0.9) kgf.

CONCLUSIONS: The literature supports the benefit of CTAR in improving swallowing in community-dwelling older adults. Our study has demonstrated that older, frail adults are able to perform CTAR and could use the ExerPhager. A future study should investigate the benefits of CTAR-SwiFt in community-dwelling older, frail adults after pneumonia.

articles.title: Impact of Hands-On Pediatric Emergency Training on Wound Suturing, Airway Management, and Orthopedic Casting Skills: Prospective Pre-Post Interventional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opportunities to practice low-frequency skills for high-acuity pediatric emergency procedures in clinical settings are limited. The Basic Emergency Skills Techniques 3N1 (BEST 3N1) workshop was designed as a structured, hands-on training program to support procedural skill development among pediatric emergency care practitioners.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate preworkshop to postworkshop changes in procedural performance and knowledge after a 3-day hands-on pediatric emergency skills workshop.

METHODS: A quasi-experimental prospective pre-post interventional study was conducted during the 8th BEST 3N1 workshop, held from February 11 to 13, 2025, at the Simulation and Skills Development Centre, Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The workshop included 24 scheduled continuing medical education hours in 3 domains: wound suturing, pediatric airway management, and pediatric orthopedic emergencies and casting. Procedural performance was assessed using complete paired preworkshop and postworkshop data for each assessment. Day 1 wound suturing and day 2 airway management were assessed using 4-item checklists scored from 0 to 8. Day 3 orthopedic casting competence was assessed using a keyword-based rubric covering equipment, procedural steps, and postapplication care, with a total score range of 0 to 30. Written knowledge was assessed using a 30-item multiple-choice test.

RESULTS: The number of paired observations differed in assessments because the analysis was based on complete matched preworkshop and postworkshop data for each outcome. Day 1 wound suturing checklist mean scores increased from 4.14 (SD 1.72) to 7.72 (SD 0.68) among 88 paired participants, with a mean change of 3.58 (SD 1.71; P<.001) points. Day 2 airway management checklist scores increased from 5.47 (SD 1.88) to 7.81 (SD 0.56) among 77 paired participants, with a mean change of 2.34 (SD 1.96; P<.001) points. Day 3 orthopedic casting total competence scores increased from 4.20 to 6.39 among 77 paired participants, with a mean change of 2.19 (SD 1.72; 95% CI 1.80-2.58; P<.001). Written knowledge scores increased from 19.04 (SD 3.77) to 22.32 (SD 3.23) among 94 paired participants, with a mean change of 3.28 (95% CI 2.16-4.39; P<.001) points.

CONCLUSIONS: The BEST 3N1 workshop was associated with improved checklist-based procedural performance, orthopedic casting competence, and written knowledge among pediatric emergency care practitioners. These findings support the use of structured hands-on workshops for high-acuity, low-frequency pediatric emergency skills.

articles.title: Adhesion G protein-coupled receptor A2 promotes tick-borne encephalitis virus replication by interacting with NS2B to enhance viral protease activity.
articles.abstract: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is a neurotropic flavivirus that causes severe neurological disease in humans, but the host factors required for its efficient replication remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify ADGRA2 as a novel host dependency factor for TBEV. Loss of ADGRA2, but not other ADGR family members, markedly restricts infection by multiple TBEV strains in human cells and primary mouse astrocytes. ADGRA2 is dispensable for viral entry but is required for efficient viral RNA replication, as demonstrated by impaired negative-strand RNA synthesis and accumulation of double-stranded RNA intermediates in ADGRA2-deficient cells. During infection, ADGRA2 is relocalized from the plasma membrane to the endoplasmic reticulum, where it functions independently of canonical WNT/β-catenin signaling. Mechanistically, ADGRA2 interacts with the viral cofactor NS2B, enhances NS2B-NS3 autocleavage and protease activity, promotes viral polyprotein processing, and facilitates NS2B/NS3 association with NS2A to enhance replication organelle biogenesis. ADGRA2 also promotes replication of Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), Zika virus (ZIKV) and Dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2), suggesting a conserved role across flaviviruses. Together, these findings reveal that a host membrane receptor can be repurposed to drive NS2B-dependent protease maturation and replication complex assembly, thereby enabling efficient flaviviral replication.

articles.title: Early emergence of HIV-1 elite neutralizers and maturation dynamics of neutralization breadth in a Chinese early infection cohort.
articles.abstract: Eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) usually takes years during human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection, and identifying early signals of their development would be valuable for vaccine design. The commonly used pseudovirus panels are largely based on historical viral sequences, which may not accurately reflect early neutralizing responses. To address this, we developed a 12-pseudovirus panel (DRVI-MS panel) that covers circulating strains in China, showing comparable genetic diversity and N-glycan composition to the global panel. Using this panel, we profiled neutralizing responses in 90 plasma samples collected at 0.5, 1, and 2 years post-diagnosis from a treatment-naive early infection cohort. Neutralization capacity remained limited during the first year but expanded in breadth and potency markedly by year 2. Notably, six elite neutralizers were identified within 2 years, including one emerging as early as 15 months, indicating that elite neutralization capacity may mature earlier than previously appreciated. The relationship between viral load and neutralization evolved from early inverse to positive associations after 2 years, likely reflecting prolonged antigen driven population-level antibody maturation. These data support the feasibility of capturing bnAb-related signals during early infection and provide a practical tool for bnAb discovery and vaccine-oriented studies.

articles.title: NDV V relies on karyopherins for nuclear import to enhance viral replication by facilitating the nuclear export of the 60S ribosomal subunit precursor.
articles.abstract: Newcastle disease (ND) is an acute, febrile, septicemic, and highly contagious infectious disease of poultry caused by the ND virus (NDV). Although vaccines against ND are widely used, reports of atypical ND persist, significantly impacting development of the poultry industry. Investigating the pathogenic mechanisms of NDV infection in host cells is crucial for the advancement of vaccines and enhancement of prevention and control strategies. In this study, we elucidated the molecular mechanism involved in the nuclear import of the NDV V protein and found that NDV V binds primarily to the nuclear import proteins KPNA4, KPNA5, and KPNB1 via its NLS region. The NDV NLS mutant (rGM-V/R142A/R152A) and parent (rGM) strains were successfully rescued using reverse genetics technology. Nuclear and cytoplasmic samples from DF-1 cells infected with rGM-V/R142A/R152A and rGM were subjected to tandem mass tag labeling and quantitative proteomics sequencing. The results indicate that nuclear entry of the NDV V protein may influence ribosome-related functions. Further investigation of the biological function of NDV V in nuclear entry revealed that it may enhance the interaction between NXT2 and TMA16 by upregulating their expression, thereby accelerating nuclear export of the 60S subunit precursor and ultimately promoting viral replication. These findings provide unique insight into the molecular mechanism responsible for facilitating NDV infection in hosts and provide a basis for exploring how other viruses interact with ribosomes.

articles.title: Elevated malonic acid and 15d-PGJ2 in MASLD rats with diabetes triggered pathological cardiac remodeling through impairment of mitochondrial health and cellular metabolism.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) significantly raises the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and makes it the leading cause of death in affected individuals. Despite growing evidence, the liver-heart connection remains poorly understood. MASLD was induced in male SD rats using an 8-week high-fat diet along with a single streptozotocin dose at week 6. Cardiac changes were assessed by echocardiography, electrocardiography, and histopathology. Two altered metabolites identified by LC-MS/MS were evaluated in cardiomyoblasts (MTT, JC-1, MitoSOX, & Seahorse) and in rats to assess cardiac structure and function. MASLD rats with diabetes exhibited increased LV mass, wall thickness, diastolic diameter, and volume, with reduced ejection fraction, fractional shortening, cardiac output, and stroke volume. Histology confirmed cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, fibrosis, and hepatic lipid accumulation. LC-MS/MS identified elevated malonic acid and 15-deoxy-12,14-prostaglandin J2 (15d-PGJ2) in serum. In cardiomyoblasts, these metabolites increased mitochondrial ROS, reduced membrane potential, and decreased metabolites such as taurine, arginine, succinate, and l-glutamine. Eight weeks of in vivo treatment with malonic acid and 15d-PGJ2 induced pathological cardiac remodeling, fibrosis, and subendocardial ischemia. Metabolite-treated hearts also showed an increase in inosine and 12R-HETE, with reduced isovaleric acid, creatine, proline, and N-acetyl-L-histidine. Altered cardiac structure and function in MASLD rats were associated with elevated serum malonic acid and 15d-PGJ2, which impair mitochondrial homeostasis and cellular metabolism. These findings support a liver-heart axis and highlight potential therapeutic targets for MASLD-related CVD.

articles.title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals cardiomyocyte injury and fibro-inflammatory remodeling in early PKP2-deficient ARVC.
articles.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is an inherited cardiomyopathy caused primarily by mutations in desmosomal genes, among which pathogenic PKP2 variants being the most common genetic cause. Previous studies on ARVC have mainly focus on its middle and late pathological stages, whereas the early cellular and molecular events triggered by PKP2 loss remain poorly defined.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We generated a cardiomyocyte-specific Pkp2 knockout mouse line and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to delineate the early cellular landscape of ARVC. PKP2 loss triggered pathological remodeling of cardiomyocytes and induced a large-scale phenotypic shift in cardiac fibroblasts from a homeostatic state to an activated, matrix-producing population. Concomitantly, proangiogenic endothelial subsets expanded and Ccr2+/Spp1+ proinflammatory macrophages accumulated, reshaping the cardiac microenvironment. Cell-cell communication network analysis demonstrated enhanced intercellular crosstalk at the early stage of ARVC, with aberrant activation of profibrotic and inflammatory signaling pathways. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining and ligand-receptor interaction analysis, we identified CCN2 may serve as a potential mediator in early-stage PKP2-related ARVC.

CONCLUSION: Our study proposes a multicellular relay model of early ARVC pathogenesis and identifies CCN2 as a putative intercellular communication factor in PKP2-deficient hearts. These findings highlight intercellular communication networks as critical mediators of disease progression and potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Hemisphere-specific neuroplasticity after basal ganglia stroke: divergent patterns of brain reorganization revealed by fALFF and ReHo.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lesion laterality modulates post-stroke neuroplasticity following basal ganglia infarction, but hemisphere-specific reorganization patterns of motor circuits remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate lateralized changes in spontaneous brain activity and local synchronization in patients with left versus right basal ganglia infarction using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI), and to explore their associations with motor recovery.

METHODS: Resting-state fMRI-derived fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) and regional homogeneity (ReHo) were analyzed in 31 patients with left basal ganglia infarction (LBGIS), 33 patients with right basal ganglia infarction (RBGIS), and 33 healthy controls. TFCE-FWE corrected two-sample t-tests and covariate-adjusted partial correlations were used to compare brain activity and link functional alterations to Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) motor scores.

RESULTS: LBGIS displayed hypoactivity in ipsilesional motor cortices alongside hyperactivation of contralesional cerebellum and prefrontal areas; ipsilesional sensorimotor ReHo positively correlated with FMA, whereas contralesional cerebellar fALFF negatively correlated with FMA. RBGIS showed reduced ipsilesional frontoparietal activity and isolated hyper-synchronization within the ipsilesional frontoparietal motor network without cerebellar recruitment, with elevated ReHo in ipsilesional precentral gyrus/SMA negatively associated with FMA. Direct group comparisons validated stronger bilateral motor-planning and contralesional cerebellar signals in LBGIS, and higher right visual-spatial fALFF in RBGIS.

CONCLUSIONS: Left and right basal ganglia infarctions elicit divergent hemispheric neuroplastic modifications in motor networks. These lateralized functional signatures could serve as imaging biomarkers for lesion-side-customized motor rehabilitation.

articles.title: The role of cellular signaling pathways in the therapeutic effects of sonodynamic therapy against periodontitis: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dysbiotic subgingival biofilms and driven by a dysregulated host response that destroys the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone. Mechanical debridement remains the cornerstone of therapy, but biofilm tolerance, anatomically inaccessible niches, and the limited action of antimicrobials on host-mediated tissue destruction leave clinically relevant gaps. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) uses low-intensity ultrasound to activate sonosensitizers and generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), offering deeper tissue reach than light-based approaches and a route to site-specific, non-antibiotic adjunctive care. Beyond microbial killing, ROS and co-released mediators may reshape host signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on signaling pathways modulated by SDT and grades it by proximity to periodontitis. Direct evidence from periodontal or jawbone-infection studies concerns NF-κB, NLRP3/caspase-1, Toll-like receptor (TLR) and NOD-like receptor signaling, IL-17 signaling, osteoclast differentiation, M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization, and AMPK and PI3K/Akt-associated osteogenesis. Mechanistic precedents from non-periodontal models concern ROS-PPARγ-NF-κB, Nrf2/ARE, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-autophagy signaling. Direct periodontal evidence is limited to a small number of preclinical studies, pathway-level claims rest mainly on transcript- or protein-level associations, and the anti-inflammatory and pro-osteogenic effects of some platforms are attributable to co-delivered nitric oxide or metal ions rather than to sonodynamic ROS. We therefore distinguish SDT-dependent from platform-dependent effects, discuss dental translational issues (delivery, ultrasound source and dosimetry, safety, peri-implantitis, systemic comorbidity), and propose research priorities: pathway-specific validation, standardized ultrasound reporting, and controlled clinical trials of SDT as an adjunct to subgingival instrumentation.

articles.title: Heat shock proteins in DNA damage response and repair: A graphical review.
articles.abstract: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are molecular chaperones primarily recognised for maintaining proteostasis, but increasing evidence indicates that they also regulate cellular responses to DNA damage. HSPs influence DNA damage sensing, checkpoint signalling, repair complex assembly, DNA repair, and damage tolerance through mechanisms that largely reflect chaperone-dependent regulation of client stability, assembly and localisation. This graphical review summarises experimental evidence linking HSP27, HSP40, HSP60, HSP70, HSP90, and HSP110 to major genome maintenance pathways, including homologous recombination, non-homologous end joining, mismatch repair, base excision repair, nucleotide excision repair, and translesion DNA synthesis. We examine how individual HSPs affect the stability, subcellular localisation, assembly, and activity of DNA repair and checkpoint proteins, while highlighting differences in the strength and type of supporting evidence. We also propose a conceptual "chaperone-to-repair shift", in which genotoxic stress may alter the relative engagement of HSP networks with DNA damage response (DDR) proteins. This proposed framework provides a testable perspective on the relationship between proteostasis and genome maintenance, without implying a universal switch from one function to the other.

articles.title: Assessing occupational exposure to imidacloprid among animal shelter workers using human biomonitoring.
articles.abstract: Imidacloprid (IMI) is a neonicotinoid insecticide used as an ectoparasite treatment for pets in professional and home-use settings. Animal shelter workers apply these treatments to pets in their care and often use multiple ectoparasite treatments per day, resulting in a potential for occupational IMI exposure. To assess IMI exposures among animal shelter workers, human biomonitoring approaches were adopted, with multiple individual spot urine samples collected over 24- or 48-hour periods from eight full-time animal shelter workers. Samples were analysed for IMI and its metabolites, IMI-olefin and OH-IMI, to assess occupational exposure to IMI. Study results show that animal shelter workers had elevated urinary concentrations of IMI and metabolites compared to a previous general population study, with concentrations comparable to pet owners using the same products. However, all urinary concentrations were below 1.4% of the Acceptable Operator Exposure Level, indicating low-level exposures among the study cohort.

articles.title: Codon Optimization Enables Recombinant Expression of Soybean GmPRR7-1 in Escherichia coli: A Rosetta(DE3) Fed-Batch Production and Purification Workflow.
articles.abstract: Pseudo-Response Regulators (PRRs) are circadian clock components that regulate plant development, flowering and abiotic stress responses. Functional studies of plant PRRs are slowed by the time required for transformation and phenotypic evaluation, so purified recombinant protein offers a practical route to in vitro interaction analyses. Heterologous production of plant PRRs in Escherichia coli is nevertheless challenging because of codon-usage differences and their aggregation-prone multidomain architecture. Here we established an E. coli expression and purification workflow for functional soybean GmPRR7-1.
