The native GmPRR7-1 coding sequence in pET-28a(+) and a codon-optimized construct in pBT7-C-HIS were screened in BL21(DE3) and Rosetta(DE3) at 16, 25 and 37°C. The native construct was not detectably expressed in either host under any condition, whereas the codon-optimized construct yielded a target-sized band, identifying codon optimization as a prerequisite for expression of this protein. The target band remained detectable in Rosetta(DE3) at 25°C; because these whole-cell lysates were not fractionated, this screening identifies a productive construct, host and induction combination rather than ranking the two hosts. Rosetta(DE3) carrying the optimized sequence was cultivated in a 5-L fed-batch bioreactor, and soluble GmPRR7-1 was recovered by single-step Ni-NTA affinity chromatography. Eluted protein corresponded to 0.83% of the soluble-fraction protein, comparable to small-scale cultures induced at 25°C (0.77%); these values describe total eluted protein rather than target-specific yield. Anti-His immunoblotting confirmed the target and detected minor His-reactive degradation products. Purified GmPRR7-1 retained specific interactions with MBP-tagged GmFDL19 and three GmLUX homologs, demonstrating a workflow that reproducibly delivers interaction-competent GmPRR7-1.

articles.title: Dietary pattern, lung function and incident COPD over 11 years in the HUNT Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Longitudinal evidence on the association of dietary patterns with lung function and COPD risk is limited and inconclusive. We examined whether adherence to a dietary pattern aligned with the latest Nordic Nutrition Recommendations (NNR2023) was associated with lung function, longitudinal change in lung function and risk of developing COPD.

METHODS: In total 5,520 individuals, 58% women, mean ± SD age 50±13 years, with baseline dietary data and spirometry measurements (2006-08 and 2017-19) were included from the Trøndelag Health Study. We constructed a dietary adherence index from nine NNR2023-relevant food and beverage categories. COPD was defined as pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) <the lower limit of normal in individuals aged ≥40 years. Clinical COPD additionally required respiratory symptoms and ≥10 pack-years. Associations were examined using multivariable regression analyses adjusted for lifestyle- and demographic covariates.

RESULTS: Adherence to the NNR-aligned dietary pattern was associated with better lung function at baseline and lower odds of incident clinical COPD, OR: 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78-0.96). Each 1-point increase in the index corresponded to 11 mL higher FEV1 and 14 mL higher FVC. Among ever-smokers, the OR was 0.90 (95% CI: 0.80-1.00) after additionally adjustment for smoking status and pack-years. Baseline diet did not predict longitudinal changes in lung function, or incident spirometry-defined COPD.

CONCLUSION: A healthy dietary pattern was positively associated with baseline lung function but not with longitudinal change in lung function or incident spirometry-defined COPD. Results for incident clinical COPD remains uncertain.

articles.title: Development, content validation and reliability testing of a measure of inhaler technique for all devices: The Portsmouth Inhaler Technique (PIT) Score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inhaler technique errors are common and associated with poorer disease control. Clinicians assess technique against device-specific checklists that differ in content, limiting comparisons across inhaler types.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate the Portsmouth Inhaler Technique (PIT) Score, a standardised, device-neutral assessment tool for adults and children.

METHODS: Inhaler technique steps were extracted from 418 published and NHS checklists and underwent three rounds of Delphi essentiality assessment by 18 experts, followed by relevance (34 experts) and clarity (62 assessors, including inhaler users) evaluation. Discriminant validity was examined by comparing PIT Scores, derived retrospectively for 677 adults in an observational study, with Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ6) or COPD Assessment Test (CAT) scores. Twenty-two experts assessed 14 standardised videos representing seven different inhaler devices to evaluate reliability; 20 repeated the assessment.

RESULTS: Seventy-two steps were refined over three rounds into a 16-step checklist with ten scored and six unscored steps. All steps met the relevance threshold (I-CVI ≥0.78); average scale-level content validity was 0.95. PIT Scores showed no meaningful correlation with ACQ6 (ρ=0.008; p=0.858) or CAT (ρ=0.077; p=0.267), supporting discriminant validity. Inter-rater reliability was excellent (Gwet's AC1=0.9177; ICC=0.9015), as was intra-rater agreement (AC1>0.92). Median PIT Score completion time was 58 seconds.

CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, the PIT Score is the first reliable clinician-observed assessment tool applying one set of scored steps to all inhaler types. Its ten scored steps give a practical, standardised record of technique across devices. Prospective evaluation in routine practice, in children and against clinical outcomes is needed.

articles.title: Intrapartum Maternal Glycemic Trajectories and the Risk of Neonatal Hypoglycemia in Type 1 Diabetes Pregnancies: A Granular Continuous Glucose Monitoring Analysis.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the longitudinal relationship between intrapartum maternal glycemic trajectories and the development of neonatal hypoglycemia (NH) in pregnancies complicated by type 1 diabetes (T1D).

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 31 pregnant women with pre-gestational T1D managed via multiple daily injections or manual insulin pump therapy. High-resolution maternal glucose trends were tracked using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and aligned retrospectively backward from umbilical cord clamping. Maternal glucose over time was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. Predictive performance and optimal clinical thresholds were evaluated via Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis.

RESULTS: NH occurred in 15 out of 31 newborns (48.4%). Longitudinal mixed-effects modeling revealed a significant group x time interaction (P <0.01), with maternal glycemic trajectories in the NH group significantly diverging from the euglycemic cohort starting at the 6-hour pre-delivery window (119 +/- 13 vs. 104 +/- 11 mg/dL, corrected P = 0.002). ROC analysis demonstrated that predictive power peaked during the terminal 2 hours of labor (Area Under the Curve, AUC = 0.88). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for large-for-gestational-age (LGA) status, terminal maternal glucose emerged as the sole independent predictor of NH (Odds Ratio = 6.72 per 10 mg/dL increase, 95% CI: 1.05-1.40; P <0.01).

CONCLUSION: Intrapartum maternal glucose trajectories significantly associate with immediate neonatal metabolic transition. Stricter peripartum glycemic control starting at least 6 hours before expected delivery may help mitigate the risk of a terminal fetal insulin surge and subsequent hypoglycemia, targeting standard consensus-based ranges.

articles.title: Thromboembolic Complications in Cushing's syndrome: Origin, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Implications.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cushing's syndrome (CS) is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), which may persist after surgery and biochemical remission. This review synthesizes current evidence on VTE risk, underlying mechanisms, clinical assessment, and prevention and treatment strategies in patients with CS.

METHODS: This narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for relevant English-language publications from 1999 through August 2026. Eligible sources included observational studies, case series, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical guidelines, and consensus statements addressing thrombotic risk, venous thromboembolism, or mechanisms of hypercoagulability in CS. Relevant findings were synthesized qualitatively and organized thematically.

RESULTS: A systematic meta-analysis reported approximately 18-fold higher odds of spontaneous VTE in patients with endogenous CS than in the general population. The prothrombotic state involves alterations in coagulation, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, platelet activation, inflammation, and venous stasis. Thrombotic risk may persist after biochemical remission, although its duration remains uncertain. The 2025 international Delphi consensus supports individualized thromboprophylaxis, with low-molecular-weight heparin preferred. Evidence supporting direct oral anticoagulants for prophylaxis remains limited. Clinical decisions should account for thrombotic and bleeding risks, including perioperative bleeding and potential drug interactions between direct oral anticoagulants and steroidogenesis inhibitors. No validated CS-specific risk prediction tool is available; a proposed framework may support individualized risk assessment. Proposed genetic, epigenetic, and non-coding RNA mechanisms remain hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSION: VTE prevention in CS requires individualized risk assessment and careful consideration of perioperative and post-remission risk. Prospective studies are needed to establish optimal prophylaxis strategies and validate CS-specific risk prediction approaches.

articles.title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices.
authors: Cardiology/CV Surgery Section, Pulmonary Vascular Disease and Cardiovascular Network.
articles.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists versus DPP-4 and SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients with Bronchiectasis and Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited disease-modifying therapies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, but their impact on bronchiectasis outcomes remains unknown.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Is GLP-1RA use, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, associated with better clinical outcomes in patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes (T2D)?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX global federated research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between June 1, 2022, and May 30, 2025. We compared clinical outcomes, including all-cause mortality, bronchiectasis exacerbation, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infections, with patients receiving DPP-4i) or SGLT2i using propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 1,029 patients per group were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i cohort, and 2,255 patients per group in the GLP-1RA versus SGLT2i cohort. Compared with DPP-4i, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.56) and reduced risks of acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.46-0.65). Similar benefits were observed compared with SGLT2i for all-cause mortality (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.40-0.60), acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.39-0.55), and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.68-0.86). Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent mortality benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups, with particularly pronounced effects in obese patients but there was no statistically significant reduction in bronchiectasis exacerbations.

INTERPRETATION: Among patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality and reduced respiratory complications compared with DPP-4i or SGLT2i. These findings suggest potential disease-modifying benefits of GLP-1RAs in bronchiectasis beyond glycemic control.

articles.title: Does Food-Related Administration Matter in Heart Failure Pharmacotherapy?
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences

articles.title: Musculoskeletal Pain in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes and Matched Controls from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The burden of musculoskeletal (MSK) pain in type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to compare the prevalence of MSK pain in adults with T1D and matched controls and examined variables associated with pain and its relationship with quality of life and functional fitness.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study used baseline Comprehensive cohort data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA). Adults with T1D (n=93) were matched 1:4 to controls (n=372) by age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, and physical activity. Pain outcomes were self-reported. Regression analyses identified variables associated with pain, and generalized estimating equations assessed between-group differences.

RESULTS: Overall prevalence of any pain was not statistically significant in T1D versus controls (37.6% vs 36.3%, p=0.851). In adjusted analyses, T1D was associated with higher odds of hand pain (OR=3.97, 95% CI 1.39-11.38). Female sex and higher BMI were associated with select site-specific pain outcomes, but blood biomarkers of glycemia (HbA1c) and inflammation had no consistent association with any pain. The presence of MSK pain was associated with lower life satisfaction (OR=0.56, p=0.002), poorer perceived health (OR=0.36, p<0.001), and reduced average grip strength (β=-1.90, p=0.049), independent of diabetes status.

CONCLUSIONS: Adults with T1D have increased odds of site-specific MSK pain, particularly in the hands, relative to controls. Routine assessment and targeted management of MSK pain should be considered to support functional health and overall well-being.

articles.title: Association Between Revascularization Timing and Outcomes for Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), yet the optimal timing of coronary revascularization in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with severe AS and stable CAD, defined as fractional flow reserve ≤0.80, instantaneous wave-free ratio ≤ 0.89, or visual stenosis ≥90%, who underwent TAVI between October 2013 and July 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: PCI-first and TAVI-first. The primary endpoint was 1-year incidence of major adverse cardiac events (MACE: all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and unplanned revascularization). The secondary endpoint was 3-year MACE stratified by PCI after TAVI among the TAVI-first group.

RESULTS: Of 1126 TAVI patients, 209 met criteria for concomitant CAD (PCI-first, n = 112; TAVI-first, n = 97). The TAVI-first group had lower frailty and fewer New York Heart Association functional class III/IV symptoms, whereas the PCI-first group had more blood transfusions. At 1 year, the crude incidence of MACE was higher in the PCI-first group, although this difference was not significant after propensity score adjustment (HR 1.62; 95% CI 0.60-5.2; p = 0.36). Among TAVI-first group, patients who underwent PCI after TAVI had a lower incidence of MACE (log-rank p = 0.007), but the 90-day landmark analysis showed no significant difference (0/24 vs. 5/62 events; log-rank p = 0.23).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with severe AS and CAD, a PCI-first strategy was associated with a higher incidence of bleeding and transfusion without improvement in short-term outcomes. A TAVI-first strategy with selective PCI during follow-up may be a reasonable alternative, although the long-term benefit of post-TAVI PCI awaits confirmation in randomized trials.

articles.title: The Role of Oxidative Stress and Antioxidant Signaling in Skin Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress represents a prevalent form of cellular and tissue damage, arising from an imbalance between diminished antioxidant defense mechanisms and elevated reactive species production. This pathological condition occurs following exposure to endogenous or exogenous stressors, triggering the intracellular accumulation of excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), reactive nitrogen species (RNS), and other free radicals that ultimately induce cellular and tissue injury. Skin wounds are a disruption or interruption of normal skin anatomical organization and functional continuity. They can be categorized into acute and chronic skin wounds based on the time of healing, and consists of four overlapping stages: hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and remodeling phases. Any mistake in any stage can lead to delayed skin wound healing, non-healing ulcers or even scar formation, which happens especially easily in diabetic patients. Impaired skin wound repair represents a significant clinical concern that may precipitate severe sequelae such as localized soft tissue infection (cellulitis), tissue necrosis (gangrene), and systemic inflammatory response (sepsis). These complications frequently culminate in the necessity for surgical limb amputation, particularly in the lower extremities. These negative consequences impose psychological and economic burdens on patients and countries. Oxidative stress plays a regulatory role throughout all four phases of cutaneous wound repair through multiple signaling cascades, including but not limited to the Keap1/Nrf2/ARE pathway and the PI3K/AKT pathway. In this review, we describe the relationships between oxidative stress and skin wound healing process, in order to provide the potential mechanisms for new options of treatment in skin wound healing via oxidative stress.

articles.title: Apixaban Benefit in Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation Accounting for Competing Risks: A Reanalysis of the ARTESIA Trial.
articles.abstract: In the ARTESIA trial, apixaban reduced stroke and systemic embolism compared with aspirin in patients with subclinical atrial fibrillation (AF), but the primary analysis treated death and AF progression as censoring rather than competing events. We estimated the absolute risk reduction (ARR) at 3.5 years treating death and AF progression as competing events. We used event-level data reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves to probabilistically impute status and timing of competing events. The ARR was 1.94% when treating death and AF progression as censoring events vs. 1.62% treating them as competing events (difference 0.33 percentage points; 95% CI 0.04 to 0.62). Absolute benefit estimates depend on how competing events are handled. Competing risk analyses can provide more realistic estimates of expected therapeutic benefit at the point of treatment decisions when competing events are common.

articles.title: Greater Translocator Protein Distribution Volume in Neurocircuitry of Anorexia Nervosa.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory stimuli are associated with onset of anorexia nervosa (AN) but whether inflammation occurs in the brain of AN is unknown. The primary objective is to determine whether [18F]FEPPA total distribution volume ([18F]FEPPA VT), PET index of translocator protein density and inflammatory marker of gliosis, is elevated in AN in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), ventral striatum (VS), dorsal caudate (DC), dorsal putamen (DP), thalamus, orbitofrontal cortex and insula. Secondary objectives are to determine the relationship of [18F]FEPPA VT in ACC to rumination severity and [18F]FEPPA VT to body mass index (BMI).

METHODS: [18F]FEPPA VT was measured in 20 medication free AN participants and 20 healthy controls. Correlations of [18F]FEPPA VT with rumination severity, and BMI, were determined.

RESULTS: [18F]FEPPA VT was elevated in AN in all ROI (linear mixed model (LMM), group effect, P = 4×10-7), particularly ACC, VS, DC and thalamus (mean 52% elevation; LMM, region by group interaction, P = 4×10-4). ACC [18F]FEPPA VT correlated positively with eating concerns (Eating Disorder Examination, r = 0.58, P = .007; Inventory of Depression and Anxiety Symptoms-II, r = 0.66, P = .002). There were no significant correlations between [18F]FEPPA VT and BMI.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater [18F]FEPPA VT is strong evidence for neuroinflammation and gliosis, particularly in ACC, VS, DC and thalamus in AN. Given such, it may be of interest to assess interventions that influence gliosis towards curative roles in future clinical trials in AN.

articles.title: Weight loss at a cost: Semaglutide and PYY3-36 aggravate pre-existing metabolic osteoporosis in female Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Incretin mimetics like semaglutide and peptide YY3-36 (PYY3-36) reduce appetite and body weight, however their individual and combined effects on bone in the setting of metabolic disease and associated osteoporosis (MetOP) lack mechanistic insights. Here, female Wistar rats were randomized to: [1] Healthy control, [2] MetOP-Saline, [3] MetOP-Sema, [4] MetOP-PYY, [5] MetOP-Sema+PYY. Animals in group 2-5 received a "Western diet" in combination with nitric oxide synthase inhibitor L-NAME to induce MetOP as previously described. Randomization to treatments occurred in week 9. After 16 weeks, femora were collected for micro-computed-tomography, histological analysis, RNA-seq, and qPCR. Serum was analyzed for bone turnover markers and steroid profiles (LC-MS/MS). Semaglutide alone and in combination with PYY3-36 significantly reduced body weight. Semaglutide induced a modest reduction in trabecular bone volume fraction (BV/TV), whereas PYY3-36 alone and in combination with semaglutide caused more pronounced trabecular deterioration, with the combination group exhibiting increased trabecular separation. Cortical bone parameters were unaffected. Osteoclast numbers were increased in the semaglutide and PYY3-36 groups. Gene expression analysis demonstrated only mild changes in femora of semaglutide-treated rats, while PYY3-36 treatment significantly upregulated angiogenesis- and extracellular matrix-associated genes. Collectively, these findings suggest that semaglutide modestly impairs bone health. PYY3-36 treatment led to deteriorated bone markers and increased resorption, potentially limiting its clinical application. Semaglutide and PYY3-36 in combination further aggravate bone loss in MetOP. These findings highlight the need to evaluate gut hormone-based weight loss strategies for long-term skeletal safety, especially in the vulnerable setting of pre-existing osteoporosis.

articles.title: The farm effect on asthma and allergies - Thirty years of research.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract: The 'farm effect' describes a strong asthma- and allergy-protective signal by farm exposure, which is surprisingly consistent across the globe. Representing a more traditional lifestyle, the farm environment appears to be a reminiscent of the environmental exposure humankind experienced since the neolithic. The farm environment is characterized by a high microbial load and diversity, which seem essential for adequate immune maturation. The aim of this review article is to delineate how research into the farm effect evolved from classical epidemiology over biomarker research, microbiome sequencing, and multi-omics analyses to emerging prevention strategies. We explore how the farm effect and the various versions of the hygiene hypothesis are closely intertwined with each simultaneously contributing the development of the other. We follow the development of our understanding of the mechanisms underpinning the farm effect, focusing on the two most consistent exposures, namely microbial exposure in animal sheds and consumption of unprocessed cow's milk. The decades of research into the farm effect represent true translational work: Moving from observation to intervention, with the advent of new therapeutic interventions on the horizon, now is the time to look back at how it all started, how our understanding has evolved over time and what this might mean for the future.

articles.title: Translocation of the environmental bacterium Aquitalea magnusonii promotes systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Impaired mucosal barrier integrity facilitates translocation of the gut microbiome into the circulation and the liver, thereby exacerbating the severity of chronic liver diseases (CLD). This study aimed to investigate the pathogenic role of non-commensal environmental bacteria, specifically Aquitalea magnusonii in CLD progression by assessing its ability to cross the intestinal barrier and induce systemic inflammation and liver fibrosis.

METHODS: Using an integrated translational framework, patient blood analyses were combined with multi-omics profiling, human intestinal epithelial models, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), hepatic stellate cells (HSC), monocytes, and alcoholic (ALD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated (MASLD) models to evaluate the translocation, virulence, inflammatory and fibrotic potential of A. magnusonii in CLD.

RESULTS: Non-commensal environmental bacteria, including Aquitalea spp. were detected in multiple organs in both ALD and MASLD models. Detection of Aquitalea DNA in patient samples and other non-commensal environmental bacteria in tap water suggested potential aquatic reservoirs. A. magnusonii produced 12 acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) associated metabolites and its outer membrane vesicles (OMV) were enriched in virulence-related proteins, supporting roles in adhesion, invasion, and immune activation. In addition, gavage with A. magnusonii led to a substantial dysbiotic shift in the gut microbiome. Mechanistically, the cell-free supernatant of A. magnusonii culture activated TLR2- and TLR4-dependent pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. Exposure to A. magnusonii or its pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) significantly increased inflammation and fibrosis in vitro and in vivo.

CONCLUSION: Non-commensal environmental bacteria, in the example of A. magnusonii, can translocate across the intestinal barrier and promote liver inflammation and fibrogenesis via metabolite production, virulence-associated OMV, and innate immune activation.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: This study highlights an underrecognized role of non-commensal environmental bacteria in chronic liver disease. Beyond gut commensals, detection of non-commensal environmental microbes such as Aquitalea was associated with markers of more advanced liver disease, while experimental studies of A. magnusonii support biological plausibility for a potential contributory role. These findings highlight the importance of considering environmental reservoirs and non-commensal pathogens in microbial contributions to CLD pathogenesis.

articles.title: Radiographic Bone Gain After Guided Bone Regeneration With a Porcine Cortical Membrane: A Retrospective Case Series.
articles.journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Guided bone regeneration (GBR) is used to reconstruct alveolar defects before implant placement. Resorbable membranes provide limited space-maintaining rigidity, whereas non-resorbable devices are more rigid but may require removal and carry exposure risks. This retrospective case series describes GBR outcomes using a resorbable porcine cortical membrane in Cawood and Howell Class IV-VI defects.

METHODS: Sixteen GBR procedures were performed in 13 patients. Site-level horizontal and vertical bone gain were measured by superimposition of pre-operative and six-month CBCT datasets; measurement agreement was assessed with Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Complications, augmentation success, one-year implant survival and marginal bone loss were recorded.

RESULTS: Among 15 evaluable sites, mean horizontal and vertical gains were 4.33 ± 1.55 mm (95% CI 3.47-5.19) and 4.11 ± 1.99 mm (95% CI 3.01-5.22), with the failed site imputed as zero (16 sites), 4.06 ± 1.84 and 3.85 ± 2.18 mm. CCCs were 0.994-0.998. One site failed after infection (augmentation success 15/16); membrane exposure occurred at 2/16 sites and refractory pain in 4/13 patients. All 27 implants placed in the 15 augmented sites were in function at one year; mean marginal bone loss was 0.41 mm.

DISCUSSION: In this small uncontrolled series, GBR using a porcine cortical membrane with a mixed autogenous/bovine particulate graft was associated with approximately 4 mm horizontal and vertical bone gain. Because the procedure combines several components and seven sites overlap a previous report, these findings extend preliminary evidence and do not establish membrane-specific efficacy. Prospective comparative studies are required.

articles.title: Changes in Ventilation Associated with Worsening Heart Failure in Ambulatory Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breathlessness is a cardinal symptom of heart failure (HF) and reflects abnormal ventilation, particularly during exercise. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing provides only a snapshot of ventilatory physiology and cannot capture longitudinal changes associated with deterioration. Continuous physiologic monitoring from implantable devices offers an opportunity to characterize ventilatory trends preceding HF events in ambulatory patients.

METHODS: The MultiSENSE study followed 900 patients with a cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator (CRT-D) modified to record high fidelity physiologic data. Ventilatory variables derived from thoracic impedance were examined before adjudicated HF events (hospitalization for HF or outpatient visit requiring IV diuretics) and between clinic visits associated with worsening dyspnea. Variables included respiratory rate (RR), tidal volume (TV), minute ventilation (MV) and Rapid Shallow Breathing Index (RSBI; RR/TV). Patient activity was assessed using a device-embedded accelerometer.

RESULTS: A total of 130 HF events from 92 patients were analyzed. In the 3 days preceding HF events, mean daily RR increased (adjusted mean change: 0.59 [95% CI: 0.31, 0.86], relative change: 3.56%, p<0.0001) and mean daily TV decreased (-0.07 [-0.10, -0.04], -7.4%, p<0.0001), resulting in a significant increase in RSBI (2.34 [1.56, 3.12], 10.5%, p<0.0001). Daily MV decreased (-0.72 [-1.2, -.23], -4.4%, p=0.0042), largely reflecting reduced activity. When accounting only for resting periods, a similar increase in RSBI was observed in the 3 days preceding HF events (1.98 [1.10, 2.86], 7.32%, p<0.0001) relative to baseline, whereas MV showed no significant change. In patients with worsening dyspnea between clinic visits, mean daily RR and RSBI increased significantly without a significant change in TV or MV.

CONCLUSIONS: Worsening HF in ambulatory patients is characterized by a shift toward rapid shallow breathing. RSBI significantly increased prior to HF events and with worsening dyspnea.. These findings suggest that RSBI may be a sensitive marker for worsening HF and may provide clinically relevant insight for monitoring ambulatory patients.

articles.title: Establishing a passive registry of patients with heart failure enabled by natural language processing and language models.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Significant budgetary and resource requirements for data collection remain a barrier to launch and maintain disease registries. Automated data collection from electronic health records (EHRs) is a possible solution, but certain data elements critical for research endeavors in heart failure (HF) are not routinely available as structured data fields.

METHODS: Using EHRs from a large tertiary care system in Boston, we address this challenge by using natural language processing (NLP) and language models. First, patients with HF were identified using diagnosis codes and NLP of physician notes. Among the patients included, ejection fraction (EF) and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class were extracted using rule-based NLP. Large language models were used to extract social determinants of health (SDoH). EHRs were deterministically linked to insurance claims data from Medicare and Medicaid and state vital statistics files for a comprehensive view of healthcare receipt and outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 69,007 patients with HF were included, among whom mean age was 75.8 years (SD, 12.8) and 51.5% were female. 38,620 patients (56.0%) were classified into HF with reduced, mildly reduced, or preserved EF with average EF of 30.8% (SD, 7.0), 45.0% (SD, 1.7), and 61.9% (SD, 7.3), respectively. 215,627 valid NYHA class mentions were extracted for 16,147 patients (23.4%) and 67,432 patients (97.7%) had some element of social history recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: The infrastructure and processes we developed can facilitate a diverse portfolio of future research activities aimed at characterizing and improving outcomes of patients with HF.

articles.title: Two-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes After Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in Severe Mitral Annular Calcification.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The SUMMIT-MAC trial is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the Tendyne Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement (TMVR) system in patients with severe mitral annular calcification (MAC). Primary outcomes demonstrated significant improvements in mitral regurgitation severity, heart failure symptoms, and quality-of-life; leading to FDA approval of Tendyne. Intermediate term TMVR outcomes have not been reported.

METHODS: The SUMMIT-MAC cohort (NCT03433274) enrolled high surgical-risk patients with severe MAC (average volume 5,679 ± 5,670; range 741 to 37,437 mm3) and significant mitral valve dysfunction. Independent assessments of mitral disease were performed at an echocardiography core laboratory and adverse events were adjudicated by a clinical events committee. Two-year follow-up visits were achieved in 95% of available patients, with an average follow-up of 18.7 months.

RESULTS: The cohort included 103 patients from 37 sites. Mean age was 78.0±6.5 years, 55% were women, 74% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mitral regurgitation was present in nearly all patients at baseline (97% grade >2+). At 2 years all-cause mortality was 32.3% (32 patients) and cardiovascular mortality was 23.6% (23 patients). 97% (56/58) of patients with available echocardiograms at 2 years had ≤1+ mitral regurgitation. Additionally, at 2 years, 84% of patients were in NYHA functional class I/II and quality-of-life improved significantly (KCCQ-OS, Δ24.2±19.6 points; p<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: In a high-risk cohort of patients with mitral valve disease and severe MAC, Tendyne TMVR had acceptable sustained clinical outcomes and quality-of-life over 2 years. The reduction of mitral regurgitation severity was sustained through 2-years post TMVR.

articles.title: Mitral Valve Repair Failure: Mechanisms, Re-repair Feasibility, and Outcomes of Reintervention. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve repair is the preferred treatment for degenerative mitral regurgitation whenever feasible and durable. Amid the increasing volume of mitral repairs, mitral valve repair failure has emerged as an increasingly recognized clinical entity in contemporary mitral surgery.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted to identify studies reporting intraoperative or interval/postoperatively detected mitral valve repair failure. Evidence synthesis included a systematic summary and analysis of incidence, failure modes, factors favoring re-repair, re-repair techniques and intervention-specific outcomes.

RESULTS: Intraoperative mitral valve repair failure was reported across nine unique studies totaling 18,429 patients undergoing initial mitral valve repair, of whom 580 (3.1%) experienced intraoperative failure requiring re-cross-clamping. Re-repair was the primary management strategy in intraoperative failure, with a pooled re-repair rate of 82%. Interval mitral valve repair failure was analyzed from 12 studies including 1,363 patients, occurring at a mean of 6 years following the index repair. Disease progression was the most frequent mechanism of interval failure (44%), followed by technical failure (35%) and new disease (17%). In interval failure, valve replacement remained the most employed strategy, while re-repair was performed in 35% of patients. Re-repair was associated with significantly superior long-term survival (78.3% vs. 58.3%; HR 2.44, 95% CI [1.79-3.33], p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Mitral valve re-repair is a safe and feasible option in selected patients with degenerative mitral valve repair failure and is associated with improved long-term survival. Early technical failures and localized, non-calcified defects with preserved leaflet tissue are most likely to benefit from re-repair.

articles.title: Successful Implementation of Standardized Longitudinal Follow-up after Surgery for Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To understand and improve long-term congenital heart surgery outcomes, longitudinal data are essential but challenging to capture. We evaluated a novel program to facilitate routine longitudinal data collection.

METHODS: Patients undergoing Society of Thoracic Surgeons Benchmark Operations at two centers (2007-2019) were included. Annual follow-up data (vital status and age-specific burden of disease questionnaires) were collected using an automated email system along with medical record and local registry data queries, with coordinator follow-up if needed. Completeness of follow-up and associated factors were analyzed in multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 4,075 subjects, vital status was captured for 98% (median follow-up 6.0 years; IQR 3.1-9.2). Vital status at one year was known for 95%; overall follow-up completeness (observed-to-potential follow-up time) was 81%. At least one follow-up questionnaire was completed by 85%, with 58% utilizing the automated email system. Those with genetic/non-cardiac abnormalities (OR 2.28, 95%CI 1.28-4.28), single ventricle palliation (Norwood OR 11.2, 95%CI 3.01-72.7; Glenn/hemi-Fontan OR 7.79, 95%CI 2.21-49.5), and tetralogy of Fallot repair (OR 2.43, 95%CI 1.11-5.59) had higher odds of known vital status. Follow-up questionnaire completion had higher odds for non-Hispanic white patients (OR 1.54, 95%CI: 1.27-1.86) and higher median income households (OR 1.05/$10,000, 95%CI: 1.01-1.09).

CONCLUSIONS: This program captured vital status and burden of disease, with one-year survival determined for nearly all patients. Automation reduced human resource needs by more than half. Future efforts will focus on expanding to other centers and improving follow-up for disadvantaged groups.

articles.title: Impaired Left Atrial Contractile Strain and Late Pacemaker Implantation After the Cox-Maze Procedure Despite Maintained Sinus Rhythm.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late bradyarrhythmia requiring permanent pacemaker implantation remains a challenge after the Cox-Maze procedure. We evaluated whether left atrial contractile strain at 1 year predicts late pacemaker implantation in patients with normal sinus rhythm.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 259 patients who underwent the Maze procedure between 2012 and 2024 and maintained normal sinus rhythm at 1 year. Left atrial contractile strain was assessed using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography.

RESULTS: Of 329 patients screened, 50 were excluded for atrial fibrillation recurrence at 1 year (1-year freedom from atrial fibrillation, 83.8%). During follow-up (median 58 months), 22 patients required pacemaker implantation. The optimal strain cutoff was -1.8% (area under the curve 0.658), and patients with impaired left atrial function (strain ≥ -1.8%) had a higher incidence of pacemaker implantation (log-rank P < 0.001). Impaired left atrial contractile strain (hazard ratio 3.99; 95% confidence interval, 1.41-11.35), fine fibrillatory waves (3.64; 1.32-10.01), and increased preoperative left atrial volume (1.004 per mL; 1.001-1.008) were independent predictors, and a combined model improved predictive accuracy (area under the curve 0.782). The excess risk was concentrated within the first 5 years after surgery (hazard ratio 8.47 versus 2.22 thereafter).

CONCLUSIONS: Impaired left atrial contractile strain 1 year after the Cox-Maze procedure independently predicts late pacemaker implantation despite stable normal sinus rhythm, particularly within the first 5 years, highlighting a dissociation between electrical and functional recovery. It may serve as a surrogate for atrial fibrosis and latent conduction disturbance, warranting intensified surveillance in high-risk patients during this period.

articles.title: Fight or Flight: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Diagnosis and Management of Mediastinal Paragangliomas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors, leading to potentially invasive clinical investigation and inadequate staging. Functional secretory activity, high germline mutation rates, multifocal disease burden, and proximity to the great vessels demand a multidisciplinary approach. We describe our longitudinal multidisciplinary experience building a center of excellence model.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of 19 patients with mediastinal paraganglioma managed at a quaternary referral center, capturing demographics, imaging, preoperative testing, operative details, and perioperative outcomes.

RESULTS: There were 14 (73.7%) females with a median age of 46.3 years (IQR 38.5-57.6 years). Sixteen (84%) of 19 patients were referred from outside centers; 9 (47.3%) underwent biopsy before referral, with three (15.8%) experiencing catecholamine crisis, pneumothorax, or hemorrhage. Nine (47.4%) tumors were adjacent to the aorta, and seven (42.1%) adjacent to the pulmonary artery, with vascular involvement in 17(89.5%) of the 19 patients. Thirteen (68%) were functional and five (26.3%) had multifocal disease. Succinate dehydrogenase mutations were found in 63.6% of patients tested. Cardiopulmonary bypass was required in 63.2%, with zero 30-day mortality. Postoperative complications occurred in 47.4%, predominantly atrial arrhythmia. Median hospital stay was four days. Four patients developed local recurrence at a median recurrence-free survival of 16.9 months, all with positive margins or multifocal disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Mediastinal paragangliomas can be safely resected within a multidisciplinary center of excellence. Early recognition, avoidance of uninformed biopsy, functional staging, preoperative alpha blockade, and tumor profiling and genetic evaluation with genetic counseling are essential components.

articles.title: Two Decades of Single Ventricle Palliation: Survival Improvement and the Persistent Burden of Fontan Morbidity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-level data on long-term outcomes after single ventricle staged palliation in East Asian cohorts are lacking. We examined era-specific trends in survival, Fontan completion, and morbidity in a Korean nationwide cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data (2002-2023). Patients undergoing Stage I palliation were stratified into four calendar-period eras and followed through December 2023. Survival and morbidity were assessed by Cox regression; Fontan completion was analyzed by Fine-Gray competing risk methods and at fixed post-palliation horizons.

RESULTS: Among 1,732 patients (median follow-up 20.0-199.9 months), adjusted mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.54 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.69) and 0.35 (95% CI, 0.26-0.48) in eras 3 and 4 versus era 1 (both P<.001), with the largest gains in hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Fontan completion did not differ across eras; at 36 months, cumulative incidence was 17.3%-19.4% (P=.80). Heart failure (HR, 2.12), thromboembolism (HR, 2.37), and reintervention hazards rose in era 4, whereas arrhythmia declined (HR, 0.26). Female sex, preterm birth, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome independently predicted mortality, as did socioeconomic position below the highest stratum in a categorical specification.

CONCLUSIONS: Over two decades, survival after single ventricle palliation improved substantially in Korea, most strikingly in hypoplastic left heart syndrome, whereas Fontan attainment did not improve at a common horizon. The rise in heart failure and thromboembolism, together with higher mortality below the highest socioeconomic stratum, identifies a growing population requiring lifelong surveillance and targeted support.

articles.title: Using an Artificial Intelligence ECG-Derived Biological Age for Risk Stratification of Patients Undergoing Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence using a convolutional neural network can estimate patients' age from ECG data. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of AI ECG-derived age in predicting outcomes following surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).

METHODS: Preoperative ECGs obtained within 30 days before surgery were used to calculate AI ECG-derived age in 5,503 patients undergoing SAVR. Age gap was defined as AI ECG-derived age minus chronological age. Associations between age gap and postoperative outcomes were evaluated. A threshold of age gap >5 years was used to define advanced ECG age.

RESULTS: Median chronological age was 73.2(65.3-79.5) years, and AI ECG-derived age was 70.4(64.6-74.8) years. Median age gap was -3.0(-8.4 to 2.5) years. In 35.7% of patients, AI ECG-derived age exceeded chronological age, and in 16.7% it was >5 years. Patients with advanced ECG age were younger but had higher rates of diabetes, renal failure, and current smoking and had higher BMI. Postoperatively, advanced ECG age was associated with increased risk of 30-day mortality (OR 1.69, p=0.043), blood transfusion (OR 1.44, p<0.001), gastrointestinal complications (OR 1.83, p=0.022), prolonged ventilation (OR 1.41, p=0.047), higher postoperative creatinine levels (B +0.09 mg/dL, p=0.014), longer ICU stay (B +13.3 hours, p=0.001), and longer hospital stay (B +0.7 days, p=0.007). Advanced ECG age was also independently associated with increased long-term mortality (HR 1.25, p=0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: AI ECG-derived age identifies a subgroup of SAVR patients with advanced physiological aging. An elevated age gap is independently associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and reduced long-term survival following SAVR.

articles.title: Breaking through the subjective barrier for acute hepatic encephalopathy grading in clinical trials.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

articles.title: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. stem extract attenuates cigarette smoke-induced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in mice by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. (COT) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its root, stem, and leaf being used for medicinal purposes. COT characterized by the efficacy of dispelling wind-dampness, invigorating blood, and relieving pain, traditional records in Quanzhou Bencao document the use for asthma, indicating that its traditional treatment in lung system disorders. Previous pharmacological studies have demonstrated that the COT stem (COTS) exhibits anti-inflammatory and protective effects in experimental models related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the systemically efficacy and molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-COPD effects of COTS remain poorly understood.

AIM OF THE STUDY: The purpose of this study is to systematically investigate the therapeutic efficacy of the extract of COTS (ECOTS) against COPD in mice through metabolomics and serum pharmacochemistry combined with network pharmacology, thereby providing experimental evidence for elucidating the underlying mechanisms through which ECOTS exerts its therapeutic effects on COPD.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD-like mouse model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects of ECOTS. The potential biomarkers were identified by metabolomics. The blood-entering components were profiled by serum pharmacochemistry. The primary targets and signaling pathways of ECOTS were predicted through network pharmacology analysis. These predictions were further validated using immunohistochemical, immunofluorescence, and Western blot.

RESULTS: ECOTS significantly suppressed inflammation and mitigated lung tissue damage in CS-induced mice. Network pharmacology screening and verification experiments revealed that the protective effects of ECOTS may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling in vivo and in vitro. Furthermore, the PI3K agonist 740 Y-P apparently impaired the effects of ECOTS in CS extract (CSE)-exposed BEAS-2B cells.

CONCLUSION: ECOTS attenuates CS-induced COPD-like pathological changes in mice, and these protective effects may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling. This study extends previous evidence for the anti-COPD activity of the COTS and provides a potential mechanistic and pharmacological basis for its further investigation in COPD.

articles.title: Miao medicine Xinlikang capsule attenuates acute erythroleukemia through immune regulation and FLI1-PI3K axis-mediated cell cycle arrest.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Acute erythroleukemia (AEL) is an aggressive subtype of acute myeloid leukemia characterized by impaired erythroid differentiation, uncontrolled expansion of erythroid progenitors, and immune dysfunction. Owing to its poor prognosis and lack of specific therapeutic options, effective alternative strategies are urgently needed. Xinlikang capsules (XLK), a Miao medicine formula approved in China, have been clinically used as an adjuvant therapy for malignant tumors. However, its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms in AEL remain unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the anti-AEL effects of XLK and clarify its pharmacodynamic material basis and molecular mechanisms.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An AEL mouse model was established by F-MuLV infection and treated with XLK for 5 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed by serum biochemical indicators, organ indices, histopathological examination, immune cell profiling, erythroid differentiation markers, and survival analysis. The chemical compositions of XLK and XLK-containing serum (XLKs) were identified by UPLC-MS/MS. The anti-proliferative effects of XLKs and its absorbed constituents were evaluated in HEL cells using MTT assays and flow cytometry. Network pharmacology, RNA-seq, Western blotting, and Fli1 shRNA knockdown were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. This integrated approach evaluates in vivo therapeutic efficacy, defines the pharmacodynamic material basis, and dissects the molecular mechanism, providing a multi-layered analytical framework for understanding the anti-AEL effects of XLK.

RESULTS: XLK markedly reduced splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, improved spleen and liver histopathological damage, normalized serum ALT and AST levels, and prolonged the survival of F-MuLV-induced AEL mice (p<0.001). XLK promoted erythroid maturation by increasing mature erythroid cells and reducing erythroid precursor accumulation. It also restored immune homeostasis, as evidenced by increased CD3+ T cells (by 50%), CD11b+ cells (by 10%), and B220+ B cells (by 46%), together with a normalized CD4+/CD8a+ ratio in the spleen. UPLC-MS/MS identified nine absorbed constituents in XLKs, among which tomentic acid, tanshinone IIA, cryptotanshinone, and apigenin exhibited notable inhibitory effects on HEL cell proliferation. XLKs suppressed HEL cell proliferation (27.69% inhibition at 72 h with 20% XLKs) and induced S-phase arrest in a time- and concentration-dependent manner. Network pharmacology and RNA-seq analyses indicated that the PI3K signaling pathway and cell cycle regulation were key pathways involved in the anti-AEL effects of XLK. Mechanistically, XLKs downregulated FLI1 and inhibited PI3K pathway activation in HEL cells, accompanied by decreased CDK2 and Cyclin B1 expression and increased Cyclin A2 (1.9-fold) and p-CDC25C (1.7-fold) expression. Furthermore, Fli1 knockdown reduced p-PI3K and attenuated the anti-proliferative effect of XLKs (8.51% reduction at 72 h), supporting a key role of FLI1-mediated PI3K signaling in XLK-induced cell cycle arrest. Among the absorbed constituents, cryptotanshinone recapitulated the downregulation of FLI1, p-PI3K, and p-mTOR, supporting its role in XLK-induced cell cycle arrest.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that XLK exerts therapeutic effects in F-MuLV-induced AEL. Mechanistically, XLK alleviated spleen and liver injury, promoted erythroid differentiation, restored immune homeostasis, and suppressed erythroleukemia cell proliferation by inducing cell-cycle arrest through modulation of the FLI1-PI3K signaling pathway, thereby exerting a therapeutic effect on AEL.

articles.title: IGF2 polymorphisms and leukocyte mRNA expression: Implications for ischemic stroke risk and prognosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2) is implicated in ischemic stroke (IS) pathogenesis. This study investigated the association of IGF2 genetic variants and leukocyte mRNA expression with IS susceptibility and post-stroke prognosis.

METHODS: Three IGF2 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs; rs3741211, rs10770125, and rs2585) were genotyped using TaqMan assays in a case-control study (2,497 IS cases and 3,135 controls), a community-based cohort (4,080 S-free subjects), and a hospital-based cohort (2,298 IS patients). Leukocyte IGF2 mRNA expression was quantified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in 318 IS cases and 315 controls.

RESULTS: In the case-control study, rs3741211 (unadjusted dominant: odds ratio [OR] = 1.130, P = 0.024) and rs2585 (adjusted additive: OR = 1.087, P = 0.047) were associated with increased IS risk. However, neither variant independently predicted incident IS in the prospective cohort (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 0.837 for rs3741211 and 0.876). IS patients had significantly lower IGF2 mRNA expression than controls (fold change [FC]: 0.740, P = 0.001), displaying a non-linear relationship with IS risk (P < 0.05). Additionally, rs3741211, rs10770125, and rs2585 were associated with IGF2 mRNA expression levels (P < 0.05). IGF2 mRNA levels negatively correlated with National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) and Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores post-discharge (P < 0.05). In the hospital-based cohort, rs3741211 AG/GG carriers had lower stroke-related mortality than AA carriers under the dominant model (adjusted HR = 0.744, 95 % confidence interval [CI]: 0.559-0.990), whereas rs10770125 GG carriers had higher hemorrhagic stroke mortality than AA/AG carriers under the recessive model (adjusted HR = 2.035, 95 % CI: 1.038-3.990).

CONCLUSION: The genetic associations with IS observed in the case-control study were not confirmed in the prospective community-based cohort. Leukocyte IGF2 mRNA expression was associated with IS status and post-stroke neurological and functional outcomes. These findings are preliminary and require independent validation.

articles.title: Lipid metabolism and pediatric tuberculous meningitis: Revealing mechanisms and new directions for diagnosis and treatment.
articles.abstract: Pediatric tuberculous meningitis (TBM), a fatal Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, causes severe neurological damage. Current diagnostics (clinical signs, CSF analysis, imaging) are often delayed or inaccurate. Emerging evidence links lipid metabolism dysregulation to TBM pathogenesis, though mechanisms remain unclear. (1) Firstly, we exploratorily performed RNA sequencing on peripheral blood from 3 pediatric TBM patients with 7 healthy control data obtained from a public GEO dataset (GSE159337) to identify 7,595 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). 3,763 upregulated genes enriched metabolic pathways, endocytosis, and MAPK signaling, while 3,832 downregulated genes linked to TGF-β signaling. Gene ontology emphasized immune responses, particularly neutrophil activation. Protein-protein interaction networks identified 41 hub genes, including CD274, TGFB1, and MMP9, with TGFB1, JUN, CD274, and MMP9 showing strong lipid metabolism correlations, suggesting a lipid-TBM risk nexus. (2) Furthermore, we validated four of these hub genes (FCGR3B, SPI1, ITGAX, MMP9) in an independent publicly available pediatric TBM study of high quality (GEO GSE111459) via ROC curve and logistic regression analysis. (3) Finally, the expression of these four hub genes were measured by qRT-PCR in an expanded set of clinical samples (13 additional TBM patients vs 12 healthy controls), confirming significantly elevated MMP9 and FCGR3B in TBM (P<0.01). This study suggests that lipid metabolism plays a role in the pathogenesis of pediatric TBM, proposing hub genes and pathways that could serve as potential supporting targets for diagnostics and therapies.

articles.title: NS5B mutations in bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) prevent the elimination of BVDV from a persistently contaminated bovine macrophage cell line treated with DB772.
articles.abstract: A widely used transformed bovine peritoneal macrophage cell line (BoMac) is known to be contaminated with bovine viral diarrhea virus of the 2a sub-genotype (BVDV2a). Studies have asserted that the culture and serial passage of BoMac cells in the presence of the antiviral compound 2-(2-benzimidazolyl)-5-[4-(2-imidazolino)phenyl]furan dihydrochloride (DB772) is sufficient to clean the cell line of the persistent contaminating infection. Here, we report that a mutation of P262A/H in the NS5B/RNA-dependent RNA polymerase region of the BVDV2a viral genome occurs when persistently infected BoMac cells were treated with DB772 in vitro and escapes the generation of a BVDV-free clean cell culture stock. Mutations at this locus have been previously reported to confer resistance against DB772 in vivo. 3D-biomolecular complex prediction of wildtype and mutant NS5B in complex with DB772 suggests that the P262A and P262H mutations generate structural changes that interfere with DB772 from accessing its binding site. These mutations lead to increased BVDV proliferation when DB722 treatment is stopped.

articles.title: Beyond glycemic index: Mixed meal postprandial glycemic response as a promising approach for Personalized Nutrition in Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Devising an effective tool for management of diet for patients with diabetes for a proper glycemic control has always been challenging due to the variability in available macronutrient content and composition of the meals along with the different factors affecting it. Traditionally, the concepts like glycemic index (GI) of food items, carbohydrate counting using the carbohydrate exchange lists have been largely guiding their food choices. These instruments, though useful, face certain paramount limitations that is, they are not mixed meal- based, intake responsive and sensitive to variations in the meal-composition, all of which is typical of different diets. The present perspective critically evaluates these and other associated issues considering supportive evidence available in this regard focusing on why mixed meal based glycemic responses are more pertinent for advising patients with diabetes. We also propose the need for developing a mixed meal- macronutrient exchange lists based on available macronutrients for patients with diabetes precisely characterizing the PPGR (post-prandial glycemic response) to different combination mixed meals in traditional diets. Furthermore, we suggest that the traditionally consumed mixed meals should be tested in different populations using continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) as an advance tool addressing the variability and possible combinations in traditional diets to obtain PPGR data sets. These then can be used for advising medical nutrition therapy for patients with diabetes recommending them with different traditional mixed meal combinations of their choice that keep their blood glucose in control.

articles.title: Optimising posaconazole dosing in paediatric patients: a population pharmacokinetic modelling and simulation study.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Posaconazole is approved for prophylaxis and treatment of invasive fungal infections in paediatric patients, but data for optimal formulation-specific dosing across the paediatric weight range remains scant. We pooled individual-level pharmacokinetic data to identify dosing regimens that optimise the probability of achieving predefined efficacy and safety targets.

METHODS: Individual concentration-time data from paediatric patients receiving posaconazole as oral suspension, delayed-release tablet, or intravenous infusion were pooled. A population pharmacokinetics model was developed using nonlinear mixed-effects modelling in NONMEM. Stochastic simulations were performed in virtual cohorts across body weights of 5-50 kg, evaluating multiple dosing regimens. Efficacy and safety were assessed as the probability of attaining a trough concentration >1 mg/L (Pefficacy) and ≤4 mg/L (Psafety), respectively.

RESULTS: Data from seven published studies comprising 309 paediatric patients (1050 serum concentrations) were aggregated. A one-compartment model with nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination best described the data. Suspension bioavailability decreased with increasing dose, and was further reduced by proton pump inhibitor use (-41.1%, 9.5% relative standard error, RSE) and diarrhoea (-29.5%, 21.4% RSE). Tablet bioavailability was estimated at 43.0% (10.4% RSE). For the oral suspension, neither 200 mg nor 400 mg four times daily achieved Pefficacy ≥90% across weight bands. For intravenous and delayed-release tablet formulations, no regimen simultaneously achieved ≥90% Pefficacy and Psafety at steady state. For these two formulations, a loading dose of 12-15 mg/kg twice daily followed by 12-15 mg/kg once daily provided the most favourable balance between early efficacy and safety on day 2.

CONCLUSIONS: The original oral suspension showed consistently low target attainment and is suboptimal in paediatric patients. For the intravenous and delayed-release tablet, a loading dose of 12-15 mg/kg twice daily followed by 12-15 mg/kg once daily is recommended as a starting regimen, with subsequent dose individualisation through model-informed precision dosing guided by therapeutic drug monitoring.

articles.title: Inhaled corticosteroids adherence and remission in severe asthma under biological therapy.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice

articles.title: Maternal and Early-life Predictors of Asthma/Wheeze at 12 Months: Findings from the Environments for Healthy Living Birth Cohort.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic childhood condition, with Australian children having the highest prevalence rates globally.

OBJECTIVE: Investigate the association between maternal factors during the perinatal period, early-life factors and asthma/wheeze diagnosis in children at 12 months of age.

METHODS: Data were obtained from 2,166 mother-child dyads enrolled in the EFHL longitudinal birth cohort (2007 -2011) across south-east Queensland and northern New South Wales, Australia. Maternal demographic, socioeconomic, health and lifestyle factors during the perinatal period and early-life factors, including infant chest infection and older siblings were correlated to childhood asthma/wheeze at 12 months. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted in R statistical software. Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations was used to account for missing data, with pooled estimates generated across 30 imputed datasets.

RESULTS: Pre-regression analyses identified associations between childhood asthma/wheeze and maternal education, maternal smoking during pregnancy, recreational substance exposure, infant chest infection and the presence of older siblings in the household. Following adjustment, the modifiable factors of infant chest infection (AOR 3.94, 95% CI 2.90-5.36), maternal asthma (AOR 2.58, 95% CI 1.58-4.20), maternal smoking during pregnancy (AOR 2.11, 95% CI 1.48-3.01), and difficult to modify factors of maternal education at secondary/trade level (AOR 2.22, 95% CI 1.39-3.53) and older siblings in the household (AOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.17-2.24) remained independent predictors (all False Discovery Rate p≤0.01).

CONCLUSION: Perinatal and early-life environmental factors were independently associated with wheeze/asthma at 12 months. Thus, targeting modifiable maternal and early-life factors may help reduce the burden of childhood asthma.

articles.title: Intraductal Infusion of Acetic Acid and Lipopolysaccharide Recapitulates Key Pathological Features of Biliary Atresia in Mice.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Recent evidence suggests that biliary atresia (BA) may represent a final common pathological outcome arising from multiple etiologic insults. This study investigated whether intraductal infusion of proinflammatory agents, without viral infection, could reproduce key features of BA.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Common bile duct infusion of 10% acetic acid and 1.5 μg/μl lipopolysaccharide (LPS) was performed through the ampulla of Vater, with catheter placement distal to the bifurcation of the common bile duct and cystic duct. Mice were evaluated at 1, 4, and 8 weeks post-infusion with biochemical, histological, and immunohistochemical analyses.

RESULTS: This procedure resulted in progressive common bile duct obstruction associated with cholestatic liver injury. Serum liver enzyme levels were significantly elevated compared with controls, consistent with hepatobiliary injury. Immunohistochemical analysis showed a significant increase in Ki-67-positive cells within the bile duct epithelium, indicating sustained bile duct proliferation. Histological examination revealed progressive hepatic fibrosis (Ishak scores 2-3), with occasional portal-to-portal bridging at 8 weeks post-infusion. Quantitative RT-PCR analysis demonstrated significant upregulation of 14 out of 15 liver genes previously reported to be associated with human BA. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed a significant increase in CD3+, CD4+, and CD8+ T lymphocytes, as well as CD68+ macrophages.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that direct intraductal delivery of nonviral proinflammatory compounds recapitulates selected pathological features observed in human BA. These findings suggest that distinct etiologic insults may lead to overlapping pathological features and may provide a complementary experimental platform for investigating pathological processes relevant to BA.

articles.title: Optimizing 3D-printed Scaffold Geometry Decreases Foreign Body Responses and Enhances Allogeneic Islet Transplant Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Cellular therapy, such as beta cell transplantation for Type 1 diabetes, is a promising approach to durably alleviate disease states. Implanting cells within porous scaffolds helps distribute cells and mechanically support implantation; however, these foreign materials can exacerbate foreign body responses (FBR). While scaffold geometry affects FBR, degradable polymers and conventional scaffold fabrication methods limit control over these parameters, yielding unpredictable geometries. Here, we combined 3D printing with the polymer polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) to produce biostable scaffolds with highly reproducible, controllable geometric scales. We then sought to reduce FBR within these scaffolds by optimizing geometric features, with a specific interest in the impact of rung size, or the delta between pores. Biocompatibility screening in a mouse model found a strong positive correlation between pore-to-pore distance and intra-device fibrosis. Spatio-proteomic analysis of explants revealed that fibrotic regions exhibited elevated levels of fibrotic proteins and increased numbers of macrophages and effector T cells, implicating contributions from both innate and adaptive immune cells. We then evaluated the 3D PDMS prototype with the lowest FBR in syngeneic and allogeneic rat islet transplant models and compared it with a conventionally fabricated PDMS scaffold with variable geometric features. While we observed no differences in syngeneic grafts, allogeneic recipients of our improved 3D-printed implants showed improved functional efficacy and lower rejection rates than those receiving conventional scaffolds. Collagen deposition was also significantly higher in conventional scaffolds, suggesting fibrosis contributed to rejection. This study shows that precise, optimized geometric scaffold features critically influence FBR in biomaterial implants and that FBR changes can accelerate or mitigate adaptive immune cell infiltration, resulting in rejection even under immunosuppression. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Porous scaffolds are widely used in tissue engineering; however, it is known that their geometric features can elicit foreign body responses (FBRs) that are detrimental to implant efficacy. To clearly interrogate the impact of geometric parameters on FBR, we combined a biostable polymer with 3D printing. Biocompatibility studies found that wider gaps between pores led to greater scar tissue, driven by both innate and adaptive immune cells. When an optimized scaffold was used to house islets within diabetic rats, it worked faster and was rejected less often than a conventionally made scaffold. These results show that carefully designed scaffold geometry can reduce immune activation and FBR, thereby improving the success of cell-based treatments.

articles.title: Overcoming the pulmonary mucus barrier in inhaled drug delivery: A disease-driven precision nanomedicine framework.
articles.abstract: The pulmonary mucus barrier is the principal bottleneck in inhaled nanomedicine, intercepting most deposited particles before they reach the epithelium. Because this barrier is remodeled differently in each disease, technology-centric carrier design has repeatedly stalled in clinical translation. This review advances a disease-adapted design framework that positions mucus barrier phenotyping as the foundation of rational formulation design. We first dissect the mucus biophysics of cystic fibrosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and lung cancer, and distill quantitative barrier parameters including mesh pore size, solids content, viscoelasticity, and mucin composition. On this basis, we critically evaluate four strategy classes spanning surface chemistry, carrier platforms, physical parameter optimization, and mucolytic or mucin-suppressive adjuvants, and map each class to the disease phenotypes it best fits through quantitative design windows. We then appraise a tiered evaluation hierarchy from artificial mucus to precision-cut lung slices and large animals, and propose minimum reporting standards for mucus collection, processing, and particle-tracking analysis so that transport data become comparable across studies. Clinical trial lessons, manufacturing constraints, and chronic-administration safety define the remaining translational boundaries. Throughout, we distinguish between mucus transport as an intermediate design parameter and therapeutic efficacy as the endpoint, and between disease-adapted design and patient-specific precision nanomedicine. This framework offers formulation scientists, model developers, and translational teams a shared quantitative basis for matching carrier design to barrier phenotype. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Inhaled nanomedicines have been vigorously pursued for the treatment of pulmonary diseases; however, their clinical translation remains challenging because the pulmonary mucus barrier intercepts most deposited particles before they reach the epithelium. Because this barrier is remodeled differently in each disease, mucus barrier phenotyping has been advocated as the foundation of rational formulation design. Quantitative barrier phenotypes of cystic fibrosis, COPD, asthma, IPF, and lung cancer are now measurable, making it possible to establish a disease-driven framework in which carrier strategies are matched to the barrier of the target pathology. This review summarizes these disease-specific phenotypes, critically maps four strategy classes onto them, and appraises the evaluation models and translational boundaries that govern clinical success.

articles.title: Multiwindow Doppler Acquisition and Potential Underassessment of Aortic Stenosis Severity.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

articles.title: Non-visual photoreception-mediated endocrine regulation: Insights and approaches from fish models.
articles.abstract: Non-visual photoreception contributes to various physiological processes across vertebrates. Although mammals largely rely on the eyes to receive light information, vertebrates also utilize non-visual photoreception in the brain. In particular, owing to the transparency of their bodies, fish can utilize non-visual photoreception in the central nervous system even more extensively. In the field of photoreception, the molecular properties of opsins and tissue-level gene expression changes have been well studied. However, the cellular mechanisms involving opsin-expressing cells and how they ultimately drive physiological functions at the whole-body level remain largely unclear. In this review, we focus on technical approaches for elucidating photoreception from the cellular to the whole-body level, introducing various live-cell imaging techniques and appropriate light sources. For live-cell imaging, model animals are exceptionally useful because transgenic and knock-in techniques allow imaging indicators to be expressed specifically in target cells. Furthermore, small fish models are particularly suited for analyzing non-visual photoreception due to their transparency. Using recent findings on direct photoreception in pituitary endocrine cells as a case study, we discuss the biological significance of non-visual photoreception from an endocrinological perspective. Additionally, due to its ability to function in response to ultraviolet light reaching deep central tissues, Opn5m serves as a promising optogenetic tool for use in freely moving small fish. Applying these tools to studies of non-visual photoreception is expected to reveal novel physiological phenomena.

articles.title: Has a consensus on alexithymia been reached? Letter to the Editor regarding Preece and Gross (2026).
Management of suspected infectious and autoimmune encephalitis in children - National Guidelines from the United Kingdom Joint Societies.
articles.abstract: Encephalitis is a rare but often devastating clinical syndrome resulting from inflammation of the brain parenchyma. Encephalitis is a neurological emergency with diverse infectious, autoimmune and inflammatory causes. It can be recognised late or missed, especially as mimics of encephalitis can make the diagnosis and appropriate treatment challenging. Delays in the recognition and treatment of encephalitis carry significant risks of morbidity and mortality. Since the first UK guideline for the management of suspected viral encephalitis in children was published in 2012, there have been substantial developments in the field. Advances in molecular diagnostics and antibody testing, alongside improved access to neuroimaging and electrophysiology have broadened the capacity to identify underlying aetiologies. The recognised spectrum of infectious and immune-mediated causes of encephalitis has expanded, and clinical experience with immunomodulatory therapies has grown considerably. A multidisciplinary national working group, representing neurology, infectious diseases, microbiology, virology, neuroimmunology and acute medicine, alongside national professional and third-sector organisations, was convened in Liverpool in 2023 to develop updated UK Joint Societies guidelines for the management of suspected infectious and autoimmune encephalitis in children. This guideline provides pragmatic, evidence-informed recommendations on the clinical recognition, investigation, diagnosis, acute management and rehabilitation of children with suspected encephalitis. It emphasises early identification and parallel consideration of infectious and immune-mediated causes, with particular attention to decision-making during the critical first 24-72hours of presentation. Standardised diagnostic and therapeutic pathways are presented to support consistent care across healthcare settings. Where the evidence base, including of diagnosis, remains limited, the need for early specialist and multidisciplinary input is emphasised. These recommendations aim to reduce mortality, limit long-term neurological morbidity, and improve outcomes for children with encephalitis across the UK.

articles.title: Host-derived lipids license proliferation of cholesterol-auxotrophic tick cells and promote flavivirus output.
articles.abstract: Sterol molecules play indispensable roles in the biology of cells and organisms.
