Yet, arthropods, including ticks, lack the capacity for de novo sterol biosynthesis and must rely on exogenous sources. How these organisms sense and utilise exogenous sterols at the cellular level remains only partially understood. Here, using the tick Ixodes ricinus IRE/CTVM19 cells cultured with full serum, or lipoprotein-deficient serum (LPDS), we found that LPDS supplementation arrested cellular proliferation. Defined lipid add-backs, cholesterol and linoleic acid, restored proliferation. After internalisation, tick cells exhibited a non-canonical cholesterol distribution, with free cholesterol accumulating predominantly within lysosomes and lipid droplets, and only marginally in plasma membrane. Availability of serum lipids also altered the expression of genes involved in lysosomal cholesterol handling, including specific niemann-pick C2 (npc2) and lysosomal integral membrane protein 2 (limp-2) transcripts. Consistent with a functional role for lysosomal trafficking, pharmacological disruption of lysosomal acidification or cholesterol export disturbed sub-cellular partitioning of cholesterol and inhibited cell proliferation. Finally, we examined whether serum lipid availability affected tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) infection. While the LPDS culture did not significantly alter cellular TBEV RNA, it reduced levels of extracellular TBEV RNA. Together, these findings identify cholesterol and linoleic acid as selective extracellular inputs that enable proliferative competence and reveal serum lipoprotein availability as a determinant of extracellular TBEV RNA production.

articles.title: Dihydroceramide redistribution and vesicular release during N. meningitidis infection in brain endothelial cells.
articles.abstract: Dihydroceramides are metabolic intermediates of de novo sphingolipid synthesis pathway that are increasingly recognized as bioactive lipids. Although dihydroceramide levels increase under various conditions of cellular stress and disease, the cellular fate of accumulated dihydroceramide has remained unclear. Here, we show that dihydroceramide accumulates rapidly in human brain microvascular endothelial cells upon infection with the meningitis-causing pathogen Neisseria meningitidis. This increase results from an early transient transcriptional downregulation of the dihydroceramide-hydrolyzing enzyme ACER3, followed by a sustained reduction in DEGS1-dependent dihydroceramide-to-ceramide conversion, as demonstrated by metabolic tracing of deuterated dihydroceramide. By combining live-cell imaging of clickable sphingolipid analogues and targeted LC-MS/MS analysis on purified subcellular fractions, we show that the accumulated dihydroceramide is redistributed in a CERT-dependent manner from the endoplasmic reticulum toward the Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane. Dihydroceramide is subsequently released primarily via large extracellular vesicles, whose sphingolipid profile differs significantly from that of small extracellular vesicles. Importantly, bacteria-free fractions of large extracellular vesicles reduce barrier resistance in recipient brain endothelial monolayers, whereas vesicles from uninfected cells do not. Taken together, these results demonstrate that during infection, accumulated dihydroceramide is not passively retained at its site of synthesis but is redistributed and released via plasma membrane-derived large extracellular vesicles. This redistribution may represent a previously unrecognized mechanism of sphingolipid homeostasis in brain endothelial cells and may contribute to altered barrier function during meningococcal disease.

articles.title: Higher HDL-C is associated with less acute kidney injury-associated delirium after CABG surgery.
articles.abstract: Delirium occurs after 15-52% of cardiac surgeries and is associated with an increased risk of long-term cognitive impairment and death. HDL-C is associated with less delirium after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery in patients ≥65 years old. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a risk factor for delirium after cardiac surgery. We hypothesized that higher preoperative HDL-C is associated with less AKI-associated delirium after CABG, particularly in patients ≥65 years old. We analyzed 13,027 medical records from CABG patients. To address potential selection bias arising from substantial missingness in HDL-C measurements, we calculated a propensity score representing the probability of HDL-C availability based on age, date of surgery, and preoperative comorbidities including hypertension, type 1 (T1D) and 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Propensity score adjusted multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate associations between HDL-C and AKI, delirium, and AKI-associated delirium. Higher HDL-C was associated with less AKI after CABG among all patients with an available HDL-C measurement (OR 0.92, p=0.04, n=3716) and in patients ≥65 years old (OR 0.86, p=0.004, n=2120). Higher HDL-C was not associated with less delirium (p=0.17) after CABG in the entire cohort but in patients ≥65 years old it was associated with less delirium (OR 0.80, p=0.046, n=2120) and with less AKI-associated delirium (OR 0.58, p=0.007, n=2120). These hypothesis-generating associations suggest that HDL-C warrants further study as a risk factor for AKI and delirium after CABG, particularly in elderly patients at high risk for both AKI and delirium.

articles.title: Association of nasal pro-resolving mediators with lung function and type 2 inflammation in adult asthma.
articles.abstract: Specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) alleviate airway hyperresponsiveness, reduce eosinophil infiltration, and promote efferocytosis in allergic mouse models. Comparable human evidence, however, is limited. This study aims to define the relationship between nasal SPMs and respiratory outcomes. In a panel study of 26 adults with mild-to-moderate asthma (MMA) and 33 adults without asthma, we collected nasal fluid samples longitudinally up to 4 times on each participant for the analysis of 21 lipid mediators, to associate with measures of lung function, airway resistance, and fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO). The same panel of lipid mediators was also measured in a subgroup of 15 paired bronchoalveolar lavage fluids (BALF) samples. Six SPMs (i.e., LXA4, LXB4, RvD2, RvD5, MaR1, and RvE4) were detected in nasal fluid, all of which were positively correlated with PGE2, 5- and 12/15-lipoxygenase (LOX) metabolites. In MMA participants, levels of RvD5, 12/15-LOX metabolites and PGE2 were lower. Atopy status, history of rhinitis, and medication use was not associated with changes in SPMs. However, the use of inhaled corticosteroids was associated with decreased levels of PGE2, a mediator known to trigger the lipid class switch from pro-inflammatory to pro-resolving responses. Higher RvD2 and RvD5 levels were associated with higher lung function while higher RvD2 levels were also associated with lower FeNO. RvD5 levels in nasal fluid were moderately correlated with those in BALF (Spearman r= 0.48, p=0.07). Our results indicate that nasal SPMs were lower in asthmatic individuals and were associated with higher lung function and lower airway inflammation.

articles.title: Mechanistic and Clinical Implications of Apolipoprotein Abnormalities in Preeclampsia.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-specific disorder characterized by hypertension and organ dysfunction. Lipid disturbances are associated with PE, but conventional lipid concentrations do not fully describe the accompanying changes in lipoprotein function. This narrative review examines apolipoprotein physiology during pregnancy, reported abnormalities in PE, and their possible mechanistic and clinical implications. Human observational and proteomic studies report changes in apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), apolipoprotein C-III (ApoC-III), and apolipoprotein E (ApoE), although their direction and magnitude vary with gestational timing, population, and disease phenotype. Experimental studies support selected pathways involving cholesterol handling and vascular protection; emerging research on apolipoprotein D (ApoD) also implicates placental ferroptosis in model systems. Direct causal evidence for an apolipoprotein M (ApoM)-sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) pathway in PE remains limited, although gestation-dependent alterations in ApoM and S1P have been reported in late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE). The available evidence supports a bidirectional conceptual framework in which placental hypoxia may influence maternal lipid and vascular dysfunction, while maternal metabolic disturbances may also aggravate placental injury. Apolipoprotein alterations could therefore be contributors, consequences, or both. Their potential use as complementary biomarkers requires prospective validation and demonstration of added value beyond established clinical and angiogenic assessment. Pregnancy-specific efficacy and safety data are also needed before apolipoprotein-directed therapies can be considered for PE.

articles.title: DNase I Mediated Degradation of Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Exacerbates Hepatic Schistosomiasis Caused by Schistosoma japonicum.
articles.abstract: Schistosomiasis caused by Schistosoma spp is a significant yet neglected tropical parasitic disease. The interaction between the host immune system and Schistosoma entails intricate mechanisms. Within the innate immune compartment, neutrophils are capable of eliminating large pathogens via the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). Nevertheless, the specific role of NETs in host defense against Schistosoma japonicum infection remains poorly understood. This study aimed to clarify the functional role of NETs in a murine model of S. japonicum infection. Our results confirmed that DNase I treatment effectively degraded NETs in vivo. Compared with infected mice without DNase I treatment, S. japonicum-infected mice receiving DNase I exhibited aggravated liver pathology, as evidenced by elevated serum levels of ALT and AST, decreased serum albumin, more severe inflammatory granulomas and hepatic fibrosis, as well as increased hepatic egg burden. It was observed that PMA-induced NETs could directly damage eggs in vitro. In conclusion, our findings suggest that DNase I treatment impairs host defense against S. japonicum infection, supporting a contribution of NETs during S. japonicum infection. Modulation of NETs formation may represent a potential therapeutic approach for schistosomiasis.

articles.title: Chronic ethanol feeding drives gut microbiome remodeling and influences cholestatic liver injury in mice.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a major cause of liver-related mortality worldwide and encompasses steatosis, cirrhosis, and alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH). AH is frequently accompanied by cholestasis, characterized by impaired bile flow and disrupted bile acid homeostasis. Although gut microbiome (GM) dysbiosis has been linked to ALD progression and cholestatic injury, its functional role in alcohol-associated cholestasis remains unclear. Mice were subjected to chronic ethanol-feeding (EF) or pair-feeding (PF) for 4 weeks. Fecal samples collected at 10 days and 4 weeks underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing. To assess the functional impact of microbiome alterations, cecal contents from male mice after 4 weeks of EF or PF were used for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Recipient mice received antibiotics during acclimatization, followed by 10 days of EF and FMT every other day. Forty-eight hours before sacrifice, mice were challenged with α-naphthylisothiocyanate (ANIT; 25 mg/kg) to induce cholestatic liver injury. Liver injury, cholestasis, and inflammation were evaluated biochemically and histologically. EF induced progressive GM remodeling, whereas PF did not. Unexpectedly, FMT from PF donors aggravated ANIT-promoted liver injury, cholestasis, and hepatic inflammation in EF recipients of both sexes. In contrast, FMT from EF donors did not significantly alter injury compared with non-FMT controls. These findings suggest that GM derived from PF and chronic EF mice differentially influence susceptibility to cholestatic liver injury in EF recipients.

articles.title: Platelets induce neutrophil apoptosis during lung viral infection.
articles.abstract: Platelets are known for their role in hemostasis. More recently, platelets are recognized as immunoregulatory cells that shape leukocyte responses during infection. Platelets are well-known for regulating neutrophil activity, yet their role in directing neutrophil apoptosis during viral inflammation remains poorly defined. Here, we investigated how platelet-neutrophil interactions regulate neutrophil apoptosis during Sendai virus (SeV) exposure. Using primary murine neutrophils, we show that platelets markedly accelerate virus-induced apoptotic commitment at early time points, with maximal effects observed at 3 hours. Annexin V/propidium iodide analysis revealed that platelet-virus interactions preferentially drive early apoptotic programs without promoting necrosis. Platelet-releasates were sufficient to induce neutrophil apoptosis, and this effect was abrogated by heat denaturation, indicating dependence on heat-labile mediators. Mechanistically, platelet releasates and viral exposure converged on caspase-3 mRNA induction and caspase-3/7 enzymatic activation, identifying executioner caspases as central effectors of platelet-amplified neutrophil apoptosis. Recombinant TNF-α enhances neutrophil apoptosis, whereas TNF-α neutralization and pharmacologic inhibition of caspase-3 attenuated platelet releasate-driven caspase activation and apoptotic commitment. Moreover, inhaled recombinant TNF-α improves survival from SeV in the platelet-depleted mouse model. Collectively, these findings identify platelets as early amplifiers of programmed neutrophil apoptosis during viral inflammation through TNF-α-dependent, caspase-mediated pathways. Platelet-driven acceleration of neutrophil turnover may contribute to inflammatory resolution in the lungs.

articles.title: Does Health Technology Assessment and Regulatory Real-World Evidence Guidance Support Advanced Causal Analytics? A Policy Review.
articles.journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health care decision making bodies such as regulators and health technology assessment (HTA) agencies have increasingly issued guidance on the use of real-world evidence (RWE). However, it is unclear if current guidance supports the use of 'advanced' causal analytics, characterised here by explicit causal estimands, and flexible assumption-lean modelling (for example, doubly robust approaches and nonparametric methods). Correct application of statistical estimators can help developers avoid statistical model mis-specification bias while achieving greater precision.

METHODS: We undertook a focused review of publicly available RWE guidance and frameworks from international HTA and regulatory bodies, that included recommendations on causal inference, considering (1) articulation of causal questions and estimands; (2) clear separation of identification assumptions from estimation choices; (3) recommendations to support selection of estimation approaches; (4) expectations for diagnostic checks; and (5) whether and how available causal frameworks are used to organise guidance.

RESULTS: Guidance primarily emphasises methods to account for confounding bias with limited direction on more granular elements around estimator selection. For example, there is uneven treatment of doubly robust estimation methods which may be endorsed in principle, yet often without sufficient discussion of approaches and practical diagnostics. Causal frameworks are mostly referenced but rarely used to structure guidance, which may have more focus on procedural or reporting elements. Estimand frameworks were frequently referenced in guidance.

CONCLUSIONS: Strengthening guidance may encourage the application of advanced causal analytics. However, challenges related to the implementation and transparency of these approaches will require upskilling efforts, practical checklists and explainable analytical pipelines.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding "External Ventricular Drainage for Refractory Intracranial Hypertension in Traumatic Brain Injury: Efficacy, Safety, and Outcomes".
PathoLec: A curated database of lectins from pathogenic agents and their host-glycan interactions.
articles.abstract: Recognition of host glycans by microbial lectins drives the early steps of several infections, yet this knowledge is organised around proteins rather than pathogenicity, and is scattered across resources. We present PathoLec, a new module of the UniLectin platform and a database of manually curated glycan-binding proteins, i.e., lectins, from pathogenic agents and of the host glycan ligands they bind. Each entry links a lectin to the pathogens expressing it, to the ligands and publication(s) documenting the binding event, to the host organisms and their affected tissues, and to the associated diseases. PathoLec documents 463 lectins, 954 experimental structures, and 221 glycans covering 1184 different lectin-ligand relationships. Besides the classical lectin- and glycan-centric routes, the module provides four new pathogen-centric query axes: pathogen agent, host organism, affected tissue and disease. PathoLec is freely available at https://unilectin.unige.ch/sugarbind/. Future developments include protein language model predictions and a combined search with GlyConnect.

articles.title: Relationship between integrated myocardial flow reserve and obstructive coronary artery disease and major adverse cardiac events: Findings from the multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is a powerful marker of prognosis in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (PET MPI), MFR cannot distinguish between epicardial and microvascular disease. Integrated MFR (iMFR) has been proposed to better detect epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) by combining MFR with focal perfusion abnormalities.

METHODS: We studied 34,761 patients as part of the REFINE PET registry of patients undergoing 82Rb or 13N-ammonia PET MPI. A subset of the above population without prior CAD (N=2,869) had a diagnostic angiogram within 180 days of PET MPI. Regions with an MFR <2 and a regional perfusion defect by total perfusion deficit (TPD) were defined as 'focally impaired' on a pixel by pixel basis. Regions with an MFR <2 without a regional perfusion defect were defined as 'diffusely impaired'. We also evaluated a separate angiographic cohort imaged with a third tracer, 18F-flurpiridaz, in the Flurpiridaz-301 trial (N=231). iMFR metrics were evaluated for the prediction of obstructive CAD and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

RESULTS: Of the 34,761 registry patients, 9,782 (28%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 3.8 years. In the angiographic cohort, 1,597 of 2,869 patients (56%) had obstructive CAD. For the diagnosis of obstructive CAD, the extent of focally impaired myocardium had an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.79), outperforming conventional minimal-segment MFR (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.74, P<0.001), but did not differ significantly from ischemic TPD or physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided the most prognostic information in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 1.32-1.38; C-statistic 0.723), compared with global MFR (C-statistic 0.722) and focally impaired myocardium (C-statistic 0.711).

CONCLUSION: The extent of focally impaired myocardium by iMFR outperformed conventional MFR for the diagnosis of obstructive CAD but performed similarly to ischemic TPD and physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided more prognostic information than focally impaired myocardium or global MFR.

articles.title: Hypertension Dissociates Radiographic and Symptomatic Progression in a Male Rat Model of Post-Traumatic Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the impact of hypertension on the relationship between structural damage and pain sensitivity in a post-traumatic osteoarthritis (OA) rat model, and explored possible neurovascular factor underlying radiographic-symptomatic dissociation in OA.

METHOD: The 6-month-old male rats underwent anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) to induce post-traumatic OA in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) and normotensive Wistar Kyoto (WKY) inbred strains. Joint structural changes were assessed via micro-CT and histology at 8 weeks post-surgery. Mechanical sensitivity and motor function were longitudinally monitored at baseline, 4-week and 8-week post-surgery. Based on lumbar dorsal root ganglia (DRG) RNA sequencing results, in vivo calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) replenishment experiment was performed for proof-of-concept.

RESULTS: SHR exhibited comparable articular cartilage degradation and subchondral bone loss to WKY following ACLT surgery. Strain-specific differences in surgical responses were confined specifically to mechanical pain processing, where WKY developed marked post-traumatic mechanical hypersensitivity (ACLT week 0 vs 8: 41.48 ± 15.76 gf vs 26.14 ± 9.404 gf; 95% CI: 0.3918 to 30.27, p = 0.0436), whereas SHR maintained hypoalgesia (ACLT week 0 vs 8: 31.88 ± 6.482 gf vs 42.73 ± 7.056 gf; 95% CI: -18.94 to -2.766, p = 0.0092), indicating a dissociation between the severity of joint damage and pain sensitivity. DRG transcriptomic analysis revealed the downregulation of CGRP-mediated nociceptive signalling in hypertensive rats. Exogenous CGRP replenishment partially restored mechanical sensitivity in SHR without affecting joint structural integrity or affective and cognitive behaviour.

CONCLUSION: Hypertension decouples structural damage from mechanical sensitivity in male rats with post-traumatic OA. While joint degradation progresses to a comparable extent in both strains, hypertensive rats maintain higher pain thresholds despite severe structural breakdown, with CGRP as a plausible neurovascular factor underlying this phenomenon.

articles.title: Antibiotic-derived peptides delivered by nanocarriers as multifunctional pharmacological modulators in chronic wound healing.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds, particularly those associated with diabetes and metabolic disorders, represent a persistent therapeutic challenge characterized by sustained inflammation, microbial colonization, oxidative imbalance, and impaired angiogenesis. Current pharmacological management relies heavily on antimicrobial agents; however, conventional antibiotics primarily address infection and exert limited influence on host pathways governing tissue repair. Recent studies indicate that peptide derivatives originating from antibiotic scaffolds retain membrane-targeting properties while also interacting with immune, redox, and cellular signaling networks relevant to wound resolution. This review examines antibiotic-derived peptides as pharmacologically active molecules whose therapeutic profile can be reshaped through nanocarrier-based delivery. Liposomal and lipid-based nanocarriers are discussed not only as drug transport systems but also as modulators of pharmacokinetics, spatial distribution, and microenvironmental exposure within the wound bed. Such systems enable sustained local presentation of peptides, potentially influencing macrophage polarization, cytokine balance, angiogenic signaling, and extracellular matrix remodeling in addition to antimicrobial effects. By integrating evidence from peptide pharmacology, wound pathophysiology, and controlled-release science, we evaluate how structural optimization and carrier design jointly determine biological activity in chronic wound settings. Key challenges, including proteolytic instability, dose localization, safety considerations, and translational scalability are analyzed to define the boundaries of clinical applicability. This perspective highlights the repositioning of antibiotic-derived peptides from infection-focused agents toward multifunctional regulators of tissue repair, providing a mechanistic basis for future pharmacological development in chronic wound therapy.

articles.title: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound ameliorates diet-induced MASLD with hepatic lipid metabolic remodeling.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global health challenge with limited therapeutic options. This study investigated the therapeutic effects of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) in diet-induced MASLD and characterized treatment-associated molecular and metabolic changes.

METHODS: An HFD-induced MASLD-like mouse model was established in C57BL/6 J mice. Mice received liver-targeted LIPUS for 20 min daily over 10 days. Metabolic phenotyping, histopathology, serum biochemistry, glucose and insulin tolerance tests, ELISA, transcriptomic sequencing, targeted metabolomics, and molecular assays were performed.

RESULTS: LIPUS ameliorated hepatic steatosis, dyslipidemia, mild liver injury, systemic insulin resistance, and circulating pro-inflammatory cytokine changes in HFD-fed mice. H&E quantification showed reduced hepatic vacuolar area after LIPUS. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses highlighted cholesterol- and bile acid-related pathways. LIPUS was accompanied by increased nuclear LXRα abundance, increased CYP7A1 protein abundance, and increased hepatic expression of Fxr, Bsep, Abcg5, and Abcg8. In parallel, SREBP-1c protein abundance and HFD-induced increases in the lipogenesis-related genes Fasn, Acly, Acaca, and Scd1 were reduced. These findings describe treatment-associated molecular changes but do not establish altered LXRα transcriptional activity.

CONCLUSION: LIPUS ameliorated diet-induced MASLD-like phenotypes and was accompanied by changes in hepatic LXRα abundance and selected cholesterol-, bile acid-, and lipogenesis-related molecular markers. These observations identify a treatment-associated molecular pattern involving LXRα and hepatic lipid metabolism but do not establish altered LXRα transcriptional activity or LXRα-dependent causality. These findings support further investigation of LIPUS as a non-invasive approach for metabolic liver disease.

articles.title: Ultrasound Teaching in UK Undergraduate Medical Education: A National Survey.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ultrasound teaching is increasingly incorporated into undergraduate medical education (UGME), yet its implementation within UK medical schools remains poorly described. This study aimed to provide the first comprehensive national overview of ultrasound teaching across UK UGME curricula.

METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2025 among UK medical schools. Respondents provided data on ultrasound curriculum integration, teaching delivery, faculty involvement, assessment methods and implementation barriers. Descriptive statistics were used to analyse responses.

RESULTS: Thirty-nine of 43 eligible medical schools responded (91% response rate). Twenty-six schools (67%) currently include formal ultrasound teaching in their curriculum, and seven further schools planned to introduce it in the 2025/26 academic year (85% if implemented). Most (69%) deliver ultrasound teaching across both early/pre-clinical and later/clinical years. Anatomy (81%) and procedural skills (65%) were the most common domains. The median total ultrasound teaching time was 5hours (IQR 3-10; n = 24), with 88% of schools providing ≤10hours. Small-group hands-on sessions were the predominant teaching method (96%), and 69% of schools did not assess ultrasound knowledge/skills. The main implementation barriers were limited curriculum capacity and trained faculty shortage (54% each). Overall, 59% of respondents supported inclusion of ultrasound as a mandatory GMC competency for graduates.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound teaching is gaining momentum within UK UGME. However, considerable variation exists in content, duration and assessment. Addressing faculty shortages, curriculum capacity and the absence of national competency standards will be essential to ensure consistent, high-quality ultrasound education across UK medical schools.

articles.title: When CTPA is not Cardiac CT: An Acquisition-Aware Approach to Cardiovascular Findings Beyond Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.abstract: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) answers a pulmonary vascular question, but the scan also covers the heart, pericardium and thoracic aorta. Cardiovascular findings in a CTPA report can be relevant, yet their interpretation is constrained by non-ECG-gated acquisition and pulmonary arterial phase contrast timing. This focused narrative review covers cardiovascular abnormalities including coronary artery and cardiac valve calcifications, pericardial effusion, pulmonary artery dilatation or right-heart enlargement, and thoracic aortic abnormalities. It explores the diagnostic value and limitations of these findings in clinical practice and offers a pragmatic framework for the acute medical take, to help clinicians decide which findings require urgent assessment, inpatient work-up, planned outpatient follow-up, or no further action.

articles.title: Effect of natural variants causing primary carnitine deficiency on the OCTN2 carnitine transporter.
articles.abstract: Primary carnitine deficiency results from defective OCTN2 carnitine transporters encoded by the SLC22A5 gene. Patients can present early in life with acute metabolic decompensation or later with skeletal and cardiac myopathy or sudden death from arrhythmia. Most identified pathogenic variants in the SLC22A5 gene are missense, but the mechanisms by which they impair OCTN2 activity remain unclear. Pathogenic variants (n=65) identified in affected patients were stably expressed in Chinese Hamster Ovary cells and assessed for their effect on carnitine transport, OCTN2 protein abundance, and subcellular localization. Functional analysis revealed two distinct mechanisms: pathogenic variants affecting hydrophilic domains were more likely to result in reduced OCTN2 protein abundance and retention of OCTN2 transporters in the cytoplasm, thus disrupting plasma membrane trafficking. By contrast, variants in transmembrane domains were more likely to retain normal OCTN2 protein abundance and membrane localization, but impaired carnitine transport activity. Incubation of selected variants with the molecular chaperone 4-phenylbutyric acid resulted in increased protein abundance for the mutants as well as the wild-type OCTN2 transporters. Carnitine transport activity improved in most variants affecting hydrophilic domains, possibly reflecting improved plasma membrane trafficking. By contrast, most of the variants localized in transmembrane domains showed little to no functional improvement despite enhanced plasma membrane localization, indicating irreversible structural or catalytic defects. This study underscores the necessity of precision medicine approaches to address both trafficking and functional deficiencies in disorders of membrane transport and provides a framework for developing targeted therapies tailored to patients' genetic profiles.

articles.title: Characterization of continuous glucose monitoring technology use in patients with diabetes at a multilingual federally qualified health center.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

articles.title: Pathogenesis and genomic architecture of azole-resistant Candida albicans isolated from the male genitourinary tract.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent genitourinary candidiasis caused by azole-resistant Candida albicans presents a significant therapeutic challenge. However, the pathogenesis and genomic architecture of these resistant strains in the male reproductive tract mucosal microenvironment remain poorly understood.

METHODS: Two C. albicans strains isolated from the glans penis (G1) and urethra (N1) of a single male patient with itraconazole treatment failure were analyzed. Antifungal susceptibility was evaluated using a commercial broth microdilution kit for MIC determination, supplemented by spotting assays. Genomic variations were profiled via WGS and cross-referenced with the FungAMR database. Ergosterol synthesis was assessed by spectrophotometry and qPCR, and in vivo virulence was evaluated using a Galleria mellonella infection model.

RESULTS: Susceptibility testing revealed that both isolates exhibited high-level cross-resistance to azoles while remaining susceptible to amphotericin B. WGS demonstrated deep clonal identity (>99.99%) and identified shared non-synonymous mutations in 67 resistance-associated genes. Azole resistance was associated with mutations in the ergosterol pathway, alongside a significant burden of copy number variations (CNVs). Spatial phenotypic heterogeneity was observed: compared to the glans isolate (G1), the urethral isolate (N1) showed a 42.5% reduction in ergosterol synthesis and significant attenuation of in vivo virulence, correlating with marked transcriptional downregulation of host-adherence factors.

CONCLUSION: This single-patient study found azole-resistant C. albicans from the male genital tract with ERG pathway mutations and structural genomic variations, alongside a virulence trade-off. These findings raise the possibility that prolonged empirical azole monotherapy may be inadequate and underscore the importance of following clinical guidelines and considering susceptibility results.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal Microbiota Dysbiosis in Entamoeba histolytica Infection: a Real-Time PCR Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Entamoeba histolytica causes a clinical spectrum ranging from asymptomatic colonization to invasive dysentery that host and parasite factors alone do not fully explain, and experimental evidence increasingly implicates the gut microbiota as a modifier of amebiasis pathogenesis. Few studies, however, have used absolute, real-time PCR-quantified bacterial abundance to test whether the magnitude of dysbiosis is associated with diarrheal severity (stool consistency) within a single cohort. We compared 23 real-time PCR-confirmed E. histolytica patients with 23 age- and sex-matched healthy controls in a case-control study in Egypt, using species-specific TaqMan assays to exclude the non-pathogenic species E. dispar and E. moshkovskii. Absolute abundance (log₁₀ gene copies/g stool) of total bacteria, Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, Bifidobacterium, the Lactobacillus group and the Clostridium leptum subgroup was determined by standard-curve-anchored SYBR Green qPCR, and between-group differences were tested, and correlations with Bristol Stool Form Scale score were assessed within infected patients, with false-discovery-rate correction. Cases showed significantly lower Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, Lactobacillus and C. leptum, and higher Bifidobacterium, than controls (all FDR q < 0.001; |Cohen's d| = 1.42-2.52), whereas total bacterial load was unchanged (p = 0.141). Symptomatic amebiasis was associated with a compositional dysbiosis independent of total bacterial biomass; however, within the 23 infected patients no taxon was significantly correlated with Bristol score (all FDR q ≥ 0.36), and inter-taxa correlations were not significant within either group, so we found no evidence that dysbiosis is associated with stool consistency (diarrheal severity). The absence of an asymptomatic E. histolytica-infected group also means the data cannot distinguish an association with disease severity from one with symptomatic infection itself. Because the design is cross-sectional, these data establish association rather than causation and cannot determine whether dysbiosis precedes or follows symptomatic infection, and, as an exploratory single-centre study of 23 patients and 23 controls, they are hypothesis-generating: any biomarker or intervention role for these taxa would require independent validation and longitudinal and functional studies.

articles.title: Seroprevalence of Trypanosoma cruzi infection in Latin American populations at risk: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Chagas disease (CD) remains a major public health challenge in Latin America (LA), yet up-to-date population-based prevalence estimates are limited. We assessed seroprevalence of T. cruzi infection among populations at risk in endemic Latin American countries through a systematic review and meta-analysis. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and SciELO to identify population-based studies reporting seroprevalence of T. cruzi among at-risk individuals in endemic countries, published between 1980 and 2021. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute prevalence checklist. Pooled prevalence estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models with a generalised linear mixed model, including sex-specific and age-group analyses. Heterogeneity was evaluated using the I² statistic. Sensitivity analyses and publication bias assessments were performed. Endemic countries were grouped into four geographical regions with similar epidemiological patterns. We included 150 studies from 16 countries, comprising more than 600,000 participants and 44,100 seropositive individuals. The overall pooled seroprevalence among at-risk populations was 4·9% (95% CI 3·6-6·6). Regional prevalence estimates were 7·6% (3·9-14·2) in Andean LA (21 studies), 3·7% (2·4-5·8) in central LA (54 studies), 10·6% (5·5-19·2) in southern LA (31 studies), and 3·3% (1·6-5·5) in Tropical LA (40 studies). Among children, pooled prevalence was 2·2% (1·5-3·3; 94 studies), with regional estimates of 5·9% (2·9-11·7) in Andean LA (15 studies), 1·4% (0·8-2·2) in central LA (33 studies), 6·5% (3·2-12·8) in southern LA (24 studies), and 0·7% (0·3-1·7) in Tropical LA (23 studies). The highest paediatric prevalences were observed in Bolivia and Argentina. In conclusion, CD seroprevalence remains substantial among at-risk populations, particularly in southern and Andean LA, with consistent patterns in children. High heterogeneity likely reflects true geographical variation and differences in study quality.

articles.title: The Cardiac and Coronary Artery Lymphatic System: A Largely Unrecognized but Vital Highway for Heart Health Maintenance and Recovery.
Caregiver Perceptions of Compassionate Extubations in a Neuroscience ICU versus Hospice.
articles.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Compassionate extubation may be performed in inpatient hospice facilities; however, how this experience compares to the hospital setting is unknown.

OBJECTIVES: This study explored caregiver perceptions of care and outcomes for patients who transferred to an inpatient hospice facility for compassionate extubation, compared to those for patients compassionately extubated in a hospital neurosciences intensive care unit (NSICU).

METHODS: Investigators identified patients with severe acute brain injury who underwent compassionate extubation in the University of North Carolina Medical Center (UNCMC) NSICU or a UNC inpatient hospice facility between January 2021 and July 2023. A research assistant audio-recorded semi-structured interviews with patient caregivers who were English-speaking and present for care with compassionate extubation. Interview transcripts were coded using a combination of deductive and inductive coding, and investigators conducted a thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Of 39 caregivers contacted, 9 from the hospital and 10 from the hospice completed interviews. Themes emerging from transcripts were environment, emotional support, and provider communications. Most caregivers were satisfied with the care delivered, but there were differences between settings and groups. Caregivers in both groups noted shortcomings in the hospital of convenience, tense environment, and bereavement services. The hospice group praised the physical and peaceful environment and compassionate care delivery. There was variability within both groups for how supportive they perceived communication.

CONCLUSION: Inpatient hospice may improve the experience for caregivers of neurologic patients undergoing compassionate extubation and allow access to increased bereavement support. Innovation in models of care for compassionate extubation, including transition to hospice, has the potential to improve patient and caregiver outcomes.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of anthropometric methods and bioelectrical impedance analysis for obesity assessment in women of reproductive age: validation against the deuterium dilution technique.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Accurate diagnosis is essential for tackling obesity. However, anthropometric methods and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) may misclassify adiposity across populations because of ethnic and physiological differences. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of anthropometric indices and BIA for obesity assessment among women of reproductive age in Kenya, using the deuterium dilution technique (DDT) as the reference method.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional analytical survey study was conducted among 256 African Kenyan women aged 20-49 years, selected through multistage sampling in Nyeri County, Kenya. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and Youden's index. Statistical significance was assessed at a 95% confidence level. The methods evaluated included body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), skinfold thickness (SFT), and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). All measurements were performed according to standardised procedures. BIA measurements followed the procedures for the MC-780U multifrequency body composition analyser, while anthropometric measurements adhered to the World Health Organization (WHO) and International Society for the Advancement of Kinanthropometry (ISAK) guidelines. Saliva collection and analysis for the deuterium dilution technique were conducted in accordance with International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) protocols. Anthropometric indices were calculated using WHO-calculators and the 4-site Durnin and Womersley equations. Body composition by BIA was assessed using the MC-780U BIA analyser, while total body water was determined from saliva samples using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy (4500 Series). Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.

RESULTS: Waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) demonstrated high sensitivity (92.5%) but low specificity (47.0%), indicating strong screening potential but overestimation of obesity. Bioelectrical impedance analysis and body mass index (BMI) exhibited high specificity (91.9% and 89.3%, respectively) but low sensitivity (49.5% and 46.7%, respectively), suggesting underestimation of obesity relative to DDT. Waist circumference was balanced with sensitivity and specificity of 78.5% and 74.5%, respectively, whereas skinfold thickness (SFT) demonstrated moderate sensitivity (81.3%) and lower specificity (61.7%). Waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) showed poor diagnostic performance (67.3% sensitivity; 63.1% specificity). ROC-AUC analysis indicated good discriminatory ability for BIA (0.854), BMI (0.810), WHtR (0.805), and WC (0.801), whereas SFT and WHR performed lower. DOR values were moderate for all methods (7.021 to 11.205) except WHR that was low. Optimised cutoff points modestly improved the sensitivity of BIA, BMI, and SFT.

CONCLUSIONS: WHtR is the most suitable screening tool, BIA and BMI are potential confirmatory tools. WC and SFT are complementary screening measures, and WHR has limited practical utility in this population. A multistep approach for diagnosis and population-specific cutoff points would improve obesity diagnosis.

articles.title: Reinfection with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 (SARS CoV-2) among healthcare workers in India.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare workers (HCWs) remain at heightened risk of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection due to sustained occupational exposure. The emergence of the Omicron variant, characterized by increased transmissibility and immune escape, had led to a rise in reinfections despite prior infection and vaccination. However, evidence on reinfection dynamics among HCWs in India remains limited.

METHODS: A multicentric prospective cohort study was conducted across 11 tertiary care hospitals in India between December 2021 and March 2023. HCWs with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection were enrolled retrospectively (within 4 weeks prior) and prospectively (8-month follow-up. Reinfection was defined using epidemiological criteria and confirmed by whole-genome sequencing wherever paired samples were available. Socio-demographic, clinical, exposure, immunological, and laboratory data were collected using standardized case report forms. Reinfection incidence was estimated, and bivariate analysis was performed to identify factors associated with reinfection.

RESULTS: Of 1,598 HCWs screened, 1,334 (83.4%) were enrolled and 1,331 (83.3%) completed follow-ups. Thirteen participants developed confirmed SARS-CoV-2 reinfection, yielding a cumulative incidence of 9.7 per 1,000 individuals and an incidence density of 2.97 per 100,000 person-days (95% CI: 1.73-5.11). The median interval between infection episodes was 193 days (IQR: 183-211). All reinfection cases were symptomatic but mild, with no hospitalizations or requirement for oxygen therapy. Whole-genome sequencing identified predominant circulation of Delta and Omicron lineages, with complete paired genome sequences confirming reinfection with genetically distinct. Although reinfection was more frequent among HCWs working in COVID-19 care areas (OR = 1.93; 95% CI: 0.63-5.95) and those aged ≥60 years (OR = 2.28; 95% CI: 0.29-18.15), these associations were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection occurred among HCWs during the Omicron-dominant period, with moderate incidence and predominantly mild clinical outcomes. Occupational exposure and recent contact history may contribute to reinfection risk. These findings underscore the importance of sustained infection prevention strategies and continued vaccination efforts to mitigate disease severity in high-risk populations.

articles.title: Breast sparganosis presenting as granulomatous mastitis without peripheral blood eosinophilia: a case report caused by Spirometra asiana.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Breast sparganosis is an uncommon tissue cestode infection that may resemble inflammatory or neoplastic breast disease. A 49-year-old Chinese woman presented with a painless left-breast mass at the 7-9 o'clock position and reported frequent consumption of locally caught wild freshwater frogs that may have been inadequately cooked. Ultrasonography showed an irregular 5.4 × 2.2 cm lesion. Peripheral eosinophils were normal, but core-needle biopsy demonstrated eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammation, raising suspicion of a parasitic infection. Surgical excision revealed one live, white, ribbon-like larva, which was removed intact. Histological examination was compatible with a plerocercoid cestode. Postoperative enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay detected anti-sparganum IgG. Mitochondrial shotgun sequencing of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded larval tissue identified Spirometra asiana. The patient received oral praziquantel at 25 mg/kg three times daily for two days without adverse effects. No apparent abnormalities were reported at five-month follow-up. This case highlights that tissue eosinophilia may provide an early diagnostic clue despite a normal peripheral eosinophil count. Diagnosis was established by recovery of the intact larva and compatible histopathology; serology was supportive, and molecular analysis enabled species identification.

articles.title: Impact of Biannual Community-Directed Treatment with Ivermectin on Onchocerciasis Transmission in Rural Tanzania: A Parasitological and Entomological Survey.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: High prevalence of onchocerciasis and epilepsy prompted a shift from annual to biannual community-directed treatment with ivermectin (CDTI). We assessed the effect of biannual CDTI on onchocerciasis transmission and progress towards WHO elimination targets.

METHODS: Cross-sectional parasitological and entomological surveys were conducted. Ov16 serology among children aged 6-10 years was conducted in 2017/18, 2021, and 2024 and ivermectin uptake was assessed. Blackflies were collected in 2024 and analysed in pools for Onchocerca volvulus infection.

RESULTS: The prevalence declined from 17.2% (95% CI: 14.7-19.9) after two decades of annual CDTI in 2017 to 13.3% (95%CI: 11.6-15.1) after four rounds of biannual CDTI in 2021 and further to 10.7% (95%CI: 9.1-12.5) after eight rounds of biannual CDTI in 2024. Non-uptake of ivermectin by children rose to 21.6% in 2024 compared to 15.8% in 2021 and 20.3% in 2017/18. Anti-Ov16 seropositivity was significantly lower in 2024 (OR=0.61, 95%CI: 0.45-0.82) compared to 2017/18 and was associated with age and residence in middle-altitude villages. Among 20,321 Simulium damnosum s.l flies analysed, 43.7% of the pools tested positive for Onchocerca volvulus, with an infectivity rate of 0.58% (95%CI: 0.47-0.71).

CONCLUSIONS: Biannual CDTI reduced transmission; however, high Ov16 seroprevalence among children and Simulium infectivity above WHO elimination thresholds indicate ongoing transmission, highlighting the need to strengthen CDTI and complementary vector control interventions.

articles.title: Beyond conventional neurodiagnostic: quantum-enabled mapping of AGE-RAGE dynamics in type 3 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 3 Diabetes (T3D) is a conceptual framework used to describe the association between cerebral insulin resistance, metabolic dysfunction and neurodegenerative processes, particularly those associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD). The advanced glycation end products (AGEs)-receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) axis has been implicated in oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling and neuronal dysfunction. However, conventional biochemical approaches often provide endpoint measurements and may not fully resolve the spatial and temporal dynamics of these processes. Advances in quantum sensing and nanotechnology offer potential tools for detecting selected physicochemical signals in biological systems, although their demonstrated capabilities vary substantially across platforms. This review examines the biological relevance of the AGE-RAGE axis in neurodegeneration and discusses the principles and types of quantum sensing technologies, including nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond and quantum dots, alongside other nanomaterial-based sensing approaches. Particular attention is given to probe functionalization, bioconjugation, signal transduction and experimental platforms that could support future investigations of AGE-RAGE-associated processes. Importantly, direct, real-time quantum sensing of AGE-RAGE interactions in living neuronal systems remain to be experimentally established. Accordingly, proposed applications involving receptor activation, downstream signaling, brain organoids, brain-on-chip systems and in vivo imaging are considered in terms of their potential, limitations and validation requirements. Challenges relating to target specificity, biological interference, biocompatibility, spatial and temporal resolution and translational feasibility are also discussed. This review outlines a prospective framework for investigating AGE-RAGE-associated signaling dynamics while distinguishing established sensing capabilities from applications that require further experimental validation.

articles.title: Neuroprotective actions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in Neurodegeneration: From mechanisms to clinical translation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been explored as potential therapeutics for neurodegenerative disorders, yet a comprehensive integration of their neuroprotective mechanisms across Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and related conditions remains to be consolidated. This review examines the multimodal effects of GLP-1RAs on neuroinflammation, autophagy, mitochondrial function, and protein aggregation, with a focus on translational relevance and alignment between preclinical findings and clinical evidence.

METHODOLOGY: A systematic synthesis of preclinical and clinical studies investigating GLP-1RA administration in neurodegenerative disease models and populations was conducted. Studies reporting neuroprotective outcomes and mechanistic pathways were included, and clinical trial data and real-world evidence for AD, PD, Huntington's disease, stroke, diabetic encephalopathy, and peripheral neuropathy were systematically evaluated.

RESULTS: Preclinical evidence revealed that GLP-1RAs modulate key pathogenic processes, including amyloid-β and tau pathology, α-synuclein accumulation, neuroinflammatory cascades, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dynamics, endoplasmic reticulum stress, autophagy, and synaptic plasticity. Clinical data provided variable support, with emerging real-world evidence suggesting potential benefits. Novel strategies-such as dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, enhanced blood-brain barrier penetration, and sustained-release formulations-were identified as promising approaches to improve efficacy, although significant gaps remain between preclinical promise and clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: This review consolidates evidence that GLP-1RAs exert broad neuroprotective effects through multiple mechanisms, but clinical translation is still evolving. The potential of GLP-1-based therapies as disease-modifying interventions for neurodegeneration warrants further investigation, with particular attention to bridging preclinical and clinical findings and optimizing drug delivery strategies.

articles.title: Nephrotoxicity following Loxosceles Envenomation: Experimental evidence from a guinea pig model.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury is one of the major complications of systemic loxoscelism and represents the leading cause of death associated with severe envenomation. Although both direct and indirect mechanisms have been implicated in venom-induced nephrotoxicity, the pathophysiological processes underlying renal injury and hematological alterations remains incompletely understood. Experimental approaches integrating functional, biochemical, urinary, and morphological assessments are essential for investigating the progression of renal damage following envenomation. In this study, we established and characterized a guinea pig model of Loxosceles intermedia envenomation, with emphasis on renal and hematological alterations. Eighteen male guinea pigs received intradermal injections of venom at doses ranging from 11.63 to 350 µg/animal and were evaluated through hematological, biochemical, urinary, electrophoretic, histopathological, and ultrastructural analyses. Renal dysfunction was evidenced by increased serum concentrations of urea, creatinine, phosphorus, and symmetric dimethylarginine, with significant associations between venom dose and renal injury biomarkers. Urinalysis revealed increased urine specific gravity, glycosuria, ketonuria, hematuria, and proteinuria, while quantitative urinary analyses demonstrated increased protein excretion and gamma-glutamyl transferase activity. Urinary SDS-PAGE electrophoresis revealed progressive changes in the urinary protein profile, with increased intensity of low- and intermediate-molecular-weight protein bands, particularly those around 20, 35-45, and 60-70 kDa, together with the appearance of higher-molecular-weight bands. Hematological analyses also identified alterations in erythrocyte and platelet counts following envenomation, supporting the occurrence of systemic hematological involvement. Histopathological examination demonstrated acute tubular necrosis, tubular degeneration, glomerular lesions, and hyaline material deposition, whereas transmission electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial damage, lysosomal phospholipidosis, and ultrastructural changes consistent with tubular injury. Overall, L. intermedia venom induced severe systemic alterations characterized predominantly by progressive renal injury, accompanied by hematological changes. These findings support the use of this guinea pig as a useful experimental model for investigating the renal and hematological effects of loxoscelism.

articles.title: Hypoxia-responsive CAIX-targeted radioligand for non-invasive imaging and radioligand therapy: from preclinical to first-in-human evaluation.
articles.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is an attractive target for radioligand theranostics because it is constitutively overexpressed in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and induced by hypoxia in several solid tumors. Existing CAIX-targeted radiotracers are constrained by delayed imaging kinetics, limited tumor retention, incomplete therapeutic-labeling compatibility, or insufficient tumor-to-background contrast. Here we report GL-261, a CAIX-targeted radioligand that appends a nitroimidazole bioreductive retention module to a CAIX-targeting pharmacophore within a DOTA-chelated scaffold. This design enables paired radiolabeling with gallium-68 for PET imaging and lutetium-177 for radioligand therapy. Nitroimidazole conjugation conferred hypoxia-dependent cellular accumulation, greater internalization (64.6% versus 45.2%), and higher CAIX-dependent tumor uptake than the comparator DPI-4452 without compromising target specificity. In xenograft models spanning different CAIX expression levels, [68Ga]Ga-GL-261 PET stratified tumors by CAIX status and was suppressed by receptor blocking. [177Lu]Lu-GL-261 showed sustained tumor retention over 168h and, at 37 MBq, produced marked tumor growth suppression without overt hematological or organ toxicity. In a first-in-human PET/CT study of 15 patients, [68Ga]Ga-GL-261 showed reproducible biodistribution, an effective dose of 8.45 × 10-2mSv/MBq, and lesion uptake that correlated with CAIX immunohistochemical expression (r = 0.93, P = 0.007 at 60min). These findings support hypoxia-responsive modification as a design strategy for CAIX-targeted radioligands and provide a translational basis for GL-261 in CAIX-expressing cancers. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trail (registration No. ChiCTR2600127500).

articles.title: Global burden of stroke-related heart failure in GBD 2021 from 1990 to 2021.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke-related Heart Failure (HF) is a modeled cause-impairment outcome in the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study. Its population distribution should be distinguished from all HF occurring among people with a history of stroke. We examined temporal patterns, demographic contributions, and socioeconomic disparities in this GBD-defined outcome.

METHODS: We analyzed GBD 2021 prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) estimates for 1990-2021 across global, regional, and national settings. Full-period estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and segmented regression described trends. Age- and sex-specific rates supplemented absolute counts. Spearman correlations, explicitly defined inequality indices, and demographic decomposition characterized differences in burden. Bayesian age-period-cohort projections were evaluated using two held-out time windows and a last-observed-rate benchmark.

RESULTS: Global prevalent cases increased from 900,446 in 1990 to 1,983,544 in 2021, while age-standardized prevalence and YLD rates declined modestly over the full period. The middle-SDI group had high aggregate burden, but this does not imply uniform country-level patterns. Male age-specific rates remained higher at ages 80-89 despite a crossover in absolute counts at age 80. Ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage accounted for 47.46% and 46.64% of prevalent cases in the subtype estimates. Population aging and growth contributed 55.95% and 49.81% of the net increase in cases. Inequality estimates depended on weighting and the selected estimator; a robust widening was not established. Forecasts performed worse than the simple benchmark in both validation windows.

CONCLUSION: Increasing absolute burden despite modest declines in standardized rates supports planning for the needs of aging populations. Country-specific estimates and local assessments of access to care should guide priorities. Count-based sex differences, ecological associations, inequality trends, and exploratory forecasts require cautious interpretation.

articles.title: KLF5-mediated NRP1 upregulation contributes to neurovascular dysfunction after ischemic stroke in male diabetic mice through dysregulated VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) exacerbates the outcomes of ischemic stroke by disrupting neurovascular homeostasis. However, the molecular mechanisms linking diabetic metabolic stress to impaired vascular and glial responses after ischemic injury remain incompletely understood. Neuropilin-1 (NRP1), a co-receptor involved in VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling, and Krüppel-like factor 5 (KLF5), a transcription factor implicated in vascular remodeling, may contribute to diabetic ischemic neurovascular dysfunction.

METHODS: Male diabetic db/db mice and male non-diabetic db/+ mice were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). Human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) and primary cortical astrocytes were exposed to high glucose combined with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R). The expression and regulatory relationship between KLF5 and NRP1 were investigated using qRT-PCR, western blotting, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-qPCR, and luciferase reporter assays. The effects of KLF5 knockdown and NRP1 overexpression on endothelial and astrocytic functions were evaluated using migration, tube formation, and cell viability assays.

RESULTS: T2DM aggravated ischemic brain injury, characterized by increased infarct volume, enhanced neuronal degeneration, worsened neurological deficits, reduced CD31 immunoreactivity, and elevated expression of KLF5 and NRP1. Mechanistically, KLF5 directly bound to the NRP1 promoter and promoted NRP1 transcription. Under high-glucose OGD/R conditions, increased KLF5 and NRP1 expression was accompanied by enhanced VEGFR2 phosphorylation and impaired endothelial migration and tube formation. KLF5 knockdown reduced NRP1 expression and VEGFR2 phosphorylation, thereby improving endothelial migration, tube formation, and astrocyte viability/migration. Conversely, NRP1 overexpression partially reversed the protective effects of KLF5 knockdown.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetic ischemic stress induces maladaptive activation of the KLF5/NRP1 axis, contributing to neurovascular dysfunction through dysregulated VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling. Targeting the KLF5/NRP1 pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for alleviating diabetic ischemic brain injury.

articles.title: AI-driven radiopharmaceutical dosimetry optimization for theranostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Personalised radioligand therapy (RLT) depends on accurate absorbed-dose estimation. Standard dosimetry requires multiple post-therapy single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) acquisitions, imposing logistical burdens. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have been proposed to streamline organ segmentation, generate synthetic imaging timepoints, and predict patient-specific doses. We evaluated the performance, methodological quality, and translational readiness of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven dosimetry in the clinical theranostics literature.

METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and regional databases (Jan 1, 2014, to March 1, 2025). Studies applying AI to dosimetry in human RLT recipients were eligible. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST) and the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2). Meta-analyses of organ segmentation (Dice similarity coefficient [DSC]) and dose prediction (concordance correlation coefficient [CCC]) used restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) random-effects models restricted to studies with independent validation sets.

PROSPERO: CRD420261349805 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1349805).

RESULTS: 58 studies met inclusion criteria covering 1847 patients (1523 [82%] male, 324 [18%] female). 23 studies with independent validation were eligible for meta-analysis. Pooled DSC was 0·87 (95% CI 0·83-0·90; 16 studies). Pooled voxel dosimetry relative absolute error (RAE) was 6·1% (4·6-8·1%; 12 studies). Pretherapy kidney dose prediction yielded pooled CCC 0·79 (0·72-0·85; 8 studies). PROBAST identified high risk of bias in 71% of prediction studies. Reducing timepoints from ≥3 to 1-2 scans increased RAE by 8·2 percentage points (5·1-11·4). AI reduced median processing time from 180 to 25 minutes.

CONCLUSIONS: On independent validation data, AI-driven dosimetry shows promising accuracy for organ-level dose estimation and substantially reduces processing time. However, the evidence base remains immature: 71% of prediction studies carry high risk of bias, only four studies report external validation, and most pooled outcomes were graded as low or very low certainty. External multicentre validation and prospective randomised trials comparing AI-guided against fixed-activity RLT are needed before clinical adoption. Current evidence primarily demonstrates technical feasibility rather than proven clinical utility.

articles.title: Molecular imaging in chronic osteoarticular infection: From bone scintigraphy to [18F]FDG PET.
authors: en nombre del grupo de Trabajo de Patología Musculoesquelética de la SEMNIM
articles.journal: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
articles.abstract: Chronic osteoarticular infection is a diagnostic challenge due to the coexistence of persistent inflammation, bone remodeling, fibrosis and post-treatment changes that limit the performance of conventional imaging techniques. Here we describe the role of the main Nuclear Medicine techniques used in this context: bone scintigraphy, labeled white blood cell scintigraphy, [67Ga]Ga-citrate scintigraphy and [18F]FDG (Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computerized tomography (PET/CT) (FDG-PET). Their pathophysiological principles, diagnostic performance, advantages, limitations and factors conditioning the precision of these techniques are analyzed as well as the anatomical localization, the presence of prosthetic material, the time since surgery and previous antibiotic treatment. Likewise, we review their application in especially complex scenarios in clinical practice, such as chronic peripheral osteomyelitis, spondylodiscitis and chronic post-sternotomy infection. Finally, the main lines of research and new radiopharmaceuticals aimed at the diagnosis of infectious disease are presented, highlighting the need for individualized selection of the imaging technique according to the clinical context for optimizing the diagnosis and directing treatment.

articles.title: Extent of myocardial deposition and its association with heart failure in ATTR amyloidosis: tomographic patterns of [99mTc]Tc-DPD uptake.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between the percentage of myocardium affected as determined by SPECT/CT and heart failure in patients with ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, and to characterize the associated tomographic uptake patterns.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: ECG-gated SPECT/CT was performed in 147 patients with ATTR confirmed by [99mTc]Tc-DPD scintigraphy, a Perugini score of ≥ 2, and exclusion of AL amyloidosis. The polar maps, obtained from the summed images, were classified into six predefined tomographic patterns. The percentage of affected myocardium was derived from the calculation of myocardial extent provided by QPS/QGS, expressed inversely to the usual percentage of extent. LVEF was derived from the gated acquisition.

RESULTS: Statistically significant differences were observed in the percentage of affected myocardium between the different tomographic patterns (p < 0.001), with the lowest values in the septal pattern (47.7 ± 8.0%) and the highest in the diffuse pattern (84.8 ± 12.9%). The presence of heart failure was associated with a higher percentage of affected myocardium both in the overall cohort (74% vs. 68%; p = 0.042) and in the subgroup of patients with Perugini grade 3 (75% vs. 68.5%; p = 0.026). There was no significant association between tomographic patterns and LVEF.

CONCLUSION: The percentage of affected myocardium calculated by SPECT/CT was associated with the presence of heart failure in patients with ATTR amyloidosis. The identification of tomographic patterns enabled this extent of myocardial involvement to be characterized, providing information that complements the Perugini scale. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) derived from ECG gating was not associated with the uptake patterns. These results suggest that quantifying the extent of myocardial deposition by SPECT/CT may be of clinical interest in ATTR.

articles.title: Incidence and predictors of de novo atrial fibrillation in patients with heart failure undergoing continuous rhythm monitoring.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). The true incidence of de novo AF in HF, however, remains uncertain. Moreover, the role of clinical variables and circulating biomarkers in AF risk stratification in this population is not well established. This study aimed to determine the incidence of AF in patients with HF using long-term continuous rhythm monitoring and to identify clinical, structural, and biomarker-based predictors.

METHODS: This multicenter, prospective study included patients with HF and reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Long-term rhythm monitoring was performed using implantable loop recorders or single-chamber defibrillators without atrial leads and with ventricular pacing < 20%. Serial blood samples were obtained at baseline, during follow-up, and during HF decompensation, and analyzed using a multiplex panel of selected biomarkers. Multivariable analyses were performed using both baseline biomarker levels and laboratory values closest to AF onset or HF decompensation.

RESULTS: A total of 345 patients were enrolled (79% male; median age 68 years; 53% with LVEF< 40%. During a median follow-up of 756 days, 86 patients (24.9%) developed AF episodes lasting > 6 minutes, and 64 patients (18.5%) died. Hypertension, left atrial volume, beta-blocker use, CA-125, NT-proBNP, COL4A1, and AT1-AA were independently associated with AF, whereas aldosterone receptor antagonist therapy was associated with a lower risk of HF (C-index, 0.74). Patients with persistent AF as the initial manifestation had significantly higher mortality than those with paroxysmal AF or no AF. NT-proBNP and COL4A1 were associated with mortality. Clinically relevant bradyarrhythmias and ventricular tachyarrhythmias were also detected.

CONCLUSION: De novo AF is a common complication in patients with HF. Integrating clinical variables, structural parameters, and biomarkers improves the identification of patients at increased risk of developing AF. Continuous monitoring enables early detection of rhythm abnormalities that may influence therapeutic management.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of posterior wall isolation in persistent atrial fibrillation is modified by ablation energy source.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior wall isolation (PWI) is a common adjunct to pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in catheter ablation of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF), yet randomized data have been discordant. Prior syntheses have pooled studies across ablation energy sources, which may obscure energy-specific effects. We examined whether the association of PWI with arrhythmia recurrence in persistent AF is modified by ablation energy source.

METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science for studies comparing PWI plus PVI with PVI alone in persistent AF. The primary endpoint was recurrence of all atrial tachyarrhythmias; secondary endpoints were recurrence of AF alone, procedural time, and procedural complications. Studies were stratified a priori by energy source (cryoballoon, radiofrequency [RF], and pulsed field [PF]). Odds ratios (OR) and mean differences were pooled using random-effects models, with subgroup differences assessed by the test for interaction.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies with 4400 patients with persistent AF (2029 PWI and PVI, 2371 PVI alone) were included. Compared with PVI alone, PWI was associated with reduced recurrence of all atrial tachyarrhythmias overall (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.40-0.73), but the effect differed by energy source (test for subgroup differences p = 0.0006): cryoballoon OR 0.34 (95% CI 0.26-0.43), RF OR 0.67 (95% CI 0.43-1.04), and PF OR 0.96 (95% CI 0.55-1.70). A concordant pattern was observed for recurrence of AF alone (overall OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.25-0.51). PWI was associated with longer procedural times, with a graded effect across energies (cryoballoon mean difference 51.1 min; p = 0.007 for subgroup differences). Procedural complications did not differ between groups overall (OR 1.29, 95% CI 0.92-1.82) or by energy source (p = 0.49).

CONCLUSIONS: In persistent AF, the association of PWI with freedom from atrial arrhythmia was concentrated in cryoballoon-based ablation and was not evident with RF or PF, without an excess of complications. These findings suggest that the conflicting literature on PWI may be explained, in part, by differences in ablation energy source rather than by the anatomic target alone. Because energy source is partly confounded with study design and the cryoballoon evidence rests on few randomized trials, this association is hypothesis-generating and merits evaluation in energy-specific randomized trials. No benefit was observed in the pulsed field ablation stratum, the modality in which adjunctive PWI is now most commonly performed, so its routine use may not confer the benefit reported with earlier energy sources.

articles.title: Tailored therapy for bradyarrhythmias: integrating leadless pacing, conduction system pacing, and cardioneuroablation.
articles.abstract: Bradyarrhythmias represent a heterogeneous group of disorders ranging from intrinsic cardiac disease to functional autonomic disturbances. Although conventional transvenous pacing remains the cornerstone of treatment, a uniform device-based approach may not adequately address the diverse pathophysiological substrates underlying bradyarrhythmias. Device-related complications, pacing-induced ventricular dysfunction, and the growing recognition of vagally mediated bradyarrhythmias have highlighted the need for a more individualized therapeutic strategy. Recent advances have expanded the available treatment options through the development of leadless pacing, conduction system pacing (CSP), and cardioneuroablation (CNA). Importantly, these therapies should not be viewed as interchangeable alternatives, but rather as complementary approaches targeting distinct clinical scenarios. Leadless pacing minimizes transvenous hardware and may be particularly advantageous in patients at increased risk of device-related complications, limited venous access, or low anticipated pacing requirements. CSP preserves physiological ventricular activation and may reduce the risk of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy in patients with a high expected ventricular pacing burden or a vulnerable ventricular substrate. Conversely, CNA provides a mechanism-based, device-free therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with functional, vagally mediated bradyarrhythmias. In this review, we propose a practical framework for patient selection based on three complementary phenotypes: the high-risk and low-pacing-burden patient, the high-pacing-burden and vulnerable ventricle, and the vagal phenotype (see Central Illustration). By integrating pathophysiology, anticipated pacing burden, ventricular susceptibility, and autonomic substrate, contemporary management can move beyond the traditional device-centered paradigm toward a tailored approach aimed at delivering the right therapy to the right patient.

articles.title: Clinical readiness of first-trimester gestational diabetes prediction: From risk score to care pathway.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess whether first-trimester gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) prediction can improve clinical decisions, rather than merely predict a later abnormal glucose test.

METHODS: We critically reviewed targeted PubMed searches, independent validations, prospective implementation studies, randomized trials and guidelines. Searches were non-systematic and selection limitations are reported.

RESULTS: Routine clinical and glycemic predictors are feasible, but transportability, calibration, and strategy-level benefit are not established consistently. RESPECT 2 demonstrated implementation feasibility; a trial of nutrition support in 519 model-selected women did not significantly reduce GDM. TOBOGM investigated treatment after early biochemical diagnosis, not care guided by a risk score. Direct trials of the complete prediction-guided strategy remain limited.
