CONCLUSION: First-trimester scores should not replace recommended diagnostic testing. Clinical adoption requires local validation, a prespecified beneficial action, evaluation of costs and harms, and comparative trials measuring maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Long-term cumulative exposure and longitudinal profiles of the cholesterol, high density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index, versus the metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) for incident heart failure risk: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index and the metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) are considered surrogate indexes of insulin resistance (IR). However, the associations of their cumulative exposure patterns and longitudinal profiles with incident heart failure (HF) have not been comprehensively investigated.

METHODS: We included 71,078 participants aged 20-98 years from the Kailuan Study who completed three consecutive health examinations between 2006 and 2015. Time-weighted cumulative measures and longitudinal profiles of CHG and METS-IR were calculated to characterize long-term metabolic exposure. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate their associations with incident HF.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 12.78 years, 1,803 incident HF events were documented. In the multivariable-adjusted model, each 1-SD increment in TW-cumCHG and TW-cumMETS-IR was associated with a higher risk of incident HF, with corresponding HRs of 1.27 (95 % CI, 1.21-1.33) and 1.37 (95 % CI, 1.28-1.48), respectively. Participants with jointly elevated TW-cumCHG and TW-cumMETS-IR had the highest risk of incident HF (HR, 1.71; 95 % CI, 1.51-1.94). K-means clustering identified three distinct longitudinal profiles for both CHG and METS-IR, with the persistently high groups exhibiting the greatest HF risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher cumulative exposure and persistently unfavorable profiles of CHG and METS-IR were independently associated with increased incident HF. Individuals with elevated levels of both indices had the highest risk of HF, suggesting that their concomitant elevation may reflect a greater cardiometabolic burden and highlighting the importance of comprehensive cardiometabolic risk management in HF prevention.

articles.title: Kidney effects of tirzepatide across albuminuria, filtration markers, and clinical outcomes: a parent-trial-level systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Whether tirzepatide's kidney effects extend from albuminuria lowering to filtration preservation and clinical outcomes remains uncertain. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through August 2026 and mapped randomized reports to independent parent trials. Ten parent trials provided kidney data; eight informed each principal synthesis. Versus insulin, tirzepatide reduced urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio by 27.0% (95% CI, 16.0%-36.6%; I2 = 37.8%; moderate certainty), whereas placebo-controlled evidence was uncertain (-18.1%; 95% CI, -43.2% to 18.3%; very low certainty). Fixed-time creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate showed no clear benefit (0.36 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI, -0.34 to 1.07; low certainty). In SURPASS-CVOT, approximate post hoc aggregate contrasts suggested larger high-risk effects for filtration and a hard-only composite, but were multiplicity-unadjusted and not formal individual-participant interaction tests. In that high-risk stratum, the hard-only hazard ratio versus dulaglutide was 0.70 (0.57-0.86), while end-stage kidney disease was not clearly reduced (1.04; 0.70-1.55). Albuminuria lowering versus insulin was reproducible; hard-outcome benefit was population- and endpoint-dependent, and dedicated kidney-outcome trials remain needed.

articles.title: Feasibility of and Adherence to a Changes in Fetal Movement Clinical Algorithm.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A one-page changes in fetal movement (CFM) clinical algorithm was developed to guide health care professionals in a timely assessment of fetal well-being when CFM is reported. The aim of the study was to evaluate feasibility and adherence to the clinical algorithm across diverse clinical settings.

STUDY DESIGN: A multicenter cohort study design.

SETTING: United States.

PARTICIPANTS: Twenty-two health care professionals (participants), including nurses, physicians, and certified nurse midwives, contributed data on 143 patients reporting episodes of CFM.

METHODS: Participants used the CFM clinical algorithm each time a patient presented with concerns about fetal movement during the 12-week study period. Data on algorithm adherence and deidentified patient characteristics were collected and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Timely evaluation within 2 hr of a patient report of CFM occurred in 87.4% of cases (n = 125). Interventions varied, with the nonstress test used most often (94.4%, n = 135). All participants reported having the necessary equipment and following the algorithm.

CONCLUSION: The CFM clinical algorithm was feasible and showed high clinician adherence, supporting timely evaluation and providing a structured framework for clinical assessment and patient education. Further research is needed to assess its effect on maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Post-Stroke Delirium and Its Impact on Additional Nursing Minutes and Nursing Tasks: A Prospective Single-Centre Case-Control Study Using Routine Data.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare people with post-stroke delirium and those without post-stroke delirium regarding the additional nursing time and nursing tasks required for their care.

DESIGN: Prospective single-centre case-control study using routine data.

METHODS: People admitted to the Stroke Centre between July and December 2023 who met the inclusion criteria were screened for post-stroke delirium. Propensity score matching was used to match people who experienced post-stroke delirium with those who did not by age, sex, stroke diagnosis and other confounding factors. Nursing time and nursing tasks were measured using the Leistungserfassung in der Pflege method.

RESULTS: Of the 564 screened people, 202 met the inclusion criteria. After matching, the cohort comprised 90 participants (45 experienced post-stroke delirium and 45 did not). Participants who experienced post-stroke delirium required substantially more nursing time, particularly for movement, personal hygiene and dressing, in-hospital transport, one-on-one care, laboratory tests, medication and treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Post-stroke delirium is associated with increased nursing workload, highlighting the importance of early identification, targeted nursing care and appropriate resource planning.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Post-stroke delirium should be considered not only a complication but also an important determinant of nursing workload, with implications for nurse staffing, workforce planning and the resource allocation in stroke units.

IMPACT: Although the clinical and prognostic impact of a post-stroke delirium is well understood, its consequences for nursing workload are not. Our findings, based on routine data, are applicable to clinical practice and relevant for nurse staffing planning as well as future health services research.

REPORTING METHOD: This study follows the RECORD extension of the STROBE statement.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct or reporting.

REGISTRATION: The study was prospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register: DRKS00032136 on 27 June 2023.

articles.title: Robot-assisted vs open inferior vena cava thrombectomy: a comparative analysis of perioperative and oncological outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the perioperative and oncological outcomes between open inferior vena cava (IVC) thrombectomy (OP-IVCT) and robot-assisted IVCT (RA-IVCT) for renal tumours with Mayo levels I-IV IVC thrombi.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent radical nephrectomy with IVCT between January 2006 and December 2023 at a high-volume centre. The patients were stratified according to the surgical approach (OP-IVCT vs RA-IVCT). Primary analysis was performed in the full cohort using multivariable regression models, with surgical approach as a covariate. The key perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, disease-free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Propensity score matching (PSM) at a one-to-one ratio was performed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Of the 226 patients, 37 underwent OP-IVCT and 189 underwent RA-IVCT. In the full-cohort multivariable analyses, RA-IVCT was independently associated with lower estimated blood loss (adjusted ratio 0.472, P < 0.001), shorter postoperative hospital stay (adjusted ratio 0.798, P = 0.027), reduced intraoperative transfusion (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.065, P = 0.002), and fewer postoperative complications (adjusted OR 0.162, P = 0.007). The operative time and intensive care unit transfer did not differ significantly between the groups. The surgical approach was not independently associated with OS (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.019, P = 0.969) or DFS (adjusted HR 0.782, P = 0.528). After PSM, 37 matched pairs were analysed. The matched analysis confirmed lower estimated blood loss, reduced transfusion requirement, shorter hospital stay, and fewer postoperative complications with RA-IVCT, whereas OS and DFS remained statistically comparable between the groups.

CONCLUSION: RA-IVCT is a safe and effective alternative to OP-IVCT for patients with renal tumours and IVC tumour thrombi. No evidence of inferior intermediate-term oncological outcomes was observed for RA-IVCT.

articles.title: Bridging Evidence and Practice: Recent Advances in Hypothyroidism Management during Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.abstract: Deficiency of thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine and triiodothyronine, results in the clinical condition known as hypothyroidism, a prevalent endocrine disorder globally, particularly in women of childbearing age. Dynamic changes occur in thyroid function during pregnancy to provide adequate levels of thyroid hormones to the mother and the fetus. Hashimoto thyroiditis remains the most widespread reason for gestational hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and in mildly iodine deficient populations. Iodine plays a vital role in the synthesis and regulation of thyroid hormones; therefore, during pregnancy, iodine consumption must be increased by 50% to produce the required amount of maternal thyroid hormones and meet the increased demand of the developing fetus. Evidence-based studies have shown that even minor alteration in maternal thyroid function can cause pregnancy-related complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes (e.g. miscarriage, perinatal death, pre-eclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, low birth weight and postpartum hemorrhage). Therefore, the timely assessment and appropriate management of gestational hypothyroidism is crucial to ensure optimal maternal and fetal outcomes. Levothyroxine remains the standard treatment for hypothyroidism, significantly reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with hypothyroidism. The present review provides an update on the diagnosis and management of hypothyroidism in pregnant women, highlighting the different types, causes, signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism, and the obstetric outcomes of each type of hypothyroidism along with the treatment strategy. Current key recommendations based on clinical evidence by health practitioners are also provided to assist in planning and choosing the individualized treatment regimen for patients with hypothyroidism before and during pregnancy.

articles.title: Association of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Use with Laboratory- and Anthropometry-Derived Indices of Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors lower body weight, and their association with liver steatosis and fibrosis scores in routine practice is uncertain. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 493 adults with type 2 diabetes of at least 5 years' duration at a tertiary hospital in Türkiye. Of these, 268 adults initiated a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) and used it regularly for at least 6 months, and 225 adults continued other therapies. All patients underwent liver ultrasonography. We compared 6-month changes in the hepatic steatosis index, the visceral adiposity index, the triglyceride-glucose index, the fibrosis-4 index and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index. Analyses used regression with prespecified clinical covariates, inverse probability weighting and propensity score matching. The hepatic steatosis index fell more in the inhibitor group (adjusted difference: -0.69, 95% confidence interval: -1.13 to -0.25, p=0.002; weighting: -0.73; matching: -0.61). The body weight fell by 2.26 kg more (95% confidence interval: -2.70 to -1.83). The ratio of alanine to aspartate aminotransferase did not differ between groups. After adding the change in body weight to the model, the difference in the hepatic steatosis index disappeared (0.12, 95% confidence interval: -0.35 to 0.58). The fibrosis-4 index was slightly lower in the inhibitor group (adjusted difference: -0.13, 95% confidence interval: -0.19 to -0.08), whereas the other three indices did not differ clearly after adjustment. In this cohort, the lower hepatic steatosis index with these drugs reflects weight loss, and the index gives little separate information on liver fat.

articles.title: Harmonising difficult-to-manage and complex-to-manage psoriatic arthritis: from divergent prevalence estimates to reproducible, mechanism-aware phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Difficult-to-manage or complex-to-manage psoriatic arthritis is increasingly recognised in clinical practice, but prevalence estimates remain difficult to interpret because studies differ in denominators, definitions of treatment failure, and methods for distinguishing persistent symptoms from objective inflammation. Building on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology difficult-to-manage definition and the Group for Research and Assessment of Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis complex-to-manage definition, this Viewpoint proposes an implementation framework to improve reproducibility across registries, trials, and translational studies. We recommend dual-denominator reporting, with estimates presented both in all patients with psoriatic arthritis and in patients exposed to biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. We also propose an auditable treatment ledger documenting drug mechanism and class, adequacy of exposure, optimisation attempts, and reasons for discontinuation. After treatment-pathway difficulty is established, patients should be stratified by dominant drivers of persistent burden: inflammatory, non-inflammatory, or mixed. Domain-specific description, impact profiling, disease duration, and prespecified sensitivity analyses should improve comparability and interpretation.

articles.title: A consensus to stall on biodiversity.
Brain health in children born extremely preterm: a multidimensional perspective.
articles.abstract: Gestational age and developmental stage of the brain at birth are major determinants of child health, and long-term consequences of preterm birth and altered brain maturation are inadequately understood simply through brain injury, survival rates, or diagnostic labels. In this Review, we conceptualise brain health in children born extremely preterm (before 28 weeks' gestation) as a developmental condition shaped by maturational timing, biological vulnerability, neonatal intensive care exposure, sensory and relational experiences, family circumstances, and social environments. We integrate evidence from research on early brain development and consciousness, long-term multidomain neurodevelopmental outcomes, neonatal intensive care practice, relational caregiving, early developmental interventions, and ethical, psychological, and social dimensions of care. Across these domains, extremely preterm birth emerges not as a single event but as a neuroplastic system that adapts to biological and environmental risks and protective factors that shape neurodevelopmental resilience and vulnerabilities and establish developmental trajectories. We argue that care for the infant born extremely preterm is optimised through a brain-health framework where care becomes a longitudinal, ethical process that integrates family support, minimises harmful exposures, promotes adaptive development, and fosters participation, wellbeing, and quality of life.

articles.title: Community health worker-led hypertension management with independent prescribing in rural Lesotho: a cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is the leading global risk factor for premature mortality, yet treatment coverage and control remain poor, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Whether community health workers can manage hypertension, including independent prescribing and titrating of antihypertensive therapy, remains unknown. We aimed to assess whether hypertension care led by community health workers with independent prescribing was non-inferior to usual facility-based care for maintaining blood pressure control among adults with treated, controlled hypertension.

METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, cluster-randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial in 103 villages in rural Lesotho. Adults with treated, controlled hypertension (<140/90 mm Hg) were eligible. Villages were randomly assigned 1:1, stratified by district and access to health facility, by an independent statistician using a computer-generated sequence to hypertension care led by community health workers, including independent prescribing and titrating of antihypertensive therapy (amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide combination pills at doses of 5 mg amlodipine and 12·5 mg hydrochlorothiazide or 10 mg amlodipine and 25 mg hydrochlorothiazide) with clinical decision support, or to usual nurse-led, facility-based care. The primary endpoint was blood pressure control at 12 months among all randomised participants except individuals who became pregnant during follow-up, with a non-inferiority margin of -10 percentage points absolute risk difference. The study has been completed and is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05684055).

FINDINGS: Between Sept 8, 2023, and May 31, 2024, we enrolled 807 participants (417 in 51 control villages, 390 in 50 intervention villages; two empty clusters; mean age 64·4 years [SD 14·3]; 82% female). At 12 months, blood pressure was controlled in 300 (78%) of 386 participants in the intervention group and 303 (74%) of 412 in the control group (adjusted odds ratio 1·29, 95% CI 0·93-1·80); non-inferiority was met. The adjusted absolute risk difference was 5·1% (95% CI -0·9 to 11·2). Serious adverse events (deaths and hospitalisations) were similar in the two groups, with no excess events attributed to the intervention.

INTERPRETATION: These findings support community-based hypertension care with task-sharing to trained community health workers as a promising approach to maintaining blood pressure control, especially in settings with limited access to physician-led and nurse-led hypertension care.

FUNDING: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, World Diabetes Foundation, and Swiss National Science Foundation.

articles.title: Cangrelor for myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock.
One class, different indications: Factor XIa inhibition after LIBREXIA-ACS.
articles.abstract: LIBREXIA-ACS was terminated early for futility. Milvexian, added to antiplatelet therapy after acute coronary syndrome, did not reduce cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke, but did not increase intracranial or fatal bleeding. The contribution of factor XI to arterial thrombosis may vary across clinical indications, while the specific factor XIa inhibitor, dose, and patient selection remain to be optimized.

articles.title: Integrative analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation and gene expression profiles associated with incident chronic kidney disease: the longitudinal Pros-RODAM cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasing rapidly in African populations, yet its molecular determinants remain poorly characterised. While epigenome-wide studies have been largely confined to high-income settings, comparable longitudinal epigenetic data from African populations are scarce, despite distinct genetic and environmental contexts. We conducted a longitudinal epigenome-wide study of CKD in an African population, integrating DNA methylation and gene expression to identify epigenetic changes associated with CKD and related kidney function decline.

METHODS: DNA methylation was profiled using the Illumina EPIC (850K) array in 274 Ghanaian participants from the RODAM-Prospective cohort (92 incident CKD cases and 182 matched controls), providing 548 DNA methylation observations across baseline and ∼6-year follow-up, with high-quality DNA methylation data available at both timepoints. Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) were performed for incident CKD, change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (ΔeGFR), and change in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ΔACR), adjusting for demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. Differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified using bumphunter with family-wise error rate control. Differential gene expression (RNA-seq) analyses were conducted, followed by covariate-adjusted expression quantitative trait methylation (eQTM) analyses to link methylation with gene expression.

FINDINGS: At baseline, significant differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were detected at INF2 (incident CKD), CLIP4 (ΔeGFR), and TMEM109 (ΔACR), alongside DMRs at HLA-DPB1 and SH2D1B (incident CKD) and ZFP57 and OR2T11 (ΔACR). At follow-up, a progression-related DMR in C4orf39/TRIM61 (ΔACR) was identified, with recurrent signals at hypermethylated HLA-DPB1 and hypomethylated ZFP57 and OR2T11 across timepoints. Integrative eQTM analysis revealed methylation-expression associations at recurrent loci including ZFP57, HLA-DRB5, SLC39A4, and SPATC1L, with predominantly inverse associations at ZFP57, HLA-DRB5, and SLC39A4, highlighting associations with metabolic and immune regulatory pathways.

INTERPRETATION: We identified epigenetic changes associated with incident CKD and kidney function decline in an African population. These methylation signals, supported by gene expression patterns, highlight immune and kidney-related pathways associated with CKD risk and progression. Our findings provide a foundation for future studies investigating the potential of epigenetic markers in CKD risk stratification and prevention in African populations.

FUNDING: European Commission; European Research Council.

articles.title: Red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio is associated with 28-day mortality and 24-h red blood cell transfusion in sepsis: A MIMIC-IV study with external assessment in an independent cohort.
articles.journal: Revista de investigacion clinica; organo del Hospital de Enfermedades de la Nutricion
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) is a potential biomarker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, but its association with mortality and early red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in sepsis remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults with Sepsis-3 in the MIMIC-IV database. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was RBC transfusion within 24h of ICU admission. LASSO-selected predictors were used to develop multiple machine-learning models. Temporal sensitivity analyses used pre-transfusion measurements for transfusion and a 24-h landmark framework for mortality.

RESULTS: Among 25,518 patients, RAR was associated with 28-day mortality (OR=1.246, 95% CI: 1.223-1.270) and 24-h RBC transfusion (OR=1.208, 95% CI: 1.187-1.230; both P<0.001). XGBoost showed the highest discrimination for mortality (AUC=0.763) and transfusion (AUC=0.766). SHAP analysis identified RAR as an important contributor to model predictions.

CONCLUSIONS: RAR is a readily available biomarker associated with 28-day mortality and early RBC transfusion in sepsis and may support outcome-specific risk assessment.

articles.title: Inflammatory response of human kidney tubular cells to palmitic acid complexed with control or glycated albumin.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dyslipidemia and hyperglycemia, along with the formation of Advanced Glycation End products (AGEs), contribute to the development of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD), increasing the likelihood of requiring renal replacement therapies and reducing lifespan. The effects of increasing concentrations of Palmitic Acid (PA) complexed with Control (C) or AGE-albumin with or without LPS challenge on inflammatory response in Human Renal Tubular Cells (HK-2) were evaluated.

METHODS: AGE-albumin was prepared by incubation with glycolaldehyde, while C-albumin was prepared with phosphate buffer. C and AGE-albumin were complexed with PA (0.1, 0.25, and 0.5 mM) and incubated with HK-2 cells for 48 h. Afterwards, the cells were exposed to either the absence or presence of lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 1 µg/mL) for an additional 24 h. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1beta) levels were measured using ELISA, and cytotoxicity was assessed by lactate dehydrogenase release.

RESULTS: Total AGEs and pentosidine were 6.5-fold and 2.6-fold higher, respectively, in AGE-albumin compared to C-albumin. PA increases the dose-dependent secretion of IL-1 beta, with a significant interaction effect with LPS, while decreasing IL-6 secretion.

CONCLUSION: PA complexed with either C-albumin or AGE-albumin, at an FFA: albumin molar ratio (7.5:1) approximating pathological conditions, together with LPS, promotes IL-1beta secretion, reinforcing the convergence between lipid overload and innate immune activation in the progression of DKD.

articles.title: Image interpretation performance among pre-registration diagnostic radiography students in Ghana: A cross-institutional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preliminary image evaluation (PIE) supports timely clinical decision-making, yet little is known about the preparedness of pre-registration diagnostic radiography students for this role. This study assessed image interpretation performance of final-year diagnostic radiography students in Ghana.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study involving 80 final-year diagnostic radiography students across three tertiary training institutions in Ghana was conducted. Participants completed a supervised 60-image interpretation test comprising chest (n = 22), axial skeleton (n = 16) and appendicular skeleton (n = 22) radiographs at their respective institutions' computer laboratories. Responses were assessed against an established reference standard. Descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis H and post-hoc tests, were used to compare performance across institutions.

RESULTS: Mean overall image interpretation test scores were 81.8% (SE: 0.84), 70.0% (SE: 1.67) and 84.6% (SE: 0.92) for Institutions X, Y and Z, respectively. Corresponding mean diagnostic classification accuracy was 88.6% (SE: 0.71), 79.4% (SE: 1.41) and 88.8% (SE: 0.78). Overall, 82.5% (66/80) achieved ≥80% diagnostic classification accuracy. Mean sensitivity was 88.4% (SE: 1.04), 83.0% (SE: 2.2) and 93.4% (SE: 1.1), while mean specificity was 88.7% (SE: 1.1), 77.0% (SE: 2.5) and 85.3% (SE: 1.5), respectively. Performance differed significantly across institutions (p < 0.05), with Institutions X and Z generally demonstrating stronger performance than Institution Y. Self-perceived image interpretation ability correlated moderately with overall test performance (r = 0.46, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Final-year diagnostic radiography students in Ghana demonstrated encouraging image interpretation performance, although substantial inter-institutional variation was evident.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Greater consistency in pre-registration image interpretation education may strengthen graduates' foundational skills for potential future involvement in PIE.

articles.title: Determinants of climate change anxiety in older adults: Maladaptation, death anxiety, and depression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change is associated with a range of physical and psychological health concerns, and some older adults may be particularly affected because of health-related, functional, social, and socioeconomic factors. However, the psychological and contextual factors associated with climate change anxiety among older adults remain insufficiently understood.

AIMS: This study aimed to examine the associations of adaptation difficulty, death anxiety, and depression with climate change anxiety among older adults and to identify psychological, sociodemographic, family-related, and health-related factors independently associated with climate change anxiety.

METHOD: This descriptive, correlational, and cross-sectional study included 350 older adults. Data were collected using the "Personal Information Form," "Climate Change Anxiety Scale," "Assessment Scale of Adaptation Difficulty for the Elderly", "Death Anxiety Scale," and "Geriatric Depression Scale.". Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, correlation tests, and multiple regression analyses to identify significant predictors.

RESULTS: Climate change anxiety scores were significantly higher among women, married individuals, and those with lower perceived income. Adaptation difficulty, death anxiety, and depression were independently associated with climate change anxiety. Together with sociodemographic, family-related, and health-related characteristics, these variables explained 50% of the variance in climate change anxiety.

CONCLUSION: Climate change anxiety among older adults was associated with adaptation difficulty, death anxiety, depression, and relevant sociodemographic and health-related characteristics. These factors should be considered when assessing climate-related psychological responses among older adults. Because of the cross-sectional design, the findings do not establish causality or directionality.

articles.title: The role of rubber and label disruptors in the re-processing of polyester from PET-rich textile Wastes.
articles.abstract: From a global perspective, the share of post-consumer textile waste subjected to recycling amounts to a mere 0.5 %, whereas most textile waste ends up in landfills or incineration. Often this is the consequence of apparel being composed of fiber blends, e.g. cotton/polyester. Recycling of such mixed textile waste at their end-of-life is challenging because of elementary differences in the structure and chemical properties of the constituents. Moreover, small fractions of impurities and contaminants as well as residues from the other fiber type(s), have commonly to be accepted to some extent. In particular, minor elements of apparel, for instance labels or rubber bands, can usually not be completely removed with reasonable effort because of chemical similarities with the main textile fibers. Consequently, during re-processing and compounding of recovered polymers, such elements and disruptors are inevitably present and are hypothesized to play a major role in the mechanical performance of recycled polymers. In this study the impact of potential disruptors commonly present in mixed fiber waste, in particular labels and rubber bands, on the mechanical performance of recovered polymers was investigated. Model formulations of polyester obtained from PET-rich waste streams with known fractions of disruptors were thermo-mechanically re-processed on a conical, co-rotating laboratory scale twin screw extruder and their mechanical properties characterized. Whereas labels had only a small impact on the mechanical performance of recovered polyester, rubber present during extrusion caused a decrease in tensile strength by more than 40 % from 63 to 36 MPa. This was assigned to degradation processes taking place in-situ at processing temperatures, resulting in chain scission and influencing the crystallization behavior.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with and without a lateral extra-articular procedure: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (R-ACLR) has less favorable outcomes than primary reconstruction. Earlier revision-specific meta-analyses included eight and ten comparative studies. The clinical value of adding a lateral extra-articular procedure (LEAP) remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes after R-ACLR performed with versus without LEAP augmentation.

EVIDENCE REVIEW: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2006, to April 30, 2026. Comparative studies reporting clinical follow-up of at least 24 months were eligible; the randomized trial also supplied objective stability measurements at 1 year. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated function, stability, failure or rerevision, and return to activity. Methodological quality and certainty were assessed using the Downs and Black checklist and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework.

FINDINGS: Fourteen studies included 1134 patients (559 with LEAP and 575 with isolated R-ACLR). The failure analysis included 11 studies and 1023 patients: 29/517 versus 69/506 events (risk ratio [RR], 0.44; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.29-0.68; P < 0.001; I2 = 3.9%). Certainty in this combined estimate was very low. LEAP augmentation was associated with less anterior laxity (Hedges' g, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.21-0.71) and fewer positive pivot shifts (RR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.30-0.87). The subjective International Knee Documentation Committee score difference was small (mean difference, 2.91; 95% CI, 0.23-5.59). Return to any sport was informed by only two studies and 87 patients (RR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.92-1.32; P = 0.278).

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: LEAP augmentation was associated with lower observed failure or rerevision risk and greater postoperative stability. Patient-reported differences were small and inconsistent. Predominantly nonrandomized evidence and very low certainty in the combined estimates limit causal inference and subgroup recommendations.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

REGISTRATION: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews, CRD420261441628.

articles.title: Focused shock wave therapy improves histological scores for acute osteochondral defects in a skeletally immature porcine knee model.
articles.journal: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) of the capitellum presents a clinical challenge in preadolescent and adolescent athletes. Although debridement is effective, residual defects remain a persistent concern, typically resulting in inferior fibrocartilage rather than hyaline cartilage, despite the high intrinsic repair potential of cartilage in skeletally immature patients. Focused shock wave therapy (FSWT) shows promise in small animal models of osteochondral defects, but its efficacy in a clinically relevant, skeletally immature large animal model remains unknown. This study evaluated the effect of a single FSWT application on acute osteochondral defects intended to represent postdebridement tissue loss in a skeletally immature porcine knee model.

METHODS: Bilateral medial femoral condyle osteochondral defects (5-mm diameter, 7-mm depth) were created in seven 6-week-old pigs. Right knees received a single FSWT application (2500 impulses, 0.20 mJ/mm2) directly to the defect immediately after its creation, and left knees served as untreated controls. At 6 weeks, evaluations included Goebel macroscopic and Niederauer histological scores, immunofluorescence analysis (SOX9, aggrecan, and COL2A1), and computed tomography to assess premature physeal closure.

RESULTS: There was no statistically significant difference in the median Goebel macroscopic score between the FSWT and control groups (5.5 [interquartile range {IQR}, 3.5, 7.8] vs. 8.5 [IQR, 4.0, 9.0], lower is better; P = 0.397). The median Niederauer histological score was statistically significantly higher in the FSWT group (14.0 [13.3, 14.7] vs. 13.0 [11.3, 13.5]; P = 0.042). Immunofluorescence showed that the median percentage of SOX9-positive cells was statistically significantly greater in the FSWT group (20.1% [12.4, 22.3] vs. 11.6% [7.4, 18.4]; P = 0.018), as was the median aggrecan-positive immunoreactive fraction (15.2% [7.1, 18.5] vs. 7.1% [6.9, 10.7]; P = 0.028). The median COL2A1-positive immunoreactive fraction showed no statistically significant difference (4.0% [3.1, 7.8] vs. 2.8% [2.4, 4.9]; P = 0.499). No premature epiphyseal closure was observed at 6 weeks.

CONCLUSION: A single FSWT application improved the 6-week histological repair of an acute osteochondral defect in a skeletally immature porcine model. This improvement was accompanied by statistically significant increases in the percentage of SOX9-positive cells and the aggrecan-positive immunoreactive fraction. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of FSWT.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Not Applicable, controlled laboratory study.

articles.title: Nutrient-sensing nuclear receptors: VDR and RAR as immune integrators in allergic and autoimmune diseases.
articles.abstract: Nuclear receptors (NRs) translate environmental and metabolic cues into transcriptional programs that calibrate immune responses. In the NR superfamily, the vitamin D receptor (VDR) and retinoic acid receptors (RARs) occupy distinctive position as vitamin-derived ligand sensors, signal as obligate heterodimers with the retinoid X receptor (RXR), and both shape T cell fate, mucosal tolerance, and epithelial barrier integrity. Dysregulation of either pathway has been mechanistically linked toward varying degree of pathophysiology of allergic asthma, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), multiple sclerosis (MS), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This review synthesizes current understanding of how VDR and RAR signaling regulate effector and regulatory T cell programs, macrophage polarization, and epithelial homeostasis in allergic and autoimmune inflammation. We examine receptor-specific transcriptional mechanisms, the immunological consequences of common VDR polymorphisms, and the therapeutic landscape spanning calcitriol analogues, non-secosteroidal VDR modulators, and retinoic acid-based interventions. We also highlight points of convergence between VDR and RAR signaling that suggest combinatorial therapeutic potential. By integrating mechanistic, genetic, and translational evidence, we propose that VDR and RAR function as nutrient-sensing immune integrators whose pharmacological modulation offers a precision route to recalibrating inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: Delayed surgery can be considered for cardiovascularly stable dogs with hemoperitoneum due to a ruptured splenic mass.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the timing of surgery affects morbidity and/or mortality of dogs with hemoperitoneum secondary to a ruptured splenic mass.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, medical records of dogs diagnosed with hemoperitoneum due to a ruptured splenic mass between 2010 and 2023 were reviewed for clinical data. Dogs were classified in the early group (early) if surgery occurred < 6 hours and the delayed group (delayed) if surgery occurred ≥ 6 hours after presentation.

RESULTS: A total of 177 client-owned dogs (99 early, 78 delayed) were included. The median duration of time from admission to surgery was 4.1 hours (range, 2.2 to 5.95 hours) for early and 14.0 hours (range, 6.02 to 68.4 hours) for delayed dogs. Early dogs were more likely to present in hypovolemic shock, have a higher shock index, and receive crystalloid boluses and RBC-containing transfusions preoperatively than delayed dogs. There was no difference in the occurrence of hypotension intraoperatively between groups. Early dogs were more likely to receive an RBC-containing transfusion during and/or after surgery and had longer hospitalization than delayed dogs. Overall survival to discharge was 94.9% (168 of 177); there was no difference between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: There was no difference in mortality based on timing of surgery. Early dogs were more likely to receive RBC-containing transfusions throughout hospitalization and have a longer hospital stay compared to delayed dogs.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Stable dogs may be able to have delayed surgery without increasing morbidity or mortality. Early surgery should be considered for dogs that have ongoing concerns for stability despite medical intervention.

articles.title: Hypertension was common and associated with serum cholesterol concentrations in dogs with Cushing syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of systemic hypertension in dogs with newly diagnosed Cushing syndrome (CS) and evaluate associations with hypothesized hypertension-associated variables.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was performed with dogs diagnosed with CS by ACTH stimulation or low-dose dexamethasone suppression testing at University of Wisconsin Veterinary Care from 2005 to 2025. Dogs with systolic blood pressure (SBP) measured within 8 weeks of diagnosis and before CS or antihypertensive treatment were included. Data included signalment, body condition score, platelet count, select serum biochemistry variables, and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio. Hypertension prevalence and associations between SBP and variables were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 117 dogs with CS, 57 dogs (49%) had SBP measured and met inclusion criteria. With an SBP cutoff ≥ 160 mm Hg, 61.4% of dogs (95% CI, 48.4% to 73.0%) were hypertensive and 26.3% were prehypertensive (SBP of 140 to 159 mm Hg). Median serum cholesterol was higher in hypertensive than nonhypertensive dogs (378.5 vs 287 mg/dL) and positively associated with SBP (OR, 1.10/10 mg/dL; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.21). Serum potassium was lower in hypertensive dogs than nonhypertensive dogs (4.4 vs 4.85 mmol/L). No significant associations were identified for urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, platelet count, age, or body condition score.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension was common in dogs with CS, yet SBP was not consistently measured at diagnosis. Serum cholesterol was associated with hypertension, and lower serum potassium concentrations were observed in hypertensive dogs.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Routine SBP assessment is warranted in dogs with CS. Cholesterol and potassium regulation may be affected in dogs with CS.

articles.title: A simple algorithm allows triaging of dogs with mitral valve disease into cardiac or noncardiac causes of dyspnea.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To create a simple algorithm for diagnosis of congestive heart failure (CHF) in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD).

METHODS: Data were collected between November 2, 2015, and December 7, 2017, from dogs presented to investigators after a tentative diagnosis of CHF by first-opinion clinicians. Investigators completed a data-submission form and provided a final diagnosis of CHF or subclinical MMVD. Data included each of the 8 variables of the original algorithm. Variables that did not change diagnostic accuracy were removed from the model.

RESULTS: 120 dogs were included: 46 with CHF and 74 with subclinical cardiac disease and an alternate diagnosis for clinical signs; 82 dogs (36 with CHF) were referred for coughing. All dogs with CHF had loud or palpable murmurs, as did 59 without CHF. Forty-five dogs with CHF and 26 without CHF lacked sinus arrhythmia. All nonpanting dogs with CHF and 7 of 56 without CHF had tachypnea or dyspnea. All dogs with CHF had moderate-to-severe left atrial enlargement versus 25 of 35 dogs without CHF. Examined in series, these 4 variables yielded an algorithm sensitivity of 98% and specificity of 95% for diagnosing CHF.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians who are presented with a dog suspected of having CHF secondary to MMVD should be able to determine whether CHF is likely using 3 to 4 simple variables: a loud or palpable murmur, lack of sinus arrhythmia, tachypnea or dyspnea, and at least moderate left atrial enlargement.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This algorithm might improve first-opinion practitioners' diagnosis of CHF in dogs with MMVD.

articles.title: Novel Point-of-Care Seismocardiographic Biomarkers for Discrimination of Severe Aortic Stenosis from Cardiac Controls.
Anemia and Iron Deficiency Across Renal Function in Hospitalized Heart Failure: Insights From OPPORTUNITIES Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for heart failure (HHF). Their prognostic contributions in the acute setting, particularly across kidney function, remain incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVES: We investigated the association of anemia, transferrin saturation (TSAT), and ID according to kidney function, with postdischarge outcomes in HHF patients.

METHODS: Consecutive HHF patients enrolled in the OPPORTUNITIES registry with available hemoglobin and TSAT at discharge. The primary endpoint was HF-free survival, a composite of all-cause death, urgent heart transplantation, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and urgent emergency department referral for HF worsening at 12 months. Adjusted Cox regression models were applied.

RESULTS: A total of 454 HHF patients were included. The median age was 77 (69-83); 37.9% were women, and 55% of patients were anemic. Anemic patients were older and exhibited a greater burden of comorbidities. Hemoglobin and TSAT showed a modest positive correlation overall (rho = 0.276, P < 0.001), which disappeared in patients with estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with a higher risk (adjusted HR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.75-0.91; P < 0.001), whereas TSAT was not independently predictive. A significant interaction between hemoglobin and renal function was observed (P = 0.025), indicating that the hemoglobin effect varied according to kidney function. Among ID definitions, only TSAT <20% independently identified patients at an increased risk (HR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.03-2.03; P = 0.035).

CONCLUSIONS: In HHF patients, the prognostic relevance of anemia varies according to renal function. TSAT <20% was the only ID definition independently associated with adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Impact of the 2026 Dyslipidemia Guideline on ASCVD Reclassification and Statin Recommendations in MESA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology (ACC)/American Heart Association (AHA)/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia recommends the use of the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs) equations to predict atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk while concurrently revising previous risk-category thresholds. The impact of these reclassifications is yet to be described.

OBJECTIVES: The authors characterized ASCVD reclassification and statin recommendations under the 2026 guideline, evaluated clinical events under this reclassification, and examined risk enhancement with risk enhancers and coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden.

METHODS: Adults (N = 6,098) from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) were assessed, comparing the Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and 2013 thresholds to PREVENT with 2026 thresholds. We evaluated the degree of directional reclassification, impact on statin recommendations, and risk enhancement with biomarkers and CAC burden.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 10 years, 6.0% of participants had an ASCVD event. PREVENT reclassified 16.4% to a lower and 13.1% to a higher risk category as compared to the PCE. The statin recommendation under PREVENT was 50.4% compared to 55.2% under PCE. Of those who were no longer recommended for statin use, 4.9% went on to have an event. Individuals who were reclassified downward but had elevated CAC or any risk-enhancing factors had a higher event rate.

CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to the 2026 guideline may lead to a small net downward reclassification of predicted ASCVD risk. Statin recommendations will fall modestly, however, not accompanied by a substantial number of subsequent events. Risk enhancers and elevated CAC identify higher risk subgroups than their PREVENT risk would suggest, emphasizing their supporting role in risk prediction.

articles.title: Association of Site Volume and MitraClip Outcomes in Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: The COAPT PAS Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The number of sites performing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) has increased. Despite concerns that low-volume sites may have worse outcomes, data are limited on the association between site volume and TEER outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the association between site volume and mitral TEER outcomes in SMR.

METHODS: The COAPT PAS (COAPT Post-Approval Study) included patients with SMR who underwent TEER with the MitraClip device from March 2019 to September 2020 following Food and Drug Administration approval. Sites were categorized by number of patients treated: low (≤25), medium (25-50), and high (>50).

RESULTS: Of 5,000 patients, 2,632 were from low-, 1,527 from medium-, and 841 from high-volume sites. High-volume sites treated sicker patients with higher Society of Thoracic Surgeons scores and prior heart failure hospitalization rates. Procedures at low-volume sites had similar device implant rates (low: 97%, medium: 99%, high: 98%), used fewer number of clips (low: 1.4 ± 0.6, medium: 1.5 ± 0.6, high: 1.6 ± 0.7 clips, P < 0.001), and had longer device (low: 68 ± 55, medium: 56 ± 53, high: 57 ± 42 min, P < 0.001) and procedure times (low: 153 ± 67, medium: 131 ± 59, high: 128 ± 56 min, P < 0.001). Technical success was comparable (low: 93%, medium: 94%, high: 95%, P = 0.92). MR reduction to ≤2+ and ≤1+ was also similar. There was no difference in heart failure hospitalization (low: 19%, medium: 18%, high: 20%, P = 0.50) or all-cause mortality (low: 23%, medium: 21%, high: 20%, P = 0.27).

CONCLUSIONS: Technical success, MR reduction, and 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable across volume strata during the early adoption phase, without significant differences between low- and high-volume centers.

articles.title: Antimicrobial stewardship in critical care: Applying PK/PD and optimised antimicrobial dosing to improve care.
articles.abstract: Life-threatening infections are common in critically ill patients and remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) aims to optimise antimicrobial use by balancing effective treatment with minimising toxicity, resistance and unnecessary exposure. This review examines AMS in critical care with a focus on antimicrobial dose optimisation. Core AMS principles in the ICU include diagnostic stewardship, appropriate antimicrobial initiation, de-escalation and treatment duration. Dose optimisation is fundamental but challenging because critical illness causes profound and dynamic changes in pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD). These alterations result in marked interpatient variability and increase the risk of subtherapeutic or toxic drug exposure. Understanding key PK parameters, including volume of distribution, clearance and half-life, together with PD targets such as Cmax/MIC, fT > MIC and AUC0-24/MIC is essential for individualising therapy. Factors including sepsis, organ dysfunction, augmented renal clearance and extracorporeal support can substantially alter antimicrobial exposure and dosing requirements. Strategies to improve target attainment include loading doses, prolonged infusions, therapeutic drug monitoring and model-informed precision dosing, although implementation may be limited by local resources. Integrating PK/PD-informed dosing into routine ICU practice can improve clinical outcomes, reduce toxicity and strengthen AMS in critically ill populations.

articles.title: The association between normal capillary refill time and 28-day mortality in septic shock patients subjected to early hemodynamic resuscitation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Capillary refill time (CRT)-guided resuscitation improves outcomes in septic shock by targeting abnormal CRT. However, whether a normal baseline CRT, resulting in no additional attempts to optimize hemodynamics, is associated with mortality remains unclear. We evaluated the association between normal baseline CRT and 28-day mortality in patients with septic shock undergoing protocolized resuscitation.

METHODS: This post-hoc analysis included all randomized patients from the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK 1 and 2 trials. CRT was classified as normal (≤3 s) or abnormal (>3 s). The primary outcome was 28-day mortality, analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression and reported as hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Secondary outcomes included ICU and hospital length of stay and 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: Among 1885 patients, 691 (36.7%) had normal baseline CRT. Despite normal CRT, many had abnormal hemodynamic features: 335 (48.5%) had heart rate > 100/min, 258 (37.3%) systolic arterial pressure < 100 mmHg, 152 (22.0%) mean arterial pressure < 65 mmHg, 157 (22.7%) diastolic arterial pressure < 50 mmHg, and 683 (98.8%) lactate >2 mmol/L. Patients with normal baseline CRT had significantly lower 28-day mortality than those with abnormal CRT (21.1% vs. 34.3%; HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.50-0.74; p < 0.001) similarly for 90-day mortality (25.9% versus 40.6%; HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.52-0.73; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK trials, normal baseline CRT was associated with significantly lower 28- and 90-day mortality, although mortality remained still quite high. Further research should investigate how treatment of septic shock patients with normal CRT can be improved.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The ANDROMEDA-SHOCK 1 trial: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03078712 (study start at: 2017-03-01). The ANDROMEDA-SHOCK 2 trial: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05057611 (study start at: 2022-03-18).

articles.title: Prognostic value of the lactate-to-albumin ratio for mortality in patients with sepsis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) has emerged as a promising prognostic biomarker; however, its performance across different mortality outcomes has not been comprehensively evaluated.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, four databases were searched, and the protocol was preregistered on PROSPERO (CRD420261381173). Prognostic outcomes were pooled as hazard ratios (HRs) and odds ratios (ORs). Discriminative performance was assessed by pooling area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.

RESULTS: 23 studies involving 9838 patients were included. Elevated LAR was associated with increased ICU mortality (HR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.02-1.51; p = 0.04; I2 = 0.02% and OR = 2.52; 95% CI: 1.10-5.76; p = 0.03; I2 = 76.08%) and overall mortality (OR = 2.25; 95% CI: 1.72-2.95; p < 0.01; I2 = 0%). Pooled AUCs were 0.76 (95% CI 0.66-0.83; p < 0.01; I2 = 90%) for 28-day mortality, 0.79 (95% CI 0.60-0.90; p = 0.01; I2 = 95.3%) for ICU mortality, and 0.82 (95% CI 0.59-0.94; p = 0.02; I2 = 95%) for in-hospital mortality.

CONCLUSION: Elevated LAR is associated with increased mortality and demonstrated moderate-to-good discriminative performance across multiple mortality outcomes in sepsis. Given its simplicity, low cost, and widespread availability, LAR may serve as a useful adjunct for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Resuscitation strategies incorporating peripheral perfusion targets in septic shock: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Resuscitation strategies incorporating peripheral perfusion targets (RSIPPT) have emerged as promising tools in septic shock. However, whether they improve clinically relevant outcomes remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate whether these strategies reduce 28/30-day mortality and improve other clinical outcomes compared with usual care.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) using a random-effects model was conducted. Electronic searches of PubMed, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were performed through May 27, 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261400115). The RoB 2 and GRADE tools were used for assessment of risk of bias and certainty of evidence (CoE), respectively.

RESULTS: Five RCTs involving 2180 patients with septic shock were included. Compared with conventional strategies, RSIPPT were not associated with significant differences in 28/30-day mortality (four RCTs; RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78-1.09; I2 = 10%; moderate CoE) or 90-day mortality (three RCTs; RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.83-1.05; I2 = 0%; low CoE). However, RSIPPT were associated with fluid reduction during the first 6-8 h of resuscitation (three RCTs; MD -264.53 mL, 95% CI -425.28 to -103.77; I2 = 1%; low CoE). No significant differences were observed in intensive care unit or hospital length of stay, organ dysfunction, vasopressor-free days, ventilator-free days, or renal replacement therapy-free days.

CONCLUSION: In early septic shock, RSIPPT were associated with a modest reduction in resuscitation fluid during the first 6-8 h. A mortality reduction was not demonstrated, although clinically important benefit or harm cannot be excluded. Differences in intervention algorithms and comparators limit attribution of these findings to peripheral perfusion monitoring itself.

articles.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for ICU pharmacotherapy training: Supporting learning while preserving clinical judgment.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in critical care practice at a time when pharmacotherapeutic decisions are becoming more complex, data-intensive, and time-sensitive. For medical residents and fellows, this creates both educational opportunities and challenges, as AI may support learning but must not replace the development of independent clinical judgment. This perspective examines potential applications of AI in ICU pharmacotherapy training, including support for just-in-time learning, case-based practice, and bedside decision support. Key limitations and risks, such as misinformation, cognitive offloading, deskilling, privacy and data security, and bias in model outputs, are discussed along with possible mitigation strategies. Future training should prioritize building competencies related to AI-assisted clinical decision-making, including critical appraisal of AI-generated outputs and communication of AI-informed decisions within interprofessional teams. AI-supported pharmacotherapy training should be guided by clear boundaries around use and continued emphasis on building foundational pharmacotherapy knowledge, patient-specific reasoning, and clinical judgment.

articles.title: Distinct associations of age, frailty, and comorbidity with AKI occurrence, mortality, and kidney function recovery in older ICU patients: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill older adults, but the associations of chronological age and baseline vulnerability to kidney outcomes remain uncertain. We examined associations of age, frailty, and comorbidity with AKI occurrence, in-hospital mortality, and kidney function recovery. This retrospective cohort included adults aged ≥60 years admitted to six intensive care units at a Brazilian university hospital from 2023 to 2025. AKI followed KDIGO creatinine criteria; frailty was measured by the modified frailty index (MFI) and comorbidity by the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Modified Poisson (AKI occurrence), time-dependent Cox (mortality), and Fine-Gray (kidney function recovery, with death as a competing event) models were used. Among 2387 patients, illness severity and chronic kidney disease prevalence increased with age. AKI developed in 1396 patients (58.5%), rising from 56.2% (60-69 years) to 63.3% (≥80 years); age, MFI (adjusted risk ratio 1.030 per point), and CCI (1.028 per point) were each associated with AKI occurrence. AKI (hazard ratio 3.135, 95% CI 2.585-3.801) and age (1.039 per year) were associated with in-hospital death, whereas MFI and CCI were not after adjustment for acute illness. Of 927 survivors with AKI, 50.2% recovered by discharge. Age was not independently associated with recovery, whereas greater MFI and CCI were associated with lower recovery. Age, frailty, and comorbidity captured distinct dimensions of risk: AKI and age were associated with in-hospital mortality, whereas baseline vulnerability, more than age, was associated with kidney function recovery, supporting frailty and comorbidity assessment in ICU risk stratification.

articles.title: Associations of indoor air per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure in schools with respiratory and skin outcomes in children: Single-pollutant, exposure-response, and mixture analyses.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract: Schools are important but under-characterized microenvironments for children's exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), with potential health implications given children's greater susceptibility. We assessed associations between indoor-air PFAS in schools and respiratory and skin outcomes in children using single-pollutant, dose-response, and mixture-based approaches. Indoor air PFAS were measured in 36 classrooms across 8 primary schools in Porto, Portugal, using passive sampling over 28 days. Health outcomes, including ever asthma, current asthma, wheezing, and eczema, were collected through standardized parent-completed questionnaires. After false discovery rate correction, perfluoropropane sulfonic acid (PFPrS) was associated with higher odds of ever asthma (aOR:1.12; 95%CI:1.04-1.27) and current asthma (aOR:1.26; 95%CI:1.06-1.50), whereas perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) was associated with lower odds of both ever (aOR:0.80; 95%CI:0.54-0.98) and current asthma (aOR:0.66; 95%CI:0.36-0.89). Perfluorobutane sulfonic acid (PFBS; aOR:1.19; 95%CI:1.03-1.35) and 6:2 fluorotelomer acrylate (6:2 FTAcr; aOR:1.18; 95%CI:1.01-1.38) were associated with higher odds of wheezing, while 8:2 fluorotelomer alcohol (8:2 FTOH) was associated with higher odds of eczema (aOR:1.31; 95%CI:1.04-1.67). Mixture-weight analyses indicated contrasting contributions of individual PFAS, with PFBS and TFA contributing positively to ever asthma, 6:2 FTAcr showing the largest positive contribution to wheezing, and PFOS contributing negatively across respiratory outcomes. A simultaneous one-quantile increase in all PFAS was not associated with any of the health outcomes after correction. These findings indicate compound- and outcome-specific associations between indoor air PFAS and children's respiratory and skin health, while highlighting the complexity of evaluating co-exposure to multiple PFAS.

articles.title: Efficacy of Digital Health Interventions for Insomnia: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is common, and treatments are limited by tolerability and access. Digital health interventions (DHIs) are increasingly used for sleep management, but evidence comparing multiple outcomes is scarce.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of DHIs on 8 sleep outcomes, including insomnia severity, sleep efficiency, total sleep time, and sleep quality.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, CBM, VIP, Wanfang, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the American Academy of Sleep Medicine's website from inception to July 2026. Two reviewers (SG and BZ) independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. We included randomized controlled trials or controlled clinical trials comparing DHIs with any control in insomnia, without language restriction, and excluded experimental sleep deprivation, conference abstracts, protocols, and nonrandomized or noncontrolled designs. Pooled standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs used restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction; 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima method. We also performed subgroup analyses by intervention category, comparator type, diagnostic criteria, and country income, plus sensitivity analyses, Egger tests, and GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) assessment.

RESULTS: We included 44 randomized controlled trials (n=10,521) published between 2004 and 2026 across 14 countries. DHIs significantly improved insomnia severity (SMD -0.91, 95% CI -1.12 to -0.70), sleep efficiency (SMD 0.59, 95% CI 0.45-0.72), total sleep time (SMD 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.29), sleep quality (SMD -0.61, 95% CI -0.78 to -0.45), and secondary outcomes (SMDs -0.37 to -0.64). However, 95% PIs crossed the null for insomnia severity (-2.04 to 0.22), total sleep time (-0.05 to 0.46), and all secondary outcomes. Subgroup analyses showed larger insomnia severity effects in high- versus upper-middle-income countries, modality differences for sleep efficiency, and comparator-type differences for total sleep time (all P<.01). Egger tests suggested small-study effects; sensitivity analyses did not change direction or significance. GRADE certainty ranged from very low to moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: Although DHIs showed statistically significant average effects on multiple sleep outcomes, wide PIs crossing or approaching the null, effects approaching or below Minimum Clinically Important Difference thresholds, and very low-to-moderate GRADE certainty indicate that the evidence remains exploratory. Subgroup analyses revealed effect modifications by country income, intervention modality, and comparator type, underscoring contextual factors. Unlike previous reviews focusing on single DHI formats or average statistical effects, this review provides stratified comparisons and integrates PIs and Minimum Clinically Important Difference conversion to distinguish statistical significance from clinical relevance. This paper provides an evidence synthesis framework showing that DHI benefits are context-dependent and insufficient for a standard clinical role. In practice, DHIs cannot be recommended as a standard substitute for face-to-face cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, although they may serve as a low-intensity option in stepped care. Large-scale, head-to-head implementation trials in diverse populations with extended follow-up are needed to define their optimal role.

articles.title: A Guytonian Atlas of Venous Return in Septic Shock: Reconstruction of Hemodynamic States.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To reconstruct venous return physiology across published studies of septic shock and characterize the distribution of circulatory states represented in the literature.

DESIGN: Exploratory physiologic reconstruction study.

SETTING: Secondary analysis of published hemodynamic observations.

PATIENTS: Adult patients with septic shock reported in studies containing sufficient information for reconstruction of mean circulatory filling pressure analogue (Pmca) and related parameters including venous return driving pressure (VRdP) and resistance to venous return (RVR).

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 150 observations were available. Median Pmca, central venous pressure (CVP), VRdP, and RVR were 17.3 mm Hg, 9.0 mm Hg, 7.9 mm Hg, and 1.04 mm Hg/min/L, respectively. Empirical quartiles identified four recurrent circulatory phenotypes: reduced filling pressure/gradient, preserved venous return, elevated venous pressure, and high-resistance venous return. The preserved venous return pattern demonstrated the highest median cardiac output (CO), whereas the high-resistance pattern exhibited the lowest flow despite comparable filling pressures. In exploratory adjusted analyses incorporating available vasopressor exposure and fluid-therapy context, VRdP remained strongly associated with CO (β, 1.03 L/min/mm Hg; 95% CI, 0.80-1.25; p < 0.001). When Pmca and CVP were entered separately, Pmca was positively associated with CO (β, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.79-1.25; p < 0.001), whereas CVP was inversely associated with CO (β, -1.03; 95% CI, -1.26 to -0.80; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Published hemodynamic observations in septic shock occupy distinct Guytonian phenotypes characterized by different combinations of circulatory filling pressure, venous pressure, and RVR. Reconstruction of venous return geometry may provide a physiologic framework for interpreting circulatory heterogeneity in septic shock.

articles.title: Economic Evaluations of Algorithm-Enabled Remote Monitoring of Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Algorithm-enabled remote monitoring using cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) is increasingly used to support earlier detection of clinical deterioration in heart failure and in at-risk populations. However, the economic value of these technologies remains uncertain because intervention design, implementation, and evaluation methods vary.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically identify, appraise, and synthesize full economic evaluations of algorithm-enabled CIED remote monitoring in adults with established heart failure or at risk of heart failure.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. Searches were performed in MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, with supplementary searches of health technology assessment sources. Eligible studies reported full economic evaluations of algorithm-enabled remote monitoring linked to CIEDs. Data were extracted using a structured form and synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity. Methodological and reporting quality were assessed using the CHEQUE (Criteria for Health Economic Quality Evaluation) checklist and CHEERS (Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards) 2022 statement. One reviewer screened records and extracted the data. A second reviewer independently checked subsets of the screening decisions and extracted the data.

RESULTS: Ten economic evaluations were included. They used models, trial data, or observational data; some were reported within health technology assessments. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in population definitions, intervention characteristics, algorithm types, monitored parameters, clinical response pathways, and economic methods. Cost-effectiveness and cost-utility analyses were most common, with time horizons ranging from short-term follow-up to lifetime modeling. Several studies reported economically favorable findings, including dominance (ie, less costly with better health outcomes) or cost-effectiveness. However, outcomes varied across studies, and favorable estimates often relied on assumptions about reduced hospitalization and length of stay, while quality-adjusted life year gains were generally modest. Reporting of key implementation factors, including alert burden and diagnostic performance, was limited.

CONCLUSIONS: There is economic evidence for algorithm-enabled CIED remote monitoring suggesting potential value in some settings, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous and difficult to compare directly across studies. Findings are sensitive to differences in intervention design, modeling approaches, and clinical input data, which limit certainty and transferability. More robust and standardized evidence is needed before economic conclusions can be applied confidently across different devices, algorithms, and health care settings.

articles.title: Association of Care Intensity With Survival and Long-Term Cost-Effectiveness in Sepsis Without Initial Organ Support After Emergency Admission: A Multicenter Cohort Study in Japan.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify subgroups of patients hospitalized for community-acquired sepsis without initial organ support who may derive survival and cost-effectiveness benefits from ICU or high-dependency care unit (HDU) admission.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: A 140-hospital Japanese database (April 2016-March 2024).

PATIENTS: Adults admitted via emergency ambulance for community-acquired sepsis not requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, mechanical ventilation, catecholamines, or renal replacement therapy before or on the antimicrobial-initiation day.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We compared ICU and HDU admissions, each vs. general ward (GW) admission, balancing patient characteristics using overlap propensity-score weighting. In-hospital mortality was estimated as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs using modified Poisson regression. Cost-effectiveness was measured by the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) in 3-year costs per quality-adjusted life year (QALY). Among 28,211 patients (GW, 18,349; HDU, 8,706; ICU, 1,156), ICU and HDU admissions were not associated with lower mortality overall (HDU vs. GW; RR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92-1.06 and ICU vs. GW; RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.92-1.22). However, HDU admission was associated with lower mortality among patients with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score greater than or equal to 6 (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75-0.99) or Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score less than or equal to 12 (RR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92). Under the Japanese (50,000 USD/QALY) and U.S. (100,000 USD/QALY) thresholds, ICU and HDU admissions were not cost-effective overall (ICERs > 200,000 USD/QALY). However, the HDU subgroup with GCS score less than or equal to 12 (ICER, 47,738 USD/QALY; 95% CI, 45,918-49,558) was cost-effective under both thresholds, and that with SOFA score greater than or equal to 6 (ICER, 55,319 USD/QALY; 95% CI, 52,018-58,624) met the U.S. threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: ICU or HDU admission was not associated with survival or economic benefits overall, whereas HDU subgroups (SOFA score ≥ 6 or GCS score ≤ 12) were associated with lower mortality and better cost-effectiveness. These findings may help optimize resource allocation.

articles.title: Interpretable Recalibration of a Sequential Organ Failure Assessment-Derived Score Using Machine Learning-Guided Optimization: Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score is central to risk stratification in intensive care units (ICUs), but its thresholds and 0- to 4-point increments were set by expert consensus in 1996 and never reestimated from outcome data. Machine learning models discriminate better while discarding the additive, point-based structure that makes SOFA auditable at the bedside, and methods for updating a legacy score rather than replacing it remain scarce.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a data-driven recalibration of a SOFA-derived score that learns thresholds and integer weights from outcome data while preserving an additive, interpretable point-based structure and to test whether it improves discrimination for ICU mortality over a prespecified SOFA-derived reference score.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study using the eICU Collaborative Research Database (208 US hospitals, 2014-2015). We analyzed 14,848 adult first ICU admissions with complete day 1 SOFA-related measurements; 133,684 (90%) of 148,532 encounters with outcome data were excluded because of at least 1 missing determination. As vasoactive dose units could not be harmonized and urine output was largely unavailable, a prespecified SOFA-derived reference score served as the comparator. The framework couples supervised discretization (univariate decision trees and interval number chosen by a penalized validation criterion) with constrained integer-weight optimization under monotonicity, integrality, and scale-anchoring constraints, plus logistic calibration. Performance was estimated from pooled out-of-fold predictions of 10-fold nested cross-validation grouped by hospital, with bootstrap CIs; final thresholds and weights were refit on the full cohort and contributed no performance estimate.

RESULTS: ICU mortality was 17.03% (2529/14,848). The recalibrated score achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.811 (95% CI 0.800-0.819) versus 0.751 (95% CI 0.740-0.761) for the reference score (paired difference 0.059, 95% CI 0.053-0.067), and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.495 (95% CI 0.477-0.515) versus 0.393 (95% CI 0.377-0.411; paired difference 0.102, 95% CI 0.087-0.116). Improvement was consistent across all 10 hospital-grouped folds and length-of-stay strata. After unweighted logistic recalibration, global calibration was adequate; the Brier score was lower (0.112 vs 0.123), whereas other calibration-error measures were higher. Discrimination approached unconstrained XGBoost (Extreme Gradient Boosting; AUROC 0.818) and exceeded penalized logistic regression (AUROC 0.775) fitted on the same folds. The advantage persisted in all 1000 resampling replications and in a prespecified sensitivity analysis expanding the cohort to 61,469 encounters (median paired AUROC difference 0.037).

CONCLUSIONS: Data-driven recalibration under explicit structural constraints can update the cutpoints and integer weights of an established clinical score without abandoning its additive, bedside-computable form and should transfer to other legacy instruments. The recalibrated score is a mortality risk model on its own 0-71 scale; an open-source calculator is provided, and external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.
