articles.title: Effectiveness of Conversational Agents for Depression and Anxiety: Systematic Review and Network Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Agent Types, Dose, and Human Support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conversational agents (CAs) are increasingly used to deliver scalable interventions for depression and anxiety, but existing evidence has often treated these tools as a single category. The comparative effectiveness of different agent types, intervention doses, and levels of human support remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This review systematically evaluated the comparative effectiveness of various CA modalities and levels of human support, as well as potential dose-response relationships across different CA types.

METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Ovid, CINAHL, and Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection (PBSC) databases was conducted from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating CA-based interventions. We conducted a random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) using postintervention outcomes and assessed inconsistency and risk of bias (RoB). Evidence certainty was assessed using the CINeMA (confidence in network meta-analysis) framework. Where data permitted, model-based network dose-response meta-analysis (MBNMA) was performed to examine dose-response associations.

RESULTS: A total of 41 studies (n=7577) were included. NMA showed that AI-enhanced intensive human support (AEIHS) appeared to produce greater symptom improvement for depression and anxiety compared with pure human digital guidance (PHDG; Hedges g=-4.28, 95% CI -5.56 to -2.99) and open-ended multimodal-enhanced chatbot (OEMM; Hedges g=-4.49, 95% CI -6.31 to -2.66), whereas most other comparisons were not statistically significant. MBNMA indicated that goal-oriented conversational agent (GOCA) and highly structured modular chatbot (HSMC) appeared to exhibit nonlinear effects, with preliminary evidence suggesting potentially enhanced response at low-to-moderate doses, though these findings require further investigation. However, publication bias was detected for depression (Egger P=.02), and the overall certainty of evidence was very low, primarily due to RoB, indirectness, and imprecision.

CONCLUSIONS: While hybrid CA models with enhanced human involvement appeared to show potential advantages over fully automated systems, the evidence base remains limited. The very low certainty of evidence constrains confidence in comparative rankings and dose recommendations. Future high-quality trials are needed to establish optimal CA architectures and intervention doses for scalable mental health care.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251145207; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251145207.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Unloading With Self-Expanding Pump During Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Increased left ventricular (LV) afterload and distension during venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support may impede myocardial perfusion in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Active LV unloading has been associated with improved outcomes. We report the first clinical use of a self-expanding percutaneous ventricular assist device (NyokAssist; magAssist, Suzhou, China) for LV unloading during VA-ECMO in a 56 year old man with AMI-related cardiogenic shock (CS). Successful coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of the culprit left circumflex (LCx) lesion were performed with NyokAssist + VA-ECMO support. The patient was successfully weaned from VA-ECMO on post-procedure day 5 and remained on NyokAssist support alone for an additional 7 days before being transferred on VA-ECMO to a heart transplant center for consideration of advanced heart failure therapies due to limited myocardial recovery. No device-related complications were observed. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of early implementation of a combined VA-ECMO and NyokAssist support strategy, enabling LV unloading, temporary hemodynamic stabilization, end-organ improvement, and VA-ECMO decannulation in a patient with AMI-related CS. As this report describes a single-patient experience, further clinical studies are warranted to define the safety, efficacy, and potential role of the use of NyokAssist in combination with VA-ECMO in the management of AMI-related CS.

articles.title: Electronic Health Record-Embedded Workflow to Operationalize Whole-Person Screening in Safety-Net Primary Care: Observational Implementation Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health systems increasingly screen patients for social and whole-person needs. Yet, electronic health record data often remain passive when no workflow translates identified needs into structured action during routine care. In safety-net and federally qualified health center (FQHC) settings, this gap is especially consequential because clinicians must address multidomain needs within time-constrained encounters while meeting documentation, coding, and referral requirements.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the implementation and recorded use of an Epic-based digital workflow that links a Whole PERSON Health Score (WPHS) assessment to a Best Practice Advisory (BPA) and SmartSet, along with a separate Power BI accountability dashboard, in a safety-net FQHC network.

METHODS: We conducted an observational implementation evaluation of the WPHS BPA-SmartSet workflow at Riverside University Health System using the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance) framework. We analyzed encounter-level WPHS assessments and BPA presentation records from January 2023 through July 2026. We examined screening reach, temporal correspondence between BPA presentations and preceding qualifying WPHS assessments, recorded downstream workflow activity, variation across clinics, and trends over time using descriptive statistics. As a sensitivity analysis, we estimated logistic regression models with clinic fixed effects and 2-way patient- and provider-clustered robust SEs to evaluate temporal patterns in SmartSet opening and downstream workflow activity.

RESULTS: During the study period, 177,821 WPHS assessments were completed among 115,022 unique patients; 173,763/177,821 (97.7%) identified at least one qualifying yellow or red domain. Among 107,010 BPA presentations involving 101,297 unique patients, 104,049 (97.2%) were linked to a uniquely identifiable most-recent qualifying WPHS assessment; among these, 99.1% (103,122/104,049) occurred within 7 days. The SmartSet was opened in 82.9% (88,736/107,010) of BPA presentations, and broad structured downstream workflow activity was documented in 82.4% (88,160/107,010); Z-code documentation in 42.6% (45,632/107,010), and referrals in 23.4% (25,061/107,010). SmartSet opening increased from 41.3% (262/634) in January 2023 to 94.3% (4262/4520) in July 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: In this safety-net FQHC setting, whole-person need was common and often multidomain, and an Epic BPA-SmartSet workflow was associated with high rates of SmartSet opening and documented downstream workflow activity across observed BPA presentations. BPA presentations were highly concordant with preceding qualifying WPHS assessments, and workflow activity increased substantially over the implementation period. For digital health leaders seeking to operationalize whole-person care, the findings support electronic health record-based decision support that surfaces identified need, bundles documentation and referral tasks, and pairs point-of-care workflow with visible implementation monitoring, rather than relying on screening alone.

articles.title: Hallucinated Evidence and Real-World Risk-Physicians' Intent to Act on AI-Generated Abstracts in Emergency Medicine and Trauma Surgery: Cross-Sectional, Vignette-Based Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in academic writing and can generate linguistically polished but factually incorrect scientific content. Such misinformation may distort evidence appraisal and, if translated into clinical practice, compromise patient care.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate physicians' likelihood of misperceiving false information embedded in LLM-generated abstracts as true and reporting an intent to use that information in future practice. We also explored which features were associated with perceived credibility and intended clinical action.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey of physicians working in emergency medicine and trauma surgery across 4 hospitals in Germany. Each participant assessed 4 abstracts generated using GPT-5 Thinking mode, of which 2 contained intentionally false claims supported by plausible explanations and 2 contained accurate claims. The primary outcome was the proportion of physicians reporting an intent to use or act on recommendations contained in abstracts with false claims. Secondary outcomes included perceived accuracy, rejection of accurate claims, and ratings of precision, structure, and grammar.

RESULTS: Twenty physicians provided 80 ratings of 4 abstracts. Overall, physicians reported that they would act on 68% (54/80) of abstracts. Using abstract truth status as the reference, the decision to act had a sensitivity of 78% (31/40), specificity of 43% (17/40), positive predictive value of 57% (31/54), and negative predictive value of 65% (17/26). The positive likelihood ratio was 1.35 (95% CI 0.98-1.85), the negative likelihood ratio was 0.53 (95% CI 0.27-1.04), and the diagnostic odds ratio was 2.55 (95% CI 0.96-6.73). True and false abstracts received similar ratings for perceived accuracy (mean 3.15, SD 0.89 vs mean 2.88, SD 1.04; P=.21), precision (mean 3.15, SD 0.89 vs mean 2.93, SD 1.00; P=.29), structure (mean 3.23, SD 0.77 vs mean 3.20, SD 0.88; P=.89), and grammar (mean 3.40, SD 0.59 vs mean 3.43, SD 0.68; P=.86). Abstracts that physicians intended to act on were rated substantially higher for perceived accuracy, precision, and structure than those they would not act on (all P<.001), whereas grammar ratings did not differ (P=.80).

CONCLUSIONS: Physicians frequently reported an intent to act on LLM-generated abstracts containing false claims, and true and false abstracts were not reliably distinguished on perceived quality measures. Perceived accuracy, precision, and structure were strongly associated with intended action, whereas grammar was not. These findings highlight the risk that persuasive scientific presentation may increase the credibility and potential clinical influence of fabricated or inaccurate AI-generated evidence.

articles.title: Assessing outcomes and recovery following anterior cervical discectomy and fusion in patients aged 75 years and older: a propensity score-matched review with 2-year follow-up.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The longitudinal efficacy of anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) in the population of older individuals is debated. The authors aimed to determine the long-term outcomes of patients aged ≥ 75 years compared to those of their younger peers.

METHODS: A prospectively collected quality registry of patients undergoing elective ACDF was retrospectively reviewed. Cohorts included patients who were ≥ 75 years compared to < 75 years of age. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were collected at baseline and 3, 12, and 24 months postoperatively. Demographics, surgical characteristics, complications, Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) dysphagia rates, North American Spine Society satisfaction, and PROMs were compared between groups. All analyses were repeated following 1:1 propensity score matching by demographics, baseline PROMs, comorbidities, symptoms, and surgical factors.

RESULTS: A total of 1155 patients met inclusion criteria with 1082 (94%) aged < 75 years and 73 (6%) ≥ 75 years. Prior to propensity score matching, the ≥ 75-year cohort had a lower mean BMI (29.0 ± 4.3 vs 30.9 ± 6.6 kg/m2, p = 0.028), fewer daily smokers (4.1% vs 16%, p = 0.005), fewer currently employed workers (5.5% vs 52%, p < 0.001), and lower rates of anxiety (15% vs 28%, p = 0.017) and depression (12% vs 23%, p = 0.041). The ≥ 75-year cohort had more osteoarthritis (47% vs 24%, p < 0.001) and coronary artery disease (23% vs 6.5%, p < 0.001). The ≥ 75-year cohort had significantly better neck pain visual analog scale, arm pain visual analog scale (AP-VAS), Neck Disability Index, EuroQol 5-Dimension, and EuroQol visual analog scale baseline scores (all p < 0.05), but similar modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scores (p = 0.2). By the 2-year follow-up, all PROM scores were similar except for the AP-VAS score, for which the ≥ 75-year cohort reported less arm pain (1.2 ± 2.5 vs 1.7 ± 2.7, p = 0.044). Propensity score matching yielded 138 patients, with 69 in each cohort. Residual demographic differences included the ≥ 75-year cohort having fewer employed workers (5.8% vs 42%, p < 0.001) and more individuals with a professional degree (25% vs 8.7%, p = 0.012). The propensity score-matched cohorts achieved parity in all baseline, postoperative, and change-from-baseline PROM scores through the 2-year follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients aged ≥ 75 years experience benefit comparable to that of younger patients across outcome measures following propensity score matching. Age alone does not predict worsened outcomes in carefully selected older patients undergoing elective ACDF, and older patients may benefit from knowledge of comparable favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Safety of responsive neurostimulation in pediatric and young adult patients with drug-resistant epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Responsive neurostimulation (RNS) is increasingly being used for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but the safety of the procedure in children remains unclear. The authors systematically reviewed published clinical outcomes in pediatric RNS, with an emphasis on complications and other adverse events.

METHODS: The authors performed a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through August 12, 2025. They included observational studies reporting outcomes of RNS in patients aged ≤ 21 years at implantation and extractable pediatric data. Two authors independently screened articles and extracted data. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least 1 complication. A sensitivity analysis restricted to extractable patients aged ≤ 18 years was also performed.

RESULTS: Thirty-five studies met inclusion criteria, representing 358 pediatric patients who underwent RNS implantation. Most studies were case series (62.9%), followed by case reports (25.7%) and cohort studies (11.4%); all were conducted in the United States. The mean patient age at implantation was 14.8 years, and the mean follow-up was 20.3 months among studies reporting follow-up. Overall, 38 patients experienced at least 1 complication. The most frequently reported complications were infection (3.4%), transient neurological deficits (3.1%), return to the operating room (2.2%), and explantation (2.0%). Less common events included stimulation-related side effects (1.4%), CSF-related complications (1.1%), and wound dehiscence and device malfunction (0.6% each). Random-effects meta-analysis demonstrated a pooled overall complication proportion of 10.3% (95% CI 7.0%-14.9%; I2 = 0.0%). In the ≤ 18-year sensitivity analysis, 31 studies comprising 203 patients were included, with a pooled complication proportion of 8% (95% CI 4%-16%).

CONCLUSIONS: Published pediatric RNS experience suggests that complications are comparable to rates reported for similar procedures and are most often transient neurological symptoms, reoperation, or infection. However, the evidence base is largely limited to small observational reports with heterogeneous outcome definitions and high risk of bias. Higher-quality multicenter prospective studies with standardized reporting and longer follow-up are needed to better define safety and effectiveness of RNS in pediatric DRE. Systematic review registration no.: CRD420261339088 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/).

articles.title: Digital Gamified Interventions Targeting Internalizing Mental Health Outcomes in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gamified digital mental health interventions have been proposed as a scalable and engaging approach to addressing the substantial treatment gap in child and adolescent mental health, including limited access to evidence-based care and difficulties with treatment engagement. However, the evidence remains fragmented, and it is unclear which specific gamification elements contribute to clinical effectiveness and sustained engagement.

OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to (1) characterize the gamification elements implemented in digital mental health interventions for children and adolescents; (2) evaluate their effects on internalizing mental health outcomes; (3) assess engagement, adherence, and user experience outcomes; and (4) descriptively explore whether specific gamification elements are associated with differences in clinical or engagement outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. Six electronic databases were searched for studies published between January 2018 and March 2026. Eligible studies examined gamified digital interventions targeting internalizing symptoms in children and adolescents. Gamification elements were systematically coded across 10 categories using a predefined coding framework. A 3-level random-effects meta-analysis was conducted for controlled studies reporting validated mental health outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 27 studies (N=28,777; mean age range 5.05-18.78 years) were included. Feedback, challenges, and progress tracking were the most frequently implemented gamification elements; social interaction and competition were rare. The meta-analysis of 5 eligible controlled studies yielded a small effect in favor of gamified interventions (g=-0.28, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.02; P=.04). However, the 95% prediction interval (-0.79 to 0.24) included zero, indicating substantial uncertainty regarding the effect expected in future comparable settings. Narrative synthesis suggested potentially more favorable effects for depression and anxiety outcomes in some clinical or at-risk samples and in interventions incorporating structured therapeutic content, although these patterns could not be formally examined as moderators. Engagement and adherence limitations were frequently reported across studies.

CONCLUSIONS: Gamified digital interventions may be associated with small improvements in internalizing outcomes in children and adolescents, although the conditions under which these interventions are most effective remain unclear. The limited evidence base and uncertainty across settings preclude firm conclusions regarding efficacy. Future research should determine which gamification elements enhance clinical outcomes and engagement, for whom they are most effective, and under which conditions.

articles.title: Assessment of outcomes in consecutive patients undergoing nerve transfer surgery for neuralgic amyotrophy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with neuralgic amyotrophy (NA) who do not recover sufficiently need better options for functional improvement. Nerve transfer surgery is a promising option, but there are no large studies evaluating the safety and effectiveness in this patient population. The objective of this study was to evaluate nerve transfer surgery outcomes in patients diagnosed with NA who were not recovering spontaneously at least 6 months after symptom onset.

METHODS: Consecutive adult patients diagnosed with NA with severe motor deficits who were not spontaneously recovering by 6 months after symptom onset who underwent nerve transfer surgery (50 patients, 59 nerve transfers) by a single surgeon were included in this retrospective cohort study. Patients were followed for 2 years postoperatively. The primary outcome was improvement in Medical Research Council motor grade in the target muscles at 24 months postoperatively compared with preoperatively. The secondary outcome was improvement in Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand score at 24 months postoperatively compared with preoperatively.

RESULTS: Fifty (85%) of the 59 nerve transfers had a good outcome. The median time from symptom onset to surgery was 9 months. The 3 most common nerve transfers were extensor carpi radialis brevis-anterior interosseous nerve (n = 18, 31%), supinator-posterior interosseous nerve (n = 16, 27%), and thoracodorsal-long thoracic nerve (n = 9, 15%). Overall, 53 (91%) of the 58 nerve transfers for which there were available data had significant improvement in the DASH score at 24 months postoperatively (preoperative mean 56 [SD 18] vs 24-month postoperative mean 26 [SD 13]) (p < 0.001). Any complication occurred in 4 (7%) nerve transfers, with superficial wound infection as the most common. No new or donor weakness occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: There is increasing recognition that many patients with NA will have severe persistent motor deficits. The authors demonstrate that nerve transfer surgery has a high success rate in restoring meaningful function in patients with NA who are not spontaneously improving. This study is the largest to date on nerve transfers in NA and utilizes standard end-to-end nerve transfers with rigorous long-term follow-up that includes both objective clinical examination and patient-reported outcomes. The safety and effectiveness shown here support adding nerve transfer surgery consideration to standard algorithms for management of NA as an important next evolution.

articles.title: Structural Multicollinearity in Interrupted Time Series Designs.
articles.abstract: Interrupted Time Series (ITS) analysis is one of the most widely applied quasi-experimental designs in health, policy, and social research. ITS models include a structural dependency between time-related predictors that can give rise to substantial multicollinearity. This feature arises from the deterministic construction of the post-intervention time variable and intensifies mechanically as the post-intervention period lengthens. As a result, collinearity is not merely a sampling artifact but a structural feature of the ITS model. To illustrate this issue, we replicate a widely cited ITS application and assess collinearity diagnostics across SAS, Stata, and R. The findings confirm that variance inflation factors for time and post-intervention terms routinely exceed conventional thresholds, demonstrating that the problem is embedded in the model architecture itself. Although mean-centering does not eliminate this dependence, alternative parameterizations may alter how it appears in numerical diagnostics. Although ITS is frequently recommended as a rigorous design for policy evaluation, this often-overlooked structural limitation has not been explicitly addressed in methodological literature. We argue that greater awareness is needed, urge researchers to report collinearity diagnostics, interpret post-intervention slopes with caution, and recommend greater diagnostic transparency and model sensitivity checks to help applied researchers recognize and account for this structural dependency.

articles.title: Use of Digital Tools and Environmental Practices Among Informal Caregivers of Older Adults in the European Union Embracing the Triple Transition: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The European Union is currently facing a demographic, digital, and environmental transition collectively known as the triple transition. Although these trends significantly impact long-term care services, they have typically been studied in isolation, overlooking potential synergies between the adoption of digital tools and environmental practices among informal caregivers of older adults. This study uniquely bridges this gap by applying an integrative social-ecological-infrastructural systems framework to examine how these transitions interact in everyday caregiving contexts.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the relationship between the use of digital tools and eco-friendly practices among informal caregivers of older adults across the European Union and whether the adoption of digital solutions related differently to specific types of eco-friendly behaviors. Unlike previous research focusing on isolated aspects of each transition, we examined their interconnections, providing empirical evidence for developing integrated policy approaches.

METHODS: Using data from the Survey of Gender Gaps in Unpaid Care, Individual and Social Activities project (n=5761 informal caregivers of adults aged ≥65 years), we analyzed the association between frequency of use of digital tools for caregiving and environmental practices. We used the social-ecological-infrastructural systems conceptual framework and the theory of planned behavior (TPB) to interpret findings. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and multilevel mixed-effects regression models.

RESULTS: A weak positive association was observed between the frequency of use of digital tools and environmentally sustainable behaviors (ρ=0.28; P<.001). Among individual behaviors, the largest associations were observed for consumption-related behaviors (fair-trade products: ρ=0.30; used items: ρ=0.30; eco-friendly products: ρ=0.25), whereas the associations were weaker for waste management and transportation choices and were not statistically significant for recycling (ρ=-0.04; P=.23) and mindful consumption of natural resources (ρ=-0.02; P>.99). Respondents using digital tools daily had scores of environmentally sustainable behavior (SESBs) 22% higher than nonusers. Demographic patterns revealed higher use of digital tools among younger, more educated, and employed caregivers, indicating that any potential digital-environmental co-occurrence may be unevenly distributed across the caregiver population.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of digital tools may be related to environmental behavior through improved access to information, peer norms, and a greater perceived ability to act, though these mechanisms were not directly tested. The stronger associations with consumption-related behaviors indicate that digital platforms may be particularly relevant to caregivers' access to eco-friendly products, second-hand goods, fair-trade options, and sustainable local services. By contrast, the lack of statistically significant correlations with recycling and resource conservation suggests that digital solutions alone may be insufficient to address behaviors that depend on structural conditions, physical infrastructure, local service availability, or established household routines. Policies should consider digital inclusion, caregiver support, and green infrastructure as interconnected areas while ensuring that older, less educated, and more burdened caregivers are not excluded from these potential co-benefits.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Discharge Instructions for Diabetic Kidney Disease: Comparative Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discharge instructions are an important component of the transition from hospital to home for patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD), whose care often involves multiple comorbidities, medications, and stage-specific management needs. However, producing complete, accurate, clear, and personalized instructions can be challenging for junior physicians.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate whether large language model (LLM) assistance improves the quality of DKD discharge instructions produced by junior physicians and whether its benefits vary according to chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage.

METHODS: The study included 101 hospitalized patients with DKD. Discharge instructions for each patient were initially drafted by a group of junior residents (resident group); subsequently, another group of residents at the same level, with the assistance of DeepSeek-V3.2 (AI-assisted group), generated a separate set of discharge instructions for the same 101 patients, resulting in a total of 202 documents. Four clinical experts, including 2 nephrologists and 2 endocrinologists, independently scored both versions of the discharge instructions using a 5-point Likert scale across 5 dimensions: completeness, accuracy, safety, clarity, and personalization. Interrater reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).

RESULTS: Interrater reliability was excellent in both the resident group (ICC=0.817, 95% CI 0.763-0.864; P<.001) and the AI-assisted group (ICC=0.860, 95% CI 0.816-0.897; P<.001). Compared with resident-only instructions, AI-assisted instructions received significantly higher scores across 5 evaluation dimensions and the overall evaluation (all Bonferroni-adjusted P<.001), with large effect sizes (r=0.741-0.927). In the resident-only group, CKD stage was negatively correlated with accuracy, safety, clarity, and overall quality (Spearman ρ=-0.33 to -0.37; all P<.001), whereas no significant correlations were observed for most dimensions in the AI-assisted group (|ρ|<0.15; P>.05). The proportion of cases achieving a ≥1-point improvement in overall quality was 99% (100/101; 95% CI 94.6%-100.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: LLM assistance improved the completeness, clarity, and personalization of DKD discharge instructions generated by junior physicians, with advantages greatest in complex cases. A human-AI collaborative model is a promising approach to reduce documentation burden.

articles.title: Clinician Competencies for Self-Management Support in Cancer: Expert Consensus Recommendations From the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Many people affected by cancer benefit from self-management, but this requires support from cancer care clinicians. Currently, there is a lack of consensus about the minimum competencies required of clinicians to facilitate effective self-management support (SMS).

METHODS: A two-round online modified Delphi study involving cancer care clinicians was conducted to reach consensus on which performance criteria from a comprehensive SMS framework for cancer nurses should be considered minimum competencies that cancer care clinicians should possess. The perspectives of people affected by cancer regarding SMS needs were collected via online interviews and further shaped the statements. The project team finalized a list of minimum competencies for care-providers (care-provider version) and a reader-adjusted version for people affected by cancer (patient version).

RESULTS: 27 clinicians and 14 people affected by cancer participated. Eighteen performance criteria from the original framework reached consensus for inclusion as minimum competencies, with participant feedback informing refinements to both the care-provider and patient versions. The performance criteria included statements from all six domains of the original framework: person-centered and motivational communication, whole-person assessment of SMS needs and capacity, health promotion theories and interventions, coaching for behavior change tailored to the individual, monitoring and evaluating change in self-management behaviors and health outcomes, and quality improvement for integration of SMS in cancer care.

CONCLUSION: The minimum competencies for SMS can be used to inform care provider education, skills assessment, and encourage patient activation for improved support, to optimize patient outcomes and health care utilization. International organizations, such as the Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer, represent an ideal forum for the dissemination and strengthening of these competencies, and for local implementation.

articles.title: Correction to "Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy as a Key Feature of MRAS-Related Noonan Syndrome: New Case and Comprehensive Literature Review".
Cardiorespiratory Fitness as Mediator in the Association Between Physical Activity and Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients with CMD or OA.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diseases like cardiovascular metabolic disease (CMD) and osteoarthritis (OA) impact health-related quality of life (hr-QoL). In the general population, hr-QoL is associated with physical activity (PA), sedentary time (ST) and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF). This study aims to examine 1) associations between device-based and self-reported PA and ST, and hr-QoL, and 2) the influence of self-reported CRF in these associations in people with (or at risk for) CMD and/or OA.

METHODS: Data from the Lifestyle front Office For Integrating lifestyle medicine in the Treatment of patients (LOFIT) study was used. Participants included patients with (or at risk for) CMD and/or OA (n=273) within the Netherlands. PA and ST were measured using device-based (activPAL™) and self-reported methods (International Physical Activity Questionnaire - Short Form and Marshall Sitting Questionnaire). CRF was assessed by estimating peak oxygen uptake per kilogram bodyweight (VO2peak mL·kg -1·min -1) using the FitMáx questionnaire. Hr-QoL was assessed using EQ-5D-5L. The associations were examined using linear regression and cross-sectional mediation models.

RESULTS: Higher levels of device-based, and self-reported PA were associated with higher hr-QoL (b=0.007, 95% CI=0.000, 0.013 per 1000 steps, b=0.001 95% CI= 0.000, 0.002 per 30 minutes). Higher levels of device-based and self-reported ST were associated with lower hr-QoL (b=-0.006, 95% CI=-0.012, -0.000 per 30 minutes, b=-0.004, 95% CI=-0.007, -0.001 per 30 minutes). A cross-sectional indirect association via CRF was observed in the association between PA and hr-QoL.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher PA and lower ST are associated with enhanced hr-QoL, where CRF influences the relationship between PA and hr-QoL in this patient population. Reducing ST could be a more feasible first step, if increasing PA is challenging. Moreover, the influence of CRF emphasizes the need for interventions focusing on improving fitness levels.

articles.title: Comparing the Effectiveness of Atropine Sulfate and Acacia Catechu in Reducing Salivary Secretion During Dental Procedures: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sialorrhea, or excessive salivation, can be a major problem during a number of dental operations. It can impair vision, increase chair time, and perhaps jeopardize the effectiveness of treatments. To treat this illness, pharmacological treatments such as atropine sulfate are frequently used. However, there has not been much research done on natural substitutes like Acacia catechu for this function.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to compare and evaluate the effectiveness of atropine sulfate and Acacia catechu in reducing salivary secretion in patients undergoing restorative dental procedures.

METHODS: A randomized controlled trial will be conducted involving 160 participants undergoing restorative dental treatments. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either atropine sulfate or Acacia catechu. Salivary flow will be measured preintervention and postintervention. The primary statistical analysis will use analysis of covariance, with postintervention salivary flow as the dependent variable and baseline salivary flow as a covariate. If a placebo arm is included, group differences will be analyzed using 1-way ANOVA followed by Tukey post hoc tests. Paired t tests will be used only for within-group pre-post comparisons.

RESULTS: Ethical approval was obtained in March 2025. Participant recruitment is scheduled to begin in June 2026 and is expected to be completed by December 2026, with final data collection anticipated by February 2027. It is anticipated that both interventions will reduce salivary flow, with atropine sulfate demonstrating greater efficacy but more side effects, and Acacia catechu offering a better side-effect profile and higher patient acceptability.

CONCLUSIONS: The trial will provide comparative evidence on the efficacy and safety of a pharmacological and a natural anticholinergic agent. If Acacia catechu proves effective, it may offer a viable, better-tolerated alternative for salivary control in clinical dental settings.

articles.title: Ambient particulate matter and blood lipids: Effect modification by dyslipidemia.
articles.abstract: We analyzed nationally representative Korean adults (KNHANES 2016-2023) to assess associations between annual particulate matter exposure and lipid profiles, with effect modification by dyslipidemia diagnosis. Exposure was assigned at the province/metropolitan level by survey year, and outcomes included TC, HDL-C, TG, non-HDL-C, and LDL-C. Survey-weighted linear regression estimated changes per interquartile range increase (PM2.5: 5.00 µg/m3; PM10: 9.00 µg/m3), adjusting for predefined covariates. Higher PM2.5 was associated with increased TC (+1.17 mg/dL), TG (+4.99 mg/dL), and non-HDL-C (+2.89 mg/dL), and decreased HDL-C (-1.72 mg/dL). PM10 showed similar significant associations. Interaction analyses revealed effect modification by dyslipidemia diagnosis for TC, TG, non-HDL-C, and LDL-C. These findings remained robust to alternative variance estimation, additional cardiometabolic adjustment, and exclusion of Asian dust (Hwangsa) days. Higher annual PM concentrations were associated with a more adverse lipid profile, with stronger associations for several lipid markers among individuals with diagnosed dyslipidemia, suggesting greater susceptibility in this group.

articles.title: A Fine-Tuned Large Language Model Workflow to Support Risk of Bias Assessment: Development, External Validation, and Reviewer Verification Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given that randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for effectiveness research, assessing their risk of bias (RoB) becomes an indispensable step in systematic reviews. Yet this task remains time-consuming and prone to reviewer subjectivity. While large language models may accelerate the process, they lack transparent, traceable judgments linked to trial reports.

OBJECTIVE: To bridge methodological gaps and improve both efficiency and consistency, this study developed and externally validated TRoB-1, a fine-tuned open-weight large language model workflow for RoB assessment of RCTs.

METHODS: TRoB-1 was developed specifically for the Cochrane risk of bias tool version 1 (RoB 1), which is the most widely adopted instrument for critical appraisal of RCTs. The workflow generates preliminary judgments and supporting quotations from reviewer-selected passages for the target RoB domains. The workflow was built on 2-stage supervised fine-tuning of Gemma 2-9B-Instruct using 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation. The training set comprised 4321 RoB records extracted from systematic reviews of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, and hypertension. The validation set consisted of 161 records from recently published RCTs covering a broader disease area. The reference standard was established by 2 independent reviewers. Two clinicians blinded to the reference standard verified TRoB-1-assisted assessments through a locally hosted web interface. Using the same reference standard, the performance of TRoB-1 raw outputs was compared with that of the Gemma 2 base workflow, and clinician-verified outputs were compared with raw TRoB-1 outputs.

RESULTS: TRoB-1 successfully generated structured outputs for all 161 validation records. In independent clinician-assisted assessments using the same workflow, raw TRoB-1 accuracy ranged from 73.3% (n=118) to 73.9% (n=119), compared with 52.2% (n=84) to 60.2% (n=97) for the Gemma 2 base model. After verification, accuracy ranged from 82.0% (n=132) to 84.5% (n=136) and macro-F1 from 0.709 to 0.776. Accuracy remained higher for raw TRoB-1 after excluding invalid base-model outputs, and verification did not change any correct judgment to an incorrect one. Clinician 1 corrected 13 initially incorrect judgments and clinician 2 corrected 18. The F1-score for judgments of high-RoB increased from 0.600 to 0.784 for clinician 1 and from 0.571 to 0.821 for clinician 2.

CONCLUSIONS: TRoB-1 combined task-specific fine-tuning, evidence-linked outputs, and clinician verification in a transparent workflow for reviewer-supported RoB assessment. The TRoB-1 web interface provides a practical platform for integrating RoB into evidence synthesis, particularly for living systematic reviews where timely updates are critical.

articles.title: Nocardia Ocular Infections with Limbal and Scleral Involvement Treated with Adjunctive Rose Bengal Photodynamic Antimicrobial Therapy: A Case Series.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Nocardia spp. are a rare source of ocular infection, frequently complicated by delay in diagnosis, complicated treatment course, and increasing resistance to first-line therapies. Rose Bengal photodynamic antimicrobial therapy (RB-PDAT) has demonstrated broad-spectrum efficacy in vitro and in vivo pilot trials. However, while there is in vitro evidence of its efficacy in Nocardia isolates, its clinical use against Nocardia has not been previously described.

METHODS: Retrospective multi-center case series.

RESULTS: We present three cases of Nocardia ocular infection treated with adjunctive RB-PDAT: two cases of Nocardia niwae and one case of N. amikacinitolerans. All patients experienced failed empiric antimicrobial therapy prior to species-directed antibiotic treatment and RB-PDAT, with infection resolution at follow-up. One case of N. niwae was notable for direct scleral extension with recurrent subconjunctival abscess formation; abscess recurrence following RB-PDAT required salvage therapy with topical linezolid, which achieved definitive resolution.

CONCLUSION: These cases represent, to our knowledge, the first cases of Nocardia ocular infection treated with adjunctive RB-PDAT as well as the 2nd and 3rd case of N. niwae ocular infection. This data adds to existing literature suggesting the important role of adjunctive and rescue therapies in Nocardia infection, notably RB-PDAT and linezolid.

articles.title: Personalized dynamic dose-finding for longitudinal observational data: an application to glucose intolerance in VLBW infants.
articles.abstract: The prescribed doses for many drugs are based on population norms or vary between physicians. For example, very low birth weight (VLBW) infants (weighing less than 1500 grams at birth) experience slower postnatal growth than in utero and receive glucose infusions to mitigate nutritional disruption. Effective treatment dosing is critical to ensure adequate neonatal weight gain while minimizing the risk of hyperglycemia. A single uniform dose is impractical due to the substantial heterogeneity in glucose metabolism among infants. Furthermore, little is known about each infant's glucose metabolism, which complicates the selection of the optimal dose value. We employ a flexible longitudinal mixed model to determine dynamic, patient-specific optimal doses for new infants. Empirical Bayes predictions of random effects are incorporated to capture individual dosage sensitivities that adapt as new data becomes available. To be viable in high-risk clinical environments, providing estimates of predictive uncertainty is crucial for supporting informed clinical decision-making that balances patient safety with treatment efficacy. We propose using the implicit value delta method to quantify the uncertainty of the predicted optimal doses. We validate the properties of our model through simulation studies and an analysis of VLBW infants in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for the first 7 days of life, which demonstrates some key differences in optimal and prescribed dosing strategies.

articles.title: Verifiable summarization of electronic health records using large language models to support chart review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Information overload in electronic health records hampers clinicians' ability to efficiently extract and synthesize critical information from a patient's longitudinal health record, leading to increased cognitive burden and delays in care. This study explores the potential of large language models (LLMs) to address this challenge by generating problem-based admission summaries for patients admitted with heart failure, a leading cause of hospitalization worldwide.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We developed an extract-then-abstract approach guided by disease-specific "summary bundles" to generate summaries of longitudinal clinical notes that prioritize clinically relevant information. Through a mixed-methods evaluation using real-world clinical notes, we compared physicians' ability to answer patient-specific clinical questions with the LLM-generated summaries vs standard chart review.

RESULTS: While summary access did not significantly reduce overall questionnaire completion time, frequent summary use significantly contributed to faster questionnaire completion (P = .002). Individual physicians varied in how effectively they leveraged the summaries. Importantly, summary use maintained accuracy in answering clinical questions (88.0% with summaries vs 86.4% without). All physicians indicated they were "likely" or "very likely" to use the summaries in clinical practice, and 87.5% reported that the summaries would save them time. Preferences for summary format varied, highlighting the need for customizable summaries aligned with individual clinician workflows.

DISCUSSION: This exploratory, mixed-methods pilot study provides one of the first extrinsic evaluations of LLMs for longitudinal summarization, demonstrating their potential to enhance clinician efficiency, alleviate workload, and support informed decision-making in time-sensitive care environments.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that problem-based longitudinal summarization could improve chart review efficiency and standardize the presentation of clinical information, Variability in summary preferences and use underscores the need for user-centered evaluations to guide the development of LLM-generated summaries that align with clinician workflows.

articles.title: Association Between Invasive Coronary Investigation Before Permanent Pacemaker Implantation and Mortality in a Historical Cohort with a One-Year Follow-Up: CorInPace Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation is standard therapy for symptomatic bradyarrhythmias. In emergencies, limited assessment may lead to underdiagnosis of concomitant coronary artery disease (CAD).

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of coronary cineangiography (CAG) before urgent PPM implantation on mortality.

METHODS: This cohort included patients undergoing urgent PPM implantation between July 2016 and June 2021, divided into those undergoing CAG (Group A) and those not undergoing CAG (Group B). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included mortality/readmission, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and hospital stay.

RESULTS: Of 895 patients, 841 were included (Group A: 160; Group B: 681). Group A patients were younger (70.2 vs. 75.2 years; P < 0.001), more frequently male (63.1% vs. 51.8%; P = 0.010), had more CAD (36.2% vs. 19%; P < 0.001), and less frequently had estimated glomerular filtration rate < 45 ml/min/1.73 m2 (10.2% vs. 22.9%; P < 0.001). Mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.96, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56 - 1.66; P = 0.898) and mortality/readmission (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.74 - 1.50; P = 0.776) did not differ between groups. Multivariate analysis showed no significant impact of CAG on either outcome. ACS was more frequent in Group A (7.5% vs. 2.7%; P = 0.005), and hospital stay was shorter in Group B (6 vs. 9 days; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In our study, CAG before PPM implantation was not associated with mortality or mortality/readmission but was associated with longer hospitalization and a higher incidence of ACS.

articles.title: Impact of Surgical Timing on Mortality in Infective Endocarditis Patients with Neurological Complications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The optimal timing of cardiac surgery in infective endocarditis (IE) patients with neurological complications remains controversial.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of early surgical intervention compared with medical therapy on in-hospital and one-year mortality, highlighting the prognostic value of neurological severity and clinical variables.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 109 patients with neurological complications out of a total of 452 patients diagnosed with infective endocarditis at our hospital between January 2013 and December 2023. The patients were divided into a surgical group (n = 48) and a medical therapy group (n = 61). Surgical cases were further classified as early (≤ 7 days) and late (> 7 days). Demographic data, echocardiographic findings, vegetation size (≥ 1 cm), mobility, causative microorganisms, and stroke severity were assessed using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) method (mild-moderate-severe). Mortality predictors over a one-year period were evaluated using multivariate logistic regression.Result: When comparing one-year in-hospital and post-discharge mortality between the medical and surgical patient groups, mortality was significantly higher in the medically treated group (54.1% and 46.4%, respectively) compared to the surgical group (16.7% and 0%, respectively, P < 0.001). No significant difference was observed between the early and late surgical subgroups. Age and NIHSS were independent predictors of in-hospital mortality, while age, treatment type, NIHSS, white blood cells, and hemoglobin were associated with one-year mortality.

CONCLUSION: In IE patients with neurological complications, early cardiac surgery, when carefully selected and managed using a multidisciplinary approach, does not increase mortality compared to late surgery and may improve long-term survival.

articles.title: Impact of Right Ventricular Dysfunction on Acute Kidney Injury and Major Adverse Cardiac and Cerebrovascular Events in Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) may influence perioperative hemodynamics after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). This study evaluated the association between preoperative RVD, defined by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) after isolated CABG.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 392 adults undergoing isolated CABG between 2020 and 2023. RVD was defined as TAPSE < 17 mm. AKI was assessed at 24 and 48 hours according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. MACCE was evaluated as a predefined composite outcome. Logistic regression was used to explore factors associated with AKI and MACCE.

RESULTS: Preoperative RVD was present in 2.3% of patients and was associated with a higher rate of KDIGO stage 1 AKI at 24 hours (P < 0.001). RVD was not independently associated with MACCE. Higher preoperative white blood cell count (odds ratio [OR] 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03 - 1.24; P = 0.013) and KDIGO stage at 48 hours (OR 7.44, 95% CI 3.32 - 18.77; P < 0.001) were associated with MACCE.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative RVD was associated with early renal vulnerability after CABG but not with MACCE. Postoperative AKI severity and preoperative inflammatory status were independently associated with MACCE. These exploratory findings require validation in larger cohorts and suggest that right ventricular assessment may improve perioperative risk stratification.

articles.title: Preoperative Dependent Functional Status Is Associated with Worse 30-Day Pulmonary Complications in Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: An Insight from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database From 2005-2021.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While current cardiac surgery risk scores do not account for preoperative functional status, it has been linked to adverse outcomes in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, in surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), preoperative functional status remains underexplored.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the impact of preoperative functional status on 30-day SAVR outcomes to provide insights into clinical decision-making and postoperative care. Methods: Patients undergoing SAVR were identified from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database from 2005 to 2021. A 1:3 propensity-score matching was applied to patients with dependent (DFS) and independent (IFS) functional status. Thirty-day outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: After propensity-score matching, DFS and IFS patients showed similar mortality (11.11% vs. 9.42%, P = 0.39) and major adverse cardiovascular events (9.91% vs. 9.11%, P = 0.66). Patients with DFS had higher risks of pulmonary complications (29.43% vs. 21.64%, P < 0.01) including pneumonia (13.21% vs. 9.21%, P = 0.04) and prolonged mechanical ventilation over 48 hours (25.83% vs. 15.42%, P < 0.01) but lower bleeding requiring transfusion (51.65% vs. 67.49%, P < 0.01). DFS patients were more likely to be discharged not to home (71.52% vs. 47.75%, P < 0.01) and had longer operation time (315.2 ± 130.5 vs. 293.5 ± 119.8 min, P < 0.01) and LOS (18.47 ± 14.30 vs. 15.07 ± 12.83 days, P < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: While SAVR is relatively safe in eligible DFS patients considering its mortality and cardiac outcomes, it is imperative to emphasize preoperative functional status assessments and closely monitor postoperative pulmonary complications.

articles.title: Establishment and Assessment of a Predictive Model for Atrial Fibrillation Complications Following Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting - A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF), the most common arrhythmia after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), occurs in 15 - 50% of cases.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the incidence and risk factors of POAF after off-pump CABG (OPCABG) and to establish a nomogram prediction model.

METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 179 patients who underwent OPCABG between October 2018 and October 2022. Patients were divided into POAF (n = 43) and non-POAF (n = 136) groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors. A nomogram was developed and evaluated for discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility.

RESULTS: POAF incidence after OPCABG was 24.04%, peaking on postoperative day two. Independent predictors identified were age, hypertension, left atrium anteroposterior dimension > 40 mm, New York Heart Association (NYHA) class ≥ III, and intraoperative potassium < 4.5 mmol/L. A nomogram incorporating these factors was developed. Validation showed excellent discriminative power (area under the curve = 0.919, 95% confidence interval: 0.8747 - 0.9637), good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.80), and significant clinical utility via decision curve analysis across a wide probability range (0.2% - 98%).

CONCLUSION: Age, hypertension, left atrium anteroposterior dimension > 40 mm, NYHA class ≥ III, and intraoperative potassium < 4.5 mmol/L were identified as independent risk factors for POAF after OPCABG, and these factors can serve as predictors for POAF. By implementing appropriate health management strategies, the POAF complications following OPCABG may be reduced.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Preoperative Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet Score and Postoperative Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) significantly increases the risk of morbidity and mortality following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Identifying preoperative prognostic indicators is critical for improving postoperative outcomes in this patient population.

METHODS: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the preoperative Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet (HALP) score and postoperative complications and mortality in T2DM patients undergoing isolated CABG surgery. A total of 675 T2DM patients who underwent isolated CABG surgery between 2018 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were grouped according to their preoperative HALP scores. Demographic characteristics, postoperative complications, intensive care and hospital stay durations, revascularization needs, and one-year mortality rates were compared between groups.

RESULTS: Patients with lower HALP scores experienced significantly higher rates of postoperative infections, pneumonia, renal dysfunction, longer intensive care unit/hospital stays, and increased one-year mortality (P < 0.001). These findings indicate a strong correlation between nutritional/immune status and surgical outcomes in diabetic patients.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative HALP score may serve as a reliable, cost-effective associated factor of postoperative complications and mortality in T2DM patients undergoing CABG. Incorporating HALP scoring into routine preoperative assessment could enhance risk stratification and perioperative management strategies.

articles.title: Results of Pulmonary Valve Replacement with The INSPIRIS RESILIA Prosthesis: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary valve replacement is increasingly common in patients with congenital heart disease. The limited durability of conventional bioprostheses has led to the introduction of the INSPIRIS RESILIA valve, initially designed for the aortic position. However, evidence on its performance in the pulmonary position is limited and heterogeneous.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement in PubMed®, Excerpta Medica dataBASE, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials. Observational studies with patients undergoing pulmonary valve replacement with the INSPIRIS RESILIA bioprosthesis were included. Data on baseline characteristics, transvalvular gradients, mortality, complications, prosthetic insuficiency, and need for reintervention were extracted. This study was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251117859).

RESULTS: Three retrospective cohort studies and two retrospective case series were identified that included pediatric and adult populations, mainly with a diagnosis of tetralogy of Fallot. The findings were consistent in showing adequate perioperative safety. Smaller studies showed favorable results. In contrast, larger studies with longer follow-up reported more rapid progression to moderate/severe pulmonary insuficiency and shorter durability of the bioprosthesis.

CONCLUSION: INSPIRIS RESILIA may be associated with acceptable short-term outcomes in pulmonary valve replacement, but its medium- and long-term durability may be inferior to that of reference bioprostheses. Medium- and long-term safety remains inconclusive due to limited follow-up, modest sample sizes, heterogeneity in definitions, possible confounding by anatomical substrate, and study limitations.

articles.title: Risk Factors of Clinically Relevant Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) is a serious but underexplored complication in cardiovascular intensive care unit (CV-ICU) patients, with often self-limiting, yet clinically relevant, worsening outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify independent predictors of new-onset UGIB in CV-ICU patients.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 50 patients who underwent bedside upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in the CV-ICU due to overt UGIB were analyzed. Clinical data, laboratory parameters, and intensive care unit (ICU)-related variables were compared between patients with clinically relevant and non-relevant UGIB. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors.

RESULTS: Clinically significant UGIB occurred in nine patients (18%), with a mortality rate of 77.8% (7/9). Multivariate analysis revealed that Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II score (odds ratio [OR] 1.47, P = 0.018), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score (OR 1.08, P = 0.045), and ICU stay before bleeding (OR 1.49, P = 0.049) were independent risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed strong discriminative ability of APACHE II (area under the curve [AUC] 0.927, sensitivity 100%, specificity 85.4%), whereas SOFA demonstrated moderate performance (AUC 0.772, sensitivity 77.8%, specificity 78.0%). The use of anticoagulants, antiplatelets, or dual therapy was not significantly associated with clinically relevant bleeding (P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Higher SOFA and APACHE II scores, as well as prolonged ICU stay, were independent risk factors for clinically significant new-onset UGIB in CV-ICU patients. APACHE II provided superior predictive accuracy compared with SOFA. Clinically relevant UGIB was strongly linked to mortality, while antithrombotic therapy type showed no significant effect.

articles.title: Effect of airway assistant training on intubation time during simulated prehospital airway management: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Challenging airways are common in the out-of-hospital setting, where delays or failure to secure the airway can result in significant morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this pilot study aimed to determine whether training paramedics in the role of airway assistant improves intubation time during a simulated regurgitating airway using suction-assisted laryngoscopy and airway decontamination (SALAD).

METHODS: Twelve qualified paramedics were randomly allocated to one of two groups (n = 6) and paired with intensive care paramedics (ICPs). Airway assistants in Group 1 completed a one-hour airway assistant training program, whereas airway assistants in Group 2 received no training. Participants completed a standardized, timed simulation using a continuously regurgitating mannequin designed to replicate the challenges of out-of-hospital intubation. The primary outcome was time to successful intubation, defined as passage of the endotracheal tube through the vocal cords with cuff inflation.

RESULTS: Airway assistant training significantly reduced intubation time. The untrained group recorded a median intubation time of 102.5 seconds (IQR 36), compared with 53 seconds (IQR 19) in the trained group. Group comparisons demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in intubation time (p = 0.009) and corresponded to a very large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.86; Hedges' g = 1.72). No association was observed between intubation time and the age or experience of either the airway assistant or the ICP. No esophageal intubations occurred in either group.

CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot study, training paramedics to perform the airway assistant role significantly reduced intubation time in a simulated regurgitating airway. These preliminary findings suggest that incorporating structured airway assistant training into prehospital education programs may improve airway management performance in challenging environments. Given the small sample size and simulated setting, larger studies are required to confirm these findings and determine whether the observed benefits translate to clinical practice.

articles.title: TOX and PD-1 are required for the maintenance of CD4 T cell precursors during chronic infection.
articles.abstract: In contrast with the well-established mechanisms that maintain exhausted CD8 T cells, our knowledge about the differentiation and in particular the molecular control of CD4 T cells in chronic infections is limited. Using the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection model, we identified that CXCR5+TCF-1+ CD4 T cells, found mainly in secondary lymphoid organs, serve as precursors for the CD4 population. These cells transition into terminally differentiated cells and combine T follicular helper (TFH) cell features (IL-21 expression) with T helper 1 (TH1) cell characteristics (CXCR6 expression and IFN-γ and TNF secretion). In the CXCR5+TCF-1+ population, CD62L+ cells exhibit the highest re-expansion potential in adoptive transfer settings. All subsets express TOX and PD-1, which ensure the maintenance of the CD4 T cell population. Absence of either factor reduces the number of CD62L+ precursors and impairs their further differentiation. Overall, we define a hierarchical framework for CD4 T cell maintenance in chronic infection and reveal common mechanisms that sustain both exhausted CD4 and CD8 T cell responses.

articles.title: Local Diagnostic Reference Levels for Pediatric Whole-body and Brain [18F]FDG PET/CT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PET/CT scanners allow anatomical and metabolic imaging but expose patients to ionizing radiation, requiring dose optimization according to the ALARA principle, especially in children. Diagnostic Reference Levels are a possibility, yet no pediatric [18F]FDG PET/CT DRLs exist in Europe. This study reports typical doses for pediatric whole-body and brain [18F]FDG PET/CT.

METHODS: A retrospective study included all PET/CT scans performed at our center in patients under 18 y (2014-2018). Patients were grouped by body weight (whole-body: 15≤30 kg, 30≤50 kg, 50≤80 kg) and age (brain: 1≤6 y, 6≤18 y), according to the ICRP 135 classification. DRLs are defined as the 75th percentile (P75) of observed values.

RESULTS: For whole-body PET, P75 (median) administered activities were 4.5 (4.4), 4.5 (4.1), and 4.7 (4.3) MBq kg-1 across weight groups. Brain PET P75 (median) values were 5.1 (4.5) MBq kg-1 (1≤6 y) and 4.0 (3.1) MBq kg-1 (6≤18 y). Whole-body CT metrics P75 (median) were: CTDIvol of 2.5 (1.6), 3.1 (2.2), and 3.9 (3.1) mGy; DLP of 211.9 (145.5), 331.0 (230.9), and 464.8 (342.6) mGy·cm. Brain CT showed a P75 CTDIvol of 3.5 mGy for both age groups, with DLPs of 75.8 and 76.2 (median: 75.8) mGy·cm.

CONCLUSION: The values reported in this article, by comparison with existing literature, show that it is possible to reduce the administered activity for certain patient categories. Local, national, or international DRLs are expected to change over time and results need to be updated in an iterative way, particularly when new technologies are implemented.

articles.title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a 68Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe.
articles.abstract: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA-anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([68Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks. Mechanistically, the ssDNA backbone demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, without exacerbating autoimmune phenotypes or inducing Toll-like receptor-mediated signaling pathways. In conclusion, this study establishes a robust proof-of-concept for pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of immune complex deposition. By directly visualizing the disease-driving renal autoantibody deposition at the preclinical stage, prior to overt organ damage, this strategy shifts LN diagnosis to non-invasive, mechanism-based molecular visualization.

articles.title: Identification of gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB)-β-ribose as a promising biomarker enabling prolonged detection of GHB intake.
articles.abstract: For several years, forensic toxicologists have sought biomarkers to extend the detection window of gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB), a drug suspected to be involved in drug-facilitated sexual assaults yet difficult to detect due to its rapid elimination, endogenous presence, and postsampling formation. In this study, we used samples from 30 participants in a double-blind, controlled trial, randomized to placebo or a single oral dose (50 milligrams per kilogram) of sodium oxybate, a GHB salt. We collected whole blood and urine samples over 5 days and used untargeted metabolomics to search for biomarkers. The most promising feature, previously suggested as a GHB-pentose, was identified as GHB-β-ribose by chemical synthesis and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Quantification showed elevated levels of GHB-β-ribose for up to 48 in blood and 24 hours in urine after GHB intake compared with endogenous levels in the placebo group and authentic forensic cases. Thus, we present GHB-β-ribose as a very promising biomarker for GHB intake, with the potential to extend the detection window for GHB.

articles.title: Battery-free ingestible electronic capsule with programmable high-output soft actuation for active gastrointestinal interventions.
articles.abstract: Ingestible capsules have garnered considerable attention due to their high gastrointestinal (GI) transitability and minimally invasive nature. However, constrained by pill-sized dimensions (approximately 2 to 4 cubic centimeters), current ingestible capsules face persistent challenges in achieving both controllable high mechanical output and sufficient onboard power delivery, limiting their capacity for effective in vivo therapeutic interventions. Here, we present a wirelessly powered ingestible electronic capsule that integrates programmable soft phase-change actuation within a rigid-soft architecture to enable programmable, high-output mechanical operations. Leveraging bidirectional thermoelectric regulation and guided rigid-soft coupling, the capsule delivers a peak force of 3.8 newtons and a volumetric stroke of ∼250 cubic millimeters within a confined geometry based on the phase-change actuation. To power this actuation, we implemented a compact wireless power transfer system that achieved a maximum load-received power per unit receiver-coil volume of 9.15 watts per cubic centimeter at a 5-centimeter transfer distance under the tested conditions. The structural adaptability of the soft actuator allows modular integration of functional end-effectors, supporting high-output tissue acquisition, site-directed delivery of model liquid or gel payloads, and active biofluid sampling under magnetic navigation. In vivo experiments in beagles demonstrated the feasibility of mechanical interventions in physiological environments. By overcoming the long-standing power and actuation constraints of capsule architecture, this work establishes a physical framework for high-output ingestible robotics and advances the development of minimally invasive robotic platforms for complex GI interventions.

articles.title: Origins of low density and low accretion rate in classical T Tauri stars.
articles.abstract: High-resolution x-ray spectroscopy of classical T Tauri stars (CTTs) reveals a soft x-ray excess, low electron density, and accretion rate inferred from helium-like oxygen (O VII). Accretion shock models have been widely studied via numerical simulations and can reproduce observations with appropriate accretion stream structures. Within the standard accretion shock framework, we propose a distinct physical model involving energy exchange between postshock hot plasma and cold infalling material during reverse shock propagation into the accretion stream. Incorporating charge exchange processes, the electron density derived from the O VII triplet shows excellent agreement with helium-like neon diagnostics and standard accretion shock model predictions. The mass accretion rate inferred from O VII emission also becomes consistent with optical results. Complementing our theoretical work, we conducted a laboratory simulation of CTT accretion shocks supported by hydrodynamic similarity principles. Time-integrated x-ray self-emission and temporal optical shadowgraphy reveal the dynamic formation of two dense clumps, the "core" and "shell," which morphologically resemble hydrodynamic oscillations driven by heating/cooling instabilities in CTT accretion shocks. The core is a standing shock formed by a preheated low-density plasma flow impinging on a carbon-hydrogen foil, while the shell is shocked aluminum plasma (the reverse shock) arising from interactions between accumulated aluminum plasma and its following flow. High-resolution experimental spectra confirm that charge exchange occurs in the shocked x-ray-emitting region. Our results demonstrate that dynamic interactions between postshock and infalling material, mediated by charge exchange cooling, is the reason for the low O VII density problem in CTTs.

articles.title: Lynx1 suppression reopens the window for effective rehabilitation after stroke in mice.
articles.abstract: Rehabilitation is an effective and reliable approach for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, its efficacy decreases during the transition from the subacute to the chronic phase after stroke, posing a major barrier to complete functional recovery. This limited efficacy during the chronic phase is believed to result from declining neural plasticity. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms regulating neural plasticity and its temporal changes after stroke remain unclear. To address this gap, we established a focal ischemic stroke mouse model that allows causal interrogation of the mechanisms responsible for the reduced efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase. Using this model, we identified Lynx1, an endogenous negative allosteric modulator of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, as a negative regulator of post-stroke neural plasticity. Lynx1 expression in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was transiently down-regulated and returned to normal levels in the peri-infarct area. Longitudinal intravital imaging revealed that Lynx1 suppression promoted synaptic clustering with increased dendritic spine turnover in the peri-infarct area, an emerging structural basis for memory formation. As anticipated, Lynx1 suppression improved spontaneous motor recovery and the efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase after stroke. Furthermore, we developed a Lynx1-targeting antisense oligonucleotide and found that its administration during the chronic phase after stroke enhanced the efficacy of rehabilitation. These findings suggest that dendritic spine dynamics in the peri-infarct area are a key determinant of rehabilitation responsiveness through the regulation of clustered spine formation and that Lynx1 may represent a promising therapeutic target for augmenting dendritic plasticity after stroke.

articles.title: Adding Nitrate to a Sucrose Rinse Reduces Acidogenicity: An in vivo Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Potential dental health benefits, including pH buffering, have been demonstrated for nitrate in placebo-controlled studies when consumed one or several hours before sugar intake. However, its immediate local effect when co-administered with sugar is unclear. Our aim was to test the local effect of adding nitrate to a sugar rinse on human saliva acidification.

METHODS: A double-blind, crossover study was conducted with three periods. In each period, 18 adults, equally distributed between men and women (n = 9 each), aged 25.4 ± 3.8 (mean ± SD), with normal salivary flow, rinsed for 2 min using 10 mL of one of the following rinses: spinach-only (blended spinach providing 8 mm nitrate), spinach+sucrose (blended spinach providing 8 mm nitrate + 20% sucrose), or sucrose-only (20% sucrose). Unstimulated saliva was collected at baseline and every 3 min up to 24 min. pH, lactate, nitrate, and nitrite were measured using Reflectoquant®. The effect of treatment and time was assessed using a linear mixed model (α = 0.05). Nitrate reduction capacity was determined in vitro using baseline saliva.

RESULTS: All saliva samples demonstrated nitrate reduction activity. The lowest pH values were observed 6 min after rinsing, with all groups differing from each other: sucrose only (6.56 ± 0.38; mean ± SD), spinach+sucrose (6.83 ± 0.37), spinach only (7.15 ± 0.44, no pH drop). The pH returned to baseline values 12 min after the spinach+sucrose rinse, but not after the sucrose-only rinse at any time point. Nitrate and nitrite concentrations increased in saliva after using spinach-containing rinses, returning to their baseline levels after 6 min and 12 min. Lower lactate levels were detected after 12 min, suggesting proton consumption during nitrate metabolism in the spinach+sucrose group.

CONCLUSION: Adding a low dose of nitrate to a sucrose rinse limited sugar-induced salivary acidification in vivo, supporting the potential for topical nitrate strategies to reduce sugar acidogenicity.

articles.title: Genome-Wide Association Studies on Dental Caries: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dental caries is a complex, multifactorial pathological disease. Despite advances in dental care, dental caries continues to pose a significant public health challenge. In addition to the behavioural factors (e.g., sugar exposure) and environmental/oral hygiene factors (e.g., fluoride exposure in water and/or toothpaste) on the development of dental caries, potential genetic influence on dental caries susceptibility is possible, but evidence is inconclusive, especially from a candidate gene approach. Over the past 2 decades, a genome-wide association study (GWAS) approach has also been applied to understand the genetic variants associated with dental caries. This study aims to systematically review GWAS on dental caries and identify relevant genetic risk variants of dental caries.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in five databases (PubMed; ScienceDirect; Embase, Global Health, MEDLINE) and one GWAS registry: GWAS Catalog in March 2024. Studies published after 2005 using GWAS approach were eligible. Q-Genie tool was used for the quality assessment.
