Study information and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) at conventional (5 × 10-8) or suggestive (5 × 10-6) GWAS significance level were extracted and synthesized.

RESULTS: A total of 16 papers were included, identifying 20 risk SNPs associated with dental caries at conventional GWAS significance level and 33 SNPs at suggestive level. No common conventional SNPs or shared gene regions were found between studies. Of these studies, the sample sizes in majority were relatively small and only one study reported all recommended quality control steps. Most studies focused on the white or European-American population and dental caries on permanent teeth. In addition, some data resources were used repeatedly in multiple studies, particularly the Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia (COHRA) cohorts, which was used in 9 studies.

CONCLUSION: This study explored the GWAS on dental caries and summarized the heterogeneities of the included studies, leading to inconsistent results. Guideline and more GWAS with larger sample size and multiethnicities are needed to fully understand the genetic basis of dental caries.

articles.title: Defining the terminology of hip and groin pain in 2026: A scoping review of consensus statements.
articles.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This scoping review summarizes the current consensus statements for classifying hip and groin pain in young and middle-aged active individuals and evaluates their citation impact. Secondarily, it asseses to what extent they have been adopted in clinical practice.

METHODS: An electronic database search was performed in September 2026 using PubMed, EMBASE and Google Scholar to identify all consensus statements outlining terminology for young and middle-aged adults with hip or groin pain, and studies investigating the clinical adoption of proposed consensus terminology classifications. Citation counts were used to quantify citation impact, and survey data were used to evaluate clinical adoption.

RESULTS: Nine consensus statements focusing on hip or groin pain in young and middle-aged adults were identified. Four papers, focused on groin pain (different entities); the terminology recommended across these statements varied considerably. All four consensus papers on the hip joint recommend the term femoroacetabular impingement syndrome and there was considerable overlap. One recent multidisciplinary consensus proposed a unified five-entity taxonomy spanning both hip joint and groin pain. The Warwick and Doha statements have been cited most frequently. The only study investigating clinical adoption found that clinicians and experts most commonly used the Doha agreement terminology in academic work and professional communication.

CONCLUSION: Consensus on the terminology and classification of hip and groin pain has evolved substantially over the past decade. Consensus statements for groin pain vary significantly in their focus (based on different entities), terminology and levels of detail for classifying patients. Greater agreement exists in the terminology and classification of hip joint-related pain. Resolving these discrepancies is essential for consistent multidisciplinary communication, reliable research synthesis and for establishing clear clinical decision-making guidelines for patients with hip and groin pain.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level V.

articles.title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity.
articles.abstract: Molecules implicated in host defense can, independent of their roles as immune mediators, regulate sleep. In mammals, cytokines such as Tumor Necrosis Factor α (TNF α) and Interleukin1β (IL1β) promote sleep. In Drosophila, infection stimulates the systemic release of a battery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). These fly immune effectors have been understudied as sleep modulators. We obtained mutants in different AMPs and characterized their functions in sleep and plasticity. AMP mutants slept less with a longer sleep latency, and lowered arousal thresholds. Group C mutant flies, doubly mutant for the anti-fungal peptides Metchnikowin (Mtk) and Drosomycin (Drs), showed the greatest impairments. These Group C mutants also showed an exaggerated sleep rebound, sleep rebound was unaltered in other mutants. While many classes of AMPs showed sleep deficits, different sets of AMP mutants exhibited specific disruptions in socialization and rocking induced sleep. To determine whether sleep amount and sleep functions were dissociable, we evaluated memory and quantified synapse abundance. Group C mutants uniquely exhibited normal learning and memory, and lower synapse abundance, despite sleeping the least. Group C mutants are thus able to carry out some sleep functions without sleeping much. Glial knockdown of Metchnikowin and Drosomycin mimicked the sleep phenotypes of the null mutants, these genes thus act from glia. While Group C mutants retained normal cognitive function, other AMP mutants showed impairments in sleep and memory. Sleep and memory defects in these AMP mutants were reversible - enhancing sleep of Bomanin mutants pharmacologically or behaviorally improved learning and memory. Together, these data suggest that AMPs are potent sleep modulators and that different classes of AMPs differently affect sleep and sleep dependent outcomes.

articles.title: GM-CSF and M-CSF driven differentiation differentially regulates Chikungunya virus infection and antiviral responses in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
articles.abstract: Chikungunya virus is an arthritogenic alphavirus causing debilitating joint pain in infected individuals. The mechanisms driving CHIKV-associated arthralgia is poorly understood, however, macrophages have been implicated as potential reservoirs of persistent viral material and mediators of immunopathology. Granulocyte Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (GM-CSF) and Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (M-CSF) are cytokines that serve as myeloid growth factors that bias macrophages toward pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory phenotypes, respectively. In this study, we examined how cytokine-driven macrophage differentiation via GM-CSF and M-CSF influences susceptibility to and responses against CHIKV infection in vitro. Using parallel donor-matched cultures of primary macrophages, we show that GM-CSF-differentiated macrophages are highly permissive to CHIKV and Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection and support robust viral replication, whereas M-CSF-differentiated macrophages are resistant to CHIKV replication and lack detectable levels of viral protein expression. Despite these differences, we observed pro-inflammatory, M1-skewing of CHIKV-infected macrophages, regardless of differentiation state. Interestingly, we observe higher production of IFNα and IP10/CXCL10 in M-CSF differentiated macrophages, suggesting that M-CSF promotes an antiviral state that restricts CHIKV infection. Stimulation of macrophages with double-stranded RNA (polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid; poly(I:C)), but not with single-stranded RNA (resiquimod, R848), recapitulated the antiviral cytokine and chemokine response induced by CHIKV infection. These findings suggest that dsRNA sensing plays a more prominent role than ssRNA sensing in driving the macrophage antiviral response to CHIKV. Together, these findings highlight macrophage differentiation as a critical determinant of CHIKV susceptibility and antiviral immunity in humans, with implications for understanding inflammatory pathogenesis during infection.

articles.title: Negative Pressure Wound Therapy After Extensive Debridement of a Pediatric Plantar Puncture-Wound Infection: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Puncture injuries of the pediatric foot can lead to deep soft-tissue infections with substantial morbidity, often requiring complex surgical management or reconstructive procedures. Although negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) is widely used in adults, its use in children remains limited, and reports of its use as definitive treatment for pediatric foot infections are rare. CASE REPORT We report the case of a 5-year-old girl who developed a severe plantar soft-tissue infection after stepping on a rusted nail. Radiographic evaluation excluded retained foreign material, whereas magnetic resonance imaging findings were suspicious for possible early osteomyelitis of the calcaneus. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics for a total of 6 weeks, along with tetanus immunoglobulin. Wound cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Surgical debridement was performed down to the tarsal bones, with removal of extensive necrotic tissue, including the fibularis brevis tendon. Postoperatively, NPWT was applied, with dressing changes twice weekly for 1 month. The wound demonstrated progressive granulation tissue formation and gradual reduction in size, ultimately achieving complete closure within approximately 2 months without the need for skin grafting or reconstructive surgery. At follow-up, the patient was pain-free, fully weight-bearing, and had full passive range of motion in the foot and ankle. Although active eversion was lost due to tendon sacrifice, no functional limitation or gait disturbance was observed. CONCLUSIONS This case suggests that NPWT, combined with timely and adequate debridement, may serve as component of definitive treatment for deep pediatric foot infections, potentially avoiding reconstructive procedures in selected patients.

articles.title: Non-invasive Temporal Interference Stimulation of the Hippocampus Ameliorates Recognition Memory Impairments in Chronic Restraint Stress Mice.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
articles.abstract: Memory impairment in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) leads to profound functional disability and poor clinical outcomes, yet effective non-invasive treatments specifically targeting this domain are lacking. In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate a non‑invasive neuromodulation strategy for memory impairments in depression. Specifically, we tested whether temporal interference stimulation (TIS), a technique capable of focally modulating deep brain structures, could alleviate memory impairments in a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model of depression. TIS at 40-Hz was applied to target the hippocampus. Memory performance was assessed using multiple behavioral tasks, and analyses including immunofluorescence, in vivo electrophysiology, western blot, and RNA‑sequencing were performed. We found that CRS stably induced depressive-like behaviors and impaired hippocampus-dependent memory, as evidenced by a reduced recognition index in the NOR test and decreased freezing time in the contextual FCT. These impairments coincided with hyperactivation of hippocampal inhibitory neurons and elevated gamma-band synchrony between bilateral DG regions. TIS significantly improved recognition memory, with a nonsignificant trend toward improvement in contextual fear memory, and attenuated the associated neural alterations, which shifted toward control levels. Concomitantly, TIS partially reversed CRS-induced changes in hippocampal gene expression related to synaptic function and upregulated GluN2B protein expression. Collectively, these findings support hippocampus-targeted TIS as a promising non-invasive neuromodulation approach and provide preclinical evidence for its potential to alleviate recognition memory impairments in depression.

articles.title: AI-powered Schizophrenia Screening with Consideration of Facial Feature and Privacy Protection.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Schizophrenia is a complex mental disorder, and early identification and intervention are crucial for improving patients' quality of life. Recently, the application of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in schizophrenia screening has attracted widespread attention. However, existing methods either prioritize privacy protection while neglecting facial features, which compromises screening efficiency, or focus on facial features without ensuring privacy protection, risking patient information leakage. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an AI-powered schizophrenia screening framework that integrates facial feature analysis with privacy protection, aiming to enhance both screening accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, we consider three facial regions, namely, the whole face, the upper face, and the upper left face, and apply illumination preprocessing to the collected images. Feature extraction is then performed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). For classification, we employ three mainstream classifiers: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB). Additionally, we propose a classifier weighted prediction model to further improve classification accuracy and robustness. Extensive experiments are conducted on two datasets, one with schizophrenia patients collected with smartphones at a hospital and the other with healthy individuals from the CAS PEAL-R1 dataset. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed scheme as measured by the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) and Precision-Recall (PR) curves, confusion matrices, sensitivity, and specificity, with 95% confidence intervals, and show that using only the upper left face causes no statistically significant loss in AUC compared with the whole face. We also investigate the impact of classifier weights and the screening time. Deployment challenges and future research directions are discussed at the end of this paper.

articles.title: Protocol for filament-induced transient middle cerebral artery occlusion with laser speckle imaging and outcome assessment in mice.
articles.abstract: The transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model in mice is important for investigating endogenous protective mechanisms and potential therapeutic strategies for ischemic stroke. Here, we present a protocol for verifying successful occlusion and reperfusion using filament-induced tMCAO, with real-time monitoring of cerebral blood flow by laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI). We also describe steps for neurological testing, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, and representative histological analyses for assessing ischemic brain injury and model quality. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Jiang et al.1.

articles.title: Associations between neighborhood cumulative environmental burden and stroke incidence and severity: the Brain Attack Surveillance in Corpus Christi (BASIC) Project.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate cumulative and interactive effects of neighborhood social and physical environment with incident stroke and initial stroke severity, overall and by race-ethnicity.

METHOD: All first-ever Mexican American (MA) and Non-Hispanic White (NHW) stroke cases between 2022-2024 in a biethnic population-based study were included. Census-tract level social vulnerability index (SVI) and physical environmental burden index (EBI) data came from the CDC (2022). Cumulative environmental burden was calculated by summing the ranks of SVI and EBI and converting to a percentile score ranging from 0-1. Poisson and linear regression models were used to estimate adjusted associations between the environmental burden indices and their interactions and stroke rates and stroke severity score, respectively.

RESULTS: Across 78 census tracts, 1,114 patients were included. Higher SVI was associated with higher stroke rates in the adjusted model, overall (90th vs 10th percentile RR=1.32, 95% CI 1.03, 1.69) and among MAs (RR=1.53, 95% CI 1.08, 2.16). Higher EBI was associated with lower stroke rates among NHWs (RR=0.78, 95% CI 0.61, 0.99) but not MAs. A multiplicative interaction between SVI and EBI was found (P=0.02). In neighborhoods with high EBI (90th percentile) but not low EBI, higher SVI was associated with higher stroke rates (RR=1.77, 95% CI 1.40, 2.23). No associations between environmental burden and stroke severity were found.

CONCLUSION: Neighborhood social environmental burden was associated with higher incident stroke rates, particularly among MAs and neighborhoods with higher physical environment burden. Findings suggest the potential importance of neighborhood social and physical environment in primary stroke prevention.

articles.title: Implementation strategies to accelerate the adoption, adherence to, and sustainment of critical care nephrology evidence-based practices.
Clinical effectiveness of outpatient cardiac rehabilitation according to myocardial injury after acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is recommended after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but whether its benefit differs by infarct size remains uncertain. We examined whether the effectiveness of CR varies according to peak creatine phosphokinase (CPK), a surrogate marker of myocardial injury.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 535 AMI survivors who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2015 and November 2025. Patients were divided into CR and non‑CR groups. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all‑cause death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or heart failure hospitalization. Patients were stratified by peak CPK (<2000 vs. ≥2000 U/L), and Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 535 patients, 165 (31%) participated in CR. CR was associated with lower MACE incidence in the overall cohort (hazard ratio [HR] 0.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.81, p = 0.01). In the high‑CPK subgroup, CR significantly reduced MACE (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.04-0.96, p = 0.04), whereas the low‑CPK subgroup showed only nonsignificant trend. Similar findings were observed in patients who underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

CONCLUSIONS: Outpatient CR was associated with improved outcomes after AMI, with greater benefit in patients with higher peak CPK. Myocardial injury severity may help identify patients most likely to benefit from CR.

articles.title: Ten commandments for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease.
Association of Second Anti-hypertensive Agent with Outcomes in People with CKD on ACEi/ARB Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB) are first-line treatment for hypertension in chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, guidelines do not recommend subsequent medication classes if additional blood pressure-lowering effect is desired.

METHODS: This target trial emulation using national outpatient data from the Veterans Health Administration from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2016, included adults with non-dialysis CKD stages G1-G5 on an ACEi/ARB who initiated treatment with a second antihypertensive medication, classified as a thiazide diuretic, loop diuretic, calcium channel blocker, or β-blocker. Outcomes included composite cardiovascular events (fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction or stroke, hospitalization for heart failure, coronary revascularization), all-cause death, and composite kidney outcomes (dialysis initiation, kidney transplantation, sustained creatinine doubling). Clinically important characteristics were included as covariates in the analysis.

RESULTS: Of 150,369 individuals already on ACEi/ARB treatment, 45,836 (30%) were prescribed a thiazide diuretic, 17,589 (12%) a loop diuretic, 33,172 (22%) a calcium channel blocker, and 53,772 (36%) a β-blocker. Those receiving thiazide diuretics and calcium channel blockers had the highest baseline blood pressure. Those receiving loop diuretics were more likely to have more advanced CKD or heart failure. Over a median (IQR) follow-up of 1282 (621, 1979) days, compared to thiazide diuretics, cardiovascular event risk was higher for calcium channel blockers, aHR 1.18 (95% CI 1.15-1.22), β-blockers, aHR 1.63 (95% CI 1.58-1.67), and loop diuretics, aHR 1.97 (95% CI 1.90-2.04). Composite kidney outcomes were also higher with calcium channel blockers, aHR 1.42 (95% CI 1.33-1.52), β-blockers, aHR 1.13 (95% CI 1.06-1.21), and loop diuretics, aHR 1.98 (95% CI 1.83-2.15).

CONCLUSIONS: Adding a thiazide diuretic rather than a calcium channel blocker, β-blocker, or loop diuretic on top of ACEi/ARB treatment was associated with favorable clinical outcomes among people with CKD.

articles.title: Four drugs, fewer pills, better outcomes? Interpreting real-world evidence in complex hypertension.
Health Care Utilization Among Patients With Coronary Artery Disease Using mHealth Wearable Devices: Feasibility Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although prior research has explored patient engagement with health care providers through software applications such as patient portals, the impact of patient engagement with mobile health (mHealth) technologies on subsequent utilization of health care resources remains poorly understood. Specifically, it remains unclear whether physiological data collected from wearable devices can be linked to future health care encounters across different modes of care utilization.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study was aimed at evaluating the feasibility of an mHealth prototype for analyzing cardiovascular disease outcomes and health care utilization among patients using digital health interventions. Specifically, we examined the feasibility of integrating physiological data from wearable devices to examine associations with future care utilization, offering early evidence for the effectiveness of patient engagement with mHealth platforms.

METHODS: Patients with a history of coronary artery disease were recruited from the cardiology clinic of a large academic medical center. Before data collection, the study coordinator trained 20 patients on the use of Garmin devices, of whom 19 were included in the analyses. Data collected from the use of wearable devices were analyzed together with electronic health record data. Patient health outcomes were tracked from June 2019 to May 2021, including approximately 1500 health care encounters that encompassed hospital and outpatient visits, telehealth visits, and other encounters. Beyond establishing the feasibility of the mHealth platform, this work provided preliminary evidence of associations between (1) mHealth device use and future health care utilization and (2) physiological data and the frequency of future health care encounters.

RESULTS: This study demonstrated the feasibility of an mHealth prototype for collecting and analyzing data to measure care utilization among patients with cardiovascular disease. Participants' use of the wearable mHealth device was associated with a statistically significant lower frequency of subsequent hospital and outpatient visits but greater utilization of other health care services, such as procedures, infusions, and medication refills, during the study period. However, none of these associations were statistically significant when the pretreatment period was restricted to the COVID-19 era. Minimum heart rate was associated with a higher frequency of future hospital and outpatient utilization, whereas activity time was associated with a higher frequency of procedural and refill visits.

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study provides preliminary evidence that mHealth device use is associated with a reduction in future inpatient and outpatient visits and an increase in the number of visits for other health care services. It also indicates that patients' physiological data, such as minimum heart rate and activity time, are associated with the frequency of future health care encounters. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory signals rather than statistically definitive conclusions. This study provides proof of concept that an integrated mHealth platform can generate physiologically meaningful measures associated with subsequent care utilization, supporting its potential as a scalable tool for patient engagement and care coordination.

articles.title: Global Statistics of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Autism Spectrum Disorder, and Conduct Disorder among School-Age Children from 1990-2021, with Forecasts to 2040.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders among school-age children represent a significant global health issue and substantially contribute to the global disease burden. This study aimed to examine the patterns and trends of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and conduct disorder (CD), which are commonly observed in school-age children, from 1990 to 2021, offering valuable insights for health policy formulation, medical resource allocation, and optimization of patient management strategies.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study for 21 regions and 204 countries, focusing on prevalence, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), gender, and different time periods to gain a deeper understanding of the health burden. We assessed correlations with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) and employed autoregressive integrated moving average modeling to forecast developments up to 2040, enabling us to better comprehend the burden and trends of these mental disorders.

RESULTS: In 2021, the prevalence rates of ADHD, ASD, and CD per 100,000 population among children aged 5-14 years were 2,374.8, 847.13, and 2,146.48, respectively; DALY rates were 29.17, 162.85, and 262.53, respectively. Compared to 1990, prevalence and DALY rates exhibited changes of -0.06, 0.03, and 0.04, respectively. Australia, Japan, and the UK exhibited particularly notable burdens, with the UK continuing to show rapid growth in ASD, while ADHD and CD increased rapidly in China and India, respectively. Gender and age analyses revealed a higher burden among males. Regions with high SDI displayed higher epidemiological indicators. For the 2040 forecast, the indicators for ADHD in terms of prevalence and DALYs are projected to be 3,796.65 and 44.33 for males, and 1,343.18 and 16.23 for females. For ASD, they are projected to be 1,103.04 and 215.23 for males, and 552.01 and 106.40 for females. For CD, they are projected to be 2,650.69 and 325.64 for males, and 1,593.57 and 200.41 for females.

CONCLUSION: This study underscores the complex epidemiological landscape of ADHD, ASD, and CD, revealing variations in burden across gender and geographical regions. It emphasizes the urgent need for healthcare professionals and policymakers to devise innovative prevention and healthcare strategies based on the current and evolving burden of these mental disorders, with the aim of alleviating the global disease burden.

articles.title: Long-Term Trends in Incidence, Attack Rates, and Early Case Fatality of Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: Dijon Stroke Registry (1985-2022).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a leading cause of disability and death worldwide. Understanding temporal trends in the burden of the disease is critical to evaluate the effectiveness of preventive strategies and identify targets for action. This study aimed to assess long-term temporal trends in incidence, attack rates, and early case fatality of ICH.

METHODS: All cases of ICH among residents of Dijon, France, were prospectively recorded between 1985 and 2022 using a population-based registry. Annual incidence and attack rates were assessed, and temporal trends were analyzed by calculating incidence rate ratio (IRR) and attack rate ratio (ARR). Case fatality was measured at 30 days.

RESULTS: A total of 1,015 ICH cases (mean age 73.5 ± 16.4 years old, 52.7% women) were recorded including 815 patients with a first-ever ICH and 200 cases of ICH as stroke recurrences. Age-standardized incidence increased progressively from 12.6/100,000/year in 1985-1991 to 20.8/100,000/year in 2011-2016 (IRR: 1.96, p < 0.001). A slight decrease was observed during period 2017-2022 (18.9/100,000/year, IRR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.61-1.06, p = 0.11). A similar trend was noted in attack rates, with a peak during 2011-2016 (27.9/100,000/year; ARR: 1.79; 95% CI: 1.47-2.20, p < 0.001) and a decrease in the most recent period (23.2/100,000/year; ARR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.69-0.99, p = 0.04). In men, a significant increase in incidence and attack rates was observed from 1985-1991 to 2011-2016, followed by a slight decline. In contrast, women showed a delayed increase in rates, with no decline in the most recent period. The 30-day case fatality rate declined between 1985 and 2010 (from 40.3% to 26.3%), followed by an increase thereafter, reaching 38.8% during the last study period.

CONCLUSION: Our study revealed an overall increase in incidence and attack rates of ICH followed by a slight decline in recent years. Sex differences in trends warrant further investigation into the contributing factors and emphasize the continued need for prevention strategies to further reduce the burden of ICH. The recent increase in early case fatality rates highlights the need for specific acute-phase treatments of ICH.

articles.title: Association between the Frequency of Individual Outdoor Activity and Risk of Incident Dementia in an Elderly Population in China: A National Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study explored the association between the frequency of individual outdoor activity and the risk of incident dementia in an elderly population in China. We aimed to provide scientific evidence to support non-pharmaceutical strategies for preventing or delaying the onset of dementia.

METHODS: A total of 8,758 participants (median age: 85 years) from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey were included in the analyses. We assessed the association between the frequency of individual outdoor activity and the risk of incident dementia using the Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses were performed, stratified by age, sex, and residence. Additionally, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings after excluding participants who, at baseline, had a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score <18 or had been diagnosed with stroke, other cerebrovascular diseases, diabetes mellitus, cancer, or Parkinson's disease.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up period of 4.33 years, 637 participants (7.27%) developed dementia. Compared with those who almost never engaged in outdoor activities, participants who engaged almost daily had a reduced risk of incident dementia by approximately 25% (HR: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.62-0.92). Subgroup analyses showed significant associations in females and participants living in cities and towns, whereas no significant differences were observed between age groups. The sensitivity analysis yielded results consistent with the primary analysis.

CONCLUSION: Frequent participation in individual outdoor activity may be associated with a reduced risk of dementia among the elderly in China. These findings support outdoor activity as a potential non-pharmaceutical strategy to delay cognitive decline and prevent dementia.

articles.title: Association between A Body Shape Index and the Prevalence of Stroke: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This investigation utilized cross-sectional NHANES data to explore the relationship between the A Body Shape Index (ABSI) and stroke, with a focus on age differences.

METHODS: A total of 40,213 participants from four NHANES cycles (2003-2018) were included in the analysis. Stroke status was determined via self-report, and ABSI was calculated using waist circumference, height, and weight measurements. To investigate the relationship between ABSI and stroke risk, we employed multivariate logistic regression models adjusted for potential confounders and used restricted cubic spline analysis to explore nonlinear associations. Additionally, subgroup analyses were conducted based on gender, age, race, and BMI.

RESULTS: Elevated ABSI was associated with higher odds of stroke (OR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.07-1.87, p = 0.002). When divided into quartiles, participants in the highest quartile (Q4) had a notably increased stroke risk compared to those in the lowest (Q1) (OR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.05-1.76, p = 0.005). Subgroup analyses revealed this association was especially pronounced across different genders, races and in individuals aged 40-59 (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.00-1.72, p = 0.04) and 60+ (OR = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.01-1.61, p = 0.004). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a nonlinear association between ABSI and the odds of stroke, with the odds increasing when ABSI exceeded 0.08.

CONCLUSION: Higher ABSI was associated with higher stroke prevalence, especially in the highest quartile and among individuals aged 40 and over, with a nonlinear increase observed when ABSI exceeded 0.08. Further longitudinal studies are needed to confirm the predictive value of ABSI.

articles.title: Trends and Impact of Early Medical Complications in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Data from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early medical complications following acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are common and might increase poststroke morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to evaluate trends in the prevalence of early medical complications over almost 2 decades and their impact on 3-month functional outcome and mortality.

METHODS: A total of 181,704 AIS patients from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry (2006-2024) were analyzed. Early medical complications included decompensated heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia, sepsis, pneumonia, urinary tract infection (UTI), deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. Functional outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) after 3 months, with favorable outcome defined as mRS ≤1. Associations between early medical complications and mRS were analyzed using multivariable Poisson regression models.

RESULTS: Among all patients, 16,279 (9.0%) had early medical complications. Pneumonia (4.2%), UTI (2.9%), cardiac arrhythmia (1.4%), and decompensated heart failure (1.4%) were most common, with significant declines in prevalence over time. Admission NIHSS scores decreased, and the use of intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy increased. Decompensated heart failure (RR = 1.85, 95% CI: 1.73-1.97, p < 0.001), sepsis (RR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.53-1.99, p < 0.001), pulmonary embolism (RR = 1.67, 95% CI: 1.33-2.10, p < 0.001), and pneumonia (RR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.57-1.72, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with 3-month mortality. Furthermore, the complications least associated with a favorable outcome were pneumonia (RR = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.32-0.41, p < 0.001), decompensated heart failure (RR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.32-0.46, p < 0.001), and sepsis (RR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.45-0.77, p < 0.001). The effect sizes did not change significantly through the observed years.

CONCLUSIONS: This study observed a significant reduction in the prevalence of early medical complications after AIS, especially decompensated heart failure, pneumonia, sepsis, and pulmonary embolism which continue to substantially affect mortality and functional outcome in AIS patients.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Digital Health Interventions on Rehabilitation Outcomes in Patients After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is the most effective treatment for end-stage knee osteoarthritis, but some patients continue to experience persistent postoperative pain, stiffness, and impaired functional recovery. Digital health interventions are increasingly used in rehabilitation after TKA, but their comparative effectiveness remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different digital health interventions on rehabilitation outcomes in patients after TKA and to compare and rank these interventions in terms of pain relief, active knee flexion range of motion (ROM), and knee function to provide evidence for selecting optimal rehabilitation strategies.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Google Scholar, Scopus, CINAHL, MEDLINE (via OvidSP), CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) meeting the inclusion criteria. The RoB 2 tool (Risk of Bias 2; Cochrane) was used to assess risk of bias, and the confidence in network meta-analysis (CINeMA) framework was used to evaluate certainty of evidence. Traditional meta-analysis and network meta-analysis (NMA) were performed using Stata (version 17.0; StataCorp LLC). A random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird method for estimating τ²) was consistently used across all analyses. For outcomes measured with the same or convertible scales, mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs were used to pool effect sizes. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values were calculated to summarize the ranking probabilities.

RESULTS: A total of 36 RCTs involving 3067 patients after TKA were included. NMA results showed that compared with conventional rehabilitation (CR), for active flexion ROM, rehabilitation robot (RR; MD 8.96, 95% CI 5.86-12.05), mobile app-based telerehabilitation (MAT; MD 6.36, 95% CI 2.81-9.91), and virtual reality (VR; MD 5.92, 95% CI 2.94-8.90) were significantly superior to CR; for the Hospital for Special Surgery knee score, VR (MD 9.53, 95% CI 5.18-13.88), intelligent rehabilitation system-based telerehabilitation (MD 6.90, 95% CI 2.35-11.44), and RR (MD 5.32, 95% CI 1.61-9.04) were significantly superior to CR; for pain, RR and MAT had relatively high ranking probabilities, but the 95% CIs of most comparisons included 0; for the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index and Timed Up and Go test, only internet videoconference-based telerehabilitation and VR-based telerehabilitation, respectively, were significantly superior to CR. The certainty of evidence for most comparisons was low or very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital health interventions may improve pain, active knee flexion ROM, and knee function in patients after TKA. In the SUCRA ranking, RR, VR, and MAT showed favorable ranking probabilities; however, because the network was predominantly star-shaped and the rankings were derived largely from indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted as suggestive rather than definitive. Further high-quality studies with direct head-to-head comparisons are needed.

articles.title: Effects of a Personalized Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot on Information Needs in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving dialysis for chronic kidney disease encounter complex self-management challenges and ongoing information needs that traditional health care often fails to meet. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances the factual accuracy of large language models (LLMs), but whether personalized RAG is more effective than general RAG remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess whether personalized constraint retrieval-augmented generation (C-RAG) is more effective than open-domain general retrieval-augmented generation (O-RAG) and standard care in reducing information needs among patients receiving dialysis and to identify predictors of chatbot engagement.

METHODS: A sequential 2-phase mixed methods study was conducted. Phase 1 evaluated 4 LLMs (Claude 3.5 Sonnet [Anthropic], Gemini 1.5 Flash [Google], CLOVA X [NAVER], and ChatGPT-4o [OpenAI]) using 60 patient-generated questions, assessed by 15 clinical experts. Phase 2 was a 3-arm parallel pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT; October-December 2025) at 3 tertiary hospitals in South Korea. Based on phase 1 findings, 2 chatbot variants were developed using GPT-4o-C-RAG, which incorporates patient-specific clinical parameters, and O-RAG, which uses the same knowledge base without personalization. Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to C-RAG, O-RAG, or standard care. The primary outcome, change in medication, dietary, and diagnostic information needs (5-point Likert scales) from baseline to 4 weeks, was analyzed using ANCOVA. Semistructured interviews with 9 participants explored underlying mechanisms.

RESULTS: ChatGPT-4o achieved the highest scores in clinical accuracy (mean 3.60, SD 0.95), safety (mean 3.67, SD 1.00), and readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 9.8, compared with 13.2-14.5 for other models). In phase 2, 42/45 (93%) enrolled participants completed the study (14 per group). ANCOVA revealed significant group differences in medication (F2,38=4.574, P=.02) and dietary (F2,38=4.232, P=.02) information needs. In Bonferroni-corrected comparisons, C-RAG had lower needs than O-RAG in both domains (observed mean 2.93, SD 1.21 vs mean 3.86, SD 0.95; Cohen d=-0.86, 95% CI -1.63 to -0.08; P=.02 for both). Against control, C-RAG showed medium-to-large but nonsignificant effects (medication Cohen d=-0.64, 95% CI -1.39 to 0.12; dietary Cohen d=-0.54, 95% CI -1.30 to 0.21). Secondary outcomes did not differ between groups. Dietary management emerged as the most frequent query topic, accounting for 29.3% (205/691) of total queries. Participants on dialysis for 1-3 years showed higher engagement (9/10, 90% engagement for 1-3 y vs 5/18, 27.8% for ≥4 y; Fisher exact P=.006). Qualitative analysis revealed 5 themes, including dietary management as the primary need and dialysis duration as a moderator of utility.

CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot trial, personalized RAG showed lower information needs than general RAG, with a large effect size (Cohen d=-0.86). The medium-to-large effects against standard care (Cohen d=-0.54 to -0.64) support a fully powered confirmatory trial (estimated 50-55 participants per group) to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Bloodstream Infection Pathogen Profiles in ICU and Non-ICU Patients in a Tertiary Hospital in Southern Anhui, China.
articles.abstract: Bloodstream infection (BSI) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in intensive care unit (ICU) patients. We retrospectively analyzed 723 adults with blood culture-confirmed BSI from January 2025 to March 2026, including 253 ICU and 470 non-ICU patients, and compared clinical characteristics, infection sources, invasive procedures, pathogen distribution, antimicrobial use, resistance phenotypes, and antimicrobial susceptibility. ICU patients had higher rates of septic shock and in-hospital mortality and more frequent catheter-related and lower respiratory tract infections and invasive procedures. Gram-negative bacteria predominated in both groups, with Escherichia coli ranking first. Coagulase-negative staphylococci, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterococcus spp. accounted for larger proportions in ICU patients. Special-use antimicrobial use, particularly carbapenem use, was higher in the ICU. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa were significantly more frequent in ICU patients, whose major Gram-negative isolates also showed broader resistance profiles. These findings support care-setting-specific pathogen and resistance surveillance to inform empirical antimicrobial therapy, antimicrobial stewardship, and infection-control strategies.

articles.title: Deep-Learning Analysis of Peripheral Blood Smear for Prediction of Acute Inflammatory States and Chronic Comorbidities: Development and Internal Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral blood smear (PBS) examination provides morphological information on immune cells that reflects systemic pathophysiology, yet whether it can be used to predict systemic states has not been systematically established.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate an integrated deep learning framework that leverages cell-level morphology from routine PBS examinations to discriminate acute inflammatory states and chronic comorbidities.

METHODS: An integrated deep learning framework was developed for PBS analysis, in which cell-level morphological features were extracted and aggregated into slide-level representations to predict systemic states. A total of 51,369 PBS examinations were used for self-supervised cell-level pretraining and 9211 for slide-level downstream tasks. Outcomes comprised acute inflammatory states and chronic comorbidities. Acute inflammatory states included white blood cell (WBC) count (categorized as low, normal, or high), elevated C-reactive protein (CRP), elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and septic shock. Chronic comorbidities included the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetes mellitus (DM). Discriminative performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with 95% CIs, computed on the test set of the development dataset and on the holdout dataset. The framework was compared with a demographic model based on age and sex and with a cell-type-only model without morphological features. As a secondary analysis, temporal validation was performed using a chronological split.

RESULTS: The framework discriminated acute inflammatory states, achieving development and holdout AUROCs of 0.852 (95% CI 0.836-0.867) and 0.849 (0.833-0.864) for WBC count, 0.891 (0.870-0.913) and 0.896 (0.876-0.915) for CRP, 0.838 (0.794-0.878) and 0.844 (0.799-0.882) for ESR, and 0.849 (0.807-0.886) and 0.822 (0.783-0.853) for septic shock. Discrimination of chronic comorbidities was more modest but consistent across the 2 datasets, with AUROCs of 0.792 (0.762-0.818) and 0.781 (0.751-0.808) for CCI, 0.696 (0.665-0.727) and 0.680 (0.654-0.708) for CVD, 0.724 (0.690-0.755) and 0.728 (0.696-0.756) for CKD, and 0.645 (0.610-0.680) and 0.638 (0.603-0.674) for DM. The framework significantly outperformed the cell-type-only model for all outcomes in both datasets but did not significantly outperform the demographic model for CVD in the holdout dataset or for DM in either dataset. AUROCs in the temporal holdout dataset ranged from 0.621 for DM to 0.883 for CRP, consistent with those in the temporal development test set (0.666 to 0.889).

CONCLUSIONS: An integrated deep learning framework for automated PBS analysis can provide information associated with inflammation-related laboratory results and clinical outcomes, with stronger discrimination for acute inflammatory states than for chronic comorbidities. These exploratory findings suggest the potential of deep learning-based PBS analysis as a novel approach to assessing systemic states in clinical practice.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation in chronic kidney disease - treatment standard.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: The prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF) is high among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). While patients with CKD Stages G1 - G3b may be treated similarly to patients without CKD, little evidence guides therapeutic strategies for CKD G4 - G5 patients. Dosing of most drugs used for rate and rhythm control requires adjustment to kidney function. Recurrence rates after cardioversion and ablation for rhythm control are higher in patients with advanced CKD than those without it. Regarding the prevention of stroke and systemic embolism, the benefit-to-risk ratio of oral anticoagulation (OAC) is disputed among patients with CKD stages G4 - G5 with AF, in particular among those receiving hemodialysis given their high risk for severe bleeding events. Novel strategies for stroke and systemic embolism prevention, particularly factor XI inhibitors and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), have not yet fulfilled their initial promise as safe and effective alternatives.

articles.title: Multimodal Nursing Care for Stroke Caregivers: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is one of the most devastating neurological conditions worldwide, leaving survivors dependent on family members for long-term care. Family caregivers of stroke survivors in India frequently experience significant physical, emotional, social, and financial burdens, particularly during the hospital-to-home transition, with little structured support available. To address this gap, the Multimodal Approach to Nursing Care (MANC) module was developed as a structured nurse-led intervention combining caregiver education, medical device management training, psychosocial support, and progressive muscle relaxation techniques.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop and validate the MANC module and evaluate its effectiveness in reducing caregiver burden and stress, and improving quality of life and caregiving competence among family caregivers of patients with cerebrovascular accident (CVA), compared with routine caregiving practices.

METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial will be conducted at the Acharya Vinoba Bhave Rural Hospital in Sawangi, Wardha, India. Ninety family caregivers of patients with CVA will be randomly allocated into experimental (n=45) and control (n=45) groups. Allocation concealment will be maintained through sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes. Given the single-researcher study design, complete blinding is not feasible. All outcome measures are standardized self-reported instruments, minimizing assessment bias. Outcomes include caregiver burden, stress, quality of life, caregiving competence, and patient health outcomes, assessed at baseline and postintervention. Data will be analyzed using appropriate parametric and nonparametric tests, with significance set at P<.05.

RESULTS: Ethical approval was obtained from the Institutional Ethics Committee, Datta Meghe Institute of Higher Education and Research (Deemed University) in December 2024 (IEC number DMIHER(DU)/IEC/2024/53), and the trial was registered with the Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI/2025/07/090412). Data collection commenced in February 2026, and recruitment is currently ongoing. Results are expected to be submitted for publication by the end of 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: The MANC intervention is anticipated to reduce caregiver burden and stress while improving quality of life and caregiving competence among family caregivers of stroke survivors, potentially serving as a replicable model for poststroke transitional care across Indian tertiary care settings.

articles.title: Circulating inflammatory proteins mediate the causal relationship between blood alliin and cancer: A two-step, multivariable Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: An association has been found between alliin and reduced risks of various cancers; however, evidence for these causal relationships remain limited. This study utilized Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to assess the potential causal relationships between circulating alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers. We selected instrumental variables from the latest and largest European genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets. First, we comprehensively assessed the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers through two-sample MR analysis. Subsequently, we repeated the validation of instrumental variables using cancer GWAS statistics from different studies and merged the results by meta-analysis. Two-step MR analysis was used to investigate whether 91 inflammatory proteins mediate the effect of alliin on the risk of cancer. Finally, multivariable MR analysis was conducted to determine the direct effects of alliin on the risk of cancer, with adjustment for potential mediators. Inverse variance weighted results were considered the primary observation outcome, and additional sensitivity analyses were conducted. Increased blood alliin levels were significantly causally associated with decreased risks of prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer, lymphoma, and colorectal cancer, with the corresponding meta-analyses also showing significant associations. In the two-step MR analysis, chemokine ligand 23 (CCL23) and oncostatin M (OSM) as well as interleukin-12B (IL12B) were the key mediators of the inverse causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of prostate cancer as well as the risks of ovarian and colorectal cancers, respectively. STAM-binding protein was a key mediator of the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of lymphoma. The results of this study support that increased blood alliin levels can reduce the risks of multiple cancers, with circulating inflammatory proteins potentially mediating this association.

articles.title: FEV1 mediates the effect of major depressive disorder on asthma phenotypes: Mendelian randomization.
articles.abstract: The causal effect between major depressive disorder (MDD) and asthma phenotypes was rarely evaluated. The objective of our study was to not only assess the potential causal links of MDD on asthma phenotypes, but also the mediating effect of forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) on asthma phenotypes caused by MDD. By using 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), Bayesian weighted MR, and mediation analysis, we explored the potential causal effect of MDD and the mediating effect of FEV1 on asthma phenotypes (childhood asthma, adult asthma, obesity asthma, allergic asthma, and nonallergic asthma) from the genome-wide association studies database. Furthermore, genetic correlation was also evaluated by the analysis of linkage disequilibrium score regression. We additionally performed multivariable MR (MVMR) analyses including body mass index and smoking to evaluate MDD estimates for asthma phenotypes. The results of univariable MR and MVMR analyses supported associations of MDD with adult asthma, obesity asthma, and allergic asthma, and MVMR analysis indicated the potential association of MDD with child asthma and nonallergic asthma. FEV1 indicated a mediated effect of MDD on adult asthma, obesity asthma, allergic asthma, and nonallergic asthma. Our analyses supported associations of MDD with asthma phenotypes. The mediation analysis suggested that FEV1 may mediate part of these associations of MDD on adult asthma, obesity asthma, allergic asthma, and nonallergic asthma.

articles.title: Clinically suspected acute myocarditis with ST-segment elevation, multiorgan dysfunction, and reversible conduction disturbance in an older patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: ST-segment elevation and marked myocardial injury require urgent exclusion of coronary occlusion. Maintenance hemodialysis adds metabolic, volume, biomarker, and bleeding-related uncertainty.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 70-year-old woman receiving thrice-weekly hemodialysis developed chest tightness, dyspnea, and upper abdominal pain during dialysis. She returned with recurrent symptoms, severe metabolic acidosis, lactate 21 mmol/L, ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3, and troponin I that increased from 13,019.45 to >25,000 ng/L.

DIAGNOSES: Coronary angiography showed unobstructed epicardial arteries with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction grade 3 flow. Clinically suspected acute myocarditis remained the leading working diagnosis, but cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and endomyocardial biopsy were not performed and other causes of myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries could not be definitively excluded. The course was complicated by pulmonary congestion, metabolic and volume instability, hepatic injury, suspected pancreatic involvement, gastrointestinal bleeding, and symptomatic sinus arrest.

INTERVENTIONS: Antithrombotic therapy was reassessed after angiography and withheld when bleeding developed. Early continuous venovenous hemofiltration was performed without circuit anticoagulation, with heparin reintroduced later when clinically appropriate. Continuous renal replacement therapy was used for volume, electrolyte, and acid-base support. A temporary transvenous pacemaker was implanted for telemetry-confirmed sinus arrest with a maximum pause of 8.78 seconds.

OUTCOMES: The maximum R-R interval decreased to 1.97 seconds, permitting pacemaker removal. At approximately 3 months, syncope had not recurred, but persistent atrial fibrillation, New York Heart Association class III symptoms, and an left ventricular ejection fraction of 47% indicated incomplete cardiac recovery.

LESSONS: In a hemodialysis patient with a ST-elevation myocardial infarction-like presentation and non-obstructive coronary arteries, subsequent management should combine a structured myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries differential with explicit diagnostic uncertainty and repeated reassessment of bleeding, metabolic, volume, infectious, and rhythm-related risks.

articles.title: Tirofiban combined with heparin versus heparin alone in acute coronary syndrome patients undergoing emergency PCI: A retrospective study of no-reflow and myocardial perfusion.
articles.abstract: The no-reflow phenomenon is an important complication of emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndrome (ACS). We examined the association between adjunctive tirofiban and in-hospital angiographic and electrocardiographic reperfusion indicators. This single-center retrospective observational study included 186 ACS patients who underwent emergency PCI between January 2021 and December 2024. According to perioperative antithrombotic treatment, patients were divided into a tirofiban plus heparin group (n = 92) and a heparin-alone group (n = 94). Because treatment assignment was nonrandom and determined by the treating interventional cardiologist, the analysis was designed to estimate associations rather than causal treatment effects. For the no-reflow outcome, a parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for clinically relevant measured confounders, including diabetes mellitus, symptom-to-balloon time > 6 hours, high thrombus burden, and pre-PCI thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (grade/flow) (TIMI) 0-1 flow. No-reflow was recorded in 8/92 (8.7%) versus 20/94 (21.3%) patients (P = .016). Final TIMI grade 3 flow occurred in 91.3% versus 79.8% (P = .028); myocardial blush grade 2-3 in 84.8% versus 68.1% (P = .008); TIMI myocardial perfusion grade 2-3 in 82.6% versus 66.0% (P = .010); and ST-segment resolution > 70% in 65.2% versus 47.9% (P = .017). The originally reported adjusted odds ratio for no-reflow associated with tirofiban was 0.36 (95% confidence interval 0.14-0.90; P = .029). Bleeding Academic Research Consortium major bleeding occurred in 3/92 (3.3%) versus 2/94 (2.1%; P = .679); Bleeding Academic Research Consortium minor bleeding in 6/92 (6.5%) versus 5/94 (5.3%; P = .733). These small event counts do not establish comparable safety. In ACS patients undergoing emergency PCI, tirofiban plus heparin was associated with a lower incidence of intraoperative no-reflow and with improved surrogate markers of epicardial and myocardial reperfusion compared with heparin alone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies with standardized treatment protocols and longer-term clinical follow-up.

articles.title: Construction of a nomogram for predicting pathological upgrading after LEEP in patients with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 based on colposcopic morphological features: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grade 1/2 diagnosed by colposcopy-directed biopsy may underestimate the final lesion grade found on excision. In patients who proceed to Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP), postoperative pathology may show histopathological upgrading relative to the preoperative biopsy. Although HPV testing and ThinPrep Cytology Test (TCT) are standard screening tools, their differential value in this LEEP-selected CIN1/2 population remains unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with pathological upgrading after LEEP and to construct an internally validated nomogram based on colposcopic morphological features. We retrospectively analyzed 122 patients who underwent LEEP for clinical indications between 2020 and 2025 with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2. Pathological upgrading was defined as biopsy CIN1 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN2, or biopsy CIN2 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN3 (invasive carcinoma included). These 2 transitions were prespecified and are clinically distinct; event counts were, therefore, also reported by baseline biopsy grade. Multivariable logistic regression was used to develop a nomogram. Discrimination and calibration were assessed with ROC analysis and bootstrap internal validation; clinical utility was explored with decision curve analysis (DCA). Pathological upgrading occurred in 46/122 (37.7%) patients in this LEEP-selected cohort, including 4/15 (26.7%) with baseline CIN1 and 42/107 (39.3%) with baseline CIN2. In the multivariable model, Reid Colposcopic Index (OR = 1.41, P = .013) and number of involved quadrants (OR = 1.93, P = .018) were significantly associated with upgrading, whereas menopausal status (OR = 2.83, P = .059) and biopsy count (OR = 0.70, P = .068) did not reach conventional significance but were retained as candidate predictors. HPV genotype category and TCT were not significantly associated with upgrading. The nomogram showed apparent AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.719-0.883) on internal evaluation; calibration and DCA supported exploratory clinical utility within this surgical cohort. In women with biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 who already had indications for LEEP, colposcopic morphological features (Reid score and lesion extent) were more informative than HPV/TCT for predicting histopathological upgrading after excision. The nomogram may assist risk stratification within this selected surgical population. An ROC-derived probability threshold of 43% is presented only as an exploratory cut-point requiring external validation and should not yet be used as a standalone rule to choose observation vs LEEP in unselected CIN1/2 patients.

articles.title: Metabolic abnormalities and colorectal cancer: An integrated secondary analysis triangulating Mendelian randomization with global burden and temporal trends.
articles.abstract: Metabolic abnormalities are plausible and modifiable contributors to colorectal cancer (CRC), but genetic evidence and population-level burden data are often reported separately. This integrated secondary analysis triangulated Mendelian randomization (MR), Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates, metabolic risk attribution, estimated annual percentage change analyses, geographic and Socio-demographic Index (SDI) comparisons, and observed age-standardized mortality trends to characterize the relationship between metabolic abnormalities and CRC from 1990 to 2021. Genetically predicted body mass index (BMI), diabetes, and familial combined hyperlipidemia (FCHL) were positively associated with CRC risk in inverse-variance weighted MR analyses, with the strongest association observed for BMI. The diabetes (odds ratio = 1.002, 95% confidence interval = 1.001-1.003) and FCHL (odds ratio = 1.0010, 95% confidence interval = 1.0003-1.0017) estimates were statistically significant but extremely close to the null, indicating minimal individual-level effect sizes on the genetic-liability scale and no basis for inferring clinically meaningful risk differences. Globally, CRC incident cases increased substantially from 916,584 in 1990 to 2,194,143 in 2021, while the age-standardized death rate declined from 15.56 to 12.40 per 100,000 population. China showed a particularly steep increase in incident cases and age-standardized incidence rate. Across SDI strata, CRC incidence rose in all strata except high-SDI settings, whereas diabetes incidence increased in every region and stratum. Low-middle SDI settings showed the clearest ecological co-burden, with rising CRC and diabetes burden occurring together. Age-specific analyses showed that CRC burden attributable to high BMI and high fasting plasma glucose increased sharply with age, with the highest attributable death and disability-adjusted life-year rates in the oldest age groups. Observed global CRC age-standardized death rates declined from 1990 to 2021 for both sexes combined, males, and females. These findings support metabolic health as an important and actionable component of CRC prevention, particularly in settings where CRC and diabetes burdens are rising in parallel. The population-level findings should be interpreted as ecological co-burden rather than proof of interaction, and the MR estimates reflect lifelong genetic liability rather than clinical relative risks. In particular, the diabetes and FCHL estimates should not be interpreted as clinically meaningful individual-level effects.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of fexuprazan versus esomeprazole for healing of endoscopic submucosal dissection-induced artificial gastric ulcers: A multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a standard treatment for gastric neoplasms but creates artificial ulcers requiring potent acid suppression. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) provide rapid and sustained acid suppression. This study compared the efficacy and safety of fexuprazan, a novel P-CAB, with esomeprazole for the healing of artificial gastric ulcers after ESD.

METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial enrolled patients who underwent gastric ESD. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either fexuprazan 40 mg or esomeprazole 40 mg once daily for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was the ulcer healing rate at 8 weeks. Secondary endpoints included the incidence of delayed bleeding and adverse events.

RESULTS: Of 105 randomized patients, 90 were included in the full analysis set (FAS) and 85 in the per-protocol set (PPS). At 8 weeks, the complete healing rate (scar stage) in the PPS was 92.68% (38/41) in the fexuprazan group and 95.45% (42/44) in the esomeprazole group (95% confidence interval: 80.08-98.46 vs 84.53-99.44, P = .67), with an absolute difference of -2.77 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -15.32-8.85). Results were consistent in the FAS (93.02% vs 95.74%, 95% confidence interval: 80.94-98.54 vs 85.46-99.48, P = .67), with an absolute difference of -2.72 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -14.75-8.27). At 8 weeks, no patients in either group remained in the active stage. No delayed bleeding occurred in either group. Treatment-emergent adverse events were minimal and similar between groups (2.00% vs 4.08%, P > .62), with no serious adverse events.

CONCLUSION: Fexuprazan 40 mg once daily showed no statistically significant difference from esomeprazole 40 mg for healing ESD-induced artificial gastric ulcers, with a favorable safety profile. These findings indicate that fexuprazan serves as a reasonable candidate for further investigation as a potential treatment option to proton pump inhibitors for post-ESD ulcer healing.

articles.title: Obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome-associated stasis dermatitis of the lower extremities: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: To investigate the association between obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) and stasis dermatitis (SD) of the lower extremities and to elucidate the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 33-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of recurrent bilateral lower-extremity edema, vesicles, hyperpigmentation, and ulceration with delayed healing. He also reported 15 years of loud snoring during sleep, accompanied by nocturnal arousals and excessive daytime sleepiness.

DIAGNOSES: Polysomnography revealed severe OSAHS, with an apnea-hypopnea index of 131.8 events/h, mean oxygen saturation of 73%, and a nadir oxygen saturation of 46%. The patient was diagnosed with severe OSAHS, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, type II respiratory failure, and lower-extremity stasis dermatitis with infected ulceration.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient was treated with noninvasive ventilation (bilevel positive airway pressure in spontaneous/timed mode). Diuretic therapy, medication adjustment, and specialized wound care were also provided.

OUTCOMES: After six months of treatment, complete epithelialization of the dermatological lesions was achieved, accompanied by a 26 kg reduction in body weight. Significant improvements were observed in daytime hypersomnolence and respiratory function.

LESSONS: OSAHS may be associated with SD of the lower extremities and may exacerbate its clinical manifestations. NIV therapy may improve ventilation, circulatory status, and oxygenation, thereby contributing to improved SD outcomes. In obese patients or those with SD that responds poorly to conventional treatment, clinicians should consider screening for OSAHS to reduce the risk of missed diagnoses and facilitate comprehensive management.

articles.title: Association between systemic immune-inflammation index and skeletal muscle mass in patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is characterized by excessive liver fat accumulation, which is associated with inflammatory responses and metabolic disruptions that may affect skeletal muscle mass. However, the specific relationship between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and skeletal muscle mass in NAFLD patients remains unclear. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using data from the 2017 to 2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The study comprised 673 adults with confirmed NAFLD who met inclusion criteria and had complete data on SII and skeletal muscle mass. Generalized weighted linear regression models were employed to assess the association, with adjustment for multiple covariates including demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. After controlling for covariates, regression analysis revealed a significant independent negative correlation between SII and muscle mass (β = -0.037, 95% confidence interval [CI] = -0.055 to -0.019, P < .001). Smooth curve analysis indicated an approximately linear relationship, with an inflection point at 536.63 (1000 cells/μL). Subgroup analyses showed more pronounced negative correlations in males (β = -0.045, 95% CI = -0.073 to -0.018, P = .001) and non-Hispanic white individuals (β = -0.129, 95% CI = -0.193 to -0.065, P < .001). Our findings provide evidence of an independent negative association between SII and skeletal muscle mass in NAFLD patients, suggesting that systemic immune inflammation may contribute to muscle loss in this population.

articles.title: Surgical management and short-term clinical and radiological outcomes in patients with cervical spondylodiscitis: A single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Cervical spondylodiscitis (CSD) is a rare but increasingly prevalent spinal infection that may cause rapid neurological deterioration because of its nonspecific clinical presentation. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term clinical and radiological outcomes of surgically treated CSD and to explore whether the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-surgery interval was associated with postoperative neurological recovery. This retrospective single-center cohort study included 25 consecutive patients who underwent surgical management for CSD between January 2016 and December 2025. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the visual analogue scale and modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score. Radiological outcomes were evaluated by measuring the local cervical kyphosis angle. Patients were stratified according to the MRI-to-surgery interval (≤24 vs >24 hours). Surgical treatment significantly improved pain, neurological function, inflammatory markers, and cervical sagittal alignment. Mean visual analogue scale scores decreased from 6.0 to 3.4 (P < .01), whereas mean mJOA scores increased from 10.68 to 14.08 (P < .01). The mean local cervical kyphosis angle improved by 5.5° (P < .01). The change in mJOA score did not differ statistically between patients undergoing surgery within 24 hours and those undergoing surgery >24 hours after MRI acquisition (P = .518); however, the timing analysis was limited by the small subgroup sizes and baseline differences in neurological status. Surgical management of CSD was associated with significant short-term clinical and radiological improvement. Although postoperative outcomes did not differ significantly according to the MRI-to-surgery interval, these findings should not be interpreted as supporting delayed surgery once surgical indications are established.

articles.title: Association between arthritis and asthma: An observational analysis of NHANES and a Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Observational studies have linked arthritis and asthma, but establishing causality is challenging due to confounding. We analyzed 30,001 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2003-2018) using survey-weighted logistic regression to assess observational associations. To infer causality, we conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis using publicly available genetic data. In the observational analysis, arthritis was significantly associated with a higher risk of asthma (adjusted odds ratio = 1.96, 95% confidence interval = 1.75-2.19), with similar findings for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA). Mendelian randomization analysis provided evidence for a positive causal effect of genetic predisposition to RA on asthma (inverse-variance weighted odds ratio = 1.037, 95% confidence interval = 1.007-1.068), but found no significant causal effect for OA. This study provides dual evidence supporting a significant and potentially causal relationship between RA and asthma. In contrast, the association with OA appears to be noncausal, likely driven by confounding factors.

articles.title: When hypertensive crisis mimics septic shock: A case report of pheochromocytoma-induced severe lactic acidosis following GLP-1 receptor agonist administration.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting tumor that may present atypically with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory features, closely mimicking sepsis and delaying diagnosis. A possible interaction with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists has been suggested but remains poorly understood.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 48-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with acute nausea, vomiting, chills, severe abdominal pain, and hypertensive crisis within hours of self-administering tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist. She was febrile, tachycardic, and markedly hypertensive, with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory markers suggestive of sepsis.

DIAGNOSES: Initial evaluation favored sepsis; however, negative cultures, sustained severe hypertension, hyperlactatemia disproportionate to perfusion status, and elevated urinary normetanephrines redirected the evaluation toward an endocrine cause. The clinical and biochemical picture supported a diagnosis of probable pheochromocytoma. Imaging revealed a fat-containing left adrenal mass initially suggestive of myelolipoma, representing a diagnostic pitfall.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient was managed with intravenous fluids, a continuous nicardipine infusion, and oral alpha-blockade with doxazosin. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics were started and later discontinued as infection became unlikely. Beta-blockade was withheld until adequate alpha-blockade was achieved. Supportive care and electrolyte correction were provided.

OUTCOMES: Blood pressure and lactate improved over 48 hours with clinical stabilization. The patient was discharged on oral alpha-blockade with plans for outpatient functional imaging (64Cu-DOTATATE positron emission tomography) and definitive surgical evaluation.

LESSONS: Pheochromocytoma should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained lactic acidosis and hypertensive crisis, even when sepsis appears likely. Catecholamine-driven type B lactic acidosis can closely mimic infectious shock. Fat-containing adrenal lesions do not exclude pheochromocytoma, and biopsy should be avoided. The temporal association with GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure is hypothesis-generating and warrants further investigation as use of these agents continues to expand.

articles.title: Pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block with lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) block versus fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) for hip surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective analgesia that preserves motor function is essential for early mobilization after hip surgery. Although fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) is recommended for total hip arthroplasty, the comparative efficacy of combined pericapsular nerve group and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve blocks (PENG + LFCN) remains uncertain.

METHODS: Databases including Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Central, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched up to December 8, 2024. Statistical analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan) (computer program, version 5.4, The Cochrane Collaboration, 2020).

RESULTS: Seven randomized controlled trials involving 572 participants were included. Compared with FICB, PENG + LFCN significantly reduced static pain at 12 hours (mean difference [MD] = -0.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.28 to -0.11; P < .0001) and dynamic pain at 6 hours (MD = -0.87; 95% CI, -1.64 to -0.10; P = .03) and 48 hours (MD = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.49 to -0.02; P = .03). It also lowered quadriceps weakness (odds ratio = 0.09; 95% CI, 0.04-0.21; P < .00001), improved limb strength (MD = 1.03; 95% CI, 0.05-2.01; P = .04), reduced patient-controlled intravenous analgesia frequency (MD = -1.64; 95% CI, -3.13 to -0.15; P = .03), and shortened mobilization time (MD = -9.04; 95% CI, -14.28 to -3.80; P = .0007).

CONCLUSION: PENG + LFCN may provide superior early analgesia and better preserve lower-limb motor function than FICB after hip surgery. However, the evidence is limited by few trials, small sample sizes, and substantial heterogeneity. Larger, adequately powered trials are warranted.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: An aggregated analysis of published case reports and case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To explore the clinical characteristics and prognostic factors of denosumab-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (DRONJ).
