METHODS: Published case studies about DRONJ were retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, and WANFANG, and relevant information was extracted for analysis. The search covered the period from the inception of each database to November 1, 2024. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to identify prognostic factors for DRONJ.

RESULTS: A total of 31 articles were included in this study. Of the 110 patients with DRONJ, 57 (51.8%) healed completely. Logistic regression analysis showed that diabetes (odds ratio [OR] 4.29, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.18-15.63, P = .027) and corticosteroid use (OR 3.44, 95%CI 1.03-11.50, P = .045) were significantly associated with a poor treatment outcome, while surgical treatment (OR 0.19, 95%CI 0.07-0.54, P = .002) was significantly associated with a lower risk of poor prognosis.

CONCLUSION: Diabetes, corticosteroid use, and surgical intervention might be associated with the prognosis of DRONJ. Given that the study was based on published case studies, the generalizability of the results should be interpreted with caution due to a high risk of publication and selection bias.

articles.title: A bibliometric analysis of haemocoagulase: Trends, impact, and future directions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemocoagulase is extensively employed for the prophylaxis and management of surgical hemorrhage owing to its favorable safety profile, rapid onset of action, and sustained therapeutic effect. However, this agent exhibits a unique pharmacological duality: despite its primary hemostatic action, it paradoxically carries a risk of inducing bleeding. Furthermore, a specific subtype of haemocoagulase possesses anticoagulant and thrombolytic properties and is utilized in the treatment of ischemic cerebrovascular diseases and sudden sensorineural hearing loss.

METHOD: Publications on haemocoagulase and related thrombin-like enzyme preparations were identified in the Science Citation Index Expanded database of the Web of Science Core Collection. The structured search was limited to English-language articles and reviews published between 1 January, 1971 and 2 November, 2025. The search combined haemocoagulase, batroxobin, reptilase, venombin A, and closely related terminology. Records were screened by title and abstract, and the final dataset was analyzed bibliometrically. CiteSpace was used for reference and keyword clustering, timeline visualization, and citation burst detection; VOSviewer was used for co-authorship and keyword co-occurrence networks.

RESULTS: The bibliometric dataset comprised 489 publications contributed by 2037 authors at 565 institutions in 40 countries or regions. China, Capital Medical University, researcher B Blombäck, and the journal *Thrombosis Research* as key contributors; early studies focused on thrombin and anticoagulation therapy, while current research emphasizes serine proteases, fibrinogen, and snake venom-related studies.

CONCLUSION: This bibliometric analysis systematically characterizes the global research landscape of haemocoagulase based on published literature. Current scholarly works on haemocoagulase mainly focus on hemorrhagic adverse events related to its clinical application, as well as its therapeutic effects on ischemic cerebrovascular disease and sudden sensorineural hearing loss, which represent the dominant research hotspots in this field. Publication, citation, and keyword patterns indicate growing research attention to broader clinical applications and combination-treatment questions. These patterns describe the published literature and do not establish clinical efficacy, comparative benefit, or causal mechanisms.

articles.title: Successful management of arrow‑rebound‑induced transcervical penetrating trauma with major vascular and pharyngolaryngeal injuries: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Penetrating neck injury involving major vessels is highly lethal. Long-trajectory transcervical penetration caused by rebounding arrows is exceptionally rare in civilians, posing significant diagnostic and management challenges.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A man in his early 50s presented to the emergency department approximately 2 hours after an arrow, rebounding from a nearby training target, penetrated his neck (entering above the left mandible, exiting on the right). He was conscious with minimal external bleeding but copious oropharyngeal secretions. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed the arrow traversing the hyoid bone and oropharynx, abutting the right common carotid artery (CCA) and compressing the right internal jugular vein (IJV).

DIAGNOSES: Open neck injury; combined right CCA and IJV injury; hemorrhagic shock; pharyngolaryngeal trauma without aerodigestive perforation; and pulmonary infection with consolidation.

INTERVENTIONS: Initial stabilization included arrow shaft shortening by firefighters. Emergency exploration under general anesthesia involved tracheotomy, cervical exploration, primary repair of the right IJV and CCA, and foreign body removal. Postoperative management in the intensive care unit included damage-control resuscitation (transfusion of 7.0 U packed red blood cells, 1100 mL plasma, and 10.5 U cryoprecipitate), antimicrobial therapy (cefuroxime, guided by cultures showing Staphylococcus epidermidis), early individualized anticoagulation (enoxaparin transitioned to rivaroxaban), and systematic correction of coagulopathy and electrolyte disturbances.

OUTCOMES: The patient was discharged on postoperative day 12 with healed wounds. Follow-up at 1, 3, 6.5 months, 1, 2, and nearly 3 years showed intact neurological function. Imaging confirmed stable right IJV occlusion. Anticoagulation was discontinued at 1 month without subsequent bleeding or thromboembolism. Although long-term imaging was limited to a 6.5-month non-contrast computed tomography, the patient remained asymptomatic without signs of venous hypertension or neurological deficits throughout the follow-up period.

LESSONS: High-quality preoperative computed tomography angiography with 3D reconstruction is critical for defining the relationship between the foreign body and vital structures. In selected patients, early individualized anticoagulation after excluding active bleeding may mitigate venous thrombosis. Systematic intensive care unit management of coagulopathy, electrolytes, and pulmonary complications is pivotal for survival.

articles.title: The association between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio and stroke among Chinese middle-aged and older adults: A cross-sectional study based on CHARLS.
articles.abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. The platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) integrates pro-thrombotic and inflammatory information, but its association with stroke in middle-aged and older Chinese adults remains inadequately characterized. In this cross-sectional study, we analyzed 11,034 participants aged ≥45 years from the 2011 baseline wave of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. PWR was calculated as platelet count divided by white blood cell count, and stroke was self-reported. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines were used to examine linear and nonlinear associations; the inflection point of the fitted spline curve was used to define a 2-piece regression model. Sensitivity analyses included exclusion of extreme PWR values and multiple imputation (m = 20); subgroup analyses were also performed. Among 11,034 participants (mean age 59.1 years), 309 (2.8%) reported a history of stroke. Continuous PWR was not linearly associated with stroke. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested an apparent nonlinear association (P for nonlinearity = .015), with an inflection point at a PWR of approximately 41.4; at or above this value, each 1-unit increment was associated with higher odds of stroke (adjusted odds ratio = 1.020, 95% confidence interval 1.009-1.030, P < .001). However, this apparent nonlinear association was not robust: after exclusion of participants with extreme PWR values, neither the overall nor the nonlinear association remained statistically significant (P = .975 and P = .936, respectively). This cross-sectional analysis provides exploratory evidence of a possible nonlinear association between PWR and prevalent stroke. However, this pattern was not robust to the exclusion of extreme PWR values, and the cross-sectional design cannot establish temporality or predictive value; the estimated inflection point should therefore be regarded as a descriptive, hypothesis-generating signal rather than an established clinical cutoff. Prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Risk-adapted active surveillance for prostate cancer: Can mpMRI, biomarkers, and genomic classifiers reduce biopsy burden without compromising safety?: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Active surveillance is the preferred management strategy for men with low-risk and selected favorable intermediate-risk prostate cancer. However, conventional surveillance protocols rely heavily on repeated systematic biopsies, which impose procedural morbidity, patient burden, and limited precision in identifying true disease progression. Risk-adapted tools, including multi parametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), molecular biomarkers, and genomic classifiers, have emerged as potential strategies to optimize surveillance intensity while preserving oncologic safety. To systematically evaluate the evidence supporting risk-adapted AS strategies incorporating mpMRI, molecular biomarkers, and genomic classifiers, with a focus on reducing biopsy burden without compromising oncologic outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed studies evaluating mpMRI, molecular biomarkers, or genomic classifiers within AS cohorts. Randomized controlled trials and prospective or retrospective cohort studies reporting surveillance-related outcomes were included. Primary outcomes included biopsy upgrading or reclassification, AS failure, and oncologic safety endpoints. Due to methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Five publications met inclusion criteria, representing four unique studies one randomized controlled trial and three observational cohorts and 1215 participants. The 2 Active Surveillance Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study publications were treated as linked reports from the same trial. Baseline mpMRI with targeted and systematic biopsy was associated with lower subsequent AS failure and upgrading, but biopsy avoidance was not directly tested. An MRI-led cohort omitted routine protocol biopsies, although the absence of a concurrent comparator precluded conclusions about equivalent oncologic safety. The 4Kscore demonstrated potential for confirmatory-biopsy triage; a hypothetical deferral strategy could have avoided 27% of biopsies but would have missed 2 Grade Group 2 upgrades. The Decipher genomic classifier independently predicted biopsy upgrading, although biopsy reduction was not evaluated. Evidence establishing the long-term oncologic safety of biopsy reduction remained insufficient.

CONCLUSION: Risk-adapted AS strategies incorporating mpMRI, molecular biomarkers, and genomic classifiers may improve risk stratification and support selective adjustment of biopsy intensity. However, current evidence does not establish the safety of routine biopsy omission or fully biopsy-free surveillance. Integration of these tools should remain individualized, with histologic reassessment when indicated and prospective validation of biopsy-deferral strategies.

articles.title: Evaluation of the effect of provincial and municipal emergency green channels (post-informatization and process optimization) on the treatment of acute ischemic stroke and study on influencing factors such as DNT and DPT.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the impact of informatization and process optimization on the treatment efficacy of the emergency green channel for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in provincial and municipal hospitals and analyzes its key influencing factors. A retrospective cohort study was conducted, enrolling patients with AIS who received reperfusion therapy via the emergency green channel from September 1, 2024, to August 31, 2025. Patients were divided into a control group (pre-optimization, n = 50) and a study group (post-optimization, n = 50) based on whether the informatization optimization was implemented ("Stroke One-Click Start," full-process electronic timestamps, cloud imaging platform, point-of-care rapid testing, and parallel pathways). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline characteristics. The door-to-needle time (DNT), door-to-puncture time (DPT), compliance rates for key time nodes, clinical prognosis, and safety indicators were compared between the 2 groups. Baseline characteristics were balanced between the 2 groups after matching. The median DNT in the study group was significantly shorter than that in the control group (42 vs 68 minutes, P < .001), and the median DPT was also significantly shortened (92 vs 128 minutes, P < .001). The compliance rate for DNT ≤ 45 minutes increased from 22.0 to 70.0% (P < .001), and the compliance rate for DPT ≤ 90 minutes increased from 16.0 to 48.0% (P < .001). The times for key nodes (e.g., door-to-CT completion time, CT completion-to-treatment time) were significantly shortened (all P < .001). The study group had a higher proportion of favorable outcomes (mRS 0-2) at discharge and at 90 days (58.0 vs 36.0%, P = .027; 64.0 vs 44.0%, P = .046), and a shorter ICU stay (P = .044), with no significant differences in safety indicators. Subgroup analysis showed that DNT was significantly shortened in all subgroups, and there was an interaction between NIHSS score and optimization effect (P = .039), with the greatest benefit observed in patients with severe stroke. In this retrospective before-and-after cohort, implementation of the bundled informatization and process-optimization pathway was associated with shorter DNT and DPT, higher compliance with key time targets, and better functional outcomes without an observed increase in safety events. These findings should be interpreted in light of the nonrandomized design and support broader implementation in appropriately resourced institutions.

articles.title: Quantitative evaluation of muscle relaxation efficacy of moving cupping therapy for chronic low back pain by shear wave elastography: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moving cupping is used to reduce pain and muscle tension in chronic low back pain (CLBP), but its effect on paraspinal muscle stiffness has not been compared with that of a sham procedure. We evaluated it using shear wave elastography (SWE).

METHODS: In this single-center, sham-controlled randomized trial, 68 adults with CLBP were assigned 1:1 by computer-generated simple randomization to moving cupping or sham cupping (four sessions over 2 weeks; 18-20 kPa vs 0 kPa). The 66 participants who received the allocated intervention had a mean age of 37.8 ± 9.0 years, and 71.2% were female. Assessors and the analyst were blinded. The primary endpoint was the change in multifidus shear modulus from baseline to the end of treatment; secondary outcomes included shear modulus at 1-week follow-up, pain intensity, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), EQ-5D-5L, and Patient Global Assessment. Intention-to-treat analyses used linear mixed-effects models; a per-protocol mixed 2-way analysis of variance served as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: A significant group × time interaction was observed for shear modulus (P < .001), as the decrease was greater with moving cupping (60.23 ± 14.83 to 10.84 ± 5.67 kPa) than with sham (57.54 ± 11.09 to 39.41 ± 9.84 kPa). At follow-up, shear modulus was 15.42 ± 7.41 vs 44.88 ± 14.22 kPa, and the change after treatment did not differ significantly between groups (P = .808). Pain also showed a significant group × time interaction (P < .001; moving cupping, 5.68 ± 1.41 to 2.44 ± 1.56; sham, 5.41 ± 1.18 to 3.41 ± 1.26), whereas ODI (P = .579) and EQ-5D-5L (P = .162) did not. No cupping-related adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: Two weeks of moving cupping reduced multifidus stiffness more than sham cupping, and the difference persisted 1 week after treatment. Pain decreased more with moving cupping, although the between-group difference was small, and there were no significant effects on disability or quality of life. Moving cupping may reduce paraspinal muscle stiffness but is not an established treatment for the broader symptom burden of CLBP.

articles.title: Efficacy comparison of 9 chemotherapy regimens in nonmetastatic Ewing's sarcoma treatment: A network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal chemotherapy for nonmetastatic Ewing's sarcoma (ES) remains undefined, with no global consensus established among the available multidrug regimens.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Chinese databases (VIP [Chinese Scientific Journal Database], WanFang, China National Knowledge Infrastructure) up to May 2024 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing chemotherapy regimens for nonmetastatic ES. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane tools (for RCTs) and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (for cohort studies). Efficacy was ranked via surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values for event-free survival and overall survival.

RESULTS: Twelve studies (3834 patients) evaluating 9 regimens were included. The top 3 regimens for event-free survival were as follows: VDC (vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide) + IE (ifosfamide/etoposide)(In)(intensified regimen) and VTC (vincristine, topotecan, cyclophosphamide) (SUCRA = 92.1%); VDC+IE(In) (SUCRA = 85.4%); VDC+IE(St)(standard regimen) (SUCRA = 79.2%). For overall survival, the ranking was similar. VDC alone ranked lowest in both outcomes.

CONCLUSION: The VDC+IE(In)+VTC combination may exhibit superior efficacy among the 9 chemotherapy regimens for nonmetastatic ES, necessitating further validation through RCTs with larger sample sizes.

articles.title: Comparison of inhalation anesthesia and total intravenous anesthesia in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The choice of anesthetic technique may influence perioperative stability and postoperative recovery. This study compared postoperative recovery between sevoflurane inhalational anesthesia and propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

METHODS: In this prospective, randomized clinical trial, 81 patients were assigned to receive either sevoflurane inhalational anesthesia (Group S, n = 40) or propofol-based TIVA (Group T, n = 41). The primary outcome was postoperative recovery quality assessed using the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) questionnaire preoperatively and 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, rescue analgesic requirement, incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, intraoperative remifentanil consumption, and perioperative hemodynamic variables.

RESULTS: No statistically significant between-group difference was detected in QoR-15 scores at 24 hours postoperatively (unadjusted mean difference [TIVA minus sevoflurane], 2.39 points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -4.83 to 9.61; P = .512). After adjustment for preoperative QoR-15 scores, the difference remained statistically nonsignificant (adjusted mean difference, 0.78 points; 95% CI, -5.91 to 7.47; P = .817). Postoperative pain scores and postoperative nausea and vomiting incidence did not differ significantly between groups. However, the proportion of patients requiring rescue analgesics at 6 hours postoperatively was lower in the TIVA group (9.8% vs 30.0%; unadjusted P = .027). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was significantly higher in the TIVA group (P < .001). Heart rate at postanesthesia care unit arrival and mean blood pressure after intubation were lower in the TIVA group (adjusted P < .05).

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in postoperative recovery quality at 24 hours was detected between propofol-based TIVA and sevoflurane anesthesia. Although rescue analgesic requirements at 6 hours were lower in the TIVA group, this secondary finding should be interpreted cautiously. The CI for the primary outcome did not exclude clinically meaningful differences; therefore, these findings do not establish equivalence between the 2 anesthetic techniques.

articles.title: Effects of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training on balance, walking speed, and activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to compare the effects of 3 weeks of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training (SBT) with those of tied-belt treadmill training (both belts driven at the same speed) on balance, functional reach, walking speed, and basic activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke, and to evaluate the feasibility and safety of the SBT protocol.

METHODS: In this single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation conducted in the inpatient rehabilitation unit of a tertiary hospital, 30 patients with subacute hemiplegic stroke (median, 13 days after onset) were randomized; 26 participants (13 per group) completed the post-intervention assessment. Thirty 30-minute treadmill sessions (twice daily, 5 days per week, for 3 weeks) were delivered in place of the routine gait-training sessions of the standard inpatient rehabilitation program. In the SBT group, the paretic limb was positioned on the slower belt at a fixed paretic-to-nonparetic belt-speed ratio of 1:2; in the control group, both belts operated at the same speed. The primary outcome was the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) at 3 weeks, compared between groups using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. Secondary outcomes were the functional reach test (FRT), modified FRT, gait speed (10-m walk test), and Korean version of the modified Barthel index, with Holm adjustment for multiplicity.

RESULTS: Both groups improved substantially (BBS, +18.8 vs +18.0 points; both P <.001); however, the baseline-adjusted between-group difference in the BBS was not significant (1.20 points; 95% confidence interval = -5.30 to 7.71; P =.706). No secondary outcome remained significant after Holm adjustment; a nominal difference in seated FRT (adjusted difference = 9.75 cm; P =.044; Holm-adjusted P =.355) was not robust in sensitivity analyses. Session completion was 99.7%, and no device- or protocol-related adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSION: In this pilot trial of patients with subacute stroke undergoing inpatient rehabilitation, SBT was feasible and well tolerated but did not demonstrate superiority over tied-belt training for balance, walking speed, or activities of daily living. An exploratory signal in seated reach warrants confirmation in adequately powered trials.

articles.title: Predictive model for acute kidney injury in critical patients with pulmonary embolism based on machine learning: A multicenter clinical study.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is recognized as an acute, critical cardiovascular condition, and acute kidney injury (AKI) is frequently observed as a complication in this clinical context. Currently, no predictive tools are available to accurately assess AKI risk in critical patients with PE. A predictive model was developed in this study to estimate AKI risk in critical PE. Data obtained from Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV were utilized for the development of training and internal validation sets, while data derived from Emergency Intensive Care Unit Collaborative Research Database were employed for external validation. Eight machine learning models were developed through least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariate logistic analysis, and a web-based calculator was subsequently deployed. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration curve assessment, and decision curve analysis to determine discrimination, calibration accuracy, and clinical utility. Feature importance within the optimal performing models was quantified through Shapley Additive eXplanation analysis. Incremental predictive value relative to the pulmonary embolism severity index score was evaluated via net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement. A total of 2187 and 2183 patients diagnosed with critical PE were enrolled by 2 centers. In the training set, 1725 (78.88%) patients had AKI, whereas 1185 (54.28%) patients had AKI in the validation set. Hypertension, heart failure, pneumonia, sepsis, ventilation, respiratory rate, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, partial pressure of oxygen, lactate, and Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score were ultimately identified as risk factors for AKI in critical PE. The extreme gradient boosting model demonstrated the most stable discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit across training (area under curve [AUC] = 0.825), internal validation (AUC = 0.771), and external validation (AUC = 0.757) sets. Shapley Additive eXplanation analysis of the optimal model revealed that Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and partial pressure of oxygen contributed substantially to AKI risk. Relative to the pulmonary embolism severity index model, the proposed model exhibited superior performance in predicting AKI. A machine learning prediction model that integrates clinical indicators with disease activity scores was constructed and externally validated to estimate the risk of AKI in critical PE. A web-based calculator was subsequently developed to enable clinicians to identify high-risk cohorts and furnish evidence-based guidance for early intervention and individualized management.

articles.title: Percutaneous cholecystostomy for acute cholecystitis in patients with cirrhosis is associated with healthcare burden and mortality.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous cholecystostomy (PC) is an option to manage acute cholecystitis (AC) in high-risk patients for cholecystectomy. Data on PC use in patients with liver cirrhosis are lacking. We used the National Inpatient Sample database to extract a retrospective cohort (October 2015-December 2019) of cirrhosis hospitalizations. Those with AC receiving PC were matched to those not receiving PC. Inhospital mortality (IHM), length of stay in days, total charges in United States Dollar, and liver disease complications were outcomes. Of 754,245 hospitalizations with cirrhosis, 2989 (0.4%) had AC with no change over time, P = .13. Of AC hospitalizations, 456 (15.3%) received PC, with no change over time, P = .845. In a propensity-matched cohort of 1335 hospitalizations (445 PC), PC was associated with higher IHM (33 vs 10.9%), mean length of stay (13.5 vs 8.5 days), total charges (174,264 vs 117,957 United States Dollar), acute kidney injury (47.4 vs 32.6%), and sepsis (40.9 vs 19.2%), P < .01 for all. In a conditional logistic model, hospitalizations with versus without PC were associated with 2-fold IHM (1.88; 1.37-2.59). One in six AC hospitalizations is managed with PC, which is associated with morbidity, use of hospital resources, and patient mortality. Prospective studies are needed to identify cirrhosis patients with AC likely to benefit from PC.

articles.title: Temporal trends in obesity prevalence, weight loss attempts, and weight loss among US adults: A repeated cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2011-2023.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to describe trends in obesity prevalence, weight loss attempts, and one-year weight loss among US adults and identify associated factors. We analyzed nationally representative data from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011 to 2023. Age-standardized body mass index, obesity (including class III), weight loss attempts, and weight loss by threshold and range were estimated by survey cycle, and trends were tested with weighted regression adjusted for sociodemographic factors. Sensitivity analyses excluded participants with missing or discrepant self-reports. Factors associated with attempts, and with weight loss versus stable weight among attempters, were examined in 2021 to 2023 using fully adjusted logistic models. Obesity prevalence rose from 34.6% in 2011 to 2012 to 41.3% in 2017 to 2020 (prevalence ratio [PR]2011-2020 1.047, 95% confidence intervals 1.026-1.067) and was 39.9% in 2021 to 2023, without significant change since 2017 to 2020 (PR2017-2023 0.981, 0.949-1.015). Class III obesity increased from 6.3% to 9.4% (PR2011-2023 1.039, 1.020-1.059). Weight loss attempts increased until 2017 to 2020 (51.0%) and then declined (47.9%; PR2017-2023 0.967, 0.938-0.997). Any weight loss increased (31.6% to 34.3%), driven by reductions of 0 to 5%, whereas weight loss >5% was stable overall (19.3% to 20.2%) and declined among attempters (31.3% to 27.8%; PR2011-2023 0.984, 0.969-0.999). Sensitivity analyses were similar. In 2021 to 2023, obesity 1 year earlier, hypertension, prediabetes, higher education, and insufficient physical activity were associated with attempts, whereas men, older adults, and smokers had lower odds. Among attempters, only older age had lower odds of weight loss. Obesity did not change significantly after 2017 to 2020, class III obesity kept rising, and clinically meaningful weight loss did not improve despite more reported weight loss.

articles.title: Knowledge structure and emerging trends in research on osteoporotic fractures and cardiovascular diseases: A bibliometric analysis from 2005 to 2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporotic fractures (OPFs) and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are major age-related conditions that frequently coexist and may be linked through shared biological mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, mineral metabolism disorders, vascular calcification, and frailty. Although research on OPFs and CVDs has expanded rapidly, the intellectual structure, collaborative patterns, and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary field remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map the global research landscape and identify emerging hotspots in OPF-CVD research from 2005 to 2025.

METHODS: English-language articles and reviews published during 2005 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on April 2, 2026. Analyses used VOSviewer 1.6.20 (Centre for Science and Technology Studies [CWTS], Leiden University), CiteSpace 6.4.R1 (Chaomei Chen, Drexel University), bibliometrix 5.3.0 in R 4.5.3 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing), and Microsoft Excel. We examined publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, co-cited references, keyword patterns, and citation bursts.

RESULTS: A total of 1236 publications were included. Annual output increased from 24 publications in 2005 to 103 in 2025, corresponding to a compound annual growth rate of 7.56%. The United States had the highest publication count, raw citation count, and TLS. Harvard University was the most productive institution, and Katie L Stone was the most productive author. Reference co-citation analysis identified 8 major thematic clusters: calcium, bisphosphonates, heart failure, frailty, renal osteodystrophy, antihypertensive drugs, osteopenia, and phosphorus. Keyword analyses suggested a descriptive shift from epidemiological associations toward bone-vascular mechanisms, risk stratification, fragility-fracture management, diagnosis, and prevention.

CONCLUSIONS: OPF-CVD research has developed into a multidisciplinary field with increasing clinical relevance. The bibliometric patterns are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causal relationships. Future research should evaluate integrated bone-cardiovascular risk assessment, pharmacological safety, and multidisciplinary care using prospective and clinically validated designs.

articles.title: Biomechanical analysis of cervical misalignment and extrication time during heavy vehicle traffic collisions: A randomized, simulation-based experimental study with professional rescuers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traffic collisions remain one of the leading global causes of morbidity and mortality. In vehicle extrication, rescue time and spinal motion restriction play a decisive role in patient prognosis. Current evidence prioritizes minimizing rescue time; however, most studies have focused on passenger vehicles, with limited evidence available regarding rescue operations in heavy vehicles. The aim of this study was to analyze cervical spine biomechanics and extrication times during the rescue of victims involved in heavy-vehicle traffic accidents.

METHODS: A comparative, simulation-based experimental study was conducted to evaluate 3 extrication techniques in a truck cab: standard manual rescue, rapid extrication device, and extrication and immobilization device. Thirty-six professional firefighters participated, organized into randomized teams. Cervical spine motion was recorded using inertial sensors placed on the cervical spine. Execution time was measured, and statistical analyses included repeated-measures analysis of variance, linear regression models, and the Cochran Q test.

RESULTS: Significant differences were observed among techniques in both cervical spine motion and extrication time. Standard manual rescue demonstrated the lowest overall cervical motion and the shortest execution time. Extrication device provided acceptable immobilization at the expense of longer execution time, whereas rapid extrication device produced greater cervical motion without temporal advantages.

CONCLUSION: In the rescue of victims from heavy vehicles, standard manual rescue offers the best balance between biomechanical safety and operational speed, supporting the optimization of rescue protocols based on objective efficiency and time-dependence criteria.

articles.title: Trends in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease incidence among Chinese adults aged 60 to 94 years from 1994 to 2023 and projections to 2035.
articles.abstract: Although the global burden of disease (GBD) study 2021 has provided national estimates of the overall burden of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in China, age-specific analyses focusing on adults aged 60 to 94 years remain limited. We extracted COPD incidence and corresponding absolute case counts among adults aged 60 to 94 years for the period 1994 to 2023 from the global burden of disease 2023 study. The data were stratified by sex and 5-year age groups. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs) were calculated using the World Health Organization standard population. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression, expressed as the average annual percent change, while age-period-cohort models were applied to disentangle the effects of age, period, and cohort. Finally, autoregressive integrated moving-average models were used to generate ASIR projections up to 2035. Between 1994 and 2023, a total of 101,325,366 incident cases of COPD were estimated in China, of which 68.11% occurred among adults aged 60 to 94 years. The ASIR exhibited a sustained downward trend, with average annual percent changes of -0.99% (95% confidence interval: -1.03% to -0.94%) in males and -1.25% (95% confidence interval: -1.31% to -1.18%) in females. Stratified analyses by 5-year age groups yielded analogous declining trends.The age-period-cohort model indicated that age, period, and cohort each exerted significant influences on the incidence of COPD. Furthermore, based on the fit to the historical data, the autoregressive integrated moving-average model projected a sustained upward trajectory until 2035 among males aged 60 to 94 years, reaching 1397.90/100,000 population by 2035, while the ASIR for females was projected to peak at 1118.82/100,000 population in 2026 and then decline to 955.32/100,000 population by 2035 assuming no additional intervention measures. Age-stratified projections revealed divergent trajectories. COPD incidence among adults aged 60 to 94 years declined significantly from 1994 to 2023, which was associated with favorable period and cohort effects, although age-related increases persisted. Projections indicated divergent trajectories by sex, underscoring the need for targeted interventions among males.

articles.title: Evaluation of preoperative and perioperative characteristics in patients admitted to a postoperative intensive care unit: A prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission is commonly considered for patients perceived to be at increased risk of postoperative complications. This study aimed to describe the preoperative and perioperative characteristics of patients admitted to a postoperative ICU and to explore associations between routinely available clinical parameters, inflammatory biomarkers, and short-term outcomes. This prospective observational study included 126 adult patients admitted postoperatively to a tertiary reanimation ICU. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, ASA physical status, anesthesia type, laboratory parameters, postoperative organ support requirements, ICU length of stay, and mortality were recorded. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) were evaluated. Continuous and categorical variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and chi-square or Fisher exact test, as appropriate. The mean age was 67.3 ± 16.1 years, and 114 (90.5%) patients were classified as ASA III. Abdominal surgery was the most common surgical category (56, 44.4%). Mean NLR and CAR values were 6.17 ± 8.36 and 1.17 ± 2.52, respectively. Two patients died (1.6%; exact 95% CI, 0.2-5.6%). Mortality was not significantly associated with NLR (P = .310), CAR (P = .845), admission SpO2 (P = .084), or hemoglobin level (P = .907). ICU length of stay showed an exploratory association with mortality (P = .004); given that only 2 deaths occurred, this observation cannot establish a prognostic relationship. In this selected postoperative ICU cohort, preoperative and perioperative characteristics did not clearly distinguish patients according to short-term outcomes. Because there was no non-ICU comparator cohort and mortality events were very limited, the findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger multicenter studies are needed to evaluate whether these parameters can support postoperative ICU admission decisions.

articles.title: Pancreaticobiliary duct stenting after endoscopic papillectomy in patients with documented adequate field visibility: A case series.
articles.abstract: Identification of the ductal orifices and stent placement can be challenging after endoscopic papillectomy. We describe procedural findings, pancreaticobiliary stent placement, and recorded early outcomes in patients with documented adequate postresection field visibility. This retrospective single-center case series reviewed 25 adults who underwent endoscopic papillectomy at Chongqing University Cancer Hospital, China, between May 2023 and May 2025. Twenty-one patients with sufficient procedural documentation were analyzed. Visibility was a retrospective description of the procedural field, not an independent predictor. Biliary and pancreatic stent placement were reported separately, with exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs). No comparison or association analysis was performed. The median age was 58 years; 11 patients were male. The median lesion diameter was 16 mm. Endoscopic resection was technically completed in all 21 patients. All included procedures were described as having adequate field visibility, with no documented bleeding that interrupted the procedure or prevented ductal assessment. Biliary stents were placed in 21 patients (100%; 95% CI, 83.9-100%), and pancreatic stents were placed in 16 (76.2%; 95% CI, 52.8-91.8%). Five patients received biliary stents alone; the reasons for pancreatic stent omission were not established. Mean procedure time was 58.3 ± 9.3 minutes, and median hospital stay was 3 days. No pancreatitis, delayed bleeding, perforation, cholangitis, intensive care admission, or readmission was documented in the available records within 30 days. All 21 patients completed 30 day follow-up. This selected case series describes biliary and pancreatic stent placement in procedures with documented adequate visibility. It cannot determine whether visibility influences duct access or adverse events. Prospective comparative studies with independently defined visibility measures are needed.

articles.title: Global trends and current state of research in clinical trials in atherosclerosis: A bibliometric study 2004 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to summarize the current state of research and global trends in clinical trials related to atherosclerosis through bibliometric analysis.

METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted for literature pertaining to clinical trials on atherosclerosis published between August 2004 and August 2024 in the Web of Science Core Collection database. Bibliometric analysis and web visualization were performed utilizing CiteSpace (Chaomei Chen, Drexel University), VOSviewer (Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Leiden University), Scimago Graphica (Scimago Lab), the Bibliometrics Online Analysis Platform (Bibliometrics Inc., https://bibliometric.com), and the R package is based on R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). The analysis encompassed the number of publications, citations, countries, institutions, journals, authors, references, and keywords.

RESULTS: A total of 1982 papers published across 646 journals from 75 countries were included. The volume of literature concerning clinical trials in atherosclerosis has exhibited a consistent yearly increase. The United States, particularly Harvard University, emerged as the leading contributor in terms of published clinical trials. Stephen J. Nicholls was identified as the most prolific author based on publication and co-citation metrics. The journal with relevant the highest number of publications and citations was Nutrition Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases. Keywords such as "atherosclerosis," "randomized controlled trial," "cardiovascular disease," "risk," "coronary heart disease," "myocardial infarction," "risk factors," and "coronary artery disease" reflect the current hotspots in atherosclerosis research.

CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates global trends and research directions in the field of atherosclerosis through bibliometric analysis and visualization of the clinical trial literature. Future investigations should emphasize the mechanisms of action and clinical trial methodologies. Young scholars are encouraged to engage in interdisciplinary collaboration, adopt innovative technologies and methods, enhance data processing skills, and remain abreast of the latest research developments to address emerging challenges and opportunities in this domain.

articles.title: Transportable early renal recovery phenotypes and 30-day major adverse kidney events after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: A MIMIC-IV discovery and eICU-CRD external-validation cohort study.
articles.abstract: Early renal recovery after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury is heterogeneous. We aimed to derive clinically interpretable early recovery phenotypes, assess their transportability through fixed-centroid external assignment, and examine associations with 30-day major adverse kidney events (MAKE30). This retrospective discovery and external-validation cohort study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV and eICU-CRD. Eligible patients were adults with a first intensive care unit stay and Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes -compatible acute kidney injury within 7 days of sepsis onset. K-means clustering integrated five renal, fluid, and hemodynamic domains across twelve 6-hour intervals after acute kidney injury onset. Stability was assessed by repeated 80% patient subsampling. eICU CRD patients were assigned to fixed MIMIC-derived centroids without reclustering. Modified Poisson models estimated adjusted risk ratios (RRs). Of 9725 Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV patients with known MAKE30 status, 2529 (26.0%) experienced MAKE30. Four phenotypes were identified in 7965 patients: low-burden rapid-recovery, preserved-diuresis intermediate-risk, oliguric kidney-failure, and shock-vasopressor. The four-cluster solution had a median adjusted Rand index of 0.939 (empirical 2.5th-97.5th percentiles, 0.892-0.990). Relative to the low-burden phenotype, adjusted MAKE30 RRs were 1.74 (95% confidence interval , 1.58-1.90), 3.80 (3.47-4.16), and 3.68 (3.34-4.06). In eICU-CRD, 4708 of 8771 patients (53.7%) could be assigned; corresponding RRs were 2.82 (2.45-3.23), 4.78 (4.00-5.72), and 4.99 (4.32-5.76). Unassigned patients had higher MAKE30 rates than assigned patients (41.1% vs 25.2%). MAKE30 associations persisted in landmark and distance-restricted analyses. Early renal recovery trajectories identified four reproducible clinical phenotypes associated with MAKE30. Fixed-centroid assignment reproduced the direction of these associations in eICU-CRD patients with sufficient trajectory data. Selective assignment and the observational design limit generalizability and preclude conclusions about phenotype-guided treatment.

articles.title: Efficacy of opioid therapy in the management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by high rates of morbidity, disability, and mortality. Traditional treatments often fail to adequately control the symptoms of advanced disease, particularly refractory dyspnea, and additional therapeutic options are needed. Opioids have been proposed as a potential option for symptom control in patients with COPD.

METHODS: To evaluate the efficacy of opioid therapy in COPD, we searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Embase, Medline, Web of Science, and PubMed for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from inception to May 2022. Two authors independently extracted data from eligible trials and assessed the risk of bias using the tool developed by the Cochrane Collaboration. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used for continuous outcomes, and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were used for dichotomous outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 439 references were screened, of which 10 RCTs met the inclusion criteria. Compared with control, opioids significantly reduced dyspnea, with an effect that exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) threshold (SMD = -0.4, 95% CI -0.6 to -0.2, P ≤ .001, I2 = 45.8%). Opioids had no significant effect on forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1; SMD = 0.1, 95% CI -0.3 to 0.4, P = .715, I2 = 0%) or on exercise capacity (SMD = 0.2, 95% CI -0.1 to 0.6, P = .217, I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: For patients with COPD, opioid therapy was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in refractory dyspnea but did not improve lung function or exercise capacity. Because the available evidence is derived from a small number of older trials with modest sample sizes and clinical heterogeneity, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Opioids are not recommended as first-line therapy; low-dose opioids may be considered as an adjunct for refractory dyspnea in selected patients with advanced COPD after optimal standard treatment has been provided.

articles.title: GLP-1-based therapies for reduction of heart failure and cardiovascular outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) based therapies have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits beyond glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, the magnitude and consistency of their effects across individual cardiovascular and heart failure outcomes remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of GLP-1-based therapies on cardiovascular mortality, hospitalization for heart failure, hospitalization for unstable angina, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), and nonfatal stroke.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE (via PubMed) and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for randomized controlled trials evaluating GLP-1-based therapies in adults with or without T2DM. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each prespecified outcome.

RESULTS: Eleven randomized controlled trials comprising 81,948 participants were included, and all studies were judged to be at low risk of bias. GLP-1-based therapy significantly reduced cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.85, 95% CI: 0.79-0.91), hospitalization for heart failure (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83-0.97), nonfatal MI (RR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.79-0.96), and nonfatal stroke (RR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81-0.97). GLP-1-based therapy was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in unstable angina compared with placebo. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed, indicating variability in the reported treatment effects. Heterogeneity was low for most outcomes, although moderate heterogeneity was observed for nonfatal MI (I² = 56%) and substantial heterogeneity for hospitalization for unstable angina (I² = 83%). For nonfatal MI, formal analyses showed no evidence of small-study effects.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1-based therapies were associated with significant reductions in cardiovascular mortality, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, and hospitalization for heart failure. These findings support the cardiovascular benefits of GLP-1-based therapies in patients with T2DM and elevated cardiovascular risk, while no significant benefit was observed for hospitalization because of unstable angina.

articles.title: In an Effort to Reduce Hypertension, Salt Substitutes Come to the Table.
Updated Guidance Released for Type 2 Diabetes Care.
Habitual Golden Milk Consumption Is Associated with a Favorable Redox and Cardiometabolic Biomarker Profile in Older Men: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Nutrition Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aging is characterized by increased oxidative stress, chronic low-grade inflammation, and metabolic alterations. Golden Milk is a milk-based beverage containing turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, and black pepper, with potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This study examined the association between habitual Golden Milk consumption and redox, inflammatory, and lipid biomarkers in older men.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 124 men aged ≥70 years, comprising 64 regular Golden Milk consumers and 60 non-consumers. Oxidative stress and antioxidant defense were assessed using malondialdehyde (MDA), peroxynitrite, glutathione (GSH), catalase, and superoxide dismutase (SOD). Inflammatory and lipid biomarkers were also measured. Between-group comparisons, effect sizes, false discovery rate correction, and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, BMI, diabetes and hypertension status were performed.

RESULTS: Compared with non-consumers, Golden Milk consumers had significantly lower MDA, peroxynitrite, CRP, total cholesterol, and triglycerides, and significantly higher GSH, catalase, SOD, and HDL-C (all FDR-adjusted p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, BMI, diabetes and hypertension status, Golden Milk consumption remained associated with lower MDA (-1.61 µmol/L), peroxynitrite (-3.45 µmol/L), CRP (-1.03 mg/L), total cholesterol (-35.05 mg/dL), and triglycerides (-29.56 mg/dL), and with higher GSH (+1.34 µmol/L), catalase (+25.72 U/mL), SOD (+43.41 U/mL), and HDL-C (+13.84 mg/dL). CRP and the granulocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio were also significantly correlated with redox biomarkers.

CONCLUSION: Habitual Golden Milk consumption was associated with a more favorable redox, inflammatory, and lipid profile in older men. Prospective studies are required to confirm these associations and establish causality.

articles.title: Real-world evaluation of the NHS testing criteria for glucokinase hyperglycaemia in pregnancy.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Criteria for Glucokinase-Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young (GCK-MODY) genetic testing are now being integrated into the National Health Service (NHS) services using fasting glucose, body mass index (BMI) and ethnicity. We aimed to assess the national screening criteria for GCK-MODY in a multi-ethnic population.

METHODS: GCK-MODY testing was offered to women with gestational diabetes that met criteria in a multi-ethnic cohort. Data from the national testing centre was used to compare patient characteristics in those positive and negative for GCK-MODY.

RESULTS: Fewer cases of GCK-MODY were found when testing using NHS criteria (0.14%) than expected (0.9%). Individuals testing positive for GCK-MODY had a higher HbA1c than negative individuals (p < 0.001). There was no difference in 2-h glucose increment (p = 0.829).

CONCLUSIONS: Current criteria may not effectively identify a high-risk cohort of individuals to test, given the prevalence of GCK-MODY in those tested, leading to over-testing. HbA1c may prove a useful additional screening parameter. Further studies are needed to improve the criteria's utility across different ethnicities.

articles.title: Clinician-Initiated Palliative Care Referral Versus Advanced Heart Failure Referral Criteria in Hospitalized Patients With Heart Failure: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The overall aim was to examine clinician-initiated palliative care referral practices in relation to referrals indicated by the advanced heart failure (AHF) referral criteria among hospitalized patients with heart failure.

DESIGN: A retrospective observational study.

METHODS: Medical records of 450 adults hospitalized with heart failure during 2023-2024 were reviewed. Clinician-initiated palliative care referral was compared with AHF referral criteria. Firth logistic regression examined referral-associated factors. Six-month mortality from the index admission was a pragmatic prognostic endpoint, not a measure of palliative care needs.

RESULTS: Among 450 patients, clinician-initiated palliative care referral was uncommon, and most patients meeting the advanced heart failure referral criteria were not referred. Agreement between the two approaches was low. Metastatic cancer and New York Heart Association functional class were associated with referral in the adjusted model. The referral criteria showed greater sensitivity for six-month mortality, whereas clinician-initiated referral showed greater specificity.

CONCLUSION: Clinician-initiated referral and the AHF referral criteria identified different proportions of hospitalized patients with heart failure. Their differing performance for six-month mortality supports further prospective evaluation; clinical utility for identifying palliative care needs remains unestablished.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: The findings identify an opportunity for nurses and multidisciplinary teams to assess needs among criteria-positive patients without specialist referral. Whether screening improves care requires prospective evaluation.

IMPACT: The study documents differences between clinician-initiated referral and AHF referral criteria in a broader hospitalized heart failure population. It provides a basis for evaluating systematic needs assessment alongside existing referral practices.

REPORTING METHOD: Reporting followed the RECORD extension of the STROBE statement.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

articles.title: Preoperative prediction of complicated acute cholecystitis using delta neutrophil index and sodium-to-CRP ratio: a parsimonious risk model.
articles.abstract: Preoperative identification of complicated acute cholecystitis (CAC) remains challenging despite advances in imaging and laboratory assessment. Reliable and clinically applicable risk stratification tools are still limited. This study evaluated the sodium-to-C-reactive protein ratio (Na/CRP) and delta neutrophil index (DNI) for preoperative prediction of CAC. This retrospective cohort study included 905 consecutive adults who underwent cholecystectomy for acute calculous cholecystitis between June 2019 and April 2026. Patients were classified as having uncomplicated or complicated acute cholecystitis according to operative and histopathological findings. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of complicated disease and develop a risk prediction model. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Among 905 patients, 175 (19.3%) had complicated acute cholecystitis. Male sex (OR 1.866, 95% CI 1.291-2.698, p < 0.001), age (OR 1.015, 95% CI 1.002-1.027, p = 0.019), DNI (OR 1.105, 95% CI 1.036-1.178, p = 0.002), and Na/CRP ratio (OR 0.751, 95% CI 0.679-0.830, p < 0.001) were independent predictors. Na/CRP demonstrated better discrimination than DNI (AUC 0.739 vs. 0.626). A model incorporating age, sex, DNI, and Na/CRP achieved the highest performance (AUC 0.766), with 85.7% sensitivity and a negative predictive value of 93.8%. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.753. Na/CRP is an independent predictor of complicated acute cholecystitis and demonstrates better diagnostic performance than DNI alone. A simple model integrating age, sex, DNI, and Na/CRP may improve preoperative risk stratification and support the identification of patients at lower risk for complicated disease when interpreted alongside clinical and radiological assessment.

articles.title: Lived experiences of type 1 diabetes and disordered eating: Insights for prevention and early intervention in Paediatric care.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The high prevalence and risks of eating disorders and disordered eating in type 1 diabetes (T1D) are well recognised, yet the aetiology is poorly understood. Current understanding draws on established eating disorder models, complemented by an emerging lived experience evidence base. This study aimed to retrospectively explore how disordered eating develops whilst growing up with T1D using lived experience in order to inform future prevention strategies within clinical practice.

METHODS: A qualitative design underpinned by an interpretivist approach was used to explore the lived experiences of adults diagnosed with T1D in childhood who self-identified as having experienced disordered eating. Eleven participants (aged 18-61; 10 females, 1 male) were recruited via social media and advocacy networks between January and October 2023. Semi-structured interviews were conducted remotely. Data were analysed inductively using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework, with attention to researcher positionality and context.

RESULTS: Analysis generated five themes that highlight how disordered eating develops and is maintained in paediatric diabetes care: Connection with others: Relationship dynamics shaped early food and diabetes behaviours; Shame and secrecy: Stigma related to weight, diabetes, and eating behaviours reinforced secrecy Identity and self-view: Identity within the healthcare system and feelings of inadequacy and control-based behaviours as well as neurodiversity and mortality. Feeling held back: Emotional and social limitations of diabetes including trauma, contributed to disordered eating; Change and transitions: Shifts in care, technology, and independence influenced disordered eating behaviours. These findings highlight illness and care-specific drivers that extend beyond body image concerns.

CONCLUSION: This study challenges dominant, weight-focused frameworks by revealing how disordered eating in T1D is shaped during paediatric diabetes care. Prevention must be embedded within routine paediatric diabetes care. Findings offer a lived-experience framework to inform more inclusive, psychologically informed paediatric diabetes services.

articles.title: Preferences for Telehealth in Rural and Mental Healthcare Services: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rural and remote settings present unique challenges to the delivery of effective and timely mental health services. Telehealth services may help to bridge the gap between providers and rural consumers, but careful design is essential to ensure services meet consumer priorities and needs and to optimise uptake. Choice-based preference studies are uniquely suited to deliver this type of evidence to inform the design of appropriate telehealth services.

OBJECTIVE: This review aims to identify evidence from discrete choice experiments and best-worst scaling studies conducted internationally on attributes of telehealth services that are significant predictors of choice, with a focus on evidence relevant to tele-mental health services in rural and remote settings.

METHODS: Four online databases (Ovid MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase and Scopus) were searched from inception until 13 November 2025 to identify discrete choice experiments and best-worst scaling studies eliciting preferences for attributes of tele-mental health services or telehealth care for other conditions among rural and remote consumers. We focused on studies published in English, and excluded studies that examine preferences for only in-person care, services that are not mental healthcare or focus only on urban consumers and for which full text versions are unavailable. Data were synthesised narratively based on an a priori identified conceptual framework of access to healthcare, and attributes were assessed for frequency and significance.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, out of a total of 2,005 screened. We identified studies examining preferences for telehealth-delivered: (1) mental healthcare in urban only or pooled urban and rural populations; and (2) other healthcare in rural only or pooled rural and urban populations, but none focusing on tele-mental healthcare services in fully rural settings. A total of 114 attributes were identified and thematically classified into five dimensions of access to healthcare: approachability, acceptability, availability and accommodation, affordability and appropriateness. Consistently significant attributes included out-of-pocket costs, wait time, and those under the categories of modality, effectiveness and interaction features. Notably, while respondents prioritised in-person over telehealth-only appointments, they preferred a combination of in-person and telehealth over in-person only appointments. Telehealth also tends to be preferred by younger patients and those experiencing less severe health conditions.

DISCUSSION: Encouraging the optimal use of telehealth delivered mental healthcare in rural settings is strongly dependent on making these services more affordable as well as available within reasonable timeframes. Moreover, while there is a strong case for effectively utilising telehealth services in rural settings, mixed service delivery models offering both in-person and telehealth options are likely to gain the most uptake among rural consumers and facilitate improved experiences and meet care needs.

articles.title: Atopic Dermatitis: Disease Burden in Young Children: Results from the PEDISTAD Global Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic relapsing inflammatory condition that imposes a considerable burden on children and their families.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to investigate the disease burden and quality-of-life impact across three age groups of children with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

METHODS: PEDISTAD is an observational global registry of children aged < 12 years with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. Physician-reported disease characteristics, atopic comorbidities, treatment patterns, and patient/caregiver-reported quality-of-life measures are being collected over a period of 10 years. Patients were enrolled in the PEDISTAD Global Registry between September 2018 and April 2024; the data reported here are from a database lock on 31 July 2024.

RESULTS: A total of 1612 patients enrolled in PEDISTAD were included in this analysis, of which 238 were aged < 2 years, 645 aged 2 to < 6 years, and 729 aged 6 to < 12 years. The age of onset of atopic dermatitis was early in life. The incidence of asthma, allergic rhinitis, and allergic conjunctivitis increased with age. Mean Eczema Area and Severity Index scores were 14.1, 13.4, and 14.7 for patients aged < 2 years, 2 to < 6 years, and 6 to < 12 years, respectively. With regard to the itch burden and resultant scratching reported by parents and caregivers of the youngest children, the numerical rating score was 5.5 and 5.8 in both 0 to < 2 years and 2 to < 6 years, respectively. For those aged 6 to < 12 years, the itch burden was highest at night, with a Numeric Rating Scale score of 4.9 versus 3.8 during the day. Patient/caregiver-reported measures of disease burden were high for all age groups. The quality of life of the entire family was affected in multiple ways, as measured by the mean Dermatitis Family Impact score, which was higher in children aged < 2 years (12.0) and 2 to < 6 years (11.9), compared with patients aged 6 to < 12 years (10.2). A high/lot of impact was reported on the sleep of the family unit (in children aged < 2 years [45.9%] and 2 to < 6 years [51.9%], compared with patients aged 6 to < 12 years (33.8%). There was a high burden of tiredness and exhaustion among caregivers, particularly in the youngest two age groups but still showing a substantial impact on the families of those aged 6 to < 12 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Children with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis have a high disease burden, with severe itch and poor sleep impacting their own health and quality of life and that of their entire family.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03687359.

articles.title: The intracellular region of truncated neurotrophin receptor TrkB-T1 is sufficient to promote brain glial reactivity, neuroinflammation and neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: The development of advanced therapies for stroke, spinal cord injury, and neurodegenerative diseases-primary causes of death, disability and dementia-requires a comprehensive understanding of the interplay between excitotoxicity, aberrant neurotrophic-signalling, glial reactivity, and neuroinflammation. Recent evidence has identified the truncated neurotrophin receptor TrkB-T1 as a potential master regulator of these processes. TrkB-T1 levels increase after stroke whereas the pro-survival full-length isoform (TrkB-FL) decreases. Furthermore, stroke-induced excitotoxicity triggers TrkB-T1 regulated intramembrane proteolysis (RIP), which produces TrkB-T1-ICD, a poorly characterised fragment containing the receptor intracellular domain and a few transmembrane amino acids. This study investigated whether the TrkB-T1 intracellular domain intrinsically contributes to neurotoxicity, reactive gliosis, and neuroinflammation. Our results predict that TrkB-T1 RIP generates a nuclear localization signal in TrkB-T1-ICD that might support nuclear translocation and injury-induced transcriptional regulation in neurons undergoing excitotoxicity. Using cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), we generated a TrkB-T1-ICD mimetic peptide (Bio-LTT1Ct) containing the TrkB-T1 intracellular region. Bio-LTT1Ct translocated to the nucleus of neurons and astrocytes, provoking cell death and inducing early transcriptional changes in neurons, resembling those triggered by excitotoxicity. In vivo, intranasally administrated Bio-LTT1Ct was brain-permeable and distributed within cortical neurons and astrocytes across both hemispheres. Notably, Bio-LTT1Ct administration was sufficient to promote TrkB isoform imbalance, glial reactivity, and acquisition of proinflammatory profiles, all considered stroke hallmarks. In conclusion, these results imply that TrkB-T1 RIP might be a central mechanism of ischaemic damage and identify the receptor's intracellular region as sufficient to recapitulate stroke-like effects, marking this pathological mechanism as a critical target for therapy.

articles.title: Playing Surface Characteristics and Their Effects on Football Performance Across Multiple Surface Types: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The characteristics of the playing surface are increasingly recognized as key determinants of football-specific performance.

OBJECTIVES: This systematic review synthesizes mechanistic and applied evidence on how natural grass, artificial turf, and sand influence physical, physiological, neuromuscular, and perceptual outcomes in football players.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, SPORTDiscus and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to 17 June 2026. Eligible studies included original peer-reviewed research involving football players performing football-related activities on natural grass, artificial turf, or other playing surfaces, provided that natural grass or artificial turf was included as a comparison condition. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool for non-randomized intervention studies and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale adapted for cross-sectional studies (NOS-xs). Results were synthesized using a qualitative narrative approach because of substantial methodological heterogeneity across study designs, surface comparisons, and outcome measures. A total of 814 records were identified, of which 16 studies met the eligibility criteria.

RESULTS: Locomotor responses were the most surface-sensitive domain: several studies reported greater external running demands on artificial turf, including higher sprint frequency, acceleration demands, and total running distance; however, results were heterogeneous and some studies observed no meaningful differences between surfaces. Sand consistently imposed greater metabolic cost and reduced running efficiency. Physiological responses (e.g., heart rate and lactate) showed variable results across studies, suggesting that internal load may be influenced not only by surface characteristics but also by task constraints, participant characteristics, and familiarity with the playing surface. Neuromuscular outcomes revealed limited acute variation, although isolated evidence indicated greater residual hamstring fatigue following exposure to artificial turf. Perceptual responses were inconsistent and appeared moderated by surface familiarity. A critical limitation across studies was the scarce reporting of objective mechanical surface properties, such as shock absorption, deformation, and rotational traction, restricting mechanistic interpretation.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the findings highlight the importance of integrating mechanical characterization, standardized football-specific protocols, and contextual covariates when evaluating player-surface interactions. These results inform evidence-based training design, load management, and pitch selection in football. PROSPERO registration number: CRD42024605254.

articles.title: Brassica rapa L. leaf hydroalcoholic extract attenuates L-NAME-induced hypertension in rats: associations with the Ang II-NO axis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory markers.
articles.abstract: Brassica rapa L. leaves are a potential source of phenolic and flavonoid compounds associated with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. This study evaluated the effects of Brassica rapa L. leaf hydroalcoholic extract (BRLHE) in L-NAME-induced hypertension in rats. 48 rats were allocated to six groups (n = 8/group). L-NAME (40 mg/kg/day) was administered orally for 28 days, with concurrent BRLHE administration (100, 200, or 400 mg/kg/day) and captopril (25 mg/kg/day). Endpoint analyses included six animals per group. BRLHE exhibited total phenolic content of 34.50 ± 0.70 mg GAE/g extract, total flavonoid content of 11.86 ± 0.43 mg QE/g extract, and a 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl IC₅₀ of 33.70 µg/mL. LC-MS/MS tentatively identified 11 phytoconstituents, including Apigenin, Berberine, Luteolin, Kaempferol, Curcumin, β-sitosterol, Caffeic acid, Rutin, p-coumaric acid, Quercetin, and Naringenin. BRLHE (400 mg/kg) reduced systolic blood pressure (120.8 ± 9.86 vs. 186.0 ± 20.52 mmHg), diastolic blood pressure (81.43 ± 10.33 vs. 145.9 ± 19.21 mmHg), and mean arterial pressure (94.49 ± 9.38 vs. 159.3 ± 19.50 mmHg) compared with L-NAME alone (P < 0.001 for all). BRLHE also improved electrocardiographic parameters, increased tissue SOD, GSH, CAT, and NOx, and reduced MDA, angiotensin II, NF-κB, TNF-α, and IL-6. Quantitative RT-PCR demonstrated increased AKT1 and NOS3/eNOS mRNA expression. Histopathological evaluation revealed attenuation of L-NAME-induced structural alterations in the cardiac, aortic, and renal tissues following BRLHE treatment. Overall, BRLHE attenuated L-NAME-induced hypertensive and associated biochemical alterations, supporting further preclinical investigation.

articles.title: Implication of Perivascular Adipose Tissue as a Potential Therapeutic Target for the Vascular Defensive Actions of Incretin-Based Therapies and SGLT2 Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is a predominant cause of illness in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. Although glucose reduction has traditionally been the principal therapeutic target for treating hyperglycemia, recent cardiovascular outcome trials have revealed that incretin-based therapies and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide significant cardiovascular benefits beyond merely lowering blood glucose levels. The precise mechanisms underlying the multifaceted vascular effects of these therapies are not fully understood. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) has been identified as an active player in regulating vascular tone and inflammation. Under physiological conditions, PVAT exhibits anticontractile and vasoprotective effects; however, under metabolic and cardiovascular pathological conditions, PVAT undergoes inflammatory and oxidative remodeling, which can lead to endothelial dysfunction, increased arterial stiffness, and hypertension. Recent experimental and translational studies suggest that incretin-based therapies and SGLT2 inhibitors may help improve the homeostasis of PVAT, consequently enhancing vascular function and regulating blood pressure. Despite these developments, the potential role of PVAT as a target for metabolic therapies has not been thoroughly reviewed. This review aims to address this critical knowledge gap and proposes PVAT and its signaling as novel therapeutic targets through which incretin-based treatments and SGLT2 inhibitors could provide vascular protection, thereby redefining cardiometabolic pharmacotherapy.

articles.title: Microplastic Detection in the Ascending Aorta: An Exploratory Study Using Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (Py-GC/MS).
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as significant environmental pollutants that have been detected in various human tissues. This pilot biomonitoring study explored polymer mass in dissected versus non-dissected ascending aortic tissue. A total of 16 ascending aortic samples (8 acute type A aortic dissection [AD] and 8 acute type B dissection with arch involvement but a non-dissected ascending aorta [ND]) were examined using pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) to screen 11 polymers. Both groups had aortic disease. Polymer-related signals were reported in all samples, with total mass estimates ranging from 1.92 to 155.58 µg/g tissue. The predominant reported polymer was polyamide 66 (PA66; 50.7%), followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC; 40.5%) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET; 8.8%). AD tissues showed a 3.9-fold higher estimated polymer burden than ND tissues (74.51 ± 42.81 vs. 19.25 ± 16.48 µg/g, p = 0.0077). PET estimates were also higher in AD tissues (7.36 ± 6.44 vs. 0.89 ± 1.49 µg/g, p = 0.025), but PET identification was tentative and polymer-specific tests were exploratory. Total polymer mass correlated with ascending aortic diameter (Spearman's rho = 0.865, p < 0.001). The age- and group-adjusted association (coefficient 0.079 mm per µg/g; p = 0.0098) was sensitive to omission of one observation (p = 0.140). These findings describe a difference in estimated polymer burden between two diseased-tissue groups. Incomplete analytical validation and possible perioperative contamination limit interpretation; particle identity, tissue localization, vascular toxicity and causality were not established. Further analytical and multicenter validation is needed.

articles.title: Effect of different CO₂ insufflation pressures on endotracheal cuff pressure, airway pressures, and postoperative respiratory complications during robotic radical prostatectomy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Robot assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which raise airway pressures that may be transmitted to the endotracheal tube (ETT) cuff. We investigated whether the level of carbon dioxide (CO₂) insufflation pressure affects ETT cuff pressure during RARP. In this single centre, three arm, parallel group randomized controlled trial, 90 patient undergoing elective RARP were randomly assigned to an intraabdominal CO₂ insufflation pressure of 10, 12, or 15 mmHg (30 per group) under a standardized anaesthetic. Cuff pressure was measured with a manometer and readjusted to baseline at eleven perioperative time points; peak and plateau airway pressures, end-tidal CO₂, and postoperative sore throat, hoarseness, and cough (1, 24, and 72 h) were also recorded. The primary outcome was the time-averaged cuff pressure during the pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg phase. Time averaged cuff pressure did not differ among the 10, 12, and 15 mmHg groups (30.3 ± 3.7, 28.7 ± 2.2, and 29.9 ± 2.8 cmH₂O; P = 0.089; pairwise differences - 1.6 to + 1.3 cmH₂O, all 95% confidence intervals within ± 3.5 cmH₂O), nor did peak cuff pressure, airway pressures, or end-tidal CO₂ at any time point. Between consecutive measurements, cuff and peak airway pressures rose and fell together at insufflation, Trendelenburg positioning, and return to supine, but the size of a patient's airway-pressure change did not predict the cuff-pressure change.
