Postoperative respiratory symptoms were infrequent and similar between groups. Within all groups, cuff and airway pressures changed significantly over time. Within the 10-15 mmHg range, CO₂ insufflation pressure had no detectable dose-dependent effect on ETT cuff pressure during RARP; between-group differences larger than approximately 3.5 cmH₂O are unlikely. Cuff pressure nonetheless frequently exceeded the recommended range, supporting regular manometric monitoring during surgery.

articles.title: A Two-Dimensional Perspective on Quality Of Life: Changes After the Balancing Everyday Life Intervention for Mental Health Service Users and Relationships to Everyday Occupations - An RCT Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the Balancing Everyday Life (BEL) intervention compared with care as usual (CAU) for mental health service users found no group differences when quality of life (QoL) was treated as a single construct. However, research suggests that (QoL) consists of two dimensions: a personalized life-and-health dimension (e.g., life satisfaction, health, leisure, and work) and an environmental dimension (e.g., safety, housing, and family situation). The current study re-examined data from the BEL study to investigate whether the BEL group and the CAU differed regarding improvements on the two aforementioned QoL dimensions and explore how changes in everyday occupations were related to QoL improvements.

METHODS: A total of 226 mental health service users were assigned to BEL or CAU. Data were collected at baseline, post-intervention, and six-month follow-up. QoL was measured using the Manchester Short Assessment of Quality of Life (MANSA) and analyzed as two dimensions. Everyday occupations were assessed through measures of actual participation and subjective experiences. Change scores were analyzed using t-tests and Pearson correlations.

RESULTS: The BEL group showed significantly greater improvement in the life-and-health dimension of QoL after the intervention, with marginal significance at follow-up. Positive perceptions of everyday occupations were moderately associated with improvements in both QoL dimensions, whereas actual activity participation showed weaker associations.

CONCLUSION: Treating QoL as a two-dimensional construct revealed intervention effects that were not detected in previous analyses. Interventions emphasizing meaningful everyday occupations may enhance QoL and recovery among mental health service users. Trial Registration The study was registered with ClinicalTrial.gov. Reg. No. NCT02619318. Retrospectively registered: 20-11-2015.

articles.title: Mechanisms Behind the Disease: Understanding the Role of APRIL in IgAN Pathogenesis: A Podcast.
articles.abstract: This podcast provides an overview of immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN), the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide and a progressive, immune-mediated chronic kidney disease (CKD) often diagnosed in early to mid-adulthood. Patients face heterogeneous presentations ranging from asymptomatic disease to proteinuria and hematuria leading to rapid loss of kidney function, with many progressing to kidney failure within a decade. Beyond renal effects, IgAN imposes substantial quality-of-life burdens, particularly affecting individuals of childbearing potential. The pathogenesis of IgAN is best explained by the four-hit process involving the overproduction of galactose-deficient immunoglobulin A1 (Gd-IgA1), development of anti-Gd-IgA1 autoantibodies, immune complex formation, and mesangial deposition of immune complexes, leading to complement activation and glomerular injury. Central to this process is dysregulated B cell activation, differentiation, and immunoglobulin class switching. A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a member of the tumor necrosis factor superfamily, promotes pathogenic IgA1 production through plasma cell survival and IgA class switching. Genetic, preclinical, and clinical evidence implicates APRIL as a key driver of IgAN pathophysiology. Management strategies such as using renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors focus on supportive care and mitigation of generic CKD drivers but do not directly address upstream immune mechanisms, leaving many patients at risk for irreversible nephron loss. With the 2025 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes guidelines, the treatment of IgAN is evolving toward earlier, proactive management that simultaneously targets IgA immune complex-mediated injury and the long-term consequences of CKD. Emerging insights into APRIL-driven pathways support the development of targeted therapies that may selectively reduce pathogenic IgA production while preserving protective immune function, offering a promising strategy to address the underlying disease mechanism and improve long-term outcomes and quality of life in patients with IgAN.

articles.title: The Impact of Lifestyle Interventions and Mental Health Management on Arrhythmias in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarise contemporary evidence on the impact of lifestyle interventions and mental health management on arrhythmias in patients with heart failure (HF), and to highlight emerging therapeutic opportunities.

RECENT FINDINGS: Lifestyle modification targets shared risk factors in both arrhythmias and HF. In atrial fibrillation (AF), weight loss, exercise, alcohol reduction, and risk factor management reduce arrhythmia burden and improve arrhythmia-related symptoms and quality of life. Similarly, in both HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), exercise training improves functional capacity and quality of life, whilst dietary interventions and weight loss are particularly beneficial in HFpEF. Mental health disorders represent novel targets for intervention for arrhythmias in HF; these conditions are common in arrhythmia and HF patients and associated with poorer outcomes, but early data suggests that mental health interventions do not reduce arrhythmia burden or cardiovascular outcomes despite improving overall psychological well-being and quality of life. Lifestyle intervention to improve physical health is central to HF and arrhythmia care and established as a central pillar of management. Mental health represents an important but under-recognised target which requires urgent further investigation.

articles.title: Non-cardiac comorbidities and functional impairment in acute heart failure: a hospital-wide real-world cohort study (COMPACT-HF).
articles.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults and is associated with non-cardiac comorbidities (NCCs) and functional impairment. Their prognostic and therapeutic implications remain incompletely characterized. COMPACT-HF was a retrospective cohort study of adults discharged after hospitalization for AHF at a tertiary teaching hospital in 2023. Comorbidity burden was assessed using the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and predefined NCCs. Functional impairment was defined as loss of ≥ 1 basic activity of daily living (ADL). Primary outcome was 12-month all-cause mortality. We included 456 patients (mean age 82.6 ± 8.6 years; 50% male); 96% had ≥ 1 NCC and 48% had functional impairment. Twelve-month mortality was 31%. CCI was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.17 per point; 95% CI 1.07-1.27, p < 0.001), while functional impairment provided additional prognostic information beyond comorbidity burden. Advanced chronic kidney disease, dementia, and active malignancy were among the NCCs most strongly associated with mortality. Among patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, dementia, advanced chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease, and functional impairment were associated with lower prescription of ≥ 3 of 4 guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes, whereas CCI was not; GDMT prescription also varied substantially according to discharge ward. In this hospital-wide real-world cohort of patients discharged alive after AHF hospitalization, NCCs and functional impairment were highly prevalent and associated with mortality, while specific clinical conditions and discharge ward were associated with GDMT implementation. Integrating comorbidity and functional assessment may improve risk stratification and support a holistic approach to AHF management.

articles.title: RCAN2 attenuates lung cancer metastasis and thrombotic tendency by downregulating tissue factor via NFATC1/SNAI1 axis.
articles.abstract: Lung cancer metastasis and cancer-associated thrombosis are major complications affecting patient prognosis. Regulator of calcineurin 2 (RCAN2) has been implicated in tumor progression, yet its role in lung cancer remains undefined. Bioinformatics analysis indicated that low RCAN2 expression in lung cancer cells correlated with poor prognosis in lung cancer patients. Lentivirus-mediated stable RCAN2-overexpressing/knockdown lung cancer cell lines were established to carry out loss- and gain-of-function experiments. RCAN2 overexpression significantly suppressed cell migration, invasion, and EMT, as evidenced by reduced SNAI1 and vimentin expression, whereas RCAN2 knockdown produced opposite effects. Notably, RCAN2 concurrently downregulated tissue factor (TF) expression in cells and secretion in cell supernatant, a key initiator of coagulation that is highly expressed in lung cancer and associated with metastatic and thrombotic risk. Mechanistic investigation revealed that RCAN2 overexpression inhibited NFATC1 nuclear translocation in lung cancer cells, thereby suppressing SNAI1 expression and subsequent TF secretion; NFATC1 inhibitor treatment reversed these effects, confirming NFATC1/SNAI1 axis dependency. In tumor-bearing mice, RCAN2 overexpression attenuated tumor metastasis, accompanied by diminished pulmonary fibrinogen deposition and reduced plasma TF levels. These findings demonstrated that RCAN2 inhibited lung cancer metastasis through the NFATC1/SNAI1 axis and suppressed TF-mediated procoagulant activity, suggesting that this regulatory network may link lung cancer metastasis control and thrombotic risk.

articles.title: Robotic versus laparoscopic transanal minimally invasive surgery (TAMIS) for rectal neoplasms: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and IDEAL framework mapping.
articles.abstract: Transanal minimally invasive surgery(TAMIS) enables local excision of selected rectal neoplasms. Robotic TAMIS(R-TAMIS) may overcome technical constraints of conventional laparoscopic TAMIS(L-TAMIS), but whether these capabilities translate into better outcomes remains uncertain. We compared R-TAMIS and L-TAMIS, examining the evidence in the context of robotic procedural maturity. PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched through 2026 for comparative studies of adults undergoing TAMIS for rectal neoplasm. Risk of bias, certainty of evidence, and procedural maturity were assessed using ROBINS-I, GRADE, and the IDEAL framework. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Six retrospective comparative cohorts including 314 patients were identified. R-TAMIS was associated with a higher likelihood of full-thickness resection (OR 11.77, 95%CI 1.40-98.85; P = 0.02), an outcome not appropriate for every lesion. R0 resection was comparable(OR 1.30, 95%CI 0.49-3.47; P = 0.60), with no significant differences in operative time, estimated blood loss, complications, conversion, readmission, or length of stay. Hospital costs tended to be higher with R-TAMIS(I²=99%). All outcomes were supported by very-low-certainty evidence. IDEAL assessment showed that R-TAMIS was introduced in centres with established L-TAMIS experience, while the robotic technique remained in an earlier phase of development. Comparative evidence shows broadly comparable outcomes. Difference in achieved excision depth requires confirmation using standardized outcome definitions and clinically appropriate case selection. These results were achieved despite greater procedural maturity of L-TAMIS and, in some cohorts, more challenging robotic case selection. This developmental asymmetry highlights the need to determine whether maturation and standardization of R-TAMIS will translate its technical capabilities into clinically meaningful advantages in appropriately selected, technically demanding lesions.

articles.title: Prevalence of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress and associated factors among Palestinian nurses in the Gaza Strip during the war.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ongoing war in the Gaza Strip has profoundly affected the psychological well-being of healthcare workers, particularly nurses, who provide frontline care amid continuous violence, displacement, and resource scarcity. Understanding the mental health consequences of these extreme working conditions is essential for developing targeted interventions and institutional support mechanisms. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress, and to examine associated factors among Palestinian nurses during the 2023-2025 war in the Gaza Strip.

METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted between August 15 and September 15, 2025, involving 260 nurses recruited from public and field hospitals across the Gaza Strip. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire incorporating the validated Arabic version of the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21). Descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression analyses were performed using SPSS version 24 to identify factors associated with psychological symptom scores.

RESULTS: Based on DASS-21 classifications, 81.5% of nurses reported elevated depressive symptoms, 86.9% reported elevated anxiety symptoms, and 69.2% reported elevated stress symptoms of varying severity. Notably, 67.7% of participants reported elevated symptoms across all three domains concurrently. Regression analysis showed that nurses with more than 10 years of experience had significantly higher depression (B = 6.67, 95% CI = 1.40 to 11.94, p = 0.013) and anxiety (B = 10.70, 95% CI = 5.62 to 15.76, p < 0.001) scores. In contrast, working more than 36 h per week was associated with significantly lower depression ((B = -3.71, 95% CI = - 6.44 to - 0.98, p = 0.009), anxiety scores (B = -4.89, 95% CI = -7.50 to -2.25, p < 0.001), and stress (B = -3.99, 95% CI = -6.54 to -1.43, p = 0.004) scores compared with those working ≤ 36 h/week. Additionally, nurses in supervisory or managerial roles had significantly lower anxiety (B = -7.37, 95% CI = - 13.38 to - 1.36, p = 0.016).

CONCLUSION: This study found a high burden of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress among nurses in the Gaza Strip during the ongoing conflict, exceeding rates reported in many comparable settings. These findings suggest that occupational workload indicators were significantly associated with nurses' psychological symptom scores in this sample. Institutional measures, including regulated working hours, psychosocial support programs, and routine mental health monitoring, are urgently needed to safeguard nurses' well-being and support healthcare system resilience under crisis conditions.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Patient and partner experiences of prostate cancer survivorship in Ireland: findings from the co-designed PRO-ACT study (CTRIAL-IE 24-45).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy among men in Ireland, yet patient and partner experiences regarding sexual wellbeing, treatment preparedness, and survivorship needs remain poorly characterised.

METHODS: The PRO-ACT study employed parallel, co-designed online surveys for patients with PCa and their partners across the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. Surveys were developed collaboratively with a patient previously treated for PCa and disseminated online between November 2024 and June 2025. Descriptive statistics summarised demographics, treatment preparedness, partner inclusion, sexual wellbeing, mental health, multidisciplinary consultation, and urinary/bowel toxicities.

RESULTS: A total of 598 patients and 538 partners participated. Preparedness for treatment-related sexual consequences was low: 66.3% of patients felt underprepared, and 53.1% of partners received no explanation. Sexual difficulties were widespread, with 85.4% of patients reporting erectile problems and 84.3% reporting decline in sexual wellbeing; 68.0% of partners also reported deterioration. Mental health impacts were substantial (patients: 58.7%, partners: 51.5%), yet psychological support was rarely offered. Urinary incontinence (63.7%), obstructive symptoms (40.4%), and bowel disturbances (40.1%) were common. Multidisciplinary involvement was inconsistent, with only 48.6% offered cross-specialty consultations.

CONCLUSIONS: This first all-island assessment demonstrates major gaps in information provision, partner inclusion, psychosexual support, and toxicity management. Findings highlight the need for structured, personalised, multidisciplinary survivorship pathways recognising sexual wellbeing and mental health as core components. Results provide actionable insights for Ireland's next National Cancer Strategy.

articles.title: Integrated hydrogeochemical characterization and numerical modeling of groundwater flow and strontium transport in an industrialized alluvial aquifer, Northern Pakistan.
articles.abstract: Groundwater is the primary water source for communities and industries surrounding the Gadoon Amazai Industrial Estate (GAIE), northern Pakistan, but its hydrochemical evolution and subsurface transport pathways remain insufficiently constrained. This study integrated groundwater chemistry, multivariate statistics, geographic information system mapping, three-dimensional groundwater-flow simulation, particle tracking, and dissolved-strontium (Sr) transport modeling. Forty groundwater samples collected in December 2024 were analyzed for physicochemical parameters, major ions, nutrients, and trace elements. Electrical conductivity (EC) ranged from 241 to 1,526 µS cm⁻1 and total dissolved solids (TDS) from 154.24 to 976.64 mg L⁻1, indicating generally fresh groundwater with localized increases in mineralization. Sr ranged from 0.159 to 1.346 mg L⁻1 (mean 0.317 mg L⁻1), remained below the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency non-regulatory lifetime health advisory value of 4 mg L⁻1, and correlated strongly with Ca (r = 0.930) and Mg (r = 0.952). A screened three-component PCA solution explained 83.80% of total hydrochemical variance, with Sr loading strongly on the dominant mineralization component, together with EC and the major ions; nitrate (NO3⁻) also loaded positively on this component. The steady-state groundwater-flow model, calibrated against 18 observation wells, achieved r = 0.996, a root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 1.692 m, and a normalized root-mean-square error (nRMSE) = 3.43%, and indicated regional flow from northeastern recharge areas toward Kundal Khwar in the southwest. Transient scenario simulations indicated localized water-table deepening through 2030. The Sr-transport model provided a close fit to the available calibration dataset (r = 0.979; nRMSE = 6.664%) and simulated plume expansion under the 2025-2030 scenario. Under this specified scenario and model parameterization, simulated Sr mass stored in the aquifer increased from 311,535 to 328,205 kg. Sensitivity analysis showed that the modeled mass was parameter-dependent, with ± 20% perturbations in storage-related parameters producing approximately ± 9% variation in total Sr mass. Because temporal Sr observations and site-specific sorption data were unavailable, the transport outputs are interpreted as scenario-based management evaluations rather than deterministic forecasts.

articles.title: Migraine: translational challenges, novel therapies and disease modification.
articles.abstract: Migraine is the most common neurological disorder, which after stroke confers the greatest neurological disability in the working population. As with other disorders of brain function, pathophysiological processes are more difficult to delineate, notwithstanding the biological complexities and clinical heterogeneity of the disorder. The current review will outline the framework upon which mechanistic pathways have been predicated. It will examine bench to bedside models: what we have learned from those which have been unsuccessful and address those which have borne fruit, presenting the clinical and exploratory insights gained. In the second part the more recent successes in drug therapeutics are summarised, from clinical trials to real world observations and limitations. With this in sight, the third part emphasises the need to reframe goals towards longer-term disease modification, addressing the impact of confounding comorbidities and moving towards a biopsychosocial model of pain.

articles.title: Molecular epidemiology, spike-protein evolution, antigenic variation, and experimental pathogenicity of G2c porcine epidemic diarrhea virus: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) is a major cause of severe enteric disease and mortality in neonatal piglets. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the molecular epidemiology, spike-protein variation, experimental pathogenicity, and control-related applications of the G2c lineage. Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, and ScienceDirect were searched for peer-reviewed original studies published from 1 January 2020 to 31 May 2026. Of 78 records identified, 26 studies met the eligibility criteria. G2c was the most frequently assigned lineage in several national, multi-provincial, and regional PEDV datasets in China, particularly in Sichuan and Guangdong. However, its distribution was geographically heterogeneous, and G2a remained predominant in Guangxi. Contemporary G2c viruses exhibited extensive spike-protein variation, including substitutions, insertions, deletions, and predicted glycosylation changes in antigenically relevant regions. Cross-neutralization studies demonstrated strain-dependent antigenic differences, but consistent lineage-wide immune escape was not established. Experimental infections showed that natural G2c isolates caused acute watery diarrhea, dehydration, intestinal villous atrophy, high viral shedding, and, in some studies, substantial mortality in neonatal or suckling piglets. Heterogeneity in experimental design prevented reliable comparison of virulence among strains. Current evidence also supports the development of G2c-specific molecular diagnostics and several vaccine approaches, including cell-adapted candidates, maternal-immunity strategies, messenger RNA vaccines, and autogenous inactivated vaccines. Overall, G2c is an epidemiologically important and pathogenic PEDV lineage. Standardized classification, whole-genome surveillance, functional antigenic studies, matched challenge experiments, and heterologous vaccine-efficacy evaluations are needed to improve disease control.

articles.title: Whole-brain white matter fractional anisotropy across baseball expertise levels: a TBSS study.
articles.abstract: While sports-related sensorimotor experience has been associated with differences in brain structure and function, evidence regarding white matter (WM) microstructural differences in high-speed open-skilled sports remains limited. Prior studies have often been constrained by small sample sizes or analyses restricted to selected tracts. To address these limitations, this study employed voxel-wise tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) to examine whole-brain fractional anisotropy (FA) in 142 participants: 50 highly skilled baseball (SB) players, 45 intermediate baseball (IB) players, and 47 non-player (NP) controls. TBSS revealed that the SB group exhibited significantly higher FA than the IB and/or NP groups across multiple projection and cerebellar pathways, including the pontine crossing tract, corona radiata, posterior limb of the internal capsule, superior cerebellar peduncle, and cerebral peduncle, as well as association pathways (superior fronto-occipital fasciculus and sagittal stratum), commissural pathways (corpus callosum and tapetum), and the fornix (crus)/stria terminalis. Follow-up ROI analyses showed significant group effects in seven of 16 selected tracts, including the pontine crossing tract, body of the corpus callosum, left superior corona radiata, bilateral posterior corona radiata, and bilateral tapetum. Across these tracts, the SB group consistently demonstrated higher FA than the IB and/or NP groups. Together, these results indicate that FA differences across expertise levels were primarily characterized by higher values in skilled players rather than a uniform increase across the three groups. These findings suggest that high-level baseball expertise is associated with spatially distributed WM microstructural differences across multiple neural systems implicated in sensorimotor, visuospatial, cerebellar, and interhemispheric processing.

articles.title: Temporal trends in patients undergoing artificial urinary sphincter implantation: explantation outcomes and early failure patterns in a tertiary reconstructive referral center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Baseline characteristics and perioperative risk profiles in patients undergoing artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation have changed over time, potentially influencing clinical outcomes. This study assessed temporal trends in patient characteristics and explantation outcomes to inform preoperative counselling and risk stratification.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included male patients undergoing AUS implantation between 2009 and 2025, stratified into four implantation periods. Explantation-free survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Risk factors for explantation were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models.

RESULTS: A total of 491 patients were included (2009-2012: N = 177; 2013-2017: N = 159; 2018-2022: N = 107; 2023-2025: N = 48), with a median follow-up of 54 months (IQR 14-116). Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, with a relative increase in prior radiotherapy from 35% to 42% over time. Explantation rates were 36%, 27%, 22%, and 17%, respectively, predominantly due to erosion and infection. In multivariable analysis, prior radiotherapy (HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.30-2.70), prior BPH surgery (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.10-2.77), and prior bulbar urethroplasty (HR 2.10, 95% CI 1.12-3.93) were independent predictors of explantation. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant differences in explantation-free survival between periods (p = 0.8), although a numerical increase in early explantations within 24 months was observed (7.9% to 13%). In a supplementary analysis focusing on early explantation, prior radiotherapy (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.38-4.39) and prior urethral surgery (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.31-4.77) were independently associated with increased risk. Later implantation periods showed an increase in early explantation risk; however, this did not reach statistical significance. The study is limited by its retrospective single-center design.

CONCLUSION: The AUS remains a durable and effective treatment option for male incontinence, with stable outcomes across implantation periods. Careful preoperative counselling and structured follow-up remain essential, particularly in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Nodulation induces systemic defense in Phaseolus vulgaris leaves against Sclerotinia sclerotiorum through ROS accumulation and COBRA-like gene expression.
articles.abstract: Mature root nodule symbiosis enhances susceptibility infection to Sclerotinia sclerotiorum by coordinating ROS, defense metabolism, cell-wall carbohydrate profiles, and specific PvCOBL gene responses in Phaseolus vulgaris. Root nodule symbiosis (RNS) enhances plant nutrition and can systemically modify plant defense responses. However, the mechanisms linking RNS to resistance against necrotrophic pathogens remain poorly understood in Phaseolus vulgaris. In this study, we investigated whether nodulation induced by Rhizobium tropici influences systemic resistance to Sclerotinia sclerotiorum and is associated with changes in reactive oxygen species (ROS), defense-related metabolism, cell wall-associated carbohydrates, and COBRA-like (COBL) gene family. A temporal analysis of nodulation (7, 14, 21, and 30 days post inoculation, dpi) revealed that resistance to S. sclerotiorum was strongly dependent on the developmental stage of symbiosis. At the mature nodule stage (21 dpi), nodulated plants (N+) exhibited approximately 7 fold lower necrotic lesion area than non-nodulated (N-) plants, whereas susceptibility was greater at immature (14 dpi) and senescent (30 dpi) stages of nodulation. Enhanced resistance at 21 dpi was associated with a 5-fold increase in H₂O₂ accumulation, elevated phenolic and flavonoid contents, increased chlorophyll levels, and changes in cell wall-associated carbohydrate profiles. Genome-wide analysis identified 14 PvCOBL genes distributed across three phylogenetic clades and revealed substantial conservation in gene structure, and the characteristic CCVS motif. Promoter and transcriptomic analyses revealed that PvCOBL genes exhibit distinct tissue-, developmental-, symbiosis-, and pathogen-associated expression patterns. RT-qPCR further identified PvCOBL9 and PvCOBL10 as promising candidates associated with nodulation-dependent pathogen responses. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nodule maturation is associated with systemic physiological and transcriptional reprogramming that contributes to reduced susceptibility to S. sclerotiorum. This work provides the first comprehensive characterization of the COBL gene family in P. vulgaris and identifies candidate genes that may link rhizobial symbiosis, cell wall-associated processes, and systemic immunity.

articles.title: The longitudinal association of chronic physical conditions with change in psychological problems from childhood to early adolescence. A population-based study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Youth with chronic physical conditions (CPCs) experience more psychological problems than peers without CPCs. The transition to adolescence may be a particularly relevant prevention window. However, previous longitudinal studies show mixed results, potentially due to reporter discrepancies. We investigated associations of CPCs with changes in psychological problems during the transition to early adolescence using a multi-informant, integrative approach. This cohort study was embedded in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, United States. Parents reported CPCs at baseline (Mage = 9.9 ± 0.6 years). Children and parents reported internalizing and externalizing problems at baseline and three-year follow-up, using the Brief Problem Monitor and Child Behavior Checklist respectively. Secondary outcomes, assessed at two-year follow-up, included positive affect, sleep, and physical activity. Associations were tested using linear mixed-effects models. Among 9,797 participants (52% male, 74% White), 16.4% had a CPC, predominantly asthma and severe obesity. CPCs were not associated with cross-sectional or longitudinal differences in child-reported psychological problems. CPCs were related to higher parent-reported psychological problems at baseline but not to longitudinal change. Associations were consistent across CPC subtypes. CPCs were cross-sectionally associated with lower positive affect, poorer sleep, and less physical activity.

CONCLUSIONS: Children with CPCs do not appear to develop more psychological problems than peers without CPCs during the transition to adolescence. Parent, but not child, reports indicated higher psychological problems among children with CPCs at baseline, reflecting informant differences. Children with CPCs showed poorer well-being and lifestyle indicators. Multi-informant, multi-domain assessments advance integrative insight into mental health development in children with CPCs.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Youth with chronic physical conditions show more psychological problems than healthy peers. • Longitudinal findings on CPC-related change over time are inconsistent, possibly due to reporter discrepancies.

WHAT IS NEW: • Using a multi-informant approach, we found no evidence that CPCs are associated with increases in internalizing or externalizing problems from late childhood to early adolescence. • Parent, but not child, reports indicated higher problems at baseline, underscoring the need to adjust for baseline levels and consider shared method bias.

articles.title: Cell-based immunotherapies for infectious diseases: current evidence and translational perspectives on cytokine induced killer (CIK) cells.
articles.abstract: The persistent global burden of infectious diseases, compounded by environmental challenges, emerging pathogens, and antimicrobial resistance, underscores the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antimicrobial agents. Cell based immunotherapies, which harness the body's immune system to combat pathogens, have gained increasing attention for their potential to provide targeted, durable, and adaptive responses. Recently, we demonstrated that clinically licensed cytokine-induced killer (CIK) cells, used in cancer treatment, significantly reduced Plasmodium-infected erythrocytes in vitro. This review focuses on the emerging role of CIK cells in infectious disease therapy, positioning them alongside other prominent immune effector cells such as CTLs, γδT cells, and NK cells. We explore the biology, recognition mechanisms, their potential feature, and cytotoxic functions of these cell populations, distinguishing direct findings in infection-specific CIK studies from mechanisms characterized in oncology or other cytotoxic lymphocytes. While CTLs, γδT cells, and NK cells have been extensively studied for their roles in early and adaptive immune responses, CIK cells traditionally investigated in oncology, are now being recognized for their potential in antiviral and antimicrobial immunity. Alongside with CTLs, γδT cells, and NK cells, we detail CIK cell phenotypes, activation strategies, effector functions, and the limited but growing body of evidence supporting their application in some viral infections. The available findings support further investigation of CIK cells as a candidate approach in selected infectious settings, while their broader antimicrobial applicability, comparative efficacy, target specificity, safety, and clinical benefit require further evaluation in these settings.

articles.title: Quality improvement in neonatal critical care nephrology and CKRT programs.
articles.abstract: Research in low-volume, high-complexity populations presents inherent challenges, particularly in pediatrics and neonatology, where patients frequently push physiological and technological boundaries. In these settings, traditional research paradigms are often limited, making quality improvement (QI) methodologies essential to advancing care. Nowhere is this more evident than in neonatal critical care nephrology. Over the past two decades, collaborative, multidisciplinary QI efforts have driven meaningful progress in the identification, risk stratification, and management of acute kidney injury (AKI) in neonates. The development of neonatal-specific AKI definitions, proactive surveillance strategies, nephrotoxin stewardship programs, and consensus-driven approaches to post-neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) discharge follow-up have improved recognition, standardized communication, and reduced practice variability across diverse care settings. As AKI recognition improves, increasing numbers of neonates are identified as candidates for kidney replacement therapy (KRT), exposing parallel gaps in quality metrics and standardized approaches to neonatal continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT). Much of current CKRT practice remains extrapolated from adult and older pediatric data, despite important physiological and technical differences in neonates and infants. Recent multicenter registries, dedicated neonatal dialysis platforms, and learning collaboratives have begun to address this gap, demonstrating improved feasibility and survival while highlighting persistent variability in prescription, delivery, and outcomes. This review synthesizes QI-driven advances across neonatal AKI and CKRT, emphasizing the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration, shared data infrastructure, and neonatal-specific quality indicators to advance equitable, standardized kidney care for vulnerable neonatal populations.

articles.title: Caffeine for prevention of acute kidney injury in neonates with perinatal asphyxia: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caffeine is associated with reduced incidence and severity of acute kidney injury (AKI) in preterm neonates. The present study assessed the reno-protective and neurological effects of caffeine in neonates ( ≥ 35 weeks) with perinatal asphyxia (PA).

METHODS: In this parallel-group, double-blind randomized controlled trial, 78 neonates of ≥35 weeks' gestation with PA defined by NICHD criteria were randomized to receive a single intravenous dose of caffeine citrate (20 mg/kg; n = 39) or normal saline (NS; n = 39) within 2 h after birth. The primary outcome was the incidence of AKI. Secondary outcomes were AKI severity, serial serum creatinine and urine output, serum cystatin-C levels, incidence and severity of hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), anterior cerebral artery (ACA) and renal artery blood flow, cerebral and renal regional tissue oxygenation (rSO2), in-hospital complications, caffeine-related adverse events, and Hammersmith Neonatal Neurological Examination (HNNE) at discharge. Intention-to-treat analysis was done in STATA.

RESULTS: Both groups had similar incidences of AKI, 11/39 (28.2%) in caffeine and 14/39 (35.9%) in NS groups; p = 0.467. Severity of AKI, serial creatinine, urine output and cystatin-C levels were comparable. Incidence and severity of HIE, ACA and renal artery blood flow, cerebral and renal rSO2, in-hospital complications including mortality, and HNNE scores at discharge were similar. Caffeine-induced complications included tachycardia and hypokalemia.

CONCLUSIONS: A single intravenous dose of caffeine at birth did not reduce the incidence and severity of AKI, HIE, and in-hospital complications. Further research is needed on dose, frequency and in neonates undergoing therapeutic hypothermia to determine reno-protective effects of caffeine.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registry of India, Registration no: CTRI/2024/08/073008, registered prospectively on 28/08/2024, https://ctri.icmr.org.in/.

articles.title: Glyoxalase - 1 inhibition reduces endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor-mediated relaxation of the rat superior mesenteric artery.
articles.abstract: EDHF-type relaxation is frequently impaired in diabetes-related diseases, possibly due to glycative toxicity. GLO1 detoxifies methylglyoxal and suppresses accumulation of AGEs, so the current study examined the potential contribution of reduced GLO1 activity to endogenous glycative stress and vascular impairment. We examined the effects of the GLO1 inhibitor BBGC on arterial relaxation, with particular emphasis on EDHF-type relaxations. The isolated rat superior mesenteric arterial rings were cultured for 24 h in high-glucose medium (approximately 25 mmol/L) with vehicle or BBGC (10-5 mol/L). No statistically significant differences were detected in overall ACh-induced relaxation or in response to SNP and cromakalim. However, BBGC markedly reduced ACh-induced EDHF-type relaxation compared to vehicle treatment. Combined SKCa and IKCa blockade virtually abolished the residual relaxation in both groups, and no between-group difference was detected during KCa-channel blockade. Aminoguanidine co-treatment increased ACh-induced EDHF-type relaxation in BBGC-treated arteries. These results suggest that BBGC attenuated EDHF-type relaxation under high-glucose culture conditions. The findings are consistent with a possible contribution of GLO1 to KCa-dependent relaxation, although the roles of MGO accumulation and channel dysfunction remain unconfirmed.

articles.title: [Social inequality and health: what role do molecular genetics, gene-environment interactions, and epigenetics play?].
articles.abstract: Due to significant progress in molecular genetic research, the understanding of genetic and epigenetic influences on human health is growing. Recently, researchers in social epidemiology have demanded incorporating (epi)genetic factors for explaining social inequalities in health. But how can this be done in a meaningful way?Robust empirical evidence for a strong effect of disease-associated genetic factors in the sense of direct health selection is scarce. In addition, the latest large-scale genome-wide association studies do not support a strong impact of genetic factors on socioeconomic position itself. However, genetic associations with indicators of socioeconomic status may be helpful in investigating the causal direction of health inequalities. The first empirical studies have suggested that socioeconomic status exerts a social causal effect on, for example, cardiovascular diseases, high body mass index (BMI), and diabetes mellitus. Socioeconomic status can also exert its indirect influence on disease development by modifying the expression of genetic effects. These gene-environment interactions may also be mediated by epigenetic changes.The incorporation of molecular (epi)genetic factors into social epidemiological research takes greater account for the complex interplay of various causes and effects across the life course and across generations. In particular, it offers the potential to identify specific pathways through which social factors influence biological pathways underlying disease development.

articles.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and lung cancer risk in patients with type 2 diabetes and pulmonary nodules.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are associated with lower risk of several cancers in observational studies, whereas randomized-trial meta-analyses indicate little or no effect; lung-cancer-specific evidence is limited.

METHODS: We emulated a target trial in the TriNetX federated network comparing new users of GLP-1RAs versus metformin among adults with type 2 diabetes and a coded pulmonary nodule. Eligibility was assessed on or before the first qualifying prescription, a 12-month washout applied in both arms, and cohorts were 1:1 propensity score matched on 51 covariates. Outcomes were ascertained from day 90 to day 1,095. Drug-target cis-Mendelian randomization (MR) tested genetically proxied GLP1R expression against lung cancer in three GWAS consortia, with colocalization.

RESULTS: Among 12,622 matched pairs, lung cancer incidence was 1.60% with GLP-1RAs versus 2.14% with metformin (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.64-0.92); distant metastasis (HR 0.58, 0.47-0.71) and systemic anti-cancer therapy (0.58, 0.46-0.74) were also lower with GLP-1RAs. Versus metformin, the lung cancer hazard ratio was 0.72 (0.56-0.92) at a 180-day and 0.77 (0.54-1.09) at a 365-day landmark; it was 0.74 (0.59-0.93) versus DPP-4 and 0.85 (0.69-1.05) versus SGLT2 inhibitors. Negative controls were null. MR showed no association between GLP1R expression and lung cancer; colocalization showed little signal at the locus.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA initiation was associated with lower short-term lung cancer incidence versus metformin, but the null SGLT2 comparison and null genetic findings do not support sustained receptor-mediated chemoprevention.

IMPACT: These findings caution against interpreting early observational signals as chemoprevention and define what future GLP-1RA-cancer studies should report.

articles.title: [Communication in the resuscitation room: a core element of crew resource management (CRM) for safe patient care : Current developments, practical examples, and key information for resuscitation room training].
articles.abstract: The care of critically ill patients in the resuscitation room is generally provided by a multi-professional and interdisciplinary resuscitation team. Current developments among institutions that set the framework for healthcare underscore that effective communication and targeted team training must be understood not as supplementary measures, but rather as fundamental to successful patient care. For example, the German Association for Emergency Medicine (DGINA) considers qualifications in team leadership and crew resource management (CRM) for medical and nursing team members in the care of critically ill, non-traumatological patients to be indispensable. Secure and effective communication is one of these qualifications and is regarded as a central element of the five non-technical skills. The role of non-technical skills and the CRM training built upon them in preventing errors related to "human factors" has increasingly gained recognition in the medical community in recent years. Despite convincing literature, there are still no legal regulations in Germany at present stipulating the content, structure, or implementation of regular CRM (resuscitation room) training.

articles.title: Integrative multi-omic profiling reveals a spatially organized GPNMB⁺ monocyte-derived macrophage-NAMPT axis driving Th17 activation and fibrotic remodeling in cholestatic liver disease.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is characterized by chronic cholestasis, inflammatory bile duct injury, and progressive liver fibrosis. However, the spatial organization and key regulatory mechanisms of its inflammatory-fibrotic microenvironment remain poorly understood.

METHODS: We integrated large-scale single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets to construct a cellular and spatial atlas of PSC and incorporated multiple chronic fibrotic liver disease cohorts for cross-disease comparison. Key macrophage-T cell interactions and regulatory mechanisms were further evaluated using in vitro and in vivo experiments.

RESULTS: PSC liver tissues showed reduced hepatocyte abundance, expansion of immune and stromal populations, and the formation of highly fibrotic niches within injury core and boundary regions. GPNMB+ monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) were detectable across multiple chronic liver diseases, but PSC-derived GPNMB+ MDMs exhibited stronger antigen-processing and MHC class II-mediated antigen-presentation programs. Spatial analyses further showed that GPNMB+ MDMs were associated with antigen-presentation, T-cell-associated, and extracellular matrix-remodeling programs in PSC lesions. Mechanistically, GPNMB+ MDMs promoted inflammatory activation and SLC7A5-associated metabolic remodeling in Th17-like T cells through NAMPT-mediated paracrine signaling. In vitro and in vivo experiments supported the contribution of NAMPT to cholestatic liver injury and fibrotic remodeling, while HMGA1 was identified as a potential upstream regulator of the GPNMB+ MDM state.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies an HMGA1-NAMPT-Th17-like T cell-SLC7A5 axis in PSC, providing new insights into cholestatic liver fibrosis and potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: a practical imaging approach.
articles.abstract: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.

articles.title: Radiomics can predict high-risk infection stones in patients with urolithiasis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Our study seeks to design and develop radiomics (Rad) models utilizing computed tomography (CT) images to predict the presence of high-risk infection stones ahead of the operation.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 576 urolithiasis patients. Preoperative CT images were used to extract the Rad features. Subsequently, multicollinearity elimination and Lasso regression were applied for feature selection and the construction of the Rad-infection score in training cohort. The validation cohort was utilized to assess its predictive performance. Additionally, the DeLong test and decision curve analysis (DCA) were adopted to compare the predictive performance between the Rad-infection score and routine clinical biomarkers. Afterward, univariate and multivariate analyses were used to identify the risk factors for high-risk infection stones. Variables with P < 0.05 in univariate analysis were included in multivariate logistic regression to develop nomograms. The base nomogram was established with only clinical independent predictors, whereas the radiomic nomogram integrated these clinical variables with the Rad-infection score.

RESULTS: The Rad-infection score, composed of 6 Rad features, could reliably predict high-risk infection stones (AUC Training cohort = 0.751, AUC Validation cohort = 0.734). As evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis (ROC) and DCA, the Rad-infection score showed favourable predictive performance and clinical benefit relative to routine clinical biomarkers. Multivariate analyses demonstrated that gender, URBC, urine culture, and Rad-infection score were independent factors for high-risk infection stones (all P < 0.05). The nomogram derived from the Rad-infection score demonstrated strong predictive value (AUC = 0.867). Its reliability was further verified by five-fold cross-validation (AUC mean = 0.849).

CONCLUSION: CT-image-based models can preoperatively identify high-risk infection stones in our cohort. The Rad-infection score outperformed conventional clinical indicators. The Rad-infection score and radiomic nomogram hold potential to aid clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Time to Surgery after Hip Fracture: Anticoagulation May Confound Surgical Delay and Outcome.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

articles.title: Carbon availability in Staphylococcus aureus infection: cellular access, metabolic fate and antibiotic response.
articles.abstract: Carbon availability during Staphylococcus aureus infection is often equated with extracellular substrate concentration, although this measurement reveals neither cellular partitioning nor the intracellular fate of acquired carbon. This distinction becomes treatment-relevant because conditions that permit bacterial survival need not be those that later favor population recovery or resistant genotypes. Here, we synthesize infection-relevant evidence across five inferential levels: local substrate pool, cellular access, intracellular carbon fate, physiological state and antibiotic response. Applying this separation across time distinguishes immediate metabolic effects on killing from subsequent population recovery and resistant-variant expansion. In a diabetic skin-infection model, hyperglycaemia increased recovery of heritable rifampicin resistance without genomic evidence of hypermutability, consistent with altered population opportunity rather than a direct carbon-to-mutation mechanism. Across the evidence reviewed, no study in S. aureus has linked the measured carbon fate of a bacterium surviving antibiotic exposure to the recovery and resistance phenotypes of its descendants. We therefore propose a two-stage, non-obligatory model in which restrictive carbon conditions can modify survival during treatment, whereas restoration or rerouting of metabolically usable carbon can restore killing, permit susceptible regrowth or favor expansion of resistant variants. The model yields a lineage-specific, falsifiable prediction: carbon-restricted survivors contribute disproportionately to the recovered population and, under continued selection, to its resistant fraction. Testing this prediction requires experiments that preserve substrate identity, cellular identity, intracellular carbon fate and ancestry through recovery. By defining this unconnected causal step, the framework makes cellular descent testable and provides a basis for evaluating metabolic interventions across antibiotic-niche combinations.

articles.title: Dermal Exposure to Bisphenols and Their Analogs: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Dermal exposure to bisphenols is an underrecognized pathway of systemic uptake, but differences in study designs and measured endpoints complicate exposure assessment. This systematic review synthesizes 71 studies examining dermal transfer, skin permeation and retention, human toxicokinetics, and exposure modeling for bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogs.

RECENT FINDINGS: BPA has the strongest evidence for systemic dermal uptake, supported by controlled human and experimental studies, while occupational biomonitoring supports exposure relevance without isolating the dermal route. Human studies demonstrate delayed BPA absorption and partial avoidance of first-pass metabolism. BPS generally shows lower transdermal passage than BPA but substantial skin retention, whereas BPAF and TGSA exhibit appreciable permeation in human-skin experiments. Thermal paper remains the best-characterized source; textiles, hygiene products, and other consumer materials represent additional potential sources, although their dermal dose estimates rely largely on modeled migration and absorption assumptions. Dermal exposure assessment requires compound- and condition-specific parameters that distinguish skin loading, retention, permeation, and systemic bioavailability. Lower permeability does not necessarily imply lower risk. Improved human toxicokinetic data, realistic migration measurements, and refined PBPK models are needed to strengthen exposure assessment and evaluation of bisphenol alternatives.

articles.title: The Neuroanatomic Diagnostic Protocol: Evidence for a Necessary Update to the Clinical Framework for Managing Chronic Cough.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic cough represents a challenging clinical problem and significant unmet global burden. For some patients, cough can be associated with conditions impacting the respiratory system, including asthma, rhinosinusitis, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. This underpinned the rationale for the development of the Anatomic Diagnostic Protocol, an etiology-based algorithm for chronic cough management used in clinical practice for over 50 years. However, despite the value of the Anatomic Diagnostic Protocol, many patients do not respond adequately to the clinical strategies promoted in the existing management framework because they either have no obvious causative disease or their cough is unresolved by standard etiology-based therapies (refractory chronic cough). This, along with the introduction of cough hypersensitivity syndrome as a unifying condition common to most patients with chronic cough, has added additional complexity for physicians in everyday practice.

FINDINGS: We introduce the Neuroanatomic Diagnostic Protocol and the rationale behind it, a proposed timely and practical update to the classic framework that unifies the known association of cough with common etiological causes, the existence of refractory chronic cough, and the core concepts of cough hypersensitivity syndrome by acknowledging the vagus nerve and its central circuits as a distinct anatomical consideration in the effective assessment and targeted management of chronic cough.

articles.title: Design, radiochemical characterization and preclinical evaluation of a 64Cu-labeled 2-methyl-8-hydroxyquinoline complex as a PET tracer.
articles.abstract: Direct radiolabeling of cellular therapeutics and leukocytes represents a vital strategy for monitoring inflammatory loci and tracking cell-based therapies in vivo. While single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) agents, such as 111In-oxine and 99mTc-HMPAO, have long served as clinical mainstays, their utility is constrained by limited spatial resolution and suboptimal quantification. To address these limitations, we developed and preclinically validated 64Cu-labeled 2-methyl-8-hydroxyquinoline (64Cu-HMQ) as a neutral, lipophilic positron emission tomography (PET) tracer intended for high-resolution, quantitative cell-tracking paradigms (e.g., autologous leukocytes, stem cells, and immunotherapeutic vectors). 64Cu-HMQ was synthesized with high radiochemical yield (> 98%) and demonstrated robust in vitro stability in both formulation buffer and human serum over 12 h. The complex exhibited an optimal partition coefficient (logP = 1.4), providing the requisite membrane permeability for intracellular transport while maintaining adequate hydrophilicity. Baseline preclinical biodistribution and PET imaging in healthy rodents revealed favorable pharmacokinetic characteristics, marked by efficient blood and systemic clearance blood clearance, combined hepatobiliary and renal elimination, and minimal non-specific background accumulation. These foundational results establish the coordination integrity and intrinsic clearance kinetics of 64Cu-HMQ, demonstrating its strong translational potential as a long-lived (T1/2=12.7 h), quantitative PET alternative to conventional 111In-oxine for direct cell labeling and non-invasive PET cell tracking. In vitro leukocyte labeling confirmed high radiolabeling efficiency (71.2 ± 3.1%) with preserved cell viability (> 95%), highlighting its potential feasibility for cell-tracking applications.

articles.title: The Application of Engineered Probiotics in the Prophylaxis and Control of Salmonella Infections.
articles.abstract: Salmonella is a major zoonotic pathogen responsible for human and animal infections, posing significant challenges to public health and disease control. Its pathogenicity relies on a suite of molecular mechanisms mediating bacterial adhesion, invasion, intracellular persistence, immune evasion, and host-microbe crosstalk. Conventional probiotics mitigate Salmonella infection through competitive exclusion, secretion of antimicrobial metabolites, intestinal barrier reinforcement, microbiota remodelling and host immunomodulation. However, their efficacy varies depending on strain, host, dose, formulation, delivery route, infection model, and intervention timing. Genetically engineered probiotics and complementary non-genetic functional enhancement strategies offer opportunities to introduce or tailor defined antimicrobial, biosensing, colonisation or ecological functions. This narrative review summarizes recent progress in genetically engineered probiotics, non-genetic functional enhancement of probiotics, and attenuated pathogen strains for Salmonella control. Genetically engineered probiotics are equipped with programmable regulatory and antibacterial modules, while non-genetic probiotic approaches include probiotic-nanomaterial biohybrids, metabolically adapted strains and microbiome-directed substrate interventions. Preclinical studies show these microbial systems can provide programmable, targeted, context-dependent functions to reduce Salmonella colonisation, though their performance is also highly context-dependent. Future studies should focus on improving functional stability, standardizing efficacy and biosafety evaluation, clarifying ecological and environmental risks, and addressing manufacturing, formulation, quality-control, and regulatory requirements for translational development.

articles.title: Association of sex and age on outcomes of maintenance treatment in pati​ents with advanced esophagogastric adenocarcinoma: an exploratory analysis of the randomized AIO-YMO-0111-MATEO trial.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Sex and age have an impact on efficacy and toxicity of chemotherapy (ctx) in patients (pts) with esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA). However, data are limited, as clinical trials frequently do not report sex-specific differences and older pts are often underrepresented.

METHODS: MATEO is an international randomized trial, confirming non-inferiority of S-1 maintenance therapy compared to continued platinum-based ctx in pts with advanced EGA without disease progression after 3 months of ctx. Toxicity pattern favored S-1 monotherapy. We conducted a post hoc exploratory analysis to assess the impact of sex and age on treatment outcomes.

RESULTS: In the per-protocol population, 112 pts (72.7%) were male and 42 (27.3%) were female. 37.7% of pts were ≥ ​70 years. Female pts more often had distal stomach tumors (64.3%), while male pts had more esophagogastric junction tumors (76.7%). In a pooled analysis, female pts showed significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) (median 9.9 vs. 4.3 months, HR 0.56 [95% CI 0.38-0.83], log-rank: p = 0.0033), and overall survival (OS) (median 14.4 vs. 12.2 months, HR 0.65 [95% CI 0.44-0.97], log-rank: p = 0.0348). No age-related differences in PFS and OS were observed between pts ≥ 70 years and < 70 years. In multivariate analyses, female sex, but not younger age, was associated with a trend towards improved OS. No significant sex- or age-specific differences in terms of toxicity were observed.

CONCLUSION: Primary tumor location differed by sex. A trend for superior outcome in female pts was observed, whereas age did not have a significant impact on outcome.

articles.title: Crude incidence rates of Tier 2 rare cancers within the RARECAREnet DIGESTIVE RARE family in Japan and the United States (2016-2020).
Heterologous expression of five RpoH paralogs of Azospirillum brasilense Sp7 in Escherichia coli unravels a small set of proteins that confer thermotolerance.
articles.abstract: Transcription of genes in bacteria is initiated by RNA polymerase which recognize the target promoters with the help of sigma factors. During heat shock, expression of genes required for coping with the adverse effects of elevated temperatures is brought about by heat shock sigma factors (RpoH). Although E. coli genome encodes one RpoH, the genome of the plant growth promoting rhizobacterium Azospirillum brasilense Sp7 encodes 5 RpoH paralogs, which, in the bacterial kingdom is the highest number documented till date. Although each of these RpoH paralogs can complement the E. coli rpoH-null mutant, they show differential ability to support growth of the complemented strain at 42 °C. Analysis of the proteomes of the E. coli rpoH-null mutant showed an upregulation of HslU, HslV, HtpG, ClpB and IbpA proteins by each of the five RpoH paralogs which indicates that they constitute a minimal "thermotolerance toolkit" necessary for the growth of E. coli at 42 °C. Comparison of the consensus sequence of the promoters of genes upregulated by each RpoH paralog reveal commonalities suggesting that all the RpoH paralogs recognize common features of the upregulated genes. Further, due to divergence in the amino acid residues of their - 10 and - 35 recognizing regions they recognize promoters of other upregulated genes as well. This study provides useful insights about the role of duplication and divergence in the evolution of bacterial sigma factors.

articles.title: How high sensitivity cardiac Troponin Point of Care Testing can be integrated into existing or new pathways for chest pain assessment in the emergency department.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of clinical and laboratory investigation
articles.abstract: Chest pain is a leading cause of Emergency Department (ED) admissions, accounting for about 10% of cases in Italy. Rapid detection of ischemic events using high-sensitivity cardiac Troponin I (hs-cTnI) enables faster rule-out and improved patient flow. However, turn-around time (TAT) may be delayed by sample transport and centralized lab processing. This study aims to assess the time and economic advantages of implementing Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) for hs-cTnI in the ED. Our observational study included 86 adults with atraumatic chest pain consecutively presenting to the ED (September-October 2024). Hs-cTnI was measured at triage using a POCT device and in the Central Laboratory. Time to result availability, ED length of stay, and operating costs were extracted from hospital systems. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, and POCT versus laboratory turnaround times were compared using the Mann-Whitney test. A statistically significant difference between central laboratory and POCT (median 80 vs 4.5) mean time between blood collection and visualization of hs-cTnI results by the ED physician was found. Even though the POCT cost per test is higher than the central laboratory, the use of POCT may help saving about €25 per patient by reducing ED length of stay (LOS). In conclusion, POCT hs-cTnI testing at triage significantly shortens time to clinical decision-making in chest pain patients, reducing ED length of stay and helping mitigate overcrowding. Despite higher analytical costs, the time saved yields an overall economic benefit, supporting POCT adoption for early risk stratification in the ED.

articles.title: GSTM1 Deficiency Exacerbates Cisplatin-Induced Kidney Injury via Increased Oxidative Stress.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin, a potent chemotherapeutic agent, is highly effective in various cancers but its use is significantly limited by kidney injury, occurring in approximately 30% of patients. Cisplatin-induced kidney injury compromises optimal dosing, reducing cancer survival, and leads to permanent eGFR decline, increasing chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk and cardiovascular mortality. Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation is central to cisplatin nephrotoxicity. Glutathione-S-transferase Mu-1 (GSTM1), a phase II detoxification enzyme, protects against oxidative stress. A common GSTM1 null deletion variant is highly prevalent in human populations. We hypothesized that GSTM1 deficiency increases susceptibility to cisplatin nephrotoxicity. Using a clinically relevant low-dose, repeat-cycle cisplatin mouse model, we found that cisplatin treatment significantly induces renal Gstm1 expression in wild-type mice, suggesting a protective role. Gstm1 knockout mice exhibited more severe kidney injury, evidenced by elevated creatinine, BUN, KIM-1, 4-HNE adducts, and histological damage. This exacerbated injury was associated with significantly higher renal ROS and NOX2 expression and mitochondrial ROS. In vitro studies using primary mouse proximal tubular cells deficient in Gstm1 and human HK-2 cells endogenously lacking GSTM1 demonstrated that GSTM1 deficiency leads to increased mitochondrial ROS and NOX2 expression following cisplatin treatment; conversely, overexpression of GSTM1 in HK-2 cells significantly attenuated cisplatin-induced mitochondrial ROS and NOX2 expression. Furthermore, GSTM1 protected against NF-κB activation and cell death. Our findings establish GSTM1 as a critical cytoprotective factor against cisplatin nephrotoxicity, mitigating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis, and identify the highly prevalent GSTM1 null variant as a potential genetic risk factor for cisplatin-induced kidney injury.

articles.title: Influence of Systolic Blood Pressure and Pulse Pressure on Heart Failure Risk in Elderly Treated Hypertensive Patients.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: It is unclear whether systolic blood pressure (BP) and pulse pressure (PP), either clinic or ambulatory, differ in their ability to predict heart failure (HF) in elderly hypertensive patients.

AIM: To evaluate the influence of clinic and ambulatory systolic BP and PP on HF risk in elderly treated hypertensive subjects.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, we assessed 1314 individuals (aged ≥ 65 years) undergoing clinic and ambulatory BP measurement. Association of BP parameters with HF was investigated by univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses. Differences between competing models were assessed by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis, Akaike's Information Criterion (AIC) and Schwarz Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC).

RESULTS: During the follow-up (7.0 ± 4.0 years), 126 HF events occurred. After adjustment for covariates, clinic systolic BP and PP were not significantly associated with HF risk, whereas daytime systolic BP, daytime PP, nighttime systolic BP and nighttime PP were, showing a hazard ratio (95% confidence interval), for each standard deviation increase, of 1.45 (1.21-1.73), 1.19 (1.01-1.43), 1.54 (1.31-1.80) and 1.29 (1.08-1.55), respectively. ROC analysis showed that models including daytime or nighttime systolic BP better predicted HF than those involving daytime or nighttime PP and that nighttime BP parameters better predicted HF than daytime ones (all P < 0.05). Comparison of competing models using AIC and BIC gave the same results.

CONCLUSIONS: In elderly treated hypertensive patients, both ambulatory systolic BP and PP are predictors of HF, but systolic BP is superior to PP and nighttime parameters are superior to daytime ones.

articles.title: Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus and Pepino Mosaic Virus Differentially Modulate Disease Severity of Bacterial Pith Necrosis and Bacterial Canker in Tomato.
articles.abstract: Worldwide tomato production is increasingly challenged by complex disease outbreaks involving multiple interacting pathogens. In Israel, recent years have seen a marked rise in vascular collapse symptoms in greenhouse-grown tomatoes, coinciding with the widespread emergence of tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) and pepino mosaic virus (PepMV). Here, we investigated the bacterial and viral agents associated with these outbreaks and examined how viral infection influences the development and severity of bacterial diseases that cause vascular collapse. Surveys conducted between 2021 and 2026 revealed that tomato pith necrosis outbreaks were associated with a diverse bacterial community dominated by members of the Pseudomonadales and Enterobacterales, while bacterial canker outbreaks were exclusively linked to Clavibacter michiganensis. Multilocus sequence analysis showed that pith necrosis-associated Pseudomonas isolates clustered primarily within the P. syringae, and P. corrugata phylogroups. Pathogenicity assays demonstrated that only a subset of pith necrosis-associated bacteria, P. mediterranea, P. capsici, P. viridiflava, and Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans, induced pith necrosis under controlled conditions, with high variability in symptom severity. Co-inoculation experiments showed that ToBRFV- and PepMV-infected plants exhibited a 40-100% increase in lesion size following inoculation with pith necrosis-associated bacteria, without a corresponding increase in bacterial colonization, whereas the same viral infections attenuated wilt symptoms caused by C. michiganensis. Together, our findings demonstrate that endemic viral infections differentially modulate bacterial disease outcomes, either exacerbating or attenuating symptoms depending on the pathogen. These results highlight the importance of multi-pathogen interactions in disease severity and have important implications for tomato disease management.

articles.title: Internal Seed Colonization, Flower-to-Seed Transmission, and Seedling Association of Didymella tanaceti in Pyrethrum.
articles.abstract: Seedborne inoculum has been proposed as a potential source of primary infection for Didymella tanaceti in pyrethrum (Tanacetum cinerariifolium). However, the location of the pathogen within seed associated tissues - that include the pericarp, seed coat and embryo - and the role of seedborne inoculum in disease establishment remain unclear. This study investigated seed colonization, internal survival, and seed-to-seedling transmission of D. tanaceti using light microscopy, histopathology, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and a fluorescently labeled isolate. In naturally infected seeds, following surface sterilization and culture-based identification, putative D. tanaceti was recovered from the outer seed layer of 27.5% of seeds, from internal tissues (inner seed layer and embryo) of 7.5% of seeds, and from both outer and internal tissues of 3.8% of seeds. Histological and SEM analyses revealed the presence of fungal propagules associated with inner tissues, particularly within inter-tegumentary spaces. In a separate flower inoculation experiment, fluorescent D. tanaceti was detected in 37.3% and 36.0% of seeds from pre- and post-anthesis inoculated treatments, respectively. Among D. tanaceti-positive seeds recovered following post-anthesis inoculation, 40.7% appeared externally asymptomatic despite lacking embryos. Finally, in a separate seed-to-seedling assay, fluorescent D. tanaceti was detected on cotyledons of 64% of seedlings emerging from inoculated seeds. These findings highlight the epidemiological importance of seedborne inoculum in pyrethrum production systems.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Transvenous Lead Extraction Using a Right-Sided Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite extensive experience with transvenous lead extraction (TLE) overall, outcomes for systems implanted on the right chest remain underexplored, largely because of their low incidence.

OBJECTIVES: The objective was to evaluate whether system laterality influences TLE outcomes.

METHODS: Using our institutional, prospectively maintained ExTRACT registry, we analyzed all consecutive patients undergoing TLE procedures at the Cleveland Clinic between 1996 and 2022. Patients were categorized by system laterality. Baseline characteristics, procedural characteristics, and complications were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the association between right-sided TLE and adverse events.

RESULTS: Among 4,989 patients, 494 (9.9%) had right-sided and 4,495 (90.1%) had left-sided TLE. Compared with left-sided cases, right-sided cases had longer total lead dwell times (13.83 vs 9.26 years, P < 0.001) and were more likely to be extracted because of infection (47.57% vs 39.71%, P = 0.001). Fluoroscopy time was longer (15.95 vs 12.1 minutes; P < 0.001), and femoral workstation use more frequent (7.89% vs 4.05%, P < 0.001), yet complete extraction was lower (94.53% vs 96.44%, P = 0.034). Right-sided TLE had higher rates of sternotomy (2.83% vs 1.25%, P = 0.004) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (2.49% vs 1.10%, P = 0.009). Thirty-day mortality was low and comparable (0.61% vs 0.47%, P = 0.727). Multivariable regression showed that right-sided TLE was associated with higher odds of sternotomy (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.01-3.46, P = 0.037) and superior vena cava or right atrial tear/perforation (OR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.01-3.78, P = 0.037).

CONCLUSIONS: Right-sided TLE is associated with a lower rate of complete extraction and increased procedural risk, particularly sternotomy and major vascular injury, compared with left-sided TLE. These findings should be carefully weighed when implanting or extracting right-sided systems.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists Across Geographic Regions in Heart Failure: A Patient-Level Pooled Analysis.
The Gut-Heart-Muscle Hypothesis in Heart Failure: Emerging Associations, Mechanistic Uncertainty, and the Potential Role of Exercise.
Cone-beam computed tomography in endodontics: patient perceptions, outcomes, and radiation awareness: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) on patient-reported outcome measures in endodontics remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to identify patients' perceived values in diagnostic imaging, investigate the impact of CBCT vs periapical radiography (PR), and assess patient knowledge of ionizing radiation.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 117 patients referred for endodontic assessment. Participants underwent a clinical assessment with PR and CBCT. A 2-part questionnaire was used to assess radiation knowledge (post-PR) and changes in perception, confidence, and treatment acceptance (post-CBCT). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and χ2 tests (P < .05).

RESULTS: Baseline radiation knowledge was limited, with 59% of participants rating their understanding as poor or very poor. Despite this, patients prioritized diagnostic accuracy over a low radiation dose. The inclusion of CBCT considerably improved patient-reported outcome measures. Overall, 79.5% of participants considered CBCT more useful and helpful than PR, 60.7% reported increased confidence in their treatment plans, and 59.0% reported greater trust in clinicians compared with PR alone. Most participants (89.7%) indicated that they would undergo CBCT for future care if clinically indicated.
