OBJECTIVES: To leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions.

METHODS: 236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset.

RESULTS: Top features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGF-A, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK-STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK-STAT, T-cell, and Toll-like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF-kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages.

CONCLUSIONS: Across cohorts, JAK-STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK-STAT-directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.

articles.title: Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Dialysis-Dependent Patients With Severe Aortic Stenosis: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The optimal treatment strategy for severe aortic stenosis (AS) in dialysis-dependent patients remains uncertain. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with surgical aortic valve replacement, with certainty assessed using GRADE. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched from inception through June 2026 for comparative studies in dialysis-dependent adults with severe AS. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality, while secondary outcomes included stroke, myocardial infarction, major bleeding, major vascular complications, permanent pacemaker implantation, and intensive care unit and hospital length of stay. Random-effects models were used, with prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Eight observational studies involving 13,312 patients were included. TAVR was associated with lower 30-day mortality than surgical aortic valve replacement (risk ratio [RR], 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42-0.98; I2 = 88%), although this association was confined to adjusted studies. TAVR was also associated with shorter intensive care unit stay (mean differences, -3.63 days; 95% CI, -5.10 to -2.15) and hospital stay (mean differences, -5.37 days; 95% CI, -8.83 to -2.23), but higher risks of permanent pacemaker implantation (RR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.42-2.91) and major vascular complications (RR, 2.96; 95% CI, 1.50-5.86). No significant differences were observed in stroke, myocardial infarction, or major bleeding. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. TAVR may offer advantages in early mortality and recovery but carries increased procedural risks, and treatment should be individualized through multidisciplinary Heart Valve Team assessment.

articles.title: Conservative Management With Deferred Revascularization in Acute Coronary Syndrome-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicating acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains associated with high mortality despite advances in medical therapy, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and mechanical circulatory support. Urgent culprit-lesion PCI remains the established strategy in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)-related CS; however, ACS-related CS is heterogeneous, and the net benefit of immediate revascularization may not be uniform, particularly in clinically fragile patients. This comprehensive review summarizes current guideline recommendations and contemporary evidence concerning medical and hemodynamic support, PCI strategies, and selective mechanical circulatory support use in ACS-related CS without mechanical complications. We also examine observational studies that included non-reperfusion cohorts, in which invasive management was deferred because of adverse clinical features or procedural infeasibility. Although these studies do not establish the superiority of conservative treatment, they demonstrate clinical settings in which stabilization without immediate PCI has been used. Experimental and pathophysiological evidence concerning ischemia/reperfusion injury, ischemic preconditioning, myocardial stunning, hibernation, and low cardiac output syndrome after coronary artery bypass grafting suggests that abrupt reperfusion may further impair myocardial function in susceptible patients. We therefore propose that a stabilization-focused conservative strategy with individualized revascularization decisions warrants prospective evaluation across a broad spectrum of patients with ACS-related CS, including selected patients with STEMI-CS. This hypothesis does not support routinely withholding PCI but highlights the need to determine which patients may benefit from delayed rather than immediate revascularization.

articles.title: Impact of nurse-led inhaler education on technique, dyspnoea and disease severity in patients with COPD: a randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of research in nursing : JRN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Correct inhaler use is essential for symptom control in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, incorrect technique remains common and may reduce treatment effectiveness.

AIMS: To evaluate nurse-led inhaler education's effects on technique, dyspnoea and severity in COPD.

METHODS: A randomised controlled trial included 90 COPD outpatients recruited between December 2022 and May 2023, assigned to an intervention group (n = 45) receiving nurse-led inhaler training or a control group (n = 45) receiving routine care. Inhaler technique, dyspnoea (modified Medical Research Council Dyspnoea Scale) and disease severity (COPD Assessment Test, CAT) were assessed at baseline and 4 weeks later. Data were analysed using independent-samples t‑tests, repeated‑measures analysis of variance, Pearson correlation and chi‑square tests.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups (p > 0.05). The intervention group showed significantly greater improvement in inhaler technique (F = 62.416, p < 0.001), lower dyspnoea scores (F = 38.029, p < 0.001) and reduced CAT scores (p < 0.001) than controls.

CONCLUSIONS: Structured nurse-led inhaler education improves inhaler technique and clinical outcomes in COPD. Findings support nursing theories of patient education and self‑management, underscoring nurses' role in chronic disease care. Policies embedding standardised, competency‑based inhaler education into respiratory nursing practice are recommended to strengthen COPD management.

articles.title: Improvement in sequelae of chronic liver disease in patients with Alagille syndrome treated with maralixibat.
articles.abstract: Maralixibat (MRX) is an orally administered, small-molecule ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitor used in the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in conditions such as Alagille syndrome (ALGS). MRX's beneficial effects on cholestatic pruritus are well described, however its effects on patients' clinical manifestations of hepatic disease are less well known. We report two cases of patients with ALGS treated with MRX who demonstrated stabilization of their esophageal varices and xanthomas, respectively. Our findings demonstrate the potential role of MRX in improving the extrahepatic manifestations of liver disease in patients with ALGS. Further studies are needed to understand the physiologic mechanisms driving these changes.

articles.title: Persistent metabolic remodeling after dietary salt reduction reveals sex differences in the adaptation to chronic high-salt intake.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive salt intake is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet its systemic metabolic consequences and its relationship to differential cardiovascular adaptations in males and females remain poorly understood. Here, we performed plasma metabolite profiling in male and female mice subjected to long-term high-salt diet (HSD) exposure during aging.

METHODS: Mice were fed HSD (8.6% NaCl) or low-salt normal diet (ND; 0.6% NaCl) from 9 to 23 months of age, with a subset of mice undergoing diet reversal to ND after 7 months of HSD. Plasma metabolites were analyzed using gas chromatography/mass spectrometry and related to previously reported measurements of arterial blood pressure and cardiac function.

RESULTS: Female mice developed salt-sensitive hypertension driven by vascular dysfunction, whereas male mice exhibited cardiac and vascular remodeling independent of blood pressure. Among 48 measured metabolites, HSD induced substantial alterations in levels of glucose, glycerol, glycerol phosphates, and fatty acids. Males showed a near-complete normalization of metabolite profiles following 7 months of salt reduction, whereas females retained a metabolomic signature different from ND despite normalization of blood pressure. In particular, metabolites related to energy metabolism, lipid handling, and osmotic balance were influenced by both diet and sex, with linoleate showing a significant sex-diet interaction. Correlation analyses demonstrated associations between metabolite profiles and cardiovascular parameters with different patterns in males and females.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that chronic high-salt consumption induces persistent plasma metabolite alterations displaying different patterns in male and female mice that are not fully reversed by a salt-lowering dietary intervention. The dissociation between physiological recovery and metabolic normalization, particularly in females, suggests that metabolic alterations may represent an additional layer of cardiovascular risk beyond blood pressure control in mice.

articles.title: Frequency-specific cortical swallowing-network responses following neuroengineering-guided individualized multichannel tDCS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuromodulatory interventions for dysphagia are increasingly explored as adjunctive rehabilitation strategies, yet their efficacy may be limited by non-individualized stimulation protocols and insufficient consideration of network-specific brain dynamics. Advances in neuroengineering now enable individualized targeting based on functional neuroimaging and computational modeling, offering the potential for precision neuromodulation of swallowing-related brain networks.

METHODS: We investigated whether individualized multichannel transcranial direct current stimulation (mc-tDCS), optimized using magnetoencephalography (MEG)-derived target localization, MRI-based finite-element head modeling, and a distributed constrained maximum intensity (D-CMI) optimization framework, modulates the cortical swallowing network. In a randomized sham-controlled crossover design, eight healthy adults underwent three stimulation conditions: low-intensity mc-tDCS (1.5 mA), high-intensity mc-tDCS (4.0 mA), and sham stimulation. Swallowing-related cortical activity was assessed before and after stimulation using MEG source reconstruction of event-related desynchronization during uncued voluntary swallowing and a visually cued swallowing task requiring precise timing. A repeated-measures Dose × Task × Time model tested the hypothesized interaction separately in five frequency bands, with Holm correction across bands.

RESULTS: No Dose × Task × Time interaction was significant after Holm correction across the five frequency bands (all adjusted p ≥ 0.274). Within-condition pre-post analyses identified alpha- and beta-band changes after 1.5-mA stimulation during challenged swallowing and a low-gamma change after 4.0-mA stimulation during uncued swallowing. Challenged-task timing accuracy increased over time, without significant Dose or Dose × Time effects.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating individualized MEG-based targeting, subject-specific head modeling, and optimized multichannel stimulation. The hypothesized Dose × Task × Time interaction was not significant. Exploratory within-condition pre-post differences were observed in alpha, beta, and low-gamma activity, but do not establish stimulation-specific effects. Larger controlled studies are needed to evaluate the physiological effects of this individualized approach.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of deep brain stimulation in paediatric drug-resistant epilepsy: a systematic review of target-specific outcomes.
Associations of Physical Activity With Mortality and Cardiovascular Diseases in Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Community-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is linked to elevated risks of mortality and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). This study aimed to investigate the dose-response associations of moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) with all-cause mortality and CVD risk in adults with CKD.

METHODS: We included 3927 UK Biobank participants with CKD. Weekly MVPA duration was evaluated by wrist-worn accelerometers and a machine learning model. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and CVDs (heart failure, myocardial infarction, and stroke). Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines were used to assess the dose-response associations.

RESULTS: CKD participants engaged in less MVPA than healthy controls. During a median follow-up of 7.92 years, 393 deaths and 445 CVDs occurred. Moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity showed nonlinear associations with mortality and CVD risk. Mortality risk declined sharply up to 150 minutes per week MVPA and plateaued thereafter. Cardiovascular disease risk reached its lowest at approximately 300 minutes per week. Compared with <150 minutes per week, ≥150 minutes per week MVPA was associated with lower risks of mortality (hazard ratio = 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51-0.80) and CVDs (hazard ratio = 0.68; 95% CI, 0.55-0.83). Replacing sedentary behavior with MVPA for 10 min/d was associated with a significantly reduced mortality rate among less active CKD participants (hazard ratio = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.56-0.86).

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with CKD, engaging in MVPA of ≥150 minutes per week was associated with significantly lower risks of mortality and CVDs. These findings underscore the value of physical activity promotion in CKD management.

articles.title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training on Blood Lipids in Children and Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of high-intensity interval training on blood lipids in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Embase, EBSCO, and CNKI were searched from inception to February 27, 2026. Randomized controlled trials reporting total cholesterol, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, or low-density lipoprotein cholesterol were included. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 1 and evidence certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Six trials involving 220 participants were included. Mean age was 12.8 (2.4) years, and mean body mass index was 28.4 (4.9 kg/m2) in 5 studies (n = 197); one study reported body mass index z scores. High-intensity interval training reduced total cholesterol (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.40; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.11; P = .007) and triglycerides (SMD = -0.73; 95% CI, -1.35 to -0.12; P = .02) but not high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (SMD = 0.35; 95% CI, -0.06 to 0.77; P = .10) or low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (SMD = -0.31; 95% CI, -0.96 to 0.35; P = .36). Risk of bias was generally low, and evidence certainty ranged from low to moderate.

CONCLUSION: High-intensity interval training may improve total cholesterol and triglycerides in youth with overweight or obesity, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited evidence base and heterogeneity.

articles.title: Alpinia zerumbet leaf extract attenuates cardiovascular remodeling in 2K1C renovascular hypertension: Association with AT1 receptor and redox-inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: Renovascular hypertension involves persistent activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, oxidative stress, inflammation, and cardiovascular remodeling. Alpinia zerumbet leaf extract (ALE) is a polyphenol-rich preparation with known antihypertensive properties. This study investigated the effects of chronic ALE treatment on cardiovascular remodeling in the two-kidney, one-clip (2K1C) model of renovascular hypertension. Male Wistar rats (45 days old; n = 11 per group) were allocated into four groups: Sham, Sham + ALE, 2K1C, and 2K1C + ALE. Animals were subjected to 2K1C surgery or laparotomy (Sham) and received ALE (50 mg/kg/day in drinking water) or vehicle for seven weeks. Blood pressure was monitored throughout the protocol, and vascular reactivity was evaluated in the mesenteric arterial bed. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses assessed structural remodeling, cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area (CSA), fibrosis, and AT1 receptor, TGF-β, and MMP-2 immunostaining in the aorta and heart. Cardiovascular oxidative damage, antioxidant defenses, inflammatory cytokines, nitrite levels, and plasma angiotensin II concentrations were also evaluated. ALE significantly attenuated the rise in systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure in 2K1C rats, despite not improving endothelial dysfunction in the mesenteric arterial bed. Treatment prevented increased AT1 receptor immunostaining in the aorta and heart without altering plasma angiotensin II levels. Furthermore, ALE partially reduced aortic hypertrophy, prevented cardiac concentric remodeling, fibrosis, and cardiomyocyte CSA, and reduced TGF-β and MMP-2 immunostaining in both tissues. In addition, ALE reduced lipid peroxidation and inflammatory cytokine levels while restoring antioxidant defenses in the plasma and cardiovascular tissues. ALE attenuates cardiovascular remodeling in renovascular hypertension, associated with reduced AT1 receptor expression and redox-inflammatory responses.

articles.title: Optimizing radon quantification in arid groundwater: Counting-time strategies and QA/QC for sub-Bq·L-1 measurements.
articles.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
articles.abstract: Low-level radon-in-water measurements in arid aquifers are constrained by counting statistics at short runtimes and by systematic air-water partition bias in closed-loop degassing systems. We define "optimization" as selecting the minimal, decision-appropriate RAD7 Big-Bottle operating configuration that meets a target minimum detection limit/limit of quantification (MDL/LOQ) and precision should be achieved here by integrating (i) a tiered counting-time strategy (screening: 30-150 min; confirmatory: 900-1500 min; ultralow: ∼3000 min), (ii) temperature/salinity/loop-volume-aware air-water conversion, and (iii) QA/QC gates (RH ≤ 7%, calibration acceptance, blanks/duplicates/drift criteria). Precision and Currie-based MDL/LOQ improve with integration time (t-1/2), with practical stability achieved at ∼900-1500 min for routine reporting. Raw air-phase readings showed a systematic enrichment (∼1.26×) relative to dissolved estimates; phase conversion removed this effect, yielding agreement diagnostics consistent with bias reduction. At long runtimes, uncertainty becomes bounded by fixed components (calibration and environmental inputs), indicating that further improvement requires tightening these terms rather than extending runtime alone. This workflow provides a traceable, decision-grade approach to sub-Bq·L-1 radon surveillance in arid groundwater monitoring programs.

articles.title: Measurement of allostatic load in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic research: An integrative review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a progressive multisystem condition linking cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic dysfunction through shared pathophysiology. Social determinants of health (SDOH) drive these processes through cumulative physiological stress, producing dysregulation across neuroendocrine, immune, cardiovascular, and metabolic systems. Allostatic load (AL), a composite biomarker index, offers a theoretically grounded framework for quantifying this multisystem dysregulation, yet its measurement remains variable. This review synthesises AL measurement in adult CKM research and recommendations for AL standardisation.

METHODS: An integrative review following Whittemore and Knafl's framework searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL for studies published from inception to June 2026. Fifteen of 1288 records met inclusion criteria. Two reviewers independently extracted and appraised data (κ = 0.95).

RESULTS: AL indices ranged from 5 to 14 biomarkers. Cardiometabolic markers were universal; neuroendocrine mediators were reported in only 5 of 15 studies (33%), and catecholamines were absent in all. Scoring approaches were incompatible across studies, and medication adjustments were inconsistent. SDOH were covariates in 7 studies, absent or descriptive only in 4, and modelled as primary exposures in only 4. Despite this heterogeneity, 14 of 15 studies (93%) reported significant associations between higher AL and adverse CKM outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: AL was consistently associated with adverse CKM outcomes, yet omission of neuroendocrine mediators in most indices limits the construct's ability to capture the full physiological stress response, leaving many indices functioning as cardiometabolic risk scores. A minimum neuroendocrine panel, medication-adjusted continuous scoring, and explicit SDOH-AL-outcome modelling are needed.

articles.title: Tissue factor-specific sdAb radiotracers for molecular imaging in solid tumors.
articles.abstract: Tissue factor (TF) expression has been associated with tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis in several cancers. With the recent FDA approval of an antibody-drug-conjugate targeting TF, tisotumab vedotin for recurrent metastatic cervical cancer, companion diagnostic tools capable of capturing tumor heterogeneity are increasingly critical. In this study, we developed and characterized single domain antibody (sdAb)-based radiotracers to non-invasively visualize tumors expressing either murine (m) or human (h) TF protein. SdAbs targeting hTF and mTF were obtained from an immune llama library. Seven candidates targeting each species' orthologue were selected, characterized in vitro and radiolabeled with 99mTc for in vivo screening in athymic nude mice bearing both mTF and hTF positive tumors. Lead anti-hTF sdAb was radiolabeled with 68Ga for PET imaging. In vitro, all sdAbs exhibited excellent affinities for their respective targets, reaching the picomolar range. When radiolabeled with 99mTc, the lead compounds showed strong uptake and specific binding in TF-positive tumors as confirmed by SPECT imaging. The lead sdAb 64B4 targeting hTF protein, demonstrated an uptake of 8.07±1.02% IA/g in BxPC-3 tumors and a tumor-to-blood ratio of 26.06±4.36. The best candidate for targeting mTF protein, sdAb 66A12, displayed an uptake of 3.30±0.22% IA/g in mTF positive tumors and a tumor-to-blood ratio of 10.70±2.83. Off-tumor uptake was detected in several organs, with unexpectedly the highest levels detected in brown adipose tissue, consistent with mTF protein expression levels determined by ELISA. We successfully developed and validated sdAb-based radiotracers targeting either mTF or hTF, enabling the noninvasive visualization of TF-expressing tumors.

articles.title: Agreement of noninvasive multimodality imaging measurements with balloon sizing in the cardiac catheterization laboratory prior to percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) dysfunction is common in repaired congenital heart defects resulting in right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction. Emerging transcatheter options enable placement of a competent pulmonary valve, obviating the need for surgery. Multimodality imaging plays a key role in determining the type and timing of intervention prior to percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI). The authors sought to assess correlation of noninvasive RVOT measurements with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and cardiac computed tomography (CT) with balloon sizing in the catheterization laboratory prior to PPVI.

METHODS: A retrospective review was performed on patients who had undergone PPVI with preprocedural CMR and cardiac CT scan. Three-dimensional multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) of the narrowest RVOT diameter on magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), whole heart sequence (WHS) images, and CT scan images were performed using commercially available software; balloon sizing prior to PPVI was recorded. Concordance correlation coefficients were used to assess agreement with the clinically acceptable limit between the modalities set at +/- 2 mm. Additionally, mean difference was used to quantify the difference in measurements among the 2 modalities.

RESULTS: For maximal waist dimensions, correlation between MRA and WHS images with balloon sizing was 0.70 to 0.79, while correlation between CT scan and balloon sizing was 0.65 to 0.75. For minimal waist dimensions, correlation between MRA and WHS images was 0.72 to 0.82; correlation between CT scan and balloon sizing was 0.64 to 0.73.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac CT and CMR are complementary modalities that provide essential information for preprocedural planning for PPVI.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Intensive Continuous Theta Burst Stimulation Over the Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Insomnia Disorder:A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The primary care companion for CNS disorders
articles.abstract: Background: Insomnia disorder affects 10%-35% of the general population and is maintained by pathological cortical hyperarousal amenable to inhibitory neuromodulation. Continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) produces rapid inhibitory effects on cortical excitability, but its efficacy in insomnia disorder has not been evaluated in adequately powered randomized sham-controlled trials. Methods: Thirty adults (n=15 per arm) meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, criteria for insomnia disorder (Sleep Condition Indicator [SCI] score <16) were randomized to active or sham cTBS targeting the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (F4 position, 80% of the resting motor threshold). The intervention comprised 21 sessions (600 pulses/session, ∼40 seconds) over 10 days.Data were collected from October 2024 to January 2026. Outcome measures were the SCI (primary), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire-10 (FOSQ-10), and World Health Organization Quality of Life-Brief (WHOQOL-BREF), assessed at baseline (day 0), posttreatment (day 10), and 2-week follow-up (day 25). The trial was conducted per Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials 2010 guidelines and analyzed using intention-to-treat mixed-effects repeated-measures analysis of variance. Results:Both groups improved significantly across all outcomes (all within-group P<.001; large effect sizes). Group×time interactions were nonsignificant for sleep-specific outcomes (PSQI: F=3.32, P=.060; SCI: F=2.14, P=.147; ISI: F=0.23, P=.720; FOSQ-10: F=0.88, P=.388). A significant and large interaction was observed for health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF: F=8.92, P =.002, ηp2=0.242), favoring active cTBS. Three participants experienced transient mild headache; no serious adverse events occurred. Conclusion: Right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex-targeted cTBS over 10 days is safe and well tolerated. Active cTBS conferred a significant and clinically meaningful advantage in health-related quality of life. Larger trials with objective sleep endpoints, medication-naive populations, and extended follow-up are warranted. Trial Registration: Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI) identifier: CTRI/2024/10/075898. Prim Care Companion CNS Disord 2026;28(6):26m04225. Author affiliations are listed at the end of this article.

articles.title: Ablation With Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter for Refractory Ventricular Tachycardia Adjacent to VSD Closure Device.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Safety regarding pulsed field ablation (PFA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) using the Sphere-9 Catheter for ventricular tachycardia (VT) near ventricular septal defect (VSD) closure devices is unknown.

CASE SUMMARY: A 64-year-old man with extensive cardiac history including VSD closure with an Amplatzer device and complete heart block status post biventricular cardioverter-defibrillator with abandoned RV lead because of fracture presented with recurrent, symptomatic VT. Electroanatomical mapping showed VT in the basal septum adjacent to the Amplatzer device. Using the Sphere-9 catheter, RFA terminated the tachycardia, and PFA was successful near the VSD closure device without apparent complication. VT was noninducible postablation.

DISCUSSION: We describe procedural reasoning and considerations to optimize safe delivery of PFA and RFA using the Sphere-9 catheter for septal VT near intracardiac hardware.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Colocalized PFA/RFA using the Sphere-9 catheter may be an effective treatment option for persistent VT near intracardiac devices for highly selected patients.

articles.title: Left Bundle Branch Optimized Resynchronization Therapy for Persistent Ventricular Dysfunction After Complex PCI and TAVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary artery disease presents challenges in patients unsuitable for surgery. Persistent left bundle branch block (LBBB) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may impair ventricular recovery.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old man underwent high-risk left main-left anterior descending percutaneous coronary intervention, complicated by cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Subsequent TAVR achieved favorable valve hemodynamics but was followed by new-onset left bundle branch block and persistent LV dysfunction. Left bundle branch pacing achieved complete correction only at high output. A coronary sinus lead was added for left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (LOT-CRTD). At 3 months, LV function fully recovered with reverse remodeling and marked symptom improvement. Why Beyond the Guideline: Optimal percutaneous coronary intervention-TAVR timing and device strategies for post-TAVR LBBB with LV dysfunction remain poorly defined in current guidelines.

DISCUSSION: LOT-CRTD may provide effective cardiac resynchronization when isolated left bundle branch pacing cannot achieve optimal correction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Sequence of PCI-TAVR remained individualized. LOT-CRT is a viable strategy to facilitate ventricular recovery for post-TAVR LBBB.

articles.title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later.

DISCUSSION: We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

articles.title: Extensive Native Aortic Valve Infiltration and Early Bioprosthetic Valve Degeneration in Low-Grade Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac manifestations of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) are extremely rare, particularly involving valves.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient with low-grade CLL presented with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Following surgical aortic valve replacement, the patient experienced rapid degeneration of her surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve, necessitating valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Re-evaluation of her excised native aortic valve tissue on histology with immunohistochemical confirmation revealed extensive CLL infiltration.

DISCUSSION: Extensive CLL infiltration of the aortic valve is an extremely rare phenomenon. This case raises the hypothesis that a clonal lymphoproliferative process may contribute to calcific aortic stenosis and possibly early bioprosthetic structural valve deterioration. Additional studies are needed to further evaluate this association.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: CLL can rarely affect cardiac valves and may contribute to the development of native valve stenosis. Additional studies are required to determine whether CLL is a risk factor for early prosthetic structural valve deterioration.

articles.title: Lived Experiences, Coping Behaviors, and Impacts of the 2022 Infant Formula Shortage on Caregivers in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of nutrition education and behavior
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Assess and explore associations between lived experiences, coping behaviors, and perceived impacts on caregivers affected by the 2022 infant formula shortage in the United States (US), referred to as the shortage.

DESIGN: Convergent mixed methods study design with cross-sectional online survey (n = 243) and semi-structured interviews (n = 14).

SETTING: National.

PARTICIPANTS: US caregivers responsible for an infant during the shortage and affected by the shortage.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES (S): Lived experiences, coping behaviors, perceived impacts of shortage.

ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics conducted. Associations tested using Pearson's Chi-Squared tests with a post hoc analysis of adjusted call residuals. Qualitative content analysis of semi-structured interviews performed.

RESULTS: Caregivers reported unmet information needs and both positive and negative social support experiences as they navigated the shortage. The most frequently reported coping behavior (55.1%) was changing planned infant feeding practices (e.g., breastfed longer than intended) because of the shortage, which were correlated with perceived impacts of the household being negatively effected (p = 0.003) and that caregiver mental health was negatively effected (p = 0.002) by the shortage. Caregiver interviews revealed detrimental physical effects on infants due to switching infant formulas, negative mental health impacts on caregivers, financial strains, and concerns about future shortages.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Efforts that link support, resources, and information to caregivers are needed to protect infant feeding, promote caregiver mental health, and safeguard against future infant formula shortages.

articles.title: A Web-Based Risk Calculator for Psychological Distress in Stable Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Development and Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) experience psychological distress that evolves in dynamic and heterogeneous patterns. Conventional cross-sectional screening and baseline-only prediction models fail to capture longitudinal heterogeneity, and few tools integrate trajectory analysis with machine learning (ML) for individualized risk stratification. This study aimed to identify longitudinal trajectories of psychological distress and develop, validate, and deploy a web-based ML risk calculator for clinical use.

METHODS: We enrolled 323 stable COPD outpatients from three tertiary hospitals in Chongqing, China, between March and December 2024. Baseline data included sociodemographic, clinical, and key psychosocial variables. Psychological distress was reassessed at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months. Growth mixture modeling (GMM) identified distinct longitudinal trajectory classes. The trajectory outcome was dichotomized for prediction: patients in the persistent low-distress group were defined as low-risk, and all others as high-risk. Candidate predictors were screened using univariate analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Eight ML algorithms were trained, internally validated, and compared, and the best-performing model was selected for final development.

RESULTS: GMM revealed four trajectories: persistent high distress (8.0%), transient threshold-exceeding distress with rapid decline (15.2%), persistent near-threshold distress with gradual decline (65.0%), and persistent low distress (11.8%). Using the persistent low-distress group as reference, nine predictors were retained: symptom burden, number of children, negative coping, payment method, perceived stress, acute exacerbation frequency, dyspnea severity, educational level, and gender. The XGBoost model achieved the best-balanced performance, with AUC values of 0.859 (training), 0.686 (validation), and 0.739 (test), indicating moderate discriminative ability. The model showed high positive predictive value but limited negative predictive value, constraining its utility for ruling out distress. A web-based calculator was subsequently developed for clinical implementation.

CONCLUSION: Stable COPD patients follow four distinct longitudinal trajectories of psychological distress. The XGBoost model provides moderate predictive performance as an exploratory risk-stratification tool. The web-based calculator may support clinicians in early identification of individuals at elevated risk of persistent psychological distress, but further validation in independent, diverse cohorts is required before widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: Race-Neutral Spirometry to Predict Residual Volume in COPD Patients: The Pittsburgh Residual Volume Calculator.
articles.abstract: Body plethysmography, the accepted standard for measuring residual volume (RV), a marker of hyperinflation used in selection for lung volume reduction procedures, has limited availability in resource-constrained settings. We previously developed and validated a spirometry-based model to estimate RV in COPD; however, that model predated race-neutral GLI reference equations and was not easily applied to real world decision making. Applying GLI global reference equations to spirometric measures from 450 adults with COPD from the University of Pittsburgh SCCOR cohort, we used fractional polynomial multiple regression analysis to determine an estimated RV % predicted (RVest%) from spirometric and demographic data:  RVest% = 909.17+4.09*FVC% - 93.15*-208.12*FEV1/FVC-2.01*Age-11.05*1(if male). This demonstrated strong predictive accuracy (R² = 0.72). For RV ≥150%, ≥175%, and ≥200% predicted, AUCs:  0.89, 0.92, and 0.91, respectively.  At RVest% ≥172, sensitivity for RV ≥175% (the most accepted inclusion threshold for volume reduction procedures)  was 94% and specificity was 90Predicted probability for a given patient's RVest%  at various true RV cutpoints, corresponding to e.g., lung volume reduction selection thresholds, can then be determined using a second provided formula. This race-neutral "Pittsburgh RV Calculator" prediction model to estimate RV can support referral decisions for lung volume reduction in under-resourced environments. (see https://www.estimaterv.com/).

articles.title: Scaling and Sustaining Diabetes Self-Management Education in Community Pharmacies: A Statewide Collaborative Evaluation of Clinical and Operational Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES: Community pharmacies are distinctively positioned to deliver diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) to populations vulnerable to diabetes-related complications, prompting this evaluation of the program reach, clinical outcomes, patient-reported quality of life (QoL), implementation barriers, and cost efficiency of a statewide collaborative initiative in New York.

INTERVENTION APPROACH: The statewide DSMES initiative was designed to expand access to accredited DSMES services in community pharmacies and support long-term sustainability and included 1) pharmacy recruitment and accreditation, 2) a sustainability program, and 3) workforce innovation.

EVALUATION METHODS: The mixed-methods evaluation included 44 accredited community pharmacies. Program reach was estimated using geospatial mapping and paired clinical and QoL outcomes were assessed through a continuous quality improvement framework. To evaluate a paraprofessional-supported hybrid workforce pilot, a comparative financial analysis was conducted using the 2024 Medicare Part B Physician Fee Schedule.

RESULTS: The initiative successfully reached priority populations, with 91% of participating pharmacies located in tracts that scored moderate to high on the Social Vulnerability Index. The program also yielded significant improvements in participant hemoglobin A1c and median QoL scores. Additionally, it demonstrated that delegating administrative workflows to paraprofessionals reduced personnel costs from $6,592 to $2,169 per 6-patient cohort, transforming an estimated $4,318 net loss into a break-even financial model.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH: Integrating this paraprofessional workforce model provides a financially sustainable pathway for community pharmacies to deliver accessible and clinically effective DSMES to priority populations.

articles.title: Technology Priorities for Diabetes Care in Rural Georgia: Findings of a Problem Discovery Workshop.
Age-Stratified Disproportionality Analysis of Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in FAERS and VigiBase.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors (BTKis) are increasingly used because of their efficacy; however, safety concerns are emerging.

METHODS: This study extracted data from FAERS and VigiBase and divided patients into four age groups. The Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) was used to identify safety signals.

RESULTS: Regarding cardiac disorders, zanubrutinib showed a specific cardiac arrest signal in the 0-60-year age group in FAERS, and the Atrial Fibrillation (AF) signal intensity increased with age in VigiBase. Conversely, the AF signals decreased across successive age groups for acalabrutinib in VigiBase and for ibrutinib in both databases. Several cardiac PTs for acalabrutinib met the signal criteria in the 61-70-year group. For skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders, multiple nail-related Adverse Drug Events (ADEs) were observed in all age groups for ibrutinib; acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib exhibited no nail-related signals, whereas other skin-related signals were primarily detected in patients aged >60 years. Regarding bleeding ADEs, thirty types were detected for ibrutinib and four for acalabrutinib; zanubrutinib showed no age-specific bleeding signals. For infections and infestations, among the PTs detected in three or more age groups, aspergillus infection, bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, and onychomycosis were consistently ranked among the top ten signals for ibrutinib based on VigiBase ROR025 across all four age groups, with ROR025 values decreasing with increasing age. Signals for different types of pneumonia were detected in all age groups for the BTKis, except in the 0-60- year age group of zanubrutinib. Moreover, the specific signals warrant further attention.

DISCUSSION: This comprehensive analysis of FAERS and VigiBase data highlights age-related differences in ADE reporting across BTKi therapies. These findings identify age-stratified reporting patterns that may help prioritize further safety investigations. A limitation of this study is the lack of integration of potential biological mechanisms underlying BTKi-related ADEs.

CONCLUSION: This study identified age-stratified reporting patterns for three BTKis in two spontaneous reporting systems. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish differences in clinical risk across age groups or causal relationships.

articles.title: Corrigendum to: Revealing the Future of Pharmacovigilance in Precision Pharmaceutical Monitoring.
articles.abstract: Following publication of the article entitled "Revealing the Future of Pharmacovigilance in Precision Pharmaceutical Monitoring" [1], certain phrases and expressions were identified that were unclear or inconsistent with established scientific terminology. To ensure accuracy and clarity of the published record, these expressions have been corrected using terminology that more accurately conveys the intended scientific meaning. These corrections are limited to the wording and terminology of the affected passages and do not alter the data, results, scientific interpretations, or conclusions of the article. The specific corrections are provided below: Table 1, Column 3, Row 6 Original text: In order to quantify the complexity of coronary illness and detect major cardiovascular events, this research focused on metabolomics indicators [74]. Corrected text: In order to quantify the complexity of coronary artery disease and detect major cardiovascular events, this research focused on metabolomics indicators [74]. The original article has been updated accordingly. This corrigendum is published to ensure transparency and accuracy of the scholarly record. The correct version of the article is available online at: https://www.eurekaselect.com/article/147119 The authors regret these errors and apologise for any inconvenience they may have caused.

articles.title: Target-triggered DNAzyme hydrogels with boron-doped atomically dispersed Fe nanozymes for one-step bacterial colorimetric sensing.
articles.abstract: Nanozyme-based bacterial detection faces two long-standing challenges: (1) dependence on multi-step enzymatic cascades that complicate assay workflows, and (2) insufficient sensitivity originating from the intrinsic low catalytic activity of nanozymes and the lack of target pre-amplification for bacterial biomarkers. To address these bottlenecks, we construct a target-triggered DNAzyme hydrogel platform integrated with boron-doped nanozymes (HCFe-B). This platform synergistically couples stimuli-responsive hydrogel-mediated controlled-release and heteroatom-doped nanozyme engineering, enabling one-step ultrasensitive bacterial detection. Upon recognition of bacterial biomarkers, the rationally designed DNAzyme hydrogel triggers one-step nanozyme release, which fully obviates the requirement for multi-step enzymatic cascades. DFT calculations verify that boron doping lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining O-O cleavage step for atomically dispersed Fe nanozymes, greatly boosting their peroxidase-like activity. As a result, nearly 1000-fold enhancement in detection sensitivity is accomplished without any target pre-amplification. Furthermore, a convolutional neural network (CNN) machine-learning model is implemented to process the readout signals. High-accuracy blind tests on human faecal samples yield an AUC value of 98.25%, alongside 100% sensitivity and 95% specificity. These results underscore the practical promise of our platform for clinical bacterial infection prevention and public-health surveillance.

articles.title: Beyond clinical training: Addressing financial literacy gaps in pediatric gastroenterology fellowship.
A dual-barrier sustained-release hydrogel based on Cu-exchanged Y zeolite and sodium alginate for infected wound healing.
articles.abstract: Bacterial wound infection and the growing crisis of antibiotic resistance urgently demand non-antibiotic wound dressings that integrate long-term antibacterial activity and high biosafety. Herein, we designed a dual-barrier sustained-release antibacterial hydrogel (CuY@SA) by embedding Cu2+-exchanged Y zeolite (CuY) into a calcium-crosslinked sodium alginate (SA) matrix. The ordered microporous zeolite acts as the first-stage reservoir to enable intrinsic Cu2+ sustained release via ion exchange, while the alginate network serves as a second physical diffusion barrier to suppress burst release and prolong delivery. The resulting CuY@SA hydrogel eliminated the initial burst and achieved nearly-linear Cu2+ release over 48 h, with an equilibrium swelling ratio of approximately 28 g g-1 in pH 7.4 PBS. In vitro, CuY@SA exhibited over 99.9% bactericidal efficacy against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, while maintaining >98% cytocompatibility with NIH-3T3 fibroblasts at hydrogel concentrations up to 10 mg mL-1. In a mouse full-thickness infected wound model, CuY@SA significantly accelerated wound closure to over 98% by day 14, promoted collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, reduced local inflammation, and caused no obvious organ toxicity or cuproptosis. Compared with the control hydrogel (Cu@SA) containing directly added free Cu2+, CuY@SA showed remarkably lower cytotoxicity and superior in vivo antibacterial activity, confirming the critical role of zeolite in precise controlled release. This work demonstrates that combining an inorganic zeolite carrier with a biopolymer hydrogel provides a simple, scalable, and effective strategy for developing safe and long-acting antibacterial wound dressings. More broadly, it highlights the untapped potential of zeolites as versatile and tunable controlled-release platforms for advanced biomedical applications.

articles.title: Ultrasonographic assessment of gastrointestinal motility and structural alterations in patients with diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate gastrointestinal contractility and structure using ultrasonography and to assess abdominal symptoms in diabetic patients.

METHODS: The study included 95 diabetic patients and 96 healthy controls. Demographic and clinical data were collected, and all participants completed the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS). Ultrasonography was performed to assess gastrointestinal wall thickness, cardiac orifice and pyloric widths, and gastrointestinal motor function, and to detect structural abnormalities. Statistical analyses included between-group comparisons and correlation analyses.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, diabetic patients had a significantly thicker duodenal wall (Z = 2.462, p = 0.014) and wider cardiac orifice and pylorus (Z = 2.386, p = 0.017; Z = 2.264, p = 0.024), larger minimum antral systolic and maximum antral diastolic areas (Z = 5.378 and 4.105, both p < 0.001), but lower antral contraction amplitude and motility index (t = 4.207, p < 0.001; t = 2.874, p = 0.005). Ultrasonography suggested a higher prevalence of gastric ulcers in diabetic patients (χ² = 4.264, p = 0.039). Diabetic patients reported higher total GSRS, upper abdominal symptom, and constipation scores (Z = 2.568, p = 0.010; Z = 2.326, p = 0.020; Z = 2.615, p = 0.009). Duodenogastric reflux correlated positively with the GSRS total score and several domain scores, including upper abdominal, lower abdominal, reflux, and dyspepsia (r = 0.231-0.326 and p = 0.001-0.024 for all).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that ultrasonography can assess gastrointestinal structure and motility and may aid clinical diagnosis and management in diabetic patients.

articles.title: Reply to Gong: Beyond Diagnostic Yield: Validating Aspergillosis Criteria in COPD.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

articles.title: When an 8-mm Coronary Artery Has No Appropriate Stent: Bailout PCI and Dual-Balloon Optimization in Giant Right Coronary Artery Ectasia.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Giant coronary artery ectasia with acute thrombotic occlusion presents a difficult interventional challenge because of the large thrombus burden, impaired washout, distal embolization, and lack of appropriately sized coronary stents. A 69-year-old woman presented with inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction caused by thrombotic subtotal occlusion of an approximately 8-mm dominant right coronary artery (RCA). Primary percutaneous coronary intervention was complicated by recurrent thrombotic no-reflow despite sequential balloon angioplasty, selective aspiration thrombectomy, large-lumen aspiration, and intracoronary antiplatelet and fibrinolytic therapy. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) demonstrated extensive residual thrombus and a true vessel diameter substantially larger than available coronary stent platforms. Because balloon deflation repeatedly resulted in vessel collapse with persistent TIMI 0-1 flow and hemodynamic instability, a 5.0-mm drug-eluting stent was implanted as a bailout scaffold. Persistent proximal malapposition was subsequently improved using simultaneous inflation of 6.0- and 4.0-mm noncompliant balloons, restoring TIMI 3 flow. Three days later, the patient developed a large left cerebellar intracranial hemorrhage requiring surgical evacuation and external ventricular drainage. Antithrombotic therapy was withheld and subsequently reintroduced in a staged, imaging-guided manner. Follow-up angiography and IVUS demonstrated preserved TIMI 3 flow, satisfactory stent expansion and apposition, and residual non-flow-limiting thrombotic material. This case highlights the limitations of conventional coronary stenting in giant ectatic arteries and the role of IVUS in guiding bailout stent optimization and follow-up assessment. It also emphasizes the need to balance stent thrombosis against recurrent intracranial bleeding. A 69-year-old woman presented with inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction caused by thrombotic subtotal occlusion of an approximately 8-mm dominant right coronary artery (RCA). Primary percutaneous coronary intervention was complicated by recurrent thrombotic no-reflow despite sequential balloon angioplasty, selective aspiration thrombectomy, large-lumen aspiration, and intracoronary antiplatelet and fibrinolytic therapy. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) demonstrated extensive residual thrombus and a true vessel diameter substantially larger than available coronary stent platforms. Because balloon deflation repeatedly resulted in vessel collapse with persistent TIMI 0-1 flow and hemodynamic instability, a 5.0-mm drug-eluting stent was implanted as a bailout scaffold. Persistent proximal malapposition was subsequently improved using simultaneous inflation of 6.0- and 4.0-mm noncompliant balloons. TIMI 3 flow was restored. Three days later, the patient developed a large left cerebellar intracranial hemorrhage with fourth-ventricular compression requiring suboccipital craniectomy, hematoma evacuation, and external ventricular drainage. Antithrombotic therapy was withheld and subsequently reintroduced in a staged, imaging-guided manner. Follow-up angiography and IVUS demonstrated preserved TIMI 3 flow, satisfactory stent expansion and apposition, and residual non-flow-limiting thrombotic material.

articles.title: C5a receptor inhibition and minimal steroids for induction of remission in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: C5a receptor (C5aR) inhibition with avacopan has enabled cumulative glucocorticoid (GC) dose reduction in ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV); however, real-world steroid use remains high. This study evaluates a minimal-GC plus avacopan-based regimen against standard-of-care GC for clinical efficacy, renal recovery, urinary biomarkers, and patient-reported outcomes (AAV-PRO). We hypothesised that this regimen would permit substantial GC reduction while maintaining clinical disease control and renal recovery.

METHODS: This two-centre retrospective study included 126 patients with newly diagnosed or relapsing AAV (70 avacopan; 56 GC). The avacopan group followed the minimal-GC plus avacopan-based regimen: prednisolone 30 mg daily for one week, then 20 mg for one week, with no protocolised upfront intravenous methylprednisolone; the GC group received a standard high-dose oral GC taper (from 1 mg/kg, capped at 60 mg/day). Both received standard induction with rituximab or cyclophosphamide. Outcomes included 12-month sustained remission, eGFR change, safety, AAV-PRO scores, and urinary sCD163, MCP-1 and C5a trajectories.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable, with median presenting eGFR 23 versus 25 mL/min/1.73 m² (P = 0.31). Median 12-month cumulative prednisolone was 390 mg with avacopan versus 3535 mg with GC (P < 0.001). Observed sustained remission was 93% versus 91% (P = 0.75) and relapse 6% versus 11% (P = 0.30). Median eGFR increase was 20 versus 18 mL/min/1.73 m² (P = 0.32), with no significant difference among those presenting with eGFR < 15 (P = 0.20). Severe infection rates did not differ significantly (6% versus 9%). AAV-PRO scores were significantly lower with avacopan (median 97 versus 197; P = 0.04). No significant between-group difference in biomarker trajectories was detected.

CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, the minimal-GC plus avacopan-based regimen showed no statistically significant differences in clinical or renal outcomes versus high-dose steroids while reducing cumulative GC exposure by ∼90%. These real-world observations support the feasibility of substantial upfront GC minimisation but should be regarded as supportive rather than confirmatory.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Blood-free full quantification of dynamic TSPO PET imaging with [11C]PBR28.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative dynamic PET imaging requires metabolite-corrected arterial input functions, traditionally obtained through invasive arterial blood sampling, limiting broader adoption of quantitative kinetic modelling. Achieving generalisability across datasets, scanners, and imaging centres remains a major challenge for data-driven alternatives.

METHODS: We developed ASTRA, a deep-learning-based framework for arterial input function estimation from dynamic brain TSPO PET. ASTRA was developed and validated using arterial measurements in one dataset (n=90), then transfer-learned and evaluated against arterial measurements at a second centre (n=52). Building upon this, ASTRA was applied to an independent clinical cohort (n=32) from the second site but without arterial reference data, where quantitative analyses had therefore not been performed, to assess whether it could reproduce previously reported semi-quantitative cross-sectional group differences. Robustness to altered tracer kinetics was evaluated in an out-of-distribution pharmacological blockade cohort (n=5).

RESULTS: ASTRA-derived quantitative estimates agreed with arterial measurements (VT: CCC=0.658-0.805), with higher uncertainty associated with greater error. In the clinical cohort, ASTRA reproduced SUVR-based group differences using DVR (p<0.001), except in the pituitary gland (p=0.12). Finally, ASTRA yielded receptor occupancy estimates (0.92±0.17) closely matching arterial values (0.94±0.12) in the blocking cohort.

CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of multi-site, non-invasive quantitative TSPO PET.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells in ischemic stroke: from biological properties and glial interactions to therapeutic implications.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Although revascularization therapies have improved outcomes in certain patients, effective interventions for neurological deficits are still lacking. White matter injury plays a central role in driving persistent functional impairments. As the cellular foundation for myelin regeneration, oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) have emerged as a promising therapeutic target. This review systematically examines the pathophysiological alterations of OPCs following ischemic stroke, including their proliferation, migration, differentiation, and maturation into myelinating oligodendrocytes, and explores their dynamic interactions with the surrounding microenvironment, including microglia, astrocytes, neurons, and endothelial cells. Accumulating evidence indicates that OPCs not only facilitate myelin repair through differentiation into oligodendrocytes but also contribute to neuroprotection and vascular remodeling by secreting neurotrophic and pro-angiogenic factors. Therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving OPCs and enhancing their differentiation, including pharmacological therapy, cell transplantation, gene therapy, bioengineering and biomaterials technology, as well as rehabilitation and physical therapy, hold considerable promise for improving neurological recovery. By positioning OPC dysfunction as a driver of persistent disability, this review outlines a translational pathway toward therapies that restore white matter integrity and functional recovery after ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Serglycin regulates macrophage differentiation and is associated with human atherosclerotic plaque stability.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Inflammation contributes to the destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques and increases the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. Serglycin (SRGN), is a proteoglycan primarily expressed by immune cells that regulates inflammation, but its role in human atherosclerotic plaques remains unclear. SRGN protein levels were quantified by ELISA in carotid endarterectomy samples from patients in the Atherosclerotic Plaque Imaging Project and compared between symptomatic and asymptomatic plaques. SRGN spatial localization was evaluated by multispectral imaging and histology. Glycosylation patterns were examined by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting. Functional effects were investigated using CRISPR-mediated SRGN knockout in THP-1 monocytes differentiated into macrophages and exposed to oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL). SRGN levels were higher in plaques from asymptomatic patients compared with plaques from symptomatic patients and localized primarily to macrophage- and lipid-rich regions. Plaque SRGN was positively associated with histological markers of plaque stability, displayed heterogeneous molecular forms and showed an inverse association with the plaque vulnerability index. In vitro, SRGN deficiency was associated with a more pro-inflammatory macrophage profile, impaired M2-like polarization, and increased lipid retention following oxLDL exposure. These findings indicate that SRGN is associated with inflammatory cell presence, lipid accumulation, and features of plaque stability in human plaques, and suggest a role for SRGN in macrophage differentiation and lipid handling in atherosclerotic lesions.

articles.title: Early Reintervention After Superior Cavopulmonary Connection Operation and Its Association With Outcomes.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite low operative mortality, superior cavopulmonary connection (SCPC) surgeries are associated with residual lesions and a burden of reintervention. Current practice has trended toward increased utilization of tactics to delay initial surgery (e.g., ductal stent or hybrid strategies). To our knowledge, the effects of these associations on likelihood of residual lesions and post-SCPC diagnostic and interventional catheterization (and their outcomes) have not been described.

AIMS: To describe the likelihood of post-SCPC catheterization, reintervention, and outcomes of these procedures.

METHODS: A single-center case series of patients undergoing SCPC 1/1/2020-3/30/2024 was performed describing the likelihood of requiring catheterization before hospital discharge, interventions performed, and outcomes (adverse events, length of stay, and mortality). Secondary analyses explored differences between patients undergoing transcatheter interventions versus diagnostic studies, regarding both indications and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 170 total SCPC operations, 26% underwent catheterization during that hospitalization, with 19% requiring reintervention. Prematurity, shorter height, younger age, and ongoing enteral feeding were associated with a higher likelihood of a post-SCPC catheterization (p < 0.05). The majority of interventions were on the left pulmonary artery (47%) or cavopulmonary anastomosis (33%). Surgical mortality was not significantly different between subjects who underwent transcatheter intervention after SCPC (3%) and those who did not undergo catheterization (1%, p = 0.38), but the likelihood was higher in those who underwent catheterization but did not undergo intervention (17%, p = 0.01). Hospital and intensive care unit length of stay were longer for subjects who underwent catheterization (p = 0.001) and intervention (p = 0.01) compared to those who did not.

CONCLUSION: Catheterization remains common after SCPC, with the majority identifying a residual lesion that was treated. With treatment of residual lesions, survival to discharge is not significantly different than unaffected patients, but length of stay is prolonged which may indicate persistent morbidity.

articles.title: Peridialytic and Home Blood Pressure in Relation to Left Ventricular Geometry in Hemodialysis Patients.
articles.journal: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In hemodialysis, the blood pressure measure that best reflects the chronic blood pressure burden related to left ventricular remodeling remains uncertain. We compared the associations of peridialytic and home blood pressure with left ventricular mass, left ventricular hypertrophy, and left ventricular geometry in maintenance hemodialysis patients.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 265 adults on thrice-weekly hemodialysis underwent 1-week predialysis, intradialytic, postdialysis blood pressure and home blood pressure monitoring. Echocardiograms interpreted by readers blinded to blood pressure data assessed left ventricular mass index, relative wall thickness, left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular concentricity, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear and logistic regression, with models adjusted for relevant clinical covariates.

FINDINGS: Predialysis, intradialytic, postdialysis, and home blood pressure were 147/77 ± 24/13, 142/75 ± 22/12, 144/75 ± 23/14, and 132/79 ± 22/12 mmHg. Left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular concentricity, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy were present in 48%, 38%, and 25%, respectively. Systolic home blood pressure showed the strongest association with left ventricular mass index (β = 0.278; R2 = 0.113; p < 0.001), whereas systolic predialysis blood pressure showed the strongest association with relative wall thickness (β = 0.211; R2 = 0.116; p = 0.002). In logistic regression analyses, home blood pressure was the blood pressure approach most consistently associated with left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular concentricity, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, with odds ratios ranging from 1.030 to 1.048.

DISCUSSION: In maintenance hemodialysis patients, home blood pressure was more consistently associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, particularly left ventricular mass index, left ventricular hypertrophy, and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, whereas predialysis systolic blood pressure showed the strongest association with relative wall thickness. The associations observed for selected peridialytic blood pressure measurements support a complementary role for home and dialysis-unit blood pressure assessment in evaluating left ventricular remodeling in this population.

articles.title: Standards Defining Echocardiography Core Laboratory (ECL) in Clinical Practice and Research.
articles.abstract: Echocardiography is extensively utilized in both clinical practice and research due to its accessibility. Echocardiography core laboratories (ECLs) adhering to societal guidelines offer superior readings and interpretations compared with the on-site assessments by reducing measurement variability and enhancing study precision. In the present work, we aim to define minimum standards for clinical echocardiography laboratories and research ECLs based on recommendations from the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging, as well as on expert opinion and our experience in European countries. Accurate acquisition of high-quality images is crucial for ensuring reproducibility, repeatability and reliability of the echocardiographic measurements. In addition to the commonly used workstations, an academic ECL must also possess the necessary capacities and skilled personnel to conduct sophisticated research projects. Personnel should hold advanced certification in echocardiography, indicating postgraduate training and experience beyond the basic cardiovascular ultrasound education. They should be capable of designing, performing, and interpreting complex echocardiography studies. Reproducibility of the ECL should be validated using a small, randomly selected sample, preferably in the early analytic phase. ECL readings and interpretations are superior to site-reported measurements and serve as the gold standard in observational studies and clinical trials. To ensure internal validity, an academic ECL should continuously evaluate/report reproducibility, repeatability and reliability. ECL should be formally acknowledged and accredited by an international scientific imaging society.

articles.title: Prognostic relevance of protein prescriptions based on adjusted body weight in critically ill overweight or obese patients - analysis of a large international database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ESPEN currently recommends using adjusted body weight (aBW) to guide protein prescriptions for critically ill overweight or obese patients. The prognostic relevance of this concept is unknown.

METHODS: We analyzed a subset of a large international point prevalence survey of nutritional practice in 785 intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Patients were included if they had been in the ICU for at least 96 h and had a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m². We modelled the association between early average protein intake (days 1-4 after ICU admission) and the cause-specific adjusted hazards of in-ICU death and ICU discharge alive within a competing risks framework. Intake was normalized to aBW, defined as ideal body weight plus 25% of the difference between actual and ideal body weight.

RESULTS: 9,068 patients were analyzed. There was no evidence of an association between early protein intake and ICU discharge alive. In contrast, very low protein intake (below approximately 0.45 g/kg aBW/day) was associated with a higher hazard of in-ICU death. Above this threshold, there was no clear evidence of a further association between protein intake and the hazard of in-ICU death. The strongest association was observed at 0 g/kg aBW/day (adjusted hazard rate 1.41 i.e. an estimated 38% higher risk, 95% confidence interval 1.17-1.69).

CONCLUSIONS: Early protein intake does not appear to be associated with time to ICU discharge among survivors. However, in critically ill patients with overweight or obesity, very low protein intake during the early acute phase may be associated with less favorable in-ICU outcomes.

articles.title: Infant mortality related to congenital heart disease in the United States, 1999-2025: trends, disparities, and projections to 2040.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital heart disease remains a leading congenital cause of infant mortality in the United States despite major advances in diagnosis and neonatal care. This study evaluated national mortality trends from 1999 to 2025, examined sex and racial disparities, and projected future burden through 2040 using time-series forecasting.

METHODS: A retrospective CDC WONDER analysis examined U.S. infant (< 1 year) CHD mortality from 1999 to 2025 using ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Deaths listing CHD as underlying or contributing cause were included. Crude mortality rates (CMRs) per 100,000 with 95% CIs were calculated. Trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression analysis to estimate annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC). Forecasts to 2040 used ARIMA and ETS models, stratified by sex and race/ethnicity.

RESULTS: From 1999 to 2025, 55,719 infant deaths related to CHD were recorded in the United States, 92.16% in medical facilities. The CMRs declined from 69.66 in 1999 to 46.44 in 2025 (AAPC - 1.32%) and is projected at 37.51 by 2040. Male mortality remained higher than female (54.86 vs. 52.04). NH Black infants had the highest mean mortality (71.87), while NH Asian/Pacific Islander infants showed the steepest decline (AAPC - 2.30%). Recent increases appeared in NH White infants after 2018 (APC 1.56%) and Hispanic infants after 2020 (APC 3.48%) overall.

CONCLUSION: Infant CHD related mortality declined substantially from 1999 to 2025 and is projected to continue decreasing through 2040; however, persistent excess mortality in male, NH Black, and Hispanic infants underscores enduring demographic disparities in outcomes.

articles.title: A clinicopathological-MRI model for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer: a single-center retrospective study with transcriptomic pathway exploration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate pretreatment prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy may help guide individualized decision-making in breast cancer. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a practical and interpretable pCR prediction model based on routinely available clinicopathological indicators and MRI-report features, and to explore potential pCR-related biological pathways using a public transcriptomic dataset.

METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective study, including 201 patients with breast cancer who received neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command from April 2021 to April 2025. Patients were divided into pCR and non-pCR groups according to postoperative pathology. Pretreatment clinicopathological and MRI-report features were collected. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify pCR-related factors, and a clinicopathological model, an MRI-report model, and a combined clinicopathological-MRI model were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, the DeLong test, calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, decision curve analysis (DCA), and 1000-times bootstrap internal validation. A nomogram was then constructed based on the combined model, and exploratory subgroup applicability was assessed using the single-center cohort. In addition, Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was performed using the available public transcriptome data, serving as a preliminary exploration of the biological functional context associated with pCR in breast cancer, and providing an exploratory biological complement to the predictive model.

RESULTS: Among the 201 patients, 60 achieved pCR and 141 had non-pCR. Multivariable logistic regression showed that HER2-positive status, Ki-67 index, and MRI maximum tumor diameter were associated with pCR. The AUC values of the clinicopathological model, MRI-report model, and combined model were 0.880, 0.703, and 0.910, respectively. Although the combined model showed improved AUC compared with the clinicopathological and MRI-report models, the incremental improvement over the clinicopathological model was limited; therefore, its clinical benefit still requires further confirmation by external validation. Calibration analysis, DCA, and bootstrap internal validation suggested good internal stability of the combined model. The nomogram showed favorable performance within the single-center cohort. Exploratory GSEA suggested that differences between pCR and non-pCR may involve TGF-beta signaling, TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB signaling, estrogen response, KRAS-related pathways, and coagulation-related pathways, with heterogeneity across HR/HER2 subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: A clinicopathological-MRI combined model incorporating HER2 status, Ki-67 index, and MRI maximum tumor diameter, together with nomogram construction, may provide a simple and interpretable research tool for predicting pCR after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer.

articles.title: PD-1/PD-L1 expression in pediatric duodenal biopsies: Association with mucosal activity and diagnostic performance in celiac disease.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The role of immune checkpoint molecules (ICMs) in celiac disease (CD) remains incompletely understood despite their expected function in limiting mucosal immune-mediated injury.
