articles.title: Is the Developmental Stage of Grapevine Clusters a Good Predictor of Ontogenic Resistance to Plasmopara viticola?
articles.abstract: Reduction patterns in grapevine berry cluster susceptibility to downy mildew (DM) due to ontogenic resistance were investigated under different viticultural conditions in northern Italy to develop mathematical equations for predicting the infection risk of Plasmopara viticola. Clusters were inoculated with sporangial suspensions of P. viticola at different developmental stages (DS), and disease severity was assessed twice weekly. The best fit was obtained using time-dependent logistic equations in which time was expressed as cluster DS (R2 = 0.876), days after DS65 (full flowering) (R2 = 0.880), or accumulated degree-days (base 0°C) after DS65 (R2 = 0.882), all with a mean absolute error below 9%. The fitted curves consistently showed high susceptibility before and during early flowering, followed by rapid increase in ontogenic resistance after full flowering, sharp decline in susceptibility, and asymptotic approach to complete resistance. The inflection point, representing the fastest decrease in susceptibility, occurred at approximately DS72, 10 days after DS65, or 245 degree-days. Bands were empirically generated so as the Mean Absolute Error for the excluded out-of-band observations remained below the 2% disease severity threshold. Bands were widest during the rapid decline in susceptibility, reflecting variability among viticultural conditions. The DS-based equation, together with the bootstrapping variability in its parameter estimation and experimental error, was used in a Monte Carlo framework to provide a stochastic distribution of the predicted DM severities. Unlike deterministic approaches, which provide a single estimate of susceptibility at a given developmental stage, stochastic approaches produce a range of possible susceptibility levels with associated probabilities.

articles.title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05371496.

articles.title: On generative artificial intelligence in scientific writing.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: Scientific communication - the dissemination of ideas, hypotheses, and discoveries - is fundamental to advancing human knowledge and to ensuring public access to new knowledge as it is generated. Growth in the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific communication has been explosive, likely driven by high uptake among an adept userbase with demanding schedules, making the efficiency gains attractive. The rapid uptake of AI is creating disruptive changes in the way scientific communication happens, affecting the methods by which abstracts, manuscripts, figures, presentations, and funding proposals are generated, and in many cases impacting the final product. In this perspective piece, we reflect on the rapidly changing landscape of AI use in scientific communication with attention to the potential immediate and long-term risks. The inherent unauthorized secondary use of the data used to train AI models raises questions about credit and plagiarism in academia. Fabricated references have proliferated in the scientific literature resulting from "hallucinations" by AI models. Meanwhile, each use of an AI model comes with an incremental risk to the environment at an already perilous time. More abstractly, AI use in scientific communication risks the process itself becoming iterative, prioritizing summation while diminishing insights that fuel the scientific engine. Finally, the friction that AI models remove from writing may risk removing an essential part of the process of scientific thinking, particularly for the next generation of scientists. While we acknowledge that AI is here to stay, we feel an element of caution is warranted in its implementation, to help preserve science and its dissemination as a fundamentally human endeavor.

articles.title: Identifying Structural Heart Disease and Prioritizing Echocardiography Through Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Tele-ECG: An External Validation of the PROVAR+ Study.
articles.abstract: Structural heart disease (SHD) is underdiagnosed where echocardiography access is limited. We evaluated the role of artificial intelligence-enabled ECG for SHD detection (AI-ECG-SHD) in cardiovascular screening. We prospectively enrolled adults undergoing public-system cardiovascular screening in two Brazilian cities. Participants underwent clinical assessment, digital 12-lead tele-ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) interpreted by cardiologists. ECG signals were analyzed using a validated AI-ECG-SHD algorithm through an application programming interface. SHD was defined as moderate/severe ventricular dysfunction/hypertrophy, wall-motion abnormalities, moderate/severe valvular disease, congenital heart disease, or pericardial disease. AI-ECG-SHD performance was assessed at a predefined threshold and discrimination compared with a model incorporating clinical variables and major conventional ECG abnormalities. Number needed to screen (NNS) was calculated. Among 3,779 participants (median age 66 years; 56.7% women), 58.7% screened AI-ECG-SHD-positive and 24.2% had TTE-detected SHD. Major ECG abnormalities (OR=3.73), age (OR=1.22/10-years), male sex (OR=1.50), Chagas disease (OR=1.89), coronary disease (OR=3.01), and heart failure (OR=1.33) independently predicted SHD. AI-ECG-SHD probability (each 10% increase) was strongly associated with SHD (OR 1.55, 95%CI 1.51-1.61; p<0.001) and showed superior discrimination versus the conventional model (AUC 0.80, 95%CI 0.78-0.82 vs 0.75, 95%CI 0.74-0.77; p<0.001). AI-ECG-SHD achieved 59.4% accuracy, 87.3% sensitivity, 50.4% specificity, 92.6% negative-predictive value, diagnostic odds ratio 7.00, and NNS 4.7. AI-guided prioritization reduced estimated time to diagnosis of 50% of SHD cases from 407 to 172 days under fixed TTE capacity. In conclusion, AI-ECG-SHD improved SHD detection over conventional prediction and may enable scalable, resource-efficient TTE prioritization in underserved public healthcare systems.

articles.title: Rat hepatitis E virus RNA detection in isolated cases of acute undifferentiated febrile illness without acute hepatitis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rat hepatitis E virus (ratHEV; Rocahepevirus ratti) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen whose clinical spectrum is predominantly hepatic. Whether ratHEV causes acute undifferentiated febrile illness (AUFI) without acute hepatitis has not been systematically evaluated.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study at a southern Spain tertiary hospital (April 2021-October 2023) evaluated patients tested for Rickettsia spp. and/or Coxiella burnetii. AUFI was defined as community-acquired fever ≥38°C lasting <21 days without localizing features or initial etiology; patients with acute hepatitis were excluded. AUFI cases were compared with contemporaneous febrile patients presenting with a localizing focus. The primary outcome was sequence-confirmed infection. Detections without sequence recovery were classified as probable infections.

RESULTS: Of 1,684 patients assessed, 312 were eligible: 81 with AUFI (median age 53 years [IQR, 37-64]; 54 [66.7%] men) and 231 comparators. Sequence-confirmed ratHEV infection occurred in 1/81 AUFI patients (1.2%; 95% CI, 0.2-6.7) and 0/231 comparators (0%; 95% CI, 0-1.6; P = 0.260). Two additional AUFI patients had detectable ratHEV RNA without sequence recovery. Combining confirmed and probable infections, ratHEV RNA was detected in 3/81 AUFI patients (3.7%; 95% CI, 1.3-10.3; P = 0.017). The confirmed infection presented as a self-limiting febrile illness without liver dysfunction, ratHEV RNA cleared upon fever resolution. The recovered genotype C1 sequence clustered with ratHEV rodent sequences from the same region.

CONCLUSIONS: RatHEV RNA was detected exclusively among AUFI patients. These findings support prospectively evaluating ratHEV as a potential cause of AUFI where the virus circulates in animal reservoirs.

articles.title: Microbiome-Targeted Interventions for Pediatric Asthma and Allergic Diseases: Current and Emerging Approaches.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract: Allergic diseases are among the most common chronic diseases of childhood and remain a major public health challenge. Increasing evidence indicates that the early-life gut microbiome plays a central role in immune maturation, making it an attractive target for allergy prevention. During the first 1000 days of life, interactions between the developing microbiome and the immune system help establish immune tolerance, while disruptions to this process increase the risk of asthma and allergic diseases. Current microbiome-targeted strategies largely focus on optimizing early-life microbial exposures through interventions such as mode of delivery, antibiotic stewardship, breastfeeding, and exposure to diverse environmental microorganisms. These approaches are already incorporated into public health recommendations and promote healthy microbiome development without directly manipulating microbial communities. Newer approaches seek to intervene more precisely through microbial transfer therapies, live biotherapeutic products, prebiotics, postbiotics, and microbial metabolite-based therapies. Although several have shown encouraging preclinical and early clinical results, evidence supporting routine clinical use remains limited. The next generation of microbiome therapeutics is likely to be defined less by changing which microbes are present than by restoring the microbial functions that establish immune tolerance. This conceptual advance is driving the development of increasingly targeted microbiome-based interventions and provides a framework for the next generation of allergy prevention strategies. Translating these mechanistic insights into safe, effective therapies that complement established public health measures represents the next major challenge in preventing asthma and allergic diseases.

articles.title: Sirtuins in Cellular Senescence and Cardiovascular Diseases: From Mechanistic Basis to Activator Development and Translational Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

articles.title: The new steatotic liver disease nomenclature identifies different risk trajectories for liver-related complications in compensated patients.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Recently, a new nomenclature for steatotic liver disease (SLD) defines metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD), according to alcohol consumption and presence of metabolic risk factors. This study aimed to identify risk factors associated with liver-related events (LREs) in patients with SLD.

METHODS: A single-center study including 335 patients with biopsy-proven SLD was conducted between 2009 and 2021. Patients with other causes of chronic liver disease or prior decompensated liver disease were excluded. The incidence of LREs and associated risk factors were analyzed using a Fine and Gray competing risk model, with non-liver-related death as a competing event.

RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included with a median follow-up of 3.6 years. Among them, 221 were classified as MASLD, 26 as MetALD, and 88 as ALD. Advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) was observed in 55% of MASLD, 50% of MetALD, and 68% of ALD patients. During follow-up, LREs occurred in 9% of MASLD patients, 19% of MetALD patients, and 30% of ALD patients. Overall mortality was 12% in MASLD, 19% in MetALD, and 21% in ALD. In multivariable analysis, advanced fibrosis, daily alcohol intake, and diabetes were independently associated with LREs.

CONCLUSIONS: Across the SLD spectrum, alcohol consumption and fibrosis stage are major risk factors for liver-related events. Accurate assessment of alcohol intake, although challenging in clinical practice, remains essential to optimize patient care.

articles.title: Improving the Quality of Care in Advanced Prostate Cancer Through Personalised Diagnostic Testing. Outcomes of a Sharing Progress in Cancer Care taskforce conducted under the auspices of the European Association of Urology.
articles.abstract: Timely biomarker assessment is essential to optimise outcomes in prostate cancer (PCa) by enabling the appropriate use of targeted therapies for defined molecular subtypes. Several approved treatments for metastatic castration-resistant PCa, including PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, immune checkpoint inhibition, and poly(ADP)-ribose polymerase inhibitors (PARPi), require confirmation of specific biomarkers such as PSMA expression, mismatch repair deficiency, or pathogenic variants in homologous recombination repair genes. Targeted agents are also moving into earlier disease stages, further increasing the need for early biomarker testing. Despite rapid therapeutic advances, access to biomarker-informed care remains inconsistent, potentially leading to delayed or missed treatment opportunities. A multidisciplinary task force of experts addressed challenges and solutions related to biomarker implementation for prostate cancer patients, integrating guideline-supported practice, evidence from published/ongoing studies up to June 2026, and their expert opinion. Biomarker implementation is multidisciplinary, with urologists and uro-oncologists having a coordinating role in integrating molecular testing into clinical workflows, from biopsy acquisition and test selection to interpretation and patient communication. Tumour heterogeneity necessitates a biopsy strategy combining targeted and systematic sampling. The possibility of lineage plasticity may warrant repeated sampling. Both germline and somatic testing are critical components of precision care, with potential emerging roles for circulating tumour DNA, digital pathology biomarkers, and advanced imaging such as PSMA PET. Institutional strategies, clinician training, multidisciplinary collaboration, and innovative testing models are required to overcome current barriers to sustainable implementation. Overall, improving the timelines and equity of biomarker-guided decision-making is urgent to fully realise the potential of precision oncology in PCa.

articles.title: Acute Stone-Related Healthcare Utilization Before Definitive Stone Surgery: Variation by Surgical Modality and Sociodemographic Characteristics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize acute stone-related healthcare utilization during the year before definitive stone surgery and examine variation by surgical modality and sociodemographic characteristics.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adults (≥ 18 years) undergoing first definitive stone surgery with ureteroscopy, shock wave lithotripsy, or percutaneous nephrolithotomy in Epic Cosmos from 2015 through 2025 were identified. Acute stone event days included unique days involving stone-related emergency department visits or hospitalizations, decompression procedures, or infections during the preceding year. Quasi-Poisson regression evaluated differences by surgical modality and, in separate modality-adjusted models, race, Social Vulnerability Index quartile, and Rural-Urban Commuting Area category.

RESULTS: Among 1,074,341 patients, 79.4% underwent ureteroscopy, 16.5% shock wave lithotripsy, and 4.1% percutaneous nephrolithotomy; 69.6% experienced at least one acute stone event day. Compared with ureteroscopy, expected event counts were higher before percutaneous nephrolithotomy (incidence rate ratio 1.18, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.22) and lower before shock wave lithotripsy (incidence rate ratio 0.63, 95% confidence interval 0.61-0.65). Compared with White patients, burden was higher among Black patients (incidence rate ratio 1.12, 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.14). Burden increased progressively across Social Vulnerability Index quartiles, reaching 16% higher in the most versus least vulnerable quartile. No meaningful differences occurred by Rural-Urban Commuting Area category.

CONCLUSIONS: Acute stone-related healthcare utilization before definitive surgery was common and varied by surgical modality, race, and neighborhood social vulnerability, but not rurality. These findings identify populations experiencing disproportionate preoperative morbidity and support further evaluation of coordinated pathways from acute presentation to definitive stone care.

articles.title: Temporal distribution of suicide within a day among children and adolescents in Japan, 1995-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the temporal distribution of suicidality is essential for timely support and care. However, it remains unclear how suicide deaths among children and adolescents are distributed within a day. We aimed to describe the temporal distribution of suicide death among this population and its variation by sex, school grade, day of the week, month, and calendar year.

METHODS: This nationwide descriptive epidemiologic study used vital statistics (death records) in Japan from 1995 to 2023. Cause and time of death were collected from death records. To estimate the 24-h distribution of suicide death, we used the kernel density estimator for circular data. We further stratified by sex, school grade, day of the week, month, and calendar year to explore variations in the distribution by these factors.

RESULTS: From 1995 to 2023, 9453 children and adolescents died by suicide and had valid information on time of death. The overall distribution showed a bimodal pattern with a primary peak at 18:00-19:00 and a secondary peak at 01:00-02:00. This bimodal pattern was more marked among boys with higher school grades. The evening peaks were consistently observed across weekdays, months, and years, while the evening peak was flatter on weekends.

CONCLUSIONS: Among children and adolescents, the distribution of suicide death showed the bimodal pattern with peaks at 18:00-19:00 and 01:00-02:00 while this distribution varied by demographics and temporal contexts. These findings highlight the importance of designing temporally targeted suicide prevention strategies for children and adolescents.

articles.title: Decoding PilQ: From pathogenicity to vaccine potential against fish Edwardsiellosis.
articles.abstract: Edwardsiella piscicida is an intracellular bacterium causing fish Edwardsiellosis. PilQ is the structural protein of type IV pili and crucial for bacterial virulence. This research aimed to investigate the pathogenic roles and immune protective effects of E. piscicida PilQ. PilQ contains a secretin-N domain and a secretin domain, classified as a member of the secretin protein family, and was located on the external membrane of E. piscicida. The PilQ mutation (TXD1ΔPilQ) significantly reduced bacterial survival under acidic and oxidative conditions, and the motility and biofilm formation of bacteria. Moreover, compared to wild E. piscicida, the PilQ mutation markedly decreased the adhesive and invasive capacity of E. piscicida to peripheral blood leukocytes (PBLs); meanwhile, the TXD1ΔPilQ could boost the reactive oxygen species (ROS) production of PBLs. On the other hand, antibody-mediated PilQ blocking yielded consistent phenotypes with PilQ gene deletion; moreover, the block of PilQ conspicuously suppressed the E. piscicida reproduction in PBLs. Additionally, we observe that recombinant PilQ (rPilQ) could bind to PBLs and activate the PBLs' ROS and acid phosphatase (ACP), and the vaccinated rPilQ could further activate head kidney macrophages (HKMs) vitality, heighten expression levels of immune genes, and boost the fish serum's antibacterial properties via enhancing the production of IgM, resulting in that rPilQ acted as a subunit vaccine against E. piscicida infection. The results provided the first evidence that PilQ is crucial to the E. piscicida virulence and acts as a potential candidate for developing subunit vaccines in teleost.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: B cells play a central role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and are a therapeutic target. We therefore assessed the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β, a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, in patients with active SLE.

METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial, we enrolled patients who were aged 18-80 years, fulfilled the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology-American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for SLE, and had active disease (defined as a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 [SLEDAI-2K] score of 8 or more and positivity for antinuclear antibodies or anti-double stranded DNA antibodies) at 30 tertiary hospitals in China. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to receive obinutuzumab β or placebo, stratified by SLEDAI-2K score and 24-h urine protein level. Patients, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment allocation. Patients received intravenous infusions of obinutuzumab β (1000 mg) or placebo on days 1, 15, 169, 183, 365, and 379. All patients maintained their background standard therapy. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients with an SLE Responder Index (SRI)-4 response at week 12 assessed in all patients who were randomly assigned and received at least one dose of study treatment (ie, the full analysis set). Safety was assessed in all patients who received any study treatment and had at least one post-dose safety assessment (ie, the safety analysis set) over 52 weeks. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05796206) and is complete. People with lived experience were not involved as research partners in this study.

FINDINGS: Between May 26, 2023, and July 29, 2024, 171 patients were screened for eligibility. Of these, 123 patients were randomly assigned to receive obinutuzumab β (n=61) or placebo (n=62) and were included in both the full analysis set and safety analysis sets. The mean age was 36·1 years (SD 10·3). 115 (93%) of 123 patients were female, eight (7%) were male, and 117 (95%) were Han Chinese ethnicity. At week 12, 32 (52%) of 61 patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 21 (34%) of 62 in the placebo group had an SRI-4 response (adjusted risk difference 19 percentage points, 95% CI 3-36; p=0·022). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 (20%) patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 14 (23%) in the placebo group. One fatal treatment-emergent adverse event (sepsis) occurred in the placebo group.

INTERPRETATION: Obinutuzumab β plus standard therapy improved SRI-4 response at week 12 in Chinese patients with active SLE, with a generally manageable safety profile over 52 weeks. These phase 2 findings support further evaluation and longer-term safety follow-up.

FUNDING: Beijing Mabworks Biotech.

articles.title: Weight management in people with HIV.
articles.abstract: Excess weight gain in people with HIV is now recognised as a common risk associated with the use of guideline-recommended antiretroviral therapy, such that nearly 50% of people with HIV are living with comorbid obesity. Weight gain and clinical obesity exacerbate cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health complications in this population and chronic weight management strategies that reduce these risks are now an urgent priority. Behavioural interventions can be offered to improve diet and increase physical activity, including increasing protein intake and promoting regular physical activity. Additionally, there is a growing body of evidence to support the use of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies in people with HIV, along with a historical literature showing the efficacy of tesamorelin; however, there are sparse data to direct the use of other approved obesity management medicines specific to this population. Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

articles.title: Induction of labour vs spontaneous labour onset and maternal and perinatal outcomes and maternal experiences: The Birth Experience Study (BESt).
articles.journal: Women and birth : journal of the Australian College of Midwives
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Induction of labour (IOL) is rising around the world, with little known about consequent outcomes in large cohorts of childbearing women.

AIM: To examine the impact of IOL vs spontaneous labour onset on maternal and perinatal outcomes, as reported by women in a national survey.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional, online, maternal self-report survey, was open in Australia from March-December 2021.

PARTICIPANTS: 7791 women who had a spontaneous onset (n = 5230), or IOL (n = 2561) were included.

ANALYSIS: Labour, birth and postnatal outcomes were classified as binary variables and percentages. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed, controlling for likely confounders.

RESULTS: Compared with spontaneous onset of labour, survey respondents having an IOL were significantly more likely to experience: forceps or vacuum; episiotomy; emergency caesarean; excessive blood loss; physical pain and/or poor or decreased physical health; birth as traumatic; regrets about their birth experience; diagnosis of PTSD; obstetric violence; and less skin-to-skin contact with their babies. Neonatal outcomes following IOL included: significantly higher odds of being distressed during labour; having jaundice; and being given formula when the mother had chosen to breast feed. There was no difference in major perineal injury or pelvic floor outcomes, or admission of the baby to special care nursery or neonatal intensive care.

CONCLUSIONS: IOL was associated with significant negative physical and psychological health impacts for women and babies compared to spontaneous labour onset. There is a need for more research on clinical and psychological impacts of IOL for women, to ensure decision making is informed.

articles.title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Single-pill combination therapy improves medication adherence and hypertension control. However, limited evidence is available on its implementation in routine clinical practice.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the long-term effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of single-pill combination therapy through team-based care for blood pressure reduction among patients with uncontrolled hypertension in primary care settings in Colombia and Jamaica.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicountry, unblinded, pragmatic, cluster randomized clinical trial. Twenty primary care clinics in Jamaica and 20 in Colombia were randomly assigned to either the single-pill combination therapy group or the standard care group. A total of 1706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension were enrolled between February 23, 2023, and September 12, 2024. The final follow-up visit occurred on September 9, 2026.

INTERVENTIONS: In the intervention group (n = 869), a team-based care approach that included physician and nurse training, health coaching, home blood pressure monitoring, and blood pressure audit and feedback was used to implement single-pill combination therapy. Single-pill combinations were purchased locally and provided to patients. In the standard care group (n = 837), patients received monotherapy or polytherapy with guideline-recommended medications covered by health insurance or government programs. The intervention lasted 18 months, with additional follow-up at 24 months.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to 18 months. Three blood pressure measurements were obtained at each of 2 visits at each time point using a standard protocol.

RESULTS: Among the 1706 enrolled participants, at baseline, the mean age was 61.4 years, 69.9% of participants were female, and 98.2% were taking antihypertensive medications. Among the 1574 participants included in the primary analysis, systolic blood pressure decreased by 19.1 mm Hg, from 145.9 mm Hg at baseline to 126.8 mm Hg at 18 months, in the intervention group and by 9.0 mm Hg, from 145.0 mm Hg to 136.1 mm Hg, in the standard care group, with a between-group difference of -10.1 mm Hg (95% CI, -13.3 to -6.9 mm Hg; P < .001). At 18 months, 69.5% of patients in the intervention group and 29.2% in the standard care group achieved systolic blood pressure less than 130 and diastolic blood pressure less than 80 mm Hg. Serious adverse events (death and hospitalization) occurred at similar frequencies in the intervention (7.9%) and standard care (9.9%) groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementing single-pill combination therapy through team-based care significantly reduced blood pressure over 18 months among adults with uncontrolled hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica. This comprehensive strategy integrating single-pill combination therapy with team-based care could be widely adopted and scaled up for hypertension control, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05405920.

articles.title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: Research Summary.
Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: Research Summary.
Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The COAST-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) has demonstrated modest success rates. Ablation of atrial low-voltage areas (LVA) has shown potential results, but more data are required.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PVI plus LVA ablation is superior to PVI alone in reducing atrial arrhythmia recurrence in patients with AF.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Single-blind randomized clinical trial in 14 AF ablation centers in Canada. Adults with persistent AF of more than 3 months were enrolled between August 2018 and September 2024 and followed up for 18 to 36 months through April 2026.

INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation or PVI alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond 90 days after a single catheter ablation procedure. Secondary outcomes included repeat ablation for AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia, emergency visits or hospitalization, arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months, procedure duration, total ablation delivery time, AF burden, and safety outcomes. The primary efficacy analysis was based on the modified intention-to-treat principle for patients who received the intervention.

RESULTS: Among 508 enrolled patients, 253 were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation and 255 to PVI alone. Mean (SD) age was 65.2 (9.0) years, 386 (76%) were male and 268 (54%) had LVA. After a mean (SD) follow-up of 21 (15) months, 124 (49.4%) randomized to PVI plus LVA and 146 (57.5%) randomized to PVI reached the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82; 95% CI, 0.65-1.04; P = .11). In the prespecified principal subgroup analysis of 268 patients with LVA, arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 68 of 138 patients (49.3%) following PVI plus LVA ablation compared with 90 of 130 patients (69.2%) following PVI alone (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66-0.91; P = .002). Arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months (37.0% vs 56.2%; HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.92) and AF burden were lower after PVI plus LVA ablation in this group. Among patients without LVA, recurrence was similar between ablation groups (56 of 113 [49.6%] vs 51 of 113 [45.1%]; HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.90-1.32). Procedure duration and ablation delivery time were longer in the PVI plus LVA ablation group. Safety outcomes were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, among patients with persistent AF, adjunctive LVA ablation did not significantly reduce atrial arrhythmia recurrence in the overall population over a mean 21-month follow-up. A prespecified principal subgroup analysis of patients with LVA suggested that adjunctive LVA ablation was consistent with reduced recurrence of atrial arrhythmias in this group.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03347227.

articles.title: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549.

articles.title: Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.
authors: FRENCHIE-Lp(a) Investigators and the French Alliance for Cardiovascular Trials (FACT) investigators network
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained <1%. Among 1561 patients (aged 61 ± 12 years; 21.3% women), median Lp(a) was 13 mg/dL at admission and remained stable over time (median difference overtime = 0 mg/dL). However, only 68.5% of patients remained in the same Lp(a) category overtime. In patients with discharge-Lp(a) ≤37 mg/dL (72.5% of the population), only 0.97% had Lp(a) >70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL.

CONCLUSION: Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention.

REGISTRATION: Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956.

articles.title: Thymectomy Extent, Immune Recovery, and Infectious Burden After Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal cardiac surgery frequently requires thymectomy, but the consequences of extensive thymic removal remain uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 105 neonates undergoing sternotomy (2015-2024), comparing infections and 6-month lymphocyte recovery after partial versus total thymectomy, with Firth regression adjusted for bypass duration and surgical era. Separate cohorts underwent paired plasma biomarker (n=8) and whole-blood RNA sequencing (n=4) analysis before and after thymectomy.

RESULTS: Among 105 neonates, 27 underwent partial and 78 total thymectomy. Multiple infections occurred in 2 of 27 (7%) after partial and 23 of 78 (30%) after total thymectomy (P=0.02); after adjustment for bypass duration and surgical era, the association was not statistically significant (Firth-adjusted odds ratio, 2.99 [95% CI, 0.82-15.85]; P=0.10). Median lymphocyte count decreased after total but increased after partial thymectomy (change, -0.8 versus +0.9×103/μL; P=0.011). Tumor necrosis factor-α decreased in all 8 biomarker participants (unadjusted P=0.0078). RNA sequencing in 4 patients (2 partial, 2 total thymectomy) identified 835 differentially expressed genes; pre-T-cell receptor α decreased in all 4 pairs (log2 fold change, -2.50; adjusted P=6×10-6).

CONCLUSIONS: Total thymectomy was associated with reduced 6-month lymphocyte recovery and higher unadjusted odds of multiple infections. The infection association was not statistically significant after adjustment, and few events (2 of 27 after partial thymectomy) limit precision and cannot exclude a clinically important effect; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Biomarker and transcriptomic findings are exploratory and cannot distinguish thymectomy from surgery, maturation, or postoperative recovery. Prospective studies are underway to evaluate thymic preservation and autologous reimplantation.

articles.title: Effects of Sotatercept on Cardiac Structure and Function in Combined Post- and Precapillary Pulmonary Hypertension in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: Analysis of the CADENCE Study.
[Post-resuscitation care 2025: neurological prognosis of post-cardiac arrest brain injury].
articles.abstract: Post-cardiac arrest brain injury represents a central component of the post-resuscitation syndrome, driven not only by the initial hypoxic-ischemic insult but also by reperfusion injury after the return or start of mechanical circulation. Complex neuronal damage accounts for a substantial proportion of mortality among successfully resuscitated patients, making reliable neurological prognostication a key objective of post-resuscitation care and clinical decision-making. The 2025 European Resuscitation Council guidelines emphasize a structured, multimodal approach to neuroprognostication. Prognosis should not rely on a single parameter; instead, it requires the integrated interpretation of clinical findings, electrophysiological data, neuroimaging results, and circulating biomarkers. This strategy aims to reduce falsely pessimistic predictions, prevent premature withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy, and avoid the unnecessary prolongation of futile intensive care in cases of irreversible brain injury. In the early phase of return of spontaneous circulation, neurological assessment may be confounded by several factors, including residual sedation, neuromuscular blockade, metabolic disturbances, and cardiorespiratory instability. Therefore, accurate prognostication depends on the correction of reversible conditions and stabilization of physiological parameters before definitive conclusions are drawn. Importantly, neurological outcome assessment is inherently time-dependent, and appropriate timing is essential for safe and evidence-based decision-making. Overall, the 2025 recommendations advocate standardized, multidisciplinary, and stepwise neuroprognostication as a cornerstone of post-resuscitation management, prioritizing patient-centered care while minimizing uncertainty and supporting long-term neurological recovery whenever possible. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1799-1809.

articles.title: [Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation in Hungarian emergency departments].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation (not in cardiac arrest) is a critical, high-risk procedure in emergency care. Internationally, safety improves through standardized procedures, equipment, documentation, and training.

OBJECTIVE: To map current practice in Hungarian emergency departments regarding who performs the procedure, the degree of regulation, the available drugs and devices, documentation practices, and training.

METHOD: We conducted a cross-sectional online questionnaire survey. Based on the department-head registry of the Hungarian Society of Emergency Medicine, we sent the questionnaire to the heads of all 44 Hungarian emergency departments. Data were collected between May and July 2026 and analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: The response rate was 52% (23/44). In 96% of the departments, the procedure was routinely performed by emergency care providers. A written protocol existed in 48% of the departments (mandatory in 17%). Propofol, a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent, and a bougie were available in all departments. Non-invasive ventilation was available in 96% of departments, videolaryngoscopes in 74%, and capnographs in 78%; however, only 39% mandated capnography. In 52% of the responding departments, no dedicated procedural documentation was produced, and 57% had no regular topic-specific training.

DISCUSSION: In the responding departments, the procedure was performed predominantly by emergency clinicians, and the basic pharmacological and equipment requirements were largely met. However, organizational safeguards for patient safety - a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation, and regular training - were often lacking, indicating both deviations from international recommendations and clear targets for improvement.

CONCLUSION: In the responding Hungarian emergency departments, the airway management practice for patients with preserved circulation was highly heterogeneous and insufficiently standardized. Priorities for improvement include a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation and a national registry, and regular training. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1835-1842.

articles.title: A Potential New Therapeutic Option for Exercise Intolerance in Patients with Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Iron Repletion in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The IRONMET-HFpEF Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is present in >50% of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and is associated with reduced exercise capacity and survival. Whether iron repletion improves exercise capacity as objectively measured by peak oxygen uptake ([Formula: see text]) is unknown. The IRONMET-HFpEF trial (Impact of Intravenous Iron Repletion on Mechanisms of Exercise Intolerance in HFpEF) sought to determine whether ferric derisomaltose (FDI) compared with placebo improves peak [Formula: see text] in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency.

METHODS: This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and iron deficiency, defined as ferritin <100 ng/mL or <300 ng/mL with transferrin saturation <20%. Participants were enrolled between December 2021 and April 2026. Single-dose ferric derisomaltose (1000 mg; n=44) or placebo (n=21) was administered once intravenously. The primary end point was the change in peak [Formula: see text] from baseline to 12 weeks with an analysis of covariance model including terms for treatment group, baseline peak [Formula: see text], and sex. Secondary end points included changes in [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, New York Heart Association class, health status assessed by the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score, and iron biomarkers at 12 weeks.

RESULTS: Among 65 randomized participants (median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 58-76 years], 72% women, transferrin saturation 16.0±7.4%, ferritin 57.8±48.9 ng/mL), 64 (98.5%) completed the study. The median baseline peak [Formula: see text] was 12.7 mL·kg-1·min-1 (interquartile range, 10.6-15.8 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the FDI group and 12.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (11.6-14.6 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, peak [Formula: see text] improved by 1.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI, 0.6-1.7) in the FDI group and was unchanged (0.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, -0.7 to 0.9]) in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, 1.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, 0.2-1.9]; P=0.02). [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, and New York Heart Association class also improved in the FDI compared with the placebo group (all P<0.05), whereas the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score did not differ significantly between groups (FDI group, +4.4 [95% CI, -2.4 to 11.2]; P=0.20). FDI increased transferrin saturation (9.4% [95% CI, 4.9%-13.9%]) and ferritin (183 ng/mL [95% CI, 128-238]) compared with the placebo group (PLSMD<0.001 for both). There were no serious adverse events related to FDI administration.

CONCLUSIONS: In the largest trial to date of iron repletion in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency, FDI improved multiple measures of exercise capacity.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04945707.

articles.title: Early third-trimester maternal cardiac function and morphometry in high-risk pregnancies that subsequently developed fetal growth restriction and/or pre-eclampsia.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate maternal cardiovascular function and cardiac morphology in early third-trimester pregnancies at high risk for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and compare findings between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or pre-eclampsia (PE) and uncomplicated pregnancies.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies at high risk for FGR referred to the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Department at the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain, between August 2022 and August 2024, for a routine second-trimester fetal anomaly scan. The patients were assessed between 27 + 0 and 28 + 6 weeks' gestation and were only included in the analysis if they did not have a diagnosis of FGR or PE at the time of evaluation; those who subsequently developed FGR and/or PE were identified during follow-up. Maternal echocardiography was performed to assess cardiac output (CO), stroke volume (SV), systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and structural parameters including left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and chamber volumes. Results were compared between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR (with or without PE), pregnancies that subsequently developed isolated PE and uncomplicated pregnancies. Multivariable analysis was performed using quantile regression of the medians for CO and SVR, adjusted for body mass index (BMI), with FGR and PE assessed independently.

RESULTS: A total of 948 patients were included in the final analysis, of whom 129 developed FGR and/or PE (including 59 that developed FGR (with or without PE) and 70 that developed isolated PE) and 819 had uncomplicated pregnancies. Median mean arterial pressure (MAP) was higher in the FGR (with or without PE) group (82.0 mmHg) and the isolated-PE group (84.8 mmHg) than in the uncomplicated group (79.7 mmHg; P = 0.027 and P < 0.001, respectively), with the isolated-PE group showing the highest MAP values (isolated PE vs FGR (with or without PE), P = 0.047). Median heart rate was elevated in the isolated-PE group (82.5 bpm) compared with the FGR (with or without PE) group (77.0 bpm; P = 0.03). In the multivariable analysis, FGR and PE were associated independently with lower CO and higher SVR prior to their development. Median SV was reduced in the FGR (with or without PE) group (59.7 mL) and the isolated-PE group (61.1 mL) compared with the uncomplicated group (64.2 mL; P = 0.030 and P = 0.016, respectively). Median BMI-indexed CO was also lower in the FGR (with or without PE) group (0.18 (L/min)/(kg/m2)) and the isolated-PE group (0.17 (L/min)/(kg/m2)) compared with the uncomplicated group (0.19 (L/min)/(kg/m2); P = 0.005 and P = 0.001, respectively). Median SVR was elevated in the FGR (with or without PE) group (1393 dynes × s/cm5) and the isolated-PE group (1339 dynes × s/cm5) compared with the uncomplicated group (1252 dynes × s/cm5; P < 0.001 and P = 0.01, respectively). Compared with the uncomplicated group, the isolated-PE group showed greater median LV myocardial thickness at end diastole (0.50 vs 0.47 cm; P = 0.003), interventricular septal thickness at end diastole (0.92 vs 0.89 cm; P = 0.031), posterior wall thickness at end diastole (0.98 vs 0.94 cm; P = 0.013) and relative wall thickness (0.45 vs 0.42; P = 0.001). Moreover, the FGR (with or without PE) group had a smaller median LV end-diastolic diameter (4.27 cm) compared with the uncomplicated group (4.48 cm; P = 0.003), indicating that preload may be reduced in patients who developed FGR (with or without PE). LV mass indexed for BMI was similar across groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Maternal cardiovascular alterations may precede the development of FGR and PE and differ by phenotype. Pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or PE showed reduced CO, but those that developed FGR reflected lower preload without tachycardia, while those that developed isolated PE showed hypertensive features with a compensatory rise in heart rate. Maternal echocardiography may aid early risk stratification and guide tailored surveillance and therapy in pregnancies at high risk for FGR. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: A Pilot Clinical and Experimental Study of Type I Collagen Matrix Implantation Versus Microfracture for Knee Cartilage Defects.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Microfracture is used to treat cartilage defects but may compromise subchondral bone integrity. Type I collagen matrix implantation has emerged as a potential alternative for advanced (Outerbridge III-IV) lesions, although supporting evidence remains limited. This study combined clinical evaluation with an animal model to validate treatment outcomes. The aim was to compare short-term clinical efficacy and cartilage repair quality of Type I collagen matrix implantation versus microfracture and to validate clinical findings in an animal model. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective, randomized, exploratory pilot translational study included both animal and clinical experiments. Full-thickness cartilage defects were created in 18 rats and treated with a blank control, microfracture, or Type I collagen implantation. After 12 weeks, gross and histological evaluations (Safranin O/Fast Green staining) were performed. Concurrently, 36 patients with knee cartilage defects were enrolled in a randomized, single-blind trial (collagen group, n=20; microfracture group, n=16) and followed for 12 months. Lysholm, International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC), and Magnetic Resonance Observation of Cartilage Repair Tissue (MOCART) scores were recorded preoperatively (Lysholm and IKDC only) and at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. RESULTS In the animal model, Type I collagen implantation produced superior cartilage and subchondral bone repair compared with the control and microfracture groups. Clinically, both groups showed significant improvement; the collagen group consistently achieved higher functional and MOCART scores (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS Type I collagen matrix implantation was associated with more favorable cartilage regeneration and better short-term clinical outcomes than microfracture, representing an effective biomaterial-assisted treatment strategy for knee cartilage defects.

articles.title: Risk of red blood cell transfusion in patients with preoperative anemia requiring cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative anemia is common and a strong predictor of perioperative red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in cardiac surgical patients. Both anemia and RBC transfusion are independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes, but their interrelationship is difficult to disentangle because RBC transfusion acts as a mediator rather than a confounder.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the relationship between preoperative anemia, RBC transfusion, and postoperative outcomes in cardiac surgery, with particular emphasis on recent advances in causal inference mediation analysis. We discuss outcome-specific mediation patterns, patient characteristics that may modify anemia and transfusion related risk, and implications for perioperative management.

EXPERT OPINION: Mediation analysis provides a valuable framework for distinguishing the direct effects of anemia from RBC transfusion-mediated effects. Current evidence suggests that RBC transfusion mediates a substantial proportion of anemia-associated mortality, whereas direct anemia effects appear more important for renal complications. Future patient blood management should move beyond uniform transfusion thresholds toward individualized strategies that account for patient's risk profile, physiological reserve, intraoperative factors and the outcome-specific balance between the potential benefits of correcting anemia and the risks of RBC transfusion.

articles.title: Optimizing colistin dosing in acute-on-chronic liver failure patients with sepsis due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) patients with sepsis represent a special population that is highly susceptible to serious infections but remains understudied for antibiotic dose optimization. Colistin, a reserve antibiotic for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, is frequently used for management of sepsis in this group of patients. There is an unmet medical need to describe a dosing regimen developed using a population pharmacokinetic approach in this group of patients.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: ACLF patients receiving intravenous colistin were enrolled. Population pharmacokinetic modeling was performed using nonlinear mixed-effects methods, with covariate analysis and bootstrap validation. Monte Carlo simulations were conducted to evaluate the probability of target attainment (PTA) across dosing regimens and renal function strata.

RESULTS: A total of 68 plasma concentrations from eligible patients admitted over 2 years were analyzed. Colistin pharmacokinetics were adequately described by a one-compartment model, with considerable inter-individual variability. Creatinine clearance was found to be a significant covariate for clearance. The probability of target attainment (PTA) for pertinent PK/PD index varied across different dosing regimens and renal function strata.

CONCLUSIONS: Colistin pharmacokinetics in patients with ACLF is highly variable, with creatinine clearance emerging as a significant covariate. We propose a creatinine-clearance-guided dosing regimen based on the findings of the study.

articles.title: Highly specific detection of PET NPs using an amino-functionalized PEC sensor based on a SnS2@MoS2 heterojunction.
articles.abstract: The rapid detection of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) nanoplastics (PET NPs) is hindered by their low concentration, high mobility and lack of a distinguishable interface with other nanoplastics. In this study, we developed an SnS2@MoS2/APTES amino-functionalized photoelectrochemical sensor capable of detecting PET NPs with high specificity. The SnS2@MoS2 heterojunction synthesized via in situ hydrothermal synthesis and the APTES self-assembled amino-functionalized interface enable PET NPs to interact with amino-functionalized interface at multiple sites through oxygen-containing groups such as ester groups, carbonyl oxygen and ether oxygen. The sensor exhibits a detection range of 0.5-800 μg mL-1 for PET NPs, with a detection limit of 0.17 μg mL-1. DFT calculations further indicate that the PET-APTES system exhibits a lower adsorption energy (-1.37 eV) and a more significant interfacial charge rearrangement, demonstrating that the APTES amino siloxane interface exhibits a polymer structural selectivity toward PET. Furthermore, this PEC sensor exhibits good recovery rates (96.04%-102.76%) in practical water samples such as seawater, bottled water and tap water. It provides a new method for interface recognition and signal conversion for the specific PEC detection of PET nanoplastics.

articles.title: Instant CMQT stabilization coupled UHPLC-MS/MS for the quantification of reduced and total forms of cysteine, homocysteine, and glutathione in blood plasma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced and total forms of cysteine (Cys), homocysteine (Hcy), and glutathione (GSH) are key players in redox homeostasis, and their dysregulation is linked to diseases such as sepsis. However, accurate quantification of reduced thiols in plasma remains challenging due to rapid air oxidation of native thiols. In this work, a thiol-specific reagent (2-chloro-1-methylquinolinium tetrafluoroborate, CMQT) that reacts rapidly under mild conditions was coupled with UHPLC-MS/MS to develop a method for the simultaneous determination of reduced and total forms of Cys, Hcy, and GSH in plasma samples.

RESULTS: CMQT rapidly stabilizes native thiols in whole blood without inducing hemolysis. The proposed method was validated for linearity, precision, accuracy and sensitivity. Calibration curves showed excellent linearity (R2 > 0.9993). Intra- and inter-day precisions ranged from 0.14% to 7.23%, and accuracy from -5.62% to 4.15%. The limits of detection for the reduced and total forms of Cys, Hcy and GSH ranged from 0.051 to 0.88 μM. The method was successfully applied to a lipopolysaccharide-induced endotoxemia mouse model, revealing that reduced Hcy and reduced GSH may serve as potential biomarkers for early and late oxidative stress, respectively. The method was also validated on human plasma samples, confirming its applicability across species and revealing sex-related thiol differences.

SIGNIFICANCE: The combination of rapid and hemolysis-free thiol stabilization with MS-based structural characterization provides a robust analytical tool for thiol redox studies and could be extended to other biological matrices.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pulmonary Hypertension: Advancements, Opportunities, and Challenges.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder associated with high morbidity and mortality. Delayed diagnosis, heterogeneous disease phenotypes, and variable treatment responses remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising tool for improving PH management. AI-based models have demonstrated promising performance in screening, diagnosis, classification, risk stratification, and prognosis prediction using multimodal data such as electrocardiography, chest radiography, computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and electronic health records. Furthermore, AI may support individualized risk assessment, treatment-response prediction, early identification of right ventricular deterioration, and longitudinal remote monitoring. Emerging technologies, including explainable AI, federated learning, large language models, and digital twins, may further advance precision medicine in PH. Despite these advances, data quality, interpretability, privacy, and clinical implementation of AI remain challenges. This review summarizes current applications, opportunities, and challenges of AI in PH and discusses future directions for AI-assisted precision healthcare.

articles.title: Lupus Retinopathy in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Prevalence, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associations with Severe Disease Activity and Antiphospholipid Antibody Status.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lupus retinopathy is an uncommon but clinically important manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) that may reflect systemic vascular injury and increased activity. However, data from South Asian populations are limited. To determine the prevalence, clinical spectrum, and factors associated with lupus retinopathy in patients with SLE, with particular emphasis on disease activity and antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) status. Methods: This hospital-based cross-sectional study included adults with SLE who met the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria and were consecutively recruited at a tertiary referral center in Bangladesh. All participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmological examinations, including dilated fundus examinations and fundus photography. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) were conducted as needed in the study. We evaluated disease activity using the SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K). We used logistic regression to examine the relationship between lupus retinopathy and other factors. We also analyzed the association between aPL status and retinopathy phenotype using Fisher's exact test. Results: Among 159 patients with SLE, 18 (11.3%) had ocular involvement and 16 (10.1%) had lupus retinopathy. Of the 16 patients with retinopathy, 11 (68.8%) had mild, 2 (12.5%) had moderate, and 3 (18.8%) had severe disease; 3 (18.8%) had occlusive and 13 (81.3%) had non-occlusive; retinonocclusive systemic disease activity was independently associated with lupus retinopathy (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 7.20; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.78-29.11; p = 0.006). Renal involvement was not independently associated with retinopathy (aOR, 2.31; 95% CI, 0.56-9.58; p = 0.247). Among patients with available aPL results, aPL positivity was not significantly associated with lupus retinopathy (41.7% vs. 26.7%; p = 0.315). However, among the 12 patients with retinopathy who had available aPL results, occlusive retinopathy occurred in 3/5 (60.0%) aPL-positive patients compared with 0/7 (0%) aPL-negative patients (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.045). OCT and FFA performed in eight patients demonstrated macular edema and bilateral retinal capillary non-perfusion in all cases. Conclusions: Lupus retinopathy affected approximately one in ten patients with SLE in this Bangladeshi cohort and was strongly associated with severe systemic disease. Although aPL positivity was not associated with retinopathy, it was associated with the occlusive phenotype in an exploratory analysis. These findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies with systematic aPL testing.

articles.title: Excess Cardiovascular Burden Among Young Patients with Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background: Young patients with cancer may develop cardiovascular complications decades earlier than the general population, yet their long-term cardiovascular risk remains incompletely defined. Most prior evidence derives from older adults or therapy-specific analyses, leaving adolescents and young adults understudied as a distinct population. Methods: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort, registry-based, and population-based studies evaluating cardiovascular outcomes or mortality among young patients with cancer (adolescents and young adults [15-39 years], <45 years, <50 years, or clearly defined young age subgroups) compared with age-matched comparators. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through 26 February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Evidence certainty was evaluated with GRADE. Random-effects models were used for pooled analyses. Results: Fifty-eight studies were included. Young patients with cancer had significantly increased risks of heart failure (HR, 4.08; 95% CI, 2.20-7.57), pulmonary embolism (HR, 4.63; 95% CI, 3.03-7.06), venous thrombosis (HR, 4.06; 95% CI, 2.51-6.58), and cardiomyopathy (HR, 3.52; 95% CI, 2.21-5.63). Cardiovascular mortality was also elevated (SMR, 4.30; 95% CI, 3.06-6.05), although a trim-and-fill analysis resulted in an adjusted pooled SMR of 1.79 (95% CI, 1.05-3.05, p = 0.0313). Overall cardiovascular disease risk was approximately 2-fold higher, with additional increases in stroke, arrhythmia, and hypertension. Heterogeneity was high for several key outcomes (I2, overall cardiovascular disease HR 96.0%; cardiovascular mortality SMR 99.1%; heart failure HR 92.5%; venous thrombosis HR 94.1%), and evidence certainty was low for most. Conclusions: Young patients with cancer face substantially increased risks of cardiovascular disease, particularly heart failure, cardiomyopathy, and thrombotic complications. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether earlier cardiovascular surveillance improves outcomes.

articles.title: An integrated analytical strategy combining UPLC-QTOF-MS-based metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing to explore the mechanism of Shenqi Jieyu decoction in coronary heart disease complicated by depression in ApoE-/- mice.
articles.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
articles.abstract: Coronary heart disease combined with depression (dual-heart disorder) exhibits high morbidity and poor prognosis, lacking safe unified therapeutic agents. Shenqi Jieyu Decoction (SQJY) relieves depressive and cardiovascular symptoms in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) patients, yet its underlying multiple potential mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an ApoE-/- mouse model of dual-heart disorder was induced via high-fat diet combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Behavioral testing, aortic pathological staining, hippocampal neurochemistry, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics of serum and cecal contents were integrated with 16S rRNA sequencing, establishing an integrated multi-omics workflow to examine the potential modulatory effects of SQJY and to explore its possible mechanism. Behavioral and pathological assays indicated that SQJY alleviated atherosclerosis and depression-like phenotypes, elevated hippocampal 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), dopamine (DA) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and suppressed neuroinflammatory cytokines. 16S sequencing suggested SQJY remodeled dysregulated gut microbiota toward a more balanced profile. Metabolomics identified disturbed sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism as important metabolic signatures that H-SQJY group corrected more extensively in cecal content (68 of 265 metabolites) than in serum (8 of 103). Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States 2 (PICRUSt2)-based prediction of microbial functions was integrated, and Spearman correlation analysis showed significant associations between predicted microbial functions, differential gut microbes and lipid metabolites. Collectively, SQJY showed concurrent potential cardioprotective and antidepressant effects, possibly through restoring gut microbial homeostasis and modulating lipid metabolic disorders. These correlative and predicted findings provide preliminary evidence for the potential application of SQJY in dual-heart disorder.

articles.title: Role of collagen in right ventricular passive anisotropic viscoelasticity with pulmonary hypertension.
articles.journal: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
articles.abstract: Collagen is a structural extracellular protein that contributes to the anisotropic elastic behavior of the right ventricle (RV). It is established that collagen is significantly altered in pulmonary hypertension (PH), including overall content, degree of cross-linking, and fiber alignment. The RV is viscoelastic, though, and how collagen contributes to the overall tissue viscoelastic behavior with PH development remains unknown. Therefore, the aim of this study was to investigate the role of collagen in the anisotropic viscoelasticity of the RV free wall (RVFW) during PH progression. Equibiaxial stress relaxation tests were performed in healthy and PH rat RVFW before and after the enzymatic breakdown of collagen via collagenase. A Fung-type quasilinear viscoelastic constitutive model was then applied to further delineate the changes in RVFW mechanics. We found that collagen degradation significantly reduced RVFW viscosity and elasticity, with stronger effects in the diseased group. The reduction in RVFW elastic behavior was stronger in the longitudinal direction than the circumferential, while the reduction in viscosity was similar between directions in both groups. Constitutive modeling results showed weakened RVFW stiffness after collagenase treatment in both groups, but distinct responses of relaxation strength coefficients between the healthy and diseased groups. In the longitudinal direction, the relaxation strength coefficients were positively correlated with the viscosity to elasticity ratio measured from experimental data in both groups. Our findings demonstrate distinct collagen deposition and morphology between healthy and diseased RVFW, suggesting that RV fibrosis results in unique regulation of RVFW mechanics.

articles.title: First use of a woven allogeneic vascular graft made of cell-assembled extracellular matrix (CAM) as an arteriovenous shunt in sheep: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: Reliable vascular access is vital for patients undergoing hemodialysis. Current arteriovenous shunts (AVS) made of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) are prone to thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, and infections. To overcome these limitations, biological Tissue-Engineered Vascular Grafts (TEVGs) were produced by weaving threads made from Cell-Assembled extracellular Matrix (CAM), i.e., extracellular matrix produced by ovine fibroblasts in culture. The woven TEVGs were designed with a 6 mm internal diameter and beveled ends to facilitate use as an AVS. They had a burst pressure (3069 ± 546 mmHg) and a compliance (4.4 ± 0.5%/100 mmHg) closer to those of native blood vessels than ePTFE prostheses. Woven TEVGs were implanted as carotid-jugular AVS in sheep and compared to ePTFE controls in a bilateral model (n = 8 animals). Grafts were easily punctured with 16G hemodialysis needles once at 4 weeks without loss of structural integrity or hemorrhagic complications. Overall TEVGs patency was 100%, while it was 87.5% for ePTFE grafts (n = 8). Histological analysis revealed an inflammatory response that decreased between 4 and 8 weeks. A luminal neotissue was observed at 8 weeks with smooth muscle cells and localized endothelialization. Localized calcification of CAM was observed and appeared to be correlated with high tissue compaction. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of using a completely biological TEVG made from woven CAM as an AVS in an allogeneic large animal model. Future studies are needed to understand and avoid the never-before-observed calcification of the CAM in a large animal model, as well as to determine longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Assessing Diastolic Function With AI and Echocardiography: From Risk Prediction to Therapeutic Targets.
Integrating polygenic and classical risk factors for cardiovascular risk stratification in a polish primary-care cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) promise improved cardiovascular risk stratification, but most validation derives from UK or Nordic biobanks. The transferability of these scores to Central European populations and their incremental value over classical risk factors in routine care remain unestablished.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether a coronary PRS derived from external European data transfers to a Polish primary-care population and adds discrimination for prevalent cardiovascular disease beyond classical risk factors.

METHODS: In the nationwide Polish LIPIDOGEN2015 primary-care cohort, we derived PRS for coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke from FinnGen data with continuous shrinkage priors and applied them to imputed genotypes. We compared allele frequencies of 1397 unrelated participants with a non-Finnish European (NFE) reference and, in 1328 participants with clinical data, related the PRS to coronary artery disease (CAD), MI and stroke recorded at baseline and to a composite including death during follow-up, with and without classical risk factors or SCORE2.

RESULTS: Allele frequencies correlated with the NFE reference (r = 0.97). Per standard deviation (SD), the coronary PRS was associated with prevalent CAD (odds ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.67) and the composite endpoint (1.26, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.51), as were two validated genome-wide scores. Adding it to classical risk factors changed the area under the curve (AUC) for the composite endpoint by 0.0017 (95% CI -0.0005 to 0.0076), from 0.860 to 0.861; results with SCORE2 were similar. The study had 80% power for odds ratios per SD of 1.31 (CAD) and 1.27 (composite).
